nodes.label: Yarn node-modules linker
nodes.rationale: Pinned so CI does not fall back to PnP: locally this comes from ~/.yarnrc.yml, which the runner has no copy of.

nodes.label: Grok memory store
nodes.rationale: Curated facts live in /mnt/Storage/my-learning/grok/; ignore ~/.grok/memory/.

nodes.label: Never-delete rule
nodes.rationale: Docs, pages, reviews and prior work are additive only; ask if removal seems required.

nodes.label: Single-agent default
nodes.rationale: Do not spawn subagents unless the user explicitly asks.

nodes.label: Explanation cadence
nodes.rationale: Each topic page must be visible in the UI as written; after a complete phase run yarn build once.

nodes.label: Claude memory store
nodes.rationale: All project memory lives in /mnt/Storage/my-learning/claude/; ~/.claude/ memory dirs are banned.

nodes.label: Global rules vs project memory split
nodes.rationale: Hard rules that must never be looked up live in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md; project-specific memory lives in the store.

nodes.label: Dev Bible
nodes.rationale: One reference that explains everything needed to build a fullstack application across MERN and PERN.

nodes.label: In-scope tech stack
nodes.rationale: Twelve technologies: CSS, JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Node.js, MongoDB, PostgreSQL, Express, Docker & Podman, Redis, Nginx, Git.

nodes.label: Parked technologies
nodes.rationale: GraphQL, tRPC and Kubernetes are named on the homepage but not committed until the eleven (now twelve with Git) are done.

nodes.label: GraphQL (parked)
nodes.rationale: Parked because it is an API-design layer that would overlap Express if pulled in early.

nodes.label: tRPC (parked)
nodes.rationale: Parked: only pays off in an end-to-end TypeScript stack.

nodes.label: Kubernetes (parked)
nodes.rationale: Parked: a layer above Docker & Nginx; only earns its place at real scale.

nodes.label: Git (in scope)
nodes.rationale: Moved into scope 2026-08-13; was parked as universal tooling rather than part of the stack itself.

nodes.label: Priority tiers
nodes.rationale: Tiers allocate effort, not importance. Keep MASTER to roughly 25–30% of topics.

nodes.label: Concept page contents
nodes.rationale: Every concept needs runnable examples, 3–8 interview questions with answers, and gotchas as symptom → cause → fix.

nodes.label: Granularity rule
nodes.rationale: A topic is a concept, not a symbol. Group things only meaningful together; never group to reduce coverage.

nodes.label: 300-line file cap
nodes.rationale: A file-size rule, never a content budget. Write the explanation first, then split on a concept boundary.

nodes.label: Chunked topic layout
nodes.rationale: A topic that exceeds the cap becomes a directory with README index and numbered chunks that each repeat the tier badge and Verified line.

nodes.label: Approved colour palette
nodes.rationale: Cool blue-biased neutrals; pine accent, deliberately not the acid-green Node cliché.

nodes.label: Handbook writing style
nodes.rationale: Concept → why it exists → runnable code → gotchas → when to use it. Second person, present tense, name the trade-off.

nodes.label: Incremental working process
nodes.rationale: Do the step that was asked, then stop. Syllabus first, then pages. Target Active LTS, not newest release.

nodes.label: Node 24 Active LTS target
nodes.rationale: Build on Node 24 until October 2026, then 26. Never use an API the target LTS lacks.

nodes.label: One docs tree per language
nodes.rationale: Everything about a technology lives under docs/<lang>/ with syllabus/, pages/ and reviews/.

nodes.label: Deploy to GitHub Pages
nodes.rationale: One deploy at a time; in-progress runs finish so a half-uploaded artifact never becomes the live site.

nodes.label: Enable corepack before setup-node
nodes.rationale: Must precede setup-node: cache: yarn shells out to yarn cache dir, which Yarn 1 refuses once packageManager pins Yarn 4.

nodes.label: Broken-links report step
nodes.rationale: onBrokenLinks is warn, so dead links never fail the build; the job reports them rather than blocking.

nodes.label: Critical 300-line rule
nodes.rationale: Write the explanation the topic deserves first, then split. Clustering at ~200–290 is evidence of budgeting.

nodes.label: Never invent output
nodes.rationale: Every number, timing and error string comes from a run that actually happened. No run means no console block.

nodes.label: No new sandboxes
nodes.rationale: Validate against official documentation or the web and name the source in the Verified line.

nodes.label: Markdown link form
nodes.rationale: Every link ends in .md and keeps every numeric prefix. The directory-slug form broke 188 links.

nodes.label: Shared-checkout claims table
nodes.rationale: Sessions claim a language before writing so parallel work does not collide.

nodes.label: CSS syllabus
nodes.rationale: Critical-path syllabus, not a CSS course. Cut twice: 230 → 119 → 74 topics.

nodes.label: CSS is resolved, not executed
nodes.rationale: You write constraints and the engine computes the result. Explains silent typos, specificity, and height: 100% doing nothing.

nodes.label: CSS scope rule
nodes.rationale: If deleting the stylesheet would delete the topic, it is CSS's.

nodes.label: CSS Master share 65%
nodes.rationale: Master is 65% because the syllabus was cut to critical-only; do not relabel rows to hit the 25–30% band.

nodes.label: CSS example policy
nodes.rationale: Measured behaviour comes from the local Firefox render; cross-browser availability comes from web-features. Keep the two apart.

nodes.label: HTTP API design half
nodes.rationale: Roughly half of this syllabus is HTTP API design that happens to be mounted on Express. Node refused to absorb REST modeling.

nodes.label: Express boundary rule
nodes.rationale: Concept → Node (or DB / Redis / Docker / Nginx). Middleware + route surface + HTTP contracts → Express.

nodes.label: Git content-addressed object store
nodes.rationale: Git is a key-value database keyed by content hash plus refs. Explains snapshots, rebase hashes, and reset flags.

nodes.label: Git scope rule
nodes.rationale: If it still applies when you delete every framework from the repo, it is Git's. Stops at the push event.

nodes.label: Git Part 2 Working with other people
Git Part 3 Git in a real project
Default initial branch still master
nodes.rationale: On git 2.55.0 git init still defaults to master; the change is scheduled for Git 3.0.

nodes.label: JavaScript syllabus
nodes.rationale: Largest syllabus on purpose: language + Web APIs + DSA + applied storefront.

nodes.label: JS Part 4 DSA and machine coding
Event loop split
nodes.rationale: Language half (job queue, microtasks) is JS Phase 7; runtime half (libuv, setImmediate, nextTick) is Node Phase 2.

nodes.label: Network split at the wire
nodes.rationale: fetch, AbortController, FormData and how CORS fails in the console are JS; status-code design and server headers are Express.

nodes.label: JavaScript has no prerequisites
nodes.rationale: First syllabus in the bible with no prerequisite outside itself.

nodes.label: JS verification policy
nodes.rationale: Parts 1, 2, 4 run in Node 24. Parts 3 and 5 never invent browser console output; unmeasured pages get a VERIFY marker.

nodes.label: Node release schedule
nodes.rationale: Odd/even unstable-vs-stable ends with v27: one major each April, LTS each October.

nodes.label: Do not skip Node Phase 0
nodes.rationale: Every Node is weird complaint traces back to skipping the runtime model.

nodes.label: Do not start Express before Phase 5
nodes.rationale: Express is a thin layer over node:http. Learning it first means learning the abstraction without the thing it abstracts.

nodes.label: PG Part 3 Node and raw pg
PG dual-half example policy
nodes.rationale: Every page carries both the SQL (or shell) and the Node pg code that issues it.

nodes.label: Recap rule Node Phase 6
nodes.rationale: Pool sizing, transaction propagation, N+1 and ORM comparison recap in ≤40 lines and link to Node Phase 6.

nodes.label: Never use localhost for pg
nodes.rationale: Examples run against 127.0.0.1:55432, never localhost — the IPv6 trap.

nodes.label: React computes a UI description
nodes.rationale: A renderer applies it. Why react and react-dom are separate, why RSC can exist, why keys matter, why mutation never works.

nodes.label: React scope rule
nodes.rationale: If removing React would remove the topic, it is React's.

nodes.label: React Part 4 Building a real app
ViewTransition still experimental
nodes.rationale: ViewTransition and gesture transitions are all over 2025–26 talks and still not in the stable package.

nodes.label: Do not skip React Phase 3
nodes.rationale: Every React is weird complaint — stale values, state that didn't update, infinite loops — traces back to the render cycle.

nodes.label: Types are erased
nodes.rationale: A checker that runs at build time and leaves nothing at runtime. Why validation still exists, why as is dangerous, why enum is unlike other types.

nodes.label: TypeScript scope rule
nodes.rationale: If removing the types would remove the topic, it is TypeScript's.

nodes.label: TS Part 3 TypeScript in the stack
TypeScript 7 native Go compiler
nodes.rationale: typescript@7.0.2 ships platform binaries; require('typescript') exports only version keys. The classic ts.* API moved.

nodes.label: erasableSyntaxOnly and strip-only mode
nodes.rationale: Node 24 runs .ts with no flag, but enum fails: TypeScript enum is not supported in strip-only mode.

nodes.label: CSS two-source verification
nodes.rationale: What does this do? measured in Firefox 153. Is it safe to ship? web-features Baseline.

nodes.label: Cascade comparison order
nodes.rationale: Origin and importance, then context, then inline styles, then layers, then specificity, then source order. First criterion that separates two declarations ends the comparison.

nodes.label: @layer
nodes.rationale: Declare precedence up front; unlayered is the implicit final layer. Load-bearing reason this phase exists.

nodes.label: CSS as a declarative constraint language
nodes.rationale: CSS states claims about elements; the engine finds the one winning value per property. There is no execution order or call stack, so you debug by asking which rules matched and which won.

nodes.label: CSSOM
nodes.rationale: The live object model a stylesheet is parsed into (document.styleSheets / cssRules). The engine consults this, not the authored text; malformed rules silently vanish from the count.

nodes.label: Parse-time value normalization
nodes.rationale: Authored text is not retained: #ff0000 becomes rgb(), padding/border shorthands expand to longhands, and unspecified longhands get defaults such as currentcolor.

nodes.label: Rendering pipeline stages
nodes.rationale: Style → layout (reflow) → paint (repaint) → composite. A change at one stage forces every later stage, never earlier ones.

nodes.label: Composite-only properties
nodes.rationale: transform and opacity run after layout and paint. Neighbours do not reflow around a transformed box, so they can overlap.

nodes.label: Layout-invalidating properties
nodes.rationale: width, height, padding, margin, inset, font-size, display, flex/grid tracks. Never animate these; left and transformX can land in the same place but only left recomputes geometry.

nodes.label: Four ways CSS reaches the page
nodes.rationale: link (default, cacheable, parallel), style (critical CSS, cached with HTML), inline style (script-computed values), and @import (avoid in delivered CSS).

nodes.label: @import serializes stylesheet requests
nodes.rationale: The imported file is undiscoverable until the importer is parsed. Measured at 500 ms delay: chained @import FCP 1076 ms vs parallel links 636 ms.

nodes.label: Inline style as a cascade decision
nodes.rationale: A normal inline declaration beats every author rule except author !important. Prefer setting a custom property inline and consuming it from a stylesheet.

nodes.label: Render-blocking CSS
nodes.rationale: The browser will not paint until matching stylesheets arrive, choosing a blank frame over FOUC. Measured: no CSS FCP 47 ms vs delayed matching sheet 671 ms.

nodes.label: Non-matching media does not block paint
nodes.rationale: media=print or a non-matching query is still fetched at low priority but does not wait. Basis of the print+onload non-critical CSS trick; styles land after first paint.

nodes.label: CSS fails silently
nodes.rationale: A mistake is discarded with no console message, exception, or build failure. A typo and a future feature are indistinguishable to the engine.

nodes.label: Declaration vs selector blast radius
nodes.rationale: An invalid declaration is dropped locally; an invalid selector in a plain comma list discards the whole rule; an unclosed brace swallows following rules.

nodes.label: Silent drop enables forward compatibility
nodes.rationale: If unknown syntax were fatal, no new CSS feature could ship without breaking older browsers. Progressive enhancement depends on this generosity.

nodes.label: CSS.supports and style round-trip
nodes.rationale: The only APIs that volunteer validity: CSS.supports(property, value), or assign to element.style and read back — empty string means rejected.

nodes.label: User-agent stylesheet
nodes.rationale: A page with no CSS is still styled: body 8px margin, heading sizes, list indent as padding, img inline, box-sizing content-box.

nodes.label: Form controls do not inherit font
nodes.rationale: UA sets an explicit 13.3333px sans-serif on button/input, beating inheritance. Fix: font: inherit, then set the page font on body or :root.

nodes.label: Cascade origin order
nodes.rationale: Normal: user-agent < user < author. !important inverts so a user accessibility override beats author !important. Any author type selector beats any UA default.

nodes.label: Modern small CSS reset
nodes.rationale: A dozen justifiable lines beat a 300-line library: border-box on * plus pseudos, margin 0, line-height 1.5, block media, font inherit on controls, overflow-wrap.

nodes.label: box-sizing: border-box
nodes.rationale: width/height include padding and border. Applied to *, *::before, *::after so generated content is not left on content-box.

nodes.label: Reset vs normalise vs nothing
nodes.rationale: Normalize.css patched 2012 engine differences that have largely converged. A small modern reset is the 2026 default; hard-resetting list-style or *:focus outline is a defect.

nodes.label: CSS at-rule map
nodes.rationale: About a dozen at-rules worth knowing: @media/@container, @supports, @layer, @scope, @property, @font-face, @keyframes, @starting-style, @page, @counter-style, @import.

nodes.label: Unknown at-rule drops its whole block
nodes.rationale: An unrecognized at-rule is discarded silently with every rule inside it. Base styling must live outside recent at-rules; enhancement only goes inside.

nodes.label: Block vs statement at-rules
nodes.rationale: Block forms wrap rules and nest; statement forms end at a semicolon. @layer has both: @layer a, b; declares order, @layer a { } fills a layer. First mention sets order.

nodes.label: @supports feature queries
nodes.rationale: Asks the engine whether it can parse a declaration or selector, then styles accordingly. Parentheses required; selectors need selector().

nodes.label: Cascade-safe fallback without @supports
nodes.rationale: Declare the fallback value first and the modern value second. Engines that cannot parse the second keep the first. Use @supports only when the fallback needs different properties.

nodes.label: @supports tests parse not correctness
nodes.rationale: An engine can parse a property, apply it partially, and pass. Cannot test at-rules directly — test a declaration that implies them, e.g. container-type: inline-size.

nodes.label: Baseline widely / newly / limited
nodes.rationale: Widely = all core browsers for 30 months (just use). Newly = all core browsers now (use, fallback if conservative). Limited = at least one missing (enhancement only, always guarded).

nodes.label: web-features Baseline dataset
nodes.rationale: npm package behind MDN/web.dev badges (1186 features in 3.34.3). status.baseline is high|low|false. Checkable in CI; :has, nesting, layers Widely since 2023.

nodes.label: Local support is not shipping safety
nodes.rationale: Firefox 153 supports anchor-positioning and accent-color (both Limited). One engine's CSS.supports true is how Limited features reach production broken.

nodes.label: Vendor prefixes in 2026
nodes.rationale: Mostly history. New features ship behind flags. Exceptions: -webkit-line-clamp still required; -webkit-backdrop-filter for Safari. Manage the rest with Autoprefixer/Lightning CSS.

nodes.label: -webkit-line-clamp still required
nodes.rationale: Unprefixed line-clamp is false in Firefox 153; -webkit-line-clamp is true. Full incantation still needs display:-webkit-box and -webkit-box-orient:vertical.

nodes.label: A -webkit- prefix is not a browser detector
nodes.rationale: Firefox implements -webkit-user-select, -webkit-box-shadow, -webkit-appearance for compatibility. Authors shipped WebKit-only CSS; prefixes as detectors failed.

nodes.label: DevTools as the CSS error console
nodes.rationale: Because CSS reports nothing, the Styles pane is the error console the language lacks. Inspect first: which rules match, which declarations lost.

nodes.label: Struck-through declaration: two causes
nodes.rationale: Cascade loss (winner in Computed) versus parse failure (warning triangle, property missing from Computed). Opposite fixes: specificity/layer vs syntax.

nodes.label: CSS debugging order
nodes.rationale: In order: is the element in the DOM, did the rule parse, did it match ($0.matches), did it win (strike-through/Computed), is the box where you think (Layout).

nodes.label: Attribute selector operators
nodes.rationale: Seven operators: presence, = exact, ~= space-list, |= hyphen prefix (lang), ^= starts, $= ends, *= contains. Specificity 0,1,0. Values case-sensitive unless i flag.

nodes.label: [class~=] vs [class*=]
nodes.rationale: ~= matches a whole space-separated token (like .a). *= is a substring over the whole string and also matches alpha/banana. *= on class is almost always wrong.

nodes.label: Style on aria-* attributes
nodes.rationale: Visual state and accessibility state cannot drift if they are the same attribute. A parallel .is-open class can be forgotten.

nodes.label: Four CSS combinators
nodes.rationale: Descendant (any depth), child >, next sibling +, subsequent sibling ~. Descendant leaks into nested components; child breaks on extra wrappers.

nodes.label: Owl selector * + *
nodes.rationale: .flow > * + * applies spacing to every child except the first because + requires a preceding sibling. Vertical rhythm without a :first-child exception.

nodes.label: Selectors evaluate right-to-left
nodes.rationale: The engine finds the key (rightmost) selector then walks left. main * is heavier than main > .thing because the candidate set is every element.

nodes.label: Form-state pseudo-classes
nodes.rationale: :checked, :required/:optional, :valid/:invalid, :user-valid/:user-invalid, :placeholder-shown, :indeterminate, :in-range/:out-of-range, :autofill.

nodes.label: :invalid vs :user-invalid
nodes.rationale: :invalid matches from page load so empty required fields paint red on arrival. :user-invalid waits until the user has interacted — the CSS replacement for a JS touched flag.

nodes.label: :placeholder-shown empty-field test
nodes.rationale: There is no :empty for inputs. :placeholder-shown requires a placeholder attribute — often placeholder=" " just to make the selector work.

nodes.label: Custom checkbox via appearance: none
nodes.rationale: Keep the real input and style it. Hiding it and styling a sibling div removes tab order and accessibility tree membership.

nodes.label: :has() parent and previous-sibling selector
nodes.rationale: Styles an element from descendants or later siblings. Baseline Widely since 2023-12-19. p:has(+ p) is a previous-sibling selector CSS could not express before.

nodes.label: :has() restrictions and cost
nodes.rationale: No :has() inside :has(); no pseudo-elements in the argument; unforgiving. Upward invalidation: 8× a class at 5000 rows (1.25 ms) — still cheaper than the JS it replaces except on huge subjects that change every frame.

nodes.label: :is() vs :where() specificity
nodes.rationale: They match identically. :is() contributes the most specific argument (an id raises every match); :where() always contributes zero. Both have forgiving argument lists.

nodes.label: :where() for overridable defaults
nodes.rationale: Resets, library base styles, and .prose rules should weigh nothing so a consumer class always wins. Zero specificity does not mean no effect — anything else wins.

nodes.label: Native CSS nesting
nodes.rationale: Baseline Widely since 2023-12-11. & is the parent selector reference, not string concatenation. At-rules nest too. Write the &.

nodes.label: Native nesting is not Sass concatenation
nodes.rationale: Sass &__title builds .card__title. Native CSS treats that as invalid and drops it. BEM suffix generation cannot survive dropping the preprocessor.

nodes.label: Nesting hides specificity growth
nodes.rationale: Each level compiles to another descendant class. Four tidy levels become 0,4,0. & in a compound with a list behaves like :is() and takes the highest parent specificity. Keep nesting to two levels.

nodes.label: :not() negation
nodes.rationale: Accepts lists and complex selectors. Specificity is the most specific argument. :not(.a, .b) means neither, not 'not a or not b'. Neutralise with :not(:where(#id)).

nodes.label: :empty whitespace trap
nodes.rationale: Requires no child nodes at all. A space or newline is a text node so pretty-printed HTML rarely matches. Comments do not count. Prefer :not(:has(*)) when it fails.

nodes.label: :root for global custom properties
nodes.rationale: Matches html in HTML documents but at class specificity 0,1,0. Top of the inheritance chain; properties on body never reach anything above body.

nodes.label: :lang() and :dir()
nodes.rationale: :lang() matches inherited language including subtags. :dir() matches computed direction including dir=auto, unlike [dir=rtl] which only sees an explicit attribute.

nodes.label: Pseudo-elements are not in the DOM
nodes.rationale: Engine-created boxes with no node. querySelector('::before') is null; generated text is absent from textContent. Reachable only via getComputedStyle(el, '::before').

nodes.label: content is mandatory on ::before/::after
nodes.rationale: Without content the pseudo-element does not exist. content:"" still creates the box. They sit as first/last children, so padding and overflow apply and they can be flex/grid items.

nodes.label: @scope donut scoping
nodes.rationale: @scope (.root) to (.limit) styles inside the root and stops at the limit inclusive. No combinator/:not() chain expresses a hole. Baseline Newly available 2025-12-12.

nodes.label: @scope does not add specificity
nodes.rationale: @scope (.card) { .title } stays 0,1,0; .card .title would be 0,2,0. Containment equivalent of :where().

nodes.label: @scope proximity cascade
nodes.rationale: When two scoped rules match, the nearer scoping root wins before specificity. The only place DOM distance participates in the cascade; enables nearest-ancestor theming.

nodes.label: Unforgiving selector lists
nodes.rationale: One invalid selector in a plain comma list discards the entire rule. Adding :popover-open to a shared list silently unstyles every other component in unsupported engines.

nodes.label: Forgiving :is() argument lists
nodes.rationale: :is() and :where() drop invalid members and keep valid ones. :not() and :has() are unforgiving. Uncertain selectors get their own rule or wrap in :is().

nodes.label: Style invalidation breadth
nodes.rationale: Matching cost is rarely the bottleneck; jank comes from how much of the tree must restyle when state changes.

nodes.label: Right-to-left selector matching
nodes.rationale: Engines start from the rightmost compound so the candidate set is small and failed ancestors prune fast.

nodes.label: Key selector bucketing
nodes.rationale: An element is only tested against rules whose rightmost part could match it.

nodes.label: :has() matching cost
nodes.rationale: Relational matching is slower than a class (1.25 ms vs 0.15 ms on 5000 nodes) but only hurts when the subject is huge and the argument changes every frame.

nodes.label: Delete unused CSS
nodes.rationale: The one selector-performance win that reliably pays: fewer bytes, less parse, fewer rules to bucket.

nodes.label: Shadow DOM style boundary
nodes.rationale: Selectors do not cross a shadow root in either direction; that is real encapsulation unlike CSS Modules or @scope.

nodes.label: :host and :host-context()
nodes.rationale: :host styles the component element; :host-context() matches when an ancestor matches, for theme adaptation.

nodes.label: ::part()
nodes.rationale: Component opts an element in for outside styling; descendants stay private — ::part(header) .title does not work.

nodes.label: ::slotted()
nodes.rationale: Styles top-level light-DOM slotted nodes only; page rules win because those nodes belong to the light tree.

nodes.label: Custom properties cross shadow
nodes.rationale: Inherited properties including all custom properties pass the boundary — the primary theming API.

nodes.label: Page beats :host
nodes.rationale: A page rule on the host element wins over the shadow stylesheet's :host regardless of specificity; shadow :host is a default.

nodes.label: :focus vs :focus-visible
nodes.rationale: :focus matches any focus including mouse click; :focus-visible is the keyboard/AT ring so outline:none on :focus is no longer needed.

nodes.label: :focus-within
nodes.rationale: Parent selector for focus containment that predates :has(); highlight a field or keep a menu open.

nodes.label: LVHA link order
nodes.rationale: Equal-specificity link states must be :link :visited :hover :active or visited links lose hover.

nodes.label: :visited privacy restrictions
nodes.rationale: Only colour properties apply and getComputedStyle lies, so sites cannot leak browsing history.

nodes.label: :target
nodes.rationale: Matches the element whose id equals the URL fragment; can drive tabs without JS at the cost of history entries.

nodes.label: :disabled vs aria-disabled
nodes.rationale: disabled removes the control from tab order and the accessibility tree; aria-disabled keeps it announceable.

nodes.label: :nth-child(An+B)
nodes.rationale: n counts from 0; matches 1-based sibling index. -n+3 is the first-three idiom.

nodes.label: :nth-child vs :nth-of-type
nodes.rationale: :nth-child counts every sibling then checks type; :nth-of-type counts only that type. p:nth-child(2) can miss or pick the wrong p.

nodes.label: :nth-child of S
nodes.rationale: of S changes what is counted. :nth-child(odd of :not([hidden])) stripes after filtering.

nodes.label: Structural selectors use DOM order
nodes.rationale: display:none and flex/grid visual order do not change :nth-child counts.

nodes.label: Three consumers, three hooks
nodes.rationale: Style on class, state on data-*/aria-*, tests on data-testid, script on data-* or js-; one consumer per hook so a rename stays local.

nodes.label: State on attributes
nodes.rationale: A single data-state value cannot accumulate stale classes; styling aria-* keeps visual and announced state the same. Specificity stays 0,1,0.

nodes.label: Never style on data-testid
nodes.rationale: A test id must stay stable and meaningless; CSS on it makes renaming a visual regression.

nodes.label: :has() removes state hooks
nodes.rationale: body:has(dialog[open]) and .field:has(:user-invalid) delete the JS that used to sync a class.

nodes.label: js- prefix convention
nodes.rationale: js-submit is queried, never styled; btn--primary is styled, never queried.

nodes.label: Five selector families
nodes.rationale: Type, class, id, universal, attribute — each couples CSS to a different contract. Class is the default.

nodes.label: Avoid id selectors in CSS
nodes.rationale: 1,0,0 specificity, uniqueness that cannot style a component twice, and ids belong to fragments/ARIA.

nodes.label: Prose type-selector pattern
nodes.rationale: Scope type selectors under .prose for CMS/Markdown you cannot class; bare h2 leaks into components.

nodes.label: Selector case sensitivity
nodes.rationale: Types are case-insensitive in HTML; class/id are sensitive; attribute values need the i flag to ignore case.

nodes.label: @layer
nodes.rationale: Declare precedence once up front. Layers sit above specificity so a later-layer class beats an earlier-layer id.

nodes.label: CSS cascade layers
nodes.rationale: Native cascade control. Unlayered acts as an implicit final layer; !important inverts layer order.

nodes.label: Specificity triple (A,B,C)
nodes.rationale: A=ids, B=classes/attributes/pseudo-classes, C=types/pseudo-elements. * combinators and :where() add nothing.

nodes.label: Lexicographic specificity compare
nodes.rationale: Compare left to right; no carrying. #nav (1,0,0) beats thirteen classes. Not a base-10 number.

nodes.label: :is() :not() :has() specificity
nodes.rationale: They add no weight of their own; they take the most specific argument. One id in the list raises every match.

nodes.label: :where() zero specificity
nodes.rationale: Always 0,0,0 regardless of contents — the tool for overridable resets and library defaults.

nodes.label: Nesting & specificity
nodes.rationale: & behaves like :is(): a parent list containing an id raises every nested rule.

nodes.label: Flat specificity strategy
nodes.rationale: Do not fight: :where() for defaults, @layer for precedence, one class per component rule, never style by id.

nodes.label: Shorthand writes all longhands
nodes.rationale: A shorthand is a complete statement of a concept, not a patch. Omitted sub-values reset to initial, so they override earlier longhands you never named.

nodes.label: border resets border-image
nodes.rationale: border sets border-image to none even though the name does not imply it. Declare border first, then border-image.

nodes.label: font resets line-height
nodes.rationale: font resets line-height to normal unless the size/line-height form is used, collapsing vertical rhythm.

nodes.label: grid vs grid-template
nodes.rationale: grid resets implicit-grid longhands including grid-auto-flow; grid-template is the narrower shorthand.

nodes.label: Cascade sorting order
nodes.rationale: Origin+importance, context, inline styles, layers, specificity, appearance. First distinguishing criterion wins; the rest are never consulted.

nodes.label: Origin and importance ladder
nodes.rationale: Eight levels: transitions, important UA/user/author, animations, then normal author/user/UA. Important reverses origin order for accessibility.

nodes.label: Inline styles are criterion 3
nodes.rationale: Not 'specificity 1000'. A normal inline beats every normal author rule; it loses to author !important because importance already separated them.

nodes.label: Author cascade ladder
nodes.rationale: Weakest: normal first layer → later layers → unlayered → normal inline → animations → important unlayered → important later layers → important first layer → important inline.

nodes.label: Transitions vs animations
nodes.rationale: Transitions sit above everything. Animations sit below important author, so !important is how you defeat a @keyframes value.

nodes.label: @layer statement form
nodes.rationale: @layer reset, base, layout, components, utilities; writes no rules. First declared is weakest. Prevents first-block appearance from silently reordering.

nodes.label: @import layer()
nodes.rationale: Assign a whole vendor stylesheet to a named layer. @import must precede every rule except @charset and @layer statements.

nodes.label: Nested layers and dot notation
nodes.rationale: framework.layout is ordered only inside framework. A nested layer can never escape its parent's position.

nodes.label: Anonymous cascade layers
nodes.rationale: Unnamed @layer {} takes position from appearance and cannot be appended to. Prefer names.

nodes.label: Unlayered implicit final layer
nodes.rationale: Unlayered declarations behave as if they were in an implicit final layer. Last wins for normal, first wins for important — so unlayered wins all normal and loses all important.

nodes.label: !important inverts layer order
nodes.rationale: Foundational layers hold the most binding constraints. A utility layer must not !important past a reset or design-system invariant.

nodes.label: Swallow a vendor stylesheet
nodes.rationale: @import vendor into an early layer so a later one-class rule wins without !important. Vendor !important still beats you via inversion.

nodes.label: revert-layer
nodes.rationale: Rolls a property back to the previous layer in the same origin, not to initial or the previous origin (that is revert).

nodes.label: Recommended layer order
nodes.rationale: reset, vendor, base, layout, components, utilities — utilities always win with one class.

nodes.label: CSS rendering pipeline
nodes.rationale: style → layout → paint → composite. Every later performance rule is downstream of which stage a property invalidates.

nodes.label: CSS fails silently
nodes.rationale: Invalid declaration dropped alone; invalid selector discards the whole rule; unclosed brace eats the next. Nothing is reported.

nodes.label: :has() parent selector
nodes.rationale: Parent and previous-sibling selector that replaces whole categories of state-toggling JavaScript.

nodes.label: Phase 2 cascade gate
nodes.rationale: Design a layer order that imports third-party CSS and needs no !important.

nodes.label: Custom properties as component API
nodes.rationale: Inherited runtime values in the cascade, not compile-time variables. var(--x, fallback) lets consumers override without extra classes.

nodes.label: Flex automatic minimum size
nodes.rationale: A flex item will not shrink below min-content; min-width: 0 is the fix — the most common flexbox bug.

nodes.label: auto-fit + minmax() card grid
nodes.rationale: Responsive card grid with no media query; highest-leverage modern layout idiom.

nodes.label: minmax(0, 1fr) track fix
nodes.rationale: A 1fr track is minmax(auto, 1fr) and will not shrink below min-content. Same problem as flex min-width: 0.

nodes.label: Container queries
nodes.rationale: Most responsive behaviour should need no breakpoint; the component's own width is the correct input.

nodes.label: Stacking contexts
nodes.rationale: z-index, opacity<1, transform, filter, will-change, isolation, contain create contexts a child can never escape.

nodes.label: oklch() and color-mix()
nodes.rationale: Perceptual lightness plus mixing hover/active/disabled from one brand token.

nodes.label: Cheap to animate
nodes.rationale: Only transform and opacity are composite-only; width/height/top/margin force layout every frame.

nodes.label: SCSS practically
nodes.rationale: Teach Sass constructs that remain after native CSS took nesting, variables and colour.

nodes.label: @use and @forward
nodes.rationale: Module system that replaced @import: namespacing, as, with, private members.

nodes.label: Sass $var vs CSS custom properties
nodes.rationale: $size is compile-time (can drive @media); --size is inherited runtime (can be themed and set from script).

nodes.label: Express 5.x on Node 24
nodes.rationale: Target Express 5.2.1 / Node 24.19.0. Thin routing and middleware layer over node:http. 11 phases, 114 topics, 78 pages.

nodes.label: Express over node:http
nodes.rationale: Not a second language or full architecture — router + middleware on http.Server.

nodes.label: Express request lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Accept → middleware chain → handler → response (or error middleware). Lost if nobody calls next and nobody writes.

nodes.label: Express route ordering
nodes.rationale: Order is load-bearing. Static segments before params or /export becomes an id. Express will not warn.

nodes.label: Express 5 path-to-regexp
nodes.rationale: * and :id? throw on Express 5; path matching was rewritten vs 4.

nodes.label: Phase 10 — Testable app and ops boundary
createApp(deps) factory
nodes.rationale: Pure factory; no listen inside. Production listens only after deps are ready. Supertest covers happy + 403 without a real DB.

nodes.label: Middleware contract
nodes.rationale: (req, res, next) => void — continue, finish, or error. The whole framework is a stack.

nodes.label: next() semantics
nodes.rationale: next() vs next(err) vs hang vs double-send. Body parser early; error middleware last.

nodes.label: Body size limits
nodes.rationale: 413 too large is DoS control, not polish. Mount JSON parsing with a hard size limit.

nodes.label: express.json and urlencoded
nodes.rationale: Content-type gated parsers. Malformed bodies become 400 into error middleware.

nodes.label: Phase 6 — REST surface and API features
Phase 7 — Layering at the Express edge
Phase 8 — Validation and authorization at the edge
Liveness vs readiness probes
nodes.rationale: Liveness is cheap. Readiness checks pool/redis. Failing readiness stops new traffic; failing liveness restarts the process — conflating them causes restart storms.

nodes.label: App boot order
nodes.rationale: validate env → connect pool → createApp(deps) → server.listen → signal ready.

nodes.label: Request-id middleware
nodes.rationale: Generate or accept X-Request-Id, set on req, return on the response, continue with AsyncLocalStorage.

nodes.label: Accept inbound request ids
nodes.rationale: Accept inbound request ids for trace continuity across gateways and clients.

nodes.label: SIGTERM graceful shutdown
nodes.rationale: Keep server from listen. On SIGTERM: stop accepting, drain, close pools.

nodes.label: Close http.Server not Express app
nodes.rationale: Call close on the http.Server returned by listen, not the Express app.

nodes.label: app.js factory vs server.js listen
nodes.rationale: server.js listens; app.js exports the factory so tests can createApp without binding a port.

nodes.label: Supertest integration tests
nodes.rationale: Hit the real Express stack with mocked services. Do not mock Express itself.

nodes.label: Mock outbound dependencies
nodes.rationale: In route tests mock outbound dependencies (DB, mail), not req/res plumbing.

nodes.label: Built-in Express middleware
nodes.rationale: Express ships json, urlencoded, static, raw/text, and Router. Application settings are not middleware.

nodes.label: Third-party middleware checklist
nodes.rationale: Check Express 5 support, maintenance, mutation surface, and next(err) vs throw before installing.

nodes.label: Prefer thin middleware wrappers
nodes.rationale: Battle-tested packages hide CVEs you never researched, but every dependency is supply-chain surface. Prefer fewer, better mounts.

nodes.label: First registered middleware runs first
nodes.rationale: Express does not sort middleware by specificity. Registration order on app is absolute.

nodes.label: App then router then route middleware
nodes.rationale: Application middleware runs before router middleware for that mount. Route-level middleware runs only for that route.

nodes.label: Scope middleware off hot paths
nodes.rationale: Global middleware is easy and expensive — it runs for health checks and static. Scope auth and loggers to routers that need them.

nodes.label: Canonical Express middleware skeleton
nodes.rationale: disable x-powered-by, json parser, routes, 404, then four-arg error middleware. Keep one composition root.

nodes.label: Parsers early, errors last
nodes.rationale: Handlers read req.body so parsers must run first. Error middleware is skipped in the normal chain and must be last.

nodes.label: Four-argument error middleware
nodes.rationale: Error middleware must be (err, req, res, next) so Express can detect it. A three-arg 404 is not an error handler.

nodes.label: Middleware contract (req, res, next)
nodes.rationale: Middleware is (req, res, next) => void. Route handlers are middleware that matched a method and path.

nodes.label: Three legal middleware endings
nodes.rationale: Respond, next(), or next(err). Returning without one of those hangs the socket.

nodes.label: Middleware factory
nodes.rationale: A factory returns middleware. Configure once, reuse with different options — no module-level mutable globals.

nodes.label: Call the factory, do not mount it
nodes.rationale: app.use(requireHeader) passes the factory with the wrong arity. Mount requireHeader('x-api-key') so each instance closes over its options.

nodes.label: Safe req attachments
nodes.rationale: Attach requestId, ctx, user, validated on req. Prefer namespaced objects when many features share the request.

nodes.label: Do not clobber Express core properties
nodes.rationale: Do not overwrite req.url/method/headers or wrap res.end/json casually. Inject DB via factory deps, not req.

nodes.label: next() vs next(err)
nodes.rationale: next() continues the stack. next(err) jumps to error handlers. On Express 5, async throws are forwarded like next(err).

nodes.label: Hang: no next and no response
nodes.rationale: Neither response nor next means the request hangs until the client times out.

nodes.label: next() after a terminal response
nodes.rationale: Calling next after res.send lets a later layer write again and throw headers-already-sent. First body still wins.

nodes.label: Cookie read/write asymmetry
nodes.rationale: Writing cookies is built in via res.cookie. Reading them needs cookie-parser or a manual Cookie header parse.

nodes.label: cookie-parser
nodes.rationale: Mount cookieParser() for req.cookies; cookieParser('secret') fills req.signedCookies. Session middleware typically depends on it.

nodes.label: Signed cookies are not encryption
nodes.rationale: Signed cookies detect tampering; they are not encryption. Secrets still need HTTPS and careful res.cookie flags.

nodes.label: req.accepts / req.is / req.get
nodes.rationale: Small req helpers avoid reinventing Accept negotiation, Content-Type checks, and case-insensitive header reads.

nodes.label: express.json()
nodes.rationale: Populates req.body only when Content-Type is JSON it understands. Wrong type skips the parser; body stays undefined, not automatic 415.

nodes.label: express.urlencoded()
nodes.rationale: HTML form posts. extended:false uses querystring; true uses qs for nested objects. Mount only what clients send.

nodes.label: Content-Type gates parsers
nodes.rationale: Parsers skip bodies they do not claim. Per-route parsers avoid parsing huge bodies on routes that never need them.

nodes.label: entity.parse.failed 400
nodes.rationale: Bad JSON is a client error. Express surfaces status 400 and type entity.parse.failed.

nodes.label: Stable public parse-error envelope
nodes.rationale: Do not leak raw parser messages. Map to a stable code and log detail server-side with a request id.

nodes.label: Multer multipart uploads
nodes.rationale: multipart/form-data is not JSON. Use Multer 2.x on Express 5. Cap size, allow-list MIME, treat the file as untrusted.

nodes.label: Never trust upload Content-Type
nodes.rationale: Clients lie. Prefer file-signature checks; generate your own object keys. Large files belong in object storage, not the API container disk.

nodes.label: Express 5 query parser simple
nodes.rationale: Express 5 defaults query parser to simple. Nested bracket queries stay literal keys, not objects.

nodes.label: query parser extended
nodes.rationale: app.set('query parser', 'extended') restores qs nested objects. Nested parsing plus object merge historically enabled prototype-pollution payloads.

nodes.label: Prefer flat public query params
nodes.rationale: simple is the safer default. Never pass raw req.query into Mongo/SQL builders even if extended is on.

nodes.label: express.raw() for webhooks
nodes.rationale: JSON parsing destroys exact bytes. HMAC webhooks need express.raw so signatures verify over the original Buffer.

nodes.label: First body consumer wins the stream
nodes.rationale: Global express.json() before a route-level raw parser leaves the hook with an empty or re-serialized body. Mount raw on /webhooks/* first.

nodes.label: req anatomy
nodes.rationale: req is Node IncomingMessage plus Express fields. method, url, path, params, query, headers are routing-time; body/cookies/user need middleware.

nodes.label: req.body needs a parser
nodes.rationale: No parser → no body. No cookie-parser → no cookies object. Writing cookies still uses res.cookie.

nodes.label: req.originalUrl
nodes.rationale: Full original path including mount and query — useful behind routers.

nodes.label: Body size limit
nodes.rationale: Treat limit as a production control. Different routes can use different limits via route-level parsers.

nodes.label: 413 entity.too.large
nodes.rationale: Oversize bodies become 413 Payload Too Large with type entity.too.large. Map that in error middleware.

nodes.label: res.cookie
nodes.rationale: res.cookie is built in. Flags decide whether browser JS can read the cookie and when it is sent.

nodes.label: httpOnly, secure, SameSite cookie flags
nodes.rationale: httpOnly blocks document.cookie for session tokens. secure is HTTPS-only and required with SameSite=None. sameSite sets CSRF posture.

nodes.label: Headers already sent
nodes.rationale: The first write wins. A second res.json/send throws Cannot set headers after they are sent to the client.

nodes.label: res.headersSent guard
nodes.rationale: In error middleware: if (res.headersSent) return next(err). Typical causes are next() after res.json or fall-through return paths.

nodes.label: res terminal methods
nodes.rationale: Pick one terminal: status, json, send, end, or redirect. Mixing json then send is how headers-already-sent starts.

nodes.label: res.json vs res.send
nodes.rationale: json always serializes as JSON with the right Content-Type. send branches on type. Chain status before the body is written.

nodes.label: Response shapes
nodes.rationale: Pick envelope vs bare resource and keep it consistent. Mixing both is worse than either choice.

nodes.label: Bare resource response
nodes.rationale: Matches pure REST textbooks and OpenAPI components cleanly; no wrapper nesting.

nodes.label: Envelope response
nodes.rationale: Envelopes extend with pagination meta without breaking clients; they add nesting noise.

nodes.label: Stable error JSON shape
nodes.rationale: Clients parse one schema; you can add code without breaking UIs.

nodes.label: SPA fallback
nodes.rationale: Client-side routers need index.html on unknown paths. Register the catch-all after API routes.

nodes.label: Named splat {*splat}
nodes.rationale: On Express 5, app.get('*') throws at boot. Use a named splat.

nodes.label: API then static then splat
nodes.rationale: Catch-all before API makes /api/users return HTML. Correct order: API → static assets → HTML fallback.

nodes.label: Bare star path invalid on Express 5
nodes.rationale: Bare * path tokens are invalid; registration throws. 2020 MERN tutorials crash on Express 5.

nodes.label: express.static
nodes.rationale: Serves files from a directory. Put it after API routes if the same app also hosts a SPA.

nodes.label: Static cache headers
nodes.rationale: Long maxAge for hashed filenames; short/none for HTML. Fingerprinted assets can be immutable; HTML points at changing hashes.

nodes.label: Static root isolation
nodes.rationale: A static root too high exposes node_modules or .env. Root only the build output directory.

nodes.label: HTTP status as contract
nodes.rationale: Useful APIs pick 201/204/400/401/403/404/409 deliberately — not always 200. Rich codes help clients; over-fine codes confuse them.

nodes.label: Headers fixed once body starts
nodes.rationale: Cannot set a header after the body is already sent. Set headers first.

nodes.label: Always-200 RPC-over-HTTP
nodes.rationale: Always HTTP 200 with {success:false} is an RPC-over-HTTP habit. Use real statuses; keep error body for details.

nodes.label: 401 vs 403
nodes.rationale: 401 unauthenticated; 403 authenticated but not allowed.

nodes.label: res.download
nodes.rationale: Suggests a filename for the Save dialog; streams from disk.

nodes.label: File send path traversal
nodes.rationale: Always set root / resolve paths carefully. Prefer object-storage signed URLs when files are large or private.

nodes.label: compression middleware
nodes.rationale: Can help JSON APIs; many production stacks terminate gzip at Nginx. Do not double-compress.

nodes.label: Express 5 async rejection forwarding
nodes.rationale: Rejected promises from async handlers reach error middleware on Express 5. You do not need express-async-errors for that baseline.

nodes.label: try/catch domain mapping
nodes.rationale: Still use try/catch when you convert errors to domain responses inside the handler without wanting the global mapper.

nodes.label: Error response contract
nodes.rationale: One public JSON shape for errors. Include a stable code. Never send err.stack when NODE_ENV === production.

nodes.label: Hide stack in production
nodes.rationale: Stack traces and internal exception messages for unexpected 500s must never appear in production error JSON.

nodes.label: headersSent delegates to default handler
nodes.rationale: If res.headersSent, return next(err) instead of writing another body.

nodes.label: Four-arg error middleware
nodes.rationale: Express detects error middleware by arity. Mount it last. Omit next and errors vanish into the wrong path.

nodes.label: Express arity detection
nodes.rationale: Function length 4: (err, req, res, next).

nodes.label: HttpError
nodes.rationale: Carry statusCode and code on thrown errors. Map domain failures once in error middleware. Avoid deep inheritance trees.

nodes.label: 404 three-arg middleware
nodes.rationale: 404 is normal middleware (3 args) after routes, not error middleware. Always sends 404 when reached.

nodes.label: Process-level errors
nodes.rationale: unhandledRejection / uncaughtException are Node topics, not Express request envelopes.

nodes.label: Operational error
nodes.rationale: Expected at the edge (bad input, not found). Expose a clear message + code. Log it.

nodes.label: Programmer error
nodes.rationale: Bugs. Hide messages (they leak paths, schemas, exploit detail) and return a generic 500. Do not keep the process alive after unknown programmer errors.

nodes.label: ETag
nodes.rationale: Express can generate weak ETags. For APIs, explicit version fields or hashes are often clearer.

nodes.label: If-None-Match 304
nodes.rationale: 304 Not Modified when the client already has the current representation.

nodes.label: If-Match 412 lost update
nodes.rationale: If-Match: v2 → 412 if current is v3 (lost update).

nodes.label: API Cache-Control
nodes.rationale: Authenticated JSON is usually Cache-Control: private, no-store. Public catalogs may use public, max-age carefully.

nodes.label: Query field allow-list
nodes.rationale: Never pass raw req.query into Mongo or SQL builders. Allow-list prevents sorting on unindexed or sensitive columns and injection-style operators.

nodes.label: Mongo operator injection
nodes.rationale: ?filter[$gt]=… succeeds when query objects are merged blindly.

nodes.label: Idempotency-Key
nodes.rationale: Clients retry POSTs. Without a key you double-charge. POST and some PATCH need keys; GET/PUT are already idempotent when implemented correctly.

nodes.label: Idempotency replay store
nodes.rationale: Store key → response (status + body) under a TTL. Replay returns the same result without re-executing side effects.

nodes.label: Idempotency payload hash 409
nodes.rationale: Same key, different body is a client bug or attack. Reject with 409 if payload hash mismatches stored request.

nodes.label: OpenAPI contract
nodes.rationale: The contract is part of the product. Drift between OpenAPI and handlers is a bug. Swagger UI is optional sugar — the artifact is the spec.

nodes.label: Shared OpenAPI Zod schemas
nodes.rationale: Use the same schemas as Zod when possible to avoid double sources of truth.

nodes.label: Offset pagination
nodes.rationale: Easy, slow on deep pages, unstable if rows insert while paging.

nodes.label: Cursor pagination
nodes.rationale: Stable for infinite scroll; opaque cursors hide storage details. Encode nothing sensitive without signing/encrypting.

nodes.label: Pagination limit cap
nodes.rationale: Always cap limit. Default e.g. 20 and max e.g. 100. Never allow limit=999999. Protects DB and API CPU.

nodes.label: REST resource modeling
nodes.rationale: Resources are nouns. Prefer /orders/12/items over /getOrderItems. Deep hierarchies complicate authorization and caching.

nodes.label: RPC-style action route
nodes.rationale: RPC-style routes are fine when the domain is an action, not a thing — name them honestly instead of inventing fake nouns.

nodes.label: Static segments before :id
nodes.rationale: /users/export captured by :id unless static segments are registered first.

nodes.label: 201 plus Location
nodes.rationale: Signals a new resource; pairs with Location when useful.

nodes.label: DELETE 204 vs 200
nodes.rationale: 204 if no body; 200 if you return the deleted representation — pick one style.

nodes.label: URL prefix versioning
nodes.rationale: Clearest default for this stack. Visible, cache-friendly, easy routers. Most common style for REST JSON APIs.

nodes.label: Header versioning
nodes.rationale: Cleaner URLs, harder to explore.

nodes.label: Media type versioning
nodes.rationale: Accept: application/vnd.app.v1+json is strict and heavy.

nodes.label: Sunset deprecation headers
nodes.rationale: Deprecate with docs + sunset headers; do not break v1 silently.

nodes.label: Inbound webhook verification
nodes.rationale: raw body + signature + timestamp skew. Persist event id for dedupe. Enqueue work; respond quickly.

nodes.label: express.raw for webhook signature
nodes.rationale: Signature is over exact bytes, not re-serialized JSON.

nodes.label: Outbound webhook 202 enqueue
nodes.rationale: Fire-and-forget from the route is a bug under load. Express only accepts the command and returns 202.

nodes.label: Controller layer
nodes.rationale: Parse/validate input already on req, call service, map status. Does not own SQL or business rules.

nodes.label: Service layer
nodes.rationale: Owns invariants and orchestration. No res.json, no Express types.

nodes.label: Repository layer
nodes.rationale: Queries/commands via drivers. Does not decide HTTP status. Driver types do not leak upward.

nodes.label: Keep Express types out of services
nodes.rationale: Services stay testable without spinning an HTTP server. Express owns where the HTTP layer stops.

nodes.label: Router factory DI
nodes.rationale: Pass dependencies into router factories. Do not import a global db singleton from every file if you care about tests.

nodes.label: createApp(deps)
nodes.rationale: Phase 10 completes composition with createApp(deps). Tests substitute fakes; boot order stays explicit.

nodes.label: Domain vs transport
nodes.rationale: Transport is HTTP; domain is product language. Crossing them freely couples tests to Express.

nodes.label: DTO at the edge
nodes.rationale: Map to a DTO at the HTTP edge so API shapes stay stable when persistence models change.

nodes.label: Fat controllers
nodes.rationale: If a handler needs scrolling, logic leaked upward. Smells: SQL in the route, 200-line try/catch, copy-pasted auth.

nodes.label: Thin handler pipeline
nodes.rationale: Auth middleware then validate middleware then thin handler then service; one use-case per handler.

nodes.label: Feature folders
nodes.rationale: orders/routes.ts with orders/service.ts; scales by domain.

nodes.label: Layer folders
nodes.rationale: routes/, services/, repos/; scales by role.

nodes.label: DTO mapping at the edge
nodes.rationale: Map API DTOs at the edge; pick feature or layer folders and stay consistent.

nodes.label: Transaction-per-request middleware
nodes.rationale: Thin wrapper only; transaction mechanism stays in Node Phase 6.

nodes.label: Background jobs from routes
nodes.rationale: Validate, persist, enqueue, respond. Never await email, webhooks, or PDF generation on the request path.

nodes.label: HTTP 202 Accepted
nodes.rationale: 202 means accepted for processing, not necessarily completed.

nodes.label: Transactional outbox
nodes.rationale: Persist in a transaction with an outbox when needed; Node Phase 7 owns retries and worker shutdown.

nodes.label: requireAuth
nodes.rationale: Parse session or Bearer JWT, attach req.user, else 401. Do not re-teach argon2 or JWT structure.

nodes.label: req.user
nodes.rationale: Authn middleware puts the authenticated principal on req, not permissions alone.

nodes.label: Query string coercion
nodes.rationale: Query and params are strings. z.number() without coerce fails; use z.coerce.number() deliberately.

nodes.label: Boolean false query trap
nodes.rationale: ?active=false is the string "false", which is truthy. Use explicit enums or coerce helpers.

nodes.label: cookie-parser
nodes.rationale: Mount cookie-parser before session so session libraries read cookies from the parsed object.

nodes.label: Cookie flags
nodes.rationale: res.cookie flags: httpOnly, secure, sameSite. Session vs JWT choice is Node Phase 8.

nodes.label: connect-redis session store
nodes.rationale: Session store is integration only; Redis syllabus owns Redis.

nodes.label: Resource ownership
nodes.rationale: Load the resource and compare owner id to req.user.id; else 404 or 403 by policy.

nodes.label: Ownership 404 vs 403
nodes.rationale: Prefer 404 when existence should stay secret; 403 when the resource is visible but forbidden. 404 avoids leaking that the id exists.

nodes.label: requireRole
nodes.rationale: Role checks after authentication. Fail closed with 403, not 401.

nodes.label: 401 vs 403 after role check
nodes.rationale: 403 when identity is known; 401 when missing.

nodes.label: Tenant from identity
nodes.rationale: Force tenantId from identity, never from raw body alone.

nodes.label: Tenant hopping / IDOR
nodes.rationale: Trusting a client-supplied tenantId enables tenant hopping / IDOR.

nodes.label: Optional auth middleware
nodes.rationale: Enriches req.user when a token is present but does not 401 when absent; for public+personalized routes.

nodes.label: Logout and revocation
nodes.rationale: Logout clears cookies / hits revocation; storage is Node/Redis.

nodes.label: Validate at the HTTP boundary
nodes.rationale: Everything from the network is untrusted. Services receive validated data, not req.body. DB-only validation is late, worse errors, and injection risk.

nodes.label: Validation middleware factory
nodes.rationale: validate({body, params, query}) returns middleware. Failure: 400 with stable codes. Success: attach parsed data.

nodes.label: req.validated
nodes.rationale: Put parsed result on req under a clear name — not mixed with raw body.

nodes.label: CORS in Express
nodes.rationale: Browsers enforce CORS, not servers alone. Dynamic origin reflection must allow-list.

nodes.label: CORS credentials vs wildcard
nodes.rationale: Credentials plus wildcard origins do not mix. Browsers forbid Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * with cookies.

nodes.label: CSRF for cookie APIs
nodes.rationale: CSRF matters when auth relies on cookies automatically sent cross-site. Bearer Authorization usually does not.

nodes.label: csurf archived
nodes.rationale: csurf is archived — do not teach it as current. Prefer double-submit cookie, SameSite, framework guidance.

nodes.label: Open redirect
nodes.rationale: Never res.redirect(userInput) unchecked. Allow-list relative paths.

nodes.label: Helmet
nodes.rationale: Helmet mounts secure default headers. It is not a full security program and does not replace auth or injection defenses.

nodes.label: Content-Security-Policy
nodes.rationale: CSP matters more for HTML apps than pure JSON APIs. APIs may disable noisy browser-only policies after review.

nodes.label: express-rate-limit
nodes.rationale: Limit by IP or user. Skip liveness probes. Keys must use the real client IP via trust proxy.

nodes.label: Login rate limits
nodes.rationale: Brute-force protection on /login is tighter than global API limits and sits on the auth routes.

nodes.label: trust proxy
nodes.rationale: app.set('trust proxy', 1) for one hop you control. Never set true on an open internet edge without understanding spoofed X-Forwarded-For.

nodes.label: req.ip behind proxy
nodes.rationale: Without trust proxy, req.ip is the load balancer so rate limits ban everyone as one IP and secure cookies misbehave.

nodes.label: Part 3 — API product
nodes.rationale: Phases 6–7: REST surface clients depend on, then Express-side controller/service/repository wiring only.

nodes.label: Phase 7 — Layering at the Express edge
nodes.rationale: Folders and function boundaries so routes stay thin. Deliverable: handlers under ~20 lines, services unit-testable without req/res.

nodes.label: Idempotency keys
nodes.rationale: Idempotency-Key header, store outcome, replay safe responses for unsafe requests.

nodes.label: Part 4 — Edge correctness & ops
nodes.rationale: Phases 8–10: parse input, attach identity, enforce access, harden headers, compose a testable app.

nodes.label: Express vs Node boundary rule
nodes.rationale: Hashing, JWT structure, Helmet ideas, Zod-as-library stay in Node. Express owns the middleware that validates, authenticates, authorizes, sets cookies, and mounts Helmet/CORS/rate-limit.

nodes.label: createApp(deps)
nodes.rationale: Pure function returns app; no listen inside; inject db/redis/queue clients. Production entrypoint only listens after deps are ready.

nodes.label: Part 1 — Foundations
nodes.rationale: Express is a routing and middleware layer on top of http.Server, not a replacement for Node.

nodes.label: Express over node:http
nodes.rationale: Express is router + middleware over node:http, not a language and not an application architecture.

nodes.label: Phase 1 — Routing and path matching
nodes.rationale: Order is load-bearing; Express will not warn you. A catch-all registered too early steals traffic.

nodes.label: Phase 2 — Middleware architecture
nodes.rationale: The whole framework is a stack of functions. Order, next, and termination are the job.

nodes.label: Middleware contract
nodes.rationale: (req, res, next) => void. next() vs next(err) vs never calling next: hang, double-send, silent drop.

nodes.label: Part 2 — HTTP surface
nodes.rationale: How Express packages Node streams and http.Server into req/res and a single error channel.

nodes.label: Phase 5 — Error handling
nodes.rationale: Four-argument error middleware last. Express 5 forwards rejected promises to next(err).

nodes.label: Body parsers
nodes.rationale: express.json() and express.urlencoded() with content-type gates, empty-body behaviour, and size limits as DoS control.

nodes.label: Error response contract
nodes.rationale: Stable JSON error body (code, message, details), no stack in production.

nodes.label: Phase 0 — How Git stores things
nodes.rationale: Only completed Git phase: 14 topics / 14 pages.

nodes.label: sandbox/git-p0
nodes.rationale: Command blocks come from sandbox/git-* scripts run in a throwaway repo with neutralized global config.

nodes.label: Never invent output
nodes.rationale: git-filter-repo and git-lfs are not installed. Those pages will be measured after install or cite upstream docs — the never-invent-output rule does not bend.

nodes.label: Phase 0 — How Git stores things
nodes.rationale: No workflow yet. What is on disk, what a commit physically is, and why later commands behave as they do. reset --soft vs --hard, rebase hashes, and deleted-branch recovery are consequences of the storage model.

nodes.label: git init still creates master on 2.55.0
nodes.rationale: The hint says the default changes in Git 3.0. 'Git defaults to main now' is false on this build.

nodes.label: A branch is 41 bytes and zero new objects
nodes.rationale: Measured with wc -c and an unchanged object count — the concrete reason branching is free.

nodes.label: Object name is reproducible without Git
nodes.rationale: printf 'blob 6\0hello\n' | sha1sum matches git hash-object. The filename is not part of the hash.

nodes.label: Content-addressed object store
nodes.rationale: Git is a key-value store keyed by the SHA of the content, plus names pointing into it. Deduplication is unavoidable once the name is the hash.

nodes.label: Hash is over type size NUL content
nodes.rationale: blob 6\0hello\n hashed with sha1sum reproduces ce013625… with no Git involved.

nodes.label: hash-object without -w only computes a name
nodes.rationale: Computing a name is not storing it. cat-file fails until hash-object -w writes the object.

nodes.label: History is immutable and cumulative
nodes.rationale: Reachable objects are never collected. A committed secret or binary is an incident; deleting the file later does not remove the blob.

nodes.label: A commit is a snapshot, not a diff
nodes.rationale: The model is snapshots; the storage uses deltas. Confusing the two makes packfiles sound like they contradict the snapshot claim.

nodes.label: Commit object contents
nodes.rationale: One tree, zero or more parents, author, committer, message. No file contents and no diff.

nodes.label: Unchanged files reuse existing blobs
nodes.rationale: Change one file in 10 000: one new blob, one new tree per directory on the path, one commit. Every other entry is a pointer.

nodes.label: Diffs are derived output
nodes.rationale: Git never recorded what you did, only what things became. A rename is inferred; git diff output depends on myers, histogram, or patience.

nodes.label: Blob
nodes.rationale: File bytes only. No name, path, mode, or timestamp. Filename lives in the tree that points at the blob.

nodes.label: Tree
nodes.rationale: Sorted directory listing of mode, type, hash, name. Empty directories cannot be committed because there are no entries to store.

nodes.label: Commit object
nodes.rationale: One tree, parents, author, committer, message. Author and committer diverge on rebase, cherry-pick, and apply.

nodes.label: Annotated tag
nodes.rationale: A real object with tagger, date, message, optional signature. Releases should use git tag -a.

nodes.label: Lightweight tag
nodes.rationale: Only a file in refs/tags/ containing a hash. Creates no object; git describe ignores it unless --tags.

nodes.label: Tree entry modes
nodes.rationale: 100644 regular, 100755 executable, 120000 symlink, 040000 directory, 160000 gitlink. No owner, group, or timestamps.

nodes.label: The three trees
nodes.rationale: HEAD, index, working tree. Every core command is a move between two of them.

nodes.label: HEAD snapshot
nodes.rationale: The snapshot of the last commit on the current branch, reached via .git/HEAD.

nodes.label: Working tree
nodes.rationale: Actual files on disk, editable by anything, tracked or not.

nodes.label: AM status code
nodes.rationale: Left column is index versus HEAD; right is working tree versus index. AM means staged and then edited; commit records the older content.

nodes.label: reset --soft --mixed --hard
nodes.rationale: All move HEAD. --mixed also resets the index. --hard also overwrites the working tree and is the only variant that can lose uncommitted work.

nodes.label: The index is a real file
nodes.rationale: .git/index is a binary file of paths with blob hashes and cached stat data. git add writes content into the object store first.

nodes.label: Staging is a copy, not a bookmark
nodes.rationale: The index recorded a hash, so later edits cannot change what is staged. Enables git add -p and recovery of staged-but-uncommitted blobs via fsck --lost-found.

nodes.label: Merge stage numbers
nodes.rationale: Stage 0 normally. During conflict: 1 base, 2 ours, 3 theirs. UU in status means stages 1/2/3 and no stage 0.

nodes.label: Cached stat data
nodes.rationale: git status skips re-hashing if size and mtime match. Network or Windows shares that lie about modes make everything look modified.

nodes.label: Ref
nodes.rationale: A file containing a hash. refs/heads/* move on commit; refs/tags/* never move; refs/remotes/* move on fetch.

nodes.label: HEAD is a symbolic ref
nodes.rationale: Usually contains ref: refs/heads/<branch>. git rev-parse follows HEAD → branch file → commit.

nodes.label: Detached HEAD
nodes.rationale: HEAD holds a raw hash. New commits advance HEAD only. Switching away abandons them unless you branch first.

nodes.label: reftable backend
nodes.rationale: Opt-in at git init --ref-format=reftable. Default is files plus packed-refs. cat .git/refs/heads/main can fail; rev-parse always works.

nodes.label: Commit graph is a DAG
nodes.rationale: Parents point backwards. Directed because pointers go one way; acyclic because a commit hash includes its parents; a graph because merges have multiple parents.

nodes.label: Dates are metadata, not structure
nodes.rationale: A commit dated 2030 can sit beneath one dated 2026. Never build logic on commit dates; use merge-base --is-ancestor.

nodes.label: Reachability
nodes.rationale: rev-list is the engine under log, fetch negotiation, and gc. main..mybranch means reachable from mybranch, not from main.

nodes.label: Merge commit second parent
nodes.rationale: Second parent is the branch merged in; first parent is the branch you were on. --first-parent reads the trunk.

nodes.label: Config layers and precedence
nodes.rationale: system → global → local → worktree → -c. Last one to set a key wins. --show-origin --show-scope names the file that won.

nodes.label: Unset does not mean unused
nodes.rationale: Built-in defaults still apply. Unset init.defaultBranch is master on 2.55.0; unset pull.rebase makes a divergent pull fail.

nodes.label: includeIf gitdir identity switch
nodes.rationale: includeIf gitdir:~/work/ points at a second file that sets user.email, so work and personal identities switch by directory.

nodes.label: .git/ directory
nodes.rationale: The whole repository is one directory. Delete it and you have ordinary files; copy it and you copied history. One rm -rf .git is irreversible.

nodes.label: Reflog
nodes.rationale: logs/ records every ref movement. Local, not pushed, expires 90/30 days. Enabled by logallrefupdates = true.

nodes.label: hooks/ is not tracked
nodes.rationale: Sample scripts ship with .sample suffix. Teams need core.hooksPath or husky to share hooks.

nodes.label: Bare repository
nodes.rationale: No working tree; .git contents sit at the top level. What a server hosts.

nodes.label: Author identity required to commit
nodes.rationale: Author and committer are fields inside the commit object. Without them there is nothing to hash. Hard failure, not a warning.

nodes.label: Identity is asserted, not authenticated
nodes.rationale: user.email is free text. Audit value comes from host push authentication; cryptographic proof needs signed commits.

nodes.label: Author versus committer
nodes.rationale: Author wrote the change; committer created this commit object. Rebase and cherry-pick preserve author.

nodes.label: Loose objects
nodes.rationale: One zlib-compressed file per object, written on commit. Path is first two hash characters plus the rest.

nodes.label: Packfile
nodes.rationale: .pack holds delta-compressed objects; .idx is hash→offset; .rev is reverse index. Measured 51 objects 204K packed to 6.03 KiB.

nodes.label: Cruft pack
nodes.rationale: Unreachable objects held with .mtimes for a two-week grace period. Why gc does not shrink a rewritten repo immediately.

nodes.label: Delta compression is below the model
nodes.rationale: cat-file still returns whole objects. Hashes are over content, never stored form. Deltas are chosen by similarity, not commit adjacency.

nodes.label: Compressed binaries do not delta
nodes.rationale: JPEGs, zips, and compiled artefacts neither delta nor compress. Each version is stored near full size forever.

nodes.label: Git is not a backup
nodes.rationale: Git versions what you committed and by default lives on one machine. Uncommitted and ignored files are outside it.

nodes.label: Git is not a deployment tool
nodes.rationale: git pull on a server leaves .git on the host, no atomic switch, no rollback, no build step.

nodes.label: Git is not a place for secrets
nodes.rationale: Deleting a credential in a later commit removes nothing. Rotate first, then rewrite, then force-push.

nodes.label: Git is not a large-file store
nodes.rationale: Already-compressed binaries get almost none of packfile savings. git-lfs is not installed on this machine.

nodes.label: SHA-1 default object format
nodes.rationale: Fresh repos use sha1. 40 hex characters. No sign of the default changing soon.

nodes.label: SHA-256 object format
nodes.rationale: Chosen at init with --object-format=sha256. 64 hex characters. No in-place conversion.

nodes.label: Hardened SHA-1 sha1dc
nodes.rationale: Git 2.13+ detects known collision attack patterns and aborts rather than writing the object.

nodes.label: SHA-1 and SHA-256 cannot interoperate
nodes.rationale: Object names are the protocol vocabulary. Hosts, tooling, and remotes assume SHA-1, so SHA-256 adoption is blocked.

nodes.label: Porcelain
nodes.rationale: Human-facing commands whose output may change. 46 main porcelain commands of 172 on PATH.

nodes.label: Plumbing
nodes.rationale: Stable machine-readable layer for scripts: rev-parse, cat-file, hash-object, commit-tree, update-ref.

nodes.label: Commit by hand with plumbing
nodes.rationale: hash-object -w, mktree, commit-tree, update-ref. Omitting update-ref leaves a valid commit reachable from no branch.

nodes.label: Part 1 — How Git works
nodes.rationale: Phases 0–3 · 61 topics · 27 Master. Storage model, daily loop, branching, reading history. Works with no network.

nodes.label: Phase 1 — The everyday loop
nodes.rationale: status, add -p, commit, the three diffs, gitignore, switch/restore, undo before push.

nodes.label: Phase 2 — Branching, merging and rebasing
nodes.rationale: A branch is a file with a hash; merging is three-input; rebasing replays patches and changes hashes.

nodes.label: Phase 3 — Reading history
nodes.rationale: Revision syntax, ranges, bisect, pickaxe, blame, show.

nodes.label: Part 2 — Working with other people
nodes.rationale: Phases 4–6 · 47 topics · 15 Master. Exists because someone else has commits you do not.

nodes.label: Phase 4 — Remotes and syncing
nodes.rationale: origin is a named URL; fetch vs pull; divergence refuses to guess; --force-with-lease and --force-if-includes.

nodes.label: Phase 5 — Undo, recover and rewrite
nodes.rationale: Framing question: has anyone else seen these commits? reset vs revert vs reflog.

nodes.label: Phase 6 — Team workflow and code review
nodes.rationale: None of this is enforced by Git. Merge, squash, or rebase-merge is a one-time team decision.

nodes.label: Part 3 — Git in a real project
nodes.rationale: Phases 7–9 · 42 topics · 7 Master. Assumes node_modules, lockfile, .env, migrations, and a front end plus API.

nodes.label: Phase 7 — The repository in a fullstack project
nodes.rationale: gitignore for Node/React, secrets never enter, lockfiles always committed, migrations are append-only.

nodes.label: Phase 8 — Hooks, CI and automation
nodes.rationale: Hooks are skippable with --no-verify. Anything that must hold is re-checked server-side.

nodes.label: Phase 9 — Speed, scale and daily ergonomics
nodes.rationale: Clone strategy for CI, deliberate global config, maintenance, auditing history size.

nodes.label: Part 4 — Depth and repair
nodes.rationale: Phases 10–12 · 41 topics · 6 Master. Plumbing, repository-scale rewrite, error-message catalogue.

nodes.label: Phase 10 — Plumbing and internals
nodes.rationale: Phase 0 proved by hand. hash-object, cat-file, write-tree, commit-tree, rev-list, packfiles, reftable.

nodes.label: Phase 11 — History surgery and migration
nodes.rationale: Every topic changes every hash after the point it touches. git-filter-repo is not installed on this machine.

nodes.label: Phase 12 — When Git goes wrong
nodes.rationale: Symptom → cause → fix catalogue. Diagnostic index to the rest of the bible.

nodes.label: JavaScript explanations
nodes.rationale: 76 of 337 topics written. Phases 0–2 complete; Master tiers in progress through Phase 7. Claimed by session 01ECVvH5.

nodes.label: 300-line cap is a file-size rule
nodes.rationale: A Master topic may run 900–1400 lines across chunks. Write first, then split. Never trim a gotcha to save lines.

nodes.label: Measured versus documentation-validated
nodes.rationale: Phases 0–2 and Phase 3 topics 01–07 are sandbox-measured on Node 24.19.0. Later pages cite MDN and the spec. No run means no console block.

nodes.label: Phase 0 — How JavaScript runs
nodes.rationale: The engine reads the whole file before it runs any of it. Twelve topics from engine/runtime/spec through reading the spec.

nodes.label: Engine reads the whole file before running
nodes.rationale: Why a SyntaxError on line 90 stops line 1, and why hoisting is a consequence rather than a rule.

nodes.label: Engine, runtime, and spec
nodes.rationale: Why document is not JavaScript, and what actually is.

nodes.label: Call stack
nodes.rationale: Execution contexts and the 12 524-frame ceiling. One half of the event loop; queues are the other half.

nodes.label: Strict mode
nodes.rationale: Six silent failures turned into errors.

nodes.label: Phase 1 — Values, types and coercion
nodes.rationale: Seventeen topics. References vs copies, coercion, and floating point account for a disproportionate share of shipped bugs.

nodes.label: The eight types
nodes.rationale: typeof for every value, and the null bug.

nodes.label: Primitives are copied, objects are shared
nodes.rationale: Why a value changed. Prerequisite for React immutable state updates.

nodes.label: == versus ===
nodes.rationale: null >= 0 is true but null > 0 is false — relational and equality coerce null differently.

nodes.label: Numbers are doubles
nodes.rationale: (1.005).toFixed(2) is "1.00", not "1.01". Cart totals should not be stored as 19.99.

nodes.label: Type coercion
nodes.rationale: [] + {} explained once. sort default string comparison and JSON.stringify omissions are coercion in disguise.

nodes.label: Strings are UTF-16
nodes.rationale: A three-person family emoji has .length 8, spreads to 5, and is 1 grapheme.

nodes.label: Phase 2 Operators, expressions and control flow
nodes.rationale: Fifteen high-frequency operator and control-flow topics. Invisible-on-review bugs are precedence (?? with ||, right-associative **) and ASI.

nodes.label: Remainder vs modulo
nodes.rationale: % is remainder and takes the sign of the dividend: -7 % 3 is -1, not 2. Real modulo is ((a % b) + b) % b.

nodes.label: Right-associative **
nodes.rationale: 2 ** 3 ** 2 is 512, not 64. ** is the only right-associative arithmetic operator. -2 ** 2 is a SyntaxError.

nodes.label: Optional chaining does not protect non-functions
nodes.rationale: nf.notAFunction?.() still throws TypeError. ?.() only guards null/undefined.

nodes.label: ~~ 32-bit wrap
nodes.rationale: ~~1e10 is 1410065408. The fast-truncate trick wraps at 32 bits; Math.trunc gives 10000000000.

nodes.label: for...in walks the prototype chain
