nodes.rationale: for...in walks the prototype chain and yields string indices on arrays.

nodes.label: Automatic semicolon insertion
nodes.rationale: Five dangerous line starts break a file that omits semicolons. Phase gate requires the exact rules, not folklore.

nodes.label: ?? mixed with || is a SyntaxError
nodes.rationale: a ?? b || c is a SyntaxError. Precedence of ?? with || is one of the five operators that actually bite.

nodes.label: Phase 3 Functions, scope and closures
nodes.rationale: this, closures and the scope chain are the three mechanisms every later phase assumes and interviews probe.

nodes.label: Closures
nodes.rationale: Closures are what make callbacks and promises hold state.

nodes.label: Lexical scope and the scope chain
Hoisting and the temporal dead zone
Master-first across all phases
nodes.rationale: Understand and Know tiers are deferred until every phase's Master topics are written. Next unit after 01-08 is Phase 4, not topic 09.

nodes.label: Phase 4 Objects, prototypes and classes
nodes.rationale: Everything non-primitive. Prototype rows make class stop being magic; copying is four operations with four failure modes.

nodes.label: The prototype chain
nodes.rationale: Phase gate: draw the prototype chain for a subclass instance and explain what super.method() looks up.

nodes.label: class desugaring
nodes.rationale: class is not magic; it desugars onto the prototype chain.

nodes.label: Shallow vs deep copy
nodes.rationale: Copying an object is four different operations with four different failure modes. structuredClone belongs here, not in Phase 5.

nodes.label: Documentation-validated pages
nodes.rationale: No new measurement sandboxes. No run means no console block. Verified lines name MDN and spec sections.

nodes.label: Phase 5 The built-in library
nodes.rationale: 26 topics grouped by object, not method. Grouping reduces noise, never coverage.

nodes.label: Phase 6 Iteration, destructuring and generators
nodes.rationale: The protocol layer. Small phase that lets for...of, spread, destructuring and Promise.all work on the same objects.

nodes.label: The iteration protocols
nodes.rationale: Symbol.iterator is a well-known-symbol-keyed method. Phase gate: write a generator that yields pages and consume it with for await...of.

nodes.label: Phase 7 Asynchronous JavaScript
nodes.rationale: Centre of gravity of the syllabus. If you only finish one phase to Master depth, finish this one. Eleven Master topics; 06 of 11 done.

nodes.label: Microtasks vs macrotasks
nodes.rationale: Assert only what Node and the browser agree on: microtasks drain before tasks. Name the runtime for anything narrower.

nodes.label: No run means no console block
nodes.rationale: Ordering claims are held to documentation. No page prints an interleaving nobody produced.

nodes.label: Spec, engine and host
nodes.rationale: ECMA-262 has no I/O. A language feature works wherever the engine is new enough; a host feature works only where that host provides it.

nodes.label: V8
nodes.rationale: Ships in Chrome, Edge, Node, Deno, Electron. Semantics match other engines; performance and feature timing do not.

nodes.label: JavaScriptCore
nodes.rationale: Safari and Bun. Broken in Safari almost always means JSC lacks a feature V8 shipped first.

nodes.label: globalThis
nodes.rationale: One spec name for the global object: window, self, or global. Measured globalThis === global on Node 24.

nodes.label: fetch is a host API
nodes.rationale: Not in ECMA-262. Node 18 shipped it via undici for portability. An older Node lacking it is a host-version problem.

nodes.label: setTimeout is a host API
nodes.rationale: Not in ECMA-262. HTML spec in browsers, separately by Node. A bare engine has no timers.

nodes.label: navigator exists on Node 21+
nodes.rationale: typeof navigator !== 'undefined' is true on Node 24. It never tested for a browser, only a name.

nodes.label: Parse, compile, execute
nodes.rationale: The engine reads the entire file before running a line. SyntaxError happens before any code runs; ReferenceError happens during execute.

nodes.label: Hoisting as the creation pass
nodes.rationale: Not code moving. Pass 2 registers declarations: functions fully built, var as undefined, let/const/class with no value.

nodes.label: Temporal dead zone
nodes.rationale: The binding exists but has no value. typeof on a TDZ name throws; typeof on a never-declared name is undefined. TDZ turns silent NaN into an immediate ReferenceError.

nodes.label: Execution context and the call stack
nodes.rationale: One thread, one stack. A frame holds arguments, locals, the defining scope, this, and the return address.

nodes.label: Stack limit is bytes, not calls
nodes.rationale: Measured 12524 frames with no locals versus 5442 with six args plus an array local. Never treat about 10000 calls as a budget.

nodes.label: V8 does not implement tail-call optimisation
nodes.rationale: TCO is in ES2015; only JavaScriptCore ships it. Writing recursion in tail position buys nothing in Chrome or Node.

nodes.label: await does not consume stack
nodes.rationale: 200000-deep async recursion succeeded. Every await returns to the event loop; the continuation is a microtask on a fresh stack.

nodes.label: Error.stackTraceLimit default 10
nodes.rationale: V8 truncates at ten frames by default. Raise to 50 or Infinity while debugging; capturing stacks is not free.

nodes.label: Strict mode
nodes.rationale: ES modules and class bodies are always strict. Know sloppy mode to recognise old files, not to opt in.

nodes.label: Strict mode turns silent failures into errors
nodes.rationale: Undeclared assignment throws, frozen writes throw, this in a plain call is undefined, duplicate params and octals are SyntaxErrors.

nodes.label: Detached method this is undefined
nodes.rationale: In a class body, a detached method throws immediately. In sloppy mode this is globalThis and the bug becomes a silent leak.

nodes.label: Top-level this differs by host
nodes.rationale: undefined in ESM, module.exports in CJS, window in a classic script. Use globalThis for the global object.

nodes.label: ECMAScript vs JavaScript
nodes.rationale: ECMAScript is ECMA-262 by TC39. JavaScript is the language plus host APIs. Names differ mostly for trademark reasons.

nodes.label: TC39 stage process
nodes.rationale: Stage 3 is where engines ship and risk lives. Stage 4 is two implementations plus tests. Never build on Stage 2 or below.

nodes.label: Engines implement proposals, not editions
nodes.rationale: Since ES2016 one small June edition snapshots Stage 4. Supported in Safari 16.4+ is useful; supported in ES2022 is not.

nodes.label: Temporal Stage 3
nodes.rationale: Measured absent on Node 24.19.0. Right long-term Date replacement; wrong to ship today. Tiered Know.

nodes.label: Four JavaScript hosts
nodes.rationale: Browser main thread, Web Worker, Node, and edge runtimes offer different globals. Workers have no DOM, window, or localStorage.

nodes.label: Shared web-platform surface
nodes.rationale: fetch, URL, AbortController, structuredClone, Intl, crypto, TextEncoder work in browser, worker, Node 24 and edge. Shared modules must stay on this list.

nodes.label: CJS bindings are not globals
nodes.rationale: require, __dirname and module are absent in ESM. Use import.meta.dirname, import.meta.filename and import.

nodes.label: defer vs async vs type=module
nodes.rationale: defer waits for parse and keeps document order. async runs on arrival with no order. type=module is deferred automatically because the import graph must be fetched first.

nodes.label: Native ESM request waterfall
nodes.rationale: The graph is discovered one level at a time. modulepreload or bundling is why bundlers remain standard despite universal ESM.

nodes.label: nomodule two-bundle pattern
nodes.rationale: Module-aware browsers ignore nomodule; older ones ignore type=module. Largely historical in 2026.

nodes.label: Test the capability, not the environment
nodes.rationale: Every user-agent check eventually misidentifies something. Ask for the capability with a real operation.

nodes.label: Safari private mode localStorage probe
nodes.rationale: Safari private browsing defines localStorage then throws QuotaExceededError on write. Probe with a real setItem.

nodes.label: Progressive enhancement
nodes.rationale: Ship a version that works everywhere, then add capability-gated improvements. Infinite scroll or a Load more button; both load products.

nodes.label: Transpiler vs polyfill
nodes.rationale: A transpiler rewrites syntax at build time. A polyfill adds a missing API at runtime. Neither substitutes for the other.

nodes.label: Ponyfill
nodes.rationale: Exports the implementation instead of patching the global. Prefer in libraries. Global polyfills only in an application entry point.

nodes.label: Unpolyfillable engine features
nodes.rationale: Proxy, WeakRef, BigInt and real #private fields cannot be reconstructed in JavaScript. Raise the floor or design around them.

nodes.label: browserslist and useBuiltIns usage
nodes.rationale: Targets come from real traffic. useBuiltIns: usage injects only referenced core-js polyfills. Stale IE11 targets bloat every user.

nodes.label: V8 compilation tiers
nodes.rationale: Ignition interprets, Sparkplug baselines, Maglev mid-tier, TurboFan fully optimises hot type-stable functions.

nodes.label: Deoptimisation
nodes.rationale: Optimised add(a,b) fell out of TurboFan after strings and objects. Nothing in the function changed — only the shapes flowing through it.

nodes.label: Keep data shapes stable
nodes.rationale: Do not tune for the JIT. Normalise payloads at the boundary so every downstream object has the same keys in the same order.

nodes.label: Cold vs warm micro-benchmarks
nodes.rationale: Identical function 28x apart cold versus warm, reproduced. A single timing measures compilation state, not the code.

nodes.label: ToPrimitive
nodes.rationale: Hint string tries toString then valueOf. Hint number or default tries valueOf then toString. + uses default; templates use string; arithmetic uses number.

nodes.label: Date overrides default ToPrimitive hint
nodes.rationale: Date makes hint default behave as string, so date + '' is a date string while date * 1 is a timestamp.

nodes.label: Default Array.sort string compare
nodes.rationale: [10, 9, 1].sort() is [1, 10, 9] because SortCompare stringifies. Specified, not a quirk.

nodes.label: ECMA-262 living standard
nodes.rationale: Read tc39.es/ecma262, not a numbered edition PDF. Host APIs are in WHATWG and Node docs, not ECMA-262.

nodes.label: node --check
nodes.rationale: Parses and reports SyntaxErrors with no execution. Diagnostic for nothing printed at all.

nodes.label: console.table and console.dir
nodes.rationale: table for arrays of objects. dir with depth null fixes Node's [Object] truncation at depth 2.

nodes.label: DevTools lazy object expansion
nodes.rationale: Logged objects expand lazily. Log structuredClone(obj) to capture the value at that instant.

nodes.label: BigInt
nodes.rationale: Arbitrary-precision integers because Number cannot represent every integer past MAX_SAFE_INTEGER. Convert huge values from strings.

nodes.label: Cannot mix BigInt and Number
nodes.rationale: 1n + 1 throws TypeError. Comparison is exempt: 1n == 1 is true, 1n === 1 is false. Division truncates: 5n / 2n is 2n.

nodes.label: JSON.stringify throws on BigInt
nodes.rationale: JSON has no BigInt type. Use a replacer to string. Do not patch BigInt.prototype.toJSON.

nodes.label: Identifiers should be strings
nodes.rationale: Postgres bigint keys and snowflake IDs are never added or averaged. Send them as strings and skip BigInt serialisation entirely.

nodes.label: const protects the binding, not the value
nodes.rationale: const cart forbids reassignment. cart.qty = 99 is legal. Default to const; let only when the binding changes.

nodes.label: Object.freeze is shallow
nodes.rationale: Top-level writes throw in strict mode; nested objects mutate freely. Deep freeze must skip already-frozen objects to survive cycles.

nodes.label: == vs ===
nodes.rationale: === compares without converting. == converts: null/undefined only each other; string to number; boolean to number first; object via ToPrimitive.

nodes.label: value == null
nodes.rationale: The one defensible == use: tests null or undefined and nothing else. ESLint eqeqeq smart allows it.

nodes.label: null >= 0 is true
nodes.rationale: Relational operators ToNumber; Number(null) is 0. == never numeric-compares null. A null stock level silently passes a bounds check.

nodes.label: Four equality algorithms
nodes.rationale: == and === treat NaN as unequal and 0 equal to -0. SameValueZero (includes, Map/Set) equates NaN. SameValue (Object.is) also distinguishes -0.

nodes.label: Number vs parseInt
nodes.rationale: Number('42px') is NaN; parseInt('42px') is 42. Number('') is 0; parseInt('') is NaN. Use Number for validation.

nodes.label: map(parseInt) radix trap
nodes.rationale: map passes (value, index). parseInt('2', 1) and parseInt('3', 2) are NaN. Use map(Number).

nodes.label: Convert at the boundary
nodes.rationale: Form values, query params, localStorage and env vars are strings. Parse once on the way in. Apply ?? default before Number because Number(null) is 0.

nodes.label: NaN
nodes.rationale: IEEE-754: NaN means a failed computation, and two unrelated failures are not the same value, so NaN !== NaN. It never throws and poisons every later arithmetic step.

nodes.label: Number.isNaN
nodes.rationale: Use Number.isNaN, not global isNaN. The global coerces first so isNaN('abc') is true; Number.isNaN answers only 'is this the NaN value?'.

nodes.label: includes vs indexOf for NaN
nodes.rationale: indexOf uses === so [NaN].indexOf(NaN) is -1; includes and Map/Set keys use SameValueZero, so NaN is found and Set([NaN,NaN]).size is 1.

nodes.label: Number.isFinite validation
nodes.rationale: Validate where the value enters with Number.isFinite, which rejects NaN and both infinities. !Number.isNaN lets Infinity through.

nodes.label: undefined (engine absence)
nodes.rationale: undefined is absence the engine produced: unassigned binding, missing property, unpassed argument, no return. Prefer omitting the property rather than assigning undefined.

nodes.label: null (deliberate emptiness)
nodes.rationale: null is absence you chose. Defaults do not fire on it; JSON.stringify keeps it. Use it at the boundary to mean 'explicitly cleared' (PATCH).

nodes.label: Default parameters fire only on undefined
Nullish coalescing ??
nodes.rationale: Default to ??. It falls back only on null and undefined, so 0, '' and false survive. Mixing ?? with || or && is a SyntaxError without parentheses. NaN is a number so ?? does not catch it.

nodes.label: == null idiom
nodes.rationale: null and undefined are loosely equal only to each other. value == null is the permitted exception to always-===; ESLint eqeqeq:'smart' allows it.

nodes.label: IEEE-754 double number type
nodes.rationale: JavaScript has one number type: a 64-bit float. 0.1 + 0.2 !== 0.3 because both are repeating binary fractions. This is not a JS-only flaw.

nodes.label: Store money as integer minor units
nodes.rationale: Do arithmetic in paise/cents; Math.round once where a fraction is created; divide by 100 only when formatting with Intl.NumberFormat. Never toFixed money — 1.005 stores as slightly less so toFixed(2) is '1.00'.

nodes.label: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER
nodes.rationale: 53-bit significand: integers above 2^53-1 collapse. JSON.parse silently corrupts bigint IDs; send IDs as strings or recover via reviver ctx.source + BigInt.

nodes.label: Octal file-mode literals
nodes.rationale: 0o755 is 493, the correct Unix mode. chmod(path, 755) silently sets wrong permissions. Legacy 0755 is SyntaxError in strict/modules.

nodes.label: Number vs parseInt prefixes
nodes.rationale: Number understands 0x/0o/0b. parseInt('0o755') is 0 because parsing stops at the letter. Always pass radix 10.

nodes.label: Object.is / SameValue
nodes.rationale: Fourth equality algorithm: === with NaN treated equal and 0 vs -0 treated unequal. React uses it so NaN state does not re-render forever. Everyday code still uses ===.

nodes.label: Signed zero -0
nodes.rationale: IEEE-754 signed zero from underflow, 0*-1, or Math.round(-0.2). Invisible under ===, String, JSON. Detect with Object.is(x,-0) or 1/x === -Infinity. Matters for Math.atan2 and Object.is deep-equals.

nodes.label: Infinity
nodes.rationale: Division by zero does not throw. Math.max() is -Infinity (identity). JSON.stringify turns Infinity and NaN into null.

nodes.label: Autoboxing
nodes.rationale: Property access on a primitive temporarily wraps it, looks up the method on String/Number/Boolean.prototype, then discards the wrapper. Assignments do not persist. null and undefined have no wrapper.

nodes.label: Wrapper constructors
nodes.rationale: Never new String/Number/Boolean: they produce objects, so typeof is 'object' and new Boolean(false) is truthy. Without new they are conversion functions returning primitives.

nodes.label: Never extend built-in prototypes
nodes.rationale: Prototype extension is global and collides. Array.prototype.flatten was renamed flat because a library had taken the name. Write a standalone function or ponyfill.

nodes.label: 02 · Primitives are copied, objects are shared
Primitive copy vs object share
nodes.rationale: Assigning a primitive copies it; assigning an object copies the reference. JS is always pass-by-value, but for objects the value is the reference.

nodes.label: structuredClone
nodes.rationale: Default deep copy: handles cycles, Map, Set, Date. Throws on functions and DOM nodes. JSON.parse(JSON.stringify) drops undefined/functions/symbols, empties Map/Set, NaN→null.

nodes.label: Immutable updates / structural sharing
nodes.rationale: React change detection is a reference comparison. Mutating in place leaves the reference identical. Return new objects only along the changed path; untouched branches keep their references.

nodes.label: UTF-16 code units
nodes.rationale: .length, charAt and slice count UTF-16 code units. Code points above U+FFFF are surrogate pairs, so '🛒'.length is 2. Naive slice can emit a lone high surrogate.

nodes.label: Unicode NFC vs NFD
nodes.rationale: é can be one code point (NFC) or e plus combining acute (NFD). They render identically and are not ===. Normalise to NFC at the boundary. macOS filenames are NFD.

nodes.label: Symbol unique primitive
nodes.rationale: Every Symbol('id') is unique. Hidden from Object.keys, for…in and JSON.stringify, but getOwnPropertySymbols and spread expose/copy them. Not privacy — use #private fields.

nodes.label: Symbol implicit string coercion throws
nodes.rationale: '' + sym and `${sym}` throw so a unique value cannot silently become a non-unique string. String(sym) is the safe conversion.

nodes.label: Eight JavaScript types
nodes.rationale: Seven primitives plus object. Arrays, dates, regexes, Map and classes are objects. Functions are objects; typeof reports 'function' as a convenience.

nodes.label: typeof null === 'object' bug
nodes.rationale: Historic tag-bit bug: objects used tag 000 and null was the all-zero pointer. Fix rejected because existing code depends on it. Always && v !== null.

nodes.label: Array.isArray
nodes.rationale: instanceof Array fails across realms (iframe, vm). Array.isArray works regardless.

nodes.label: ToBoolean
nodes.rationale: if (x) is ToBoolean. Objects never convert to a primitive here, so [] is truthy even though [] == false. '0', 'false', {} and new Boolean(false) are all truthy.

nodes.label: ToNumber
nodes.rationale: null becomes 0; undefined becomes NaN. A missing value fails loudly; a null price silently becomes free.

nodes.label: + concatenation vs arithmetic
nodes.rationale: If either operand of + is a string after ToPrimitive, + concatenates. -, *, / and % always ToNumber both sides.

nodes.label: {} + [] parse vs coerce
nodes.rationale: As a statement {} is an empty block and +[] is ToNumber('') = 0. In expression position it is concatenation to '[object Object]'.

nodes.label: Convert at the boundary
nodes.rationale: Form values, query params, localStorage and env vars are strings. Parse and Number.isFinite once on the way in so the rest of the code works with real types.

nodes.label: JSON.stringify equality failures
nodes.rationale: Key order, dropped undefined, Date→string, Map/Set→{}, NaN/Infinity→null, throws on cycles. Wrong as a general equality function.

nodes.label: Shallow equality
nodes.rationale: One level, Object.is per field, Object.hasOwn not in. Right for immutable React props because a changed branch already has a new reference.

nodes.label: Deep equality
nodes.rationale: Prefer a library (fast-deep-equal, isDeepStrictEqual). Prefer an ETag/updatedAt over deep-comparing API bodies.

nodes.label: % is remainder not modulo
nodes.rationale: Result takes the sign of the dividend. -7 % 3 is -1. True modulo for wrap-around: ((a % b) + b) % b.

nodes.label: ** right-associative
nodes.rationale: 2 ** 3 ** 2 is 512. -2 ** 2 is a SyntaxError because the committee refused to pick between -4 and 4.

nodes.label: Automatic semicolon insertion
nodes.rationale: ASI inserts a semicolon only where the code would otherwise be a syntax error. If the next line can continue, it will.

nodes.label: Restricted productions
nodes.rationale: A newline after return/throw/break/continue/yield/postfix ++ forces a semicolon. return\n{a:1} yields undefined.

nodes.label: Logical assignment ||= &&= ??=
nodes.rationale: The write is inside the short-circuit. a ||= b skips the setter when a is truthy; a = a || b always writes. Load-bearing on setters, proxies, Vue/MobX and frozen objects.

nodes.label: Bitwise ToInt32 wrap
nodes.rationale: Every bitwise operator converts to 32-bit signed first. ~~1e10 is 1410065408. Use Math.trunc. Only 31 usable flags; 1 << 31 is negative.

nodes.label: Bitwise permission flags
nodes.rationale: & is looser than !== so (flags & MASK) !== 0 needs parentheses. For app-scale domain flags a Set of strings is usually clearer.

nodes.label: Labelled break and continue
nodes.rationale: One good use: exit nested loops. Prefer extracting a function and return. Labels are not goto — they cannot jump backwards or leave a function.

nodes.label: break in switch inside a loop
delete creates array holes
nodes.rationale: delete arr[1] does not shorten the array; it leaves a hole that map preserves. Use splice or filter/toSpliced. Never delete on arrays.

nodes.label: in vs Object.hasOwn
nodes.rationale: in walks the prototype chain so 'toString' in {} is true. Object.hasOwn checks own keys only.

nodes.label: Comma operator
nodes.rationale: Evaluates left to right, returns the last. Lowest precedence so x = 1, 2, 3 assigns 1. One readable use: two-pointer for header.

nodes.label: Relational comparison algorithm
nodes.rationale: ToPrimitive hint number, then lexicographic if both strings else ToNumber. No null special case: null >= 0 is true while null == 0 is false. NaN makes every relation false so !(a<b) is not a>=b.

nodes.label: Date relational vs identity
nodes.rationale: Two Dates for the same instant satisfy <= and >= via valueOf timestamps but ==/=== are identity and false. Compare +d1 === +d2.

nodes.label: Guard clauses
nodes.rationale: Early returns for failures so the happy path is last and unindented. Highest-value refactor for nested conditionals.

nodes.label: Ternary vs if
nodes.rationale: Ternary chooses a value; if chooses an action. One level inline; two or more align as a decision table or extract a function.

nodes.label: Always use braces
nodes.rationale: A brace-less body contains only the first statement. Apple's goto-fail TLS bug. Also interacts badly with ASI. Enable ESLint curly.

nodes.label: Expression vs statement
nodes.rationale: Expressions produce a value; statements perform an action. Only expressions are legal where a value is expected — JSX, arrow implicit return.

nodes.label: IIFE parentheses
nodes.rationale: function at statement start is a declaration and requires a name. Parentheses force expression position. Remaining uses: const that needs several statements.

nodes.label: Logical operators return operands
nodes.rationale: && and || return an operand, not a boolean; that one fact explains default-value bugs and the JSX 0 trap.

nodes.label: && and || return operands
nodes.rationale: a && b yields a if falsy else b; only ! always returns a boolean.

nodes.label: Logical short-circuiting
nodes.rationale: The right side is skipped when the left decides; that is why &&/|| cannot be functions.

nodes.label: Nullish coalescing ??
nodes.rationale: Falls back only on null/undefined, so a legitimate 0 survives; mixing ?? with &&/|| unparenthesised is a SyntaxError.

nodes.label: JSX && zero trap
nodes.rationale: 0 && element is 0; React renders 0 as text. Force a boolean with count > 0.

nodes.label: Loops
nodes.rationale: Choose a loop by whether you can break and whether you can await; forEach answers no to both.

nodes.label: for...of
nodes.rationale: Default over iterables; supports break/continue/return and await; index via entries().

nodes.label: forEach cannot break or await
nodes.rationale: return only exits the callback; async callbacks' promises are discarded, causing silent races.

nodes.label: for...in walks the prototype
nodes.rationale: Yields inherited enumerable keys and string indices; prefer Object.keys or for...of.

nodes.label: var loop shared binding
nodes.rationale: var is function-scoped so every closure sees the final value; let creates one binding per iteration.

nodes.label: do...while cursor pagination
nodes.rationale: Body must run once before the next-cursor condition exists.

nodes.label: Optional chaining ?.
nodes.rationale: Short-circuits the chain to undefined on null/undefined only; over-applying hides bugs.

nodes.label: Optional chaining three forms
nodes.rationale: obj?.prop, obj?.[expr], fn?.(); obj?[k] is a SyntaxError because the dot stays.

nodes.label: Optional chaining short-circuits the chain
nodes.rationale: From the nullish link onward nothing evaluates, including arguments; parentheses end the chain.

nodes.label: ?.() is not a callable guard
nodes.rationale: Guards only null/undefined; a present non-function still throws TypeError.

nodes.label: ?. with ?? idiom
nodes.rationale: Missing path becomes undefined; ?? supplies the default without treating 0 as missing.

nodes.label: Operator precedence
nodes.rationale: Do not memorise twenty levels; learn the five cases that bite and parenthesise the rest.

nodes.label: ** is right-associative
nodes.rationale: 2 ** 3 ** 2 is 512; only **, ternary, and assignment associate right.

nodes.label: + string poison
nodes.rationale: + groups left to right; where the first string sits changes 1+2+"3" vs "1"+2+3.

nodes.label: && binds tighter than ||
nodes.rationale: a || b && c is a || (b && c); mixed ?? is a SyntaxError instead.

nodes.label: Comparisons do not chain
nodes.rationale: 3 > 2 > 1 is (true) > 1 → 1 > 1 → false; write a < x && x < b.

nodes.label: Bitwise & looser than ===
nodes.rationale: flags & MASK === 0 parses as flags & (MASK === 0); parenthesise the mask test.

nodes.label: Comma operator lowest precedence
nodes.rationale: Evaluates every operand and returns the last; looser than assignment.

nodes.label: Spread and rest
nodes.rationale: Same ... syntax; rest collects on the left of = or in parameters, spread expands everywhere else.

nodes.label: Array vs object spread
nodes.rationale: [...x] uses Symbol.iterator; {...x} copies own enumerable keys. [...{}] throws; {...[]} works.

nodes.label: Spread is a shallow copy
nodes.rationale: Nested references are shared; later keys win; undefined still overwrites a default.

nodes.label: Rest parameters
nodes.rationale: Must be last; excluded from fn.length; object rest omits a key without mutation.

nodes.label: Spread argument stack limit
nodes.rationale: Math.max(...hugeArray) can throw RangeError; reduce instead.

nodes.label: switch
nodes.rationale: Compares with === and falls through unless stopped; use object lookup for key-to-value maps.

nodes.label: switch uses ===
nodes.rationale: 1 and '1' are different cases; case NaN never matches because NaN !== NaN.

nodes.label: switch fallthrough
nodes.rationale: Without break/return/throw, execution continues; stacked empty cases are the idiomatic share.

nodes.label: switch body is one block
nodes.rationale: Cases are labels, so two let x collide; brace each case body.

nodes.label: Arrow functions and this
nodes.rationale: An arrow is a different callable: no own this, arguments, super, new.target, or prototype.

nodes.label: call, apply and bind
nodes.rationale: call/apply invoke now; bind returns a new function with this fixed.

nodes.label: Closures
nodes.rationale: A function plus the variables it still sees; captures the variable, not the value.

nodes.label: Declarations, expressions and arrow functions
nodes.rationale: Three forms hoist, name, and construct differently; the error string identifies the form.

nodes.label: Function declaration hoisting
nodes.rationale: Name and body exist from the top of the scope, even after return.

nodes.label: Function expression TDZ vs var TypeError
nodes.rationale: const/let throw Cannot access before initialization; var f is undefined so the call is TypeError.

nodes.label: Inferred function .name
nodes.rationale: Assignment targets name the function; only an unbound expression has name === "".

nodes.label: Named function expression inner binding
nodes.rationale: inner is visible only inside the body, giving a recursion handle that survives reassignment.

nodes.label: Hoisting and the temporal dead zone
nodes.rationale: Nothing moves; entering a scope creates every binding. What fills the slot differs by declaration kind.

nodes.label: Scope-entry bindings
nodes.rationale: function starts callable; var starts undefined; let/const/class start empty; import is usable after side effects.

nodes.label: Temporal dead zone
nodes.rationale: A stretch of time after the binding exists and before initialisation; not a region of source.

nodes.label: Lexical scope and the scope chain
nodes.rationale: Scope is decided by where code is written, not where it is called.

nodes.label: Lexical scoping
nodes.rationale: Lookup walks outward at write time; this is what makes closures possible.

nodes.label: Parameters
nodes.rationale: The parameter list is its own language: own scope, TDZ, evaluation order, and simple vs non-simple.

nodes.label: this
nodes.rationale: this is an argument decided by the call site, not a variable decided by definition.

nodes.label: Four this binding rules
nodes.rationale: Default, implicit, explicit, and new; extracting a method into a variable loses implicit this.

nodes.label: Lexical this and missing bindings
nodes.rationale: An arrow has no this; this is a free variable resolved through the scope chain.

nodes.label: Arrow this is a free variable
nodes.rationale: Lookup finds the nearest ordinary function; object literals are not scopes so method arrows see module undefined.

nodes.label: call/apply/bind cannot change arrow this
nodes.rationale: They fail silently on this while still passing arguments; bind still returns a function.

nodes.label: Arrow has no prototype
nodes.rationale: prototype is genuinely absent; new throws TypeError: A is not a constructor. this/arguments/super/new.target are inherited, not missing.

nodes.label: Arrow inherited arguments
nodes.rationale: Inside a function an arrow reports the outer arguments.length; use rest parameters.

nodes.label: Arrow syntax and when not to use one
nodes.rationale: Concise bodies are expressions; braces start a block. Arrows are for callbacks, not methods or constructors.

nodes.label: Concise-body object-literal trap
nodes.rationale: n => { value: n } is a labelled statement returning undefined; wrap as ({ value: n }).

nodes.label: Class field arrow vs prototype method
nodes.rationale: One closure per instance, own enumerable, not stubbable on the prototype; use when a detached handler must keep this.

nodes.label: The three methods
nodes.rationale: All three set this; only bind defers the call. apply takes an array.

nodes.label: Function.prototype.apply
nodes.rationale: Second argument must be array-like or CreateListFromArrayLike throws.

nodes.label: Function.prototype.bind
nodes.rationale: Returns a new function object every time, so inline bind never matches removeEventListener.

nodes.label: thisArg coercion strict vs sloppy
nodes.rationale: Strict passes thisArg through; sloppy boxes primitives and maps null/undefined to globalThis.

nodes.label: What bind does
nodes.rationale: A bound function is an exotic object: prefixed name, reduced length, no own prototype, permanent this.

nodes.label: bind permanence
nodes.rationale: Later call/apply/bind cannot change this; further bind still accumulates leading arguments.

nodes.label: bind and new
nodes.rationale: new discards bound this but keeps bound args; [[Construct]] delegates so instanceof still holds.

nodes.label: Handwritten bind
nodes.rationale: Naive apply misses new; new.target plus prototype linking restores construct, but .name/.length/absent prototype are exotic.

nodes.label: Borrowing, partial application and cost
nodes.rationale: call/apply/bind survive as borrowing, type tags, and left-to-right partial application.

nodes.label: Array method borrowing
nodes.rationale: Array methods need only length and integer keys; Array.from replaced most slice.call uses.

nodes.label: Object.prototype.toString.call type tag
nodes.rationale: typeof cannot tell Array from null; toString.call reads the internal tag but loses to Symbol.toStringTag.

nodes.label: apply and spread stack limit
nodes.rationale: Both overflow at ~200k arguments with RangeError; reduce has no such limit. Limit depends on remaining stack.

nodes.label: Partial application with bind
nodes.rationale: Fills arguments only from the left; hoist bind out of hot loops.

nodes.label: What is captured
nodes.rationale: A closure holds the binding and reads it at call time, not a snapshot.

nodes.label: Closure captures the variable
nodes.rationale: A reader created while x was 'first' returns later values after reassignment.

nodes.label: IIFE loop-variable capture
nodes.rationale: A parameter is a fresh binding per call; let automates the pre-ES6 IIFE fix.

nodes.label: let per-iteration binding
nodes.rationale: Closures mutating their own n yield [10,11,12] then [20,21,22]; one shared binding would be [10,20,30].

nodes.label: Private state and memory
nodes.rationale: The same capture that gives privacy also keeps memory alive as long as the function lives.

nodes.label: Counter factory private state
nodes.rationale: Each factory call is a new scope; closures created together share that one scope.

nodes.label: V8 captures referenced variables
nodes.rationale: Unused 300k-row arrays added 0 MB; referencing one element retained 69 MB. Engine optimisation, not a spec guarantee.

nodes.label: Stale-closure bug
nodes.rationale: Closing over a copy freezes the creation-time value; React effects hit the same mechanism.

nodes.label: Block functions and the parameter list
nodes.rationale: Hoisting errors that do not look like hoisting: block-level functions and parameter-list TDZ.

nodes.label: Block-level function declarations
nodes.rationale: Strict: block-scoped and hoisted in the block. Sloppy: Annex B, engine-dependent, even if (false).

nodes.label: Parameter list TDZ
nodes.rationale: Defaults initialise left to right; a = b, b = 2 throws Cannot access 'b' before initialization.

nodes.label: Parameter scope is parent of body
nodes.rationale: Defaults cannot see body functions or var; a default closure captures the parameter, not a shadowed body var.

nodes.label: Two-step scope entry
nodes.rationale: Nothing is relocated. Scope entry first creates a binding for every declaration, then code runs. What differs is whether the slot is initialised.

nodes.label: Value hoisting
nodes.rationale: Functions (and function*, async function) are usable before their line because the slot holds the finished function.

nodes.label: Declaration hoisting
nodes.rationale: var is referenceable before its line without ReferenceError, but the value is always undefined until assignment.

nodes.label: Behavioral hoisting
nodes.rationale: let/const/class create a dead zone above their line: the binding exists but is uninitialised.

nodes.label: Side-effect hoisting
nodes.rationale: import bindings are available early and the imported module's side effects run before the rest of the file.

nodes.label: HoistableDeclaration
nodes.rationale: The spec term is not 'hoisting'. HoistableDeclaration covers function declarations only.

nodes.label: Three binding error types
nodes.rationale: 'x is not defined' means no binding; 'x is not a function' means the binding holds a non-callable; 'Cannot access before initialization' means uninitialised TDZ.

nodes.label: var declaration vs initialization split
nodes.rationale: var x = 1 is two operations: the declaration hoists to function scope as undefined; the assignment stays where it is.

nodes.label: Function declaration value hoisting
nodes.rationale: The only form that is usefully hoisted: the slot holds the finished function before the first line runs.

nodes.label: Function expression not hoisted
nodes.rationale: var f = function(){} hoists the binding as undefined; calling it above the line is TypeError, not ReferenceError.

nodes.label: var and function name collision
nodes.rationale: At scope entry the function wins regardless of source order. Only an initializer overwrites it at execution time.

nodes.label: Script top-level var as non-configurable global
nodes.rationale: In a classic script, top-level var becomes a non-configurable globalThis property. Modules do not do this.

nodes.label: Temporal dead zone
nodes.rationale: A stretch of time, not of code. The binding exists from block entry but is empty until the declaration runs; a read throws ReferenceError.

nodes.label: TDZ is temporal not positional
nodes.rationale: A function defined above a let may mention it; only a read that runs before the declaration throws.

nodes.label: Declaration closes the TDZ
nodes.rationale: let x; initialises to undefined and ends the zone. const without an initializer is a parse-time SyntaxError.

nodes.label: Self-reference initializer
nodes.rationale: let x = x throws because the RHS is evaluated before the binding is initialised. var y = y silently assigns undefined.

nodes.label: Per-iteration loop binding
nodes.rationale: for (const item of items) is legal because each iteration declares a new binding rather than reassigning one.

nodes.label: typeof throws in the TDZ
nodes.rationale: typeof still reads the binding. It returns 'undefined' only for names with no binding at all.

nodes.label: TDZ is a feature
nodes.rationale: Fails at the wrong line instead of later undefined; lets const have one observable value; makes a shadow own the name for the whole block.

nodes.label: Engine TDZ error messages
nodes.rationale: V8 names the variable; SpiderMonkey says lexical declaration; JavaScriptCore omits the name.

nodes.label: globalThis feature detection
nodes.rationale: globalThis.X !== undefined is a property access and cannot hit a dead zone.

nodes.label: Class lexical declaration
nodes.rationale: class is TDZ, block-scoped, and never creates globalThis properties — like let, not like function.

nodes.label: Class inner immutable binding
nodes.rationale: Inside the class body the class name is const-like. Outside it is a reassignable let-like binding.

nodes.label: extends evaluated at declaration
nodes.rationale: extends is an expression run when the class statement executes, not at new. Mutual extends is impossible.

nodes.label: Circular ES module import TDZ
nodes.rationale: Depth-first evaluation can read a hoisted import before the exporter initialises it. Same error string as a local let.

nodes.label: Import live read-only view
nodes.rationale: Imports are const-like live views. Only the exporting module can reassign; property mutation is allowed.

nodes.label: CommonJS circular require
nodes.rationale: require has no dead zone: a cycle returns a partially populated module.exports, usually with undefined properties.

nodes.label: Lexical scope
nodes.rationale: A function's free variables resolve where it is written, not where it is called. That is what makes closures possible.

nodes.label: Scope chain
nodes.rationale: Lookup walks innermost to outermost and stops at the first match. Outer scopes never see inner bindings.

nodes.label: What creates a scope
nodes.rationale: Functions, modules, blocks for let/const/class, for-heads with let/const, and catch. Object literals do not.

nodes.label: Shadowing
nodes.rationale: An inner binding hides the outer one for its scope without overwriting it. let cannot redeclare a parameter at function top level.

nodes.label: with statement
nodes.rationale: Injects an object's properties into the scope chain, defeating static slot resolution. SyntaxError in strict mode.

nodes.label: Direct eval
nodes.rationale: Can introduce bindings into the surrounding scope. Indirect eval (0, eval)(...) runs in global scope instead.

nodes.label: Function scope vs block scope
nodes.rationale: var ignores blocks and attaches to the nearest function. let/const attach to the nearest block.

nodes.label: const fixes the binding not the value
nodes.rationale: The name cannot be pointed at something else; object and array contents can still change.

nodes.label: Object.freeze
nodes.rationale: Shallow. Nested objects remain mutable. Strict mode throws on a frozen write; sloppy fails silently.

nodes.label: Module top level is not global
nodes.rationale: Top-level var is a global only in a classic script. ES modules and CommonJS keep it off globalThis.

nodes.label: Accidental global
nodes.rationale: Assigning to an undeclared name creates a global in sloppy mode and throws ReferenceError in strict/modules.

nodes.label: const by default
nodes.rationale: const first, let when you reassign, var never. Use-before-declaration then throws instead of producing undefined.

nodes.label: Default parameter expression
nodes.rationale: Stored unevaluated; runs at call time, left to right, only for omitted arguments.

nodes.label: Only undefined triggers a default
nodes.rationale: null is a value. APIs that return null for missing data will not fall back unless you use ?? in the body.

nodes.label: Parameter list TDZ
nodes.rationale: Defaults initialise left to right. A forward reference throws only when that argument is omitted.

nodes.label: No Python mutable-default trap
nodes.rationale: list = [] constructs per call. The trap returns if the default names a shared outer binding.

nodes.label: Function.length and defaults
nodes.rationale: length counts parameters before the first default or rest. Express and Mocha dispatch on arity.

nodes.label: Parameter scope vs body scope
nodes.rationale: Any default creates a parameter scope. A var of the same name in the body is a different binding.

nodes.label: Arity is never enforced
nodes.rationale: Too few arguments become undefined; extras are ignored by the parameter list but still counted by arguments.

nodes.label: Rest parameters
nodes.rationale: A real array, empty rather than undefined when nothing extra is passed. Must be last; cannot have a default.

nodes.label: arguments object
nodes.rationale: Array-like, no array methods, absent in arrows. Prefer rest in new code.

nodes.label: Sloppy-mode arguments aliasing
nodes.rationale: On a simple sloppy parameter list, arguments[i] and the parameter share one slot. Strict, default, rest, or destructuring turns it off.

nodes.label: Non-simple parameter list
nodes.rationale: Any default, rest, or destructured parameter. Disables aliasing, forbids a body 'use strict', and changes .length.

nodes.label: Destructured parameter = {}
nodes.rationale: x = 0 defaults a missing property; = {} defaults a missing object. Every nesting level needs its own default.

nodes.label: Positional plus options object
nodes.rationale: Two or three required positionals, then a destructured options object. JavaScript will not check arity for you.

nodes.label: Four this binding rules
nodes.rationale: this is a hidden first parameter filled by the call site: new, then explicit, then implicit, then default.

nodes.label: Default this binding
nodes.rationale: Bare fn() is undefined in strict/module/class code and globalThis in sloppy. Module top-level this is undefined.

nodes.label: Implicit this binding
nodes.rationale: obj.fn() binds this to whatever is left of the last dot. The rest of the chain is irrelevant.

nodes.label: Explicit this binding
nodes.rationale: call/apply invoke immediately; bind returns a new function with this fixed. A bound function cannot be re-bound.

nodes.label: new this binding
nodes.rationale: Create object, link Fn.prototype, call with this bound, return it unless the constructor returns another object. A returned primitive is ignored.

nodes.label: this precedence
nodes.rationale: new beats bind beats call/apply beats implicit beats default. new on a bound function discards bound this but keeps bound arguments.

nodes.label: Lost this
nodes.rationale: Implicit binding is a property of the call site. Assigning, destructuring, or passing a method drops the receiver.

nodes.label: thisArg
nodes.rationale: forEach/map/filter/some/every/find/findIndex/flatMap accept a thisArg. reduce and sort do not.

nodes.label: bind identity trap
nodes.rationale: bind returns a new function each call, so removeEventListener never matches. Store the bound function once.

nodes.label: Class field arrow
nodes.rationale: Per-instance own property capturing constructor this. Survives detach; cannot be super-called or stubbed on the prototype.

nodes.label: Arrow callback this fix
nodes.rationale: An arrow has no this, so the inner obj.method() keeps its receiver. Wrong as the method itself at module scope.

nodes.label: class is half sugar
nodes.rationale: Lookup machinery is unchanged — methods go on Ctor.prototype. Five other behaviours are real language features.

nodes.label: Five non-sugar class features
nodes.rationale: Always-strict body; TypeError without new; non-enumerable methods; TDZ/block scope; private elements.

nodes.label: Three class member destinations
nodes.rationale: Fields are own per instance; methods live on Ctor.prototype; statics live on the class object; #fields are private slots.

nodes.label: Four existence checks
nodes.rationale: in, Object.hasOwn, hasOwnProperty, and !== undefined disagree on inherited keys and on keys holding undefined.

nodes.label: Existence-check decision table
nodes.rationale: Object.hasOwn by default for data. in for feature detection. !== undefined only when missing and undefined mean the same thing.

nodes.label: Object.keys own enumerable string keys
nodes.rationale: keys/values/entries share one definition. They drop inherited, non-enumerable, and symbol keys. Same set as JSON.stringify.

nodes.label: Object.fromEntries
nodes.rationale: Reverse of Object.entries. Gives objects the map/filter they do not have via the entries round trip.

nodes.label: Method shorthand
nodes.rationale: Not equivalent to prop: function(){}. Not constructable, and super works.

nodes.label: __proto__ prototype setter
nodes.rationale: { __proto__: x } sets the prototype, not a property. { __proto__ } and { ['__proto__']: p } are different.

nodes.label: Integer-index key order
nodes.rationale: Integer-like keys first ascending, then strings by insertion, then symbols. Not the order you wrote.

nodes.label: Shallow copy
nodes.rationale: spread, Object.assign, slice, Array.from copy one level. Nested references are shared. Usually the right answer for immutable updates.

nodes.label: structuredClone
nodes.rationale: Deep clone that rebuilds cycles. Silently drops prototypes and private elements; throws DataCloneError on some types.

nodes.label: JSON round-trip clone
nodes.rationale: Deep but loses seven documented things and cannot handle cycles. Fine only for already JSON-shaped data.

nodes.label: Prototype chain
nodes.rationale: An object is own properties plus a link. Lookup walks until it finds a name or reaches null. Nothing is copied onto instances.

nodes.label: [[Prototype]] vs Fn.prototype
nodes.rationale: [[Prototype]] is the lookup link on every object. Fn.prototype is an ordinary property used by new. Object.getPrototypeOf(Fn) is Function.prototype.

nodes.label: A method is not attached
nodes.rationale: A method is an ordinary function reachable through an object. The binding is created by the dot and does not travel.

nodes.label: Four this fixes
nodes.rationale: Default to wrapping at the call site. Arrow field for always-callback handlers. bind in the constructor for stable identity.

nodes.label: Private elements
nodes.rationale: No desugaring. # prefix; parser-enforced. Fields, methods, statics, and accessors. Cannot be deleted or created by assignment.

nodes.label: Private access SyntaxError
nodes.rationale: obj.#field outside the declaring class is a parse-time SyntaxError. The file never runs.

nodes.label: Private brand check
nodes.rationale: #x in obj is legal only inside the declaring class. Stronger than instanceof because privates cannot be forged or added later.

nodes.label: Private elements are not inherited
nodes.rationale: JavaScript has no protected. Parent and child can reuse the same #name as independent slots.

nodes.label: Private is encapsulation not secrecy
nodes.rationale: A debugger shows them. JSON.stringify and structuredClone drop them. Maintenance property, not a security boundary.

nodes.label: Static members
nodes.rationale: Live on the class object, which is not on the instance prototype chain. instance.staticThing is undefined.

nodes.label: this in a static method is the class
nodes.rationale: new this(...) makes a factory inherit: User.create builds a User because extends also links class objects.

nodes.label: Static initialization block
nodes.rationale: Statements plus private-scope access. Evaluated at the class statement, top to bottom with static fields.

nodes.label: Accessor recursion trap
nodes.rationale: get name() { return this.name; } calls itself until the stack blows. Back with #name.

nodes.label: Class body is always strict
nodes.rationale: No opt-out. Unbound this is undefined; implicit globals and several silent failures become errors.

nodes.label: Class constructors require new
nodes.rationale: Calling without new is TypeError. A constructor function would silently assign to the wrong this.

nodes.label: Class methods are non-enumerable
nodes.rationale: Hand-assigned prototype methods show up in for...in. Class methods do not.

nodes.label: Instance field vs prototype method
nodes.rationale: A field is an own enumerable property per instance. A method is one shared non-enumerable function. Mutable defaults must be fields.

nodes.label: Derived field initialization order
nodes.rationale: Base: fields at constructor start. Derived: immediately before super() returns. An overridden method called from the parent constructor sees uninitialised fields.

nodes.label: delete removes own properties only
nodes.rationale: Does not free memory, remove variables, or touch the prototype. Deleting an own key unshadows the inherited one.

nodes.label: delete return value
nodes.rationale: true does not mean anything was deleted. false (or TypeError in strict) only reports an own non-configurable property.

nodes.label: delete on an array leaves a hole
nodes.rationale: length is unchanged. Use splice, filter, or toSpliced. Holes make array methods inconsistent and slower.

nodes.label: V8 HiddenClass
nodes.rationale: Objects sharing a shape share a HiddenClass so inline caches stay fast. Frequent add/delete generates HiddenClass and descriptor-array overhead.

nodes.label: V8 dictionary mode
nodes.rationale: Slow mode: properties in a hash table, no descriptor array, inline caches do not work. One delete is not documented to trigger it.

nodes.label: Rest destructuring to omit a key
nodes.rationale: const { password, ...safe } = user builds a new stable-shape object. Shallow; nested copies survive.

nodes.label: Map for dynamic keys
nodes.rationale: map.delete is first-class, no HiddenClass cost, any key type. If you delete in a loop you wanted a Map.

nodes.label: in operator
nodes.rationale: Walks the prototype chain, so user keys like constructor match Object.prototype. Throws TypeError on primitives, null, and undefined — unlike property access, in does not auto-box.

nodes.label: Object.hasOwn
nodes.rationale: ES2022 static own-only check. Works on null-prototype objects, immune to a shadowed hasOwnProperty, and coerces primitives instead of throwing.

nodes.label: Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty
nodes.rationale: Legacy own-only check looked up on the receiver, so Object.create(null) throws and a JSON hasOwnProperty key can lie.

nodes.label: hasOwnProperty.call fallback
nodes.rationale: Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(obj, prop) bypasses null-prototype and shadowing. Keep only for pre-ES2022 runtimes.

nodes.label: in for behaviour, hasOwn for data
nodes.rationale: Feature detection needs the chain (DOM methods live on prototypes). Dictionary keys from users must be own-only or constructor/toString become true.

nodes.label: undefined versus missing key
nodes.rationale: !== undefined, ?., and ?? cannot tell a present undefined from absence. PATCH/options need Object.hasOwn. JSON.stringify drops undefined, so the wire distinction is present-vs-absent or null-vs-absent.

nodes.label: Nullish coalescing ?? versus ||
nodes.rationale: ?? falls back only on null/undefined so retries: 0 survives; || treats every falsy as missing. Mixing ?? with || or && is a SyntaxError without parentheses.

nodes.label: Array holes three states
nodes.rationale: Present value, present undefined, and a hole all read as undefined. Only in/Object.hasOwn distinguish them. map/forEach skip holes; spread and for...of visit them as undefined.

nodes.label: Private field brand check
nodes.rationale: ES2022 #field in obj asks whether this class constructed the object. Unforgeable unlike instanceof (Symbol.hasInstance, reassigned prototype, cross-realm). Legal only inside the declaring class; avoids try/catch TypeError on undeclared privates.

nodes.label: Object.fromEntries
nodes.rationale: Inverse of Object.entries. Accepts any pair iterable including Map, URLSearchParams, FormData, Headers. Always builds a plain object; unlike Array.from it ignores this.

nodes.label: entries-fromEntries object map/filter
nodes.rationale: Objects have no map/filter. Convert to pairs, use array methods, convert back. Safer pick than delete. Loses symbols, non-enumerables, inherited keys, prototype, accessors, descriptors, and numeric key order. Shallow.

nodes.label: fromEntries duplicate-key loss
nodes.rationale: URLSearchParams/FormData can repeat keys; an object cannot. Last assignment wins, so tag=a&tag=b becomes {tag:"b"}. Use getAll or keep the params object.

nodes.label: Object.keys values entries
nodes.rationale: Same own enumerable string-keyed set that JSON.stringify serialises. Coerce non-objects; throw TypeError on null/undefined. Integer-index keys sort ascending and come back as strings.

nodes.label: Own enumerable string-keyed set
nodes.rationale: Those three words decide what keys/values/entries, JSON.stringify, and (almost) spread silently drop: inherited, non-enumerable, and symbol keys.

nodes.label: for...in enumeration
nodes.rationale: Same enumerable string keys as Object.keys but also walks the prototype chain. Smell on a plain object; Object.keys/entries should be the default.

nodes.label: Reflect.ownKeys
nodes.rationale: Only one-call way to get every own key — enumerable or not, strings and symbols. Use with getOwnPropertyDescriptor for a faithful clone.

nodes.label: Object keys are strings or symbols
nodes.rationale: Everything else stringifies, so o[1]===o["1"] and two objects collide on [object Object]. That collision is why Map exists.

nodes.label: Three-tier property order
nodes.rationale: Integer indices ascending, then other strings by insertion, then symbols by insertion. Numeric-ID objects silently reorder; JSON.stringify follows the same rule.

nodes.label: Integer-index key definition
nodes.rationale: Only the canonical string of a non-negative integer. "-1", "01", "007", "1.5", and "1e2" sort with ordinary strings.

nodes.label: Object method shorthand
nodes.rationale: Not equivalent to prop: function(){}. Methods cannot be constructors (TypeError) and only methods have super via a home object. Arrows in literals capture enclosing this, not the object.

nodes.label: Object spread
nodes.rationale: Copies own enumerable string and symbol keys shallowly, excluding the prototype. Spreading a class instance drops methods. Later spreads win; a spread after an explicit key silently overwrites it.

nodes.label: Object.assign
nodes.rationale: Mutates the target and triggers its setters (MDN warning). Keeps the target prototype. Not interchangeable with { ...a, ...b }.

nodes.label: Getter and setter properties
nodes.rationale: Look like data properties but run functions. Spread and Object.assign invoke getters and store a snapshot. Preserve with getOwnPropertyDescriptors.

nodes.label: Duplicate object keys last wins
nodes.rationale: After ES2015 duplicates are legal even in strict mode because computed keys cannot be checked at parse time. Only private class elements must stay unique.

nodes.label: __proto__ colon form
nodes.rationale: Dedicated creation-time syntax that sets [[Prototype]] and creates no property. Shorthand {__proto__} and computed {["__proto__"]:v} are ordinary properties. Non-object/non-null x is a silent no-op.

nodes.label: Object.create(null) dictionary
nodes.rationale: No inherited keys and no __proto__ accessor to pollute. Cost: no toString/hasOwnProperty — string conversion throws; existence checks need Object.hasOwn. Prefer Map unless a plain-object shape is required.

nodes.label: Prototype pollution
nodes.rationale: JSON.parse is not the hole — "__proto__" is a normal own key in JSON. Recursive merge that assigns target["__proto__"] hits Object.prototype's accessor and pollutes every object, including ones created earlier.

nodes.label: Shorthand property names
nodes.rationale: {a} means {a:a}. Cannot rename, so API casing boundaries stay verbose. Pairs with destructuring as the pick-fields idiom.

nodes.label: Computed property names
nodes.rationale: Expressions in [] evaluate in source order while the object is built and may have side effects. Only literal form that accepts a symbol key.

nodes.label: Conditional property spread idiom
nodes.rationale: ...(cond && {key}) keeps one expression. Spreading a falsy non-object is a defined no-op. Avoids delete, which is slower on hot objects.

nodes.label: JSON round-trip clone
nodes.rationale: Seven documented losses: undefined/functions/symbols omitted-or-nulled, NaN/Infinity→null, Date→string, Map/Set→{}, BigInt throws, cycles throw, symbol/non-enumerable skipped. Acceptable only for already-JSON-shaped data.

nodes.label: Hand-written deep clone
nodes.rationale: Interview answer, not production. Still drops prototype, descriptors, accessors, and private fields. Ship structuredClone.

nodes.label: Visited WeakMap before recurse
nodes.rationale: Register the empty clone in a WeakMap before walking children so cycles terminate and shared identity is preserved. After the loop never terminates. WeakMap so bookkeeping does not pin every visited object.

nodes.label: structuredClone
nodes.rationale: Language deep clone via the structured clone algorithm. Rebuilds cycles, preserves Map/Set/Date/RegExp/typed arrays. Loses prototype, descriptors, private fields, RegExp.lastIndex. Clones data, not types.

nodes.label: structuredClone transfer option
nodes.rationale: Moves transferable buffers instead of copying; original is detached (byteLength 0). Only when finished with the source.

nodes.label: DataCloneError
nodes.rationale: DOMException when any part is not serialisable — functions, DOM nodes, Promise, WeakMap, Symbol. Better than JSON silently dropping functions.

nodes.label: Shallow copy
nodes.rationale: Top-level properties become independent; nested objects stay shared. Spread, Object.assign, slice, Array.from, concat are all shallow. [...users] is a new array of the same user objects.

nodes.label: Deep copy
nodes.rationale: Duplicates the whole graph so nothing is shared. Reach for it only for snapshots, defensive copies of input you will mutate, or data handed to untrusted code.

nodes.label: Copy the path, share the rest
nodes.rationale: Idiomatic React/Redux updates copy only changed levels. Shared identity makes prev===next a valid change check and is what React.memo needs. Deep-cloning state defeats memoisation.

nodes.label: Prototype chain lookup
nodes.rationale: Walk own then each [[Prototype]] until a match or null. A miss is the most expensive lookup. Nothing is copied onto instances. Array methods live on Array.prototype, not the array.

nodes.label: Property shadowing
nodes.rationale: The first own match hides the further one. The prototype value is untouched and still reachable via Object.getPrototypeOf(o).b.

nodes.label: [[Prototype]] internal slot
nodes.rationale: Not a property. Read with Object.getPrototypeOf. obj.__proto__ is a deprecated accessor inherited from Object.prototype, so it is absent on null-prototype objects.

nodes.label: Constructor.prototype property
nodes.rationale: Ordinary property only functions have — the [[Prototype]] given to new instances. Not the function's own prototype; Object.getPrototypeOf(Box) is Function.prototype.

nodes.label: new operator
nodes.rationale: Creates an object whose [[Prototype]] is Fn.prototype, calls Fn with this bound to it, returns it unless the body returns an object. Methods are shared, not copied. Lookup is dynamic.

nodes.label: class as prototype sugar
nodes.rationale: Class methods land on Ctor.prototype; the chain is identical. Adds #private, extends, strict bodies, throw-without-new, and non-enumerable methods. Hand-assigned prototype methods stay enumerable.

nodes.label: Object.create
nodes.rationale: Sets [[Prototype]] with no constructor call. Second-argument descriptors default every flag to false — silent read-only unless stated.

nodes.label: prototype.constructor back-reference
nodes.rationale: Own property of Fn.prototype. Replacing prototype wholesale drops it — hence Child.prototype.constructor = Child. Writable and forgeable; never use for type checks. Some built-ins read it via Symbol.species.

nodes.label: Writes create own properties
nodes.rationale: Reads walk the chain; assignment does not. Inherited setters intercept the write; inherited read-only throws in strict mode. Inherited defaults work because assignment shadows.

nodes.label: Shared mutable prototype state
nodes.rationale: Fn.prototype.items = [] is one array. push mutates after a read, so no shadow is created and every instance sees the change. Put mutable values on the instance (class field or constructor).

nodes.label: Object.setPrototypeOf
nodes.rationale: Engines specialise access on the creation-time chain; changing it de-optimises compiled code. Prefer {__proto__: proto} or Object.create at creation. Deep chains tax every miss.

nodes.label: this from the call site
nodes.rationale: obj.f() binds this to obj. Finding an inherited method and resolving properties it reads are two lookups that can land at different levels. Methods are not owned by their object.

nodes.label: Detached method
nodes.rationale: Assigning, destructuring, or passing obj.method as a callback drops the receiver. Strict (modules/classes) gives undefined and TypeError; sloppy substitutes globalThis and silently creates globals.

nodes.label: Array method thisArg
nodes.rationale: forEach/map/filter/some/every/find/findIndex/flatMap take a thisArg. reduce/reduceRight use the second argument as initialValue; sort has none. Arrows work everywhere.

nodes.label: Function.prototype.bind
nodes.rationale: Returns a new function whose this is permanent — bind only works once; call/apply cannot override. Constructor bind installs an own property that shadows the prototype method.

nodes.label: Arrow class field
nodes.rationale: Field initialiser runs with this already the instance; the arrow captures it. One function per instance, not on the prototype — subclasses cannot override normally and super cannot reach it.

nodes.label: Call-site arrow wrapper
nodes.rationale: Best default: explicit, free, method stays on the prototype and overridable. Wrong for removable listeners because each arrow is a new function.

nodes.label: removeEventListener identity match
nodes.rationale: Removal matches by function identity. An inline arrow cannot be removed. Store one bound function or arrow field and pass it to both add and remove.

nodes.label: Array push and pop
nodes.rationale: Back-of-array adders return the new length; removers return the element. Do not re-index the rest of the array. Non-mutating twins: [...arr, x] and arr.slice(0, -1).

nodes.label: Array shift and unshift
nodes.rationale: Front operations re-index the whole array. Draining a large queue with shift() is quadratic.

nodes.label: Array splice and toSpliced
nodes.rationale: Remove, insert, replace. Omitted deleteCount deletes to the end — splice(2) on ten elements drops eight. Beats delete (no hole). Never splice in a forward loop. toSpliced is the non-mutating twin.

nodes.label: new Array(n) holes
nodes.rationale: Creates holes, not undefined slots, so new Array(5).map(f) does nothing. Never create holes; then the hole-behaviour table stops mattering.

nodes.label: Array.from
nodes.rationale: Accepts iterables and array-likes; spread accepts only iterables. mapFn second argument. Array.from({length:n}, fn) is never sparse.

nodes.label: Array.of
nodes.rationale: Exists because Array(3) is holes while Array(1,2,3) is values. Use Array.of whenever argument count is dynamic.

nodes.label: Array length writable property
nodes.rationale: One more than the highest index, not a count of present values. Non-enumerable so Object.keys skips it. arr.length=0 truncates in place; arr=[] replaces the binding.

nodes.label: Array iteration method table
nodes.rationale: Same walk, different return and early-stop. forEach returns undefined and cannot break (MDN names for...of). map always same length; filter ≤ length; find/findIndex/some/every stop early.

nodes.label: map(parseInt) radix bug
nodes.rationale: ["1","2","3"].map(parseInt) is [1, NaN, NaN] because the index arrives as radix.

nodes.label: every on empty array is true
nodes.rationale: Vacuous truth. [].every(x => x.inStock) is true — a validation bug if emptiness should fail.

nodes.label: async forEach trap
nodes.rationale: forEach does not await. Async callbacks return discarded promises; MDN's example prints 0 instead of 14.

nodes.label: JSON.stringify
nodes.rationale: Lossy and silent except BigInt and cycles (TypeError). undefined/functions/symbols omitted in objects, nulled in arrays. Sees the same own enumerable string-keyed set as Object.keys. Map/Set become {}.

nodes.label: JSON.parse
nodes.rationale: SyntaxError on trailing commas, single quotes, empty bodies. The parse itself is safe from prototype pollution; the merge afterwards is not.

nodes.label: JSON.parse reviver
nodes.rationale: Must end with return value or every other key is deleted. Innermost-first. Only place to repair stringify losses (e.g. revive *At dates). context.source for 64-bit precision.

nodes.label: Map
nodes.rationale: Any key type, insertion order for all keys, size, direct iteration, cheaper add/remove. NaN is a usable key via SameValueZero. JSON.stringify(map) is {}.

nodes.label: WeakMap
nodes.rationale: Required when keys must not keep objects alive (visited-set in a clone, per-object metadata). Not iterable and not serialisable.

nodes.label: Map when keys are data
nodes.rationale: Use a Map when keys are data; an object when keys are code. Tells: delete in a loop, Object.keys(o).length in a hot path, or Object.create(null) for user keys.

nodes.label: SameValueZero Map keys
nodes.rationale: Map key equality treats NaN as equal to NaN, so m.set(NaN,"ok"); m.get(NaN) works. Objects cannot have a NaN key.

nodes.label: Array.prototype.reduce
nodes.rationale: Four-argument callback, no thisArg. Holes skipped; stored undefined is not. Wins for scalar folds, pipe, promise sequencing. MDN has a when-not-to-use section.

nodes.label: reduce initialValue
nodes.rationale: Omitted: accumulator is element 0, iteration starts at 1, TypeError on an empty array. Always pass an initial value.

nodes.label: reduce spread-accumulator anti-pattern
nodes.rationale: Spreading the accumulator each step is O(N²). The accumulator is private — mutating it is not an immutability violation. Prefer flat, Object.groupBy, Set, filter.

nodes.label: Object.groupBy and Map.groupBy
nodes.rationale: Named replacement for the grouping fold. Map.groupBy usually beats Object.groupBy because object key order re-sorts integer-like keys.

nodes.label: Array.prototype.sort
nodes.rationale: Default is a UTF-16 string sort; sort mutates and returns the same array.

nodes.label: Four sort rules
nodes.rationale: Always pass a numeric comparator; copy or toSorted; keep the comparator total; undefined and holes go last.

nodes.label: String immutability
nodes.rationale: Strings are immutable so string methods never mutate and need no defensive copy.

nodes.label: slice vs substring and replace vs replaceAll
nodes.rationale: Use slice not substring; never build a regex from user input — replaceAll with a string matches literally.

nodes.label: push pop shift unshift
nodes.rationale: Adders return the new length; removers return the element or undefined. All four mutate in place.

nodes.label: shift re-indexes the array
nodes.rationale: shift and unshift re-index every remaining element; pop and push touch one slot.

nodes.label: O(n²) shift queue
nodes.rationale: n shifts re-index up to n elements. Use an index cursor or reverse-then-pop.

nodes.label: Non-mutating end equivalents
nodes.rationale: Spread or slice instead of push/pop/shift/unshift when the array is shared or is React state.

nodes.label: Array.prototype.splice
nodes.rationale: In-place remove/insert/replace. Returns the removed elements, not the array.

nodes.label: Array.prototype.toSpliced
nodes.rationale: ES2023 non-mutating counterpart; returns the new dense array, not the removed items.

nodes.label: Omitted splice deleteCount
nodes.rationale: splice(i) deletes from i to the end; splice(i, 0) inserts. Omitting deleteCount is not 0.

nodes.label: splice in a forward loop
nodes.rationale: Removing at i shifts later items down so i++ skips the next. Filter or iterate backwards.

nodes.label: delete vs splice on arrays
nodes.rationale: delete leaves a hole and length unchanged; splice removes, closes the gap, decrements length.

nodes.label: Array length writable property
nodes.rationale: Writable nonnegative integer < 2³². Shrinking truncates; growing creates holes. Not a count of values.

nodes.label: Sparse array holes
nodes.rationale: A hole is an absent index property, not stored undefined. From new Array(n), elision, length grow, or delete.

nodes.label: Three array index states
nodes.rationale: Present value, present undefined, or hole. Reading both last two is undefined; only in/hasOwn distinguish.

nodes.label: Hole-skipping array methods
nodes.rationale: forEach map filter some every reduce skip holes. for-of spread Array.from find includes join sort treat holes as undefined.

nodes.label: includes vs indexOf on holes
nodes.rationale: includes(undefined) is true on a hole; indexOf(undefined) is -1 because indexOf skips holes.

nodes.label: Array.from
nodes.rationale: Accepts iterables and array-likes; never sparse; optional mapFn maps during construction with only (element, index).

nodes.label: Array.of
nodes.rationale: Always treats arguments as elements, unlike new Array(n) which is a length.

nodes.label: Array constructor holes
nodes.rationale: One numeric argument is a length of holes; any other count is elements. new Array(n).map skips holes.

nodes.label: Array-like vs iterable
nodes.rationale: Array-likes have length and indices but no Symbol.iterator. Spread throws; Array.from works.

nodes.label: Iteration callback arity
nodes.rationale: Callbacks receive (element, index, array). Most methods take thisArg; reduce and sort do not.

nodes.label: map(parseInt) radix trap
nodes.rationale: map passes index as parseInt radix, so ["1","2","3"].map(parseInt) is [1, NaN, NaN].

nodes.label: forEach async trap
nodes.rationale: forEach does not wait for promises. async callbacks are discarded; filter(async) keeps everything because promises are truthy.

nodes.label: find visits holes
nodes.rationale: find/findIndex visit every index treating holes as undefined; forEach/map/filter/every skip holes.

nodes.label: Mutation during iteration
nodes.rationale: Visit range is fixed first. Appends are skipped; removals skip the next item. Do not mutate the array being iterated.

nodes.label: Array.prototype.forEach
nodes.rationale: Always returns undefined and cannot break except by throwing. Wrong tool for early exit or await.

nodes.label: Array.prototype.map
nodes.rationale: Allocates a same-length array of return values. Not a loop for side effects.

nodes.label: Array.prototype.filter
nodes.rationale: New array of all matches after a full pass. filter(...)[0] is a misuse of find.

nodes.label: Array.prototype.find
nodes.rationale: First match or undefined; stops early. findIndex returns -1; never truthiness-check the index.

nodes.label: every vacuous truth
nodes.rationale: every([]) is true; some([]) is false. Gates need length > 0 && every(...).

nodes.label: JSON.parse
nodes.rationale: Invalid JSON throws SyntaxError. Trailing commas and single quotes are illegal. Empty body throws.

nodes.label: JSON.parse reviver
nodes.rationale: Transforms parsed values depth-first, children first, root last under key "". Must return value or the property is deleted.

nodes.label: reviver context.source
nodes.rationale: Primitives only. Original JSON text before double rounding. Use to rebuild BigInt IDs past MAX_SAFE_INTEGER.

nodes.label: JSON __proto__ is ordinary
nodes.rationale: JSON.parse treats __proto__ as an own property. Pollution comes from a later merge assigning through it.

nodes.label: JSON.stringify
nodes.rationale: Lossy and silent except BigInt and cycles, which throw. Sees own enumerable string keys like Object.keys.

nodes.label: JSON.stringify silent drops
nodes.rationale: undefined/functions/symbols omitted in objects and null in arrays; NaN/Infinity become null; Map/Set become {}.

nodes.label: toJSON hook
nodes.rationale: Serialiser uses toJSON's return value. Date uses it (ISO string). Cleanest per-type control.

nodes.label: JSON.stringify replacer
nodes.rationale: Function redacts (undefined omits); array is a deny-by-default key allowlist. Symbol keys cannot be re-included.

nodes.label: Map does not serialise
nodes.rationale: JSON.stringify(map) is {}. Convert with fromEntries (string keys only) or JSON.stringify([...map]) to keep key types.

nodes.label: Map when keys are data
nodes.rationale: Use Map when keys come from data; use an object when keys are a small fixed set you wrote. JSON edges stay objects.

nodes.label: Map.groupBy vs Object.groupBy
nodes.rationale: Prefer Map.groupBy: any key type and insertion order. Object.groupBy stringifies and re-sorts integer-like keys.

nodes.label: WeakMap weak keys
nodes.rationale: Keys must be objects; entries are collectable. Not iterable, no size. A strong Map here leaks memory.

nodes.label: Six Map vs Object differences
nodes.rationale: Accidental prototype keys, any key type, insertion order, size property, direct iteration, frequent add/remove.

nodes.label: Map SameValueZero
nodes.rationale: Like === except NaN equals NaN and 0 equals -0. Same algorithm as Set and Array.prototype.includes.

nodes.label: Map
nodes.rationale: set returns the map for chaining and reduce. delete returns whether the key existed.

nodes.label: Array.prototype.reduce
nodes.rationale: Callback is (acc, cur, index, array). Second argument is initialValue, so no thisArg. Equivalent to a for-of fold.

nodes.label: reduce initialValue
nodes.rationale: Without it the first element is the acc, iteration starts at 1, empty throws TypeError, single element skips the callback.

nodes.label: Array.prototype.reduceRight
nodes.rationale: Needed only when the operation is not associative — compose, string building, nested wrapping.

nodes.label: reduce pipe and asyncPipe
nodes.rationale: Fold over functions: pipe applies each; asyncPipe sequences via acc.then(fn).

nodes.label: reduce spread O(N²) anti-pattern
nodes.rationale: Spreading the accumulator each step copies N²/2 keys. Mutate the private acc or use a for-of loop.

nodes.label: Named methods instead of reduce
nodes.rationale: flat, groupBy, flatMap, Set dedupe, find, filter. Grouping is the most common legitimate-looking misuse.

nodes.label: reduce readability rule
nodes.rationale: Scalar folds and folds over functions are clear. A growing-collection reduce is usually a loop or groupBy.

nodes.label: sort mutates in place
nodes.rationale: sort returns the same array reference. const sorted = arr.sort() is not a copy.

nodes.label: ES2019 stable sort
nodes.rationale: Equal elements keep relative order. Enables two-pass multi-column sorts. Before ES2019 stability was engine-dependent.

nodes.label: Array.prototype.toSorted
nodes.rationale: ES2023 non-mutating sort; returns a shallow-copied dense sorted array.

nodes.label: ES2023 non-mutating array family
nodes.rationale: toSorted, toReversed, toSpliced, with. All return a new dense array and leave the original alone.

nodes.label: undefined and holes sort last
nodes.rationale: undefined then holes always go to the end; the comparator is never called for them.

nodes.label: Default sort is string sort
nodes.rationale: Converts to strings and compares UTF-16 code units, so [1,30,4,21,100000] becomes [1,100000,21,30,4].

nodes.label: sort comparator contract
nodes.rationale: Negative before, positive after, zero or NaN equal. Only the sign matters, so a-b works for numbers.

nodes.label: Five comparator consistency rules
nodes.rationale: Pure, stable, reflexive, anti-symmetric, transitive. Violations do not throw; order is implementation-defined.

nodes.label: Fisher-Yates shuffle
nodes.rationale: sort(() => Math.random()-0.5) breaks every consistency rule. Use Fisher-Yates.

nodes.label: Decorate-sort-undecorate
nodes.rationale: Map to {item,key}, sort on key, map back. Avoids O(n log n) key recomputation and unstable computed keys.

nodes.label: String.prototype.slice
nodes.rationale: Negatives count from the end; start>end yields "". Matches Array.prototype.slice. Prefer over substring.

nodes.label: String.prototype.substring
nodes.rationale: Negatives become 0; start>end swaps arguments and hides bugs.
