nodes.label: String.prototype.at
nodes.rationale: Accepts negative indices; brackets do not. Out of range is undefined; charAt returns "".

nodes.label: String.prototype.split
nodes.rationale: No separator yields [whole]. "".split(",") is [""] not []. limit truncates and discards the rest.

nodes.label: Code units vs code points
nodes.rationale: split("") and length are UTF-16 code units; spread and Array.from yield code points. Intl.Segmenter for graphemes.

nodes.label: String trim family
nodes.rationale: trim/trimStart/trimEnd remove whitespace only; no trim(char). Use at the input boundary.

nodes.label: padStart target length
nodes.rationale: First arg is total length, not pad count. Never truncates. Multi-char pads repeat then cut.

nodes.label: String.prototype.replace
nodes.rationale: With a string pattern replaces only the first match.

nodes.label: String.prototype.replaceAll
nodes.rationale: Replaces all. Regex must be global or TypeError. String patterns are literal — safer than RegExp(userInput).

nodes.label: Replacement $ patterns
nodes.rationale: $& $` $' $1 $<name> $$ are special. Use the function form so dynamic replacements stay literal.

nodes.label: Destructuring
nodes.rationale: Array patterns match by position; object patterns match by name. Defaults apply to undefined, not null.

nodes.label: Three destructuring traps
nodes.rationale: null bypasses defaults; function f({a}){} throws without = {}; destructuring methods detaches this.

nodes.label: for...of
nodes.rationale: Iterates values via Symbol.iterator. Supports break and await. Default for values.

nodes.label: for...in
nodes.rationale: Iterates keys including inherited. Almost never for arrays: string indices, non-index keys, skips holes.

nodes.label: forEach cannot break or await
nodes.rationale: return inside forEach returns from the callback only. forEach(async) discards promises.

nodes.label: Spread two operations
nodes.rationale: Array/arg spread needs an iterable; object spread copies own enumerable properties. [...obj] throws; {...arr} works; {...map} is {}.

nodes.label: Spread argument RangeError
nodes.rationale: Math.max(...huge) or push(...huge) can exceed the engine argument limit.

nodes.label: Spread-in-loop is quadratic
nodes.rationale: out = [...out, x] each iteration copies the growing array. Quadratic by construction.

nodes.label: Options object parameters
nodes.rationale: Named, order-independent args. Cost is one allocation. Worth it past two or three parameters.

nodes.label: Destructured param = {}
nodes.rationale: function f({a} = {}) so a missing argument is not TypeError on undefined.

nodes.label: Destructuring detaches this
nodes.rationale: const {start} = timer is assignment; start() loses this. APIs meant to be destructured return closures.

nodes.label: Destructuring and fn.length
nodes.rationale: A destructured parameter counts as 1; a default stops the count, so ({a}={}) => {} has length 0.

nodes.label: Destructuring
nodes.rationale: Pattern-matching on the left-hand side of an assignment: the shape of the expected value becomes bindings.

nodes.label: Array vs object destructuring
nodes.rationale: Array destructuring matches by position; object destructuring matches by name. Array elements cannot be renamed; object properties can.

nodes.label: Destructuring defaults apply to undefined only
nodes.rationale: Defaults fire only when the value is undefined, not null. JSON payloads use null for missing, so defaults are routinely bypassed.

nodes.label: Nested destructuring
nodes.rationale: Intermediate names are paths, not bindings. Nesting throws when an intermediate is missing; default each risky level or use optional chaining.

nodes.label: Object rest omit-a-key
nodes.rationale: Rest must be last. Object rest is the idiomatic omit-a-key, better than delete: new object, stable shape, no mutation. Shallow; own enumerable only.

nodes.label: Destructuring swap idiom
nodes.rationale: The RHS array is fully evaluated before assignment, so [a, b] = [b, a] needs no temporary.

nodes.label: Parentheses for object assignment
nodes.rationale: A statement starting with { is a block. Assigning without declaring needs ({ a, b } = obj). Arrays have no such problem.

nodes.label: Destructuring null or undefined throws
nodes.rationale: Throws even with empty patterns. Guard with ?? {} or a = {} parameter default. Other values coerce to objects.

nodes.label: for...in
nodes.rationale: Iterates enumerable string keys including inherited prototype properties. Almost never the right loop.

nodes.label: for...of
nodes.rationale: Iterates values via Symbol.iterator. Works on arrays, strings (code points), Map, Set, NodeList, generators. Not plain objects.

nodes.label: Array.prototype.forEach
nodes.rationale: Iterates values with numeric index. Skips holes, cannot break, does not await, returns undefined.

nodes.label: Object.entries as iterable adapter
nodes.rationale: Plain objects are records, not sequences. Object.entries/keys state which view you want; for...of then consumes that iterable.

nodes.label: Never for...in on arrays
nodes.rationale: Index arrives as a string, non-index properties are included, and property enumeration skips holes while for...of visits them as undefined.

nodes.label: Loop capability table
nodes.rationale: If the body needs break, continue, return from the enclosing function, or await, forEach and array methods are out. MDN: no way to stop forEach except throwing.

nodes.label: return inside forEach is continue
nodes.rationale: return exits the callback only. The enclosing function always continues — a silent compile-clean bug. Use find or for...of.

nodes.label: await only works in a real loop
nodes.rationale: forEach discards async callback promises: work is not awaited and rejections are unhandled. for...of+await is sequential; Promise.all+map is concurrent.

nodes.label: Sequential for...of vs Promise.all
nodes.rationale: for...of+await when operations depend on each other or the target cannot take parallel load. Promise.all starts every request at once.

nodes.label: Labeled break for nested loops
nodes.rationale: break/continue accept a label to exit two loops. Only works with real loops, not forEach. Extracting to a function and return is often cleaner.

nodes.label: for...of live iterator vs forEach snapshot
nodes.rationale: forEach fixes its range before the first callback. for...of re-reads length, so push during iteration over the same array is an infinite loop.

nodes.label: Array and call spread
nodes.rationale: In array literals and argument lists, ... consumes an iterable via Symbol.iterator. Plain objects throw TypeError.

nodes.label: Object spread
nodes.rationale: Copies own enumerable properties. Does not need an iterable. Spreading a Map/Set/Date/class instance yields {} or method-less objects.

nodes.label: Spread vs rest
nodes.rationale: Same three dots, opposite directions. Rest collects on the left or in parameters (must be last, only one). Spread expands on the right or in a call.

nodes.label: Spread is shallow
nodes.rationale: MDN: multidimensional arrays are not safe to copy with spread. Use structuredClone for a genuinely independent graph; shallow is usually the right default.

nodes.label: Conditional object-spread no-op
nodes.rationale: Spreading a non-object into an object is silently a no-op, which makes ...(cond && { key }) work.

nodes.label: Spread replaces apply
nodes.rationale: f(...args) does what f.apply(null, args) did, composes with fixed args and new. apply remains only for setting this.

nodes.label: Spread argument-count limit
nodes.rationale: Spreading a large array into a call can RangeError. Use reduce for max, loop or concat for append.

nodes.label: Later-wins object merge
nodes.rationale: { ...defaults, ...overrides } is replace, not deep merge. A later spread after an explicit key overrides it.

nodes.label: Immutable spread updates
nodes.rationale: Copies only the changed level and shares untouched branches — what makes prev.items === next.items a valid change check.

nodes.label: Quadratic spread-in-loop
nodes.rationale: out = [...out, x] copies the accumulated array each iteration. Use map or push.

nodes.label: Array.from vs spread
nodes.rationale: Array.from accepts array-likes without iterators, maps while converting, and builds n slots. Spread is shorter when an iterator exists.

nodes.label: Run-to-completion
nodes.rationale: Whenever a function runs it cannot be preempted. Explains both why JS needs no locks and why a 200 ms loop freezes everything.

nodes.label: Single-threaded code, concurrent platform
nodes.rationale: Your JavaScript is one thread; fetch, timers, and workers are not. await suspends the function, not the thread.

nodes.label: The event loop
nodes.rationale: An agent maintains a heap, a stack of execution contexts, and a queue of jobs. The loop pulls one job, runs it to completion, pulls the next.

nodes.label: Job complete when stack empty
nodes.rationale: MDN: a job is considered completed when the stack is empty. Explains why try/catch cannot reach a later callback.

nodes.label: Microtasks vs macrotasks
nodes.rationale: Two queues; microtasks have absolute priority. A task runs one job; a microtask drain runs every microtask including ones queued during the drain.

nodes.label: Promise
nodes.rationale: A state machine that runs forwards exactly once. An object representing eventual completion or failure; you attach callbacks instead of passing them in.

nodes.label: Promise three states
nodes.rationale: pending / fulfilled / rejected. Transition is one-shot and irreversible. Resolved is not fulfilled — a resolved promise can still be pending.

nodes.label: Callback
nodes.rationale: A function passed into another function as an argument, invoked to complete a routine. Says nothing about timing.

nodes.label: Promise chaining
nodes.rationale: then returns a new promise representing the previous step and your handler. Flat chains follow from that plus adoption.

nodes.label: Tasks vs microtasks
nodes.rationale: Tasks: setTimeout, setInterval, event dispatch, initial script — one per turn. Microtasks: then/catch/finally, await continuations, queueMicrotask, MutationObserver — all of them after the current task.

nodes.label: Microtask drain until empty
nodes.rationale: After each task the loop runs all microtasks, including those queued during the drain, until the queue is empty.

nodes.label: Microtask starvation
nodes.rationale: A self-re-arming microtask chain never returns to the task queue — no timers, events, or rendering. A recursive setTimeout yields; a recursive then does not.

nodes.label: Rendering between tasks
nodes.rationale: The browser schedules rendering between tasks after the microtask queue is empty. await null cannot yield to paint; await setTimeout(0) or scheduler.yield() can.

nodes.label: 1, 4, 3, 2 ordering
nodes.rationale: Synchronous first, then the entire microtask queue, then one task. Nested timers drain their microtasks before the next timer task.

nodes.label: Node nextTick and setImmediate
nodes.rationale: process.nextTick drains before the promise microtask queue; setImmediate is a check-phase task. Relative setTimeout(0) vs setImmediate is context-dependent.

nodes.label: async always returns a promise
nodes.rationale: No path out of an async function is not a promise. A return fulfils, a throw rejects, a returned promise is adopted.

nodes.label: async never throws synchronously
nodes.rationale: A throw anywhere, including before the first await, becomes a rejection. try { asyncFn() } without await catches nothing.

nodes.label: async return vs Promise.resolve identity
nodes.rationale: Promise.resolve(p) returns the same native promise. An async function must create its own and resolve it with p, so references differ.

nodes.label: async/await desugars to then
nodes.rationale: await 1 becomes Promise.resolve(1).then(continuation). Semantics equal a chain; the gain is try/catch, loops, if/else, and locals in one scope.

nodes.label: Exactly where await suspends
nodes.rationale: Top-level code up to and including the first await runs synchronously. At await, control exits and returns to the caller.

nodes.label: Awaited expression runs immediately
nodes.rationale: await fetch(url) starts the request now; only the waiting is deferred. Starting several calls then awaiting them is concurrency.

nodes.label: await always costs one tick
nodes.rationale: Even an already-fulfilled promise or await null still pauses until the next microtask. No fast path.

nodes.label: Top-level await
nodes.rationale: Allowed in modules only, not CommonJS. Delays evaluation of every importing module; reserve for genuine initialisation.

nodes.label: await assimilates thenables
nodes.rationale: await cares about the then shape, not the class. An object with an unrelated then field is assimilated.

nodes.label: Three-pass async ordering method
nodes.rationale: Pass 1 walk the synchronous path to each first await. Pass 2 drain microtasks (re-queue at each await). Pass 3 run one task and repeat.

nodes.label: await does not block the thread
nodes.rationale: await suspends the function, not the thread. A hot loop after an await still freezes everything — run-to-completion applies to continuations.

nodes.label: await in a for loop is sequential
nodes.rationale: Each iteration waits for the previous. Correct when steps depend on each other; a waterfall when independent.

nodes.label: await inside forEach is ignored
nodes.rationale: forEach discards the callback return, so promises are never awaited and rejections float. Use for...of or Promise.all(map).

nodes.label: Two async functions interleave
nodes.rationale: Both run synchronously to their first await, then resume in queue order. Concurrency without parallelism.

nodes.label: Callbacks are not inherently async
nodes.rationale: map's callback and readFile's callback are the same construct. Only the callee's documentation tells you the timing.

nodes.label: When a callback is still the right tool
nodes.rationale: Synchronous work, many-shot events, and pure scheduling. Promises are one-shot and cannot model a stream of events.

nodes.label: Error-first callback convention
nodes.rationale: An async callback cannot throw — the stack is gone — so the error travels as data in argument zero. On success the first argument is null, not omitted.

nodes.label: Missing return after if (err)
nodes.rationale: An if does not end the block the way catch does. Fall-through starts the success path with undefined and the stack points at the wrong function.

nodes.label: try/catch cannot reach an async callback
nodes.rationale: The try finishes when the callee returns. The callback runs later on a fresh stack. Put try inside the callback and route errors as cb(err).

nodes.label: Zalgo sometimes-async callback
nodes.rationale: A function that calls its callback synchronously on some paths and asynchronously on others. Defer the fast path with queueMicrotask.

nodes.label: Call the callback exactly once
nodes.rationale: Every exit path must invoke the callback once. A guard that returns without calling back hangs forever with no object left behind.

nodes.label: Inversion of control
nodes.rationale: You hand the rest of your program to someone else's function. They decide when, how often, and with what arguments it runs. Failures are silent.

nodes.label: Callback trust-table failures
nodes.rationale: Too early (Zalgo), too late, never, twice, wrong arguments, swallowed throw. None produce an exception.

nodes.label: once wrapper
nodes.rationale: A called flag that ignores a second invocation. Exactly what a promise provides structurally by settling once.

nodes.label: MDN three promise guarantees
nodes.rationale: Never invoked before the current event-loop run completes; invoked even if attached after settling; multiple then handlers in insertion order.

nodes.label: Callback hell
nodes.rationale: Nesting is forced because a callback has no return value to sequence on. The real cost is per-level error handling, not indentation.

nodes.label: Named functions do not fix callback hell
nodes.rationale: Hoisting removes indentation and nothing else: sequence becomes invisible, closures are lost, per-level if(err) remains, trust bugs remain.

nodes.label: Promise as the return-value fix
nodes.rationale: A real fix must give the operation a return value representing the eventual result so steps sequence by return rather than by call.

nodes.label: then returns a new promise
nodes.rationale: Each link represents the previous step and this handler. Combined with adoption, each result becomes the next argument at the same level.

nodes.label: Floating promise
nodes.rationale: A started promise that was not returned. Sequencing breaks (next handler gets undefined immediately) and its rejection cannot reach the chain catch.

nodes.label: Always return the promise
nodes.rationale: MDN's most consequential chaining rule. Prefer concise arrow bodies so a missing return is impossible.

nodes.label: A chain is strictly sequential
nodes.rationale: Each link waits for the previous. Independent work belongs in Promise.all and friends. Chaining independent requests is an accidental waterfall.

nodes.label: reduce-over-then sequencing
nodes.rationale: [f1,f2,f3].reduce((p,f) => p.then(f), Promise.resolve()) runs an unknown number of dependent steps in order.

nodes.label: Default thrower error propagation
nodes.rationale: There is no special skip-to-catch rule. Each then without onRejected uses (x) => { throw x; }, so a rejection walks link by link.

nodes.label: .then(f, g) vs .then(f).catch(g)
nodes.rationale: Two-argument then handles only upstream rejections. A throw in f rejects the next promise and is not caught by g. Trailing catch catches both.

nodes.label: Handling restores the chain
nodes.rationale: After a catch the chain is fulfilled. Later then runs on both success and recovered-failure paths. Re-throw to stop.

nodes.label: Nest then to scope a catch
nodes.rationale: A nested catch only sees its scope. The pattern for letting optional steps fail while a critical failure still reaches the outer handler.

nodes.label: Chains catch programming errors
nodes.rationale: A TypeError in a handler lands in the same catch as a network failure. In the callback pyramid it would escape to uncaughtException.

nodes.label: finally is a link, not a clause
nodes.rationale: finally attaches to the promise immediately before it. It is transparent and does not mark a rejection handled. A chain ending in finally still reports unhandled rejection.

nodes.label: Promise executor is synchronous
nodes.rationale: new Promise(fn) calls fn immediately on the current stack. Wrapping slow work in a promise does not offload it.

nodes.label: Each chain link costs a microtask
nodes.rationale: Handlers always run asynchronously even when already settled. A hundred-link chain of sync handlers freezes the frame; yield a task to paint.

nodes.label: queueMicrotask
nodes.rationale: Runs after the current JS execution context exits but before event handlers, timeouts, or other callbacks. Prefer it over Promise.resolve().then when you only want scheduling: no promise allocation, and exceptions surface as uncaught errors.

nodes.label: Sometimes-async / Releasing Zalgo
nodes.rationale: A function that is synchronous on a cache hit and asynchronous on a miss fires events before the caller can attach a listener. A function should be always-async or never-async, never sometimes.

nodes.label: Batching within one event-loop turn
nodes.rationale: The length===1 check schedules one queueMicrotask flush; later calls in the same turn join the array. Microtasks run after all synchronous code and before rendering, so the batch is complete and nothing paints twice.

nodes.label: Microtask try/catch gap
nodes.rationale: A surrounding try/catch only guards the synchronous act of scheduling. Handle errors inside the callback.

nodes.label: Promise
nodes.rationale: An object representing eventual completion or failure. You attach callbacks to the returned object instead of passing them into a function.

nodes.label: Resolved
nodes.rationale: Resolved describes the decision, not the outcome. resolve(anotherPromise) locks onto the inner promise immediately while leaving the outer pending.

nodes.label: One-shot promise state machine
nodes.rationale: The transition happens at most once and is irreversible. That is why a promise cannot model a stream of events.

nodes.label: Thenable
nodes.rationale: The language asks whether an object has a callable then, not whether it is a native Promise. An unrelated then field gets assimilated.

nodes.label: Promise state is not readable
nodes.rationale: No promise.state or promise.value. A synchronous isSettled() would reintroduce Zalgo.

nodes.label: Promise.prototype.then
nodes.rationale: Returns a new promise that is always pending when returned. The handler always runs asynchronously, even if the current promise is already settled.

nodes.label: Identity and thrower default handlers
nodes.rationale: A missing onFulfilled is (x)=>x; a missing onRejected is (x)=>{throw x}. Error propagation is just the default thrower, one link at a time.

nodes.label: Promise.prototype.catch
nodes.rationale: Shortcut for then(undefined, onRejected). A catch that returns normally restores the chain to fulfilled.

nodes.label: Promise.prototype.finally
nodes.rationale: Transparent: a return is ignored and the original outcome passes through. A throw or rejected/pending return still replaces the outcome.

nodes.label: Executor throws catch cannot see
nodes.rationale: Only a synchronous throw during the executor becomes a rejection. Async throws and throws after resolve() are not converted.

nodes.label: Returning a value vs a promise
Promise adoption / flattening
nodes.rationale: Return a plain value and it is wrapped. Return a promise or thenable and it is adopted, never nested as Promise<Promise<T>>.

nodes.label: Forgotten return in then
nodes.rationale: A handler that returns nothing fulfils immediately with undefined; the inner promise floats and its rejection is unhandled.

nodes.label: async function adoption
nodes.rationale: return somePromise from an async function does not produce a nested promise. return await p and return p usually behave identically.

nodes.label: One thread, and what runs elsewhere
Run to completion
nodes.rationale: A function cannot be preempted. That is why JS needs no locks, and why a long sync loop freezes rendering.

nodes.label: await does not block the thread
nodes.rationale: await suspends the async function, not the thread. It cannot slice a long synchronous computation.

nodes.label: Web Workers
nodes.rationale: A separate agent with its own thread, heap and event loop. Isolation by structured clone preserves run-to-completion.

nodes.label: Event loop
nodes.rationale: Enables asynchronous programming while remaining single-threaded. An agent has a heap, a stack, and a job queue.

nodes.label: Job complete when stack is empty
nodes.rationale: That is the definition of run-to-completion and why rendering cannot happen until the call stack fully unwinds.

nodes.label: setTimeout delay is a floor
nodes.rationale: setTimeout(fn, 10) means not before 10 ms. The callback also waits for the current job, queued jobs, and the entire microtask queue.

nodes.label: Node vs browser event loop
nodes.rationale: Both drain one job at a time with microtasks before tasks. Node uses libuv phases plus process.nextTick; the browser also schedules rendering.

nodes.label: Phase 18 Building the store front end
nodes.rationale: Framework-free on purpose so a later React break is a named solution, not API surface to memorise.

nodes.label: Phase 7 Asynchronous JavaScript
nodes.rationale: Centre of gravity of the JS syllabus. If only one phase is finished to Master, finish this one.

nodes.label: Phase 8 Modules, errors, memory and the toolchain
Phase 13 Complexity and JavaScript's real costs
Phase 17 Machine coding
nodes.rationale: The brief's custom-functions requirement: bind, debounce, Promise.all and EventEmitter from an empty file.

nodes.label: Phase 11 Network, storage and data transfer
One thread, many I/O
nodes.rationale: A 3-second for-loop stalls every request; a 3-second database query does not.

nodes.label: libuv thread pool
nodes.rationale: Four threads for files, DNS lookups, crypto and zlib. Sockets never touch them.

nodes.label: ESM and CommonJS interop
nodes.rationale: On Node 24, require(esm) works; top-level await is the one hard boundary. require(esm) returns the namespace, so default is at .default.

nodes.label: Phase 2 Async and the event loop
Node event loop phases
nodes.rationale: Six phases in a fixed order, plus nextTick and the microtask queue which are not phases at all.

nodes.label: CPU-bound work in Node
nodes.rationale: Node's one real weakness; the fix is never async.

nodes.label: Buffer
nodes.rationale: Raw bytes outside the V8 heap. subarray shares memory; allocUnsafe can leak a previous request's data.

nodes.label: Stream backpressure
nodes.rationale: write() returning false is the whole protocol. pipeline over pipe because pipe leaks descriptors.

nodes.label: Path traversal
nodes.rationale: join vs resolve is a security boundary. Resolve, check with the separator, then realpath.

nodes.label: Atomic writes
nodes.rationale: Temp file in the same directory, fsync, rename. Skip the same-directory step and you get EXDEV.

nodes.label: Graceful shutdown
nodes.rationale: server.close() alone hangs forever. Sweep idle connections and force at the deadline.

nodes.label: Event loop lag
nodes.rationale: Idle p50 is the resolution; max is the smoke alarm.

nodes.label: PID 1 and signals
nodes.rationale: npm start as PID 1 swallows SIGTERM.

nodes.label: node:vm is not a security sandbox
FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED job queue
nodes.rationale: 20 jobs, 3 workers, 20 unique claims and no double delivery.

nodes.label: Transactional outbox
nodes.rationale: The order committed and nothing was ever enqueued. One transaction fixes it.

nodes.label: Job idempotency
nodes.rationale: Run twice: 2 emails, or 1 and a rowCount of 0.

nodes.label: Backoff and jitter
nodes.rationale: Without jitter all 500 clients retried in one 100 ms bucket.

nodes.label: Timeout budgets
nodes.rationale: fetch has no timeout. A 500 ms budget gave the second call 300 ms, not a fresh 500.

nodes.label: Concurrency limiting
nodes.rationale: Promise.all peaked at 200 in-flight; mapLimit(8) at 8.

nodes.label: Graceful worker shutdown
nodes.rationale: SIGTERM finished the job in 2125 ms; SIGKILL left it active with nobody working it.

nodes.label: Dead-letter queues
nodes.rationale: BullMQ has no DLQ — the failed set is a holding area.

nodes.label: Password storage
nodes.rationale: ~422,000 MD5 guesses/sec against about 11 scrypt hashes — and 23 logins/sec the thread pool allows.

nodes.label: Sessions vs JWT
nodes.rationale: The whole trade is revocation against a lookup. Short expiry plus refresh is sessions with extra steps.

nodes.label: SSRF
nodes.rationale: A custom DNS guard is never called for a literal IP.

nodes.label: ReDoS
nodes.rationale: 28 characters bought 3.6 s of CPU, during which a 10 ms interval fired zero times.

nodes.label: Node Permission Model
nodes.rationale: Locked down to one readable directory, the process still opened a TCP connection — there is no --allow-net.

nodes.label: Prototype pollution
nodes.rationale: JSON.parse is innocent; the recursive merge is the bug.

nodes.label: node:test runner
nodes.rationale: *.spec.mjs is not discovered — a suite named that way runs 0 tests and exits 0.

nodes.label: Forgotten await fails the file
nodes.rationale: The test prints ✔ but the runner reports generated asynchronous activity after the test ended, fails the file, and exits 1.

nodes.label: --test-rerun-failures false green
nodes.rationale: The state file replays previous passes; a test edited to throw still printed ✔ (passed on attempt 0) and exited 0.

nodes.label: Contract testing
nodes.rationale: A renamed field caught in 18 ms, in the backend's own suite.

nodes.label: listen(0) for API tests
nodes.rationale: listen(0), or EADDRINUSE with a race deciding which file fails.

nodes.label: V8
nodes.rationale: Google's JavaScript engine: parses, compiles, garbage-collects. The brain.

nodes.label: libuv
nodes.rationale: C library for async I/O: event loop and waiting for files and sockets. The hands.

nodes.label: C++ bindings
nodes.rationale: Glue so fs.readFile in JavaScript calls read() in the OS.

nodes.label: Event loop is the program
nodes.rationale: Your file is the setup for the program. The event loop is the program.

nodes.label: Blocking vs non-blocking
nodes.rationale: Blocking holds the thread until the answer is ready; non-blocking returns immediately.

nodes.label: await yields lock-free safety
nodes.rationale: No locks between callbacks, but a read-modify-write spanning await can interleave.

nodes.label: Network I/O uses kernel readiness
nodes.rationale: Sockets use epoll/kqueue/IOCP with no extra threads.

nodes.label: setImmediate work chunking
nodes.rationale: Yield between chunks so other callbacks can run; total work slightly slower, process stays responsive.

nodes.label: Sync suffix in a request path is a bug
nodes.rationale: Sync is fine at startup before the server listens; in a request handler it stalls everyone.

nodes.label: Four event-loop blocking fixes
nodes.rationale: Async version; chunk with setImmediate; worker_threads; queue out of the request.

nodes.label: UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE
nodes.rationale: Default 4, max 1024. Created lazily; size is fixed after first use. Set in the environment before start.

nodes.label: dns.lookup thread-pool trap
nodes.rationale: dns.lookup calls getaddrinfo and uses the pool; outbound HTTP can starve fs. resolve4 is a real DNS query with no threads.

nodes.label: Thread pool vs worker_threads
nodes.rationale: Pool runs C/C++ ops you never see; worker_threads run JS in their own isolate.

nodes.label: CORS is a browser policy
nodes.rationale: CORS is enforced by the browser, not HTTP. Node and curl ignore it.

nodes.label: Isomorphic / universal code
nodes.rationale: Code written only against the shared standard surface so one module works in both hosts.

nodes.label: setTimeout return type differs
nodes.rationale: Browser returns a number; Node returns a Timeout with ref/unref/refresh.

nodes.label: process.exit vs exitCode
nodes.rationale: exit() abandons pending work including buffered stdout; exitCode lets the loop drain.

nodes.label: __dirname vs process.cwd()
nodes.rationale: __dirname is where the file lives and never changes; cwd is where node was started.

nodes.label: process.env values are strings
nodes.rationale: DEBUG=false is the truthy string 'false'. Convert at the edge.

nodes.label: Active LTS
nodes.rationale: Frozen feature set, actively maintained. Node 24 is Active LTS as of August 2026.

nodes.label: Odd/even LTS rule ending
nodes.rationale: From v27 every annual April major becomes LTS in October. Node 26 is the last odd/even line.

nodes.label: Pin Node in the repo
nodes.rationale: .nvmrc, engines, pinned Dockerfile tag, CI node-version-file. npm engines is advisory unless engine-strict.

nodes.label: Node flags before the script
nodes.rationale: Everything after the filename is process.argv. A misplaced --watch is silently ignored.

nodes.label: node --env-file
nodes.rationale: Real environment wins; no variable expansion; missing file is a hard error unless --env-file-if-exists.

nodes.label: NODE_OPTIONS
nodes.rationale: --eval, --print, --test, --env-file are forbidden so an inherited env cannot hijack every process.

nodes.label: Deno
nodes.rationale: Secure by default, TypeScript first-class. Deno 2 added npm, package.json and node_modules.

nodes.label: Bun
nodes.rationale: JavaScriptCore + Zig. Runtime, package manager, bundler and test runner in one binary.

nodes.label: Choose Node for production apps
nodes.rationale: Ecosystem completeness and operational maturity beat hello-world throughput. Most apps are bound by the database.

nodes.label: V8 four-tier compilation
nodes.rationale: Ignition → Sparkplug → Maglev → TurboFan. Fast to start, slow to optimise.

nodes.label: Hidden classes
nodes.rationale: Objects with the same properties in the same order share a shape so V8 can cache offsets.

nodes.label: CommonJS require and the module cache
CommonJS module wrapper
nodes.rationale: Node wraps each file in a function(exports, require, module, __filename, __dirname).

nodes.label: module.exports vs exports
nodes.rationale: exports is a local alias. Assigning to exports severs the link; require returns module.exports.

nodes.label: require.cache
nodes.rationale: A module runs once per resolved path. Core modules are not in the cache.

nodes.label: require is synchronous
nodes.rationale: Reads and compiles on the main thread. Fine at startup; a latency spike in a handler.

nodes.label: ESM live bindings
nodes.rationale: An import is a view onto the exporter's variable, read-only from the importer.

nodes.label: Top-level await
nodes.rationale: Importers wait for it transitively; it makes the module un-require()-able (ERR_REQUIRE_ASYNC_MODULE).

nodes.label: ESM requires file extensions
nodes.rationale: ESM does not probe .js / index.js. ./math and ./math.js are different requests.

nodes.label: Prefix-only builtins
nodes.rationale: node:sea, node:sqlite, node:test, node:test/reporters have no bare alias; require('test') loads npm.

nodes.label: cjs-module-lexer named exports
nodes.rationale: Static analysis of CJS source synthesises named exports; computed keys are invisible.

nodes.label: require() of ESM
nodes.rationale: Stable in Node 24. Returns the namespace object; default is at .default. Fails on TLA.

nodes.label: Dual package hazard
nodes.rationale: Separate CJS and ESM builds can load twice; module-scope state exists twice.

nodes.label: JSON import attribute
nodes.rationale: import data from './x.json' with { type: 'json' }. Prevents substituting executable JS.

nodes.label: CJS probes, ESM does not
nodes.rationale: CJS adds .js/.json/.node and index.js; ESM fails with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND or ERR_UNSUPPORTED_DIR_IMPORT.

nodes.label: package.json type field
nodes.rationale: Nearest package.json decides .js parse mode. .mjs always ESM, .cjs always CJS.

nodes.label: Hoisted undeclared dependencies
nodes.rationale: npm flattens so require('lodash') can find a transitive copy until that dependent drops it.

nodes.label: CJS partial exports on cycle
nodes.rationale: Node returns the half-built module.exports. Assigned-before-require is visible; after is undefined.

nodes.label: ESM TDZ on cycle
nodes.rationale: Bindings exist but const/let values are in the TDZ. Loud ReferenceError instead of silent undefined.

nodes.label: Extract shared module to break cycles
Conditional exports
nodes.rationale: First matching key wins. types first, default last.

nodes.label: Subpath imports #internal
nodes.rationale: Private aliases inside the package. # prefix cannot collide with npm.

nodes.label: ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED
nodes.rationale: Once exports exists it is exhaustive, including the real file path.

nodes.label: enableCompileCache
nodes.rationale: Persists V8 compilation to disk. Call first, or set NODE_COMPILE_CACHE. Keyed by Node version and arch.

nodes.label: module.register hooks
nodes.rationale: resolve and load hooks on a separate thread. Register before the target is imported.

nodes.label: dependencies vs devDependencies
nodes.rationale: Does the running application import it? Production uses --omit=dev.

nodes.label: npx
nodes.rationale: Local .bin first, else download and execute. A typo'd name is an attack vector.

nodes.label: package.json type field
nodes.rationale: Most consequential field: decides how every .js file is parsed. Absent type triggers MODULE_TYPELESS_PACKAGE_JSON and a reparse cost. Set explicitly; type is scoped to the nearest package.json.

nodes.label: main vs exports
nodes.rationale: main is the old single entry; exports takes precedence, supports subpaths and conditions, and blocks unlisted deep imports.

nodes.label: package.json scripts
nodes.rationale: Scripts prepend node_modules/.bin to PATH. Avoid pre/post hooks because they run implicitly; postinstall is a supply-chain risk.

nodes.label: node --run
nodes.rationale: Minimal script runner: no pre/post scripts, no .npmrc, faster startup; use npm run when a script needs npm's environment.

nodes.label: package.json engines
nodes.rationale: Declaration not enforcement unless engine-strict=true. State a floor not a ceiling so future Node majors are not locked out.

nodes.label: package.json files allowlist
nodes.rationale: Without files, npm publishes almost everything. README, LICENSE and package.json always ship; node_modules never does. Verify with npm pack --dry-run.

nodes.label: dependencies vs devDependencies vs peerDependencies
nodes.rationale: dependencies ship to consumers; devDependencies are omitted in production; peerDependencies expect the host to provide the package so plugins do not duplicate a framework.

nodes.label: postinstall scripts
nodes.rationale: Run automatically on every install of the package — debugging surprise and supply-chain risk. Prefer an explicit user-run script.

nodes.label: node_modules hoisting
nodes.rationale: npm and yarn flatten transitive deps into top-level node_modules so duplicates collapse; that is how undeclared imports can accidentally resolve.

nodes.label: phantom dependencies
nodes.rationale: A package your code imports without declaring it because hoisting put it at top-level. Breaks when the real dependent drops it.

nodes.label: pnpm content-addressable store
nodes.rationale: One copy per version in a global store; node_modules is symlinks exposing only declared deps. Undeclared require fails immediately; disk is shared across projects.

nodes.label: Corepack
nodes.rationale: Pins package manager version via packageManager field. Ships with Node but must be enabled once per machine.

nodes.label: npm workspaces
nodes.rationale: One install and one lockfile; local packages are symlinked. Do not give build orchestration. Root needs private:true to block accidental publish.

nodes.label: scoped package names
nodes.rationale: Scoped packages default to private (paid). Public publish needs --access public or publishConfig.access. Forgetting this is the common first-publish failure.

nodes.label: npm pack dry-run
nodes.rationale: Only way to see the tarball contents before publish. Catch secrets going out and needed files staying home. Then install the tgz as a consumer smoke test.

nodes.label: npm version
nodes.rationale: Edits package.json, commits and tags. Refuses a dirty tree. A published version is permanent; unpublish is 72 hours and unused only.

nodes.label: npm deprecate
nodes.rationale: Realistic recovery from a bad release: deprecate plus a new version. Treat every publish as permanent.

nodes.label: npm publish --provenance
nodes.rationale: CI-only signed attestation linking the tarball to commit and workflow. Meaningful because no human laptop was involved.

nodes.label: npm dist-tags
nodes.rationale: Pre-releases need --tag so they do not become latest. Without it every plain npm install gets the beta.

nodes.label: dual CJS/ESM packages
nodes.rationale: ESM-only is the default now that require(esm) works on Node 22.12+/24.15. Shipping both costs the dual-package hazard of two copies of module state.

nodes.label: semantic versioning
nodes.rationale: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH records maintainer intent, not a guarantee. A patch that fixes a bug your code depended on is still a break. 0.x anything may break; ^0.3.1 allows only 0.3.x.

nodes.label: caret and tilde ranges
nodes.rationale: ^1.2.3 allows <2.0.0; ~1.2.3 allows <1.3.0. ^ is npm default so package.json does not describe what you are running.

nodes.label: package-lock.json
nodes.rationale: Records exact version, resolved URL and integrity hash for the whole tree. Commit it always including for libraries; consumers ignore it and use their own lockfile.

nodes.label: lockfile integrity hash
nodes.rationale: Makes install verifiable not just reproducible. A tampered tarball fails even if the version number matches.

nodes.label: npm ci
nodes.rationale: Installs the lockfile exactly, deletes node_modules first, never writes the lockfile, fails if package.json and lock disagree. Use in CI, Docker, production.

nodes.label: package.json overrides
nodes.rationale: Force a nested dependency version when the parent has not updated. You override the parent's declared compatibility — verify it works.

nodes.label: Node type stripping
nodes.rationale: Default since v23.6.0, Stability 2 as of v24.12.0. Replaces type annotations with whitespace so stack traces stay correct. Never type-checks.

nodes.label: erasable TypeScript syntax
nodes.rationale: Annotations, interface, type, generics, import type erase cleanly. enum, runtime namespace, parameter properties must generate JS and throw ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX in strip-only mode.

nodes.label: tsc --noEmit
nodes.rationale: Native .ts execution removes the build, not the check. Dropping tsc --noEmit from CI silently switches to decorative annotations.

nodes.label: ERR_UNSUPPORTED_NODE_MODULES_TYPE_STRIPPING
nodes.rationale: Node refuses to strip types inside node_modules so published packages must ship JS plus .d.ts. Bounds startup cost.

nodes.label: TypeScript import specifiers
nodes.rationale: Running .ts directly requires importing ./helper.ts. The tsc convention of importing ./helper.js assumes you compile first. Mixing them fails under one of the two commands.

nodes.label: autocannon HTTP load
nodes.rationale: Right tool when the claim is about the running service: RPS plus p50/p95/p99, error rate, and server saturation under concurrency.

nodes.label: microbenchmarks
nodes.rationale: Lie because V8 over-optimizes monomorphic toys, DCE can erase unused work, and a 3 ns win does not move p99 when the DB takes 40 ms. Consume results into a sink.

nodes.label: TTL and write-path invalidation
nodes.rationale: TTL bounds how wrong you can be; it is not the only invalidation. Delete or overwrite on write when updates must show sooner. Pick TTLs from product tolerance and origin load.

nodes.label: cache stampede
nodes.rationale: Many concurrent misses on one expired hot key overload the origin. Mitigate with single-flight, distributed locks, jittered TTLs, or stale-while-revalidate.

nodes.label: single-flight cache fill
nodes.rationale: In-process Map of inflight promises collapses concurrent misses. Does not protect a multi-pod fleet — that needs a distributed lock or soft TTL.

nodes.label: in-process vs Redis cache
nodes.rationale: In-process is fastest and per pod; after scale-out you have N independent caches. Redis is shared, networked, operational. Choose by coherence needs.

nodes.label: unbounded cache leak
nodes.rationale: Module-level Map with no max or TTL. Bound by count and bytes; LRU or Redis maxmemory.

nodes.label: unremoved event listeners
nodes.rationale: Emitter retains the function, which retains its closed-over scope. on/off must share the same function reference.

nodes.label: closure retention of large objects
nodes.rationale: A timer callback that closes over hugeBuffer keeps the allocation alive. Close over the derived scalar instead.

nodes.label: uncleared timers and handles
nodes.rationale: setInterval without clearInterval, plus unclosed servers, Redis clients, and fs.watch keep the process from settling.

nodes.label: AsyncLocalStorage request context
nodes.rationale: Preserves reqId across await without threading an extra argument. Does not cross worker threads or child processes; not a security boundary.

nodes.label: x-request-id header
nodes.rationale: Accept a well-formed incoming id, mint UUID when missing, echo on the response, forward on egress, persist on job payloads. Validate length and charset.

nodes.label: --cpu-prof
nodes.rationale: Samples during the run and writes .cpuprofile on exit. Hard kill (-9) skips flush. Wrong tool when lag is low and you are I/O bound.

nodes.label: --heap-prof
nodes.rationale: Allocation timeline-style profile. For what is retained right now, prefer heap snapshots.

nodes.label: Node Inspector --inspect
nodes.rationale: Live CPU/Memory session without waiting for exit. Exposing --inspect on a public IP is a remote code surface — treat like a root shell.

nodes.label: diagnostics_channel hasSubscribers
nodes.rationale: Performance gate so the hot path stays cheap when nobody is listening. Keep payloads small and immutable.

nodes.label: TracingChannel
nodes.rationale: Request-shaped helper (tracePromise) around a named channel. Many OTel instrumentations subscribe to diagnostics_channel under the hood.

nodes.label: Sentry issue grouping
nodes.rationale: Groups the same crash across events, tracks first/last seen per release, pages on new issues. Complementary to logs and OTel — not a replacement.

nodes.label: error tracker release
nodes.rationale: Usually git SHA. Without it, 'new in this deploy' is guesswork. Load-bearing field on SDK init.

nodes.label: captureException on handled errors
nodes.rationale: If you only hook uncaughtException, production's most common failures — the ones you already catch — never reach the tracker.

nodes.label: monitorEventLoopDelay
nodes.rationale: Histogram values are nanoseconds. Idle p50 sits near the sampling resolution, so do not alert on p50 below that floor. max is the smoke alarm; p99 is the trend.

nodes.label: lag vs I/O wait
nodes.rationale: Downstream API slowness is not loop lag. Sync bcrypt/image resize is. GC thrashing shows as bursty lag. Lag says you are stuck, not why.

nodes.label: bottleneck-first method
nodes.rationale: The bottleneck is the resource that is full. Quantify, check golden signals and loop lag, time dependencies, profile only if CPU/loop is hot, change one thing, remeasure.

nodes.label: low lag high p99
nodes.rationale: Waiting on I/O or a queue, not blocking the event loop. Look at downstream and pool wait times, not a CPU profile.

nodes.label: flame graph width
nodes.rationale: Width is portion of CPU samples in that stack subtree. Will not show await time; empty app frames usually mean I/O bound.

nodes.label: 0x flame graphs
nodes.rationale: Low-ceremony capture plus interactive HTML around the same family of data as --cpu-prof.

nodes.label: Clinic.js
nodes.rationale: Doctor for early triage (CPU vs I/O vs memory); Flame when CPU is already known hot; Bubbleprof for async delay; Heapprofiler for allocation views.

nodes.label: V8 generational GC
nodes.rationale: New objects start young and cheap to scavenge; survivors age into old space where major GC pauses are costlier and show up as loop lag.

nodes.label: --max-old-space-size
nodes.rationale: Old-space budget, not a cgroup RSS limit. Measured 256 MB flag produced ~448 MB heap_size_limit. Too high and the kernel OOMKiller fires first.

nodes.label: latency traffic errors saturation
nodes.rationale: From Google SRE workbook. Node examples: duration histograms, QPS, 5xx ratio, event-loop lag / pool wait / queue depth. Alert on percentiles and error ratio, not averages or raw counts.

nodes.label: Prometheus label cardinality
nodes.rationale: route must be the template (/orders/:id), never raw URL or userId. Identity belongs in logs and traces.

nodes.label: liveness probe
nodes.rationale: Kill me if I am stuck. Must depend on almost nothing. A DB check here turns a dependency blip into a restart storm.

nodes.label: readiness probe
nodes.rationale: Stop sending me traffic if I cannot serve. Allowed to check the pool (select 1, short timeout). Fail first on SIGTERM so the balancer drains before exit.

nodes.label: acceptingTraffic flag
nodes.rationale: Flip true only after config, pools, and listen. Flip false on SIGTERM before closing the server.

nodes.label: v8.writeHeapSnapshot
nodes.rationale: Returns a path to a .heapsnapshot. Diff two snapshots under the same load; sort by retained size growth. Snapshotting is expensive — canary only.

nodes.label: heap retainer path
nodes.rationale: The reference chain to a GC root (module-scope Map, timer, server) is the line of code that should have released the object.

nodes.label: leak vs large cache
nodes.rationale: A cache with a cap is a policy. An unbounded Map is a leak with a product name. Restart 'fixes' heap until the curve returns.

nodes.label: trace vs span
nodes.rationale: A span is one timed operation with attributes and status. A trace is the tree of spans sharing a trace id.

nodes.label: W3C Trace Context
nodes.rationale: traceparent/tracestate is the standardized inter-service join key — the cousin of x-request-id.

nodes.label: trace sampling
nodes.rationale: 100% traces at scale melt the backend. Head-based ratio for cost, always sample errors/slow requests, tail sampling in the collector after duration is known.

nodes.label: performance.now
nodes.rationale: Monotonic high-resolution clock inside the process. Prefer over Date.now() which can step on NTP and produce negative or wild durations.

nodes.label: performance marks and measures
nodes.rationale: Named timestamps and the duration between them. Clear entries in long-lived processes or the buffer grows.

nodes.label: PerformanceObserver
nodes.rationale: Observe entryTypes including gc. Histogram duration and watch multi-ms spikes; do not alert on individual GC entries.

nodes.label: pino child logger
nodes.rationale: Bind reqId/orderId once so every subsequent line carries them. One child per request. base holds process-lifetime facts; children hold per-request facts.

nodes.label: pino redact
nodes.rationale: Strips matching keys before write. Defense in depth, not a substitute for not putting secrets on the object.

nodes.label: pino err serializer
nodes.rationale: log.error({err}, msg) with stdSerializers.err preserves type, message and stack. log.error(err) often serializes as an empty object.

nodes.label: pino-pretty
nodes.rationale: Development only. Production stdout must be one JSON object per line for shippers and aggregators.

nodes.label: process.memoryUsage()
nodes.rationale: Returns rss, heapTotal, heapUsed, external, and arrayBuffers so you can tell OS charge from V8 live heap.

nodes.label: RSS resident set size
nodes.rationale: Alert on RSS and cgroup memory for Kubernetes OOM risk; kubelet kills on container memory, not V8 heapUsed.

nodes.label: V8 heapUsed
nodes.rationale: heapUsed climbing under flat traffic is the leak signal; heapTotal growth can just be V8 reservation.

nodes.label: v8.getHeapStatistics()
nodes.rationale: heap_size_limit is not always equal to --max-old-space-size; the limit covers more than old space.

nodes.label: Active handles and requests
nodes.rationale: Open servers, timers, and sockets keep the loop alive; prefer process.report over underscore APIs in production.

nodes.label: Prometheus pull scrape
nodes.rationale: Pull keeps service discovery, failure detection, and timestamps with the collector; Pushgateway is the short-lived-job exception.

nodes.label: GET /metrics endpoint
nodes.rationale: Keep /metrics off the public internet via an internal listener, NetworkPolicy, or sidecar scrape.

nodes.label: Metric cardinality
nodes.rationale: Never label by userId, orderId, full URL, or exception message; identity belongs in logs and traces.

nodes.label: Startup time — compile cache, snapshots, lazy requires
module.enableCompileCache()
nodes.rationale: Containers that wipe /tmp every start get no cross-restart benefit unless the cache directory is persisted.

nodes.label: Lazy dynamic imports
nodes.rationale: Lazy speeds cold start but moves cost to first use; eager-import the hot path.

nodes.label: Time to readiness
nodes.rationale: Measure phases through listen+ready; DNS to Postgres often dominates import time.

nodes.label: Structured logging
nodes.rationale: One JSON object per event with stable fields; the library is optional, the schema is not.

nodes.label: Log levels as a dial
nodes.rationale: Default production to info; fleet-wide debug fills disks and logging bills.

nodes.label: console.log stdout backpressure
nodes.rationale: console is synchronous on some destinations; a slow stdout pipe can block the event loop under a traffic spike.

nodes.label: Node diagnostic report
nodes.rationale: JSON dump of stacks, handles, versions, and resource usage; may contain sensitive env and is not free to write.

nodes.label: node:trace_events
nodes.rationale: Low-level Node/V8 categories, not product distributed tracing; scope to a critical section.

nodes.label: What to log and what never to log
Never log secrets or payment data
nodes.rationale: Passwords, tokens, PAN/CVV, government ids, and private keys must not appear; log stores often have wider read access than the database.

nodes.label: Log data minimization vs redaction
nodes.rationale: Minimization means not putting sensitive fields on the object; redaction is a seatbelt for fields that slipped through.

nodes.label: Blue/green deploy
nodes.rationale: Two full environments; rollback is a second flip if sessions and schemas allow.

nodes.label: Canary deploy
nodes.rationale: Needs real golden-signal metrics, not only pods ready; include write paths in the canary mix.

nodes.label: Expand/contract migrations
nodes.rationale: Old and new code run together in canary/rolling; incompatible schema breaks one colour.

nodes.label: Boot sequence — validate, connect, listen, ready
Validate connect listen ready
nodes.rationale: Any other order accepts requests the process cannot serve, or fails halfway with sockets already open.

nodes.label: Shutdown is the reverse of boot
nodes.rationale: SIGTERM → fail readiness → drain → close server → close pools → exit.

nodes.label: CI/CD — Node version matrix, caches, artifacts
yarn install --immutable
nodes.rationale: Fail when the lockfile would change so CI cannot silently drift.

nodes.label: Promote image digest
nodes.rationale: Production must run the exact bits that passed staging, not a hopeful rebuild on the deploy agent.

nodes.label: Dockerizing Node — multi-stage, non-root, layer cache
Multi-stage Node Dockerfile
nodes.rationale: Copy lockfile and package.json before source so code edits do not invalidate the dependency layer.

nodes.label: Non-root container USER
nodes.rationale: CVE classes that write to the filesystem or load code become worse as root.

nodes.label: Environment parity
nodes.rationale: Align runtime version, lockfile, and config shape; secrets and scale must still differ.

nodes.label: Honest staging
nodes.rationale: SQLite in staging while prod uses Postgres is a lie for dialects, transactions, and concurrency.

nodes.label: Image size and hardening — distroless, alpine, slim
node:24-bookworm-slim
nodes.rationale: Default for most fullstack APIs: glibc, good addon compatibility, still slim.

nodes.label: Alpine musl vs glibc
nodes.rationale: Native addon prebuilds often target glibc first; Alpine can fail at runtime without a musl build.

nodes.label: Container PID 1
nodes.rationale: PID 1 must reap zombies and forward signals; make Node PID 1 with exec-form CMD.

nodes.label: npm start swallows SIGTERM
nodes.rationale: npm as PID 1 often does not forward SIGTERM to Node, so graceful handlers never run and the orchestrator SIGKILLs after grace.

nodes.label: One process supervisor
nodes.rationale: Do not run pm2 inside Kubernetes; double supervision fights on restarts and muddies PID 1.

nodes.label: Behind a reverse proxy — X-Forwarded-*, trust proxy, TLS
X-Forwarded-* headers
nodes.rationale: Only trust forwarded headers if the socket peer is the proxy; otherwise clients forge IPs.

nodes.label: Scaling — vertical vs horizontal, cluster vs replicas
Vertical vs horizontal scaling
nodes.rationale: One Node process uses one JS core well; extra cores need more processes.

nodes.label: cluster module vs replicas
nodes.rationale: Inside Kubernetes prefer replicas over nesting cluster in each pod.

nodes.label: Autoscale on lag not only CPU
nodes.rationale: CPU-only HPA misses I/O-bound APIs that are slow but idle on CPU.

nodes.label: Serverless Node — cold starts, connection reuse
Warm isolate connection reuse
nodes.rationale: Hundreds of isolates times pool size exhausts Postgres; cap pool at 1 or use a proxy.

nodes.label: Serverless isolate freeze model
nodes.rationale: Process may freeze or die without SIGTERM; setInterval is not a background worker.

nodes.label: 12-factor config
nodes.rationale: Config in the environment, validated at start, no production secrets in the repo, no silent defaults for connection strings.

nodes.label: NODE_ENV is not a feature flag
nodes.rationale: NODE_ENV=production changes dependency behaviour; use explicit flags for product tiers.

nodes.label: Zero-downtime deploys — rolling restarts, drain, readiness
Readiness vs liveness
nodes.rationale: Failing readiness removes traffic without killing the pod mid-drain; liveness restarts.

nodes.label: HTTP server.close drain
nodes.rationale: Keep-alive can hold server.close open; track sockets and destroy idle ones after timeout.

nodes.label: Node.js core contribution
nodes.rationale: Contribute when the bug is truly in core and you can provide tests — not to work around app bugs.

nodes.label: C++ addons and the embedder API
C++ addon
nodes.rationale: Crashes inside the addon take down the whole Node process; try/catch cannot catch a segfault.

nodes.label: Node-API
nodes.rationale: Preferred stable ABI for new addons versus raw V8 or NAN.

nodes.label: Node embedder API
nodes.rationale: Your C++ binary hosts Node; typical HTTP services consume Node as host, they do not embed.

nodes.label: Custom module loaders
nodes.rationale: Intercept resolve/load for transpile, mock, or policy. Power tools for tooling authors, not app servers.

nodes.label: Loader resolve hook
nodes.rationale: Maps a specifier to a URL; chain with next() to defer to default resolution.

nodes.label: Loader load hook
nodes.rationale: Returns source for a URL so a loader can transpile or substitute modules.

nodes.label: node --import loader registration
nodes.rationale: Modern Node registers loaders via --import a registration module; pin Node 24 docs.

nodes.label: Prefer compiled JS over production loaders
nodes.rationale: On-the-fly transforms hurt startup, complicate debugging, and drift from the CI artifact.

nodes.label: Foreign Function Interface (FFI)
nodes.rationale: Call C ABI functions in an existing shared library from JS without a dedicated Node addon.

nodes.label: FFI wrong-type undefined behaviour
nodes.rationale: A wrong argument/return declaration is process-level undefined behaviour and can corrupt memory.

nodes.label: FFI versus Node-API addon
nodes.rationale: FFI ships JS plus a vendor lib with runtime types; a Node-API addon ships a compiled .node with compile-time safety and better chatty-API performance.

nodes.label: Node-API (N-API)
nodes.rationale: Stable C ABI for native addons so a binary can survive Node major upgrades better than NAN/V8-bound addons.

nodes.label: node-addon-api
nodes.rationale: C++ wrappers over Node-API (types, maybe-unwrap) that make addon code less error-prone.

nodes.label: process.versions.napi
nodes.rationale: Reports the Node-API version of the runtime; Node 24.19.0 reports 10.

nodes.label: Native addon prebuilds
nodes.rationale: Ship per-platform binaries (prebuildify/prebuild) so users and CI do not need a compiler.

nodes.label: Node-API sits between C++ and V8
nodes.rationale: Early addons called V8 APIs and broke every Node major. Node-API is the stable surface: Your C++ → Node-API → Node/V8.

nodes.label: node:vm
nodes.rationale: Runs a string of JavaScript in a configured V8 context for soft isolation, tests, and REPLs.

nodes.label: vm.createContext and runInContext
nodes.rationale: createContext freezes an API object; runInContext evaluates a string against it, optionally with timeout.

nodes.label: vm constructor-chain breakout
nodes.rationale: this.constructor.constructor("return process")() against createContext({}) returned process.version on Node 24.19.0.

nodes.label: node:vm is not a security sandbox
nodes.rationale: Node documents vm as not a security mechanism. Hostile code reaches the outer realm; untrusted code needs a process or container.

nodes.label: Startup snapshot
nodes.rationale: Freezes a V8 heap after bootstrap so the next launch skips re-parsing and re-running init.

nodes.label: Snapshot tied to Node/V8 build
nodes.rationale: Snapshots are invalid after a Node patch; rebuild in CI per runtime artifact.

nodes.label: Snapshot versus compile cache versus SEA
nodes.rationale: enableCompileCache stores compilation artifacts; a snapshot stores initialised heap; SEA packages a single binary. Compile cache is the practical first win.

nodes.label: V8 flags
nodes.rationale: Engine knobs for heap limits, GC tracing, and compilation. Listed with node --v8-options on the deployed binary.

nodes.label: --max-old-space-size
nodes.rationale: Most common production V8-related flag; caps old-space growth. Heap limit is not always equal to the number passed.

nodes.label: --trace-gc
nodes.rationale: GC logging for debugging; noisy and not a production default.

nodes.label: V8 flags are diagnostics not casual perf knobs
nodes.rationale: Most apps need none beyond --max-old-space-size. Random blog flags add risk; document any non-default with an owner.

nodes.label: WASI
nodes.rationale: Portable system interface for Wasm modules — host-gated files, clocks, and similar — not a full OS.

nodes.label: uvwasi
nodes.rationale: Node's WASI implementation; process.versions.uvwasi reports 0.0.23 on Node 24.19.0.

nodes.label: WASI preopens
nodes.rationale: Map guest paths to host directories. Overly broad maps (guest / → host root) leak or overwrite data.

nodes.label: WASI is not safe because Wasm
nodes.rationale: The host chooses directories and env the guest sees. Misconfigured preopens are data exposure, same as dangerous Wasm imports.

nodes.label: WebAssembly in Node
nodes.rationale: Near-native portable compute for a profiled CPU hotspot without rewriting the app as a C++ addon.

nodes.label: WebAssembly.instantiate
nodes.rationale: Load .wasm bytes (or streaming variants) plus host imports; no ambient Node APIs inside the module.

nodes.label: Wasm versus worker_threads versus N-API
nodes.rationale: Workers give threads at JS speed; Wasm gives portable compute; N-API gives full native power and a build matrix.

nodes.label: AbortController
nodes.rationale: Standard cancellation remote: abort() stops in-flight work that accepted the paired signal.

nodes.label: AbortSignal
nodes.rationale: Read-only side handed to callees: aborted, reason, throwIfAborted(), abort event. Never hand out the controller.

nodes.label: AbortSignal.timeout
nodes.rationale: Deadline signal that actually aborts work, unlike Promise.race against setTimeout. Timer is unrefed.

nodes.label: AbortSignal.any
nodes.rationale: Combined signal that aborts when the first input does and adopts that reason — cancellation counterpart of Promise.race.

nodes.label: AbortSignal.throwIfAborted
nodes.rationale: Throws signal.reason if already aborted; check before starting and between units of work.

nodes.label: Promises cannot be cancelled
nodes.rationale: A promise is a view of a result with many consumers. Cancellation belongs to the work, via AbortController.

nodes.label: async and await
nodes.rationale: Syntax over promises: async makes a function return a promise and permits await. Adds no new capability.

nodes.label: Top-level await
nodes.rationale: ES modules can await outside a function; importers wait. Makes the module impossible to require() from CommonJS.

nodes.label: await inside forEach
nodes.rationale: Array.forEach ignores the returned promise so async work floats. Use for...of or Promise.all(map).

nodes.label: await yields to microtasks not the event loop
nodes.rationale: Body runs synchronously to the first await; resumption is a microtask. A loop of already-resolved awaits never lets timers or I/O run.

nodes.label: async_hooks
nodes.rationale: Experimental lifecycle hooks (init/before/after/destroy) that track the async context tree. For APM vendors, not app code.

nodes.label: AsyncResource.bind
nodes.rationale: Captures the current async context and restores it when a callback later runs — the fix for EventEmitter and queue context loss.

nodes.label: executionAsyncId and triggerAsyncId
nodes.rationale: Id of the executing async context and the id that created it. The tree AsyncLocalStorage walks.

nodes.label: node:diagnostics_channel
nodes.rationale: Supported instrumentation: named channels with near-zero cost when nobody is subscribed. Prefer over createHook.

nodes.label: Do not use createHook in application code
nodes.rationale: Experimental, fires on every async op, and console.log inside a hook recurses. Use AsyncLocalStorage and diagnostics_channel.

nodes.label: for await...of
nodes.rationale: Loop for sequences that arrive over time. Awaits each value; strictly sequential, one item in memory.

nodes.label: async generator
nodes.rationale: async function* can await and yield. Consumer pull pauses the producer — free pull-based backpressure.

nodes.label: Symbol.asyncIterator
nodes.rationale: Protocol: a method returning { next() → Promise<{value, done}> }. Async generators produce it.

nodes.label: Pull-based backpressure
nodes.rationale: The generator is suspended at yield until the consumer asks for the next value, so a slow consumer slows the producer.

nodes.label: AsyncLocalStorage
nodes.rationale: Per-request ambient context (request id, tenant) that survives await without adding a parameter to every signature.

nodes.label: run() versus enterWith()
nodes.rationale: run(store, fn) scopes the store to fn and descendants. enterWith leaks into the rest of the current async context; prefer run().

nodes.label: Error-first callback convention
nodes.rationale: cb(err) or cb(null, value), exactly once, always asynchronously. The contract util.promisify depends on.

nodes.label: util.promisify
nodes.rationale: Wraps an error-first last-argument callback API into a promise. Prefer built-in fs/promises etc. when they exist.

nodes.label: util.promisify.custom
nodes.rationale: Author-supplied promise form checked first when the mechanical (err, value) translation is wrong.

nodes.label: new Promise only to wrap callbacks
nodes.rationale: The one legitimate use of the Promise constructor is wrapping a callback or event API. Wrapping already-promise code is an antipattern.

nodes.label: Promise.all
nodes.rationale: Settles when all fulfil; rejects on first failure with that reason. Waiting primitive, not a concurrency limiter.

nodes.label: Promise.allSettled
nodes.rationale: Waits for every input; never rejects. Returns {status, value|reason} so partial success is inspectable.

nodes.label: Promise.race
nodes.rationale: Settles with the first to settle, success or failure. Used for timeouts; does not stop losers.

nodes.label: Promise.any
nodes.rationale: Settles with the first fulfilment, ignoring rejections. All-reject throws AggregateError with .errors.

nodes.label: Combinators do not cancel losers
nodes.rationale: race/all stop waiting, not working. Timed-out HTTP still holds a socket. Real stop requires AbortSignal.

nodes.label: Unbounded Promise.all
nodes.rationale: Starts every item immediately. Exhausts FDs, pools, memory, or a remote rate limit on a real dataset.

nodes.label: Bounded mapLimit worker pool
nodes.rationale: Exactly N workers claim a shared cursor. JS single-thread makes next++ atomic; results[i] preserves order.

nodes.label: Pool versus chunked Promise.all
nodes.rationale: Chunking waits for the slowest in each batch and idles workers. A pool keeps every worker busy continuously.

nodes.label: CPU-bound work
nodes.rationale: Busy compute on the single JS thread. While it runs, no request, timer, or health check is handled.

nodes.label: Chunking with setImmediate
nodes.rationale: Split work into ~10–50ms pieces and await setImmediate so the loop can drain I/O. Bounds latency, not throughput.

nodes.label: worker_threads
nodes.rationale: Real parallelism on another thread. Spawn is expensive; use a pool (piscina). Data is structured-cloned unless transferred.

nodes.label: libuv thread pool crypto APIs
nodes.rationale: crypto.pbkdf2, scrypt, and async bcrypt run off the loop; *Sync variants block it. Cheapest password-hashing fix.

nodes.label: async does not stop CPU from blocking
nodes.rationale: async changes the return value, not whether the body blocks. There is no await that yields inside a tight loop.

nodes.label: Error codes not messages
nodes.rationale: Messages are prose and get reworded. code is a stable contract (ENOENT, ERR_USER_NOT_FOUND). instanceof can fail if the class module is duplicated.

nodes.label: Custom error class
nodes.rationale: Extend Error, set name and a stable code, carry structured context as properties, forward options so {cause} works.

nodes.label: error.cause
nodes.rationale: Standard wrap that keeps the root error attached. Wrap when adding information; rethrow bare otherwise.

nodes.label: AggregateError
nodes.rationale: Several failures in one error (.errors). Promise.any throws one when every input rejects.

nodes.label: Operational versus programmer errors
nodes.rationale: Operational (timeout, 404, disk full) are handled. Programmer (TypeError) crash and restart — retrying reproduces the bug.

nodes.label: try/catch with await
nodes.rationale: A rejected promise throws at the await. Without await the try finishes synchronously and the rejection is unhandled.

nodes.label: .catch() placement
nodes.rationale: Mid-chain .catch recovers and the chain continues fulfilled. End-of-chain is a final net. Covers only upstream.

nodes.label: Catch only what you can handle
nodes.rationale: A giant try cannot say what failed. Recover or add {cause} locally; let the rest propagate to a boundary.

nodes.label: Event loop phases
nodes.rationale: Fixed order per tick: timers → pending → idle/prepare → poll → check → close. nextTick and microtasks drain between phases.

nodes.label: Poll phase
nodes.rationale: Waits for I/O then runs I/O callbacks. An idle server spends its life blocked here consuming no CPU.

nodes.label: Check phase (setImmediate)
nodes.rationale: Runs setImmediate. After poll in the same tick, so inside an I/O callback setImmediate always beats setTimeout(0).

nodes.label: setTimeout(0) versus setImmediate from main
nodes.rationale: From the main module their order is a genuine race. Inside I/O it is always setImmediate first.

nodes.label: process.getActiveResourcesInfo
nodes.rationale: Lists handles keeping the process alive. unref() excludes a handle from the exit count without cancelling it.

nodes.label: Floating promise
nodes.rationale: A promise-returning call nobody awaited or .catch'd. Since Node 15 an unhandled rejection terminates the process.

nodes.label: Unhandled rejection is fatal
nodes.rationale: Node 15+ exits with code 1 on unhandledRejection by default. A process handler is a detector, not a fix.

nodes.label: void plus .catch for fire-and-forget
nodes.rationale: Deliberate background work must be explicit and handled. void signals intent; .catch is what makes it safe.

nodes.label: @typescript-eslint/no-floating-promises
nodes.rationale: Lint that flags discarded promises. Needs TypeScript type information; strongest practical TS argument in Node.

nodes.label: Microtasks versus macrotasks
nodes.rationale: Microtasks (then/await/queueMicrotask) drain completely between phases. Macrotasks (timers, setImmediate, I/O) belong to a phase.

nodes.label: process.nextTick
nodes.rationale: Node-only queue drained at a checkpoint before microtasks. Drains to exhaustion including newly queued ticks — starvation risk.

nodes.label: queueMicrotask
nodes.rationale: Web-standard microtask. Prefer over nextTick except when you must run before pending promise continuations.

nodes.label: nextTick after promises at ESM top level
nodes.rationale: The nextTick-before-promises rule fails at ESM top level because module evaluation is itself a microtask. Inside a timer callback the familiar order returns.

nodes.label: Poll blocking vs blocked event loop
return await inside try is not redundant
Return or it is not chained
setImmediate always wins inside I/O callbacks
High water marks and buffer tuning
StringDecoder
nodes.rationale: Buffers a trailing incomplete UTF-8 sequence and prepends it to the next write so chunk.toString() cannot permanently replace a split character with U+FFFD.

nodes.label: Per-chunk toString corruption
nodes.rationale: Chunk boundaries fall on byte offsets, so decoding each chunk independently substitutes U+FFFD for both halves of a multi-byte character.

nodes.label: stream.setEncoding
nodes.rationale: Installs a StringDecoder internally. Prefer this in application code; stay in buffers when bytes matter.

nodes.label: Character vs token boundaries
nodes.rationale: StringDecoder fixes character boundaries only. A regex still misses a token split across chunks; that needs a framing Transform.

nodes.label: Transform streams
nodes.rationale: Reusable pipeline middle: _transform and _flush. The hard part is that chunk boundaries do not respect data structure.

nodes.label: _flush
nodes.rationale: Runs after input ends and before downstream 'end'; the only place buffered tail state can be emitted.

nodes.label: Web Streams
nodes.rationale: WHATWG ReadableStream, WritableStream, and TransformStream — globals in Node since v18; fetch bodies are web streams.

nodes.label: Readable.toWeb / fromWeb
nodes.rationale: Convert once at the boundary. Node chunks are Buffers; web chunks are Uint8Array. Repeated conversion adds wrapper queues.

nodes.label: ReadableStream lock
nodes.rationale: Exactly one reader at a time. for-await, pipeTo, and getReader all lock; a second getReader throws TypeError.

nodes.label: ReadableStream.tee
nodes.rationale: Duplicates a stream into two branches. The faster branch buffers until the slower reads — an abandoned branch grows unbounded.

nodes.label: Prefer Node streams in Node
nodes.rationale: Use Node streams for pipeline, object mode, and Node APIs. Use web streams for edge/browser, fetch-only code, or CompressionStream.

nodes.label: Why streams exist
nodes.rationale: Process data in chunks so peak memory stays constant. Buffered 216 MB log peaked 670 MB RSS vs 88 MB streamed.

nodes.label: ERR_STRING_TOO_LONG
nodes.rationale: V8 strings cap at 0x1fffffe8 characters (~512 MB). readFile(path,'utf8') on a larger file throws with no workaround except streaming.

nodes.label: Time to first byte
nodes.rationale: A streamed response sends as soon as the first chunk exists; buffering waits for the last byte and can time out proxies.

nodes.label: Default highWaterMark 64 KB
nodes.rationale: stream.getDefaultHighWaterMark(false) is 64 KB (raised from 16 KB in Node 22). Chunks split lines, JSON, and multi-byte characters freely.

nodes.label: When not to stream
nodes.rationale: Buffer bounded small data (config, 10 KB JSON). Streams add backpressure complexity and cannot JSON.parse or sort without a streaming parser.

nodes.label: node:zlib streams
nodes.rationale: gzip, deflate, and brotli as Transform streams so compression drops into a pipeline with constant memory.

nodes.label: Brotli default quality 11
nodes.rationale: createBrotliCompress() with no options uses quality 11: 75.7 s on 19 MB vs 0.78 s for gzip 6. Intended for pre-compressed static assets.

nodes.label: gzip level trade-off
nodes.rationale: Level 9 is 2.2× CPU of level 6 for 0.8% smaller. Level 1 is usually right for dynamic responses; 9 belongs in a build step.

nodes.label: zlib on libuv thread pool
nodes.rationale: Stream zlib runs on the 4-thread libuv pool shared with fs and dns.lookup. Four concurrent gzips match one; eight double wall time.

nodes.label: maxOutputLength zip-bomb cap
nodes.rationale: A few KB of gzip can expand 1000×+. Cap decompressed size; maxOutputLength throws ERR_BUFFER_TOO_LARGE.

nodes.label: Compress in nginx or CDN
nodes.rationale: Keep CPU out of the event loop and thread pool. Compress in Node only for files you write, required upstreams, or no-proxy environments.

nodes.label: decodeStrings
nodes.rationale: Default true converts written strings to Buffers before _transform. decodeStrings:false passes the original string through.

nodes.label: Transform is sequential
nodes.rationale: One chunk at a time preserves order and forbids in-transform parallelism. Use readable.map({concurrency}) or a bounded pool instead.

nodes.label: Async generator pipeline stage
nodes.rationale: Same backpressure and error propagation without the callback contract. Write a Transform class only for reuse, _writev, _destroy, or custom HWM.

nodes.label: Transform callback contract
nodes.rationale: Call callback exactly once. Never calling hangs the pipeline; twice throws ERR_MULTIPLE_CALLBACK. callback(null,v) emits one chunk.

nodes.label: Chunk boundary problem
nodes.rationale: A per-chunk regex misses a token that straddles the 64 KB mark. Verified: tok_live_ split across chunks was not redacted.

nodes.label: SplitLines framing
nodes.rationale: Hold everything after the last newline as a tail, push complete lines, emit remainder in _flush. Frame first, then operate on records.

nodes.label: _flush emits the last record
nodes.rationale: Files without a trailing newline drop the last record if _flush is omitted.

nodes.label: writeFile is not atomic
nodes.rationale: Opens with 'w', truncates immediately, then writes. Crash, ENOSPC, or a concurrent reader sees a truncated file.

nodes.label: Atomic write pattern
nodes.rationale: Write a unique temp file in the same directory with 'wx', sync(), then rename over the target. rename is atomic within one filesystem.

nodes.label: EXDEV cross-device rename
nodes.rationale: rename across mounts throws EXDEV. In containers /tmp is often a different mount, so write-to-tmpdir-then-move is broken.

nodes.label: mkdtemp
nodes.rationale: Creates a directory atomically with a random suffix so there is no window to pre-create or symlink a predictable temp path.

nodes.label: Mid-stream upload size limit
nodes.rationale: Count bytes as they arrive and destroy past the limit. Content-Length is client-supplied and absent under chunked encoding.

nodes.label: readdir withFileTypes
nodes.rationale: Dirent already knows type, avoiding one stat per entry and thousands of extra thread-pool ops on large directories.

nodes.label: readdir order not guaranteed
nodes.rationale: Filesystem-dependent (ext4 vs overlayfs). Sort explicitly or numbered migrations run in the wrong order.

nodes.label: opendir walk
nodes.rationale: Async iterator over one entry at a time for huge trees. Constant memory vs readdir({recursive:true}) materialising the whole array.

nodes.label: rm recursive force
nodes.rationale: Modern rm -rf. Replaces deprecated rmdir({recursive}) (DEP0147). force makes a missing path a no-op for finally cleanup.

nodes.label: Dirent.parentPath
