nodes.rationale: Replaced deprecated Dirent.path. Full path is path.join(entry.parentPath, entry.name).

nodes.label: FileHandle
nodes.rationale: open() returns a handle owning an OS descriptor. Close in finally; GC does not reliably reclaim leaked fds.

nodes.label: EMFILE
nodes.rationale: Per-process fd limit. One leaked handle per request exhausts the budget; every later file and socket fails. Invisible on a high-ulimit laptop.

nodes.label: 'wx' exclusive create
nodes.rationale: Atomic create-if-absent; fails with EEXIST. How you build a lock file without a check-then-create race.

nodes.label: FileHandle.stat
nodes.rationale: Stats the open descriptor, not the path, so it cannot race with a rename. Closes the Content-Length race.

nodes.label: FileHandle.sync
nodes.rationale: fsync — only way to know bytes reached disk rather than the page cache. Required before rename in the atomic-write pattern.

nodes.label: createReadStream / createWriteStream
nodes.rationale: Filesystem entry points into streams. Live on node:fs, not fs/promises. Constructor never throws; open happens later.

nodes.label: HTTP range requests
nodes.rationale: end is inclusive. {start:3,end:7} is five bytes, matching Range: bytes=3-7. Return 416 for out-of-range.

nodes.label: Async stream open errors
nodes.rationale: ENOENT, EACCES, EISDIR arrive as 'error' events. pipeline converts them into a rejection.

nodes.label: Serve file over HTTP
nodes.rationale: stat first (404 before headers), Content-Length from stat().size, pipeline with AbortSignal, treat ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE as normal.

nodes.label: createWriteStream truncates
nodes.rationale: Default flags 'w' empties an existing file as soon as the stream is created, even if nothing is written. Use 'a' to append.

nodes.label: node:fs/promises
nodes.rationale: Default filesystem API. Every operation returns a promise; errors are exceptions with a code; nothing blocks the event loop.

nodes.label: err.code
nodes.rationale: Branch on code (ENOENT, EEXIST, EACCES, ENOSPC, EMFILE, EXDEV), never message text. Swallowing all errors hides EACCES as empty config.

nodes.label: rename atomicity
nodes.rationale: Atomic within one filesystem: readers see old or new, never a partial write. Across devices throws EXDEV.

nodes.label: fs/promises thread pool overlap
nodes.rationale: 200 async reads 45 ms with 23 timer ticks vs 200 sync 86 ms and 0 ticks. Unbounded Promise.all still hits EMFILE.

nodes.label: node:os
nodes.rationale: Reports what the host looks like. In a container that is a lie for cores and memory.

nodes.label: os.cpus / totalmem container lie
nodes.rationale: A 0.5-CPU / 512 MB pod on a 64-core node still sees 64 CPUs and host RAM. Sizing a WorkerPool from cpus().length is a classic production bug.

nodes.label: os.availableParallelism
nodes.rationale: Respects CPU affinity masks but still misses CFS quota (--cpus=0.5). Prefer configured WORKER_CONCURRENCY.

nodes.label: process vs os
nodes.rationale: process.memoryUsage / cpuUsage describe this process. os.totalmem / loadavg describe a machine you may be sharing.

nodes.label: Path traversal
nodes.rationale: Any filesystem path built from user input is a security boundary. ../, absolute paths, encoded separators, and symlinks each escape.

nodes.label: safeResolve containment check
nodes.rationale: path.resolve(ROOT, input), require equal-to-root or startsWith(ROOT+sep), then realpath and repeat to defeat symlinks.

nodes.label: ROOT + path.sep prefix
nodes.rationale: startsWith('/srv/uploads') is true for /srv/uploads-evil/x. The separator plus exact-equal for the root itself is required.

nodes.label: Generated storage keys
nodes.rationale: Best defence: store under UUIDs, keep original name as metadata, address by ID. No user string reaches the filesystem.

nodes.label: Zip-slip
nodes.rationale: Archive entries named ../../etc/cron.d/x write outside the extract root. Apply the same containment check to every entry.

nodes.label: path.join
nodes.rationale: Concatenates and normalises. An absolute later argument is treated as a relative segment, so join(root,'/etc/passwd') looks contained.

nodes.label: path.resolve
nodes.rationale: Always absolute; restarts at any absolute argument. The right tool for validating user input against a root.

nodes.label: path.posix
nodes.rationale: Use for URL paths, S3 keys, tar entries, Docker and git paths — always forward slashes. Default path.join writes backslashes on Windows.

nodes.label: import.meta.dirname
nodes.rationale: ESM replacement for __dirname on Node 21.2+. Undefined for non-file: URLs; then use fileURLToPath(import.meta.url).

nodes.label: path.extname last only
nodes.rationale: report.tar.gz yields .gz. Extension-based file-type checks are trivially bypassed (evil.php.jpg); sniff content.

nodes.label: umask
nodes.rationale: Per-process bits to remove. Common 022 turns requested 0o666 into 0o644. mode is a maximum, not a guarantee.

nodes.label: stat().mode & 0o777
nodes.rationale: mode includes file type (0o100644). Compare only after masking. Always write octal 0o600; chmod(600) is 0o1130.

nodes.label: realpath
nodes.rationale: Fully resolved absolute path following every symlink. What a containment check needs. readlink returns the raw possibly-relative target.

nodes.label: symlink
nodes.rationale: symlink(target, path) mirrors ln -s. Relative targets resolve against the link's directory, which is the traversal escape.

nodes.label: Hard link
nodes.rationale: Second name for the same inode; one filesystem only. nlink>1 means delete may not free space until the last name and last fd are gone.

nodes.label: TOCTOU
nodes.rationale: Time-of-check to time-of-use. exists then readFile can lose the file or have it swapped for a symlink. Do the operation and handle ENOENT.

nodes.label: existsSync
nodes.rationale: Not deprecated (unlike fs.exists DEP0018). Fine at startup/CLI. Never a security check or request-handler guard.

nodes.label: stat
nodes.rationale: Follows symlinks and describes the target. Never reports isSymbolicLink()===true; throws ENOENT on a broken link.

nodes.label: lstat
nodes.rationale: Does not follow. Identifies links and is the only one that works on a broken symlink. Use it before deletion.

nodes.label: ino + dev identity
nodes.rationale: How you tell two paths are the same file. Path strings cannot see hard links, bind mounts, or case-insensitive filesystems.

nodes.label: Three fs flavors
nodes.rationale: Promise (default), callback (legacy), sync (startup only). Sync returns inline; promise on a microtask; callback in a later phase.

nodes.label: Sync fs blocks the event loop
nodes.rationale: 200 readFileSync blocked a 1 ms timer for 86 ms with zero ticks. One thread runs all JS; a sync syscall owns it.

nodes.label: When sync fs is correct
nodes.rationale: Before listen (config, certs), CLI/build scripts, a dedicated worker_thread, and crash handlers with no future event-loop turn.

nodes.label: Hidden sync I/O
nodes.rationale: require() inside a handler, existsSync, template engines loading with readFileSync, and console.log to a file are all sync.

nodes.label: WHATWG URL
nodes.rationale: URL and URLSearchParams are globals implementing the same standard as the browser. Handle encoding and relative resolution string concat gets wrong.

nodes.label: url.parse deprecated
nodes.rationale: DEP0169. Known parsing differences from the standard have caused SSRF bypasses. Use new URL().

nodes.label: host vs hostname
nodes.rationale: host includes the port; hostname does not. An allowlist on host fails the moment a port appears.

nodes.label: URLSearchParams
nodes.rationale: Decodes on read, encodes on write. get returns only the first repeated key — a real authorisation-bypass shape. Use getAll.

nodes.label: SSRF URL check
nodes.rationale: Check protocol and hostname on the parsed object, never a regex on the raw string. Incomplete without pinning the resolved IP.

nodes.label: fileURLToPath / pathToFileURL
nodes.rationale: Only correct file: conversions. file://+path misses %20 and Windows drive letters. Most fs APIs accept a file: URL directly.

nodes.label: Virtual filesystem
nodes.rationale: An object implementing the fs interface without a disk. Stream constructors accept an fs option so you can substitute without monkey-patching.

nodes.label: memfs
nodes.rationale: Full in-memory fs for tests. Fast and isolated, but one device so EXDEV, umask, permissions, and EMFILE never appear.

nodes.label: node:sea getAsset
nodes.rationale: Assets live inside a single executable, not on disk. Branch on isSea(); prefix-only builtin (require('sea') hits npm).

nodes.label: Inject fs as a dependency
nodes.rationale: Tests pass memfs, production passes fs/promises, no global mock. Leaves the door open for S3 later. Do not mock tests whose subject is the filesystem.

nodes.label: fs.watch
nodes.rationale: OS events (inotify/FSEvents/ReadDirectoryChangesW). Fast, inconsistent. One writeFile produced two change events. Often silent on Docker mounts.

nodes.label: fs.watchFile
nodes.rationale: Polls with stat (default 5007 ms). Reliable on network/Docker mounts; expensive at scale. Deletion is curr.mtimeMs===0. Must unwatchFile.

nodes.label: chokidar
nodes.rationale: Debounces, distinguishes add/change/unlink, awaitWriteFinish, auto-polls for network mounts, handles editor atomic-save.

nodes.label: Do not watch files in production
nodes.rationale: Containers are immutable, events fail on production volumes, a partial write can be loaded, and the reload path is under-tested. Prefer restart or SIGHUP.

nodes.label: inotify ENOSPC
nodes.rationale: Per-user watch limit, not disk space. One watch per directory; recursive watch over node_modules exhausts max_user_watches.

nodes.label: child_process.spawn
nodes.rationale: No shell, streams stdout/stderr. Output bounded by what you consume. Child blocks if the pipe fills and nobody reads.

nodes.label: child_process.exec
nodes.rationale: Runs through /bin/sh -c so pipes and globs work. Buffers with maxBuffer 1 MB. Never interpolate untrusted input.

nodes.label: child_process.execFile
nodes.rationale: No shell; argv array to execve. Default choice for running one binary. Same 1 MB maxBuffer as exec.

nodes.label: child_process.fork
nodes.rationale: Another Node process plus an IPC message channel.

nodes.label: maxBuffer
nodes.rationale: Cap on buffered stdout/stderr for exec/execFile, 1 MB default. Exceeding kills the child with ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_STDIO_MAXBUFFER.

nodes.label: Explicit child env
nodes.rationale: Children inherit process.env by default, handing DB URLs and API keys to ffmpeg. Pass a minimal env with PATH only.

nodes.label: Workers vs child processes
nodes.rationale: Child process ~56 ms to ready and ~49 MB RSS. Four workers ~23 MB vs ~196 MB for four processes. Children are for other programs or crash isolation.

nodes.label: node:cluster
nodes.rationale: One Node process uses one core. cluster forks a worker per core sharing one listening port. On Kubernetes prefer replicas; cluster is for a single VM and zero-downtime reload.

nodes.label: os.availableParallelism
nodes.rationale: Respects cgroup CPU limits and affinity. cpus().length reports the host and over-forks in a constrained container.

nodes.label: SCHED_RR connection round-robin
nodes.rationale: Round-robin distributes accepts, not requests. Keep-alive pins many requests to one worker.

nodes.label: Sticky sessions
nodes.rationale: Pinning clients to a worker hides in-memory state. Prefer Redis sessions, rate limits, and pub/sub so workers stay stateless.

nodes.label: Set-Cookie array header
nodes.rationale: Node has no cookie API. Cookie request headers join with '; '. Set-Cookie must be an array so each cookie is its own header line.

nodes.label: HttpOnly Secure SameSite
nodes.rationale: HttpOnly blocks XSS exfiltration, Secure blocks plaintext HTTP, SameSite is the CSRF defence. A session cookie wants all three.

nodes.label: URLSearchParams is the wrong cookie parser
Opaque session id vs JWT cookie
uncaughtException
nodes.rationale: Handlers exist to log a fatal error before dying. Installing a listener suppresses default termination; the handler must exit non-zero.

nodes.label: uncaughtExceptionMonitor
nodes.rationale: Observes a fatal error without suppressing Node's default termination. Correct hook for crash reporters like Sentry.

nodes.label: dns.lookup
nodes.rationale: Calls getaddrinfo on the libuv thread pool. Respects /etc/hosts and the OS cache. Used by http, https, net, and fetch.

nodes.label: dns.resolve
nodes.rationale: Speaks DNS via c-ares as non-blocking network I/O. Ignores host files and the OS cache. Node itself caches neither.

nodes.label: DNS rebinding SSRF
nodes.rationale: Validate-then-connect resolves twice. Pin the checked address for the connection.

nodes.label: global fetch (undici)
nodes.rationale: Does not throw on 4xx/5xx. Rejects only when the exchange fails. Check res.ok. Implemented by bundled undici.

nodes.label: fetch Response body is single-use
nodes.rationale: An unread body holds its pooled connection. Consume or cancel every body including error paths.

nodes.label: server.close
nodes.rationale: Stops new connections and waits for existing ones. Idle keep-alive sockets never end, so the callback never fires.

nodes.label: closeIdleConnections
nodes.rationale: Must be swept on an interval. Connections become idle as in-flight requests finish.

nodes.label: closeAllConnections
nodes.rationale: Destroys in-flight responses. Forced-exit backstop, not the strategy.

nodes.label: CORS
nodes.rationale: CORS is a browser rule, not access control. A Node fetch with a spoofed Origin reads the whole response.

nodes.label: http.createServer
nodes.rationale: Hands two streams and nothing else. A thrown handler never becomes a 500.

nodes.label: headersTimeout requestTimeout connectionsCheckingInterval
nodes.rationale: Timeouts are enforced by a 30s default sweep. Lowering requestTimeout alone does nothing until the next check.

nodes.label: TCP head-of-line blocking
nodes.rationale: HTTP/2 removes HTTP-layer HOL only. A lost TCP segment stalls every multiplexed stream, which is why HTTP/3 uses QUIC over UDP.

nodes.label: TLS certificate chain
nodes.rationale: Node uses a compiled Mozilla trust store, not the OS store. A missing intermediate is the common works-in-browser fails-in-Node bug.

nodes.label: rejectUnauthorized false
nodes.rationale: Disables chain and hostname verification. Encryption remains; authentication is gone.

nodes.label: mTLS
nodes.rationale: Rejection happens in the handshake, so failures are socket errors with nothing in HTTP logs.

nodes.label: fork IPC channel
nodes.rationale: Messages are copied JSON by default. An open channel keeps both processes alive.

nodes.label: http.Agent
nodes.rationale: keepAlive has defaulted to true since Node 19. maxSockets is a concurrency limit disguised as a pool setting.

nodes.label: undici Dispatcher
nodes.rationale: Default dispatcher has no per-origin cap. Parallel fetch opens a socket per in-flight request. Node bundles undici but does not export it.

nodes.label: TCP is a byte stream
nodes.rationale: TCP preserves order and delivery, not grouping. Three writes can arrive as one data event.

nodes.label: Idempotency-Key
nodes.rationale: Generate once per logical operation and reuse across retries. A key regenerated inside the retry loop defeats deduplication.

nodes.label: AbortSignal.timeout
nodes.rationale: fetch has no default timeout. The deadline covers the whole exchange including the body stream.

nodes.label: Timeouts shrink down the call graph
util.parseArgs
nodes.rationale: Core CLI parser. No number type, no generated help, no subcommands. Strict mode throws on unknown options.

nodes.label: The process object and exit codes
process.exitCode vs process.exit
nodes.rationale: process.exit terminates immediately and can truncate a large pending pipe write to one buffer (65536 bytes).

nodes.label: req is a readable stream
nodes.rationale: There is no req.body. An unbounded read is a denial-of-service vector.

nodes.label: Mid-stream body size limit
nodes.rationale: Content-Length is a client claim and is absent on chunked transfers. Count bytes as they arrive.

nodes.label: SharedArrayBuffer
nodes.rationale: The one piece of memory two threads can touch at once. Reach for it only when profiling says the copy is the problem.

nodes.label: Atomics
nodes.rationale: Non-atomic increment is read-modify-write. Four threads lost 1.8M of 8M updates in one run and zero in the next.

nodes.label: child_process.exec
nodes.rationale: Hands the string to /bin/sh. Quoted interpolation was defeated by closing quotes and by $(...) inside double quotes.

nodes.label: child_process.execFile
nodes.rationale: Passes arguments to execve. Removes shell injection, not argument injection or path traversal. shell:true restores the shell.

nodes.label: Quoting is not a shell defence
SIGTERM
nodes.rationale: Installing a listener replaces default terminate. A handler that forgets to exit hangs until SIGKILL.

nodes.label: PID 1 exec-form CMD
nodes.rationale: CMD npm start makes /bin/sh PID 1 and does not forward SIGTERM. Node is SIGKILLed after the grace period (exit 137).

nodes.label: Node SEA
nodes.rationale: The Node binary with a CommonJS blob injected by postject. 121 MB for a trivial script. CLI distribution, not server deploy.

nodes.label: Chunked transfer encoding
nodes.rationale: Omit Content-Length and Node sets Transfer-Encoding: chunked automatically so the first byte reaches the client while the rest is still being produced.

nodes.label: Server-Sent Events
nodes.rationale: One long-lived chunked HTTP response, server to client only — no upgrade, survives HTTP/1.1 proxies. Prefer over WebSockets when traffic is one-way.

nodes.label: Last-Event-ID resumption
nodes.rationale: The browser stores SSE id: and replays it as Last-Event-ID on reconnect so the server can resume instead of replaying or dropping events.

nodes.label: pipeline over pipe for streaming
nodes.rationale: .pipe() leaves both ends open when a client disconnects, so a database query keeps running. pipeline propagates destruction.

nodes.label: WebSocket HTTP upgrade handshake
nodes.rationale: Client GET with Upgrade: websocket and Sec-WebSocket-Key; server replies 101 Switching Protocols. Begins as HTTP so it carries cookies and traverses HTTP proxies.

nodes.label: ws npm WebSocketServer
nodes.rationale: Node ships only a WebSocket client (global WebSocket, stable from v22.4.0). Server side is ws from npm — what Socket.IO and Fastify wrap.

nodes.label: WebSocket ping/pong heartbeat
nodes.rationale: Sleeping laptops, dropped mobile signal and expired NAT mappings leave TCP open. Periodic ping plus isAlive and terminate() reaps dead sockets.

nodes.label: WebSocket Origin check
nodes.rationale: Handshakes are not covered by CORS or same-origin policy. Any origin can open a socket with the user's cookies. Validate Origin and authenticate on upgrade.

nodes.label: Worker thread V8 isolate
nodes.rationale: Each worker is an OS thread with its own isolate and event loop, for CPU-bound JS only. Startup ~60 ms — same as a fork — so never create one per request.

nodes.label: Worker thread pool
nodes.rationale: Fixed workers, a queue, replace on death, reject in-flight tasks, close() for shutdown. Size availableParallelism()-1. Production: piscina.

nodes.label: postMessage transfer list
nodes.rationale: Default postMessage copies via structured clone. Transfer list moves a buffer zero-copy and detaches it (byteLength 0). SharedArrayBuffer when both sides need it.

nodes.label: pg.Pool
nodes.rationale: One pool per process at module scope. max is a concurrency ceiling, not a speed limit — callers queue as waitingCount. Size from max_connections / processes.

nodes.label: Connection leak
nodes.rationale: pool.connect() without release() is invisible until the pool is exhausted hours later. Prefer pool.query(); if you check out, release in finally.

nodes.label: pool.on('error') idle listener
nodes.rationale: Idle pooled connections can die (failover, pg_terminate_backend). Unhandled 'error' on the pool kills Node. Log and do not rethrow; the pool replaces the socket.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL server-side cursor
nodes.rationale: pool.query buffers the whole result (300 MB RSS for 500k rows). A cursor holds one batch on a checked-out client. QueryStream adds backpressure but is ~5.7x slower for a pure loop.

nodes.label: Keyset pagination
nodes.rationale: Paginated APIs should not hold a cursor across requests. Use WHERE id > $1 ORDER BY id LIMIT n. OFFSET walks and discards skipped rows.

nodes.label: Lazy pool connect
nodes.rationale: new pg.Pool() does no I/O. Bad host/password surfaces on the first query — after the process joined the load balancer. Await select 1 at boot.

nodes.label: Liveness vs readiness probes
nodes.rationale: Liveness must not hit the database — failure restarts the fleet. Readiness queries select 1 with its own timeout and returns 503 so traffic stops.

nodes.label: statement_timeout vs query_timeout
nodes.rationale: statement_timeout is server-side (57014, connection survives). query_timeout only rejects the promise — the server keeps running the query.

nodes.label: Driver vs builder vs ORM
nodes.rationale: The choice is who writes the SQL and what happens when it is wrong. Layer overhead is sub-millisecond; N+1 and indexes dominate. One tool owns schema, migrations and the pool.

nodes.label: pg_advisory_lock for migrations
nodes.rationale: Lock on a fixed key before reading schema_migrations so two deploys cannot both run the same file. Session lock; take it on a dedicated client.

nodes.label: Expand and contract migrations
nodes.rationale: Old and new code run together during rollout. Add nullable columns first, deploy writers of both, drop later. A rename is three deploys. Prefer roll-forward over downs in production.

nodes.label: MongoClient
nodes.rationale: MongoClient is the pool and topology monitor — one per process, default maxPoolSize 100. connect() at boot turns a bad URL into a failed deploy.

nodes.label: ObjectId vs string _id
nodes.rationale: BSON equality is type-strict: findOne({_id: urlString}) returns null forever. Wrap with new ObjectId after ObjectId.isValid.

nodes.label: w=majority write concern
nodes.rationale: Majority acknowledgement survives failover. Single-node ack is faster and can lose the write when the primary steps down.

nodes.label: Mongoose validators skip updates
nodes.rationale: updateOne/findOneAndUpdate skip validators because no document is hydrated. pre('save') likewise does not fire for updates — password hashing in that hook stores plaintext.

nodes.label: Mongoose .lean()
nodes.rationale: Returns plain objects instead of hydrated documents — 136 ms vs 57 ms for 5001 docs. Lose save(), virtuals, getters. Default on reads that go to JSON.

nodes.label: N+1 query
nodes.rationale: One query for the list plus one per item. Cost is round trips, not query work — 101 queries 111 ms vs 2 batched 7 ms on localhost. Promise.all makes pool exhaustion worse.

nodes.label: Batch with ANY / $in
nodes.rationale: Collect parent ids, one child query with = ANY($1) or $in, group in memory. Works across services where a join is impossible. DataLoader is this per tick.

nodes.label: DatabaseSync
nodes.rationale: Bundled SQLite 3.53.3, fully synchronous because it is a local file. Slow queries block the event loop. Not a networked PostgreSQL replacement.

nodes.label: SQLite autocommit vs explicit transaction
nodes.rationale: Each write outside a transaction is its own fsync. 1000 inserts: 66 ms autocommit vs 1 ms in one BEGIN/COMMIT.

nodes.label: SQL placeholders $1
nodes.rationale: Parameters are bound after the statement is planned, so values cannot become syntax. Identifiers (ORDER BY column) cannot be parameters — use an allow-list.

nodes.label: Simple query protocol stacked statements
nodes.rationale: pool.query with no parameters uses the simple protocol, which runs multiple semicolon-separated statements — DROP TABLE works. Any parameter switches to extended protocol (42601).

nodes.label: MongoDB operator injection
nodes.rationale: JSON body {password: {$ne: null}} matches any password. Validate types at the boundary and compare with {$eq: String(value)}. Disable $where.

nodes.label: pg int8 and numeric as strings
nodes.rationale: bigint exceeds 2^53 and numeric is arbitrary-precision decimal. Returning a float would corrupt money. count(*) + 1 concatenates to "50001".

nodes.label: pg date local-midnight trap
nodes.rationale: A DATE becomes a JS Date at local midnight, then JSON.stringify ships yesterday in UTC+offsets. Keep DATE as a string via setTypeParser(1082).

nodes.label: PostgreSQL SQLSTATE error codes
nodes.rationale: Match err.code not err.message. 23505 unique → 409; 25P02 aborted transaction; 57014 statement_timeout; 53300 too many clients.

nodes.label: Drizzle SQL-first schema
nodes.rationale: Schema is TypeScript; queries compose into SQL you can print with .toSQL(). Sits on your pg.Pool. Safer default when queries get non-trivial.

nodes.label: Prisma 7 driver adapter
nodes.rationale: url in datasource is a hard error (P1012); URL moves to prisma.config.ts. Client requires PrismaPg adapter over a pg pool.

nodes.label: Prisma include is two queries
nodes.rationale: include issues a second IN (...) query, not a join. Batched, not N+1, but nested includes multiply round trips.

nodes.label: Read-your-own-writes
nodes.rationale: Async replica can miss a just-committed write — measured 0 rows on idle localhost. Pin post-write reads to primary via ALS, endpoint intent, or session pin.

nodes.label: Primary and replica pools
nodes.rationale: Replica is physically read-only (25006 / pg_is_in_recovery). Adds read capacity, not latency. A transaction must stay entirely on the primary.

nodes.label: Driver-type boundary
nodes.rationale: One module owns SQL and mapping so business logic never sees rows, snake_case, Number(bigint), or 23505. Domain tests then need no database.

nodes.label: Retry and backoff on transient failures
Transient database errors
nodes.rationale: Retry ECONNREFUSED/57P01/08006 and 40001/40P01 (serialization/deadlock). Never retry 23505, 42601, 28P01. Retry the whole transaction from BEGIN, never one statement (25P02).

nodes.label: Idempotent write retry
nodes.rationale: A timeout is not knowing whether the write committed. Retry only reads or writes keyed with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. Mongo already retries once via retryWrites.

nodes.label: pool.query BEGIN bug
nodes.rationale: Each pool.query may use a different connection. Concurrent flows can ROLLBACK each other's transactions. Appears to work when the process is idle.

nodes.label: withTransaction helper
nodes.rationale: Checkout one client, BEGIN, run fn(client), COMMIT or ROLLBACK, release in finally. Propagate via explicit executor or AsyncLocalStorage. No HTTP inside a transaction.

nodes.label: 25P02 aborted transaction
nodes.rationale: A failed statement poisons the Postgres transaction. Further commands return 25P02 until ROLLBACK. Continue only via SAVEPOINT / ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT.

nodes.label: Mongo session.withTransaction
nodes.rationale: Requires a replica set. Every operation must pass {session} or it commits independently. withTransaction retries the callback — it must be idempotent.

nodes.label: Full jitter
nodes.rationale: random(0, backoff) breaks synchronized retry waves. 500 clients no-jitter all landed in one 100 ms bucket; full jitter max bucket 122. Equal jitter when a minimum spacing is required.

nodes.label: Thundering herd of retries
nodes.rationale: Correlated failures plus deterministic backoff make every client retry at once, knocking a recovering service over again. Backoff sets rate; jitter breaks sync. A circuit breaker stops calls.

nodes.label: mapLimit bounded parallelism
nodes.rationale: Promise.all starts everything at once (peak 200 for 200 items). N runners pull a shared synchronous index. Bind limit to the scarcest resource; count the product across layers.

nodes.label: Dead-letter queue
nodes.rationale: Where poison jobs go when retrying no longer helps. BullMQ's failed set is not a DLQ — it mixes today's transients with last month's poison. Store full payload, error, attempts, correlation id.

nodes.label: UnrecoverableError
nodes.rationale: A 4xx other than 429 should die on the first attempt. Classify the error rather than counting retries. Replay into the original queue with a derived jobId and idempotent handlers.

nodes.label: Deadline propagation
nodes.rationale: Thread one AbortSignal through every layer so a cancelled request stops the DB, outbound calls and worker slot it started.

nodes.label: AbortSignal.any composition
nodes.rationale: Compose timeout, client disconnect and shutdown; whichever fires first cancels the shared signal.

nodes.label: Cooperative cancellation
nodes.rationale: A signal is not preemptive. Loops must throwIfAborted; a synchronous JSON.parse cannot be interrupted.

nodes.label: Propagation stops at the queue
nodes.rationale: A cancelled request must not cancel work already enqueued or already committed.

nodes.label: Graceful worker shutdown
nodes.rationale: On SIGTERM stop claiming, finish in-flight jobs, then close pool and Redis. Close worker first.

nodes.label: SIGKILL leaves job active
nodes.rationale: SIGKILL mid-job leaves active:1 with no error. Recovered only when the visibility timeout expires.

nodes.label: Acknowledge last
nodes.rationale: Ack after the durable effect. Ack first plus crash is silent loss; ack last plus crash is a duplicate.

nodes.label: Exec-form PID 1
nodes.rationale: CMD npm run worker makes a shell PID 1; SIGTERM never reaches node. Use CMD ["node", "src/worker.js"].

nodes.label: Job idempotency
nodes.rationale: Every job will run twice because delivery is at-least-once. A non-repeatable handler is a pending incident.

nodes.label: Domain-derived idempotency key
nodes.rationale: order-paid-email:${orderId} is stable across attempts. crypto.randomUUID() inside the job deduplicates nothing.

nodes.label: jobId vs handler dedup
nodes.rationale: jobId stops a duplicate enqueue. Only a handler-level unique insert stops redelivery of a claimed job.

nodes.label: Ledger-guarded balance update
nodes.rationale: Insert a ledger row on conflict do nothing, then apply the delta only if rowCount is 1, in one transaction.

nodes.label: Job queue four properties
nodes.rationale: Durable store, exclusive claim, visibility timeout, acknowledgement. Exactly-once is not on the list.

nodes.label: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED claim
nodes.rationale: Atomic update ... where id = (select ... for update skip locked limit 1) returning. skip locked avoids serializing workers.

nodes.label: BullMQ Redis queue
nodes.rationale: Retries, backoff, delayed jobs and dashboards already written. Enqueue is not transactional with the app database.

nodes.label: Identifier-only job payload
nodes.rationale: Put {orderId}, not the order. The job runs later; a copied object is stale and leaks PII into another store.

nodes.label: At-least-once delivery
nodes.rationale: No queue offers exactly-once. A worker can finish and die before ack; the timeout redelivers.

nodes.label: Outbound side-effects as jobs
nodes.rationale: Email, webhooks and CRM calls belong on the queue so a provider outage delays a job instead of failing checkout.

nodes.label: Outbound job four properties
nodes.rationale: Idempotent on a domain key, bounded by a timeout, classified 4xx vs 5xx/429, recorded locally.

nodes.label: Webhook fan-out
nodes.rationale: One dispatcher enqueues one delivery job per subscriber. A loop over N subscribers retries the ones that already succeeded.

nodes.label: Stalled job
nodes.rationale: The worker vanished. Nothing is reported; attemptsMade does not increase. Only the expiring lease recovers it.

nodes.label: Visibility timeout
nodes.rationale: BullMQ lockDuration or locked_until. Set above p99 duration. A job that outlives it is claimed twice.

nodes.label: UnrecoverableError
nodes.rationale: 4xx except 429 fail permanently. Retrying a 422 turns a clear error into a slow mystery.

nodes.label: Retry only transient and safe
nodes.rationale: Both questions must be yes. A timeout is transient but retrying an unguarded POST /charge duplicates money.

nodes.label: Timeout is unknown not failure
nodes.rationale: The request may have completed after you stopped waiting. The retry is a second execution.

nodes.label: Retry at one layer
nodes.rationale: Client × service × job attempts multiply (5×5×5=125). Pick the outermost layer that knows the operation.

nodes.label: Throw and let the queue retry
nodes.rationale: An inner retry loop multiplies attempts and holds the worker slot while sleeping.

nodes.label: setInterval is not a scheduler
nodes.rationale: It drifts, overlaps, runs once per process, and dies on restart.

nodes.label: pg_try_advisory_lock schedule lock
nodes.rationale: Must use a checked-out client. pool.query can reuse one session so both instances report true.

nodes.label: Queue-owned repeatable jobs
nodes.rationale: BullMQ upsertJobScheduler or a platform CronJob: one run across N workers, survives deploys.

nodes.label: Catch up from state not clock
nodes.rationale: Process where processed_at is null, not where created_at::date = today. A late run then self-heals.

nodes.label: Request path minimum
nodes.rationale: Keep only what the next screen depends on. Email, media, exports and fan-out are jobs.

nodes.label: Event-loop blocking in handlers
nodes.rationale: 120 ms CPU produced 1246 ms p95 at 10 concurrent vs 19 ms queued. One loop serializes everyone.

nodes.label: 202 Accepted for queued work
nodes.rationale: 200 lies that the work is done. 202 plus a status the client can read.

nodes.label: Fake queue after res.json
nodes.rationale: Work after the response has no retry, no visibility and dies on deploy.

nodes.label: Store UTC convert at the edge
nodes.rationale: An instant is unambiguous. A calendar date depends on who is looking. Store the user's timezone.

nodes.label: timestamptz not timestamp
nodes.rationale: timestamptz stores an instant. timestamp is a wall-clock reading with no zone.

nodes.label: Calendar vs elapsed arithmetic
nodes.rationale: Adding 7*24h across DST moved 7:00 a.m. New York to 8:00 a.m. Use calendar arithmetic in a named zone.

nodes.label: Midnight stored as an instant
nodes.rationale: Compute the deadline once in the zone that owns the rule. Then expires_at <= now() is zone-independent.

nodes.label: fetch has no default timeout
nodes.rationale: Node fetch waits as long as the socket stays open. AbortSignal.timeout(ms) is the built-in bound.

nodes.label: Timeout budget
nodes.rationale: One deadline for the operation; each step gets remaining time. Three 5s timeouts are a 15s request.

nodes.label: Timeouts shrink down the stack
nodes.rationale: A caller's timeout must exceed the callee's. Otherwise the client gives up while you still hold resources.

nodes.label: statement_timeout vs query_timeout
nodes.rationale: statement_timeout is server-enforced and cancels the query. query_timeout only stops the client wait.

nodes.label: Dual-write problem
nodes.rationale: A row and a queue message cannot commit together. Reversing order or try/catch leaves a new window.

nodes.label: Transactional outbox
nodes.rationale: Insert the event in the same database transaction as the business row. One commit, no divergence.

nodes.label: Outbox relay
nodes.rationale: Mark published_at then enqueue. Crash republishes. At-least-once plus jobId outbox:${id}.

nodes.label: Postgres jobs table is the outbox
nodes.rationale: When the queue is the same database, writing the jobs row inside the transaction needs no relay.

nodes.label: Worker as a separate process
nodes.rationale: Same image, two entry points. CPU isolation, independent scale, independent failure.

nodes.label: Worker concurrency
nodes.rationale: In-flight promises on one event loop. Helps I/O, not CPU. Must match the DB pool size.

nodes.label: Split queues by latency
nodes.rationale: Receipts on a fast queue, exports on a bulk one. A shared queue lets video starve password resets.

nodes.label: Oldest-job age alert
nodes.rationale: A stopped worker produces no errors. Alert on oldest waiting job age and completion rate.

nodes.label: Audit event
nodes.rationale: Actor, closed-vocab action, target, before/after, outcome, requestId. Written next to the decision.

nodes.label: HMAC hash chain
nodes.rationale: Each record MACs a canonical body plus prev. Edit or mid-chain delete breaks verification.

nodes.label: External head-MAC anchor
nodes.rationale: Truncating the end leaves a shorter valid chain. Publish the head MAC somewhere the app cannot rewrite.

nodes.label: Append-only is a storage property
nodes.rationale: Opening with 'a' does not stop the same process truncating. Enforce with chattr, object-lock or revoked DELETE.

nodes.label: Authentication
nodes.rationale: Who you are. One chokepoint. 401 means unknown.

nodes.label: Authorization
nodes.rationale: What that identity may do. A decision at every object, not one middleware.

nodes.label: Broken object-level authorization
nodes.rationale: Logged in, no ownership check. Changing the id returns someone else's record. Put owner in the WHERE.

nodes.label: 404 not 403 for foreign objects
nodes.rationale: A 403 confirms the record exists and leaks the thing you are protecting.

nodes.label: Identity in token authz from DB
nodes.rationale: JWT roles are a snapshot. A demoted admin keeps powers until expiry.

nodes.label: CSRF
nodes.rationale: The browser attaches the victim's cookie to an attacker-composed write. Authority problem, not input.

nodes.label: SameSite=Lax
nodes.rationale: Browser default withholds cookies from cross-site POST. Set it explicitly; Node writes no flags by default.

nodes.label: Origin allowlist check
nodes.rationale: Compare new URL(origin).origin. Guard Origin: null. Prefer Origin, fall back to Referer.

nodes.label: Signed double-submit CSRF token
nodes.rationale: HMAC the nonce over the session id. Plain double-submit fails if a subdomain can set the cookie.

nodes.label: CORS does not prevent CSRF
nodes.rationale: CORS governs reading the response. A form POST still writes. Simple requests have no preflight.

nodes.label: JSON.parse is inert
nodes.rationale: JSON.parse cannot construct classes or execute. Risk is eval, new Function, YAML tags, or revive libraries.

nodes.label: Open redirect
nodes.rationale: //evil and /\evil start with / and resolve off-origin. startsWith('/') is not a check.

nodes.label: safeNext origin compare
nodes.rationale: new URL(next, BASE) then compare origin. Return pathname+search+hash, never a full URL.

nodes.label: Mass assignment
nodes.rationale: Spreading req.body onto a record lets the client set isAdmin. Allowlist fields; a denylist fails open on new columns.

nodes.label: AES-256-GCM AEAD
nodes.rationale: Confidentiality plus integrity. CBC decrypts tampered ciphertext with no error; GCM authenticates.

nodes.label: GCM IV reuse
nodes.rationale: Same key and IV produce the same keystream. c1 XOR c2 XOR known plaintext recovers the other message.

nodes.label: Envelope encryption
nodes.rationale: KEK wraps a per-row DEK stored with v and kid. Rotation re-wraps DEKs instead of re-encrypting data.

nodes.label: Ed25519 over RSA for new work
nodes.rationale: Faster keygen and signing, 64-byte signatures, no parameters. RSA only for interoperability or verify-heavy legacy.

nodes.label: HSTS
nodes.rationale: Browser refuses the first plaintext request. The header on HTTP is ignored. includeSubDomains and preload are commitments.

nodes.label: Session cookie flags
nodes.rationale: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, Max-Age, __Host- prefix. Node validates none of them.

nodes.label: X-Forwarded-Proto is forgeable
nodes.rationale: Trust req.socket.encrypted when Node terminates TLS. Trust the header only if a controlled proxy overwrites it.

nodes.label: TLS 1.3 session event
nodes.rationale: getSession() in the connect callback looks like a ticket and does not resume. Cache the 'session' event.

nodes.label: Injection shape
nodes.rationale: Untrusted data concatenated into a string an interpreter reads as instructions. Fix: separate channels, not escaping.

nodes.label: SQL $1 placeholders
nodes.rationale: A parameter can never become a statement. Identifiers cannot be placeholders; allowlist column names.

nodes.label: NoSQL operator injection
nodes.rationale: {"password":{"$ne":null}} logged in as admin. Coerce to string/$eq and validate body shape.

nodes.label: exec vs execFile
nodes.rationale: exec runs a shell. execFile with an args array treats report.txt; id as one filename. shell:true is DEP0190.

nodes.label: Parse don't validate
nodes.rationale: A parser returns a new typed value. The raw body stops existing, so added fields cannot leak through.

nodes.label: Boundary check order
nodes.rationale: Content-type, size cap, JSON.parse, schema. A 20 MB body blocked the loop 40.7 ms before any schema ran.

nodes.label: z.strictObject
nodes.rationale: Reject unknown keys on writes. z.object() strips them; looseObject keeps inherited properties.

nodes.label: z.coerce pitfalls
nodes.rationale: Number("")/[]/null become 0. z.coerce.boolean maps "false" to true. Repeated query keys arrive as arrays.

nodes.label: Validation is not authorization
nodes.rationale: role: z.enum(['user','admin']) is a valid escalation. Omit fields the caller may not set.

nodes.label: TOTP
nodes.rationale: HMAC of the 30-second time step with a shared secret, dynamically truncated to six digits. RFC 6238.

nodes.label: TOTP drift window and replay
nodes.rationale: Accept ±1 step. Record the accepted step and reject anything not newer, or the code is reusable for 90s.

nodes.label: TOTP is not phishing-resistant
nodes.rationale: A proxy can relay the code in its window. WebAuthn/passkeys are origin-bound and will not sign a lookalike.

nodes.label: Hashed MFA recovery codes
nodes.rationale: Ten single-use codes hashed like passwords. Without them, support becomes a weaker recovery path.

nodes.label: HMAC-SHA256
nodes.rationale: SHA-2 is length-extendable, so hash(secret+message) is not a signature. HMAC's inner/outer construction closes that; compare tags with timingSafeEqual.

nodes.label: Modulo bias
nodes.rationale: 256 does not divide 100, so randomBytes(1)[0] % 100 skews buckets; use crypto.randomInt.

nodes.label: CSPRNG APIs
nodes.rationale: Math.random is a recoverable PRNG. randomUUID for ids; randomBytes(32) base64url for secrets.

nodes.label: KeyObject vs Buffer key
nodes.rationale: A Buffer is converted on every HMAC/cipher call; createSecretKey once at startup.

nodes.label: OAuth 2.0
nodes.rationale: Delegated authorization: issues an access token so an app can act on a user's behalf. Says nothing reliable about who the user is.

nodes.label: PKCE
nodes.rationale: Binds the authorization code to the client that started the flow so an intercepted code cannot be redeemed without the verifier.

nodes.label: OAuth state parameter
nodes.rationale: CSRF protection for the callback; without it an attacker can feed their code and link accounts.

nodes.label: Confused deputy via access token
nodes.rationale: An access token is a bearer API credential, not an assertion addressed to you. Validate an ID token whose aud is your client id.

nodes.label: path.join is not a security boundary
nodes.rationale: join normalises .. faithfully: path.join('/srv/app/uploads', '../../../etc/passwd') returns /etc/passwd.

nodes.label: Resolve then verify containment
nodes.rationale: Compare against root + path.sep, not a bare prefix; startsWith(root) matches sibling uploads-evil.

nodes.label: Node Permission Model
nodes.rationale: Blast-radius reduction for your own dependencies, not a sandbox for untrusted code. Policy lives only on the CLI.

nodes.label: --allow-child-process escape
nodes.rationale: The child is a new process with no permission model, so granting it discards every other restriction.

nodes.label: Prototype pollution
nodes.rationale: JSON.parse is inert; damage is a recursive merge that reads target['__proto__'] and writes onto Object.prototype.

nodes.label: Fixed window limiter
nodes.rationale: Boundary permits double the limit: 5/s allowed 10 requests in 80 ms.

nodes.label: INCR then EXPIRE race
nodes.rationale: Death between INCR and EXPIRE leaves ttl -1 and locks that client forever. Use one atomic Lua script.

nodes.label: Fail open vs fail closed
nodes.rationale: Open for fairness APIs; closed for login/payment. Never fail open silently.

nodes.label: Regular expression denial of service
nodes.rationale: A backtracking match runs on the event loop; one request stalls the whole process. Node 24 has no regex timeout.

nodes.label: Content-Security-Policy
nodes.rationale: A CSP with unsafe-inline in script-src is not a CSP. Roll out via Report-Only first.

nodes.label: CORS is not access control
nodes.rationale: CORS relaxes the browser same-origin rule. Dangerous only with cookie auth plus reflected Origin and Allow-Credentials.

nodes.label: Session fixation
nodes.rationale: Rotate the id on every privilege change so a pre-login id cannot ride the authenticated session.

nodes.label: Idle and absolute session timeouts
nodes.rationale: Idle alone lets a daily session live forever; absolute alone logs out active users. Redis TTL cannot express the absolute cap.

nodes.label: Opaque session
nodes.rationale: Default for a single browser app: revocable instantly because the server holds the truth.

nodes.label: JWT
nodes.rationale: Valid until expiry because validity is a signature check. A denylist rebuilds sessions with extra steps.

nodes.label: Short access JWT plus opaque refresh
nodes.rationale: Accept a revocation window equal to the access token lifetime; choose that window deliberately.

nodes.label: Server-side request forgery
nodes.rationale: The server fetches a user URL from inside the network: cloud metadata 169.254.169.254, loopback admin ports, private ranges.

nodes.label: Custom lookup skips literal IPs
nodes.rationale: http.request lookup is never called for a literal IP. Parse-time net.isIP is required alongside connect-time checks.

nodes.label: npm allowScripts
nodes.rationale: npm 12 blocks install scripts unless listed in allowScripts; approval is a reviewable diff.

nodes.label: Provenance attestations
nodes.rationale: Stronger than a registry signature: Sigstore statement that the tarball was built by a specific CI workflow from a specific commit.

nodes.label: min-release-age cooldown
nodes.rationale: Most malicious versions are unpublished within days; refusing anything younger than a week removes nearly the whole window.

nodes.label: Login user enumeration
nodes.rationale: Skipping the password hash for unknown emails is an 83 ms oracle. Hash against a dummy with the same parameters.

nodes.label: extractable false CryptoKey
nodes.rationale: Key material can never be read back into JavaScript; node:crypto KeyObject has no equivalent.

nodes.label: Cross-site scripting
nodes.rationale: An encoding bug, not a filtering bug. Encode on output for the known context.

nodes.label: JSON in a script tag breakout
listen(0) ephemeral port
nodes.rationale: Hardcoded ports race under file concurrency and produce intermittent EADDRINUSE in CI.

nodes.label: Missing await after test ended
nodes.rationale: On Node 24 the test still prints a tick; the file fails. A swallowed catch makes it truly silent.

nodes.label: Consumer-driven contract
nodes.rationale: Consumer owns the schema of fields it actually reads. A generated-from-model contract can never fail.

nodes.label: Coverage is not verification
nodes.rationale: Measures which lines executed, not whether anything was checked. 100% can ship a float-money bug.

nodes.label: Test data factory
nodes.rationale: Valid defaults plus one-field overrides so a schema change is a one-line edit, not forty.

nodes.label: Linter vs formatter
nodes.rationale: A formatter rewrites layout; a linter finds legal but wrong code. They are different jobs.

nodes.label: p99 latency
nodes.rationale: A 45 ms mean can hide a 4 s p99; a page of 100 requests hits the tail every load.

nodes.label: Mocking — mock.fn, mock.method and mock timers
t.mock auto-restore
nodes.rationale: t.mock restores everything it touched when the test ends; the top-level mock does not and leaks into later tests. Use t.mock unless you have a reason not to, or call mock.restoreAll() in afterEach.

nodes.label: mock.method spy versus stub
nodes.rationale: Two arguments spies (original still runs); a third argument stubs. Spy when the real behaviour is harmless.

nodes.label: mock.timers
nodes.rationale: Mock timers and real I/O do not mix — faked setTimeout also fakes a query's internal timeouts. Enable only the APIs you need.

nodes.label: Mocking fetch
nodes.rationale: Fine for unit-testing response mapping. For headers, retries, timeouts or AbortSignal, use a real ephemeral server.

nodes.label: mock.module()
nodes.rationale: Escape hatch for a dependency you cannot inject. Prefer dependency injection: no flag, no import-order rule, no experimental warning.

nodes.label: Module mock import-order trap
nodes.rationale: Mock first, then dynamic-import the module under test. A static import resolves bindings before the mock exists; later await import() returns the cached module.

nodes.label: mock.module Stability 1.0
nodes.rationale: Early development; namedExports already renamed to exports in Node 24. Pin the Node version if the suite depends on it.

nodes.label: node:assert — strict mode and deep equality
node:assert/strict
nodes.rationale: Legacy node:assert uses ==; equal(1, '1') and deepEqual({a:1},{a:'1'}) both pass. An assertion that ignores type is worse than none.

nodes.label: partialDeepStrictEqual
nodes.rationale: Honest use is a response with server-generated fields. Dishonest use is hiding a shape you have not thought about.

nodes.label: node:test
nodes.rationale: No dependency, no transform, no config. A test fails when it throws — that is the whole contract.

nodes.label: node --test file discovery
nodes.rationale: *.spec.mjs is not discovered. A suite named that way runs zero tests and still exits 0.

nodes.label: Test isolation process vs none
nodes.rationale: Default process isolation prevents module state leaking between files. none is a local speed-up, not a CI setting.

nodes.label: Property-based testing
nodes.rationale: Asks whether there are inputs you did not think of. If a property finds nothing, question the generator before concluding the code is correct.

nodes.label: Mutation testing
nodes.rationale: Asks whether tests actually check anything. Surviving mutants at a >= boundary showed 100% line coverage still missed the comparison.

nodes.label: Mutation score
nodes.rationale: Not a target to chase. Equivalent mutants and log-message mutations are not worth killing. 100% is as suspect as 100% coverage.

nodes.label: --test-randomize
nodes.rationale: Finds inter-test coupling. Same three shared-state tests: seed 7 passed entirely, which is why the bug survives in file order.

nodes.label: --test-rerun-failures
nodes.rationale: Replays recorded passes without executing. A test edited to throw still reported green. Local iteration only — never CI.

nodes.label: --experimental-test-tag-filter
nodes.rationale: Key is tags, plural, array. Singular tag: is silently ignored so a filtered CI job can run zero tests and exit 0.

nodes.label: --test-force-exit
nodes.rationale: Legitimate for a third-party leak you cannot close. For your own code it hides a defect that also blocks production shutdown.

nodes.label: --test-shard
nodes.rationale: Safest CI speed-up here — unlike rerun-failures or tag filtering it cannot make a broken suite look green.

nodes.label: Request vs response compatibility direction
nodes.rationale: Response: adding is safe, removing or narrowing is not. Request: relaxing is safe, tightening is not. Same verb, opposite answers.

nodes.label: Expand-migrate-contract
nodes.rationale: A rename is a removal plus an addition. Add the new field, migrate consumers, remove the old only after telemetry shows zero usage.

nodes.label: Adding an enum value to a response
nodes.rationale: Breaking: exhaustive switches and TypeScript unions meet a value they have no branch for. Ship handling first, then emit.

nodes.label: Field meaning change same type
nodes.rationale: Worst change: euros becoming cents validates perfectly and is off by 100. Never redefine a field — add a new one and deprecate.

nodes.label: --test-update-snapshots
nodes.rationale: Blind updates rewrite the expectation and go green. Run without the flag first; a snapshot change is a code review event.

nodes.label: Committed .snapshot file
nodes.rationale: The file is the expected value. Uncommitted, CI regenerates it and the test asserts nothing.

nodes.label: Test doubles — stub, spy, mock, fake
Stub
nodes.rationale: Returns canned values; assert on the result of the code under test. The double you should reach for most often.

nodes.label: Mock (interaction double)
nodes.rationale: Assert on the call only when the call is the behaviour — payments, emails, webhooks. Not loggers or metrics.

nodes.label: Fake
nodes.rationale: A second implementation that can drift. Keep it small and back it with one integration test against the real thing.

nodes.label: Over-mocking
nodes.rationale: Number of doubles equals number of collaborators. Seven doubles for one assertion is a design report: extract pure functions.

nodes.label: Dependency injection
nodes.rationale: Pass the dependency in. Injection needs no flag, no import-order rule, and makes mocking mostly unnecessary.

nodes.label: No DI container in Node
nodes.rationale: A function taking an object already is DI. A container adds indirection and a second language. Wire the graph by hand in main.mjs.

nodes.label: Inject database handle
nodes.rationale: Caller hands a pool normally or a checked-out client inside a transaction, so one transaction can span repositories.

nodes.label: Testcontainers under podman
nodes.rationale: Needs DOCKER_HOST at the rootless podman socket and TESTCONTAINERS_RYUK_DISABLED=true. Without the second, Ryuk fails with an unhelpful log-stream error.

nodes.label: If mocking removes the risk, do not mock
nodes.rationale: A repository is mostly SQL. Mocking pool.query tests that you can write a mock. Draw the unit/integration boundary at I/O, not at one class.

nodes.label: *.itest.mjs separate suite
nodes.rationale: A filename glob cannot be silently wrong. The runner tag filter is experimental and silently matches nothing on tag: instead of tags.

nodes.label: Vitest and Jest — when they earn their place
Vitest
nodes.rationale: Earns its place for a shared frontend runner, jsdom, or first-class TypeScript — not because it tests Node backends better.

nodes.label: Jest
nodes.rationale: Native ESM still needs --experimental-vm-modules plus transform: {}. For a new ESM project in 2026 that is hard to justify.

nodes.label: vi.mock hoisting
nodes.rationale: Vitest's transform hoists vi.mock above imports, so it avoids the import-order trap that mock.module has. Bought with a transform step.

nodes.label: Phase 2 — Async and the event loop
PostgreSQL client/server model
nodes.rationale: One OS process per connection — why connections are expensive enough to pool.

nodes.label: psql
nodes.rationale: The verification tool for the rest of the syllabus. Master the shell before racing ahead to SQL text.

nodes.label: Phase 10 — Indexes and the query planner
Why an index is not used
PostgreSQL object-relational server
nodes.rationale: A long-running program that stores data, enforces rules, and answers SQL over a network protocol — not an embedded library, not SQL syntax alone.

nodes.label: Database cluster
nodes.rationale: One data directory on disk that may contain many databases. The server process writes WAL and data files for that cluster.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL License
nodes.rationale: BSD-style permissive license; no single commercial owner of core. The engine is free; managed hosting is the product.

nodes.label: App is a guest with a connection
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL owns durable multi-user truth; the Node process stays a client. You pay an external process to run, back up, and upgrade.

nodes.label: Process-per-connection backend
nodes.rationale: Each client connection is a dedicated OS backend that holds session state and can crash without taking down other clients.

nodes.label: max_connections
nodes.rationale: Server-wide cap on concurrent backends. Every app, admin session, and tool shares that budget (sandbox default 100).

nodes.label: Node connection pool
nodes.rationale: One global Pool at module scope reuses backends. pool.query borrows a client; it does not fork a new process per query.

nodes.label: Connection approximates a process
nodes.rationale: Isolation and simpler memory accounting cost RAM and startup per backend. That cost is why PgBouncer exists (Phase 13).

nodes.label: Cluster database schema table
nodes.rationale: You connect to a database. Schemas are folders of names inside one database, not separate databases.

nodes.label: search_path
nodes.rationale: Default is "$user", public. Unqualified names resolve in that order. Schema is session state, changeable with SET search_path.

nodes.label: Qualify names in migrations
nodes.rationale: Always write app.users in migrations and multi-schema apps so a path change cannot silently hit another table.

nodes.label: shared_buffers
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL's shared 8 KB page cache used by all backends. Alpine default measured at 128MB; production is tuned higher.

nodes.label: OS page cache
nodes.rationale: Kernel caches file pages the server read or wrote. A shared_buffers miss may still be fast if the OS cache is warm.

nodes.label: Pooling does not replace shared buffers
nodes.rationale: Pooling reuses backends; shared buffers cache data pages. Different layers. Too-large shared_buffers fights the OS cache.

nodes.label: Write-ahead log
nodes.rationale: Every committed change is recorded in WAL before it is treated as durable. COMMIT succeeds only after the needed WAL is flushed.

nodes.label: WAL then heap double write
nodes.rationale: Once to WAL immediately for durability; later to heap/index via dirty shared buffers, checkpoints, and the background writer.

nodes.label: wal_level replica
nodes.rationale: Usual default on PostgreSQL 18.4; supports physical replication. Never delete WAL files by hand.

nodes.label: Role is user and group
nodes.rationale: A user is a role with LOGIN; a group is a role usually without LOGIN used for membership. One catalog concept.

nodes.label: session_user vs current_user
nodes.rationale: session_user is who authenticated; current_user can change after SET ROLE. Node uses the connection-string role.

nodes.label: Least-privilege app role
nodes.rationale: Container bootstrap is a superuser — fine for learning, wrong as the production app role. App DML only; not arbitrary DDL.

nodes.label: Container-first local Postgres
nodes.rationale: Pin major (postgres:18-alpine), reset in one command, match CI. Prefer that over a host distro package until you need native.

nodes.label: 127.0.0.1 and published port 55432
nodes.rationale: Node resolves localhost to ::1 first; IPv4 publishes fail. Non-default 55432:5432 avoids colliding with a host Postgres on 5432.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL connection URI
nodes.rationale: postgresql://USER:PASSWORD@HOST:PORT/DATABASE, or PGHOST/PGPORT/PGUSER/PGPASSWORD/PGDATABASE. DATABASE_URL is an app convention, not read by psql.

nodes.label: pg_hba.conf
nodes.rationale: Decides who may connect how (trust, scram-sha-256, peer) from which addresses. Managed providers force TLS plus password/SCRAM.

nodes.label: SQLSTATE 28P01
nodes.rationale: invalid_password / authentication failure. Map this when diagnosing auth failures from Node.

nodes.label: inet_server_port vs published port
nodes.rationale: inet_server_port() is the listen port inside the container (5432), not the host-published port (55432).

nodes.label: Never log the connection string
nodes.rationale: URIs embed secrets. Error handlers and APM breadcrumbs become credential stores if they print DATABASE_URL.

nodes.label: Postmaster
nodes.rationale: Supervisor that accepts connections and starts backends. Managed by the service or container; do not kill random postgres PIDs.

nodes.label: Client backend
nodes.rationale: The process that runs SQL for one connection. Client backends scale with connections.

nodes.label: Background workers
nodes.rationale: WAL writer, checkpointer, background writer, autovacuum launcher, I/O workers, logical replication launcher — labeled in pg_stat_activity.backend_type.

nodes.label: Major vs minor version
nodes.rationale: 17→18 needs pg_upgrade, dump/restore, or logical replication. 18.3→18.4 is the same on-disk major: install and restart.

nodes.label: Five-year major support
nodes.rationale: A new major roughly once a year; each major is supported about five years. Upgrade minors promptly; treat majors as a project.

nodes.label: server_version_num 180004
nodes.rationale: 180004 means major 18, minor 4. Gate multi-major app code with version_num; pin postgres:18-alpine.

nodes.label: template0
nodes.rationale: Pristine factory image. datallowconn is usually false; use only as TEMPLATE template0 when template1 is dirty.

nodes.label: template1
nodes.rationale: Default source for CREATE DATABASE. Custom encodings or extensions installed here appear in every new database.

nodes.label: CREATE DATABASE copies a template
nodes.rationale: Requires superuser or CREATEDB. App runtime roles must not. Day-to-day apps connect and migrate; CREATE DATABASE is provisioning.

nodes.label: Engine folklore that no longer holds
nodes.rationale: MySQL 8 is strict by default (CHECK, ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY). SQLite has transactional DDL. Sequence gaps happen on every engine.

nodes.label: MySQL transactional DDL outlier
nodes.rationale: SQLite sides with PostgreSQL on transactional DDL. MySQL cannot roll back CREATE TABLE — the difference that changes a migration plan.

nodes.label: Differences that survive measurement
nodes.rationale: Isolation default, identifier case folding (createdAt → createdat), RETURNING vs UPDATE…LIMIT, BOOLEAN, concurrency ceiling, JS driver types.

nodes.label: Columns vs jsonb phase gate
nodes.rationale: Move on when you can choose columns vs jsonb and know when FTS or partitioning is justified.

nodes.label: jsonb operators
nodes.rationale: Master-tier: arrow accessors and containment.

nodes.label: Full-text search tsvector
nodes.rationale: Understand-tier: tsvector. Justified only when search is a real requirement — the phase gate.

nodes.label: Transactional outbox
nodes.rationale: Events that cannot be lost: write the event in the same transaction as the business row.

nodes.label: LISTEN NOTIFY
nodes.rationale: At-most-once delivery. Not a durable event bus.

nodes.label: Least privilege GRANT REVOKE
nodes.rationale: Master-tier: Roles, GRANT and REVOKE. Phase gate: privileges are least.

nodes.label: PgBouncer transaction vs session pool
nodes.rationale: External pooler exists because process-per-connection is expensive. Transaction vs session pool is the decision.

nodes.label: Physical backup and PITR
nodes.rationale: WAL archiving plus a base backup. Phase gate: restore a backup once.

nodes.label: No-new-sandboxes validation
nodes.rationale: Topics 07–18 validated against official docs. No page carries a console block that was not produced by a run that happened.

nodes.label: Secrets: no URI in logs
nodes.rationale: Master-tier secrets page. Completes the Phase 13 gate: secrets are safe.

nodes.label: Default type stack
nodes.rationale: Default to bigint + text + timestamptz + numeric for money. Never write = NULL.

nodes.label: Money never in float
nodes.rationale: Master-tier: numeric vs float. Modelling money covers currency, rounding, allocation.

nodes.label: IDENTITY over serial
nodes.rationale: Master-tier primary keys. Phase gate: 1-N and N-N with identity PKs, FKs, and CHECKs without an ORM.

nodes.label: Transactional DDL
nodes.rationale: Wrap migrations in a transaction. PostgreSQL can roll back CREATE TABLE; MySQL cannot.

nodes.label: Parameterized queries
nodes.rationale: Never string-build values. Phase gate: INSERT…RETURNING, UPDATE with WHERE, parameterize every user value.

nodes.label: INSERT RETURNING
nodes.rationale: Ids without a second query. A surviving difference versus engines that lack RETURNING.

nodes.label: OFFSET degrades
nodes.rationale: Master-tier LIMIT/OFFSET. Keyset pagination in Phase 9 is the replacement.

nodes.label: LEFT JOIN plus WHERE bug
nodes.rationale: Manufactured NULLs filtered by WHERE turn a LEFT JOIN into an INNER JOIN. Explain from evaluation order.

nodes.label: NOT IN NULL trap
nodes.rationale: EXISTS beats JOIN + DISTINCT. NOT IN over a nullable set returns nothing. Phase 6 repeats the same trap for subqueries.

nodes.label: HAVING vs WHERE
nodes.rationale: Filter groups, not rows. WHERE runs before grouping.

nodes.label: CTE as optimization fence
nodes.rationale: A name for a subquery — and when it is a fence. Phase gate: say whether a CTE is inlined or fenced.

nodes.label: Pool at module scope
nodes.rationale: Master-tier wiring. Phase gate: open a pool, parameterize, map 23505, never leak clients.

nodes.label: Forward-only migrations
nodes.rationale: Migrate forward-only and seed idempotently without runtime DDL in requests. IF NOT EXISTS is not migrations.

nodes.label: Allowlisted dynamic WHERE
nodes.rationale: Param array plus identifier allowlists. Phase gate: list/filter/sort is allowlisted; transactions use try/catch/finally release.

nodes.label: The folklore that no longer holds
Default isolation READ COMMITTED vs REPEATABLE READ
Identical username and password auth errors
Includes are not a migration runner
The query buffer and the editor
VACUUM does not shrink index files
CIC cannot run in a transaction
Expression index
nodes.rationale: Index the function result when the query cannot leave the column bare. The query must spell the expression identically; each queried expression needs its own index.

nodes.label: IMMUTABLE index expression
nodes.rationale: Anything whose result depends on session TimeZone or now() is STABLE, not IMMUTABLE, and cannot be indexed (42P17). Name the zone: date_trunc('day', ts, 'UTC') or (ts AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')::date.

nodes.label: Expression-index statistics
nodes.rationale: ANALYZE collects statistics for the expression itself under the index name in pg_stats, so the planner stops guessing selectivity.

nodes.label: Case-insensitive unique index
nodes.rationale: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ON users (lower(email)) enforces case-insensitive uniqueness without citext.

nodes.label: Referencing-side FK index
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL indexes the referenced PK/UNIQUE side automatically but never the referencing column. Without that index every parent DELETE scans the child table.

nodes.label: Missing FK index audit
nodes.rationale: Query pg_constraint contype='f' for FKs whose leading index columns do not match conkey, requiring indisvalid so a failed CONCURRENTLY build does not count.

nodes.label: GIN for jsonb, arrays and full text; pg_trgm for LIKE
GIN index
nodes.rationale: GIN indexes the parts of a value — jsonb keys, array elements, lexemes, trigrams — making @>, @@, ? and LIKE '%x%' indexable. Selective needles win; a 16% match was slower than seq scan.

nodes.label: jsonb_ops
nodes.rationale: Default GIN opclass stores keys and values separately. Serves @> and existence operators ? / ?| / ?&.

nodes.label: jsonb_path_ops
nodes.rationale: Hashes whole paths; smaller and faster for @> only. Existence operators fall back to sequential scan.

nodes.label: pg_trgm gin_trgm_ops
nodes.rationale: Trigram GIN makes infix LIKE/ILIKE indexable. Patterns shorter than three characters produce too few distinguishing trigrams and can be slower than a seq scan.

nodes.label: GIN pending list
nodes.rationale: GIN buffers inserts in a pending list (gin_pending_list_limit 4MB). Cost is deferred to VACUUM or a query that scans the unmerged list; fastupdate=off pays on insert instead.

nodes.label: gist_trgm_ops distance ordering
nodes.rationale: ORDER BY col <-> 'text' is nearest-neighbour. GIN cannot do it; gist_trgm_ops can, at a larger index size.

nodes.label: BRIN index
nodes.rationale: Block Range INdex stores min/max per 128-page range. Tiny filter, not a lookup; needs physical correlation near ±1. 24 kB vs 64 MB B-tree on 3M ordered rows.

nodes.label: Physical correlation
nodes.rationale: pg_stats.correlation near 1 or −1 makes BRIN useful. Shuffled data at 0.0119 caused the planner to ignore the BRIN index entirely.

nodes.label: Hash index
nodes.rationale: Equality only. Cannot UNIQUE (0A000), range, ORDER BY, INCLUDE, or index-only scans. Crash-safe since PostgreSQL 10. Smaller on wide keys.

nodes.label: GiST index
nodes.rationale: Framework for overlap, containment and distance on types with no total order: ranges, PostGIS, inet, nearest-neighbour.

nodes.label: Exclusion constraint
nodes.rationale: EXCLUDE USING gist (room WITH =, during WITH &&) raises 23P01 on overlap. Needs btree_gist for equality types. Cannot be expressed with UNIQUE or CHECK.

nodes.label: Why an index is not being used
Function-wrapped column
nodes.rationale: lower(email) or created_at::date defeats a B-tree on the bare column. Index the expression or rewrite so the column is bare.

nodes.label: Cast on the indexed side
nodes.rationale: Casting the indexed column casts every row and skips the index. Cast the literal or parameter instead. Hand-added :: is the trap; pg sends untyped text.

nodes.label: Low selectivity
nodes.rationale: When a value matches most of the table the planner correctly ignores the index. Forcing it for 99.89% active rows was slower than seq scan.

nodes.label: Stale planner statistics
nodes.rationale: A never-analyzed table has reltuples=-1 (unknown). Stale stats after 200× growth estimated 1 row vs 400001 actual and chose a bad index-only scan.

nodes.label: Non-indexable predicate shape
nodes.rationale: <> , NOT IN and leading-wildcard LIKE cannot seek a B-tree. OR is fine only if every branch has its own usable index (BitmapOr).

nodes.label: Index-only scans, INCLUDE and the visibility map
Index-only scan
nodes.rationale: Answers from the index without touching the heap when every selected column is in the index and the visibility map marks pages all-visible.

nodes.label: Visibility map
nodes.rationale: VACUUM sets all-visible bits (relallvisible). A freshly loaded table has relallvisible=0 so a covering index still heap-scans.

nodes.label: INCLUDE columns
nodes.rationale: Payload stored in index leaves but not part of the sort key: returnable, not searchable or sortable. Required when UNIQUE must stay on the key alone.

nodes.label: Heap Fetches
nodes.rationale: Count of rows that still needed a heap visit during an index-only scan. One UPDATE took Heap Fetches from 0 to 58.

nodes.label: Leftmost-prefix rule
nodes.rationale: Index on (a,b,c) serves (a), (a,b), (a,b,c) but not b or c alone. Phone-book order: surname then first name.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL 18 skip scan
nodes.rationale: Can probe once per distinct leading value when that column has few distincts (Index Searches: 7). Not chosen for 5000-value leading columns.

nodes.label: Equality then range column order
nodes.rationale: Put equality predicates first, then the range/sort column. (user_id, created_at) used 23 buffers vs 396 for the reverse order.

nodes.label: Partial index
nodes.rationale: CREATE INDEX ... WHERE indexes only matching rows. 8792 kB full vs 104 kB for 4000 live of 400000. Writes to the other 99% never touch it.

nodes.label: Partial-index predicate implication
nodes.rationale: The planner must prove the query WHERE implies the index WHERE. Write the predicate as a literal, not a parameter, so generic plans still match.

nodes.label: Partial UNIQUE
nodes.rationale: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ON slugs (slug) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL: any number of deleted duplicates, exactly one live. Still raises 23505.

nodes.label: pg_stat_statements
nodes.rationale: Ranks statements by total time after normalising literals to $n. Requires shared_preload_libraries and a restart.

nodes.label: total_exec_time ranking
nodes.rationale: Order by total, not mean. A 18 ms query run 500 times (9240 ms) outranks an 87 ms query run twice (173 ms).

nodes.label: shared_preload_libraries
nodes.rationale: pg_stat_statements hooks the executor and must be preloaded. CREATE EXTENSION alone leaves an empty view.

nodes.label: pg_stat_statements.max dealloc
nodes.rationale: Default 5000 distinct normalised statements. Overflow evicts least-executed; growing dealloc means raise max or stop unparameterised IN-list churn.

nodes.label: Seq scan vs index scan vs bitmap heap scan
Sequential scan
nodes.rationale: Correct when most of the table qualifies. Forced index scan on 80% of 500k rows was 3× slower with 400358 vs 3712 buffers.

nodes.label: Index scan
nodes.rationale: Walk the index and fetch each heap row. Chosen for a handful of rows; random I/O but very few of them.

nodes.label: Bitmap heap scan
nodes.rationale: Bitmap Index Scan collects locations, then heap is read in physical order. Recheck Cond / Heap Blocks: lossy= means the bitmap exceeded work_mem.

nodes.label: random_page_cost
nodes.rationale: Default 4.0 assumes spinning disks. On SSD ~1.1 makes index scans more attractive. Change this instead of disable_seqscan.

nodes.label: ANALYZE
nodes.rationale: The planner plans against a sample, not live data. Last step of every bulk load. Takes SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE so reads and writes continue.

nodes.label: pg_stats
nodes.rationale: null_frac, n_distinct, most_common_vals/freqs, correlation. n_distinct -1 means unique per row; negative fraction scales with table size. reltuples=-1 means never analyzed.

nodes.label: Extended statistics
nodes.rationale: CREATE STATISTICS (dependencies, ndistinct, mcv) ON correlated columns. Independence assumed otherwise: 33607 estimated vs 100000 actual, corrected to 100990.

nodes.label: default_statistics_target
nodes.rationale: Histogram buckets and MCV count. Raise per column with ALTER COLUMN SET STATISTICS, not globally. Target 1000 took 1309 ms ANALYZE.

nodes.label: autovacuum analyze threshold
nodes.rationale: Fires at threshold + scale_factor × reltuples (50 + 10%). Too late on large tables; lower autovacuum_analyze_scale_factor to 0.01.

nodes.label: idx_scan
nodes.rationale: How many times the planner chose the index. Zero after a full business cycle is a drop candidate, but exclude UNIQUE, check stats_reset, replicas, and quarterly jobs.

nodes.label: Duplicate indexes
nodes.rationale: Group pg_index by indrelid, indkey, indclass, indexprs, indpred, indisunique. A PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE already is an index; adding another on the same column is dead weight.

nodes.label: stats_fetch_consistency cache
nodes.rationale: idx_scan lags: backends flush on a timer and the reader caches a snapshot. pg_stat_clear_snapshot() plus a wait; never judge unused from seconds-old reads.

nodes.label: Index
nodes.rationale: A second sorted copy of some columns maintained on every write so some SELECTs can stop scanning. A PRIMARY KEY is already a unique index.

nodes.label: Index write cost
nodes.rationale: One index nearly doubled a 200000-row insert (1239→2266 ms); three tripled it (4035 ms) with 36 MB of indexes vs 15 MB heap. Key width, not column count, drives size.

nodes.label: ACID
nodes.rationale: Atomicity via abort-on-error, consistency via constraints, isolation via snapshots, durability via WAL flush before COMMIT returns.

nodes.label: Aborted transaction 25P02
nodes.rationale: After a statement error the transaction accepts nothing but ROLLBACK. COMMIT on an aborted transaction is silently executed as ROLLBACK.

nodes.label: DEFERRABLE constraint
nodes.rationale: UNIQUE/PK/EXCLUDE/FK can be deferred to commit, enabling legal intermediate states such as a unique-column swap. CHECK and NOT NULL are always immediate.

nodes.label: synchronous_commit
nodes.rationale: Off buys ~6× on 500 single-row commits (1042→170 ms) for a window of lost recent commits, not corruption. One transaction of 500 inserts was faster (128 ms) with durability on.

nodes.label: WAL
nodes.rationale: Every change writes a WAL record before the data file. Measured 112 bytes for one small UPDATE. WAL volume is what replication and PITR ship.

nodes.label: Advisory lock
nodes.rationale: Named mutex keyed by a number, not a row. For single-runner cron, migrations, file imports. Advisory: the database enforces the lock, not the invariant.

nodes.label: pg_try_advisory_lock
nodes.rationale: Never waits; returns true/false immediately. Re-entrant and reference-counted within a session. Two-int form is a separate key space from the bigint form.

nodes.label: Session vs transaction advisory lock
nodes.rationale: Prefer pg_advisory_xact_lock — released at COMMIT/ROLLBACK and cannot leak. Session locks survive COMMIT and a pooled connection can return still holding them; release(true) if state is unknown.

nodes.label: Autocommit
nodes.rationale: Every unwrapped statement is its own transaction. Two pool.query calls get two xids.

nodes.label: pool.query BEGIN bug
nodes.rationale: BEGIN via pool.query works on an idle pool (same connection) and fails under load: UPDATE autocommits on another backend while ROLLBACK hits an empty transaction. Load-dependent.

nodes.label: withTransaction helper
nodes.rationale: pool.connect(), BEGIN on that client, COMMIT, ROLLBACK.catch in catch, release() in finally. Isolation goes on BEGIN itself (25001 if SET after first query). Nested BEGIN only warns 25001.

nodes.label: Deadlock 40P01
nodes.rationale: Cycle of lock waits. After deadlock_timeout PostgreSQL aborts the cheaper victim with 40P01. DETAIL names both processes; queries are only in the server log.

nodes.label: Consistent lock order
nodes.rationale: The fix is locking rows in a stable order via SELECT ... ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE, not retry. Opposite order deadlocked in 1155 ms; same order both committed in 326 ms.

nodes.label: deadlock_timeout
nodes.rationale: Default 1s. PostgreSQL does not check for cycles on every wait. Every deadlock costs at least that second. log_lock_waits logs waits past this threshold.

nodes.label: Idle in transaction
nodes.rationale: BEGIN then silence. wait_event=ClientRead: the server waits on the client. Holds a pool slot, locks, and possibly the vacuum horizon. Distinct from idle (no transaction).

nodes.label: idle_in_transaction_session_timeout
nodes.rationale: Kills a backend idle in transaction longer than N (25P03). statement_timeout does not help — no statement is running. Terminates the connection; pg emits 'error', not a rejected promise.

nodes.label: transaction_timeout
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL 17+. Kills any transaction older than N whether idle or busy (25P04). Covers the always-active long batch the idle timeout misses.
