nodes.label: REPEATABLE READ
nodes.rationale: One snapshot for the whole transaction, taken at the first statement not BEGIN. Read-only RR cannot fail with 40001. Writers updating a changed row get 40001 concurrent update.

nodes.label: SERIALIZABLE
nodes.rationale: Outcome equals some serial execution. Tracks read/write dependencies. High-conflict: 135 attempts / 115 retries / 12.4s vs 20 attempts / 71ms for FOR UPDATE in id order.

nodes.label: Write skew
nodes.rationale: Two transactions read an overlapping set then write different rows, breaking an invariant neither saw break. RR allows it; SERIALIZABLE aborts one with 40001 read/write dependencies.

nodes.label: Serialization failure 40001
nodes.rationale: Retry the whole transaction on 40001/40P01 with bounded attempts, jittered backoff outside the checked-out connection, and no external side effects inside the body.

nodes.label: Long-running transactions and the xmin horizon
xmin horizon
nodes.rationale: VACUUM may only remove versions no running transaction could need. One old transaction pins cleanup for every table. Idle read-only READ COMMITTED does not pin; RR/SERIALIZABLE, any writer, and a running SELECT do.

nodes.label: VACUUM blockers
nodes.rationale: Find by xact_start, backend_xmin, backend_xid in pg_stat_activity. Outside that: replication slots xmin, hot_standby_feedback, prepared xacts. File grew 27→40 MB with a blocker.

nodes.label: The lost update, and four ways to stop it
Lost update
nodes.rationale: Read-modify-write under READ COMMITTED: 20 concurrent increments produced qty=2 with no error. Last writer wins with a stale absolute value.

nodes.label: SQL arithmetic UPDATE
nodes.rationale: SET qty = qty + 1 is atomic in one statement. Fastest fix (20/20, 37.9 ms) when the new value is expressible in SQL.

nodes.label: SELECT FOR UPDATE
nodes.rationale: Row lock serialises the read-modify-write so application logic can run. 20/20 correct at 58 ms. Hold the lock only until COMMIT; no I/O in the window.

nodes.label: Optimistic version column
nodes.rationale: UPDATE ... WHERE version = $2; rowCount 0 means lost the race. Right for edit forms spanning requests or low contention. Worst on a hot row: 170 retries, 337 ms.

nodes.label: MVCC
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL never overwrites a row. UPDATE writes a new version and marks the old one ending; DELETE only stamps xmax. Explains lock-free reads, table growth, and why VACUUM exists.

nodes.label: xmin xmax ctid
nodes.rationale: xmin created this version, xmax ended it, ctid is the physical (page, slot). ctid moves on every UPDATE and is not a stable identifier.

nodes.label: Snapshot
nodes.rationale: xmin:xmax:in-progress — oldest still-running xid, one past last completed, and older-than-completed still-running ids. Visible if xmin committed before the snapshot and xmax had not.

nodes.label: HOT update
nodes.rationale: Heap-Only Tuple: new version on the same page and no indexed column changed, so indexes are untouched. Index on the updated column disables HOT entirely (0%).

nodes.label: fillfactor
nodes.rationale: Reserves free space per page for future versions. fillfactor 100: 0.1% HOT, 4→24 MB. fillfactor 70: 76.6% HOT, ended at 13 MB. Requires VACUUM FULL to rewrite existing pages.

nodes.label: READ COMMITTED
nodes.rationale: Default isolation: a fresh snapshot per statement. Maximum concurrency and no 40001 retries; a read-then-write sequence can silently produce wrong data.

nodes.label: Non-repeatable read
nodes.rationale: Same row changes mid-transaction (balance 100 → 999). Allowed by READ COMMITTED.

nodes.label: Phantom read
nodes.rationale: New matching rows appear mid-transaction (count 2 → 3). Allowed by READ COMMITTED.

nodes.label: Dirty read
nodes.rationale: Reading uncommitted data. PostgreSQL never permits this; READ UNCOMMITTED is mapped to READ COMMITTED.

nodes.label: Statement-level snapshot
nodes.rationale: Snapshot is fixed when the statement starts. A long SELECT is internally consistent even if another session commits mid-scan.

nodes.label: UPDATE WHERE re-evaluation
nodes.rationale: An UPDATE that waited on a row lock re-evaluates WHERE against the newly committed version and may report rowCount 0.

nodes.label: FOR UPDATE
nodes.rationale: Strongest row lock; conflicts with every other row-lock mode. Held until the transaction ends, not the statement.

nodes.label: FOR NO KEY UPDATE
nodes.rationale: Update non-key columns only. Conflicts with all modes except KEY SHARE.

nodes.label: FOR SHARE
nodes.rationale: Row must not change while you read it. Conflicts with UPDATE and NO KEY UPDATE.

nodes.label: FOR KEY SHARE
nodes.rationale: Weakest mode; what an FK insert takes. Conflicts only with FOR UPDATE so parent non-key updates are not blocked.

nodes.label: FOR UPDATE NOWAIT
nodes.rationale: Fail immediately with 55P03 if any selected row is locked. For 'someone else is editing this'.

nodes.label: lock_timeout
nodes.rationale: Bounds wait for a lock without killing a slow-but-progressing query. Prefer SET LOCAL so it does not leak on pooled connections.

nodes.label: Tuple-header row locks
nodes.rationale: Row locks live in xmax plus flag bits, not the lock manager. pg_locks is empty; use pg_blocking_pids().

nodes.label: SKIP LOCKED
nodes.rationale: Omit locked rows instead of waiting. Turns a table into a concurrent work queue; trades FIFO for parallelism.

nodes.label: SKIP LOCKED job queue
nodes.rationale: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED then commit the claim before work. 8 workers, 200 jobs: 168.6 ms, 0 duplicates vs 593 without locking.

nodes.label: At-least-once job delivery
nodes.rationale: Committing the claim early leaves crashed workers' rows in running. A reaper plus idempotent handlers is the guarantee; exactly-once is not configurable.

nodes.label: SAVEPOINT
nodes.rationale: Only way to survive a statement error inside a transaction. PostgreSQL has no real nested transactions.

nodes.label: ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT
nodes.rationale: Undoes work after the marker and leaves the transaction open. Plain ROLLBACK ends it. Must be taken before the failing statement.

nodes.label: RELEASE SAVEPOINT
nodes.rationale: Discards the marker but keeps the work. Later ROLLBACK TO that name is 3B001.

nodes.label: Savepoint subtransaction
nodes.rationale: Each writing savepoint burns a real xid. Per-statement SAVEPOINT/RELEASE cost 2.3×; past 64 subxids the cache overflows and other sessions pay SubtransSLRU waits.

nodes.label: ACCESS EXCLUSIVE
nodes.rationale: Most DDL takes this lock; it conflicts with everything including SELECT.

nodes.label: DDL lock queue
nodes.rationale: A waiting ALTER blocks later SELECTs even though ACCESS SHARE is compatible with the current holder. How a 2 ms ADD COLUMN takes a site down.

nodes.label: Safe DDL migration pattern
nodes.rationale: SET lock_timeout then retry. Split rewrites into a short lock plus unlocked backfill (NOT VALID then VALIDATE, CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY).

nodes.label: Metadata-only DDL
nodes.rationale: ADD COLUMN with a constant default is catalog-only since PG 11 (2.0 ms on 200k rows). Volatile defaults and non-coercible type changes rewrite the table.

nodes.label: VACUUM
nodes.rationale: Marks dead row versions reusable under SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE. Does not return space to the OS.

nodes.label: VACUUM FULL
nodes.rationale: Rewrites the table under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE and returns space. Use only after a permanent shrink; pg_repack is the live-table answer.

nodes.label: Autovacuum
nodes.rationale: Fires at threshold + scale_factor × live_rows (default 50 + 20%). Large hot tables need a per-table override.

nodes.label: HOT updates
nodes.rationale: fillfactor 70 raised HOT from 0.1% to 76.6% and cut a 24 MB table to 13 MB. An index on the updated column drives HOT to 0%.

nodes.label: XID wraparound
nodes.rationale: 32-bit xids; if the counter advances 2^31 past xmin the row looks future-dated and vanishes. VACUUM freezes old rows to prevent it.

nodes.label: XID freezing
nodes.rationale: Marks a row visible to everyone, immune to wraparound. relfrozenxid / age() is what you monitor.

nodes.label: Anti-wraparound autovacuum
nodes.rationale: Starts at autovacuum_freeze_max_age = 200 million. Alert here, not at the 2.134-billion WARNING which is only ~10 million xids before writes stop.

nodes.label: Audit trigger
nodes.rationale: AFTER ROW trigger writing to_jsonb(OLD/NEW). Attached to the table so migrations and psql cannot bypass it. Measured ~1.24× write cost.

nodes.label: WHEN IS DISTINCT FROM
nodes.rationale: Evaluated before entering plpgsql so no-op updates skip the call (0.86×). <> is NULL when either side is NULL.

nodes.label: AFTER versus BEFORE triggers
nodes.rationale: BEFORE to change the row, AFTER to react. NEW assignment in AFTER is silently discarded; RETURN NULL in BEFORE silently drops the row.

nodes.label: jsonb_build_object
nodes.rationale: Explicit key allowlist. Prefer over to_jsonb(row) for client payloads so new columns do not leak.

nodes.label: jsonb_agg
nodes.rationale: Over zero rows returns NULL not []; over a LEFT JOIN with no match returns [{nulls}]. Need FILTER plus coalesce to [].

nodes.label: jsonb_to_recordset
nodes.rationale: Turns a JSON array parameter into typed rows for INSERT ... SELECT.

nodes.label: Shape JSON in JS not SQL
nodes.rationale: jsonb_agg 284.8 ms vs flat join + JS 90.7 ms; json_agg 131.2 ms. Use SQL constructors when the shape is the point, not serialisation.

nodes.label: Column versus jsonb
nodes.rationale: If you can name the field in a requirement it is a column. jsonb is for unenumerable shape. Same two facts: 22 MB vs 1736 kB (~13×).

nodes.label: Generated column hybrid
nodes.rationale: Promote queried keys to GENERATED ALWAYS AS (payload->>'k') STORED columns. Derived from the document so it cannot drift.

nodes.label: No foreign key on a jsonb key
nodes.rationale: CHECK on a jsonb key works; a FOREIGN KEY cannot reference one (42601). Referential integrity is the guarantee you actually give up.

nodes.label: CREATE EXTENSION
nodes.rationale: Installs a package of types/functions per database. Available means files on disk; installed means CREATE EXTENSION ran here.

nodes.label: Extensions are per database
nodes.rationale: CREATE DATABASE does not copy extensions. digest() worked in one DB and raised 42883 in a new one on the same server.

nodes.label: pg_stat_statements
nodes.rationale: First extension to enable. Also needs shared_preload_libraries and a restart; CREATE EXTENSION alone returns nothing.

nodes.label: postgres_fdw
nodes.rationale: Foreign table is a query against another server. IMPORT FOREIGN SCHEMA snapshots remote definitions.

nodes.label: FDW pushdown
nodes.rationale: Full remote aggregate 2.9 ms vs 41.9 ms when a VOLATILE predicate forces shipping rows. Read EXPLAIN VERBOSE Remote SQL.

nodes.label: FDW is not two-phase commit
nodes.rationale: Local commit can succeed while the remote fails. Treat FDW as a read tool.

nodes.label: dblink
nodes.rationale: Older string-query mechanism with no pushdown. Still useful for a query not tied to the local transaction.

nodes.label: Full-text search
nodes.rationale: Documents become tsvector, queries become tsquery, @@ matches them. Good enough that most apps never need a separate search server.

nodes.label: tsquery
nodes.rationale: to_tsquery must never see raw user input; use the query parsers instead.

nodes.label: GIN jsonb_ops
nodes.rationale: Default GIN: indexes keys and values separately. Serves @> (4.5 ms) and ?; 17 MB; cannot serve ->>.

nodes.label: GIN jsonb_path_ops
nodes.rationale: One hash per path-plus-value. Smaller/faster for @> (1.1 ms, 13 MB) but cannot serve ?.

nodes.label: jsonb expression index
nodes.rationale: Index (doc->>'tag') for a hot key: 0.9 ms and 1352 kB. Expression must match the query exactly, including casts.

nodes.label: jsonb operator families
nodes.rationale: Accessors dig a value out; predicates ask a question. Which family you use decides whether a GIN index can help.

nodes.label: LISTEN/NOTIFY
nodes.rationale: Transactional wake-up with no extra broker. At-most-once, 8000-byte payload, dedicated listener connection. Use as a hint beside durable state.

nodes.label: pg_notify
nodes.rationale: Takes a string channel used exactly as given and can be computed. NOTIFY folds unquoted identifiers.

nodes.label: Notification queue
nodes.rationale: Shared 8 GB queue until every listener has read. A stuck listener is a database-wide problem.

nodes.label: NOTIFY at-most-once
nodes.rationale: A notification sent while nobody is listening is discarded. Combine with a transactional outbox if the event must not be lost.

nodes.label: Materialized view
nodes.rationale: Stores the query result as a table. Not automatically faster; wins only when the underlying query is genuinely expensive.

nodes.label: REFRESH CONCURRENTLY
nodes.rationale: Diffs new vs old so it needs a unique index (else 55000). 1.6× slower but does not block readers (2 ms vs 32 ms wait).

nodes.label: Matview staleness
nodes.rationale: Nothing refreshes it. Schedule the refresh; a trigger-driven refresh puts a full recompute inside a write transaction.

nodes.label: Partitioning
nodes.rationale: Payoff is dropping a month in milliseconds, not query speed. RANGE for time series, LIST for enums, HASH to spread writes.

nodes.label: Partition pruning
nodes.rationale: Skips partitions that cannot match. 15.6 ms with the key vs 32.9 ms Parallel Append across five partitions — about 2×, not 5×.

nodes.label: DETACH and DROP PARTITION
nodes.rationale: DETACH 5 ms (metadata); DROP 10 ms for 103353 rows vs a DELETE that writes a dead tuple per row.

nodes.label: DEFAULT partition
nodes.rationale: Catches keys outside every range; without it INSERT is 23514. Keep it empty by creating future partitions ahead of time.

nodes.label: Partition key in primary key
nodes.rationale: Every unique constraint must include the partition key. No global index, so uniqueness on any other column cannot be enforced across partitions.

nodes.label: pg_trgm
nodes.rationale: Compares overlapping three-character sequences. Finds typos FTS cannot; has no stemming. Also makes ILIKE '%x%' indexable.

nodes.label: word_similarity <%
nodes.rationale: % compares whole strings (0.273 vs a long title). <% scores the query against the best word (1.000). Query goes on the left.

nodes.label: gin_trgm_ops
nodes.rationale: Makes ILIKE '%x%' a Bitmap Heap Scan: 87.0 ms → 1.13 ms. Cannot serve ORDER BY <->.

nodes.label: gist_trgm_ops
nodes.rationale: Serves ORDER BY <-> nearest-neighbour. Larger (22 MB vs 9 MB GIN).

nodes.label: pgvector
nodes.rationale: Embeddings next to the row so a relational filter and similarity search share one query and transaction. Not bundled in stock images.

nodes.label: HNSW index
nodes.rationale: 50k 384-d vectors: 88 ms exact → 2.1 ms (42×). Build 22.9 s; index 98 MB vs 78 MB table. Results are approximate.

nodes.label: Vector distance operators
nodes.rationale: <-> L2, <=> cosine, <#> negative inner product. All are distances so ORDER BY ASC is nearest-first.

nodes.label: HNSW 2000-dimension limit
nodes.rationale: Column holds up to 16000 dimensions; HNSW indexes at most 2000 (54000). halfvec indexes up to 4000.

nodes.label: PL/pgSQL
nodes.rationale: Required for trigger bodies. A black box to the planner: fixed 1000-row estimate wrecks joins. Default: sql for one query, plpgsql for triggers, app otherwise.

nodes.label: LANGUAGE sql
nodes.rationale: Can be inlined so the planner sees real statistics (60 rows vs plpgsql's 1000). Standalone timing is the same; joins are where it matters.

nodes.label: Function volatility markers
nodes.rationale: IMMUTABLE foldable and indexable; STABLE inlinable; VOLATILE (default) blocks inlining. Lying about IMMUTABLE gives wrong answers, not errors.

nodes.label: CREATE PROCEDURE
nodes.rationale: Exists so it can COMMIT mid-body. Invoked with CALL. Useless inside an application BEGIN/COMMIT wrapper (2D000).

nodes.label: Procedure mid-body COMMIT
nodes.rationale: Same COMMIT in a FUNCTION is 2D000. Only works when no transaction is already open. Failures leave work partly done; the procedure must be resumable.

nodes.label: Set-returning functions in FROM
nodes.rationale: An SRF returns rows, so it belongs in FROM where rows enter a query. In SELECT two SRFs lockstep-pad with NULL; in WHERE they raise 0A000.

nodes.label: unnest bulk-insert bridge
nodes.rationale: One array parameter per column keeps the bind count fixed. VALUES hits the 65535 protocol cap at 21845 three-column rows; unnest has no such ceiling.

nodes.label: jsonb_to_recordset
nodes.rationale: One JSON parameter for any number of rows with types declared in AS. Convenient when the body is already JSON; unnest is generally faster.

nodes.label: generate_series
nodes.rationale: Gap filling: endpoints are inclusive (hourly over one day is 25 rows); descending needs a negative step; step 0 raises 22023.

nodes.label: WITH ORDINALITY
nodes.rationale: The only way to preserve array input order once values become rows. pos is bigint, which pg returns as text.

nodes.label: ROWS FROM zip
nodes.rationale: Explicit lockstep zip of two SRFs in FROM; same padding as two SRFs in SELECT but readable.

nodes.label: LATERAL unnest
nodes.rationale: Explodes a per-row array by referencing the left-hand row.

nodes.label: Transactional outbox
nodes.rationale: You cannot write to a database and a queue atomically. Write the event in the same transaction as the business row, then publish separately.

nodes.label: Dual-write bug
nodes.rationale: Save-then-enqueue has no spanning transaction. Measured: orders=1 | jobs enqueued=0 when Redis was down.

nodes.label: Outbox relay
nodes.rationale: A separate process claims unpublished rows and publishes them. At-least-once: can publish then crash before setting published_at.

nodes.label: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
nodes.rationale: Competing relays must not claim the same row. Measured 3 workers / 20 jobs: 20 unique claims, 94ms vs 189ms serialised.

nodes.label: At-least-once delivery
nodes.rationale: Publishing to the broker and marking published_at are two systems. Exactly-once delivery does not exist; exactly-once effect does.

nodes.label: Idempotent consumer
nodes.rationale: Unique idempotency key plus ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; rowCount=0 means already handled.

nodes.label: LISTEN/NOTIFY as wake hint
nodes.rationale: NOTIFY is at-most-once; keep the poll as backstop. The table is the source of truth.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL triggers
nodes.rationale: A trigger runs code the application cannot see, skip, or ask for. Right for data invariants; wrong for business behaviour and external side effects.

nodes.label: BEFORE trigger
nodes.rationale: Can modify NEW and cancel the row with RETURN NULL. Use to change the row (updated_at, normalisation).

nodes.label: AFTER trigger
nodes.rationale: Return value is ignored; the row is already written. Use to react: audit, notify, cascade.

nodes.label: Row vs statement trigger
nodes.rationale: One UPDATE of 1000 rows: 1000 row firings, 1 statement firing. Statement triggers also fire on zero-row statements.

nodes.label: Transition tables
nodes.rationale: REFERENCING OLD TABLE / NEW TABLE lets a statement trigger audit bulk changes in one insert.

nodes.label: Trigger WHEN clause
nodes.rationale: Evaluated before the plpgsql call. Measured 0.86× of an unconditional row trigger. Cannot be used on INSTEAD OF.

nodes.label: RETURN NULL cancels the row
nodes.rationale: Silent drop: 10 submitted, 5 stored, rowCount reported 5. Prefer RAISE EXCEPTION when the caller should know.

nodes.label: Alphabetical trigger firing order
nodes.rationale: Fires by trigger name, not creation order. Prefix 01_/02_/03_ if order matters.

nodes.label: SQL views
nodes.rationale: A stored query, not stored data. pg_relation_size is 0. Substituted before planning so the planner sees one combined query.

nodes.label: View predicate pushdown
nodes.rationale: Filter on a GROUP BY key: 0.8ms / 60 rows. Filter on the aggregate: 135.8ms / 300000-row seq scan — 170×. Aggregates, DISTINCT, windows, LIMIT, set ops are fences.

nodes.label: Views cannot take parameters
nodes.rationale: CREATE VIEW ... WHERE customer = $1 raises 42P02. Workaround: LANGUAGE sql STABLE SRF, or filter at the call site.

nodes.label: Automatically updatable view
nodes.rationale: One base table, no aggregate/DISTINCT/GROUP BY/window/set op. Otherwise 55000; needs INSTEAD OF.

nodes.label: WITH CHECK OPTION
nodes.rationale: Without it a write can insert a row that immediately vanishes from the view. With it: 44000 at insert time.

nodes.label: View hard dependencies
nodes.rationale: 2BP01 on DROP COLUMN/TABLE a view uses. CREATE OR REPLACE can only append columns.

nodes.label: security_invoker views
nodes.rationale: Default owner privileges bypass caller RLS. PG15+ security_invoker=true uses the caller's privileges.

nodes.label: tsvector
nodes.rationale: Sorted set of lexemes with positions. english stems and drops stop words; simple lowercases and keeps everything.

nodes.label: to_tsvector
nodes.rationale: Configuration is part of the data. Document indexed as english will not match a query parsed as simple.

nodes.label: to_tsquery
nodes.rationale: Parses tsquery syntax, not prose. Two words, an apostrophe, or a quote raise 42601. Never give it a search box.

nodes.label: websearch_to_tsquery
nodes.rationale: Search-engine syntax: quotes=phrase, -=negation, or=|. Never raises; silently discards unparseable tokens.

nodes.label: Prefix query :*
nodes.rationale: Full-text matches whole lexemes. rout → 0 rows; rout:* → 13336. Type-ahead appends :* to the last token.

nodes.label: english vs simple configurations
nodes.rationale: english for descriptions (stemming); simple for SKUs, tags, codes. Serve both from one config and everyone is slightly wrong.

nodes.label: GIN index on tsvector
nodes.rationale: 200002 products: 1165ms seq scan → 17.36ms Bitmap Heap Scan (~66×). Query expression must match the indexed expression exactly.

nodes.label: IMMUTABLE to_tsvector trap
nodes.rationale: One-arg to_tsvector(body) reads session default_text_search_config so it is not IMMUTABLE — 42P17. Name the config.

nodes.label: Generated tsvector column
nodes.rationale: Same speed as an expression index (17.87 vs 17.36ms). Chosen to combine columns, carry weights, and stop expression-mismatch misses. coalesce required.

nodes.label: setweight A–D
nodes.rationale: Default rank weights {0.1,0.2,0.4,1.0} for D–A. Title match counts 5× a body match. Weights do nothing until ranking.

nodes.label: ts_rank
nodes.rationale: Not indexable. Index finds matches; rank runs on each. Narrow the match rather than optimise the rank.

nodes.label: ts_rank_cd
nodes.rationale: Also accounts for cover density. Better for multi-word queries. Not bounded 0–1.

nodes.label: ts_headline
nodes.rationale: Re-reads original text so it cannot use the index. Apply after LIMIT, never before.

nodes.label: Full-text cannot find typos
nodes.rationale: Stemming normalises grammar, not misspellings. router against a document saying routr → 0 rows. That is pg_trgm's job.

nodes.label: jsonb -> accessor
nodes.rationale: Returns jsonb so it chains. Use for every step except the last.

nodes.label: jsonb ->> accessor
nodes.rationale: Returns text and terminates the chain. ->> 'tags' renders the whole array as text, not an element.

nodes.label: jsonb #> / #>> path operators
nodes.rationale: Prefer #>> when the path is fixed and more than two levels, or built as a text[] parameter.

nodes.label: Missing key vs JSON null
nodes.rationale: ->> returns SQL NULL for both. Distinguish with ? (presence) or jsonb_typeof = 'null'.

nodes.label: jsonb_typeof
nodes.rationale: ->> flattens 1 and "1" to the same text. Type distinction survives only via jsonb_typeof or jsonb comparison.

nodes.label: jsonb @> containment
nodes.rationale: Asks whether the right-hand document appears inside the left. GIN can serve it; ->> = cannot. Measured 4.5ms Index Cond vs 35.4ms seq scan.

nodes.label: jsonb ? key exists
nodes.rationale: True even when the value is JSON null. jsonb_path_ops cannot serve existence operators.

nodes.label: jsonpath @? / @@
nodes.rationale: Comparisons and wildcards that containment cannot express. @? asks whether a path matches; @@ evaluates a boolean path.

nodes.label: jsonb_path_ops vs jsonb_ops
nodes.rationale: path_ops is smaller and faster for @> but has no entry for a bare key, so ?/?|/ ?& seq-scan.

nodes.label: jsonb mutation operators
nodes.rationale: || is shallow; every mutation produces a new document so UPDATE rewrites the whole column.

nodes.label: GIN cannot serve ->> equality
nodes.rationale: A GIN index on a jsonb column indexes structure. doc->>'tag' = 't42' is a different expression and falls back to a filter.

nodes.label: App role should not own the schema
nodes.rationale: DDL is an ownership right with no GRANT form. Injected DROP TABLE is 42501 for a non-owner and a completed migration for an owner.

nodes.label: Two connection strings
nodes.rationale: Migrations as owner, request path as app. If both live in the same .env a compromised process reads both.

nodes.label: GRANT USAGE not CREATE
nodes.rationale: CREATE on the schema lets the app create tables it then owns, silently eroding the boundary.

nodes.label: ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES
nodes.rationale: Stops every migration from needing a manual GRANT. Keyed FOR ROLE the owner, so hand-created tables miss it.

nodes.label: work_mem
nodes.rationale: Per sort/hash operation. Worst case is work_mem × operations × concurrency — how servers get OOM-killed.

nodes.label: effective_cache_size
nodes.rationale: Allocates nothing. Leaving it at 4 GB on a large server biases the planner to sequential scans.

nodes.label: random_page_cost
nodes.rationale: Default 4.0 models a spinning disk. On SSD, 1.1 is the usual highest-value one-line change.

nodes.label: pg_settings.context
nodes.rationale: Tells you restart vs reload before planning a change. Read pending_restart after.

nodes.label: Disaster drill
nodes.rationale: An untested backup is a belief. A drill converts an unknown RTO into a known one.

nodes.label: Recovery Time Objective
nodes.rationale: Measure detection, decision, fetch, restore, verify, repoint. Restore usually dominates — measured 4× dump time.

nodes.label: Point-in-time recovery
nodes.rationale: The most likely disaster is a bad migration or wrong DELETE. Replicas replicate the mistake; only PITR helps.

nodes.label: Disaster runbook
nodes.rationale: Must live outside the systems it describes. Someone who did not write it must be able to follow it.

nodes.label: Backup retention window
nodes.rationale: Choose against how long a problem might go unnoticed. Slow corruption discovered weeks later defeats a 7-day window.

nodes.label: log_statement=all leaks parameters
nodes.rationale: Parameterised queries keep values out of statement text and pg_stat_activity, not the log. DETAIL: Parameters: $1=… and log_parameter_max_length defaults to -1.

nodes.label: Three-legged monitoring stool
nodes.rationale: pg_stat_activity (now), pg_stat_statements (aggregate), the log (which statement was slow). You need all three.

nodes.label: Logical replication
nodes.rationale: Copies decoded row changes, not WAL bytes. Cross-major-version, per-table, writable target. Wrong tool for HA.

nodes.label: Replica identity
nodes.rationale: How the subscriber identifies the row for UPDATE/DELETE. Default PK. Without it inserts work and the first update fails.

nodes.label: Replication slot
nodes.rationale: Guarantees WAL retention until consumed. An abandoned slot fills the publisher disk. Alert on inactive + retained; set max_slot_wal_keep_size.

nodes.label: Sequences are not replicated
nodes.rationale: The single most common upgrade-day failure: 23505 unique violations on first insert after cutover.

nodes.label: Minor vs major upgrade
nodes.rationale: 18.3→18.4 is a restart; 17→18 is a data migration. On-disk format is the dividing line.

nodes.label: pg_upgrade
nodes.rationale: Migrates the catalog rather than rewriting rows. Run --check days in advance with the old server still running.

nodes.label: pg_upgrade --link / --swap
nodes.rationale: Trade rollback for speed. After the new cluster starts (link) or transfer begins (swap), the old cluster is unsafe. Verified backup is the only rollback.

nodes.label: Post-upgrade statistics
nodes.rationale: PG18 transfers most optimizer stats (not CREATE STATISTICS). Still run vacuumdb --all --analyze-in-stages.

nodes.label: Logical-replication upgrade path
nodes.rationale: Near-zero downtime because publisher and subscriber may differ in major version. Downtime is stop-writes, advance sequences, flip the connection string.

nodes.label: Managed PostgreSQL
nodes.rationale: Removes sysadmin work and none of the application work. Missing indexes, long transactions, connection exhaustion and locking migrations remain yours.

nodes.label: Direct vs pooled endpoint
nodes.rationale: The most common connection incident. Differ by one token or port; the wrong choice fails only under load. Migrations/DDL/LISTEN need direct.

nodes.label: pg_stat_statements
nodes.rationale: total_exec_time beats mean_exec_time. queryid is not guaranteed stable across major versions.

nodes.label: Oldest transaction age
nodes.rationale: Leading indicator for bloat, lock waits, pool exhaustion and replication conflicts. If you monitor one thing beyond disk, monitor that.

nodes.label: pg_dump and pg_restore
nodes.rationale: Logical backup from one consistent snapshot. Portable across majors and selective to a table. Restore measured at 4× dump time.

nodes.label: Restore rebuilds indexes
nodes.rationale: Indexes and constraints are separate manifest items. pg_restore -t can restore zero indexes including the PK.

nodes.label: pg_hba.conf
nodes.rationale: Runs before privileges exist. First matching rule only; if its method fails the connection fails — no fall-through.

nodes.label: First matching HBA rule wins
nodes.rationale: A broad rule near the top makes every rule below it dead. Order specific before general.

nodes.label: scram-sha-256
nodes.rationale: Default password method. A scram rule cannot authenticate an md5-stored password; the reverse works.

nodes.label: trust authentication
nodes.rationale: Does not check the password. Measured: a deliberately wrong password connected. POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD=trust replaces the image's scram line.

nodes.label: pg_hba_file_rules
nodes.rationale: Parsed view with evaluation order. A syntax error survives reload (old rules stay); a restart turns it into an outage.

nodes.label: HBA failure messages
nodes.rationale: no entry = no match; rejects connection = reject method; password failed covers wrong password, missing role, and expired VALID UNTIL.

nodes.label: Connection limits and PgBouncer
nodes.rationale: A PostgreSQL connection is an OS process. 40 clients non-overlapping → 1 backend; 40 concurrent → exactly default_pool_size.

nodes.label: Transaction pooling
nodes.rationale: The answer and a source of intermittent bugs. Session features (prepared statements historically, SET) break.

nodes.label: Pool exhaustion 08P01
nodes.rationale: 5 open transactions, pool 5: two clients waited 120204 ms then 08P01. Saturation becomes a hang at the 120s default.

nodes.label: Physical backup and PITR
nodes.rationale: Base backup + every WAL record since = land on any second. The base backup need not be filesystem-consistent; log replay repairs it.

nodes.label: archive_command
nodes.rationale: A failing archive_command is an outage: unarchived WAL is retained until the disk fills. Alert on pg_stat_archiver.failed_count.

nodes.label: recovery_target_action=pause
nodes.rationale: Default pause. Verify before promoting; timelines mean a wrong attempt can be repeated.

nodes.label: Streaming replication replicas
nodes.rationale: Consumer half only. Managed provider runs it; you get broken by stale reads and recovery conflicts.

nodes.label: Stale read / read-your-writes
nodes.rationale: Looks like the save button didn't work — no error. Write committed on primary, not yet replayed on replica.

nodes.label: Recovery conflict 40001
nodes.rationale: A read-only query is killed because replay needed to remove rows the query still required. Load-dependent and invisible in development.

nodes.label: Row-level security
nodes.rationale: Moves which rows a user may see into the database so a missing WHERE stops being a data breach. Default-deny: enable with no policy and the table looks empty.

nodes.label: FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY
nodes.rationale: Table owners bypass RLS by default. An app connecting as schema owner is unprotected and its tests pass.

nodes.label: USING vs WITH CHECK
nodes.rationale: UPDATE needs WITH CHECK as well as USING, otherwise a user can modify a row they own into one they should not.

nodes.label: SET LOCAL for RLS identity
nodes.rationale: A plain SET persists on a pooled connection into the next request — measured — which is a cross-tenant exposure.

nodes.label: Roles, GRANT and REVOKE
nodes.rationale: Least privilege is GRANT statements; a new role can do almost nothing. Role=identity, privilege=verb on an object, ownership outranks both, effective privileges are the union of inherited roles.

nodes.label: TLS to the database
nodes.rationale: sslmode=require encrypts but verifies nothing. verify-full authenticates the server. Enforce TLS in pg_hba with hostnossl reject + hostssl.

nodes.label: Zero-downtime schema changes
nodes.rationale: A waiting ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock blocks everything behind it. Schema change and code deploy are never simultaneous; expand-and-contract.

nodes.label: Changing a setting, and where to start
nodes.rationale: pg_settings.context decides restart vs reload vs SET. ALTER SYSTEM writes postgresql.auto.conf which overrides postgresql.conf.

nodes.label: The memory settings
nodes.rationale: shared_buffers, work_mem, maintenance_work_mem, effective_cache_size. Only one allocates what people think; effective_cache_size allocates nothing.

nodes.label: Planner, WAL, and timeouts
nodes.rationale: random_page_cost=4.0 models spinning disks. max_wal_size=1GB causes checkpoint spikes. Timeouts stop incidents.

nodes.label: Parameters in the log, and auto_explain
nodes.rationale: Parameterised queries do not keep values out of the log. auto_explain.log_analyze instruments every statement.

nodes.label: What to log
nodes.rationale: Defaults log almost nothing. Turn on duration, lock waits, temp files; never log_statement=all in production.

nodes.label: The providers, and connecting correctly
nodes.rationale: Every provider has a direct and a pooled endpoint. Wrong endpoint fails only under load. Migrations need the direct endpoint.

nodes.label: What you give up on managed PostgreSQL
nodes.rationale: No superuser, no filesystem, parameter groups, extension allowlist. Application-side problems remain yours.

nodes.label: Database health and alerting
nodes.rationale: pg_stat_database for system health. Alert on connections, oldest xact, idle-in-xact, lag, dead tuples, deadlocks, temp_bytes, disk.

nodes.label: pg_stat_statements — finding the expensive query
nodes.rationale: The query killing the database is usually a fast one run constantly. Sort by total_exec_time, not mean.

nodes.label: Reading pg_stat_statements
nodes.rationale: Counters are cumulative. Diff snapshots. High stddev_exec_time flags unstable plans.

nodes.label: Table health
nodes.rationale: pg_stat_user_tables for seq scans, dead tuples, autovacuum. Unused indexes via idx_scan=0 with cautions.

nodes.label: What is happening right now
nodes.rationale: pg_stat_activity is the 90-second incident query: xact_age, state, wait_event, query.

nodes.label: Dump formats and what is in them
nodes.rationale: Four formats. -Fc is the default: compressed, TOC, selective and parallel restore. Roles are not in pg_dump.

nodes.label: Restoring
nodes.rationale: Restore is ~4x dump because indexes rebuild. Dump is a REPEATABLE READ snapshot holding ACCESS SHARE.

nodes.label: Exhaustion, sizing and the Node side
nodes.rationale: One idle-in-transaction bug exhausts the pool. query_wait_timeout defaults to 120s. Smaller pool is usually faster.

nodes.label: The Node side, observing, and alternatives
nodes.rationale: Set connectionTimeoutMillis. Release in finally. Alert on SHOW POOLS cl_waiting/maxwait.

nodes.label: Pool modes
nodes.rationale: Transaction mode multiplexes; session state does not follow the client. SET LOCAL, not SET.

nodes.label: Why connections cost
nodes.rationale: A connection is a process. replicas × pg.Pool max is the real count. pg.Pool ≠ PgBouncer.

nodes.label: Base backups and WAL archiving
nodes.rationale: Physical backup + WAL archive enables PITR. archive_command failure fills pg_wal and becomes an outage.

nodes.label: Least privilege as GRANT statements
nodes.rationale: Least privilege is not a written policy; it is GRANT statements, and a new role can do almost nothing.

nodes.label: sslmode=require
nodes.rationale: Encrypts always but verifies nothing; stops sniffing not an active attacker.

nodes.label: sslmode=prefer default
nodes.rationale: libpq default; silently falls back to plaintext when the server stops offering TLS.

nodes.label: Waiting ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock queue
nodes.rationale: A 5 ms ALTER can cause a 30 s outage because new queries do not jump the queue behind a waiting ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock.

nodes.label: ADD CONSTRAINT … NOT VALID then VALIDATE
work_mem
nodes.rationale: Allocated per sort/hash operation per query, not per connection; worst case work_mem × ops × concurrent queries.

nodes.label: effective_cache_size
nodes.rationale: Allocates nothing; planner hint about shared buffers plus OS page cache.

nodes.label: SET LOCAL work_mem on pooled connections
fsync vs synchronous_commit
nodes.rationale: fsync=off risks unrecoverable corruption; synchronous_commit=off can lose recent xacts without corruption.

nodes.label: Parameters leak into the log
nodes.rationale: pg_stat_activity shows $1 but log_statement=all writes DETAIL Parameters; log_parameter_max_length defaults to -1 (full).

nodes.label: ALTER ROLE PASSWORD plaintext in log
auto_explain.log_analyze overhead
nodes.rationale: Instruments every statement, not only slow ones; documented extremely negative performance impact.

nodes.label: Migrations must use direct endpoint
nodes.rationale: Transaction pooling breaks advisory locks and CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY.

nodes.label: Application-side work remains yours
nodes.rationale: Managed hosting removes sysadmin work, not missing indexes, long xacts, connection exhaustion, or locking migrations.

nodes.label: total_exec_time vs mean_exec_time
nodes.rationale: A 4 ms lookup run 500000 times costs far more than an 8 s report; slow-query logs never surface the former.

nodes.label: Cache hit ratio (blks_hit)
nodes.rationale: blks_read is shared-buffer misses, often served from OS page cache; treat as trend not purchase signal.

nodes.label: Roles are cluster-wide, not in pg_dump
pg_dump client must be newer or equal
Process-per-connection
nodes.rationale: Each connection is an OS process; isolation is the point and the price. Do not raise max_connections — put a pooler in front.

nodes.label: Session features broken in transaction mode
Smaller pool is usually faster
nodes.rationale: Beyond cores×2 extra backends add contention not throughput. Size small and timeout short, or neither.

nodes.label: Idle-in-transaction pool blast radius
nodes.rationale: Five open transactions exhausted default_pool_size=5; two more clients waited 120204 ms then 08P01.

nodes.label: Archiving fails dangerously
nodes.rationale: Unlike pg_dump, a failing archive_command retains WAL on disk until the disk fills — a backup problem becomes an outage.

nodes.label: Point-in-time recovery
nodes.rationale: PITR trades procedure for precision: more steps than a logical restore, in exchange for landing on the exact second before the damage. Value is contingent on rehearsal.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL timelines
nodes.rationale: A new timeline after recovery keeps original WAL history intact so a wrong PITR is not fatal.

nodes.label: Recovery time objective
nodes.rationale: A restore you have never timed is not a recovery plan, it is a hope.

nodes.label: recovery_target_action pause
nodes.rationale: Default pause lets you verify the landing point before promoting; promote immediately forecloses a retry.

nodes.label: 08.2 Query conflicts and routing reads safely
Hot-standby recovery conflict
nodes.rationale: Replay of primary VACUUM can cancel a replica SELECT with retryable SQLSTATE 40001.

nodes.label: hot_standby_feedback
nodes.rationale: Eliminates early-cleanup conflicts by exporting the standby snapshot into the primary vacuum horizon, causing primary bloat.

nodes.label: Replica read routing hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Reads that feed writes belong on the primary; a stale replica read of a balance before a debit is a correctness bug.

nodes.label: Read-your-writes
nodes.rationale: Async replicas do not provide the guarantee that a client sees its own committed writes.

nodes.label: pg_stat_replication LSN stages
nodes.rationale: flush_lsn is durability; replay_lsn is visibility. Replication separates the two.

nodes.label: synchronous_commit
nodes.rationale: Only remote_apply waits for replay. on does not mean synchronous replication unless synchronous_standby_names is set.

nodes.label: SET LOCAL app identity
nodes.rationale: Plain SET on a pooled connection leaks tenant identity into the next request — a cross-tenant data leak, measured in ex54.

nodes.label: RLS policy as query predicate
nodes.rationale: Index policy columns as the leading composite key; every query is tenant-scoped whether the app wrote it that way.

nodes.label: BYPASSRLS job role
nodes.rationale: Exactly one unfiltered role, named for that purpose; the application must not use it.

nodes.label: RLS as authorization backstop
nodes.rationale: Filter in the application because it is clear and fast; enable RLS underneath because people are fallible. On Supabase, RLS is the whole mechanism.

nodes.label: USING versus WITH CHECK
nodes.rationale: USING guards the row you started with; WITH CHECK guards the row you end up with. An UPDATE needs both.

nodes.label: Column grants are additive
nodes.rationale: A column grant cannot restrict; table-wide SELECT via any inherited role makes the column list irrelevant. Use a view as the boundary.

nodes.label: ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES
nodes.rationale: Defaults are keyed on the creating role, not the schema. Omit FOR ROLE and a DBA records a rule for postgres while migration tables stay ungranted.

nodes.label: public schema CREATE revoked in PG15
MAINTAIN privilege
nodes.rationale: VACUUM without MAINTAIN returns success and only a WARNING, so automated jobs can silently skip tables.

nodes.label: Identity sequence needs no USAGE grant
Expand/contract migration
nodes.rationale: Every deploy must be compatible with the schema before and after it; never remove in the same step that adds a replacement.

nodes.label: Safe SET NOT NULL via CHECK
Invalid concurrent index
nodes.rationale: A failed CONCURRENTLY build is ignored for queries but still consumes write overhead.

nodes.label: ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock queue
nodes.rationale: A 5 ms ALTER can outage for 30 s because later readers cannot jump the queue behind waiting DDL.

nodes.label: GIN-indexable array containment
nodes.rationale: @> uses GIN; = ANY(arr) does not, even though they are logically equivalent.

nodes.label: Array versus child table
nodes.rationale: Arrays cannot carry foreign keys (42804) or per-element metadata; MVCC rewrites the whole row on any element change.

nodes.label: interval calendar arithmetic
nodes.rationale: interval '1 month' equals interval '30 days' for comparison but addition uses the real calendar.

nodes.label: Metadata in Postgres bytes in object storage
nodes.rationale: Large uploads belong outside the database because backups, WAL, replication and memory all grow with the blobs.

nodes.label: Cast the literal never the column
nodes.rationale: A cast on the indexed column turned a 0.199 ms index-only scan into a 47.9 ms sequential scan.

nodes.label: Composite type as column
nodes.rationale: No per-field constraints or FKs; adding a field rewrites every table using the type; pg returns an unparsed string.

nodes.label: enum vs CHECK vs lookup table
PostgreSQL ENUM
nodes.rationale: Cannot drop a value (0A000); cannot use a newly added value in the same transaction (55P04).

nodes.label: Lookup table for statuses
nodes.rationale: Default choice: adding a value is an INSERT, and the table can carry labels and sort order.

nodes.label: bigint primary keys
nodes.rationale: Exhausting an int sequence is 2200H and a full ACCESS EXCLUSIVE rewrite; measured cost of bigint is about 20% on a narrow table.

nodes.label: bigint arrives as a JavaScript string
jsonb
nodes.rationale: Only jsonb supports equality, containment and GIN; json cannot be GIN-indexed (42704).

nodes.label: jsonb key versus real column
nodes.rationale: Promote a key to a column as soon as you filter or join on it; a jsonb key has no CHECK, FK or cheap B-tree.

nodes.label: numeric plus currency column
nodes.rationale: Never double precision — 1000 × 0.01 sums to 9.999999999999831. Never the money type.

nodes.label: Keep numeric money as a string in JS
inet type
nodes.rationale: Holds a host address with optional netmask, 10 bytes vs 16 as text, validates input (22P02), normalises IPv6 so equivalent forms compare equal, and supports GiST-indexable containment operators.

nodes.label: cidr type
nodes.rationale: Holds a network only; host bits set raise 22P02. That distinction is why both inet and cidr exist: cidr is a range, inet is an address that may know its range.

nodes.label: macaddr and macaddr8
nodes.rationale: 6-byte and 8-byte hardware addresses with the same normalisation pattern as inet.

nodes.label: Built-in geometric types
nodes.rationale: point, line, lseg, box, path, polygon, circle with <->, @>, && — Cartesian and GiST-indexable. point arrives in Node as {x,y}.

nodes.label: PostGIS geography for Earth
nodes.rationale: Built-in geometry is Cartesian; <-> on lat/lng degrees is not metres. PostGIS geography, SRS and real distance functions are required for maps.

nodes.label: citext
nodes.rationale: Case-insensitive text plus case-insensitive UNIQUE (23505 on a case variant). Folds case via collation, not Unicode composition; extension required.

nodes.label: lower() unique expression index
nodes.rationale: No-extension fallback for case-insensitive uniqueness; every query must use lower() or it silently misses rows.

nodes.label: SQL three-valued logic
nodes.rationale: NULL is absence; comparisons yield unknown. WHERE keeps only true, so col = NULL matches nothing. Use IS NULL or IS NOT DISTINCT FROM.

nodes.label: NOT IN with NULL drops all rows
nodes.rationale: 2 NOT IN (1, NULL) expands to true AND unknown → NULL, so the row is dropped. Prefer NOT EXISTS.

nodes.label: NOT EXISTS anti-join
nodes.rationale: Handles NULL correctly and usually plans as an anti-join rather than a hashed subplan.

nodes.label: IS DISTINCT FROM
nodes.rationale: Null-safe comparison; WHERE v IS DISTINCT FROM 30 includes NULLs that v <> 30 drops.

nodes.label: Aggregates ignore NULL
nodes.rationale: count(*) counts rows; count(col) counts non-nulls. sum() over all-NULL is NULL not 0 — wrap with coalesce(sum(v), 0).

nodes.label: UNIQUE allows many NULLs
nodes.rationale: NULLs are not equal so they do not conflict; three NULLs accepted. PostgreSQL 15+ UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT allows at most one.

nodes.label: UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL 15+ option that treats NULLs as equal for uniqueness, raising 23505 on a second NULL.

nodes.label: NULL sort order
nodes.rationale: NULLs sort last ASC and first DESC. Reversing a sort changes LIMIT results; override with NULLS FIRST/LAST and match the index.

nodes.label: NULL is not the empty string
nodes.rationale: '' IS NULL is false. || with NULL yields NULL; concat() ignores NULLs. Oracle conflates them; PostgreSQL does not.

nodes.label: Node undefined becomes SQL NULL
nodes.rationale: pg converts undefined parameters to NULL, so a missing request key silently nulls a column. Build partial updates from present keys.

nodes.label: numeric exact decimal
nodes.rationale: Exact software decimal. numeric(12,2) is 12 digits, 2 after the point. Default for money; 1000×0.01 sums to 10.00.

nodes.label: double precision (float8)
nodes.rationale: Fast approximate binary float. 1000×0.01 stored as 9.999999999999831 so WHERE total = 10 finds nothing. Use for measurements, not money.

nodes.label: Integer cents in bigint
nodes.rationale: Exact and as fast as float8 (27.7 ms vs 76.8 ms numeric on 300k sums). Units become implicit; name columns total_cents.

nodes.label: numeric field overflow 22003
nodes.rationale: Exceeding declared precision errors; extra scale rounds silently.

nodes.label: numeric half-away-from-zero rounding
nodes.rationale: 2.5::numeric(2,0) → 3; float-to-int uses half-to-even → 2. numeric NaN compares equal to itself so it can be indexed.

nodes.label: pg returns numeric as a string
nodes.rationale: Converting to JS Number would discard exactness. Do arithmetic in SQL or use a decimal library; never setTypeParser(1700, parseFloat).

nodes.label: PostgreSQL range types
nodes.rationale: First-class intervals (int4range, tstzrange, daterange, …) with @>, &&, <<, -|-. pg returns the text form '[1,10)'.

nodes.label: Half-open range default
nodes.rationale: [1,10) includes 1 excludes 10. Discrete types canonicalise [1,10] to [1,11). Touching intervals do not overlap, so back-to-back bookings are legal.

nodes.label: Exclusion constraint
nodes.rationale: EXCLUDE USING gist (room WITH =, during WITH &&) forbids same-room overlap (23P01). Index-enforced, so concurrent read-then-write cannot both insert.

nodes.label: btree_gist extension
nodes.rationale: Required so GiST can mix scalar equality with range overlap in one exclusion constraint.

nodes.label: Multirange types
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL 14+. Plain range union of gapped ranges raises 22000; int4multirange holds {[1,5),[10,15)} as one value.

nodes.label: text type
nodes.rationale: Default string type. Same implementation, size and speed as varchar(n) (13 MB / ~26 ms on 300k rows).

nodes.label: varchar(n)
nodes.rationale: Column insert raises 22001 over length; explicit ::varchar(n) truncates silently. Widening is metadata-only (2.4 ms); narrowing rewrites (305 ms / 200k).

nodes.label: char(n) blank-padded
nodes.rationale: Pads to width (51 vs 4 bytes for 'abc' in char(50)); comparison ignores trailing spaces. Avoid except genuinely fixed-width codes.

nodes.label: text plus CHECK length
nodes.rationale: Cannot be cast away, visible in \d, and changeable with NOT VALID + VALIDATE without rewriting the table.

nodes.label: Collation from libc (musl vs glibc)
nodes.rationale: Sort order comes from the column/database collation via the C library, so Alpine musl and Debian glibc can order the same strings differently.

nodes.label: Session TimeZone setting
nodes.rationale: Display and interpretation only, not storage. Changes timestamptz print, bare timestamp literals, current_date, date_trunc and ::date grouping.

nodes.label: AT TIME ZONE in the query
nodes.rationale: Makes day-bucketing independent of the session. Two events at 21:00Z/23:30Z on 15 June group to 15 June in UTC and 16 June in Asia/Kolkata.

nodes.label: set_config for bindable timezone
nodes.rationale: SET has no parameter slots (42601 at $1). set_config($1,$2,true) is the LOCAL form; interpolating a user zone is an injection hole.

nodes.label: IANA time zone names
nodes.rationale: Follow DST and historical rules. Abbreviations like IST are ambiguous; fixed offsets silently get DST wrong. Store the name, not an offset.

nodes.label: Pin pool timezone to UTC
nodes.rationale: options: '-c timezone=UTC'. Plain SET leaks across pooled release(); SET LOCAL is safe inside a transaction.

nodes.label: timestamptz
nodes.rationale: 8-byte UTC instant. Does not store a zone; converts on input/output. Same instant displays as 04:30+00, 10:00+05:30, 00:30-04.

nodes.label: timestamp without time zone
nodes.rationale: Stores the digits and discards the offset. Same value means different instants to every reader. Only for floating wall-clock values with a stored zone name.

nodes.label: now() vs clock_timestamp()
nodes.rationale: now() is transaction start and stays constant; clock_timestamp() is wall clock per call.

nodes.label: date to JS Date midnight trap
nodes.rationale: pg turns date into Date at local midnight; in Asia/Calcutta that is 18:30 UTC the previous day. Fix with to_char or setTypeParser(1082, v => v).

nodes.label: uuid v4 (random)
nodes.rationale: Random PK: 1727 ms / 8552 kB index vs bigint 947 ms / 4408 kB on 200k inserts. Scatters B-tree writes and splits pages half-empty.

nodes.label: uuidv7() time-ordered
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL 18 built-in. First 48 bits are a millisecond timestamp, recovering locality (1356 ms / 6184 kB) but leaking creation time via uuid_extract_timestamp().

nodes.label: bigint identity primary key
nodes.rationale: Sequential appends stay on the rightmost leaf. Smaller, faster, readable. Common pattern: bigint PK plus a uuid unique column for public ids.

nodes.label: Never store UUID as text
nodes.rationale: 16 bytes as uuid vs 40 as text, plus string comparison and no format validation. pg sends uuid as a string; invalid values fail with 22P02.

nodes.label: Round money once at the end
nodes.rationale: Rounding at each step discards information that compounds. Carry full precision, round at the charging boundary, and store both inputs and rounded outputs.

nodes.label: Largest-remainder allocation
nodes.rationale: 100/3 → 33.33×3 = 99.99. Floor each share, then give leftover pennies to largest remainders so parts sum exactly to the whole.

nodes.label: Store FX rate with the transaction
nodes.rationale: fx_rate numeric(18,8) and fx_rate_at timestamptz are part of the record. Converting at query time makes historical reports change.

nodes.label: Append-only ledger
nodes.rationale: Immutable signed entries; derive balance with SUM. Mutable balances lose history, corrupt permanently, and contend. Snapshot periodically if reads get slow.

nodes.label: Never parseFloat numeric from pg
nodes.rationale: numeric arrives as a string on purpose. Compute in SQL or a decimal library; do not override the type parser.

nodes.label: numeric plus currency column
nodes.rationale: An amount without a currency is incomplete. Composite FK (invoice_id, currency) can force child rows to match the parent currency.

nodes.label: Do not use the money type
nodes.rationale: Locale-dependent via lc_monetary; dump/restore can misinterpret; no currency identity. Docs warn against it for financial records.

nodes.label: ISO 4217 minor units
nodes.rationale: Not every currency has two decimals (JPY 0, some 3). Hard-coded ÷100 is wrong by 10× or 100×. Store minor_units per currency.

nodes.label: Always declare numeric scale
nodes.rationale: Bare numeric allows 16383 fractional digits so 19.990000001 ≠ 19.99. Totals numeric(14,2); unit prices more scale; rates numeric(18,8).

nodes.label: Constant DEFAULT add is catalog-only
nodes.rationale: Since PostgreSQL 11 a constant default is stored once and applied on read — 4 ms at 200k rows. Old three-step dance is obsolete for constants.

nodes.label: Volatile DEFAULT rewrites the table
nodes.rationale: gen_random_uuid() needs a distinct value per row — 902 ms rewrite. Add nullable, batch-backfill, then set default and NOT NULL.

nodes.label: NOT VALID then VALIDATE CONSTRAINT
nodes.rationale: CHECK (col IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID is 3 ms ACCESS EXCLUSIVE; VALIDATE is 25 ms under SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE so reads/writes continue. Then SET NOT NULL can use the CHECK as proof (PG 12+).

nodes.label: Batched backfill
nodes.rationale: One UPDATE over millions holds row locks, huge WAL, and VACUUM's horizon. Batches of a few thousand commit separately.

nodes.label: ALTER TABLE ACCESS EXCLUSIVE
nodes.rationale: Every ALTER takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE. A 3 ms change can outage if it queues behind a long read; later queries queue behind it. Use SET LOCAL lock_timeout.

nodes.label: ALTER TABLE rewrite vs catalog-only
nodes.rationale: relfilenode change means rewrite. int→bigint, narrowing varchar, volatile DEFAULT, SET LOGGED/UNLOGGED rewrite; widening varchar, DROP COLUMN, varchar→text do not.

nodes.label: Add-backfill-swap type change
nodes.rationale: Add new column, batch-backfill, keep current with a trigger, then drop/rename in a short lock_timeout transaction. Interruptible unlike one ALTER TYPE.

nodes.label: Batch ALTER subcommands
nodes.rationale: One statement = one lock acquisition and at most one rewrite pass covering all changes.

nodes.label: COMMENT ON
nodes.rationale: Catalog documentation; pg_dump includes it. Read with obj_description/col_description or \d+. information_schema does not expose comments.

nodes.label: Comments belong in migrations
nodes.rationale: A hand-typed psql comment is lost on rebuild. Comments are not inherited and vanish when an object is dropped/recreated. COMMENT ON replaces; NULL deletes.

nodes.label: CHECK does not reject NULL
nodes.rationale: NULL >= 18 is unknown; CHECK rejects only false. Pair CHECK with NOT NULL, or write CHECK (col IS NULL OR …).

nodes.label: DEFAULT now() is transaction start
nodes.rationale: Two inserts 150 ms apart in one transaction got identical timestamps. Use clock_timestamp() for wall-clock per row.

nodes.label: Explicit NULL bypasses DEFAULT
nodes.rationale: DEFAULT applies only when the column is omitted or DEFAULT. ORMs that send null for unset fields override every default.

nodes.label: Named constraints for API mapping
nodes.rationale: err.constraint plus SQLSTATE (23505→409, 23514→422, 23502→422, 23503→409) turns DB errors into field messages. Auto-generated names change on rename.

nodes.label: CREATE TABLE as the client contract
nodes.rationale: Identity, FKs, CHECKs, money type, timestamptz and FK indexes are decisions every client must obey. DDL via pg returns command CREATE and null rowCount.

nodes.label: GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY vs serial
nodes.rationale: ALWAYS rejects a manual id with 428C9, preventing the sequence from drifting out of step.

nodes.label: Types are expensive to reverse
nodes.rationale: Be liberal with constraints, conservative with types. Constraints relax with NOT VALID; type representation changes rewrite under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE.

nodes.label: Unqualified CREATE TABLE follows search_path
nodes.rationale: Default "$user", public can land the table in an unexpected schema. Schema-qualify DDL in migrations.

nodes.label: DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED
nodes.rationale: Checked at COMMIT. INITIALLY IMMEDIATE is usually right: fail-fast unless SET CONSTRAINTS … DEFERRED. Applies to UNIQUE, PK, EXCLUDE, FK — not NOT NULL.

nodes.label: Circular foreign keys
nodes.rationale: Immediate insert of mutual references fails 23503. Deferral lets both rows exist before the check. Often a modelling smell versus a nullable FK plus flag.

nodes.label: Defer UNIQUE to swap values
nodes.rationale: Swapping positions 1 and 2 collides midway under immediate UNIQUE. A bare unique index cannot be deferred.

nodes.label: Deferrable UNIQUE cannot be ON CONFLICT arbiter
nodes.rationale: Upsert needs an immediate arbiter. Deferring a unique constraint silently removes it as an ON CONFLICT target.

nodes.label: DROP defaults to RESTRICT (2BP01)
nodes.rationale: dependent_objects_still_exist. The error/NOTICE list is the dry-run. Prefer dropping named dependents over blanket CASCADE.

nodes.label: DROP CASCADE is schema not data
nodes.rationale: Drops views and the child's FK constraint; the child table and its rows survive, now orphanable. Opposite of ON DELETE CASCADE.

nodes.label: Rename before drop
nodes.rationale: Rename to old_deprecated_DATE so leftover code fails with 42703 immediately; drop a deploy later. Turns irreversible data loss into a reversible mistake.

nodes.label: ON DELETE actions
nodes.rationale: NO ACTION 23503, RESTRICT 23001, CASCADE deletes children, SET NULL, SET DEFAULT. Map both 23503 and 23001 to HTTP 409.

nodes.label: NO ACTION vs RESTRICT
nodes.rationale: Difference is timing: deferred NO ACTION checks at COMMIT; RESTRICT always fires immediately (23001).

nodes.label: Index every FK referencing column
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL indexes the referenced PK, not the child column. Unindexed parent DELETE scanned 300k children in 33.6 ms vs 8.7 ms indexed.

nodes.label: Application cannot enforce referential integrity
nodes.rationale: Check-then-insert is not atomic; another transaction can delete the parent between them. Only the database evaluates the constraint as part of the write.

nodes.label: GENERATED ALWAYS AS STORED
nodes.rationale: Computed on write from same-row IMMUTABLE inputs and stored. Cannot drift because writes raise 428C9.

nodes.label: Generated expression must be IMMUTABLE
nodes.rationale: now(), random(), nextval(), other tables, STABLE locale functions → 42P17. Falsely marking IMMUTABLE silently freezes a wrong stored value.

nodes.label: No VIRTUAL generated columns in PG 18
nodes.rationale: STORED only. For compute-on-read use a view or expression index. Changing the expression is drop + re-add and rewrites the table.

nodes.label: Table inheritance
nodes.rationale: NOT NULL and CHECK inherit; PK, UNIQUE and FK do not. Two child rows can share id 1. Parent FKs do not see child rows. Avoid for new work.

nodes.label: Declarative partitioning
nodes.rationale: Enforces the key across partitions (23505). Unmatched partition key → 23514. Every unique constraint must include the partition key.

nodes.label: ONLY keyword
nodes.rationale: Without ONLY, SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE on a parent include children. DELETE FROM parent can wipe child rows.

nodes.label: Shared schema with RLS
nodes.rationale: Default tenancy model: one migration, trivial cross-tenant queries, scales to millions. Schema/DB-per-tenant for contractual isolation, not reassurance.

nodes.label: SET LOCAL never SET for tenant identity
nodes.rationale: Plain SET persists on a pooled connection into the next request — cross-tenant exposure under concurrency when RLS keys on that setting.

nodes.label: tenant_id leads every index
nodes.rationale: Every query is tenant-scoped via code and RLS, so an index that does not lead with tenant_id cannot serve the filter.

nodes.label: Schema- or database-per-tenant
nodes.rationale: Structural isolation at the cost of N migrations, hard cross-tenant queries, and a permanent operational tax. Choose when isolation is a contract.

nodes.label: Identifier folding to lower case
nodes.rationale: Unquoted identifiers are lower-cased before lookup; quoted ones are stored verbatim. Creating "UserAccounts" means every future reference must be quoted.

nodes.label: snake_case naming convention
nodes.rationale: Use unquoted snake_case because that is what unquoted identifiers become. Plural tables, singular columns; constraint names follow PostgreSQL generated patterns.

nodes.label: Constraint names are an API
nodes.rationale: err.constraint plus SQLSTATE turns a database error into a field-level message (23505 + users_email_key). Auto-generated names change on column rename; name constraints explicitly.

nodes.label: 63-byte identifier limit
nodes.rationale: max_identifier_length is 63 bytes, truncated silently with a notice. Two long names that differ only after byte 63 collide; non-ASCII hits the limit sooner.

nodes.label: Reserved word user
nodes.rationale: SELECT * FROM user resolves to current_user, not a table. Plural users and other plural table names dodge most reserved-word collisions.

nodes.label: Repository-layer snake_case to camelCase
nodes.rationale: Map once in the repository. Unquoted AS userId folds to userid, so per-query aliases need quotes and drift.

nodes.label: Store every fact exactly once
nodes.rationale: Normalization is a checklist for finding duplicated facts. Duplication permits contradiction that concurrent writers can create and the database cannot resolve.

nodes.label: First normal form
nodes.rationale: One value per column. Comma-separated product_names cannot be joined, indexed, or counted without parsing; fix with a child table.

nodes.label: Second normal form
nodes.rationale: No partial dependency on part of a composite key. product_name on order_items depends only on product_id, not (order_id, product_id).

nodes.label: Third normal form
nodes.rationale: No dependency between non-key columns. customer_city belongs on customers, not orders. Test: every non-key column depends on the key, the whole key, and nothing but the key.

nodes.label: Historical snapshot vs denormalization
nodes.rationale: unit_cents on an order line is a different fact from products.price_cents. Copying price at sale time is required; joining would rewrite past invoices.

nodes.label: Deliberate denormalization
nodes.rationale: Trade write complexity for read speed: counters, generated columns, materialized views. Measure first; prefer forms the database maintains.

nodes.label: Normalize by default
nodes.rationale: A slow read is measurable and fixable later; inconsistent data is often unfixable and erodes trust. Denormalize against EXPLAIN, not a hunch.

nodes.label: GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY
nodes.rationale: SQL-standard identity refuses manual inserts with 428C9. serial accepts them without advancing the sequence, later colliding with 23505.

nodes.label: serial is not a type
nodes.rationale: serial creates an integer, a sequence, and a default. The sequence is owned by the column and dropped with the table. Identity is is_identity, not column_default.

nodes.label: bigint identity, not int
nodes.rationale: int stops at 2,147,483,647. Sequences advance on attempts, so failures burn the range faster than row count. Migrating int→bigint rewrites under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE.

nodes.label: bigint ids as JavaScript strings
nodes.rationale: pg returns bigint as a string because 64-bit exceeds Number.SAFE_INTEGER. Treat ids as opaque strings; user.id + 1 becomes '11'.

nodes.label: Natural vs surrogate keys
nodes.rationale: Surrogate keys win because natural keys change. Natural keys fit immutable reference data (ISO codes). A surrogate does not replace UNIQUE on the natural key.

nodes.label: UUID primary keys
nodes.rationale: 16 bytes vs 8; v4 UUIDs destroy btree insert locality. Prefer UUIDv7 if client-generated ids are required. Adding uuid DEFAULT gen_random_uuid() rewrites the table.

nodes.label: Composite primary keys
nodes.rationale: Natural fit for join tables: PRIMARY KEY (post_id, tag_id) is the uniqueness rule. Leading column serves one direction; the other needs its own index.

nodes.label: One-to-many relationship
nodes.rationale: FK on the many side. NOT NULL makes it mandatory; ON DELETE CASCADE or RESTRICT; always index the referencing column (measured 4× slower unindexed).

nodes.label: One-to-one via unique FK
nodes.rationale: Make the FK the primary key of the child. Without uniqueness it is one-to-many wearing a one-to-one name (second profile → 23505).

nodes.label: Many-to-many join table
nodes.rationale: Join table with PRIMARY KEY (a_id, b_id). A surrogate id would permit the duplicate the composite key forbids.

nodes.label: Composite key serves one direction
nodes.rationale: On 20k join rows, WHERE post_id used Index Only Scan; WHERE tag_id did Seq Scan. Almost always add a second index on the trailing column.

nodes.label: Self-referencing tree
nodes.rationale: parent_id nullable marks a root. ON DELETE CASCADE deletes whole subtrees. Arbitrary depth needs a recursive CTE.

nodes.label: Join table becomes an entity
nodes.rationale: When the relationship carries role, joined_at, quantity it deserves a domain name (memberships). Add a surrogate only if something must reference the relationship.

nodes.label: Schema as namespace
nodes.rationale: A schema is a namespace inside a database. Identical SELECT FROM items returns different rows under tenant_a vs tenant_b via search_path.

nodes.label: search_path
nodes.rationale: Ordered list of schemas for unqualified names. Default is "$user", public. SET search_path persists on a pooled connection and leaks across requests.

nodes.label: Three multi-tenant layouts
nodes.rationale: Shared tables + tenant_id (cheapest, weakest); schema per tenant (catalog multiplies, stops at low thousands); database per tenant (strongest, a pool each).

nodes.label: SET LOCAL search_path
nodes.rationale: SET LOCAL inside a transaction reverts on commit/rollback. Schema names cannot be $1; validate against pg_namespace then escapeIdentifier.

nodes.label: RLS tenant isolation
nodes.rationale: ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY with USING (tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant_id')::bigint) so a forgotten WHERE cannot leak another tenant.

nodes.label: public CREATE revoked since PG15
nodes.rationale: Since PostgreSQL 15, public no longer grants CREATE to PUBLIC. SECURITY DEFINER functions need an explicit search_path to avoid shadowing.

nodes.label: Sequences are non-transactional
nodes.rationale: nextval takes a value and releases immediately so concurrent inserters never block. Rollbacks and failed inserts keep their values — gaps are the design.

nodes.label: Sequence gaps
nodes.rationale: Sources: rollback, unique failure, CACHE n, crash recovery (last_value WAL-logged periodically). Gapless invoice numbers need a serialised counter row.

nodes.label: Sequence OWNED BY
nodes.rationale: serial/identity sequences drop with the table (0 left after DROP). Hand-created sequences survive unless ALTER SEQUENCE … OWNED BY. Ownership does not restrict nextval.

nodes.label: setval sequence repair
nodes.rationale: After explicit ids: setval(seq, max(id)+1, false). is_called false means next nextval returns the given value; true returns the one after.

nodes.label: RETURNING over currval
nodes.rationale: currval is session state and errors 55000 if nextval was never called; lastval() is whichever sequence was touched last. RETURNING is unambiguous and one round trip.

nodes.label: UNLOGGED tables
nodes.rationale: Skip WAL: ~1.5× faster (150→98 ms / 100k inserts). Truncated on crash recovery, never replicated, survive clean restart. Right for regenerable staging and caches.

nodes.label: TEMPORARY tables
nodes.rationale: Private to one session in pg_temp_N, dropped with the session. Shadow permanent names via search_path. Live in temp_buffers (default 8 MB), not shared_buffers.

nodes.label: Temp tables vs connection pooling
nodes.rationale: CREATE on connection A and INSERT on B → 42P01. Hold one checked-out client. ON COMMIT DROP prevents leftover temp data on reused pooled connections.

nodes.label: CTE instead of a temp table
nodes.rationale: If the data is only needed in one statement, WITH staging AS (…) avoids DDL, locks, catalog churn and the pooling problem.

nodes.label: Transactional DDL
nodes.rationale: CREATE/ALTER/DROP roll back like DML. A later failure vanished a successfully created table. Most engines commit DDL implicitly; PostgreSQL does not.

nodes.label: CONCURRENTLY cannot run in a transaction
nodes.rationale: CREATE/DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY, VACUUM, CREATE/DROP DATABASE fail with 25001. A failed CONCURRENTLY build leaves an INVALID index still maintained on writes.

nodes.label: Keep DDL transactions short
nodes.rationale: ACCESS EXCLUSIVE is held until commit; an open transaction pins VACUUM's cleanup horizon database-wide. Atomicity is free; duration is not.

nodes.label: Unique column accepts unlimited NULLs
nodes.rationale: Two NULLs are not equal under SQL three-valued logic. Measured: 3 NULLs inserted into a UNIQUE column. SQL-standard, not a PostgreSQL quirk.

nodes.label: NULLS NOT DISTINCT
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL 15+: NULLs compare as equal so only one is allowed (second → 23505). Works on index and constraint forms; no sentinel COALESCE needed.

nodes.label: Unique constraint vs unique index
nodes.rationale: Same btree. FK can only target a constraint. Only an index can be partial, on an expression, or built CONCURRENTLY. Production: CONCURRENTLY then UNIQUE USING INDEX.

nodes.label: Partial unique index for soft delete
nodes.rationale: UNIQUE among live rows: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX … (email) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL. Constraints cannot be partial, so tombstones would block re-registration.

nodes.label: Case-insensitive uniqueness
nodes.rationale: UNIQUE (email) treats Alice@x.com and alice@x.com as different. Fix with unique index on lower(email) (queries must match the expression) or a non-deterministic ICU collation.

nodes.label: Uniqueness only under concurrency via the constraint
nodes.rationale: Application pre-check has a window between read and write. 20 workers produced 20 duplicates and no errors. Map 23505 to 409 via err.constraint.

nodes.label: Shared schema as the tenancy default
nodes.rationale: Only model that scales to thousands of tenants; migrations run once; reporting is ordinary SQL. Weak isolation is bought back with repository + RLS + tests.

nodes.label: tenant_id leads every index
nodes.rationale: Every query is tenant-scoped (explicitly and via RLS). Index (created_at) is nearly useless; (tenant_id, created_at) serves the real filter. Most common shared-schema perf failure.

nodes.label: Uniqueness is per tenant
nodes.rationale: UNIQUE (tenant_id, slug) so tenant B can reuse a slug tenant A took. A global unique is unintended cross-tenant coupling.

nodes.label: RESTRICTIVE RLS plus FORCE
nodes.rationale: RESTRICTIVE so isolation applies regardless of permissive policies. FORCE so the table owner cannot bypass. Connect as a non-owner application role.

nodes.label: set_config LOCAL for app.tenant_id
nodes.rationale: SET LOCAL x = $1 is 42601. Use set_config('app.tenant_id', $1, true) inside a transaction. Plain SET persists across pool handoff (measured in ex54).

nodes.label: Schema-per-tenant
nodes.rationale: Right when isolation is contractual, schemas genuinely differ, or per-tenant restore is routine. Cost: N migrations, UNION reports, growing catalog, safety-critical search_path.

nodes.label: Database-per-tenant
nodes.rationale: Rare: tens of large tenants needing strict isolation and resource limits. Pooling multiplies; onboarding is provisioning; no cross-tenant SQL.

nodes.label: Tenancy decision order
nodes.rationale: Contractual isolation first, then tenant count (thousands force shared), then cross-tenant query frequency, then genuine schema variation. Default shared + RLS.

nodes.label: Shared → separated is reversible
nodes.rationale: Filter by tenant_id and copy out. Separated → shared remaps colliding identities everywhere. Start shared when the requirement is uncertain.

nodes.label: Tenant onboarding
nodes.rationale: Shared: INSERT (ms). Schema: CREATE SCHEMA + N migrations (seconds–minutes). Database: provision + pool. Self-serve signup makes the latter a product constraint.

nodes.label: Tenant deletion and erasure
nodes.rationale: Separated: DROP SCHEMA/DATABASE CASCADE. Shared: DELETE in FK order, generate table list from information_schema, or ON DELETE CASCADE. Backups retain data for the retention window.

nodes.label: Noisy neighbour in shared schema
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL has no intra-database isolation. Per-role timeouts, separate pools per tier, rate limits, reporting replica. Hybrid: long tail shared, whales dedicated.

nodes.label: BYPASSRLS analytics role
nodes.rationale: Cross-tenant admin/billing queries need a dedicated BYPASSRLS role, not the table owner. Owner bypass is implicit and indistinguishable from an oversight.

nodes.label: Tenant isolation test suite
nodes.rationale: A reads B by id → 0 rows; insert/update to B's id rejected; no context → 0 or error; sequential requests on one pooled connection must not inherit tenant.

nodes.label: application_name carries tenant
nodes.rationale: pg_stat_statements normalises tenant id as a parameter. Put tenant in application_name so pg_stat_activity and the slow-query log attribute work per tenant.

nodes.label: tenant_id as future shard key
nodes.rationale: Shared schema shards later because tenant_id is already the partition key. Keep it on every table and avoid cross-tenant FKs.

nodes.label: now() is transaction start time
nodes.rationale: now() aliases transaction_timestamp(); two inserts 150 ms apart share a timestamp. statement_timestamp() is per statement; clock_timestamp() is wall clock.

nodes.label: date maps to JS Date at local midnight
nodes.rationale: pg maps date to Date at local midnight. On UTC+5:30, date '2026-01-01' becomes 2025-12-31T18:30:00Z. Return to_char or setTypeParser(1082).

nodes.label: date_trunc bucketing
nodes.rationale: Correct way to bucket for reports (timestamp, sortable, indexable). Pass a timezone: date_trunc('day', ts, 'Europe/Berlin') or local midnight lands in the previous UTC day.

nodes.label: age() vs timestamp subtraction
nodes.rationale: age returns a symbolic interval (1 mon is 28–31 days). Subtraction is elapsed time. pg returns interval as PostgresInterval, not a number.

nodes.label: interval 1 day vs 24 hours
nodes.rationale: Differ on DST: 1 day keeps wall-clock time (23 or 25 h); 24 hours is elapsed. Same time tomorrow vs token expires in 24 hours.

nodes.label: timestamptz for instants
nodes.rationale: timestamptz stores UTC and renders in TimeZone. timestamp without zone is a wall-clock reading with no recoverable zone. SET TIME ZONE on a pool leaks like search_path.

nodes.label: DELETE with no WHERE
nodes.rationale: WHERE is optional. Measured: DELETE FROM d_all removed 10 rows with no warning. Wrap in BEGIN and check the count. To empty a table, prefer TRUNCATE.

nodes.label: DELETE takes no LIMIT
nodes.rationale: DELETE … LIMIT is 42601. Batch via ctid IN (SELECT ctid … LIMIT n). Never store ctid; it changes on update.

nodes.label: ON DELETE RESTRICT vs NO ACTION
nodes.rationale: Both refuse; 23001 vs 23503. NO ACTION is deferrable to commit (default). RESTRICT checks immediately and cannot be deferred. CASCADE is transitive and silent.

nodes.label: Batched DELETE on live tables
nodes.rationale: One 100k DELETE 115 ms vs 10 batches 484 ms (4.2× slower). Batching releases locks, stays interruptible, does not pin VACUUM, bounds WAL/replication lag.

nodes.label: DELETE leaves dead tuples
nodes.rationale: 47 MB table stayed 47 MB after deleting half and after VACUUM. VACUUM FULL rewrote to 24 MB under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE. VACUUM truncates only trailing empty pages.

nodes.label: Soft delete is an UPDATE
nodes.rationale: Setting deleted_at fires no cascade, unique constraints still see the row, every query needs WHERE deleted_at IS NULL. Idempotent: second delete rowCount 0.

nodes.label: DISTINCT ON
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL-only: keep the first row per group as ORDER BY produced them. DISTINCT ON (user_id) … ORDER BY user_id, at DESC is latest event per user, whole row.

nodes.label: DISTINCT ON ORDER BY rule
