nodes.rationale: A migration is a numbered file that runs exactly once, inside a transaction, with the fact recorded in the database. Drop any property and the schema is unreproducible.

nodes.label: schema_migrations tracking table
nodes.rationale: version PK, applied_at, checksum. The database records its own version. version PK answers 'has this run?' by constraint, not app logic.

nodes.label: Forward-only migrations
nodes.rationale: Down migrations are rarely tested and cannot restore DROP COLUMN data. Recovery is a new forward file plus backup restore.

nodes.label: Migration checksum
nodes.rationale: Never edit a shipped file. Runner re-hashes and fails if checksum changes, so two environments cannot share a version with different schemas.

nodes.label: Lexical migration filename order
nodes.rationale: Filename sort is lexical: 1, 10, 11, 2. Surfaces as 42P01 on a fresh database. Fix with zero-padding or UTC timestamps.

nodes.label: Timestamped migration filenames
nodes.rationale: UTC timestamps avoid branch collisions on counter names. Ordering is authorship time, which may not be dependency order. Tools generate these.

nodes.label: Migrations as a deploy step
nodes.rationale: Not at app boot. Failure should stop the deploy, app role should lack CREATE/ALTER, and ACCESS EXCLUSIVE must not block old instances still serving traffic.

nodes.label: Writing a minimal migration runner
nodes.rationale: A correct runner is about sixty lines. Write it to learn the mechanism; switch when you need CONCURRENTLY, baselining, dry-run, or JS data migrations.

nodes.label: migrate()
nodes.rationale: Creates schema_migrations, checks out one client, BEGIN, pg_advisory_xact_lock, lexical .sql sort, sha256 checksum, apply+INSERT, COMMIT.

nodes.label: One client for lock and apply
nodes.rationale: BEGIN, advisory lock and every migration must share one session. pool.query would split them across connections.

nodes.label: Lock before reading tracking table
nodes.rationale: pg_advisory_xact_lock immediately after BEGIN, before SELECT from schema_migrations. Locking after the read leaves a window both runners see empty.

nodes.label: Batch vs per-file transaction
nodes.rationale: Batch is all-or-nothing and simpler. Per-file resumes after failure, releases locks between files, and is the only way a CONCURRENTLY file can opt out. Tools default to per-file.

nodes.label: Schema drift
nodes.rationale: Drift is live schema vs what code assumes. Migrations prevent most of it; a boot-time check turns 42703 into a deploy that refuses to start.

nodes.label: checkSchema() boot check
nodes.rationale: Compare EXPECTED columns against information_schema.columns; process.exit(1) on mismatch. A container that will not start is rollback-able.

nodes.label: What a naive drift check misses
nodes.rationale: numeric(p,s) reports as numeric; varchar length in character_maximum_length; identity is is_identity not column_default; indexes and constraints live in other catalogs.

nodes.label: Generate drift expectation in CI
nodes.rationale: Hand-maintained EXPECTED drifts. Generate after migrations, or catalog-diff a scratch DB against production, or generate types.

nodes.label: Seeding
nodes.rationale: A seed runs more than once. If twice is not identical to once, it is a data-corruption script.

nodes.label: ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
nodes.rationale: Requires a unique constraint. Measured rowCount 2, 0, 0. Bare INSERT raises 23505. SELECT-then-INSERT is not idempotent under concurrency.

nodes.label: Identity consumed on skipped conflict
nodes.rationale: ON CONFLICT still evaluates the row and draws identity first. Three runs of two rows left last_value at 6. Sequences are not gapless.

nodes.label: DO NOTHING versus DO UPDATE
nodes.rationale: DO NOTHING for rows a human may edit. DO UPDATE SET col = EXCLUDED.col for reference data the code depends on.

nodes.label: Seeding is not migration
nodes.rationale: Migrations change schema, run once, not edited after shipping. Seeds run every time and are editable. Reference data later migrations depend on belongs in a migration.

nodes.label: SQL in .sql files, not template literals
nodes.rationale: SQL in JS strings is invisible to formatters, linters and psql. Files cost a loader and restore tooling, diffs and a boundary against concatenation.

nodes.label: sql() file loader
nodes.rationale: Resolve from import.meta.url, cache in a Map in production. process.cwd() works in tests and fails in production.

nodes.label: Multi-statement .sql result array
nodes.rationale: No params: simple protocol, query() is an array, res.rows is undefined. Non-empty params: 42601 cannot insert multiple commands. Keep app query files to one statement.

nodes.label: Named SQL parameters
nodes.rationale: Comment headers or a :name shim that emits real $n placeholders. Regex must not rewrite :: casts. Values never enter SQL text.

nodes.label: Resetting between test runs
nodes.rationale: Reset strategy sets suite speed. Fastest option requires every query on one injected client.

nodes.label: Transaction rollback per test
nodes.rationale: 0.8 ms measured vs TRUNCATE 4.4 ms. Discards only the test's writes; seed survives. Requires injected client and no nested COMMIT. Cannot test commit-only effects.

nodes.label: TRUNCATE RESTART IDENTITY CASCADE
nodes.rationale: One statement lists every table to avoid deadlock. CASCADE for FKs (0A000 otherwise). RESTART IDENTITY or next id is 10001 after 10k rows.

nodes.label: Drop and migrate once per suite
nodes.rationale: Only strategy that tests migrations. Seconds, not milliseconds. Combine with rollback per test.

nodes.label: Wrapping a migration in BEGIN/COMMIT
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL transactional DDL is why a failed migration leaves nothing and why forward-only is practical here unlike MySQL.

nodes.label: Transactional DDL
nodes.rationale: Failed third CREATE rolled back two successful tables. Tracking insert must share the transaction or applied and recorded diverge.

nodes.label: Statements that cannot be in a transaction
nodes.rationale: CREATE/DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY, VACUUM, CREATE DATABASE fail with 25001. Runners use a per-file -- migrate: no-transaction directive.

nodes.label: INVALID leftover CONCURRENTLY index
nodes.rationale: Failed CONCURRENTLY build leaves an unused index that still costs writes. Find with pg_index WHERE NOT indisvalid; DROP and rebuild.

nodes.label: SET LOCAL lock_timeout
nodes.rationale: SET LOCAL scopes to the transaction so it does not leak onto a pooled connection. 55P03 plus transactional DDL means retry is safe.

nodes.label: Issuing DDL through the driver
nodes.rationale: CREATE TABLE is client.query. Success is no thrown error; rowCount is null and fields is empty.

nodes.label: Identifiers cannot be parameters
nodes.rationale: CREATE TABLE $1 raises 42601 at parse time. Dynamic identifiers need format('%I')/quote_ident/escapeIdentifier behind an allowlist.

nodes.label: Simple vs extended query protocol
nodes.rationale: No params or []: simple protocol, multi-statement, array of results. One parameter: extended, one statement only. Empty array is not 'some parameters'.

nodes.label: ADD COLUMN DEFAULT without rewrite
nodes.rationale: Since PG 11, ADD COLUMN NOT NULL DEFAULT stores the default as catalog metadata. relfilenode unchanged. Type changes generally rewrite.

nodes.label: DDL locks and the blocking they cause
nodes.rationale: What the same DDL does to a table being read. ACCESS EXCLUSIVE conflicts with everything including SELECT's ACCESS SHARE.

nodes.label: ACCESS EXCLUSIVE
nodes.rationale: ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN takes AccessExclusiveLock. CREATE INDEX takes ShareLock (writes block, reads proceed). CONCURRENTLY permits writes.

nodes.label: Lock queue convoy
nodes.rationale: 12 ms ALTER behind a 3 s read blocked later SELECTs for 2.4 s. Locks grant in request order so strong lockers cannot starve. Pool exhausts as 'too many clients'.

nodes.label: lock_timeout vs statement_timeout
nodes.rationale: lock_timeout bounds lock wait (55P03). statement_timeout bounds execution; a waiter is not executing. Set lock_timeout per migration session.

nodes.label: Startup races and advisory locks
nodes.rationale: ensureSchema() at boot is a bug. IF NOT EXISTS is idempotent, not concurrency-safe.

nodes.label: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS race
nodes.rationale: Catalog check and insert are not atomic. 228/500 failed with 23505 on pg_type_typname_nsp_index.

nodes.label: Silent startup seed race
nodes.rationale: 20 workers, 20 duplicate admin rows, zero errors. Worse than CREATE race because it is silent data corruption.

nodes.label: pg_advisory_xact_lock
nodes.rationale: Transaction-scoped lock on a chosen bigint. 500/500 succeeded. Session-scoped pg_advisory_lock can wedge after a crash. Same mechanism real tools use.

nodes.label: Sort and filter allowlists
nodes.rationale: ?sort=price reintroduces injection after everything else is parameterized. Values can be parameters; column names and ASC/DESC cannot.

nodes.label: Allowlist as a key-to-SQL map
nodes.rationale: Lookup of request keys to SQL you wrote, not validation. ORDER BY $1 binds as a constant and silently does nothing; concatenating an identifier can stacked-DROP.

nodes.label: Passing a client through services
nodes.rationale: One transaction across repositories works only if every function uses the same client. Handing the pool breaks atomicity with no error.

nodes.label: Pool instead of client half-commit
nodes.rationale: insertOrder(client) rolled back; insertItem(pool) committed. orders=0 items=1. Different backend pids; PostgreSQL has no reason to object.

nodes.label: db as first argument
nodes.rationale: Only the handler names pool. Services that open their own transaction cannot be composed. grep pool in services/repositories should be empty.

nodes.label: AsyncLocalStorage ambient client
nodes.rationale: Removes the forgotten-argument bug. ?? pool fallback reintroduces silent autocommit when async context is lost. Throw if no store.

nodes.label: create — INSERT ... RETURNING
nodes.rationale: Answer with the row the database stored, not the one the client sent. RETURNING avoids a second query and a race.

nodes.label: INSERT ... RETURNING
nodes.rationale: Generated id, DEFAULT now(), GENERATED columns and trigger-set values come back in one round trip. currval is session-scoped and unsafe through a pool.

nodes.label: Name RETURNING columns
nodes.rationale: RETURNING * publishes whatever the table has, including a later password_hash. Name the mapper's columns. 201 + Location is the usual response.

nodes.label: createMany via unnest
nodes.rationale: One array parameter per column stays under the 65535-parameter cap. RETURNING order is not guaranteed; return a correlating column.

nodes.label: delete hard vs soft
nodes.rationale: Hard delete removes the row and cascades. Soft delete is an UPDATE that makes every query wrong until you add deleted_at IS NULL. Schema-wide, not per-endpoint.

nodes.label: Hard delete with RETURNING
nodes.rationale: rowCount 0 is 404, not an error. ON DELETE CASCADE fires. Missing-row delete is not thrown.

nodes.label: Soft delete UPDATE
nodes.rationale: SET deleted_at = now() WHERE id AND deleted_at IS NULL. No FK cascade. Not an audit log. AND deleted_at IS NULL keeps retries from overwriting the timestamp.

nodes.label: Partial unique index for live emails
nodes.rationale: Full unique index blocks re-registration (23505). UNIQUE (email) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL. A lookup without the predicate can hit either row; a partial index is unusable without it.

nodes.label: findById and the not-found decision
nodes.rationale: A missing row is a successful empty result. Every 404 is application policy. The decision is where you add it.

nodes.label: findX vs getX
nodes.rationale: find returns null when absence is expected; get throws NotFoundError when absence is impossible. rows[0] ?? null, never undefined (JSON drops the key).

nodes.label: 22P02 malformed id is 400
nodes.rationale: GET /users/abc against bigint raises 22P02. Validate at the edge; map SQLSTATE as backstop. Not 404.

nodes.label: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE inside a request
nodes.rationale: Pessimistic answer to lost updates: lock at read, queue instead of retry. Meaningless outside a transaction.

nodes.label: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE
nodes.rationale: Locks returned rows until commit. Two concurrent adds produced 130 with no retries. Readers still see the old MVCC version.

nodes.label: Do slow work first, lock last
nodes.rationale: Eight 100 ms requests: 863 ms with work inside the lock vs 143 ms with lock only to write. Re-read the locked row before writing.

nodes.label: NOWAIT vs SKIP LOCKED
nodes.rationale: NOWAIT raises 55P03 immediately (409). SKIP LOCKED omits locked rows — right for job queues, wrong for point lookup (looks like not found). lock_timeout also 55P03, different message.

nodes.label: Lock rows in consistent order
nodes.rationale: Opposite lock orders deadlock (40P01). ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE. FOR UPDATE OF table restricts join locking.

nodes.label: Idempotent writes
nodes.rationale: Any network write will be called twice. The second call is a condition to handle, not a bug to prevent.

nodes.label: Idempotency-Key unique constraint
nodes.rationale: Client UUID in a header. Unique index is correctness: 10 racing INSERTs → 1 success, 9× 23505. ON CONFLICT only shapes the response.

nodes.label: DO UPDATE so RETURNING fires
nodes.rationale: DO NOTHING RETURNING gives rowCount 0 on replay. SET key = EXCLUDED.key is a no-op UPDATE so RETURNING returns the original row. (xmax = 0) AS was_inserted distinguishes 201 from 200.

nodes.label: idempotency_keys response table
nodes.rationale: Store status+response when the body cannot be recomputed from the row. request_hash rejects key reuse with a different body (422). Scope PRIMARY KEY (user_id, key). In-flight → 409.

nodes.label: Keyset (cursor) pagination
nodes.rationale: Remember the last row and ask for what comes after. 1.23 ms vs 295.87 ms OFFSET at the same depth on 500k rows.

nodes.label: Tuple comparison (created_at, id) < ($1, $2)
nodes.rationale: Row constructor matches a composite index. Hand-written OR form looks equivalent and is ~160× slower. Sort key must be total; nullables silently truncate the walk.

nodes.label: list with filtering, sorting and pagination
nodes.rationale: Filters are parameters, sort is an allowlist, pagination is two more parameters plus a tiebreaker. Wrong combination duplicates rows with no error.

nodes.label: Assembled list query
nodes.rationale: buildWhere + orderClause + LIMIT/OFFSET as last parameters. Clamp limit. Number() junk input; uncoerced 'abc' is 22P02.

nodes.label: Unique ORDER BY tiebreaker
nodes.rationale: ORDER BY grp over 30k rows: 54 distinct / 46 repeats paging 100. Append , id. Instability is between offsets, so repeating page 1 does not catch it.

nodes.label: OFFSET is the wrong default
nodes.rationale: OFFSET n produces and discards n rows. Concurrent inserts shift the window. Keyset for infinite scroll/public APIs; OFFSET for page-number admin UIs. Prefer hasMore over count(*).

nodes.label: Optimistic concurrency
nodes.rationale: Default for human-timescale edits. No locks when uncontended. Lost updates span two HTTP requests that no transaction can cover.

nodes.label: Lost update
nodes.rationale: Two requests both read 100, wrote 110 and 120; both reported ok; expected 130. No error.

nodes.label: version column
nodes.rationale: UPDATE … SET balance, version = version + 1 WHERE id AND version = $n. Increment in the same statement. Stale write is rowCount 0 → 409. updated_at fails when now() is shared in one transaction.

nodes.label: rowCount 0 is 404 or 409
nodes.rationale: Missing row and stale version look identical. Re-read or a data-modifying CTE (updated/conflict/empty). Never report 404 for a conflict.

nodes.label: Retry only relative operations
nodes.rationale: Add-N can retry. Absolute 'set to what the user saw' is a 409. Cap attempts and back off. ETag/If-Match is the HTTP spelling (412).

nodes.label: A repository module per resource
nodes.rationale: Not a class or SQL abstraction. A module of functions whose first argument is whatever will run the query, so the same function works standalone and in a transaction.

nodes.label: Executor contract
nodes.rationale: db first. Pool and Client are interchangeable if the repo never calls pool.connect() itself. That leak is why tests inject a client.

nodes.label: One-pass predicate and parameter builder
nodes.rationale: Build predicate strings and the parameter array in the same loop so $n numbering cannot drift. Built separately you get a runtime error or an injection hole.

nodes.label: Placeholder from params.length
nodes.rationale: params.length after the push is the 1-based $n. A separate i++ drifts on a branch that increments without pushing.

nodes.label: Bound parameter cannot become SQL
nodes.rationale: The statement is parsed before the value is bound. apple'; DROP TABLE fs_items; -- as $1 returned 0 rows and left the table intact.

nodes.label: = ANY($1) for variable-length IN
nodes.rationale: One array parameter keeps statement text constant. Generated IN ($1,$2,$3) fills pg_stat_statements; IN () is a syntax error; ANY('{}') matches nothing.

nodes.label: Omit WHERE when there are no filters
nodes.rationale: WHERE 1=1 works but leaves a permanently true predicate in every plan and log. Emit WHERE only when where.length > 0.

nodes.label: ILIKE wildcard escaping
nodes.rationale: A user searching % is not injection — the parameter is still a value — but it matches every row and can DoS a large table. Escape \, %, _ and declare ESCAPE '\'.

nodes.label: Sorting cannot use the parameter builder
nodes.rationale: ORDER BY needs an identifier. Identifiers cannot be parameters; ORDER BY $1 silently sorts by a constant.

nodes.label: ORDER BY $1 silent no-op
nodes.rationale: The parameter binds as a constant string, so every row sorts by the same value. Sorting by name and by price returned byte-identical output and no error.

nodes.label: Concatenated identifier injection
nodes.rationale: No parameter array uses the simple query protocol, which permits stacked statements. ?sort=name; DROP TABLE fs_items CASCADE; -- executed 2 statements and the table was gone. Same payload as $1 left the table intact.

nodes.label: SORTABLE lookup map
nodes.rationale: An allowlist is not validation. Use the request key into an object whose values are SQL you authored. User input never reaches the query. Direction is a ternary, never interpolated.

nodes.label: Null-prototype or Map allowlist
nodes.rationale: A plain object resolves ?sort=constructor or ?sort=__proto__ to something truthy that is not a column.

nodes.label: quote_ident and format %I
nodes.rationale: Quoting stops stacked statements but is not authorization. An attacker can still order by any real column, including password_hash. %s is unquoted substitution.

nodes.label: FILTERABLE column and operator spec
nodes.rationale: Both the column and the operator come from the map. Letting the client choose ?op=>= is the same identifier hole.

nodes.label: withTransaction
nodes.rationale: connect, BEGIN, fn(client), COMMIT; ROLLBACK in catch (its own try/catch so it cannot replace the original error); release in finally.

nodes.label: pool.query BEGIN is not a transaction
nodes.rationale: Each pool.query checks out its own connection. On an idle pool it appears to work (same pid). With 8 concurrent inserts, 7 of 8 writes survived ROLLBACK.

nodes.label: 25P02 aborted transaction
nodes.rationale: After the first error every later statement is refused, including SELECT 1. COMMIT on an aborted transaction rolls back and reports success.

nodes.label: SAVEPOINT for an optional step
nodes.rationale: ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT rewinds to the savepoint, not the failing statement — both item inserts vanished including the one that succeeded. Thousands of savepoints overflow the 64-XID subtransaction cache.

nodes.label: Idle in transaction from a non-query await
nodes.rationale: A 1240 ms payment call held the transaction open 1223 ms: occupies a pool slot, holds locks, and pins xmin so VACUUM cannot clean tables the endpoint never touches.

nodes.label: Partial updates — COALESCE vs a built SET list
COALESCE partial-update form
nodes.rationale: A static statement cannot distinguish absent from explicit null. PATCH {nickname: null} left the nickname unchanged.

nodes.label: Built SET list from client keys
nodes.rationale: Object.entries sees present-and-null. Column names go through an allowlist; only values are parameters. A crafted key was rejected by membership.

nodes.label: IS DISTINCT FROM no-op skip
nodes.rationale: SET city = city still wrote a row version (rowCount 1). AND city IS DISTINCT FROM $2 skipped it. <> is NULL when either side is NULL.

nodes.label: Naming a SET column does not defeat HOT
nodes.rationale: COALESCE naming indexed b kept 1090 HOT of 2500; built SET of unindexed a had 1096. Changing b dropped HOT to 0.

nodes.label: Executor db argument
nodes.rationale: Every repository function takes something with .query(text, params) as its first argument. It never imports the pool. BoundPool and Client returned identical results from the same function body.

nodes.label: Pool vs Client at the wire
nodes.rationale: pool.query checks out, runs one statement, and returns the connection. Consecutive calls can be different sessions and snapshots. A client is one connection held for a transaction.

nodes.label: Forgotten client.release
nodes.rationale: With max: 2, call 3 failed after 1501 ms. pool.end stayed pending until stranded clients were released.

nodes.label: toDomain mapper
nodes.rationale: Lives next to the SELECT list. It is an allowlist: a later column does not appear in the API until named here. Missing SELECT returns undefined, not an error.

nodes.label: bigint arrives as a String
nodes.rationale: pg will not silently lose precision past Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER. id === 2 is false because id is '2'. Treat ids as opaque strings.

nodes.label: rowCount vs rows.length
nodes.rationale: rowCount is rows affected; rows is what was returned. UPDATE without RETURNING has rowCount 3 and rows.length 0. rowCount is null, not 0, for CREATE TABLE.

nodes.label: A missing row is not an error
nodes.rationale: SELECT matching nothing is success: rowCount 0, rows [], rows[0] undefined. Normalise to null so JSON.stringify does not drop the key.

nodes.label: Switch on err.constraint not message
nodes.rationale: Every unique violation is 23505. Only constraint distinguishes email_taken from username_taken. err.message is translated prose.

nodes.label: err.detail leak
nodes.rationale: 23505 detail echoes the submitted key value. 23514 detail is the entire failing row, including columns the client never sent.

nodes.label: OFFSET vs keyset at depth
nodes.rationale: OFFSET 499980 produced 500000 rows and 501918 buffers to return 20 — 295.87 ms vs 1.23 ms keyset. OFFSET does not skip rows; it produces and discards them.

nodes.label: Row constructor (a, b) < ($1, $2)
nodes.rationale: Lexicographic comparison matching ORDER BY. Becomes Index Cond (0.99 ms, 23 buffers). Expanded OR becomes Filter and removed 250001 rows (158.12 ms).

nodes.label: Index Cond vs Filter
nodes.rationale: Index Cond decides where the scan starts and stops. Filter is applied to rows already produced.

nodes.label: base64url cursor encoding
nodes.rationale: base64 + and / are not URL-safe. Keep timestamp precision; keep bigint id as a string. Base64 is not security — sign if the cursor must not be forgeable.

nodes.label: Fetch limit + 1 for hasMore
nodes.rationale: The extra row is cheaper than count(*) over the predicate. nextCursor is null at the end of the collection.

nodes.label: Mixed-direction keyset trap
nodes.rationale: (a,b) < (x,y) means DESC on both. Against ORDER BY created_at DESC, id ASC it returned plausible wrong ids. Needs the expanded comparison plus a matching mixed-direction index.

nodes.label: Nullable sort column excludes later pages
nodes.rationale: Comparison against NULL is never true. Page 1 includes nulls (no WHERE); later pages drop them. Measured 250000 of 500000 excluded. NULLS LAST does not fix the predicate.

nodes.label: When OFFSET is still right
nodes.rationale: At 50 pages OFFSET was 0.9× keyset. At 500 pages keyset was 6.4× faster. Use OFFSET for shallow page-number UIs; keyset for feeds, APIs, exports, crawlers.

nodes.label: Shaping the response in SQL vs in JavaScript
jsonb_agg nested shaping
nodes.rationale: Slowest option measured: 284.8 ms vs 90.7 ms JS grouping. 232 ms was server CPU parsing jsonb. json_agg was 131.2 ms. Payload 2.0 MB vs 1.2 MB flat.

nodes.label: Flat join grouped in JavaScript
nodes.rationale: Default: one join, Map-group in JS behind the repository mapper. Two queries + JS was 103.3 ms — a wash. Keeps one query serving several response shapes.

nodes.label: N+1 one query per parent
nodes.rationale: 298.6 ms for 500 orders; 2986 ms extrapolated to 5000. The one to avoid.

nodes.label: jsonb_agg empty-children trap
nodes.rationale: LEFT JOIN plus jsonb_agg yields [{sku:null}]. Need FILTER (WHERE child.id IS NOT NULL) and coalesce(..., '[]'::jsonb) because an aggregate over zero rows is NULL.

nodes.label: Types change through jsonb
nodes.rationale: numeric as a column is the string '11.00'; through jsonb it is the number 11. timestamptz goes Date → string. jsonb also reorders keys.

nodes.label: Per-test transaction rollback
nodes.rationale: BEGIN in beforeEach, ROLLBACK in afterEach. 1.66 ms vs 42.50 ms truncate-and-reseed (25×). Parallel-safe because nothing is committed.

nodes.label: Sequences are not transactional
nodes.rationale: A rolled-back insert still consumed an id (last_value 2002 → 2003). Never assert on a literal id.

nodes.label: Pool cannot see the test fixture
nodes.rationale: Uncommitted data is invisible to other connections. Test client saw 1 row; pool saw 0. The harness enforces the executor contract.

nodes.label: Remap BEGIN/COMMIT to savepoints in tests
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL has no nested transactions. An inner COMMIT ends the test transaction; 1 row leaked. After remapping, 0 rows survived.

nodes.label: created_at and updated_at — trigger or application code
created_at DEFAULT now()
nodes.rationale: A DEFAULT covers every insert path including COPY. No trigger needed. Use timestamptz, not timestamp.

nodes.label: BEFORE UPDATE updated_at trigger
nodes.rationale: App-managed updated_at stayed stale on an UPDATE that never mentioned it. Trigger moved it. Cost 1.23–1.29× on the update (328.9 vs 266.8 ms). BEFORE can assign NEW; AFTER would need a second UPDATE.

nodes.label: now() is the transaction timestamp
nodes.rationale: Every row in one transaction shares updated_at. clock_timestamp() moved 303 ms. That is why updated_at cannot be an optimistic-concurrency version.

nodes.label: Mapping snake_case columns to camelCase fields
Unquoted identifiers fold to lower case
nodes.rationale: CREATE TABLE t (fullName text) stores fullname. Quoting forever, miss one quote, 42703. snake_case is the convention where what you type is what you get.

nodes.label: Explicit JS field mapper
nodes.rationale: 31.6 ms over 20000 rows, tied with SQL alias (33.2 ms). An allowlist by construction. Reverse direction is a lookup map, not camelToSnake().

nodes.label: Generic snake-to-camel rewriter
nodes.rationale: 2.3× slower (75.3 ms). Publishes every column like SELECT *. oauth2_token → oauth2Token → oauth_2_token. Rewrites keys inside jsonb payloads.

nodes.label: Quoted SQL alias trap
nodes.rationale: ORDER BY customerName after AS "customerName" failed with 42703 column "customername" does not exist. Fine for a fixed SELECT list, awkward for a dynamic one.

nodes.label: Phase 2 — Data types and the relational model
Phase 3 — DDL tables constraints schema design
Phase 8 — Schema and data from Node
Phase 10 — Indexes and the query planner
Phase 1 — JSX and what a component returns
Phase 3 — State and the render cycle
React 19.2.8 / react-dom 19.2.8
nodes.rationale: Target latest dist-tag as of August 2026. Browser experiments in Firefox 153.0; Node 24.19.0.

nodes.label: React claimed by session 52a29103
nodes.rationale: Owner since 2026-08-13 for the whole of docs/react/. Other sessions must not write React pages.

nodes.label: Sandbox-proven versus documentation-validated
nodes.rationale: Phases 0–1 keep sandbox console blocks. From Phase 2 onward claims are validated against react.dev/MDN with no invented output.

nodes.label: Phase 0 is not optional
nodes.rationale: Every 'React is weird' complaint — reset state, doubled effects, one-update-behind values — traces back to how React runs.

nodes.label: Phase 0 load-bearing pages
nodes.rationale: Pages 01, 03, 04 and 07: What React is; Render/reconcile/commit; Reconciliation; StrictMode.

nodes.label: sandbox/react-p0
nodes.rationale: Every Phase 0 console block is produced by a named script in sandbox/react-p0/.

nodes.label: React 19 ships no UMD build
nodes.rationale: Browser experiments are bundled with esbuild and served to Firefox over puppeteer-core.

nodes.label: Phase 0 gate
nodes.rationale: Explain type-change remounts without saying virtual DOM; what the DOM contains during render; what StrictMode double-mount tests.

nodes.label: JSX is not a template language
nodes.rationale: JSX is syntax for one function call. Costly mistakes: 0 appearing in a list, onclick never firing, typed text following the wrong row.

nodes.label: Index keys do not remount
nodes.rationale: Measured: React keeps the nodes and rewrites their text. Missing-key warning is suppressed after the first offending list.

nodes.label: The && zero trap
nodes.rationale: {items.length && <List/>} can put a 0 on the screen because 0 and NaN do not vanish.

nodes.label: Phase 1 gate
nodes.rationale: Hand-compile JSX including where key goes; predict swap with index vs stable keys; explain the && zero.

nodes.label: Function components
nodes.rationale: React calls it, not you — a new function object per render destroys the subtree.

nodes.label: Purity
nodes.rationale: Same inputs, same output; no writes to anything that existed before.

nodes.label: Composition over configuration
nodes.rationale: Pass the <Button>, not three props describing one.

nodes.label: Controlled vs uncontrolled
nodes.rationale: Who owns the value, and why undefined decides it forever.

nodes.label: Lifting state up
nodes.rationale: Remove, hardcode, add state — and the re-render that moves with it.

nodes.label: Nesting rule is type identity
nodes.rationale: Reconciliation compares component types by reference. HOCs, lazy() and memo() called in render are the same remount bug.

nodes.label: propTypes removed silently
nodes.rationale: React 19 ignores propTypes with no warning, so an upgrade quietly deletes runtime prop checks.

nodes.label: Skipping a render is a hint
nodes.rationale: shouldComponentUpdate docs say React may re-render anyway — memoization is not a correctness mechanism.

nodes.label: ref as a prop
nodes.rationale: React 19 made ref ordinary and retired forwardRef for function components.

nodes.label: Portals
nodes.rationale: Moves the DOM node, keeps the React tree — including events.

nodes.label: Phase 2 has no sandbox
nodes.rationale: Validated against react.dev Learn/Reference, React 19 upgrade guide, and legacy.reactjs.org.

nodes.label: useState
nodes.rationale: State belongs to a position, and React finds it by counting hook calls.

nodes.label: State is a snapshot
nodes.rationale: Setting state only changes it for the next render.

nodes.label: Object.is comparison
nodes.rationale: React compares state with Object.is. Mutate and the update vanishes with no error.

nodes.label: State belongs to a position
nodes.rationale: Together with snapshot and Object.is, this is why lists, keys and remounts behave as they do.

nodes.label: Updater functions
nodes.rationale: Required, not stylistic, in three cases; also removes state from an effect's dependency array.

nodes.label: Automatic batching
nodes.rationale: Everywhere since React 18. Batching decides how many renders; the snapshot decides the value.

nodes.label: Derived state
nodes.rationale: The sync-with-an-effect antipattern costs a visible frame.

nodes.label: Bail-out is not a promise
nodes.rationale: useState caveat: React may still call your component before skipping children. Safe only because purity is assumed.

nodes.label: Resetting state with key
nodes.rationale: The supported 'this is a different thing now'.

nodes.label: Props changed is not a re-render trigger
nodes.rationale: Two reasons to re-render — and 'props changed' is not one.

nodes.label: Effects synchronize with external systems
nodes.rationale: Not a lifecycle callback. An effect is caused by rendering, and setup/cleanup are a pair React may run any number of times.

nodes.label: The dependency array is not a preference
nodes.rationale: Lying produces an effect that reads one render's values forever. To remove a dep you must prove the linter it is not read.

nodes.label: Cleanup contract
nodes.rationale: setup → cleanup → setup must be indistinguishable from setup alone. Cleanup runs with old values, tied to deps not lifetime.

nodes.label: useEffectEvent
nodes.rationale: Latest props and state without a dependency. Stable in React 19.2, not experimental.

nodes.label: useLayoutEffect
nodes.rationale: After DOM mutation, before paint — and it blocks painting.

nodes.label: Effect timing relative to paint is not guaranteed
nodes.rationale: An interaction-caused effect may run before paint, and React may repaint before processing state set inside an effect.

nodes.label: You might not need an effect
nodes.rationale: Twelve cases; only one survives as an effect.

nodes.label: Phase 4 in progress
nodes.rationale: 12 of 18 topics written; topics 13–18 unwritten.

nodes.label: react package
nodes.rationale: 42 public exports. No render, no createRoot, no document.createElement anywhere in source.

nodes.label: react-dom package
nodes.rationale: 7148 KB vs react 168 KB (42.7×). Events, hydration, streaming, DOM property tables.

nodes.label: Declarative UI
nodes.rationale: Write what the UI is for a given value; never write transitions. Trade-off: give up direct DOM control and pay a diff.

nodes.label: react / react-dom version-match rule
nodes.rationale: They share private internals. A mismatch is undefined behaviour, usually a crash inside the renderer.

nodes.label: Duplicate React hook error
nodes.rationale: Two copies of react: hooks live in module-level internals so copy A calling copy B finds nothing.

nodes.label: React element
nodes.rationale: Frozen plain object: $$typeof, type, key, props. Not a DOM node. Creating one runs nothing.

nodes.label: JSX compiles to jsx()
nodes.rationale: Automatic runtime from react/jsx-runtime. Children become a children prop; key is a third argument.

nodes.label: $$typeof
nodes.rationale: Symbol mark of a genuine element. Cannot survive JSON, so a server cannot send a fake renderable element — XSS mitigation.

nodes.label: key is not a prop
nodes.rationale: React 19 installs a non-enumerable getter that warns and returns undefined. Pass the value again under another name.

nodes.label: <Greeting /> does not call Greeting
nodes.rationale: It holds a reference. React decides whether, when, and how many times to call it.

nodes.label: Render phase
nodes.rationale: React calls component functions to get elements. Repeatable and discardable. DOM still shows previous UI.

nodes.label: Reconcile phase
nodes.rationale: Diffs the new element tree against the current one. Part of render; can be thrown away.

nodes.label: Commit phase
nodes.rationale: Applies DOM operations, then refs, layout effects, passive effects. Cannot be thrown away.

nodes.label: Render must be pure
nodes.rationale: React may call it more than once and throw the result away. Observable work in the body happens an uncontrolled number of times.

nodes.label: Children commit before parents
nodes.rationale: Refs and layout effects run bottom-up so a parent can assume children's DOM exists.

nodes.label: useEffect after paint
nodes.rationale: Default place for fetching, subscriptions, logging, timers.

nodes.label: useLayoutEffect before paint
nodes.rationale: Measure or mutate DOM before the user sees the frame. Blocks painting.

nodes.label: root.render() schedules work
nodes.rationale: DOM is still null on the line immediately after the call.

nodes.label: Reconciliation
nodes.rationale: O(n) because different types mean different trees and key identifies children. Unit is (position, type, key).

nodes.label: Type change unmounts the subtree
nodes.rationale: Changing a parent div to span resets a grandchild. Extra nesting is also a new position.

nodes.label: key among siblings
nodes.rationale: Stable, unique among siblings, derived from data. Index keys shift state onto the wrong items.

nodes.label: Components defined inside components remount
nodes.rationale: New function identity every render => new type => remount every keystroke.

nodes.label: Reset state on purpose with key
nodes.rationale: ProfileEditor key={userId} so drafts do not leak across users.

nodes.label: Fiber
nodes.rationale: Internal record of one tree node. Linked list of child/sibling/parent replaced recursion so rendering is interruptible.

nodes.label: Fiber double buffering
nodes.rationale: current and work-in-progress trees point at each other via alternate. DOM node's __reactFiber$ may be last render.

nodes.label: Hook records on the fiber
nodes.rationale: Function components have no instance. useState lives in a linked list of hook records keyed by call order.

nodes.label: Fiber does not make React faster
nodes.rationale: It makes rendering schedulable. A slow render is still slow.

nodes.label: HostComponent vs FunctionComponent
nodes.rationale: tag 5 type is a string (li); tag 0 type is your function. Host belongs to the renderer.

nodes.label: createRoot
nodes.rationale: The only client entry in React 19. From react-dom/client. Two methods: render and unmount.

nodes.label: hydrateRoot
nodes.rationale: Expects server-rendered HTML and attaches handlers. Argument order is container first, opposite of render.

nodes.label: ReactDOM.render removed
nodes.rationale: Gone in 19, not deprecated: TypeError: ReactDOM.render is not a function. Also hydrate, findDOMNode, unmountComponentAtNode.

nodes.label: One root per container
nodes.rationale: Second createRoot warns; two roots then throw NotFoundError: Node.removeChild on unmount. Cache the root for HMR.

nodes.label: Unmounted root cannot be reused
nodes.rationale: unmount() runs cleanups and empties the container. Further render throws Cannot update an unmounted root.

nodes.label: createRoot error options
nodes.rationale: onUncaughtError, onCaughtError, onRecoverableError — the hook for reporting a whole tree.

nodes.label: StrictMode
nodes.rationale: Development-only detector. Doubles components, lazy initialisers, and initial effect mount. No production cost.

nodes.label: StrictMode double-mount
nodes.rationale: setup → cleanup → setup asserts cleanup fully undoes setup. Measured: 2 renders, 2 setups, 1 cleanup in dev.

nodes.label: didInit ref is the wrong fix
nodes.rationale: Silences the symptom; the effect still cannot re-run. Breaks on Back, Fast Refresh, or Activity.

nodes.label: Development vs production bundle size
nodes.rationale: Measured: 1,125,752 vs 194,799 bytes. Selected by process.env.NODE_ENV dead-code branch.

nodes.label: React release channels
nodes.rationale: latest for apps; canary for frameworks; experimental for React's team; beta/rc are frozen leftover tags.

nodes.label: Canary is for frameworks
nodes.rationale: Server Components land in canary first. Frameworks pin an exact canary build and take responsibility.

nodes.label: Backport patches
nodes.rationale: Same fix lands on 19.2, 19.1 and 19.0 the same day. backport tag points at 19.0.8.

nodes.label: React Foundation
nodes.rationale: Moved under the Linux Foundation on 24 February 2026. RFCs still required. Day-to-day team unchanged.

nodes.label: Pin react and react-dom exactly
nodes.rationale: Caret ranges can resolve them to different patches of shared internals.

nodes.label: beta dist-tag is stale
nodes.rationale: Still points at 19.0.0-beta from 2024. Dist-tags are not retired when a cycle ends.

nodes.label: React 19 additions
nodes.rationale: use, useActionState, useOptimistic, cache, form resource hints, useFormStatus. ref is an ordinary prop.

nodes.label: React 19.2 additions
nodes.rationale: useEffectEvent, Activity, cacheSignal, captureOwnerStack, Partial Pre-rendering, Performance Tracks.

nodes.label: useActionState
nodes.rationale: State + action + pending. Replaces deprecated useFormState from react-dom.

nodes.label: Activity
nodes.rationale: Hide a subtree, keep its state, unmount its effects. Pre-render the next screen without showing it.

nodes.label: ViewTransition is experimental-only
nodes.rationale: Not in 19.2.8 latest despite React Labs posts. Also addTransitionType, startGestureTransition, SuspenseList.

nodes.label: Document metadata hoisting
nodes.rationale: title, meta and link hoist to head from anywhere in the tree.

nodes.label: defaultProps ignored on function components
nodes.rationale: Use default parameters. Silent — not an error.

nodes.label: Vite SPA starter
nodes.rationale: npm create vite --template react-ts. Measured hello-world: 193.27 kB / 60.62 kB gzip, built in 306ms.

nodes.label: Create React App sunset
nodes.rationale: Announced 14 February 2025. Still on npm 5.1.0, not marked deprecated — why tutorials still show it.

nodes.label: Vite vs React Router vs Next.js
nodes.rationale: Choice is about the server, not React. MERN/PERN default is Vite SPA behind an existing Express API.

nodes.label: Vite server.proxy for Express
nodes.rationale: Forward /api to localhost:3000 so development is same-origin and needs no CORS.

nodes.label: SPA fallback
nodes.rationale: Direct visit to /orders/42 404s in production unless the host rewrites to index.html.

nodes.label: React Compiler
nodes.rationale: babel-plugin-react-compiler 1.0.0 since 7 Oct 2025. Per-fiber cache array via react/compiler-runtime. Memoizes JSX itself.

nodes.label: Compiler is not a linter
nodes.rationale: Compiled a component that mutates a prop with no complaint. Validation is eslint-plugin-react-hooks.

nodes.label: Compiler bail-out is silent
nodes.rationale: Conditional hooks leave the function as written. Symptom is a missing speed-up, never a broken build.

nodes.label: What the compiler compiles
nodes.rationale: Components and hooks that actually call hooks. use-prefixed helpers with no hooks are left alone.

nodes.label: React DevTools
nodes.rationale: Components and Profiler panels. Highlight updates, hide StrictMode logs, filter host elements.

nodes.label: Profiler API
nodes.rationale: onRender(id, phase, actualDuration, baseDuration, …). Inert in production unless react-dom/profiling.

nodes.label: actualDuration vs baseDuration
nodes.rationale: actual far below base means memoization is working. Measured: 8 ms vs 21 ms after memo settled.

nodes.label: Confounded memo measurement
nodes.rationale: First render after swapping Cell for MemoCell remounts 400 rows (31 ms). Next update is 8 ms.

nodes.label: Performance Tracks
nodes.rationale: React 19.2 console.timeStamp marks: 837 in development, 0 in production. Lanes, phases, component names.

nodes.label: Host config
nodes.rationale: createInstance, appendChild, commitUpdate, … ~30 functions. react never learns what a node is.

nodes.label: React Native
nodes.rationale: Same React, different renderer. Learn once, write anywhere — not write once, run anywhere.

nodes.label: @react-three/fiber
nodes.rationale: Declarative WebGL — 3D scenes as components. latest=9.7.0 as of 2026-07-31.

nodes.label: ink
nodes.rationale: Terminal renderer. latest=7.1.1.

nodes.label: react-reconciler
nodes.rationale: Build a custom renderer. 0.33.0, no stability guarantee. Almost never appropriate.

nodes.label: react-test-renderer deprecated
nodes.rationale: Still published 19.2.8 but deprecated. Asserted against internals. Use React Testing Library.

nodes.label: Signals vs re-render
nodes.rationale: React's unit of update is the component; signals update bindings. Stale closures, deps and memo are consequences of React's choice.

nodes.label: Preact
nodes.rationale: 13.0 KB min / 5.4 KB gzip vs React 189.8 / 59.2 for the same counter. Near-identical API; no RSC.

nodes.label: When not to choose React
nodes.rationale: Embedded widget (Preact), mostly-static site (Astro), or a team already fluent in Vue/Svelte.

nodes.label: Compiler is React's answer to signals
nodes.rationale: Keep the re-render model; move memoization into a build step.

nodes.label: Four attribute outcomes
nodes.rationale: Renamed, passed through, dropped, or (in 19) class/for accepted with a warning.

nodes.label: className and htmlFor
nodes.rationale: class and for are reserved words. Raw class/for also reach the DOM since React 16, with a dev warning.

nodes.label: onclick is silently dropped
nodes.rationale: Unknown on* is parsed as an event and discarded. Production prints nothing. Highest-cost typo on the page.

nodes.label: Boolean attributes
nodes.rationale: Known booleans: true emits empty attr, false removes it. disabled="false" is truthy. aria-* and data-* stringify.

nodes.label: null/undefined remove attributes
nodes.rationale: Idiomatic conditional omit: href={isExternal ? url : undefined}.

nodes.label: style must be an object
nodes.rationale: A string throws. The one attribute where pasted HTML fails loudly.

nodes.label: Unknown host props
nodes.rationale: String/number: lowercased with a warning. Boolean: dropped. on*: dropped as unknown event.

nodes.label: Capitalization decides host vs component
nodes.rationale: Lowercase → string type (host). Uppercase → identifier. Hyphen → custom element. Member expression is always a component.

nodes.label: Lowercase component is a silent host element
nodes.rationale: function button() in scope + <button/> never calls it. No error in either build.

nodes.label: Element type is invalid … undefined
nodes.rationale: Capitalized identifier is undefined — default vs named import. Production: minified error #130.

nodes.label: Do not call components as functions
nodes.rationale: Header() has no fiber: hooks belong to the caller, no independent state or bail-out.

nodes.label: four conditional forms (&&, ternary, early return, lookup)
innerHTML XSS surface (img onerror, iframe srcdoc)
JSX braces take expressions not statements
null/undefined/true/false render nothing; 0 and NaN render
style prop takes a camelCased object
key compiles to a third argument
index keys keep slots not items
JSX prop spread is object-literal spread
Objects are not valid as a React child (#31)
React onChange is the DOM input event
React 19 class API removals (string refs, legacy context)
five reasons that justify a split
who owns the value (props vs local state)
ES6 default parameters fire only on undefined
A component is a function React calls
nodes.rationale: Who calls the function is the definition that matters: React owns timing, repetition, position and identity.

nodes.label: HOC wraps rather than mutates
nodes.rationale: A function that takes a component and returns a new one that renders the original with extra props.

nodes.label: Never apply a HOC during render
nodes.rationale: A new enhanced type each render remounts the subtree and wipes state. Apply once at module level.

nodes.label: HOC wrappers do not copy statics
nodes.rationale: The wrapper is a different function object; copy statics or use hoist-non-react-statics.

nodes.label: HOC ref forwarding after React 19
nodes.rationale: ref is now an ordinary prop, so spreading props forwards it. Class instance refs and React 18 still need forwardRef.

nodes.label: Why hooks replaced HOCs
nodes.rationale: Silent prop collisions and unreadable wrapper stacks. Hooks name values at the call site.

nodes.label: HOCs wrap around a component
nodes.rationale: A hook cannot wrap from the outside. memo, forwardRef, error boundaries, instrumentation stay HOC-shaped.

nodes.label: HOC displayName convention
nodes.rationale: Without displayName DevTools shows WithUser or Anonymous for every wrap.

nodes.label: createPortal
nodes.rationale: createPortal(children, domNode, key?) is renderable, not a component or hook. The node must already exist.

nodes.label: Portals follow the React tree
nodes.rationale: Only DOM placement changes. Events, context, state, error boundaries and Suspense follow the React parent.

nodes.label: Portals escape CSS containment
nodes.rationale: overflow:hidden, stacking contexts and transformed fixed ancestors trap overlays. document.body sidesteps all three.

nodes.label: dialog showModal top layer
nodes.rationale: Native top layer escapes stacking without moving the node and brings focus trap, Escape and inertness.

nodes.label: Portal accessibility obligation
nodes.rationale: React provides none of focus move, trap, restore, Escape or inert background. Follow WAI-ARIA Modal practices.

nodes.label: Native events follow the DOM
nodes.rationale: Click-outside listeners see portal clicks as coming from body. Compare against the portal node.

nodes.label: createPortal is client-only
nodes.rationale: There is no DOM on the server. Render after mount or use a framework portal.

nodes.label: Props immutable by contract not enforcement
nodes.rationale: React does not freeze props or nested objects. Ask the parent for a new object instead of mutating.

nodes.label: Mutating a prop appears to work
nodes.rationale: The write and the read are microseconds apart. Failure arrives later via remount, siblings, memo, StrictMode or abandoned renders.

nodes.label: One-way data flow
nodes.rationale: Props down, events up. Only the owner can change a value, so debugging walks up to that useState.

nodes.label: Mutating array methods on props
nodes.rationale: sort, reverse, splice, push mutate in place. Use a copy or toSorted, toReversed, toSpliced.

nodes.label: Reassigning a destructured prop is not a mutation
nodes.rationale: A local rebinding is unobservable outside the call. Writes through the object are the violation.

nodes.label: Component, PureComponent, shouldComponentUpdate
nodes.rationale: Always render, shallow compare, or write the comparison. Function equivalents: plain, memo, memo with compare.

nodes.label: Shallow Object.is comparison
nodes.rationale: New objects, arrays or inline functions make every check fail. You pay the comparison and never skip.

nodes.label: PureComponent and mutation are exclusive
nodes.rationale: A mutated same-reference update is silently dropped. Wrong UI, no warning.

nodes.label: Memoization does not stop context updates
Skipping a render is a hint
nodes.rationale: React may re-render anyway. Code that only works because a render was skipped is already broken.

nodes.label: memo compares props only
nodes.rationale: useState already bails out on the same state. PureComponent also compared state.

nodes.label: React assumes purity and never verifies it
nodes.rationale: Same props, state and context produce the same output. Every optimisation is a bet on that.

nodes.label: ref is an ordinary function-component prop
nodes.rationale: Spreads, wrappers and HOCs now carry ref because it is in props.

nodes.label: forwardRef deprecated not removed
nodes.rationale: Still works in 19. Libraries supporting 18 still need it. No announced removal date.

nodes.label: Ref cleanup functions
nodes.rationale: A callback may return a cleanup. Implicit arrow returns now look like cleanups: add braces.

nodes.label: findDOMNode removed in React 19
nodes.rationale: Slow, fragile, first-child only, broke abstraction. Replace with a ref on the real element.

nodes.label: Render prop pattern
nodes.rationale: A function prop the component calls to decide what to render. children works and reads better.

nodes.label: Wrapper hell
nodes.rationale: Each render prop adds a JSX nesting level. Hooks compose as lines instead.

nodes.label: Why hooks replaced render props
nodes.rationale: No extra tree nodes, values usable anywhere in the component, linear composition, better types.

nodes.label: When render props still win
nodes.rationale: The host controls placement, values are per-item, or render must happen inside a boundary. A hook cannot render.

nodes.label: Inline render props defeat memoization
nodes.rationale: A new function each render makes PureComponent or memo always see a change. useCallback only if the child is memoized.

nodes.label: Class components still supported
nodes.rationale: Not recommended for new code, no new features, not scheduled for removal. defaultProps kept; string refs and legacy context gone.

nodes.label: this.setState merges
nodes.rationale: useState replaces. Porting a state object wholesale silently drops unspread fields.

nodes.label: this binding in class handlers
nodes.rationale: Extracted methods lose the receiver; class bodies are strict so this is undefined. Prefer class-field arrows.

nodes.label: One contextType per class
nodes.rationale: A second context needs a render prop or wrapper. useContext has no such limit.

nodes.label: Instance fields become useRef
nodes.rationale: Timer ids, sockets and caches persist without triggering a render. useState would re-render on every assignment.

nodes.label: Three lifecycles collapse into one effect
nodes.rationale: Setup covers mount and update, cleanup covers unmount. Mimicking three methods misses the sync model.

nodes.label: UNSAFE_ lifecycles
nodes.rationale: They run before commit, so an abandoned concurrent render has already executed them. Signal of pre-16.3 code.

nodes.label: Error boundaries require a class
nodes.rationale: No function equivalent for getDerivedStateFromError or componentDidCatch in React 19.

nodes.label: getDerivedStateFromError vs componentDidCatch
nodes.rationale: Static method is render-phase and must be pure. Instance method is commit-phase logging with the component stack.

nodes.label: What error boundaries do not catch
nodes.rationale: Event handlers, async, SSR and the boundary itself. React 19 adds onUncaughtError and onCaughtError.

nodes.label: getDerivedStateFromProps usually should not translate
nodes.rationale: Copying a prop into state is duplicated state. Derive during render instead.

nodes.label: Slots, children and the context hole
children as the free slot
nodes.rationale: A wrapper has a hole the parent fills with arbitrary JSX.

nodes.label: Named element props (slots)
nodes.rationale: Community name, not a React API. Name regions, keep primary content in children, do not slice children by index.

nodes.label: Compound components
nodes.rationale: Free-form children plus context so parts share state and can be arranged freely.

nodes.label: The context hole
nodes.rationale: Create the element where the value lives and pass the finished element down. Intermediates never mention the value.

nodes.label: RSC composition via children
nodes.rationale: A Client Component can receive a Server Component as children but cannot import one. Composition keeps server code out of the bundle.

nodes.label: Composition over configuration
nodes.rationale: A prop that exists only to be rendered should have been the rendered thing. Design decisions stay props.

nodes.label: Twelve-boolean component costs
nodes.rationale: Unbounded API, untested combinations, bundled unused deps, hidden markup.

nodes.label: Elements are ordinary values
nodes.rationale: JSX builds a descriptor; creating an element does not render it.

nodes.label: When configuration is the right answer
nodes.rationale: Keep props for data, owned behaviour, closed variant sets and enforced consistency.

nodes.label: The switch warning, and supporting both
Mode is value === undefined
nodes.rationale: Decided on first render and must not change. Empty string and 0 are controlled; null and missing are not.

nodes.label: value={x ?? ''} fix
nodes.rationale: ?? only replaces null and undefined. || also wipes 0 and empty string.

nodes.label: Supporting controlled and uncontrolled
nodes.rationale: Decide with !== undefined, write internal state only when uncontrolled, always fire the callback.

nodes.label: Never sync a prop into state with an effect
nodes.rationale: Creates a second copy, a race, and a first render with the wrong value.

nodes.label: Controlled is per piece of state
nodes.rationale: Informal terms. A DataTable can mix controlled sort with uncontrolled column width.

nodes.label: Start uncontrolled, control when needed
nodes.rationale: Control for coordination, persistence, validation, programmatic set or external data. Not in case.

nodes.label: Controlled API naming
nodes.rationale: value/onChange, open/onOpenChange, defaultX for initial. Call with the next value, name for what happened.

nodes.label: Reset uncontrolled state with key
nodes.rationale: A changing key remounts a fresh instance. Lighter than controlling solely to reset.

nodes.label: Component identity and the nesting rule
Reconciliation compares type by reference
nodes.rationale: Object.is on the function. Same body evaluated twice is two components. Same type at same position keeps state.

nodes.label: Never nest component definitions
nodes.rationale: A new function each parent render remounts the subtree: state, refs, effects, DOM, focus and scroll.

nodes.label: Four disguises of the nesting bug
nodes.rationale: Local arrows, HOCs in render, inline map values, lazy or memo called during render.

nodes.label: Deliberate remount with key
nodes.rationale: key participates in position. Change it when the record identity changes.

nodes.label: eslint no-unstable-nested-components
nodes.rationale: Not in the recommended set. Enable it; React itself cannot warn.

nodes.label: What makes a function a component
React calls it, not you
nodes.rationale: A helper is a function you call. Ownership lets React attach state, effects, position and identity.

nodes.label: <Widget /> is not Widget()
nodes.rationale: Direct calls inline the result into the caller. Hooks join the caller's list and break if conditional.

nodes.label: Capitalization makes JSX emit a function
nodes.rationale: Lowercase emits a string tag. The function never runs.

nodes.label: One props argument
nodes.rationale: Built fresh each render so props identity is always new. defaultProps removed for functions in React 19.

nodes.label: Hooks matched by call order
nodes.rationale: No name, no key, just position on the fiber. Conditional hooks shift every later slot.

nodes.label: Re-render blast radius moves up
nodes.rationale: A child re-renders because its parent did. Prop comparison is not the default path.

nodes.label: Own state at the closest common parent
nodes.rationale: Every extra level adds a subtree. Push state down when only one branch reads it.

nodes.label: Pass expensive subtrees as children
nodes.rationale: The element object is created outside the stateful wrapper, so React skips that subtree without memo.

nodes.label: Split state or components by update frequency
memo is last, not first
nodes.rationale: Comparison cost, silent failure on fresh objects, no context stop. Structural fixes survive the Compiler.

nodes.label: Lift vs composition vs context vs store
nodes.rationale: Server data is a cache, not lifted UI state. Props first, composition next, context when props become unwieldy.

nodes.label: Remove, hardcode, then add state
nodes.rationale: Hardcoding first separates data-flow bugs from state-update bugs.

nodes.label: Closest common parent owns the state
nodes.rationale: Count components that render based on the value, not pass-throughs. Invent a component solely to own state if needed.

nodes.label: Single source of truth
nodes.rationale: One owner per piece, not all state in one store. The same information in two places is the forbidden case.

nodes.label: Inverse data flow
nodes.rationale: Data down as props, changes up as function calls. The child does not know what the parent does with the event.

nodes.label: Pass handlers not setters
nodes.rationale: A setter leaks the owner's shape. A named event callback survives array-to-Map or local-to-server.

nodes.label: StrictMode, the Compiler and how purity is enforced
Doubling is the test
nodes.rationale: React cannot inspect purity, so it runs the function twice and lets the damage double.

nodes.label: What StrictMode double-invokes
nodes.rationale: Component body, useState init, useMemo, useCallback, reducers, class constructor/render/SCU, setState updaters.

nodes.label: What StrictMode cannot catch
nodes.rationale: Production-only paths, unrun branches, idempotent writes, event handlers, later-update effects. A clean run is not proof.

nodes.label: Compiler is the stricter static checker
nodes.rationale: It analyses and bails out rather than rewriting impure components. Skipped list is a purity report.

nodes.label: useRef guard is the wrong StrictMode fix
nodes.rationale: Hides the symptom. The effect still cannot be remounted safely under navigation or Activity.

nodes.label: Abandoned concurrent renders cannot roll back side effects
The two rules of a pure component
Mind your own business
nodes.rationale: Do not change objects or variables that existed before the call: props, state, context, refs, module variables.

nodes.label: Same inputs, same output
nodes.rationale: Inputs are props, state and context only. Time, Math.random, window and localStorage are untracked.

nodes.label: Module-level mutation during render
nodes.rationale: react.dev Cup example: StrictMode doubling yields 2, 4, 6 instead of 1, 2, 3.

nodes.label: Writing a ref during render
nodes.rationale: A ref exists before the render. Mutability by design does not exempt it.

nodes.label: useSyncExternalStore for external sources
nodes.rationale: Window size, media queries and mutable singletons need a tracked subscription.

nodes.label: Local mutation
nodes.rationale: Objects created during this render are yours. Did this object exist before the render started?

nodes.label: Side effects belong in event handlers
nodes.rationale: Handlers run later, outside the rule. useEffect is the fallback after handlers are exhausted.

nodes.label: Three tiers of impurity cost
nodes.rationale: StrictMode today, next feature or Compiler tomorrow, abandoned concurrent render in production.

nodes.label: The purity rule is smaller than people think
nodes.rationale: React requires not mutating shared data, not unconditional immutability. Handlers and effects can do anything.

nodes.label: Automatic batching
nodes.rationale: React waits until all code in the event has run before processing state updates, preventing half-finished renders. React 18 made batching apply everywhere, not only in React event handlers.

nodes.label: flushSync
nodes.rationale: The only per-callback opt-out of batching. Uncommon last resort: may force Suspense fallbacks, run pending Effects, and flush unrelated pending work.

nodes.label: await is a batch boundary
nodes.rationale: Updates before and after an await live in different tasks, so they batch separately. Automatic batching is not one render per function.

nodes.label: Half-finished renders
nodes.rationale: Without batching, each update can paint a frame where one related value has changed and another has not. Batching is a correctness feature, not only a performance one.

nodes.label: useState bail-out
nodes.rationale: If the new value is Object.is-identical, React skips re-rendering the component and its children. React may still call the component first; the optimisation is safe only because purity is assumed.

nodes.label: Same-value updater idiom
nodes.rationale: Return the existing reference from an updater to signal no change. More reliable than wrapping the setter when the current value is out of scope.

nodes.label: memo vs useState bail-out
nodes.rationale: Bail-out compares new state vs old on every set. memo compares props shallowly when the parent re-renders. Neither substitutes for the other.

nodes.label: Derived state
nodes.rationale: If a value can be calculated from existing props or state, calculate it during rendering. That removes cascading updates and makes out-of-sync state unrepresentable.

nodes.label: useEffect-that-syncs-state antipattern
nodes.rationale: Storing a derivable value and syncing it with an effect costs an extra render and commits a stale frame to the DOM before the effect runs.

nodes.label: Store selectedId, derive the object
nodes.rationale: A stored selected object goes stale on edit and dangles on delete. find by id reflects edits automatically and yields null when the item is gone.

nodes.label: useMemo for expensive derivation
nodes.rationale: Expensive calculations stay derived via useMemo. State plus an effect creates a second source of truth that only usually agrees.

nodes.label: Immutable updates
nodes.rationale: React compares state with Object.is. Mutate and the reference is unchanged, so the update vanishes with no error.

nodes.label: Too many re-renders
nodes.rationale: The throw is a guard on consecutive re-renders, not a diagnosis. Effect loops often never throw because each iteration is a separately scheduled update.

nodes.label: Shape 2: effect sets its own dependency
Shape 3: new object identity in a dependency array
nodes.rationale: Dependencies are compared with Object.is. A fresh object, array, or function literal is a new reference every render, so the effect always re-runs.

nodes.label: Lazy initial state
nodes.rationale: useState(expensive()) evaluates every render and discards the result after the first. Passing a function runs the work once per instance.

nodes.label: Initializer purity (Strict Mode)
nodes.rationale: Strict Mode double-invokes the initializer in development and discards one result. Side effects belong in an effect, which has cleanup.

nodes.label: Lazy ref pattern
nodes.rationale: useRef has no lazy form; a function argument becomes the ref contents. Initialise to null and assign inside if (ref.current === null).

nodes.label: State preserved by position and type
nodes.rationale: Same type at the same render-tree position keeps state. A different type at that position destroys the entire subtree. Position is not DOM position.

nodes.label: Conditional wrapper remount
nodes.rationale: Adding a wrapper in one branch changes depth, so React unmounts the old subtree. Keep one tree shape and vary className instead.

nodes.label: Top-down depth-first render
nodes.rationale: A parent must finish before its children, because React cannot know the children until the parent returns them.

nodes.label: Bottom-up effect order
nodes.rationale: Effects run children-first so a parent measuring a child finds mounted refs. ref.current is null during render because refs attach at commit.

nodes.label: Cannot update a component while rendering a different component
Resetting state with key
nodes.rationale: A key becomes part of position. A changed key unmounts the old subtree and mounts a new one with fresh state, covering children an effect would miss and avoiding a stale frame.

nodes.label: What a key change destroys
nodes.rationale: State, refs, DOM nodes, focus, scroll, CSS animations, uncontrolled inputs, and every effect cleanup. Use when a reset is wanted, not as a general refresh.

nodes.label: Index keys attach state to position
nodes.rationale: Index keys do not remount. React matches key 0 to key 0, so per-row state stays with the slot while data moves underneath.

nodes.label: Lift per-row UI state to the list
nodes.rationale: Keying expandedId by item id removes per-position state that can attach to the wrong row. Uncontrolled inputs still need correct keys.

nodes.label: State is a snapshot
nodes.rationale: Setting state only changes it for the next render. The variable in a given render is a const; handlers close over that invocation.

nodes.label: Stale closure
nodes.rationale: A timeout or interval created in one render reports that render's snapshot, even seconds later. Usually correct for the action as started; a bug only when current value is needed.

nodes.label: Five principles for structuring state
nodes.rationale: Group related state; avoid contradictions; avoid redundant state; avoid duplication; avoid deep nesting. Framed as database normalisation.

nodes.label: Impossible states
nodes.rationale: Two booleans give four combinations, some meaningless. A single status value makes invalid combinations unrepresentable.

nodes.label: Flatten nested state
nodes.rationale: A lookup table keyed by id turns deep spreads into single-level updates. Flatten in response to pain, not pre-emptively.

nodes.label: The update queue
nodes.rationale: Per state variable, React walks queued updates in order. A plain value replaces the running value; an updater transforms it. Each variable has its own queue.

nodes.label: Updater function
nodes.rationale: setX(x => ...) applies a transformation to pending state in the queue, not the render snapshot. Required for multiple updates, later-running callbacks, and concurrent sources.

nodes.label: Three cases where updaters are required
Updating state during render
nodes.rationale: Legal only for the currently rendering component, inside a condition that makes itself false. Restarts before children render and before commit, so the stale value never paints.

nodes.label: useState
nodes.rationale: Returns a per-render snapshot and a setter. State lives outside the component, keyed by position, matched by hook call order.

nodes.label: Hook call order / state slots
nodes.rationale: There is no name. React matches slots by call order. A hook inside a condition shifts later slots when the condition flips.

nodes.label: Initial value is only initial
nodes.rationale: useState's argument is read once at that position. A later prop change does not update it. Derive, remount with key, or accept a deliberate draft.

nodes.label: Two render triggers
nodes.rationale: Initial render, or a state update in the component or an ancestor. A prop change is a symptom of the parent rendering, not a trigger.

nodes.label: Four things that stop render descent
nodes.rationale: useState bail-out, memo, unchanged element identity (children trick), and the React Compiler.

nodes.label: Mutating vs copying array methods
nodes.rationale: push/unshift, pop/shift/splice, index assignment, sort and reverse mutate. Prefer spread, filter, slice, map, or copy-then-mutate.

nodes.label: structuredClone vs Immer
nodes.rationale: A deep clone destroys structural sharing, throws on functions/DOM nodes, and costs the whole tree. Immer copies only touched paths.

nodes.label: Treat objects in state as read-only
nodes.rationale: Mutation does not merely skip a render — it retroactively corrupts every previous snapshot that captured the same object.

nodes.label: Two mutation failures
nodes.rationale: Mutate without a setter: React is never asked. Mutate then set the same reference: Object.is bails out. The second looks correct.

nodes.label: Spread is shallow
nodes.rationale: {...person} copies the artwork reference. Mutating next.artwork.city still mutates the original. Copy every level on the path; share the rest.

nodes.label: Local mutation exception
nodes.rationale: Mutating a freshly created object nothing else holds is fine. Only the object handed to the setter must be new.

nodes.label: Cleanup contract
nodes.rationale: React runs setup and cleanup as many times as needed. The only correct effect is one where setup → cleanup → setup is indistinguishable from setup alone.

nodes.label: An effect has its own lifecycle
Effect start/stop lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Components mount, update, unmount. Effects only start and stop synchronizing. One mount can contain many start/stop cycles.

nodes.label: One effect per synchronization process
nodes.rationale: One effect has one dependency array. Merging processes unions their deps, so each restarts for the other's reasons.

nodes.label: Reactive values
nodes.rationale: Props, state, and values declared inside the component are reactive. ref.current and location.pathname are not, because they live outside render data flow.

nodes.label: StrictMode door-lock extra cycle
nodes.rationale: React starts and stops the effect one extra time in development to verify cleanup is the inverse of setup, not to simulate a rare user journey.

nodes.label: Fetching data in an effect
nodes.rationale: A legitimate effect that react.dev still recommends replacing. Four downsides: no server fetch, waterfalls, no cache, and race-condition boilerplate.

nodes.label: ignore-flag race guard
nodes.rationale: Network responses may arrive out of order. Cleanup flips ignore so a stale response cannot set state. Pair with clearing state before the new fetch.

nodes.label: Network waterfall
nodes.rationale: A child cannot render — and so cannot fetch — until its parent has. Nested mount-time fetches serialise even when independent.

nodes.label: useData custom hook
nodes.rationale: Extracting the race guard is valuable. It does not add cache, deduplication, or pre-mount fetch. Framework loaders or TanStack Query / useSWR do.

nodes.label: Queueing a Series of State Updates (react.dev)
You Might Not Need an Effect (react.dev)
ignore flag
nodes.rationale: let ignore = false inside setup so each run has its own flag; cleanup sets it true. Fixes the render, does not cancel the request.

nodes.label: AbortController in an effect
nodes.rationale: Cleanup calls abort(); catch must ignore AbortError or cancel becomes a visible error.

nodes.label: AbortError
nodes.rationale: Aborted fetch rejects with a DOMException named AbortError; treating it as failure flashes an error on every keystroke.

nodes.label: Start with ignore, abort when the request is the cost
nodes.rationale: ignore is what react.dev documents and works with any promise. AbortController when payloads, search-as-you-type, or mobile bandwidth make the request itself costly.

nodes.label: Neither race guard is a cache
nodes.rationale: Both stop the wrong data rendering. Neither deduplicates, caches, or starts the request earlier.

nodes.label: Eight legitimate dependency-removal moves
nodes.rationale: Move outside, move inside, depend on primitives, call during render, updater form, useEffectEvent, event handler, split effects.

nodes.label: Edit the code, not the array
nodes.rationale: You cannot choose dependencies. To remove one, prove to the linter it is not read.

nodes.label: Extra setup+cleanup cycle
nodes.rationale: Development-only cycle before the first real setup: setup → cleanup → setup. Asserts mount-path symmetry.

nodes.label: StrictMode only doubles the mount
nodes.rationale: The extra cycle is attached to mounting, not every re-run. Dependency-change leaks pass a green StrictMode.

nodes.label: Double render vs extra effect cycle
nodes.rationale: Double render finds impurity; extra effect cycle finds missing cleanup. Event handlers are in neither.

nodes.label: Partial StrictMode skips the extra effect cycle
nodes.rationale: Child-only double mount cannot happen in production, so React declines to simulate it. The check requires StrictMode at the root.

nodes.label: Callback refs get the same extra cycle
nodes.rationale: Missing ref cleanup doubles registry counts. React 19 ref cleanup functions make symmetry expressible.

nodes.label: The dependency array is not a preference
Reactive values
nodes.rationale: Props and all variables and functions declared directly inside the component. Setters, dispatch, and ref objects are stable and not dependencies.

nodes.label: You cannot choose Effect dependencies
nodes.rationale: Every reactive value the setup reads must be declared. The list is determined by the surrounding code.

nodes.label: Omitted deps freeze the first render
nodes.rationale: An empty array means only the first setup ever runs, so the effect keeps that render's roomId forever. No error, quietly wrong.

nodes.label: react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
nodes.rationale: Computes the correct array from the code. Disabling converts a compile-time complaint into a runtime bug months later.

nodes.label: Three dependency-array forms
nodes.rationale: No array: after every commit. Empty: after initial commit only. Populated: initial plus Object.is change, positionally.

nodes.label: cleanup(old) then setup(new)
nodes.rationale: Cleanup closes over the render that created it, so it disconnects the old room, not the new one.

nodes.label: Async setup is not allowed
nodes.rationale: An async function returns a Promise, not a cleanup. Declare an inner async function and return a real cleanup.

nodes.label: One effect per concern
nodes.rationale: Merging concerns unions their dependency lists, so each concern tears down for the other's reasons.

nodes.label: Effect Events
nodes.rationale: Non-reactive pieces of Effect code. Always see latest props and state; calling them does not re-run the surrounding Effect.

nodes.label: Unstable Effect Event identity is a runtime assertion
nodes.rationale: Identity changes every render on purpose. Putting one in a dependency array re-runs the effect every render and makes the bug obvious.

nodes.label: Do not use useEffectEvent to avoid dependencies
nodes.rationale: Wrapping the whole effect body to reach [] hides real staleness. Only genuinely event-like logic belongs in an Effect Event.

nodes.label: useLayoutEffect blocks paint
nodes.rationale: The guarantee is the blocking: React refuses to let the browser paint until the code and its state updates finish. Prefer useEffect.

nodes.label: Measure then place
nodes.rationale: Tooltip renders anywhere, measures height, re-renders in the right place. Two renders either way; layout effect only hides the first.

nodes.label: useLayoutEffect does nothing on the server
nodes.rationale: No layout information and no paint on the server. Options: useEffect, client-only, isMounted, or useSyncExternalStore.

nodes.label: Layout-effect setState runs remaining Effects immediately
nodes.rationale: A state update inside useLayoutEffect executes all remaining Effects including useEffect, dragging unrelated work onto the paint-blocking path.

nodes.label: Synchronize with an external system
nodes.rationale: If you are not synchronizing with a browser API, widget, network, or non-React component, you probably do not need an Effect.

nodes.label: Effects versus events
nodes.rationale: Effects are caused by rendering; events by a particular interaction. Ask why it happens. If the answer names a user action, it is not an effect.

nodes.label: componentDidMount is the wrong model
nodes.rationale: useEffect(fn, []) stays connected to the first room forever. Synchronization with real deps and cleanup handles mount, update, and unmount.

nodes.label: Effects only run on the client
nodes.rationale: They cannot produce server HTML. They are the legal place for window, document, localStorage after mount.

nodes.label: Passive-effect paint timing is unguaranteed
nodes.rationale: Interaction-caused Effects may run before paint; React may also paint before processing state updates inside them. For a guarantee use useLayoutEffect or setTimeout.
