nodes.label: You might not need an effect
Do not use Effects to transform data or handle events
nodes.rationale: Transform at the top of the component. By the time an Effect runs you do not know what the user did.

nodes.label: Twelve You-Might-Not-Need-an-Effect cases
nodes.rationale: Only fetching data (case 12) survives as an effect, and even there a framework or cache library is preferred.

nodes.label: Idempotent widget setup
nodes.rationale: setZoomLevel twice is a no-op. showModal twice throws and needs close() in cleanup. The test is the API, not the widget.

nodes.label: Declare the listener inside setup
nodes.rationale: removeEventListener matches on identity. A handler recreated between setup and cleanup removes nothing and listeners accumulate.

nodes.label: Animation cleanup resets, it does not reverse
nodes.rationale: Undo means restore the initial value or reset the tween timeline, not play the animation backwards.

nodes.label: Analytics Effects need no cleanup
nodes.rationale: The double logVisit is development-only and must not skew production metrics. A POST that mutates application state has neither property.

nodes.label: setup → cleanup → setup must be indistinguishable
nodes.rationale: The user should not be able to tell production's single setup from development's extra cycle. Incomplete cleanup fails that invariant.

nodes.label: Cleanup is not unmount code
nodes.rationale: Cleanup runs on dependency change, unmount, and the StrictMode extra cycle. It is tied to the effect's dependencies, not the component's lifetime.

nodes.label: When cleanup is not the answer
Buying a product is not an Effect
nodes.rationale: No cleanup fixes a purchase that fires because the page rendered. You want to buy when the user clicks Buy. Same POST verb as analytics, opposite answer.

nodes.label: Remount principle
nodes.rationale: Visiting a page should not differ from visiting it, clicking a link, then pressing Back. StrictMode remounts once in development to verify that.

nodes.label: Objects and functions differ if created at different times
nodes.rationale: Object.is fails every render for a literal created in the component body. Contents did not change; identity did.

nodes.label: Four object-and-function moves
nodes.rationale: Move static values outside the component; construct dynamic ones inside the effect; depend on primitives; call a function prop during render.

nodes.label: Updater form removes a state dependency
nodes.rationale: setMessages(msgs => [...msgs, received]) does not read messages, so the chat does not reconnect on every message.

nodes.label: Split into several Effects
nodes.rationale: Different parts that re-run for different reasons belong in different Effects.

nodes.label: Suppressed interval always shows 1
nodes.rationale: eslint-disable with [] keeps the first render's onTick, which always calls setCount(0 + 1). The counter is frozen at first-render arithmetic.

nodes.label: Refs used to hide a dependency
nodes.rationale: Reading ref.current is not tracked, so a ref can smuggle a reactive value past the linter and produce the same stale-forever bug.

nodes.label: An effect chain cannot be replayed
nodes.rationale: It is attached to state changing, not to the user acting. Undo, history, and time-travel re-fire the whole cascade.

nodes.label: Compute all next state in the event handler
nodes.rationale: A chain of effects is often stored derived values. Compute during render; put the rest in the one handler that knows a card was played.

nodes.label: Logic that belongs to an event
Share handler logic with a plain function
nodes.rationale: Hoisting shared follow-up into an Effect fires it on mount and every product change. An ordinary function in the component body is enough.

nodes.label: Same POST, opposite homes
nodes.rationale: visit_form analytics stays in an Effect because the form was displayed. Registration POST belongs in handleSubmit because the user pressed the button.

nodes.label: State-as-a-trigger antipattern
nodes.rationale: setJsonToSubmit in the handler plus an Effect that posts when it is non-null reconstructs intent after the fact. Both the state and the Effect should disappear.

nodes.label: Notify the parent in the same event
nodes.rationale: An Effect calling onChange(isOn) runs too late and costs two renders. Calling setIsOn and onChange in the same handler batches into one.

nodes.label: Lift state up instead of copying it
nodes.rationale: If two components need the same value, the question is which one should own it, not how to copy it with an Effect.

nodes.label: Four state buckets
nodes.rationale: Server state, URL state, form state, and UI state. Most global state is a cache of somebody else's data.

nodes.label: Phase 12 — Data and state in a real app
Phase 13 — Routing, structure and the app shell
Part 3 — Concurrent React and the server
Concurrent, Suspense, Actions, and RSC are one idea
nodes.rationale: Concurrent rendering makes a render interruptible. Suspense turns unreadiness into a state. Actions build on transitions. Server Components exist because Suspense can stream.

nodes.label: Phase 8 — Concurrent rendering, Suspense and transitions
Phase 9 — Forms, Actions and optimistic UI
Phase 10 — Server Components and Server Functions
Phase 11 — Server rendering, hydration and the DOM APIs
Phase 4 — Effects and synchronization
nodes.rationale: The most misused hook, almost always because it is understood as run-after-render instead of synchronize-with-something-outside-React.

nodes.label: Phase 6 — Rendering performance and the React Compiler
Phase 7 — Custom hooks and the Rules of React
Phase 1 — JSX and what a component returns
Phase 3 — State and the render cycle
react.dev You Might Not Need an Effect
TypeScript explanations hub
nodes.rationale: One page per syllabus topic; console blocks from sandbox/ts-p0 and siblings. Verified 2026-08 on TypeScript 7.0.2 and Node 24.19.0.

nodes.label: TypeScript 13-phase syllabus
nodes.rationale: Phases 0–1 written (30 topics). Next is Phase 2 narrowing. Parts: type system, types at scale, in the stack, rigour and tooling.

nodes.label: Phase 0 · How TypeScript runs
nodes.rationale: 13 pages on what the tool is, what it leaves behind, and which of the three programs that accept .ts actually reads types.

nodes.label: Erasure is the load-bearing fact
nodes.rationale: Once 'types are deleted and never checked at runtime' is internalised, enum's reputation, erasableSyntaxOnly, runtime validation, and why a green bundler proves nothing stop being separate facts.

nodes.label: sandbox/ts-p0 measurement suite
nodes.rationale: ex1-erasure.sh … ex9-node-runs-ts.sh. typescript 7.0.2 and typescript5 5.9.3 side by side.

nodes.label: Phase 0 measurement corrections
nodes.rationale: strict defaults true in TS7; TS7 speed-up is 3× not 10×; compiler API moved to unstable/; tsc emits broken JS and exits 2.

nodes.label: Phase 1 · The type vocabulary
nodes.rationale: 17 pages. Inferred types read from emitted .d.ts, not editor tooltips. sandbox/ts-p1/.

nodes.label: sandbox/ts-p1 measurement suite
nodes.rationale: ex1-inference-widening.sh … ex7-object-types.sh. Emit declarations and read inferred types from .d.ts.

nodes.label: Phase 1 measurement corrections
nodes.rationale: Weak-type detection stops when a required property is added; interface vs type error folklore failed; TS2589 only at depth 5000; reduce infers from elements; plain symbol accepted as computed key.

nodes.label: Phase 1 phase gate
nodes.rationale: Model an API payload — optional fields, a status union, a nested object, a list — without any, and say why each choice is not a neighbour.

nodes.label: TypeScript is a checker, not a runtime
nodes.rationale: TypeScript reads code and complains. It is not a language the computer runs. By execution time every annotation is gone, like a comment.

nodes.label: tsc emit-on-error default
nodes.rationale: Default tsc reports errors and still emits JS, exiting 2. --noEmitOnError and --noEmit exit 1 and write nothing. Ignoring exit 2 ships rejected output.

nodes.label: Types are promises, not runtime checks
nodes.rationale: No runtime type representation or check. An API, JSON.parse, or as can lie. That gap is Phase 9 — types at the boundary.

nodes.label: tsc --noEmit as CI gate
nodes.rationale: Bundlers and Node strip without checking. A required tsc --noEmit with a respected exit code is the only automatic check.

nodes.label: Type erasure
nodes.rationale: Most TS syntax is deleted on the way to JS. 15 lines in, 7 out: interface, type, generics, annotations, satisfies, as vanish. Runtime logic is untouched.

nodes.label: Erasable vs non-erasable syntax
nodes.rationale: Erasable syntax describes values that already exist. Non-erasable syntax creates runtime values: enum, runtime namespace, parameter properties, legacy import=, experimental decorators.

nodes.label: Numeric enum IIFE
nodes.rationale: enum becomes an IIFE building a two-way map (Status.Pending=0, Status[0]='Pending'). Real object, resists tree-shaking.

nodes.label: Parameter properties emit assignments
nodes.rationale: constructor(private readonly id: string) becomes field declarations plus this.id = id. private and readonly themselves are erased.

nodes.label: private is compile-time only
nodes.rationale: private is erased; JS can read o.id. #private is the runtime-enforced form.

nodes.label: as const object plus derived union
nodes.rationale: const Status = {Pending:'pending'} as const; type Status = (typeof Status)[keyof typeof Status]. Erasable, readable logs, same call sites.

nodes.label: export {} module marker
nodes.rationale: Compiler adds export {} so a file with no imports/exports stays a module instead of a script sharing global scope.

nodes.label: Three ways to run TypeScript
nodes.rationale: tsc checks then emits; esbuild/swc/Vite/Babel strip and emit without checking; Node 24 strips and executes. Only tsc reads types.

nodes.label: Transpiler is fast because it is blind
nodes.rationale: esbuild deleted a Cart annotation, assigned a string to total, exited 0; runtime TypeError. Speed is skipping the type graph, not doing it better.

nodes.label: Node 24 type stripping
nodes.rationale: node file.ts strips annotations and runs JS with no flag, no tsconfig, no check. Same lying.ts prints HEAVY and exits 0.

nodes.label: Pair a fast runner with tsc --noEmit
nodes.rationale: Whatever runs the code, tsc --noEmit runs beside it. The build step became optional; the check never did.

nodes.label: Published libraries always need tsc
nodes.rationale: Node refuses to strip types inside node_modules (ERR_UNSUPPORTED_NODE_MODULES_TYPE_STRIPPING). Libraries ship .js plus .d.ts from tsc.

nodes.label: Strip-only mode
nodes.rationale: Node runs TS by deleting types, never transforming. Syntax that needs a transform is rejected at parse as SyntaxError, not a catchable exception.

nodes.label: ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX
nodes.rationale: Load-time SyntaxError for enum, namespace, and parameter properties in strip-only mode. The module never evaluates.

nodes.label: erasableSyntaxOnly
nodes.rationale: Makes tsc reject non-erasable syntax with TS1294 at check time. Defaults false in 7.0.2. Enable whenever anything runs .ts directly.

nodes.label: Whitespace type stripping
nodes.rationale: Annotations are replaced with whitespace so every character position is preserved and stack traces match without a source map. That forbids generating an IIFE or inserting this.id = id.

nodes.label: --experimental-transform-types
nodes.rationale: Escape hatch that transforms enums. Experimental, warns every start, reintroduces source maps. Rewriting syntax is cheaper.

nodes.label: const enum is not erasable
nodes.rationale: const enum disappears by inlining values — a transform — so it errors under erasableSyntaxOnly and isolatedModules. Do not use preserveConstEnums.

nodes.label: strict flag
nodes.rationale: A switch over seven checks that decides what the language means. Without strictNullChecks, string includes null.

nodes.label: strict defaults to true in TypeScript 7
nodes.rationale: tsc --help --all reports default: true on 7.0.2 and false on 5.9.3. Unflagged loose.ts reports TS7006, TS18047, TS2564, TS18046.

nodes.label: Seven flags under strict
nodes.rationale: noImplicitAny, strictNullChecks, strictPropertyInitialization, useUnknownInCatchVariables, strictFunctionTypes, strictBindCallApply, alwaysStrict.

nodes.label: strictNullChecks
nodes.rationale: Load-bearing flag. Without it null is assignable to every type so | null is decoration. With it, user.name after a nullable find is TS18047 until narrowed.

nodes.label: TS5052 strictPropertyInitialization requires strictNullChecks
nodes.rationale: Never-assigned and assigned-undefined are the same without null tracking, so the flag cannot stand alone.

nodes.label: noUncheckedIndexedAccess is not in strict
nodes.rationale: Separate opt-in; tsc --init enables it anyway. Makes arr[0] and record[key] return T | undefined.

nodes.label: tsconfig.json two jobs
nodes.rationale: Defines which files are the project (include/exclude/files/references) and what rules they are checked under (compilerOptions).

nodes.label: "types": [] ambient inclusion off
nodes.rationale: Default auto-includes every @types/* found walking up node_modules. [] means none unless imported. Measured: 5.9.3 pulled @types/mdx from three directories up.

nodes.label: exclude only removes roots
nodes.rationale: An excluded file imported by an included file is still checked. exclude is not a veto.

nodes.label: isolatedModules
nodes.rationale: Guarantee every file can be transpiled alone. Rejects type re-exports without export type, const enum, ambient-only scripts.

nodes.label: verbatimModuleSyntax
nodes.rationale: Emit imports exactly as written. Forces import type for type-only imports; removes compiler guesswork a single-file transpiler cannot perform.

nodes.label: tsc --init TypeScript 7 scaffold
nodes.rationale: nodenext, esnext, types:[], strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, exactOptionalPropertyTypes, verbatimModuleSyntax, isolatedModules, skipLibCheck. No include/outDir/rootDir.

nodes.label: TypeScript 7 native compiler
nodes.rationale: Compiler rewritten as a native binary in platform optional deps (@typescript/typescript-linux-x64 etc). tsc is a thin Node wrapper. Language unchanged.

nodes.label: TypeScript 7 measured 3× speedup
nodes.rationale: 300 files, 1500 lines, --noEmit --strict: 7.0.2 0.76s vs 5.9.3 2.32s. First run claimed 10× because 5.9.3 also loaded ancestor @types.

nodes.label: Compiler API moved to typescript/unstable
nodes.rationale: require('typescript') exports only version and versionMajorMinor. createProgram is undefined. Live surface: typescript/unstable/sync, /async, /ast (409 exports).

nodes.label: Ambient @types follows cwd not sources
nodes.rationale: 5.9.3 resolves @types relative to cwd. Moving fixture to /tmp did not help while cwd stayed in the repo. Assert equal diagnostic counts before comparing timings.

nodes.label: TypeScript 6.0 deprecation bridge
nodes.rationale: JavaScript-implemented 6.0 carries deprecations so a large project can fix issues on the familiar compiler before the native 7 jump. Tooling is the risky part.

nodes.label: TypeScript 7 changed option defaults
nodes.rationale: strict, esModuleInterop true; moduleResolution bundler or node16/nodenext following module. Unset projects behave differently on 7.

nodes.label: Four sources of types
nodes.rationale: Inference, bundled .d.ts (types/exports), DefinitelyTyped @types/*, or a local ambient .d.ts. Plus lib for the ambient environment.

nodes.label: TS7016 missing declaration file
nodes.rationale: Module resolved; JS found; no description so the import would be any. noImplicitAny turns that silence into TS7016.

nodes.label: A declaration is a promise, not a check
nodes.rationale: Nothing verifies shout really takes a string. The compiler enforces your assertion. Get it wrong and it confidently enforces the wrong thing.

nodes.label: Annotate boundaries, infer the interior
nodes.rationale: Annotate parameters and exported returns. Interior annotations add noise and can lose information (Record<string,number> drops known keys).

nodes.label: Language server is not the build
nodes.rationale: Editor is a long-lived server on open files, often the bundled compiler, including unsaved buffers. CI is tsc --noEmit, cold, the include set, the repo version.

nodes.label: Editor vs CI compiler version drift
nodes.rationale: Same loose.ts: 7.0.2 four errors, 5.9.3 exit 0, because the strict default changed. Fix: Use Workspace Version and typescript.tsdk.

nodes.label: Editor vs CI file-set disagreement
nodes.rationale: A file nobody imports and include misses is checked when opened and never in CI. Ambient @types also depend on cwd.

nodes.label: Stale TS Server state
nodes.rationale: Incremental cache can go stale after checkout, install, or tsconfig edit. Restart TS Server; delete .tsbuildinfo if it persists.

nodes.label: Checking is not transpiling
nodes.rationale: A transpiler reads one file; a checker reads the whole program. That structural difference is why esbuild is fast, cannot type-check, and why isolatedModules exists.

nodes.label: tsc --emitDeclarationOnly
nodes.rationale: Transpilers cannot emit .d.ts because declarations need the type graph they skip. Publishing always involves tsc even when JS is bundled elsewhere.

nodes.label: Separate typecheck and build scripts
nodes.rationale: dev: vite; build: vite build; typecheck: tsc --noEmit; ci: typecheck && test && build. Nothing depends on the build catching type errors.

nodes.label: Set rootDir explicitly
nodes.rationale: Unset, rootDir is the common ancestor of every input. A scripts/seed.ts silently moves output from dist/server.js to dist/src/server.js.

nodes.label: exclude dist from the program
nodes.rationale: Otherwise a previous build's .d.ts and .js become inputs and produce duplicate-identifier errors.

nodes.label: Second tsconfig when rules differ
nodes.rationale: Need two configs when lib/types/module differ (app vs vite.config), not merely when folders differ. Keep rootDir/outDir/include out of the shared base.

nodes.label: package.json and tsconfig module agreement
nodes.rationale: "type": "module" with module: nodenext. main/types/exports must point at what outDir produces.

nodes.label: TypeScript minors can break builds
nodes.rationale: Minors add checks. A caret range lets a colleague's npm install produce errors yours does not. Pin the exact compiler and upgrade in its own PR.

nodes.label: lib.d.ts updates break untouched files
nodes.rationale: TS ships updated DOM and ES declarations. A lib change produces errors in code you did not write. Read breaking changes and lib.d.ts updates.

nodes.label: 5 → 6 → 7 upgrade path
nodes.rationale: 5.9.3 last JS 5.x; 6.0 deprecation bridge; 7.0.2 native. Application code often jumps 5→7; tooling that imports typescript is the risk.

nodes.label: // @ts-check
nodes.rationale: First comment in a .js file turns the checker on. With allowJs, tsc --noEmit --checkJs reports TS2345 in a file Node still runs unchanged.

nodes.label: checkJs project-wide
nodes.rationale: "checkJs": true checks every .js. // @ts-nocheck opts a stubborn file out. Per-file @ts-check is the adoption path.

nodes.label: JSDoc type annotations
nodes.rationale: @param, @returns, @type, @typedef, @template, import('./x.js').T. Conditional/mapped types get unreadable — convert that file to .ts.

nodes.label: TypeScript Playground
nodes.rationale: Isolation: reproduce without your tsconfig/@types/editor version, toggle one option, switch compiler versions, inspect emitted JS, share a runnable link.

nodes.label: any turns checking off
nodes.rationale: Assignable to everything and from everything. Property access, call, and index all allowed and produce any. Spreads through inference with no error. Measured: two any lines produced zero diagnostics.

nodes.label: unknown requires narrowing
nodes.rationale: Everything assignable to unknown; unknown assignable to nothing except unknown and any. TS18046 / TS2322 until you prove what it is.

nodes.label: never empty type
nodes.rationale: No value has it. Return type of functions that throw or loop; assignable to everything vacuously; result of narrowing everything away (exhaustiveness).

nodes.label: void means ignore the return
nodes.rationale: Not undefined and not never. A void function returns undefined at runtime; void says the value is not part of the contract.

nodes.label: unknown at the door, never any
nodes.rationale: Correct type for every input you did not create. fetch JSON as unknown then schema.parse. JSON.parse returns any — assign to unknown and validate.

nodes.label: Functions returning values assign to void
nodes.rationale: A function returning something is assignable to () => void. Lets forEach(x => list.push(x)) compile. Trap: useEffect(() => fetchData()) returns a Promise as cleanup.

nodes.label: Array types T[] / Array<T>
nodes.rationale: Same type. Inference unions elements and forgets length. mixed[99] type-checks as the element union.

nodes.label: Tuple types
nodes.rationale: Fixed length, positional meaning, optional and rest elements, named labels (docs only). Arity is checked.

nodes.label: as const for heterogeneous returns
nodes.rationale: return [value, inc] without as const infers (number | (() => void))[]. as const makes readonly [number, () => void]. Most common custom-hook type bug.

nodes.label: readonly T[]
nodes.rationale: Removes mutating methods from the type; does not freeze at runtime. T[] → readonly T[] is fine; reverse is not. Parameters you do not mutate should be readonly T[].

nodes.label: Call signature
nodes.rationale: Object/interface form can carry properties (Express middleware). Arrow form is callable only. Multiple call signatures are overloads; first match wins.

nodes.label: Construct signature
nodes.rationale: new (id: string) => Widget types the constructor, not an instance. Generic factory: Ctor: new (id: string) => T.

nodes.label: typeof MyClass is the static side
nodes.rationale: Every class creates two types: C is the instance; typeof C is constructor plus statics. 'Property create does not exist on Repo' is this confusion.

nodes.label: abstract new construct signature
nodes.rationale: abstract new (...args: any[]) => T accepts abstract classes; a plain new signature rejects them. Needed for mixins and registries over bases.

nodes.label: Hybrid call/construct type
nodes.rationale: Call signature plus construct signature plus properties. Rare in new code; common in .d.ts for older JS (jQuery $).

nodes.label: enum vs union vs const object
nodes.rationale: Three ways to model a fixed set. Union and const-object erase; enum emits an IIFE. Default: string-literal union.

nodes.label: String-literal union
nodes.rationale: type Status = 'pending' | 'shipped'. Zero runtime, readable serialisation, no import. Cannot iterate members at runtime.

nodes.label: const object plus derived union
nodes.rationale: Runtime iteration and named constants. Same name for const and type is legal — value and type namespaces are separate.

nodes.label: Enums are nominal
nodes.rationale: Two enums with identical members are not interchangeable. Unusual in TS; string-literal unions are structural.

nodes.label: const enum is the worst option
nodes.rationale: Inlines values at call sites — a whole-program transform. Banned by isolatedModules; breaks esbuild/swc/Vite.

nodes.label: Function types
nodes.rationale: A contract with a caller. Parameters must be annotated unless contextual; return types inferred but worth writing on exports.

nodes.label: Fewer parameters is assignable
nodes.rationale: Ignoring an argument is safe; demanding one the caller never sends is not. Makes map(x => …) legal. Reverse: Target signature provides too few arguments.

nodes.label: Contextual typing of callbacks
nodes.rationale: When the target type is known, parameter types are inferred. Remove the annotation and they revert to implicit any (TS7006).

nodes.label: Overload implementation is not callable
nodes.rationale: Only declared overloads are visible. Invalid calls report against the overload list. First matching overload wins; specific first. Prefer union/generic when return type does not depend on args.

nodes.label: Default vs optional parameters
nodes.rationale: x?: string is string | undefined in the body. x = 'a' is optional for callers and string in the body. Default makes the emitted signature optional.

nodes.label: Intersection types A & B
nodes.rationale: Both at once. Every member of every operand is required. Mixin pattern for composing named fragments.

nodes.label: Union widens values, intersection widens members
nodes.rationale: | widens the set of values and narrows usable members; & does the reverse. Or feels permissive for values but makes the type less useful until narrowed.

nodes.label: Conflicting intersection members become never
nodes.rationale: type TB = {x:string} & {x:number} is silent. TB['x'] is never. Failure appears at assignment: Type 'string' is not assignable to type 'never'.

nodes.label: interface extends vs intersection
nodes.rationale: extends reports TS2430 at the declaration. & produces an unsatisfiable type silently. Prefer extends for layered domain shapes.

nodes.label: Intersections distribute over unions
nodes.rationale: (A | B) & C becomes (A & C) | (B & C). Adds a shared field to every branch of a discriminated union without breaking the discriminant.

nodes.label: Branded type via intersection
nodes.rationale: string & { readonly __brand: 'UserId' } — a string no ordinary string has. Created at a validated boundary; exists only in the type system.

nodes.label: as const is not as T
Produce undefined, accept null at the boundary
type by default, interface when merging
instanceof fails across realms and duplicate packages
Compiler does not check guard body
Phase 6 Modules, declarations and the build
300-line file-size cap
nodes.rationale: Caps how much lives in one file, never how much a topic gets explained. Write first, then split on a concept boundary at 301 lines.

nodes.label: Priority tiers
nodes.rationale: Tiers allocate effort, not importance: Master, Understand, Know, When Needed — assigned for fullstack application development.

nodes.label: Verified line policy
nodes.rationale: Every number, timing and error string comes from a run that happened. No run means no console block.

nodes.label: Link form .md with numeric prefixes
nodes.rationale: Directory-slug links broke 188 links; every link ends in .md and keeps every numeric prefix.

nodes.label: Critical-path CSS syllabus
nodes.rationale: Cut twice on instruction: 230→119 advanced-only, then 119→74 critical-only. Architecture, tokens, CSS Modules and Tailwind dropped; SCSS kept as usage.

nodes.label: CSS owns what the browser paints
nodes.rationale: If deleting the stylesheet would delete the topic, it is CSS's. classList and requestAnimationFrame stay in JavaScript.

nodes.label: Single-engine limitation
nodes.rationale: Only Firefox 153.0.3 is installed. Measured behaviour is labelled with the engine; availability comes from web-features.

nodes.label: CSS example policy
nodes.rationale: Claims checked against a real render: getComputedStyle, getBoundingClientRect, CSS.supports, and Baseline keys.

nodes.label: Measured vs Baseline sources
nodes.rationale: What it does is measured in Firefox 153; whether it is safe to ship comes from web-features.

nodes.label: Phase 0 gate parsed matched won
nodes.rationale: Move on when a rule that is not working can be diagnosed as parsed, matched, or won — without editing at random.

nodes.label: CSS is resolved not executed
nodes.rationale: A stylesheet is claims about elements. There is no call stack; you debug by asking which rule won.

nodes.label: Parse-time value normalisation
nodes.rationale: Authored text is not retained. #ff0000 reads back as rgb(255, 0, 0); shorthands expand to longhands.

nodes.label: Shorthand expansion
nodes.rationale: A later shorthand writes every longhand it owns, including ones you never named, so border: 1px solid resets border-color to currentcolor.

nodes.label: Cascade
nodes.rationale: Last one wins is only the final tiebreak after origin, importance, layer and specificity.

nodes.label: transform and opacity composite-only
nodes.rationale: transform moves x without changing width/height. Neighbours do not reflow, so overlap is a feature and a trap.

nodes.label: visibility hidden vs display none
nodes.rationale: visibility:hidden keeps the box in layout (paint change). display:none removes it and forces reflow of neighbours.

nodes.label: Inline style attribute
nodes.rationale: Beats every author rule except author !important. Right only for script-computed values, preferably custom properties.

nodes.label: @import request serialisation
nodes.rationale: Browser cannot discover the imported file until the importer is parsed. 500 ms delay: chained @import FCP 1076 ms vs parallel links 636 ms.

nodes.label: CSS blocks first paint
nodes.rationale: Browser chooses a blank frame over a wrong frame. 47 ms no CSS vs 671 ms with one 600 ms delayed sheet.

nodes.label: Non-matching media does not block paint
nodes.rationale: media=print painted at 38 ms vs 671 ms for a matching sheet. Still downloaded, just not waited for.

nodes.label: media print onload flip
nodes.rationale: Load non-critical CSS without blocking; styles land after first paint so only use below the fold.

nodes.label: Silent discard of unknown CSS
nodes.rationale: Forward compatibility: a typo and a future feature are indistinguishable. Unknown syntax as error would prevent new CSS from shipping.

nodes.label: Invalid selector discards whole rule
nodes.rationale: .c, ::nonsense is not reduced to .c. One experimental selector in a list of eight silently disables the other seven.

nodes.label: User-agent cascade origin
nodes.rationale: Weakest origin: any author rule beats any UA default. !important inverts so user accessibility overrides cannot be defeated.

nodes.label: Form controls do not inherit font
nodes.rationale: UA sets 13.3333px sans-serif on button and input. Explicit declaration beats inheritance; fix is font: inherit.

nodes.label: Modern small reset
nodes.rationale: Six justified lines beat a 300-line library. Normalize.css patched 2012 engine differences that have largely converged.

nodes.label: box-sizing border-box universal
nodes.rationale: Applied to *, *::before, *::after so generated content is not left on content-box.

nodes.label: Never remove focus outline
nodes.rationale: *:focus { outline: none } is an accessibility defect. Replace with :focus-visible, never delete.

nodes.label: Unsupported at-rule drops whole block
nodes.rationale: Rules inside @container do not exist for an engine without container queries. Base styling must stay outside.

nodes.label: @layer
nodes.rationale: First mention sets order. Layer order is compared before specificity; unlayered styles beat all layered ones.

nodes.label: @supports selector()
nodes.rationale: @supports (:has(a)) is a malformed declaration test and is always false. Selectors need selector().

nodes.label: Cascade-safe value fallback
nodes.rationale: Declare fallback then modern value. @supports is for when the fallback needs different properties, not just a different value.

nodes.label: @supports tests parse not correctness
nodes.rationale: An engine can parse a property, apply it partially, and pass the test.

nodes.label: Progressive enhancement contract
nodes.rationale: Base outside any recent at-rule; enhancement inside; enhancement must undo the base. Delete the guard once Baseline is Widely available.

nodes.label: Local support is not shipping safety
nodes.rationale: Firefox 153 CSS.supports is true for anchor-positioning and accent-color, both Limited. It works here is how those reach production broken.

nodes.label: Vendor prefixes failed as a strategy
nodes.rationale: Authors shipped -webkit- only. Browsers now ship behind flags. Firefox implements several -webkit- properties for compatibility.

nodes.label: -webkit-line-clamp still required
nodes.rationale: Unprefixed line-clamp is false in Firefox 153; -webkit-line-clamp is true. Feature is Limited availability.

nodes.label: Styles pane strike-through
nodes.rationale: Struck through means the rule matched and lost, or failed to parse if a warning triangle is present. Those need opposite fixes.

nodes.label: CSS debugging order
nodes.rationale: In the DOM? Parsed? Matched ($0.matches)? Won (strike-through / Computed)? Box where expected? Steps 2 and 3 are the ones people skip.

nodes.label: Class selector
nodes.rationale: Default because it says nothing about the document. .card survives a div becoming an article.

nodes.label: Type selector
nodes.rationale: For content you do not control. Scope under .prose so bare h2 does not leak into components.

nodes.label: ID selector
nodes.rationale: Avoid in component CSS: specificity 1,0,0, cannot repeat, and ids belong to anchors and ARIA.

nodes.label: Owl selector * + *
nodes.rationale: Applies spacing to every child except the first. Vertical rhythm without a :first-child exception.

nodes.label: Right-to-left selector matching
nodes.rationale: Engine finds the key selector first. main * is heavier than main > .thing because the candidate set is every element.

nodes.label: Style on aria attributes
nodes.rationale: Visual state and accessibility state cannot drift because they are the same attribute. A parallel .is-open class can be forgotten.

nodes.label: ~= vs *= on class
nodes.rationale: *= is a substring match over the whole string and also matches column-header. ~= matches a whole list item.

nodes.label: Unforgiving selector list
nodes.rationale: Adding :popover-open to a six-selector shared rule silently unstyles all six in engines that do not know it.

nodes.label: :is()
nodes.rationale: Matches identically to :where() but contributes the specificity of its most specific argument to every match.

nodes.label: :where()
nodes.rationale: Always specificity zero. Tool for defaults meant to be overridden: resets, libraries, .prose content styles.

nodes.label: :has()
nodes.rationale: Parent selector and previous-sibling selector. Widely available since 2023-12-19. Unforgiving; no nested :has().

nodes.label: :has() replaces ancestor class toggles
nodes.rationale: body:has(dialog[open]) cannot get out of sync the way classList.add/remove on an error path can.

nodes.label: :has() matching cost
nodes.rationale: 5000 rows: querySelectorAll class 0.15 ms vs :has(:checked) 1.25 ms. Not free; JS to keep a class in sync costs more.

nodes.label: Pseudo-elements are not in the DOM
Styling hooks that are not classes
Declaring layers and fixing their order
Phase 9 Motion and the cost model
Sass variables vs CSS custom properties
Express.js syllabus
nodes.rationale: 11 phases in 4 parts, 114 topics. Roughly half is HTTP API design that Node refused to absorb. Target Express 5.2.1 on Node 24.19.0.

nodes.label: Express 5.x target
nodes.rationale: Inventory verified on Express 5.2.1. Do not start before Node Phase 5 (node:http). Prefer Node Phase 8 before Express Phases 8–9.

nodes.label: Concept vs Express surface boundary
nodes.rationale: Concept → Node (or DB / Redis / Docker / Nginx). Middleware + route surface + HTTP contracts → Express.

nodes.label: Foundations part (phases 0–2)
nodes.rationale: Express over node:http, routing, middleware. Do not skip: every middleware-did-not-run bug traces here.

nodes.label: Node Phase 5 prerequisite
nodes.rationale: node:http, request bodies as streams, signals, graceful HTTP shutdown. Learning Express first means learning the abstraction without the thing it abstracts.

nodes.label: Express.js explanation pages
nodes.rationale: Claimed by session 8679dc8c on 2026-08-14. 78 pages exist; progress counts topics brought to standard. Phases 0–3 done (38 of 114).

nodes.label: Documentation-validated from Phase 2 on
nodes.rationale: No sandbox runs from Phase 2 on. No console block unless a run actually produced it.

nodes.label: Phase 0 — Express over node:http
nodes.rationale: Express is not a second language and not an application architecture. Seven pages; first three are load-bearing.

nodes.label: Phase 0 gate
nodes.rationale: Draw the object graph, point to where a request is lost if nobody calls next and nobody writes a response, and name what Express 5 broke about app.get('*').

nodes.label: Express as middleware engine with a router
nodes.rationale: Not a language and not an application architecture. Programmable routing and middleware on top of Node's http.Server. Business rules, databases, and queues are called from handlers.

nodes.label: app is a request listener
nodes.rationale: express() returns a function. Pass it to http.createServer(app) or call app.listen. Express fills the function Node already expects. Sandbox-measured: typeof app === 'function' and app.handle exists.

nodes.label: What Express is not
nodes.rationale: Not a language, ORM, or auth product. Password hashing lives in Node; Express only mounts identity middleware. Debugging hangs still needs node:http.

nodes.label: Ecosystem over peak throughput
nodes.rationale: Express optimises for ecosystem and familiarity. Fastify can win raw benchmarks; you pay with a smaller middleware universe. Right default for most MERN/PERN APIs.

nodes.label: http.Server, app, and Router object graph
nodes.rationale: http.Server owns the socket. app owns settings and the top-level stack. Router is a portable mountable stack. Only the server listens. Confusing them is how middleware never runs.

nodes.label: http.Server
nodes.rationale: Created by http.createServer(app) or app.listen. Owns port, SIGTERM, and server.close. Express does not own process signals.

nodes.label: Express app
nodes.rationale: express() result: settings, top-level middleware, mounts. Itself a request listener. Only app owns application settings.

nodes.label: express.Router
nodes.rationale: A portable stack of routes/middleware you mount on app or another router. Has no mountpath; inside a request the equivalent is req.baseUrl.

nodes.label: app.listen is createServer sugar
nodes.rationale: app.listen(port) is http.createServer(app).listen(port). Prefer explicit server for TLS, WebSockets, or tests that import app without listening.

nodes.label: Prefer shallow feature routers
nodes.rationale: Many routers keep files small. Deep nested mounts make req.baseUrl vs req.path debugging harder.

nodes.label: Express request lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Server accepts → app stack top to bottom → handler or 404 → or four-arg error middleware. No parallel Express event loop; it is Node's loop.

nodes.label: next()
nodes.rationale: Each middleware sends and stops, calls next() to continue, or next(err) to jump to error middleware. Express will not auto-continue.

nodes.label: next(err)
nodes.rationale: Skip remaining normal middleware and jump to the error-handling stack.

nodes.label: Four-argument error middleware
nodes.rationale: Signature must be exactly (err, req, res, next). Register last. Express 5 forwards thrown/rejected handlers here.

nodes.label: Hang if no next and no response
nodes.rationale: If nothing calls next and nothing writes a response, the client hangs. next() after res.json yields Cannot set headers after they are sent.

nodes.label: 404 middleware after all routes
nodes.rationale: After all routes, as normal middleware that sends 404 — not as error middleware (no err).

nodes.label: One JS thread
nodes.rationale: Express does not process two requests on two threads. Concurrency is async I/O, not multi-threaded handlers.

nodes.label: express()
nodes.rationale: Returns an application — a request-handler function with use, get, settings, and listen sugar.

nodes.label: Separate createApp from listen
nodes.rationale: listen is a side effect. Tests import the app without binding a port; production controls boot order. Never listen at import time (EADDRINUSE).

nodes.label: https.createServer(options, app)
nodes.rationale: app.listen is not enough for HTTPS. Prefer explicit createServer in production once TLS or multi-protocol shows up.

nodes.label: Application settings (app.set / app.get)
nodes.rationale: App-wide defaults. Do not confuse app.get('etag') (setting) with app.get('/etag', handler) (route).

nodes.label: x-powered-by
nodes.rationale: Default true; advertises Express. Disable in production APIs. Not a security boundary by itself. Measured: app.disable sets it to false.

nodes.label: query parser default simple
nodes.rationale: Express 5 default is simple (was extended in 4). Nested a[b]=1 is not an object. Measured on 5.2.1: query parser = "simple".

nodes.label: trust proxy
nodes.rationale: Default false. Without it, req.ip is the proxy. Affects IP, protocol from X-Forwarded-*, secure cookies, and rate-limit keys. Never true blindly.

nodes.label: strict and case-sensitive routing unset
nodes.rationale: Measured undefined, not false. Express never assigns them until you app.set. Unset behaves as off. app.get('strict routing') === false never runs on a fresh app.

nodes.label: etag default weak
nodes.rationale: Measured etag = "weak". Affects automatic ETag generation for some responses.

nodes.label: Express 5 path-to-regexp rewrite
nodes.rationale: Illegal patterns throw at registration — process fails before any request. Sandbox-measured: app.get('*') Missing parameter name; /user/:id? Unexpected ?; /*splat accepted.

nodes.label: Named splat /*splat
nodes.rationale: SPA fallbacks that used app.get('*') must move to /*splat or /{*splat} to match the root. req.params.splat is an array of segments, not a string.

nodes.label: Async handler rejections forward to next
nodes.rationale: Rejected promises from async handlers go to error middleware. express-async-errors is an Express 4 habit. Still need try/catch to handle locally. Measured: 500 { error: 'async boom' }.

nodes.label: Removed Express 4 APIs
nodes.rationale: app.del, old req.param() behaviour, etc. Stay on 4 to avoid migration cost; move to 5 for supported async and modern path rules (Multer 2.x bump).

nodes.label: When Express is the right default
nodes.rationale: Team already knows it, largest middleware ecosystem, CRUD/JSON where clarity beats micro-benchmarks. This bible uses Express as the HTTP edge for MERN/PERN for those reasons.

nodes.label: Fastify
nodes.rationale: Choose when schema-driven validation and throughput matter more than the widest Connect middleware ecosystem. Plugin/encapsulation model.

nodes.label: Hono
nodes.rationale: Edge / ultra-light routing, modern DX, not married to Connect middleware.

nodes.label: NestJS
nodes.rationale: Full batteries with DI and modules. Out of this bible's Express track. Can wrap Express or Fastify later.

nodes.label: Raw node:http
nodes.rationale: Learn HTTP itself here first. Possible for production APIs, rarely pleasant. Leaving Express does not mean leaving Node.

nodes.label: Express 5.2.1 current line
nodes.rationale: npm latest is 5.2.1; latest-4 is 4.22.2. 'Express is unmaintained' FUD is outdated social posts.

nodes.label: Phase 1 — Routing and path matching
nodes.rationale: How URLs become handlers. Order is load-bearing — Express will not warn you when the wrong route wins. 9 of 9 topics documentation-validated 2026-08-14.

nodes.label: Route is method + path
nodes.rationale: Register the methods you mean. Path match is not enough. Helpers: get, post, put, patch, delete, all, plus use.

nodes.label: Wrong method is 404 not 405
nodes.rationale: Express has no built-in 405 or Allow header. FAQ: 404 is not an error — all middleware and routes ran and none responded. Implement 405 yourself for strict APIs.

nodes.label: app.all
nodes.rationale: Matches all HTTP verbs, including QUERY. Convenient for CORS preflight experiments; hides method mistakes on public APIs.

nodes.label: app.get covers HEAD unless app.head registered first
nodes.rationale: Docs caveat: app.get covers HEAD if app.head was not called for the path before app.get. Body is stripped.

nodes.label: req.params
nodes.rationale: Come from the path pattern. Always strings. Coerce and validate at the edge; never trust req.params.id as a number.

nodes.label: req.query
nodes.rationale: Query strings are not part of the route pattern. They land after the path matches. Duplicate keys become arrays under simple.

nodes.label: simple vs extended query parser
nodes.rationale: simple (Node querystring): a[b]=1 stays a literal key. Express 4 extended (qs) produced nested objects. Upgrades break req.query.filter.status.

nodes.label: Express docs qs vs simple contradiction
nodes.rationale: req.query reference still says default uses qs (Express 4 leftover). Settings table and migration guide say simple. Read back app.get('query parser').

nodes.label: Router as mini-app
nodes.rationale: Routing guide: a complete middleware and routing system. Mount at a prefix so feature modules stay small. Paths inside a router are relative to the mount.

nodes.label: mergeParams
nodes.rationale: Parent path params are not accessible from sub-routes by default. express.Router({mergeParams: true}) exposes postId inside /posts/:postId/comments.

nodes.label: req.baseUrl
nodes.rationale: URL path on which a router instance was mounted. req.path excludes the mount; req.originalUrl is full path + query.

nodes.label: API versioning via router mounts
nodes.rationale: Mount v1 and v2 routers at /api/v1 and /api/v2. Phase 6 expands strategy.

nodes.label: First match wins
nodes.rationale: A param route registered before a static sibling steals the static path. Express will not warn. /users/export hits :id with id export.

nodes.label: Static segments before params
nodes.rationale: More specific paths before general ones. No universal catch-all until every real route is registered. Express does not rank by specificity.

nodes.label: SPA fallback last
nodes.rationale: Catch-all before API routers serves API JSON as index.html. API mounts first, static + /*splat fallback last.

nodes.label: Illegal paths throw at registration
nodes.rationale: Upgrade pain is front-loaded. Broken deploys beat intermittent routing bugs. Not the same as middleware order bugs, which fail at request time.

nodes.label: Express 5 path migration map
nodes.rationale: '*' → /*splat or /{*splat}; /:file.:ext? → /:file{.:ext}; regex alternation → array of paths. Named wildcard yields an array of segments.

nodes.label: Named splat params are arrays
nodes.rationale: Migration guide: {splat: ['foo','bar']}. Request reference: /files/images/image.png → req.params.file = ['images','image.png'].

nodes.label: router.param
nodes.rationale: Runs when a named param is present. Signature (req, res, next, value). Sugar for repeated preload — not an application architecture.

nodes.label: param callback runs once per cycle
nodes.rationale: Documented guarantee: called only once in a request-response cycle even if the parameter matches multiple routes. Load, 404, attach req.item.

nodes.label: app.param
nodes.rationale: Same idea at application scope. Prefer router scope to limit blast radius.

nodes.label: app.route / router.route
nodes.rationale: Chain verbs on one path to reduce redundancy and typos. Organizational sugar, not required. Harder to split across files when handlers grow.

nodes.label: mountpath is an app property
nodes.rationale: A Router never gets mountpath — mounted or not. Measured undefined before and after app.use. A sub-app (express()) reports /reports. Use req.baseUrl during a request.

nodes.label: sub-app mount event
nodes.rationale: A sub-app fires a mount event when attached, with the parent app passed to the callback.

nodes.label: Host-based routing
nodes.rationale: Branch on req.hostname via vhost-style middleware. For most JSON APIs, path prefixes beat multi-host apps. Multi-host usually belongs on Nginx.

nodes.label: createApp(deps)
nodes.rationale: Returns app without listening. Inject db/redis/queue clients. Tests and serverless adapters need the app without binding a port.

nodes.label: X-Request-Id middleware
nodes.rationale: Accept inbound x-request-id or crypto.randomUUID(). Set on req and response. Continue with AsyncLocalStorage. Accept inbound IDs for trace continuity across gateways.

nodes.label: AsyncLocalStorage for request id
nodes.rationale: Carry request id across async hops. Owned conceptually by Node Phase 10.

nodes.label: Supertest
nodes.rationale: Hit the real Express stack with mocked services. Do not mock Express itself. request(app).get(...).expect(200).

nodes.label: Mock outbound deps not req/res
nodes.rationale: Mock DB and mail, not Express plumbing. Node Phase 9 covers the broader testing curriculum.

nodes.label: Auth test token helper
nodes.rationale: Mint sessions or JWTs without copying production crypto. Keep secrets local and deterministic.

nodes.label: Do not hit the real IdP in route tests
nodes.rationale: Slow, flaky, and out of process. Contract tests can cover IdP separately.

nodes.label: Liveness vs readiness
nodes.rationale: Failing readiness stops new traffic; failing liveness restarts the process. Conflating them causes restart storms. Liveness is cheap; readiness checks pool/redis.

nodes.label: App boot order
nodes.rationale: validate env → connect pool → createApp(deps) → server.listen → signal ready. Production listens only after deps are ready.

nodes.label: Restart storms
nodes.rationale: A readiness failure that is treated as liveness kills and respawns the process in a loop.

nodes.label: SIGTERM graceful shutdown
nodes.rationale: On SIGTERM stop accepting, drain in-flight work, then close pools. Keep the listen() return value to close later.

nodes.label: http.Server.close
nodes.rationale: Call close on the http.Server from listen(), not on the Express app object.

nodes.label: server.js vs app.js
nodes.rationale: server.js listens; app.js exports the factory. Feature flags and serverless-http adapters are When Needed.

nodes.label: Phase 10 — Testable app and ops boundary
nodes.rationale: Composition root for HTTP. Docker/Nginx depth lives in their syllabi.

nodes.label: createApp factory
nodes.rationale: Pure factory; no listen inside. Production listens only after deps are ready.

nodes.label: Request id middleware
nodes.rationale: X-Request-Id plus AsyncLocalStorage hook.

nodes.label: Supertest against createApp
nodes.rationale: Route tests with mocked services; no real listen or DB.

nodes.label: Auth helpers in tests
nodes.rationale: Helpers mint sessions or JWTs for 403-path coverage.

nodes.label: HTTP composition root
nodes.rationale: One place wires middleware, routes, and deps. createApp({mocks}) under Supertest covers happy plus 403 paths without a real DB.

nodes.label: Middleware signature (req, res, next)
nodes.rationale: (req, res, next) => void for normal middleware; four args for errors. An Express app is a series of middleware function calls.

nodes.label: Three legal middleware endings
nodes.rationale: Respond, next(), or next(err). Returning without one of those is not an ending Express understands — the socket waits.

nodes.label: Route handlers are middleware
nodes.rationale: Same contract with a method and path filter in front.

nodes.label: Hanging request
nodes.rationale: If middleware does not end the cycle it must call next(); otherwise the request is left hanging. Audit if-arms and async paths.

nodes.label: return next() style
nodes.rationale: return next() only returns from your function; next is what continues the chain. return avoids running code after next by accident.

nodes.label: First registered runs first
nodes.rationale: Express does not sort middleware by specificity. Registration order on app is absolute.

nodes.label: App, router, and route middleware levels
nodes.rationale: App stack in registration order, then the mounted router stack, then route-specific middleware and handler.

nodes.label: Router mount path stripped
nodes.rationale: A router's own mount path is stripped and not visible to the middleware.

nodes.label: Scoped vs global middleware
nodes.rationale: Global middleware is easy and expensive (runs for health checks and static). Scope auth to /api so probes on /health do not break.

nodes.label: next()
nodes.rationale: Continues to the next non-error middleware. next after a response means header errors.

nodes.label: next(err)
nodes.rationale: Skips remaining non-error middleware and jumps to error handlers. Mount those last.

nodes.label: Double send
nodes.rationale: First body wins; second write throws Cannot set headers after they are sent to the client.

nodes.label: res.headersSent guard
nodes.rationale: Documented custom-handler guard: if (res.headersSent) return next(err). After a write the default error handler closes the connection.

nodes.label: next('route')
nodes.rationale: Advanced skip-to-next-route feature — rare. Default is next().

nodes.label: Express 5 async throw forwarding
nodes.rationale: On Express 5, throw inside async handlers and rejections are forwarded like next(err).

nodes.label: Configurable middleware factory
nodes.rationale: A function that accepts options and returns middleware. Every built-in follows it: express.json({limit}), express.static(root, options), express.urlencoded({extended}).

nodes.label: No module-level middleware options
nodes.rationale: Module-level let options lets tests and concurrent apps clobber each other. Closure over options makes each instance independent.

nodes.label: Factory passed as middleware
nodes.rationale: app.use(requireHeader) passes the factory, not the instance — wrong arity and behaviour. Call it: app.use(requireHeader('x-api-key')).

nodes.label: validate(schema) factory
nodes.rationale: Same pattern powers validation middleware: validate(schema) returns (req, res, next) => …

nodes.label: Canonical Express skeleton
nodes.rationale: disable x-powered-by, json parser, routes, 404 (3-arg), error handler (4-arg). Keep one composition root instead of ad-hoc app.use across files.

nodes.label: Body parsers early
nodes.rationale: Handlers and validators read req.body. If they run before express.json(), req.body is empty. Size limits also need to apply before business logic.

nodes.label: Error middleware last
nodes.rationale: Error-handling middleware is defined last, after other app.use() and routes. If registered before routes, those routes never fall into it.

nodes.label: Four-argument error middleware
nodes.rationale: You must provide four arguments to identify it as error-handling middleware, even when next goes unused.

nodes.label: 404 handler
nodes.rationale: Goes at the very bottom of the stack below all other functions, just above errors. A 404 is not an error and never reaches the error handler.

nodes.label: req field attachments
nodes.rationale: Attaching fields on req is how identity and timing flow down the chain. Typical later attachments: req.user, req.validated.

nodes.label: req.user
nodes.rationale: Authentication middleware attaches it after verifying session or token. Implicit req.user is convenient and hides dependencies.

nodes.label: Namespaced req.ctx
nodes.rationale: Docs do not enumerate a reserved list; treat request and response references as the list. A single namespaced object is the safe habit.

nodes.label: Do not clobber core req/res properties
nodes.rationale: Do not overwrite req.url, method, headers, query, params, or res.end/json wholesale. Routing and security depend on them.

nodes.label: res.locals
nodes.rationale: Documented request-scoped place for values.

nodes.label: res.on('finish') timing
nodes.rationale: Only store scalars you need; do not retain req in global arrays or you leak memory.

nodes.label: Inject deps via factory not req
nodes.rationale: Avoid putting DB clients on req. Lifecycle and testing — inject via app.locals or factory deps instead.

nodes.label: Express built-in middleware
nodes.rationale: express.json, urlencoded, raw, text (based on body-parser), express.static (serve-static), express.Router. Application settings are not middleware.

nodes.label: Third-party middleware checklist
nodes.rationale: Check Express 5 support, maintenance, whether middleware is the right shape, what it mutates, and whether it calls next(err) or throws.

nodes.label: Middleware supply-chain surface
nodes.rationale: A battle-tested package saves time; every dependency is supply-chain surface. Prefer fewer, better mounts. Defaults are not a security review.

nodes.label: Phase 2 — Middleware architecture
nodes.rationale: Target Express 5.2.1 on Node 24.19.0. The whole framework is a stack of functions. Order, next, and termination are the job.

nodes.label: Phase 2 gate
nodes.rationale: Place body parser, auth, routes, and error middleware in the only order that works, and diagnose a hang as forgot next vs forgot to send.

nodes.label: req as IncomingMessage plus Express fields
nodes.rationale: Some properties exist only after middleware runs. Document what the app attaches so handlers do not assume ghosts.

nodes.label: req.body
nodes.rationale: By default undefined, populated when you use body-parsing middleware.

nodes.label: req.cookies
nodes.rationale: Needs cookie-parser and defaults to {} only once that middleware is mounted. Not built into Express.

nodes.label: req.ip and req.ips
nodes.rationale: Derived from the left-most X-Forwarded-For entry whenever trust proxy is not false; otherwise ips is an empty array. Wrong behind a proxy until trust proxy is set.

nodes.label: req.originalUrl
nodes.rationale: Full original path including mount and query — useful behind routers.

nodes.label: JSON.stringify omits undefined
nodes.rationale: A console block that prints body: undefined cannot be a real res.json run — undefined object properties are omitted. Known error left in place.

nodes.label: express.json
nodes.rationale: Defaults: limit 100kb, type application/json, strict true, inflate true. Populates req.body only when Content-Type matches.

nodes.label: express.urlencoded
nodes.rationale: For HTML form posts. Express 5 default extended is false (querystring library); true uses qs for nested objects.

nodes.label: Content-Type parser gate
nodes.rationale: Wrong type means empty body, not a thrown error — usually not an automatic 415. Body is undefined if no body, type unmatched, or an error occurred.

nodes.label: urlencoded extended:false default
nodes.rationale: Express 5 change. Nested form fields are missing unless you set extended:true and still validate.

nodes.label: Per-route body parsers
nodes.rationale: Global express.json() is simple. Per-route parsers avoid parsing huge bodies on routes that never need them.

nodes.label: Parser limit option
nodes.rationale: Default 100kb on json, urlencoded, raw, and text. Treat limit as a production control. Different routes can use different limits.

nodes.label: entity.too.large
nodes.rationale: Express/body-parser type for an over-limit entity. Map it to a stable error body in error middleware.

nodes.label: query parser simple
nodes.rationale: Express 5 default. Node querystring: repeated keys become arrays and bracket syntax is never interpreted. Safer default; breaks old nested-query clients.

nodes.label: query parser extended
nodes.rationale: Opt-in via app.set('query parser', 'extended'). a[b]=1 becomes {a:{b:'1'}} via qs. Allow-list filter keys if enabled.

nodes.label: qs vs simple docs contradiction
nodes.rationale: req.query reference still says the parser by default uses qs — stale Express 4 text. Settings table and migration guide agree on simple.

nodes.label: Nested query prototype pollution
nodes.rationale: Nested objects are historically used in prototype-pollution payloads (?__proto__[x]=y). Never pass raw req.query into Mongo/SQL builders.

nodes.label: entity.parse.failed
nodes.rationale: Typical status 400. Reaches the four-arg handler through next(err). strict:true is why only objects and arrays are accepted at the top level.

nodes.label: Stable parse-error envelope
nodes.rationale: Default handler writes err.stack in development. Map to {code:'BAD_JSON', message:'Invalid JSON body'} and log detail server-side with a request id.

nodes.label: 415 unsupported type
nodes.rationale: Odd Content-Type values can skip the parser. Reject unsupported types with 415 if the API is strict.

nodes.label: express.raw
nodes.rationale: Parses into a Buffer. Default type application/octet-stream, limit 100kb. Widen type for JSON webhooks.

nodes.label: express.text
nodes.rationale: Parses into a string. Default type text/plain. Still set limits.

nodes.label: Webhook HMAC over raw bytes
nodes.rationale: JSON parsing destroys the exact bytes. Signatures are over the exact byte sequence, not a re-serialized object. Verify then JSON.parse if needed.

nodes.label: First matching parser consumes the stream
nodes.rationale: Global JSON before a route-level raw webhook handler leaves an empty or wrong body. Mount raw on /webhooks/* before global JSON.

nodes.label: No built-in multipart parser
nodes.rationale: Built-in list is json, urlencoded, raw, text, static, Router. multipart/form-data is not JSON.

nodes.label: Multer 2.x
nodes.rationale: Multer latest 2.2.0 as of 2026-08-14. Pin multer@2 for Express 5. Parse multipart, enforce counts/sizes, memory vs disk.

nodes.label: Never global multer
nodes.rationale: Multer README: never add multer as a global middleware since a malicious user could upload files to a route you did not anticipate.

nodes.label: Multer fileSize defaults to Infinity
nodes.rationale: An uncapped upload is the default. Memory storage plus large or many files can OOM.

nodes.label: Untrusted upload originalname and mimetype
nodes.rationale: Multer README has no explicit warning; this bible's advice. Clients lie. Generate your own object keys. Prefer file-signature checks.

nodes.label: Object storage for uploads
nodes.rationale: Large files belong in S3-compatible object storage, not the API container writable layer. Cleanup temp paths on failure.

nodes.label: Cookie read/write asymmetry
nodes.rationale: res.cookie is built in; req.cookies needs cookie-parser. Writing Set-Cookie works without the package.

nodes.label: cookie-parser
nodes.rationale: Not in Express built-in list. cookieParser('secret') populates req.signedCookies. Session middleware typically depends on cookie parsing.

nodes.label: Signed cookies
nodes.rationale: Detect tampering with a server secret; they are not encryption. Still visible to the client unless httpOnly and not encrypted by default.

nodes.label: req.accepts, req.is, req.get, req.range
nodes.rationale: req.is returns the matching content type or false. req.accepts returns the best Accept match or false. req.get is case-insensitive with Referrer/Referer interchangeable.

nodes.label: Phase 3 — Requests and body parsing
nodes.rationale: Target Express 5.2.1 on Node 24.19.0. Everything clients send — and the limits that keep one request from taking the process down.

nodes.label: Phase 3 gate
nodes.rationale: Mount JSON parsing with a hard size limit, handle a huge body without hanging, and receive multipart without trusting Content-Type alone.

nodes.label: Known body:undefined console error
nodes.rationale: Pages 01 and 02 print body:undefined which no real run can produce. Left unrewritten because inventing replacement output is worse than a flagged error.

nodes.label: One terminal response method
nodes.rationale: Pick one terminal method. Mixing json then send is how headers-already-sent starts. Every branch ends with send/json/end/redirect.

nodes.label: res.json
nodes.rationale: Sends a JSON response converted with JSON.stringify. Prefer json for JSON APIs.

nodes.label: res.send
nodes.rationale: Chooses Content-Type from the body: Buffer → octet-stream, String → text/html, Array/Object → JSON. Flexible and easy to misuse.

nodes.label: res.status
nodes.rationale: Chainable alias of Node response.statusCode. Must precede the terminal body call.

nodes.label: res.sendStatus
nodes.rationale: Sets the status and sends its string body — a terminal call, not a variant of res.status.

nodes.label: res.redirect
nodes.rationale: Defaults to 302. Overload accepts an explicit code.

nodes.label: HTTP status as contract
nodes.rationale: Useful APIs pick 201/204/400/401/403/404/409 deliberately — not always 200. Align with OpenAPI and stick to it.

nodes.label: Headers fixed once body starts
nodes.rationale: res.set, res.type, and res.vary are only meaningful before the first write. res.headersSent flips once headers go out.

nodes.label: Express 5 status 100–999
nodes.rationale: Express 5 restricts res.status() to 100–999 and rejects anything outside that range. An Express 4 habit of passing a made-up code now throws.

nodes.label: 204 No Content
nodes.rationale: Success with no response body (e.g. DELETE). Use res.status(204).end().

nodes.label: 401 vs 403
nodes.rationale: 401 unauthenticated; 403 authenticated but not allowed.

nodes.label: Always-200 RPC-over-HTTP
nodes.rationale: Always HTTP 200 with {success:false} is an RPC-over-HTTP habit. Use real statuses; keep error body for details.

nodes.label: Phase 4 — Responses and static files
nodes.rationale: What leaves the process: status, body shape, files, cookies, SPA fallback. Target Express 5.2.1 on Node 24.19.0.

nodes.label: Phase 4 gate — one response per path
nodes.rationale: Every success and error path ends in exactly one response with a deliberate status and consistent JSON shape; SPA fallback does not steal /api.

nodes.label: Response shapes
nodes.rationale: Pick envelope vs bare resource and keep it consistent. Mixing both is worse than either choice. Express has no opinion; res.json just JSON.stringifies what you hand it.

nodes.label: Bare resource response
nodes.rationale: Matches pure REST textbooks and OpenAPI components cleanly; no wrapper nesting.

nodes.label: Envelope response
nodes.rationale: Envelopes extend with pagination meta without breaking clients; they add nesting noise.

nodes.label: Stable error JSON shape
nodes.rationale: Clients parse one schema; you can add code without breaking UIs. Shape is { error: { code, message } }.

nodes.label: JSON.stringify omits undefined
nodes.rationale: An envelope field set to undefined disappears from the response rather than appearing as null. Make absent-vs-null an explicit decision.

nodes.label: Headers already sent
nodes.rationale: The first write wins. A second res.json / send throws Cannot set headers after they are sent to the client.

nodes.label: Cannot set headers after they are sent
nodes.rationale: Something tried to write status/headers/body after the response started. Causes: next() after res.json, error middleware after a handler already responded, fall-through return res paths.

nodes.label: res.headersSent guard
nodes.rationale: In error middleware: if (res.headersSent) return next(err); so a second write is not attempted.

nodes.label: express.static
nodes.rationale: Serves files from a directory as middleware. Put it after API routes if the same app also hosts a SPA. Prefer a CDN or Nginx for heavy static traffic.

nodes.label: Static cache headers
nodes.rationale: Long maxAge for hashed filenames; short/none for HTML. Fingerprinted assets can be immutable; HTML points at changing hashes. Default weak ETags are fine for many apps.

nodes.label: Static root isolation
nodes.rationale: A static root too high exposes node_modules or .env. Root only the build output directory. Express 5 dotfiles defaults should not serve secrets.

nodes.label: SPA fallback
nodes.rationale: Client-side routers need index.html on unknown paths. Register the catch-all after API routes.

nodes.label: Named splat {*splat}
nodes.rationale: On Express 5, app.get('*') throws at boot. Use a named splat.

nodes.label: API then static then splat
nodes.rationale: Catch-all before API makes /api/users return HTML. Correct order: API → static assets → HTML fallback.

nodes.label: Bare star path invalid on Express 5
nodes.rationale: Bare * path tokens are invalid; registration throws. 2020 MERN tutorials crash on Express 5.

nodes.label: res.cookie
nodes.rationale: Built in. Flags decide whether browser JS can read the cookie and when it is sent. Reading cookies needs cookie-parser.

nodes.label: httpOnly cookie flag
nodes.rationale: Blocks document.cookie. Stops trivial XSS from stealing session tokens via JavaScript.

nodes.label: SameSite cookie flag
nodes.rationale: CSRF posture for cookie-based sessions. SameSite=None requires secure.

nodes.label: Secure cookie flag
nodes.rationale: HTTPS only. Required with SameSite=None. Typically enabled when NODE_ENV === production.

nodes.label: Streaming and downloads
nodes.rationale: res.sendFile and res.download stream files with safer path options. For big dynamic bodies, pipe a stream and handle errors mid-flight.

nodes.label: res.sendFile
nodes.rationale: Serves one file inline on a route. Use when the file is chosen by logic — auth, tenancy, a lookup. Path must be absolute unless root is set. Errors arrive in the callback, not as thrown exceptions.

nodes.label: res.download
nodes.rationale: res.sendFile plus Content-Disposition: attachment. Transfers the file as an attachment with a filename you choose.

nodes.label: res.attachment
nodes.rationale: Sets Content-Disposition and infers Content-Type from the extension. Must run before the body is sent.

nodes.label: sendFile root option
nodes.rationale: When root is set, Express validates the relative path resolves within that root — the documented traversal guard. Without it, path.join of client input can escape to ../../etc/passwd.

nodes.label: stream.pipeline over pipe
nodes.rationale: A bare .pipe() leaves the source open when the destination fails or the client disconnects, leaking handles. pipeline destroys every stream in the chain on failure.

nodes.label: Set headers before first stream byte
nodes.rationale: Once the stream writes, status and headers are frozen. A mid-flight failure leaves a truncated 200. Validate and authorise before the pipe starts. The catch only logs; it cannot rescue the response.

nodes.label: compression middleware
nodes.rationale: Compressing in Node costs event-loop time. Terminate gzip at Nginx or the CDN when you have one. Never double-compress. Use the middleware when Express is the edge or you need per-route control.

nodes.label: Signed URL offload
nodes.rationale: When files are large or private, issue a signed URL to object storage. Node then spends no bandwidth, memory, or event-loop time on the transfer.

nodes.label: Stream vs buffer trade-off
nodes.rationale: Streaming keeps memory flat regardless of payload size. You give up changing status after the first byte. Buffering keeps error handling simple until size makes it untenable.

nodes.label: Phase 5 — Error handling
nodes.rationale: One funnel for failures. Express 5 forwards async rejections — you still design the envelope.

nodes.label: Phase 5 gate — same public envelope
nodes.rationale: Thrown async errors, next(err), and malformed JSON all produce the same public envelope without stack traces when NODE_ENV=production.

nodes.label: Four-arg error middleware
nodes.rationale: Error middleware has four parameters. Express detects it by arity. Mount it last.

nodes.label: Error middleware arity detection
nodes.rationale: Function length 4: (err, req, res, next). Omit next and Express treats it as normal middleware; errors vanish into the wrong path.

nodes.label: Express 5 async rejection forwarding
nodes.rationale: Rejected promises from async handlers reach error middleware on Express 5. You do not need express-async-errors for that baseline. Express 4 often needed wrappers or next(err).

nodes.label: Handler-local try/catch for domain mapping
nodes.rationale: Still use try/catch when you convert errors to domain responses inside the handler without wanting the global mapper.

nodes.label: Error response contract
nodes.rationale: One public JSON shape for errors. Include a stable code. Never send err.stack when NODE_ENV === production.

nodes.label: Hide production stacks and 500 messages
nodes.rationale: Stack traces and internal exception messages for unexpected 500s must never appear in production error JSON. Use a generic Internal Server Error when status >= 500 or err.expose === false.

nodes.label: Domain-to-HTTP status mapping
nodes.rationale: Carry statusCode on errors you throw. Map domain failures once in error middleware — not with ad-hoc res.status in every catch. 400/422 validation, 401 unauthenticated, 403 forbidden, 404 missing, 409 conflict, 429 rate limit, 503 upstream, 500 bug.

nodes.label: HttpError class
nodes.rationale: Thin helper: statusCode, code, message; expose = statusCode < 500. Avoid deep inheritance trees.

nodes.label: 401 vs 403
nodes.rationale: 401 = who are you?; 403 = I know who you are and you may not.

nodes.label: Operational errors
nodes.rationale: Expected at the edge: bad input, not found, 409. Client sees a clear message + code.

nodes.label: Programmer errors
nodes.rationale: Bugs such as Cannot read properties of undefined. Client sees a generic 500. Messages leak paths, schemas, and exploit detail.

nodes.label: Request-scoped vs process-level errors
nodes.rationale: At the HTTP edge: expose operational, hide programmer, log both. Do not keep the process alive after unknown programmer errors in a bad state. Express error middleware is for request-scoped failures; uncaughtException is Node.

nodes.label: 404 as three-arg middleware
nodes.rationale: 404 is normal middleware (3 args) after routes, not error middleware. It always sends 404 when reached. Error middleware mounts after it.

nodes.label: Process crashes are Node topics
nodes.rationale: unhandledRejection / uncaughtException belong to Node Phase 5. Structured logging of errors is Node Phase 10 plus request-id middleware. Request 404/500 envelope stays in Express.

nodes.label: REST resource modeling
nodes.rationale: Resources are nouns. Collections are lists of them. Prefer /orders/12/items over /getOrderItems.

nodes.label: Collection, item, and sub-resource
nodes.rationale: GET /users list+POST create; GET /users/:id read/update/delete one; /users/:id/orders owned hierarchy.

nodes.label: RPC-style action routes
nodes.rationale: Fine when the domain is an action, not a thing — POST /payments/:id/refund. Name them honestly instead of inventing fake nouns. Acceptable for multi-step operations that are not natural CRUD.

nodes.label: Static segments before :id
nodes.rationale: /users/export is captured by :id if the param route is registered first. Static segments first.

nodes.label: Deep hierarchy vs flatten
nodes.rationale: Deep hierarchies mirror the domain and complicate authorization and caching. Flatten when joins explode.

nodes.label: CRUD to HTTP status mapping
nodes.rationale: Create 201 + Location; read 200; replace/update 200 or 204; delete 204 or 200. Failures: 400 validation, 404 missing, 409 conflict.

nodes.label: 201 Created with Location
nodes.rationale: Signals a new resource; pairs with Location when useful.

nodes.label: Everything returns 200
nodes.rationale: Envelope-only APIs hide status. Use real statuses; body for details.

nodes.label: Offset pagination
nodes.rationale: GET /items?limit=20&offset=40. Easy, slow on deep pages, unstable if rows insert while paging.

nodes.label: Cursor pagination
nodes.rationale: Stable for infinite scroll; opaque cursors hide storage details. Encode nothing sensitive without signing/encrypting. Prefer for large or volatile lists.

nodes.label: Cap pagination limit
nodes.rationale: Default limit (e.g. 20) and max (e.g. 100). Never allow limit=999999. Protects DB and API CPU from accidental or malicious full-table pulls.

nodes.label: Allow-list filter and sort fields
nodes.rationale: Never pass raw req.query into Mongo or SQL builders. Allow-list fields and operators. Prevents sorting on unindexed or sensitive columns and injection-style operators.

nodes.label: Mongo operator injection via query
nodes.rationale: ?filter[$gt]=… injects operators when query objects are merged blindly. Fix with allow-list plus parameterized queries.

nodes.label: Bounded full-text search
nodes.rationale: Search endpoints that hit full-text indexes belong behind explicit q params and timeouts. Do not run unbounded scans on the request thread.

nodes.label: URL prefix versioning
nodes.rationale: Most common style for REST JSON APIs: /api/v1/users. Visible, cache-friendly, easy routers. Clearest default for this stack.

nodes.label: Header versioning
nodes.rationale: Accept-Version: 1. Cleaner URLs, harder to explore.

nodes.label: Media-type versioning
nodes.rationale: Accept: application/vnd.app.v1+json. Strict, heavy.

nodes.label: Deprecate with sunset headers
nodes.rationale: Deprecate with docs + sunset headers; do not break v1 silently.

nodes.label: Idempotency keys
nodes.rationale: Clients retry POSTs. Without an idempotency key you double-charge. Store the first response and replay it. Needed most on POST and some PATCH; GET/PUT are already idempotent when implemented correctly.

nodes.label: Replay stored idempotent response
nodes.rationale: Client sends Idempotency-Key on unsafe requests. Server stores key → response (status + body) under a TTL. Replay returns the same result without re-executing side effects.

nodes.label: Idempotency payload mismatch 409
nodes.rationale: Same key, different body is a client bug or attack. Reject with 409 if payload hash mismatches stored request.

nodes.label: ETag
nodes.rationale: Conditional requests avoid useless transfers. Express can generate weak ETags; for APIs, explicit version fields or hashes are often clearer.

nodes.label: If-None-Match 304
nodes.rationale: If-None-Match matching the current ETag yields 304 Not Modified when the client already has the current representation.

nodes.label: If-Match lost-update 412
nodes.rationale: If-Match: v2 → 412 if current is v3. Detects lost updates.

nodes.label: Cache-Control private no-store
nodes.rationale: Authenticated JSON is usually Cache-Control: private, no-store. Public catalog may use public, max-age carefully. Static hashed assets use long max-age + immutable.

nodes.label: OpenAPI contract
nodes.rationale: The contract is part of the product. Write or generate OpenAPI 3.x for public routes. Swagger UI is optional sugar — the artifact is the spec. Even internal APIs gain onboarding, client generation, contract tests, and explicit breaking-change review.

nodes.label: OpenAPI and handler drift
nodes.rationale: Drift between OpenAPI and handlers is a bug. CI should fail on breaking changes or route/doc mismatch. Use the same schemas as Zod when possible to avoid double sources of truth.

nodes.label: Phase 6 REST surface and API features
nodes.rationale: Product surface clients depend on. Node handed these topics to Express on purpose. Gate: cursor pagination, versioned mount, idempotent POST, OpenAPI matching handlers.

nodes.label: Inbound webhooks
nodes.rationale: Receive with raw body, HMAC (or provider scheme), timestamp replay window, persist event id for dedupe, then enqueue and respond quickly.

nodes.label: Outbound webhooks
