nodes.rationale: Fire-and-forget from the route is a bug under load. Express accepts the command and returns 202; Node Phase 7 jobs deliver.

nodes.label: express.raw on webhook path
nodes.rationale: Signature is over exact bytes, not re-serialized JSON. Need the raw body from Phase 3 express.raw.

nodes.label: HMAC with crypto.timingSafeEqual
nodes.rationale: Verify HMAC or provider scheme with a constant-time compare so signature checks do not leak via timing.

nodes.label: Webhook timestamp replay window
nodes.rationale: Reject old timestamps so a captured signed payload cannot be replayed later.

nodes.label: Webhook event id dedupe
nodes.rationale: Persist event id so the same delivery is processed at most once.

nodes.label: Phase 7 layering at the Express edge
nodes.rationale: Thin HTTP edge. Repository and transaction mechanism stay in Node Phase 6. Gate: short handlers, services unit-test without req/res, one slow side effect enqueued.

nodes.label: Controller service repository
nodes.rationale: Controllers translate HTTP. Services own rules. Repositories own queries. Driver types do not leak upward. Express owns where the HTTP layer stops.

nodes.label: Controller layer
nodes.rationale: Parse and validate input already on req, call the service, map status. Does not own SQL or business rules.

nodes.label: Service layer
nodes.rationale: Owns invariants and orchestration. No res.json and no Express types so services stay testable without spinning an HTTP server.

nodes.label: Repository layer
nodes.rationale: Queries and commands via drivers. Does not decide HTTP status. Node Phase 6 owns how repositories and transactions work.

nodes.label: Domain vs transport
nodes.rationale: Transport is HTTP. Domain is product language. Crossing them freely couples tests to Express. No Request types in domain.

nodes.label: DTO at the edge
nodes.rationale: Stable API shapes when persistence models change. Controller maps req.validated into the service and toUserDto on the way out.

nodes.label: req.validated
nodes.rationale: Parsed input attached by Zod middleware. Controllers pass it into services instead of raw req.body.

nodes.label: Fat controller
nodes.rationale: If a handler needs scrolling, logic leaked upward. Smells: SQL in the route, 200-line try/catch with five status codes, copy-pasted auth checks.

nodes.label: Thin handler pipeline
nodes.rationale: Auth middleware then validate middleware then thin handler then service. One use-case per handler. RBAC lives in route-level middleware or the service for multi-resource rules.

nodes.label: Router factory dependency injection
nodes.rationale: Pass dependencies into router factories. Do not import a global db singleton if you care about tests. Tests substitute fakes; boot order stays explicit.

nodes.label: usersRouter factory
nodes.rationale: usersRouter({userService}) builds an express.Router and delegates list to the injected service.

nodes.label: createApp(deps)
nodes.rationale: Phase 10 completes composition with createApp(deps).use('/users', usersRouter({userService})).

nodes.label: Enqueue side effects from routes
nodes.rationale: Validate, persist, enqueue, respond. Never await email, webhooks, or PDF generation on the request path. Use an outbox in the same transaction when needed (Node 7).

nodes.label: HTTP 202 Accepted for queued work
nodes.rationale: 202 means accepted for processing, not necessarily completed.

nodes.label: Transactional outbox from routes
nodes.rationale: orders.create(input) in a transaction with outbox when needed. Cross-link Node Phase 7 for outbox, retries, and worker shutdown.

nodes.label: Feature folders
nodes.rationale: orders/routes.ts plus orders/service.ts. Feature scales by domain. Teams pick one convention and stay consistent.

nodes.label: Layer folders
nodes.rationale: routes/, services/, repos/. Layer scales by role rather than by domain.

nodes.label: Map API DTOs at the edge
nodes.rationale: Map API DTOs at the edge so persistence models can change without shifting the public shape.

nodes.label: Transaction-per-request middleware
nodes.rationale: A thin Express wrapper; the transaction mechanism stays Node Phase 6.

nodes.label: Phase 8 validation and authorization at the edge
nodes.rationale: Passwords and JWT structure live in Node Phase 8. Here: middleware surface. Gate: missing token 401, wrong role 403, bad body 400; services never see raw req.body.

nodes.label: Validate at the HTTP boundary
nodes.rationale: Everything from the network is untrusted. Parse it before services run. The principle outlives Zod, Valibot, or hand parsers. Validating only in the database is late, worse errors, and injection risk.

nodes.label: validate middleware factory
nodes.rationale: validate({body, params, query}) returns middleware. Schemas are Understand-level library surface; the factory and boundary habit are Master.

nodes.label: Attach parsed data on req.validated
nodes.rationale: On success attach parsed data under a clear name on req, not mixed with the raw body.

nodes.label: VALIDATION_ERROR 400
nodes.rationale: On parse failure set statusCode 400 and code VALIDATION_ERROR, then next(err).

nodes.label: Query and params are strings
nodes.rationale: ?limit=20 is the string "20". z.number() without coerce fails; use z.coerce.number() deliberately.

nodes.label: Boolean("false") trap
nodes.rationale: ?active=false is the string "false", which is truthy. Non-empty strings are truthy in JavaScript. Use explicit enums or coerce helpers.

nodes.label: requireAuth middleware
nodes.rationale: Parse session or Bearer JWT, attach req.user, else 401. Does not re-teach argon2 or JWT structure — Node Phase 8.

nodes.label: req.user principal
nodes.rationale: Authn middleware puts the authenticated principal on req, not permissions alone.

nodes.label: 401 UNAUTHENTICATED
nodes.rationale: No resolvable user from session or token. Identity is missing.

nodes.label: cookie-parser before session
nodes.rationale: Session libraries read cookies from the parsed object, so cookie-parser must mount first.

nodes.label: res.cookie flags
nodes.rationale: httpOnly, secure, sameSite — Phase 4. Express mounts cookie/session middleware and sets flags. Sessions vs JWT is Node Phase 8.

nodes.label: connect-redis session store
nodes.rationale: Session store is integration only. Redis syllabus owns Redis.

nodes.label: requireRole middleware
nodes.rationale: Role checks after authentication. Fail closed with 403, not 401. Missing req.user is still 401.

nodes.label: 403 FORBIDDEN
nodes.rationale: 403 when identity is known but the role is not allowed. 401 when identity is missing.

nodes.label: Resource ownership
nodes.rationale: Load the resource, compare owner id to req.user.id. Prefer 404 when existence should stay secret; 403 when the resource is visible but forbidden. Document the choice.

nodes.label: 404 to hide private resource existence
nodes.rationale: 404 instead of 403 for another user's private doc avoids leaking that the id exists.

nodes.label: tenantId from identity
nodes.rationale: Force tenantId from identity, never from raw body alone. Client-supplied tenantId enables tenant hopping / IDOR.

nodes.label: Tenant hopping IDOR
nodes.rationale: Trusting a client-supplied tenantId lets a caller hop tenants.

nodes.label: Logout cookie clear and revocation
nodes.rationale: Logout clears cookies or hits revocation. Storage is Node/Redis.

nodes.label: Optional auth middleware
nodes.rationale: Enriches req.user when a token is present but does not 401 when absent. Useful for public plus personalized routes.

nodes.label: trust proxy
nodes.rationale: app.set('trust proxy', 1) for one hop of reverse proxy you control. Never set true on an open internet edge without understanding spoofed X-Forwarded-For.

nodes.label: req.ip behind a proxy
nodes.rationale: Without trust proxy, req.ip is the load balancer. Rate limits and secure cookies misbehave. All traffic appears as one IP and rate limiting bans everyone.

nodes.label: X-Forwarded-For spoofing
nodes.rationale: trust proxy true on an open edge trusts client-supplied forwarded headers. Nginx syllabus covers termination in depth.

nodes.label: CORS in Express
nodes.rationale: Browsers enforce CORS, not servers alone. cors({origin: allow-list, credentials: true}).

nodes.label: Credentials cannot use wildcard origin
nodes.rationale: Browsers forbid credentialed requests with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *. Credentials and wildcard origins do not mix.

nodes.label: Dynamic origin reflection allow-list
nodes.rationale: Reflecting any Origin with credentials is a bug. Dynamic origin reflection must allow-list.

nodes.label: Helmet
nodes.rationale: Helmet mounts secure default headers. Addresses common missing security headers, not auth or injection by itself. Not a full security program.

nodes.label: CSP for HTML vs JSON APIs
nodes.rationale: CSP matters more for HTML apps than pure JSON APIs. APIs may disable noisy browser-only policies; still review each toggle.

nodes.label: express-rate-limit
nodes.rationale: Limit by IP or user. Keys must use the real client IP via trust proxy. standardHeaders true, legacyHeaders false.

nodes.label: Skip liveness probes in rate limits
nodes.rationale: skip when req.path === '/health' so probes do not consume the window.

nodes.label: Stricter login rate limits
nodes.rationale: Brute-force protection on /login is tighter than global API limits and sits on the auth routes.

nodes.label: CSRF on cookie session APIs
nodes.rationale: CSRF is a concern for a JSON API only when auth relies on cookies the browser sends automatically cross-site.

nodes.label: Bearer tokens skip CSRF
nodes.rationale: Authorization Bearer tokens are not sent automatically by the browser, so classic CSRF does not apply.

nodes.label: csurf is archived
nodes.rationale: Do not teach csurf as current; prefer double-submit cookie, SameSite, and Node Phase 8 guidance.

nodes.label: Open redirect via res.redirect
nodes.rationale: Never res.redirect(userInput) unchecked; allow-list relative paths. Cross-link Node SSRF and open-redirect pages.

nodes.label: Timeouts and secrets at the edge
Request timeout soft deadline
nodes.rationale: Timeout middleware is a soft deadline at the Express edge; deep budgets stay in Node Phase 7.

nodes.label: Fail boot if required env missing
nodes.rationale: Validate env at boot, not on first request, so the process fails fast before taking traffic. Node 12-factor.

nodes.label: Validated config module
nodes.rationale: Edge code only reads process.env via a validated config module.

nodes.label: trust proxy
nodes.rationale: Behind a proxy, trust proxy is what makes req.ip the real client IP.

nodes.label: Phase 9 gate
nodes.rationale: Behind a proxy req.ip is correct; CORS allows the SPA with credentials; rate limits key properly.

nodes.label: Node vs Express technology boundaries
nodes.rationale: Async, streams, logging, retries stay in Node; drivers/models stay in DB syllabi; Redis owns cache/queues; Nginx/Docker own TLS and containers. Express owns middleware mounts and trust proxy.

nodes.label: 38 sections to 3 parts 9 phases
nodes.rationale: Early 2026-08-10 consolidation of a fragmented 38-section draft; later superseded by the 4-part 11-phase inventory.

nodes.label: Master tier share about 28 percent
nodes.rationale: Demote JSON parse failures, custom errors, templates, complex Multer, advanced CORS so Master stays on routing, middleware lifecycle, Zod basics, Helmet and rate-limit.

nodes.label: Approve proposed Express structure
nodes.rationale: 108 topics, 28 Master (26%), 4 parts under the 300-line cap; additions only, nothing removed.

nodes.label: Express 5 path-to-regexp break
nodes.rationale: app.get('*') and :id? throw on Express 5.2.1; SPA history fallback must use /*splat.

nodes.label: query parser default simple
nodes.rationale: Express 5 default is simple not extended; nested a[b]=1 becomes a literal key; proto pollution vector is off by default.

nodes.label: Cookie read write asymmetry
nodes.rationale: res.cookie is built in; req.cookies needs cookie-parser. Without it cookies are undefined.

nodes.label: Request-id correlation middleware
nodes.rationale: Mint or accept X-Request-Id on req and carry it with AsyncLocalStorage; mechanism is Node Phase 10, mount is Express.

nodes.label: Validate at boundary is Master
nodes.rationale: The habit outlives Zod; flip Zod schemas to Understand and promote the HTTP-boundary principle to Master.

nodes.label: Hold Express 8-10 until Node 8
nodes.rationale: Preferred sequencing: write Express 0-7 now (Node Phase 5 only); hold 8-10 until Node Phase 8 validation and headers exist.

nodes.label: Half the syllabus is HTTP API design
nodes.rationale: Node refused REST modeling, pagination, versioning, idempotency and ETags; they live on Express because the framework shapes the routes.

nodes.label: Quality cliff after Phase 3
nodes.rationale: 29 finished pages in Phases 0-3; Phases 6-10 are accurate outlines. Quality degrades monotonically, not bimodally.

nodes.label: Express does not enforce If-Match
nodes.rationale: Stale If-Match is ignored; Express generates ETags but never enforces preconditions. Lost-update protection is application code (412/428).

nodes.label: trust proxy true spoofs req.ip
nodes.rationale: trust proxy: true takes the leftmost X-Forwarded-For hop, which the client sent. Combined with IP-keyed rate limits this is a bypass.

nodes.label: fetch cannot verify 304
nodes.rationale: Sending If-None-Match through fetch returns 200 with a body; the same request via node:http returns 304 empty. Use node:http or curl.

nodes.label: pagesPlanned bookkeeping
nodes.rationale: progress.js recorded pages with no pagesPlanned so the UI treated 78 short pages as finished. First recommended pass is visibility, not rewrite.

nodes.label: 114 Express topics 28 Master
nodes.rationale: After Claude's six additive rows and one tier flip: 114 topics, Master 25%, about 90 explanation pages.

nodes.label: Concept to Node middleware to Express
nodes.rationale: Concept lives in Node or DB/Redis/Docker/Nginx. Middleware, route surface, and HTTP contracts live in Express.

nodes.label: Express over node:http
nodes.rationale: Express is a routing and middleware layer on http.Server, not a language and not an application architecture.

nodes.label: Middleware contract
nodes.rationale: next() vs next(err) vs never calling next: hang, double-send, or silent drop. Order is load-bearing.

nodes.label: Body parsers and size limits
nodes.rationale: express.json and urlencoded with hard size limits are a DoS control; empty-body and malformed JSON have their own error path.

nodes.label: SPA history fallback /*splat
nodes.rationale: express.static plus history fallback; app.get('*') throws on Express 5.

nodes.label: Express 5 async error forwarding
nodes.rationale: Rejected promises from async handlers forward to next(err) automatically.

nodes.label: Controller service repository wiring
nodes.rationale: Controllers parse HTTP and call services; services own rules; repositories own queries. Mechanism stays in Node.

nodes.label: Validate at the HTTP boundary
nodes.rationale: Untrusted input never reaches services raw; the habit outlives any schema library. Master row.

nodes.label: createApp factory
nodes.rationale: Pure function returns app; no listen inside; inject db/redis/queue clients so tests import the factory.

nodes.label: trust proxy Master row
nodes.rationale: Correct client IP and protocol behind Nginx; rate limits and secure cookies fail without it.

nodes.label: Git is a content-addressed object store
nodes.rationale: Not a diff engine or a timeline: a key-value database keyed by content hash plus refs that name entry points.

nodes.label: Default initial branch still master
nodes.rationale: git init on 2.55.0 still defaults to master; the hint says the default will change to main in Git 3.0.

nodes.label: Git syllabus stops at push
nodes.rationale: If it still applies when every framework is deleted, it is Git's. CI and deploy start in Node Phase 11.

nodes.label: Phase 0 How Git stores things complete
Object name is SHA of header plus content
nodes.rationale: blob 6\0hello\n hashed with sha1sum reproduces ce013625…; filename is not part of the name, so identical files share one object.

nodes.label: Refs are names pointing at hashes
nodes.rationale: A branch is a 41-byte file; creating one copies no objects. Deleting a branch does not delete commits.

nodes.label: History is immutable and cumulative
nodes.rationale: A committed secret is an incident: later deletes do not remove the blob. Large blobs make every clone heavier forever.

nodes.label: A commit is a snapshot not a diff
Snapshot model
nodes.rationale: Every commit names a complete tree. Diffs are derived. Unchanged files reuse existing blobs so snapshots are cheap.

nodes.label: Packfile delta compression
nodes.rationale: Deltas are a packfile storage layer. No command's behaviour depends on them; 51 loose objects packed to 6.03 KiB on git 2.55.0.

nodes.label: Blob
nodes.rationale: File bytes only: no name, path, mode, or timestamp. The filename lives in the tree.

nodes.label: Tree
nodes.rationale: Sorted listing of mode, type, hash, name. Empty directories cannot be committed because they produce no entries.

nodes.label: Lightweight tag
nodes.rationale: A file in refs/tags containing a hash; creates no object. Releases should use annotated tags.

nodes.label: Tree modes 100644 100755 120000 040000 160000
nodes.rationale: Git records the executable bit and symlink-versus-file only. Owner, group, and other permissions are lost.

nodes.label: AM status short
nodes.rationale: A is index versus HEAD added; M is working tree versus index modified. Commit would record the earlier staged content.

nodes.label: reset soft mixed hard
nodes.rationale: All three move HEAD. mixed also resets the index. hard also overwrites the working tree and is the only variant that can destroy uncommitted work.

nodes.label: The index is a real file
.git/index binary file
nodes.rationale: Staged is not a flag. git add writes a blob then records mode, hash, stage, path. Staging is a copy, not a bookmark.

nodes.label: Index merge stages 0 1 2 3
nodes.rationale: Stage 0 is normal. During a conflict a path holds 1 base, 2 ours, 3 theirs. UU means those three exist and no stage 0.

nodes.label: Cached stat data
nodes.rationale: status skips re-hash when size and mtime match. Network or Windows shares that lie about modes make every file look modified.

nodes.label: git add -p
nodes.rationale: The index can hold a blob that exists in neither HEAD nor the working tree, so hunks can be staged independently.

nodes.label: Git ref
nodes.rationale: A ref is a file containing a hash. Namespaces: refs/heads, refs/tags, refs/remotes, refs/stash. Inspectable as text, but a bad hash write is not prevented.

nodes.label: Branch is a moving ref
nodes.rationale: A branch is a ref under refs/heads that advances on commit. Creating one writes 41 bytes and no objects; deleting one deletes no commits.

nodes.label: Detached HEAD
nodes.rationale: Legitimate for inspecting a commit or building a tag. Commits made there are abandoned on switch-away unless you branch first; recovery is via reflog.

nodes.label: Branching is a 41-byte file write
nodes.rationale: git branch writes 41 bytes; object count is unchanged. Delete-the-branch is recoverable because objects stay reachable via the reflog.

nodes.label: git update-ref
nodes.rationale: Prefer update-ref over editing ref files: it writes the reflog entry recovery depends on.

nodes.label: The commit graph is a DAG
Commit DAG
nodes.rationale: Directed because parents point one way; acyclic because a commit hash includes its parents; a graph because merges have multiple parents.

nodes.label: Commit dates are metadata not structure
nodes.rationale: A commit dated 2030 can sit under one dated 2026. Never build logic on dates; use ancestry via merge-base --is-ancestor.

nodes.label: Rebase versus merge trade-off
nodes.rationale: A DAG records parallel work honestly. Rebase flattens for readability by rewriting what happened; merge keeps truth at the cost of a harder history.

nodes.label: Five config scopes
nodes.rationale: system → global → local → worktree → -c. Last wins; nothing merges for a single-valued key.

nodes.label: Unset config uses built-in defaults
nodes.rationale: On 2.55.0 unset init.defaultBranch is master, not main. Unset pull.rebase makes a divergent pull fail rather than guess.

nodes.label: Token in remote URL
nodes.rationale: .git/config is plaintext; an embedded credential is easy to leak when sharing a repo or image.

nodes.label: .git directory
nodes.rationale: The whole repository is one directory. Copy it and you copy history; delete it and the working tree becomes untracked files.

nodes.label: .git/logs reflog
nodes.rationale: Enabled by logallrefupdates=true. Local, not pushed; expires 90 days reachable / 30 unreachable.

nodes.label: One directory removes safety rails
nodes.rationale: Portable, inspectable, offline — and rm -rf .git is irreversible. Mitigations are social: push often.

nodes.label: Author identity required to commit
nodes.rationale: Author and committer are fields inside the commit object, so there is nothing to hash without them. Hard failure, not a warning.

nodes.label: Identity is asserted not authenticated
nodes.rationale: user.email is free text. Audit value is the host's push auth; cryptographic proof needs signed commits.

nodes.label: Delta compression
nodes.rationale: Deltas are chosen by similarity across the repository, not by commit adjacency. Hashes are over content, never the stored form.

nodes.label: Cruft pack
nodes.rationale: gc parks unreachable objects with mtimes for a two-week grace period. Why rewritten repos do not shrink immediately.

nodes.label: Packing is below the object model
nodes.rationale: 'Git stores diffs' is false of the model and true of bytes on disk. cat-file still returns whole objects.

nodes.label: Git is not a deployment tool
Git is not a place for secrets
Git is not a large-file store
Permanent history is the feature and the trap
nodes.rationale: Nothing is lost, every clone is complete — which is why a committed secret is an incident and a committed binary is permanent weight.

nodes.label: SHA-1 and SHA-256 do not interoperate
nodes.rationale: No in-place conversion; hosts and tooling assume 40-character hashes. Cryptography is better; ecosystem cost is prohibitive.

nodes.label: Object hash framing
nodes.rationale: Git hashes type, space, length, NUL, then content. A generic SHA-1 collision is not directly usable as a Git object swap.

nodes.label: Never parse porcelain output
nodes.rationale: Porcelain output may change between versions and is affected by aliases and config. Scripts use plumbing or status --porcelain.

nodes.label: Syllabus Phase 0 — How Git stores things
Part 3 — Git in a real project
Syllabus Phase 12 — When Git goes wrong
Event loop split language vs Node
nodes.rationale: Job queue, microtasks and promise resolution live in JS Phase 7. libuv phases, setImmediate and process.nextTick belong to Node Phase 2.

nodes.label: Network split at the wire
nodes.rationale: fetch, AbortController, FormData and console CORS failures are JS Phase 11. Status-code design and server headers belong to Express.

nodes.label: 300-line cap is file size not content budget
nodes.rationale: Write the explanation first, then split on a concept boundary. A Master topic may run 900–1400 lines across chunks.

nodes.label: The engine, the runtime and the spec
ECMA-262 spec
nodes.rationale: The spec has no I/O. A conforming engine can compute a value but cannot show it.

nodes.label: JavaScript host
nodes.rationale: A language feature works everywhere the engine is new enough. A host feature works only where that host provides it.

nodes.label: Hoisting
nodes.rationale: Not code moving. Bindings are registered in the compile pass; values arrive in execute.

nodes.label: Temporal dead zone
nodes.rationale: A TDZ binding exists but has no value. typeof on it throws; typeof on a never-declared name returns undefined.

nodes.label: Execution contexts and the call stack
Stack limit is bytes not calls
nodes.rationale: Measured 12524 frames with no locals versus 5442 with six args plus an array local on Node 24.

nodes.label: V8 does not implement tail-call optimisation
await tears down the stack frame
Strict mode rules
nodes.rationale: Turns silent sloppy failures into errors. ES modules and class bodies are strict always.

nodes.label: this is undefined in a strict plain call
nodes.rationale: undefined this fails at the mistake. sloppy this === globalThis silently corrupts globals.

nodes.label: TC39 stage process
nodes.rationale: Stage 3 is when engines ship and risk remains. Stage 4 is two implementations plus tests. Never build on Stage 2 or below.

nodes.label: Engines implement proposals not editions
nodes.rationale: The useful question is the runtime floor, not ES6. Editions are yearly snapshots of already-finished proposals.

nodes.label: Capability detection
nodes.rationale: Test the capability with a real operation. Safari private mode defines localStorage then throws on setItem.

nodes.label: Phase 0 How JavaScript runs
nodes.rationale: The engine reads the whole file before it runs any of it; hoisting and SyntaxError-on-line-90 follow from that.

nodes.label: script defer
nodes.rationale: Downloads in parallel, runs after HTML is parsed, in document order. Safe default for classic scripts; DOM is complete so no DOMContentLoaded wrapper is needed.

nodes.label: script async
nodes.rationale: Runs the moment it arrives; no order between async scripts. Only for independent third-party code.

nodes.label: script type=module
nodes.rationale: Deferred automatically and strict; the whole import graph must be fetched and parsed before execute, so deferral is a consequence of modules.

nodes.label: Module request waterfall
nodes.rationale: The graph is discovered one level at a time. modulepreload or bundling flattens it; this is why bundlers remain standard despite native ESM.

nodes.label: nomodule two-bundle pattern
nodes.rationale: Module-aware browsers ignore nomodule; older ones ignore type=module. Exactly one of the pair runs. Mostly historical in 2026.

nodes.label: Console API beyond log
nodes.rationale: table, dir({depth:null}), group, time, count, assert, error/warn (stderr). Node log truncates nested objects at depth 2.

nodes.label: node --check
nodes.rationale: Parses and reports SyntaxErrors with no execution and no side effects.

nodes.label: node --inspect-brk
nodes.rationale: Breaks on the first line so breakpoints can be set before anything runs. debugger; is a no-op unless a debugger is attached.

nodes.label: DevTools lazy object expansion
nodes.rationale: A logged object is expanded later by reference. structuredClone at log time captures the instant.

nodes.label: Transpiler
nodes.rationale: Rewrites syntax at build time so an older parser can read it. Syntax fails at parse time and takes the whole file down.

nodes.label: Polyfill
nodes.rationale: Adds a missing API at runtime. A missing method fails at call time on one interaction. Patches the global.

nodes.label: Ponyfill
nodes.rationale: Exports the implementation instead of patching the global. Prefer in libraries; reserve true polyfills for an app entry you control.

nodes.label: browserslist
nodes.rationale: Single control for Babel and bundlers. Stale IE11 targets force ES5 plus a large core-js for everyone.

nodes.label: useBuiltIns usage
nodes.rationale: Babel injects only the core-js polyfills the source actually references for the browserslist targets. entry pulls a fixed block.

nodes.label: Unpolyfillable engine features
nodes.rationale: Proxy, WeakRef, BigInt and real #private fields need engine capabilities that cannot be reconstructed in JavaScript.

nodes.label: Feature detection
nodes.rationale: Test the capability, never the browser or environment. Use typeof so an undeclared name does not throw.

nodes.label: navigator exists in Node 21+
nodes.rationale: typeof navigator !== 'undefined' is true on Node 21+, so SSR hydrates as if it were a browser. Probe document or the specific API.

nodes.label: localStorage write probe
nodes.rationale: Safari private mode defines localStorage then throws QuotaExceededError on every write. Existence is not usability.

nodes.label: Progressive enhancement
nodes.rationale: Ship a version that works everywhere, then add capability-gated improvements. A Load more button beats a dead page.

nodes.label: User-agent sniffing
nodes.rationale: The UA string is a compatibility fiction. Acceptable only for a documented engine bug with a removal condition, store links, or analytics.

nodes.label: V8 compilation tiers
nodes.rationale: Ignition interprets bytecode; Sparkplug is a fast baseline; Maglev mid-tier; TurboFan fully optimises hot type-stable functions.

nodes.label: Deoptimisation
nodes.rationale: Optimised code is discarded when a later call violates observed types. Measured: add(a,b) lost optimisation after strings and objects.

nodes.label: Keep data shapes stable
nodes.rationale: Do not tune for the JIT. Normalise payloads at the boundary so functions see consistent types and objects share keys in the same order.

nodes.label: Cold versus warm micro-benchmark
nodes.rationale: Same function, same input: cold 0.21ms vs warm 0.0074ms, about 28x. Single-shot timings measure compilation state.

nodes.label: ECMA-262 living standard
nodes.rationale: Read tc39.es/ecma262, not a numbered-edition PDF. Host APIs like fetch and document live in WHATWG, not ECMA-262.

nodes.label: Abstract operations
nodes.rationale: Internal non-callable algorithms in SmallCaps — ToPrimitive, ToNumber, Get — reused so every operator shares one set of rules.

nodes.label: ToPrimitive
nodes.rationale: Hint string tries toString then valueOf; number and default try valueOf then toString. Symbol.toPrimitive overrides. + uses default; templates use string; arithmetic uses number.

nodes.label: Array sort default string compare
nodes.rationale: [10,9,1].sort() is [1,10,9] because SortCompare converts to strings. Specified, not a quirk.

nodes.label: Date Symbol.toPrimitive default-as-string
nodes.rationale: Date overrides default hint to behave as string, so date + '' is a date string while date * 1 is a timestamp.

nodes.label: JavaScript eight types
nodes.rationale: Seven primitives plus object. Arrays, dates, regexes, Map and class instances are objects. typeof function is a convenience, not a ninth type.

nodes.label: typeof null === object
nodes.rationale: Historic type-tag bug: objects used tag 000 and null was the all-zero pointer. A fix was rejected. Detect null with v === null.

nodes.label: Array.isArray
nodes.rationale: instanceof Array fails across realms because each iframe or vm has its own Array constructor.

nodes.label: Primitive versus object
nodes.rationale: Primitives copy on assignment, compare by value, and are immutable. Objects share by reference, compare by identity, and are mutable.

nodes.label: Primitives copied objects shared
nodes.rationale: Always pass-by-value; for objects the value is a reference. A function can mutate the referent but cannot rebind the caller's name.

nodes.label: Shallow copy
nodes.rationale: Spread and Object.assign copy one level. Nested arrays stay shared; pushing to shallow.items mutates cart.items.

nodes.label: structuredClone
nodes.rationale: Default deep copy: handles cycles, Map, Set, Date. Throws DataCloneError on functions and DOM nodes. JSON round-trip mangles those plus undefined, Symbol, NaN.

nodes.label: Structural sharing
nodes.rationale: React change detection is a reference compare. Return new objects along the changed path; leave untouched branches shared so updates stay cheap.

nodes.label: == versus ===
nodes.rationale: === never converts. == converts: null/undefined only to each other; string to number; boolean to number first; object via ToPrimitive.

nodes.label: Four equality algorithms
nodes.rationale: == and === treat NaN unequal and 0 equal to -0. SameValueZero (includes, Map/Set) treats NaN equal. SameValue (Object.is) also distinguishes -0.

nodes.label: null == undefined only
nodes.rationale: The one defensible == use: value == null tests null or undefined and nothing else. eqeqeq smart permits it.

nodes.label: null >= 0 is true
nodes.rationale: Relational operators ToNumber both sides; Number(null) is 0. == never numeric-compares null. A null stock silently passes >= 0.

nodes.label: Eight falsy values
nodes.rationale: false, 0, -0, 0n, '', null, undefined, NaN. Everything else is truthy including '0', 'false', [], {}, and new Boolean(false).

nodes.label: ToBoolean
nodes.rationale: if (x) uses ToBoolean and never converts an object to a primitive. [] is truthy while [] == false is true because equality does convert.

nodes.label: Empty objects are truthy
nodes.rationale: Check array.length, Object.keys(obj).length, or map.size. if (items) is always true even for [].

nodes.label: null versus undefined
nodes.rationale: undefined is absence the engine produced; null is absence you chose. Prefer undefined by omission; use null to signal cleared in a payload.

nodes.label: Defaults fire only on undefined
nodes.rationale: f(undefined) and f() get the default; f(null) and f(0) do not. Same rule for destructuring, so API null bypasses defaults.

nodes.label: Nullish coalescing ??
nodes.rationale: ?? falls back only on null and undefined. || falls back on every falsy value including 0, '', false, and NaN. Mixing ?? with || or && is a SyntaxError without parens. NaN ?? 1 is NaN.

nodes.label: JSON.stringify drops undefined
nodes.rationale: undefined omits the field; null keeps it. In a PATCH, that is leave-alone versus set-to-empty.

nodes.label: Numbers are IEEE-754 doubles
nodes.rationale: One numeric type. 0.1 + 0.2 is 0.30000000000000004 because 0.1 is a repeating binary fraction. Not JS-specific.

nodes.label: Money as integer minor units
nodes.rationale: Store paise or cents. Arithmetic in integers. Round once explicitly. Divide by 100 only when formatting with Intl.NumberFormat.

nodes.label: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER
nodes.rationale: 2^53-1 = 9007199254740991. Beyond it distinct integers collapse: MSI+1 === MSI+2.

nodes.label: JSON.parse corrupts large integer IDs
nodes.rationale: JSON.parse turns numbers into doubles. Send IDs as strings, or recover digits via the reviver ctx.source and BigInt.

nodes.label: toFixed is not a rounding function
nodes.rationale: (1.005).toFixed(2) is '1.00' because 1.005 is stored slightly low. It also returns a string.

nodes.label: const protects the binding
nodes.rationale: const cart = {}; cart.qty = 1 is legal; cart = {} throws TypeError. The name never points at something else.

nodes.label: Object.freeze is shallow
nodes.rationale: Blocks add/remove/change of own properties one level deep. Nested writes still work. Throws in strict, silent in sloppy. Deep freeze needs an isFrozen cycle guard.

nodes.label: const let var
nodes.rationale: const and let are block-scoped with TDZ. var is function-scoped and initialises undefined. for-of creates a fresh binding so const is correct there.

nodes.label: ToPrimitive coercion
nodes.rationale: Hint string: toString then valueOf. number/default: valueOf then toString. Symbol.toPrimitive overrides.

nodes.label: ToNumber
nodes.rationale: null becomes 0; undefined becomes NaN. A null price silently becomes free; a missing value becomes NaN and poisons later arithmetic.

nodes.label: + concatenates if either side is a string
nodes.rationale: After ToPrimitive, if either operand is a string, + concatenates. Every other arithmetic operator ToNumbers both. Form values are always strings.

nodes.label: {} + [] statement parse
nodes.rationale: As a statement {} is an empty block, leaving unary +[] which is ToNumber('') = 0. In expression position it is concatenation.

nodes.label: Number versus parseInt
nodes.rationale: Number demands the whole string; Number('42px') is NaN. parseInt reads a prefix. Number('') is 0; parseInt('') is NaN. Use Number plus Number.isFinite.

nodes.label: map(parseInt) radix trap
nodes.rationale: map passes (value, index); index becomes radix so ['1','2','3'].map(parseInt) is [1, NaN, NaN]. Always pass radix 10.

nodes.label: Convert at the boundary
nodes.rationale: Form fields, query params, localStorage, dataset and env vars are always strings. Parse and validate once on the way in. Apply ?? before Number because Number(null) is 0.

nodes.label: Strings are UTF-16 code units
nodes.rationale: .length, charAt and slice count 16-bit units. Code points above U+FFFF are surrogate pairs. slice(0,1) on an emoji can yield a lone \ud83d.

nodes.label: Intl.Segmenter graphemes
nodes.rationale: 👨‍👩‍👧 is 8 code units, 5 code points, 1 grapheme. Truncate and reverse at grapheme level. Word granularity is locale-aware.

nodes.label: Unicode NFC versus NFD
nodes.rationale: é can be U+00E9 or e plus combining acute. They render the same and are not ===. Normalise NFC at the boundary. Sort with Intl.Collator, not default sort.

nodes.label: NaN !== NaN
nodes.rationale: IEEE-754: two failed computations are not the same value. Only JS value not equal to itself. Propagates silently through later arithmetic.

nodes.label: Number.isNaN versus isNaN
nodes.rationale: Global isNaN coerces first so isNaN('abc') is true. Number.isNaN is true only for the NaN value. Prefer Number.isFinite to also reject Infinity.

nodes.label: includes versus indexOf for NaN
nodes.rationale: indexOf uses === so [NaN].indexOf(NaN) is -1. includes and Map/Set keys use SameValueZero so NaN is found and deduped.

nodes.label: Symbol unique property key
nodes.rationale: Symbol('id') === Symbol('id') is false. Hidden from keys/for-in/JSON.stringify but copied by spread and Object.assign. Not privacy.

nodes.label: Symbol.for global registry
nodes.rationale: Process-wide lookup so independent modules share one symbol. Plain Symbol() is always unique.

nodes.label: Well-known symbols
nodes.rationale: Symbol.iterator drives for-of and spread. Also asyncIterator, toPrimitive, toStringTag, hasInstance.

nodes.label: Symbol implicit string coercion throws
nodes.rationale: '' + sym and template interpolation throw. String(sym) and toString work. Silent stringify would defeat uniqueness.

nodes.label: BigInt
nodes.rationale: Arbitrary-precision integers past 2^53-1. Create from a string for large values; a number literal is already rounded. Division truncates.

nodes.label: Cannot mix BigInt and Number
nodes.rationale: 1n + 1 throws TypeError. Comparison is allowed: 1n == 1 is true, 1n === 1 is false. Mixing would silently lose precision.

nodes.label: JSON.stringify throws on BigInt
nodes.rationale: JSON has no BigInt type. Use a replacer to string; do not patch BigInt.prototype.toJSON.

nodes.label: JSON.stringify equality trap
nodes.rationale: Key order changes the string; undefined is dropped; Date becomes ISO; Map/Set become {}; NaN and Infinity become null. Throws on cycles.

nodes.label: Shallow equality
nodes.rationale: Same key set, each value compared with Object.is. What React uses for props and deps because immutable updates give changed branches new references.

nodes.label: Deep equality
nodes.rationale: Recurse with Date/RegExp/Map/Set and prototype checks. Track visited pairs for cycles. Prefer ETag or updatedAt over comparing API bodies.

nodes.label: Autoboxing
nodes.rationale: Property access on a primitive wraps it, reads the method from String/Number/Boolean.prototype, then discards the wrapper. Assignments do not persist.

nodes.label: Wrapper constructors
nodes.rationale: new String/Number/Boolean produce objects. typeof is object; === fails; new Boolean(false) is truthy. Called without new they convert to primitives.

nodes.label: Number literal method-dot trap
nodes.rationale: 5.toFixed(2) is a SyntaxError because 5. starts a decimal. Write (5).toFixed(2).

nodes.label: Object.is (SameValue)
nodes.rationale: Fourth equality algorithm: === with NaN and -0 fixed. Use inside comparison helpers (React, shallowEqual) so NaN fields do not retrigger; keep === for everyday code.

nodes.label: SameValueZero
nodes.rationale: NaN equals NaN; 0 equals -0. Used by includes and Map/Set keys.

nodes.label: Strict equality ===
nodes.rationale: NaN not equal to itself; 0 equals -0. Used by ===, indexOf, and switch.

nodes.label: Loose equality ==
nodes.rationale: Same NaN/-0 outcomes as === in this table; used only by ==.

nodes.label: Signed zero -0
nodes.rationale: IEEE-754 signed zero from underflow, 0*-1, -1/Infinity, Math.round(-0.2). Invisible to ===, includes, String, JSON.stringify. Detect with Object.is(x,-0) or 1/x===-Infinity. Matters for atan2 and Object.is deep-equal.

nodes.label: Infinity and -Infinity
nodes.rationale: Division by zero does not throw. Propagates silently. JSON.stringify turns Infinity and NaN into null.

nodes.label: Number.isFinite validation
nodes.rationale: Rejects NaN and both infinities. Number.isNaN(Infinity) is false so overflow passes a NaN-only check.

nodes.label: Math.max empty identity
nodes.rationale: Math.max() and Math.max(...[]) return -Infinity, the identity for max — not 0 and not an error.

nodes.label: Literal bases are notation only
nodes.rationale: 0b, 0o, 0x, decimal, and exponent forms all produce number. Only the n suffix changes the type to bigint.

nodes.label: Numeric separators
nodes.rationale: Underscores ignored by the parser. Illegal leading, trailing, doubled, or next to the decimal. _1000 is a ReferenceError (identifier), not SyntaxError.

nodes.label: Octal file-mode literal 0o755
nodes.rationale: 0o755 is decimal 493. chmod(path, 755) silently sets wrong permissions. Legacy 0755 is SyntaxError in strict/modules.

nodes.label: Number vs parseInt prefixes
nodes.rationale: Number understands 0x, 0o, 0b. parseInt honours 0x but parseInt('0o755') and parseInt('0b1010') are 0. Always pass radix 10.

nodes.label: Literal rounding above MAX_SAFE_INTEGER
nodes.rationale: Any-base literals above 2^53-1 are rounded at parse time. Use BigInt literals such as 0xffffffffffffffffn.

nodes.label: Phase 1 — Values, types and coercion
nodes.rationale: Seventeen topics. Disproportionate bugs come from references vs copies, coercion, and floating point (cart totals).

nodes.label: Phase 1 gate
nodes.rationale: Predict []==false, ''==0, null==undefined from the algorithm, and never store a cart total as 19.99.

nodes.label: Remainder % not modulo
nodes.rationale: Result takes the sign of the dividend (C). -7%3 is -1. Breaks wrap-around indices going backwards.

nodes.label: True modulo idiom
nodes.rationale: ((a%b)+b)%b is always non-negative for a positive divisor. Measured ((-7%3)+3)%3 is 2.

nodes.label: Exponentiation ** right-associative
nodes.rationale: Only right-associative arithmetic operator. 2**3**2 is 512. Replaces Math.pow.

nodes.label: -2 ** 2 SyntaxError
nodes.rationale: Committee refused to pick between -(2**2)=-4 and (-2)**2=4. Grammar requires parentheses.

nodes.label: Overloaded + concatenation
nodes.rationale: If either operand is a string after ToPrimitive, + concatenates. Other arithmetic operators coerce to number. Unary + throws on BigInt.

nodes.label: No integer division
nodes.rationale: / always yields a double. trunc vs floor differ on negatives (-3 vs -4 for -7/2). Page count is Math.ceil(total/perPage).

nodes.label: Prefix vs postfix increment
nodes.rationale: Postfix returns before mutate; prefix after. Use as statements or in for headers, never nested.

nodes.label: Logical assignment skips the write
nodes.rationale: a||=b is a&&(a=b) with assignment inside the short-circuit. Setters, proxies, Vue/MobX, and frozen objects see zero writes when the condition fails.

nodes.label: Nullish assignment ??=
nodes.rationale: Fills only null/undefined. ||= overwrites 0, '', false. Idiom: (byCategory[k]??=[]).push(item).

nodes.label: Assignment is an expression
nodes.rationale: Associates right to left. Why a=b=5 works and if(x=5) assigns then tests truthiness.

nodes.label: Destructuring assignment parentheses
nodes.rationale: ({x,y}=obj) needs parens because a leading { starts a block. Array destructuring needs none.

nodes.label: += inherits + overloading
nodes.rationale: One string operand turns an accumulator into text. Classic reduce bug when the seed is ''.

nodes.label: Logical operators return operands
nodes.rationale: 'a'&&'b' is 'b'; 0&&'b' is 0. Only ! returns a boolean. Cannot be replaced by a function because that would evaluate both arguments.

nodes.label: Short-circuit evaluation
nodes.rationale: Right side is not evaluated when the left decides. Guards expensive or unsafe calls.

nodes.label: ?? cannot mix with && or ||
nodes.rationale: Unparenthesised mix is SyntaxError, same philosophy as -2**2. (a??b)||c and a??(b||c) can differ.

nodes.label: ?? default-value idiom
nodes.rationale: Default to ??. || replaces legitimate 0, '', false. 0??'f' is 0.

nodes.label: JSX {count && <X/>} zero trap
nodes.rationale: 0&&anything is 0 and React renders 0 as text. Force a boolean: count>0&&….

nodes.label: Optional chaining ?.
nodes.rationale: Short-circuits the chain to undefined when the left is null or undefined. Forms: obj?.prop, obj?.[expr], fn?.().

nodes.label: ?. short-circuits the entire chain
nodes.rationale: empty?.a?.[side()] does not call side(). Parentheses end the chain: (u?.profile).name throws. One ?. does not protect later links.

nodes.label: ?.() does not test callability
nodes.rationale: Guards only null/undefined. A present non-function still throws TypeError. Also does not catch undeclared variables.

nodes.label: Optional chaining is read-only
nodes.rationale: obj?.a=1 is SyntaxError: Invalid left-hand side in assignment.

nodes.label: ?. with ?? default
nodes.rationale: cart?.items?.[0]?.qty??1 preserves a legitimate 0 unlike ||.

nodes.label: Reserve ?. for genuinely optional values
nodes.rationale: On a guaranteed value, ?. converts a loud TypeError into an undefined that fails far away. Assert the invariant instead.

nodes.label: for…of default loop
nodes.rationale: Works on every iterable, supports break/continue/return and await. Get the index via entries().

nodes.label: forEach cannot break or await
nodes.rationale: return exits the callback only. Async forEach ignores the returned promise — silent race. Use for…of or Promise.all(map).

nodes.label: for…in walks prototypes and stringifies indices
nodes.rationale: Includes inherited enumerable keys; array indices arrive as strings so i+1 concatenates. Prefer Object.keys and for…of.

nodes.label: let fresh binding per iteration
nodes.rationale: var is one shared binding (timers log 3 3 3). let creates a fresh binding per iteration so closures capture their own value.

nodes.label: do…while cursor pagination
nodes.rationale: Body runs at least once — fetch a page before you know whether a next cursor exists.

nodes.label: Spread vs rest
nodes.rationale: Same ... syntax, opposite direction. Rest collects on the left of = or in a parameter list; spread expands everywhere else.

nodes.label: Array spread vs object spread
nodes.rationale: [...x] uses Symbol.iterator; {...x} copies own enumerable properties. [...{}] throws; {...['x','y']} yields {"0":"x","1":"y"}.

nodes.label: Spread copies are shallow
nodes.rationale: Nested values stay the same references. Spread each changed level for structural sharing, or structuredClone for a deep copy.

nodes.label: Object spread later keys win
nodes.rationale: {...defaults,...overrides}. A key present as undefined still overwrites — spread does not skip it.

nodes.label: Rest excluded from fn.length
nodes.rationale: Rest must be last. ((a,...r)=>0).length is 1. Libraries that inspect arity see only fixed parameters.

nodes.label: Math.max(...arr) argument cap
nodes.rationale: Very large spreads throw RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded. Use reduce. Empty spread is -Infinity.

nodes.label: Relational comparison algorithm
nodes.rationale: ToPrimitive hint number, then both strings → lexicographic else ToNumber. No null special case, so null>=0 is true while null==0 is false. NaN makes every comparison false.

nodes.label: Lexicographic string comparison
nodes.rationale: '2'>'10' is true. '10'>9 is true (numeric) but '10'>'9' is false (text). Convert numeric strings at the boundary.

nodes.label: Intl.Collator / localeCompare
nodes.rationale: Code-unit sort puts Z before a and é after z. numeric:true also fixes item2 vs item10.

nodes.label: Dates compare but do not equal
nodes.rationale: Relational uses valueOf timestamps so d1<=d2&&d1>=d2 can be true while d1==d2 is false (identity). Compare +date or getTime().

nodes.label: Object relational comparison is silent
nodes.rationale: {}<={} is true because both ToPrimitive to '[object Object]'. Compare a field.

nodes.label: NaN poisons every relational
nodes.rationale: !(a<b) is not equivalent to a>=b when NaN is possible. Guard with Number.isFinite.

nodes.label: Guard clauses
nodes.rationale: Early returns for failures so the happy path is last and unindented. Highest-value refactor for nested ifs.

nodes.label: Ternary chooses a value
nodes.rationale: Wrong for actions. One level inline; two or more align as a decision table or extract a function.

nodes.label: Object lookup instead of branching
nodes.rationale: When every branch maps a key to a value, STATUS_LABEL[status]??'Unknown' beats switch. Not for branches with different shapes or side effects.

nodes.label: Always brace if bodies
nodes.rationale: Brace-less bodies caused Apple goto-fail TLS. Interacts badly with ASI. Enable ESLint curly.

nodes.label: if uses ToBoolean
nodes.rationale: if(stock) treats 0 as absent. Compare explicitly: stock>0 or stock!=null.

nodes.label: switch uses ===
nodes.rationale: switch(1) and switch('1') differ. switch(NaN) matches no case NaN. Convert form/query strings before switching.

nodes.label: switch fallthrough
nodes.rationale: Without break/return/throw, execution continues. Stacked empty cases are idiomatic. Prefer return over break. Comment non-empty fallthrough.

nodes.label: switch body is one block
nodes.rationale: Cases are labels, not scopes. Two let x declarations collide. Brace each case body.

nodes.label: Exhaustive default that throws
nodes.rationale: Omitted default is a silent no-op. Throw so new statuses are loud; TypeScript never checks pair with this.

nodes.label: Five precedence bugs
nodes.rationale: Do not memorise twenty levels. Learn ** right-assoc, + string poison, && tighter than ||, typeof tighter than +, comparisons do not chain.

nodes.label: + string position changes the answer
nodes.rationale: 1+2+'3' is '33'; '1'+2+3 is '123'. Left-to-right; first string poisons the rest.

nodes.label: && binds tighter than ||
nodes.rationale: a||b&&c is a||(b&&c). Always parenthesise mixed &&/||. Mixing ?? is SyntaxError instead.

nodes.label: typeof binds tighter than +
nodes.rationale: typeof 1+1 is 'number1'. Unary operators bind very tightly.

nodes.label: Comparisons do not chain
nodes.rationale: 3>2>1 is false: true>1 becomes 1>1. 1<2<3 being true is coincidence. Write a<x&&x<b.

nodes.label: & is looser than ===
nodes.rationale: flags&MASK===0 parses as flags&(MASK===0). Write (flags&MASK)!==0.

nodes.label: Right-associative operators
nodes.rationale: Only ** , ternary, and assignment. Ternary chaining makes aligned decision tables parse as a?x:(b?y:z).

nodes.label: Expression vs statement
nodes.rationale: Expressions produce a value; statements perform an action. Only expressions are legal where a value is expected.

nodes.label: {} block vs object literal
nodes.rationale: {}+[] as a statement is 0 (empty block then +[]); as an expression is '[object Object]'. Same reason destructuring and arrow object returns need parens.

nodes.label: IIFE needs parentheses
nodes.rationale: function at statement start is a declaration and requires a name. Parens force expression position. Remaining uses: top-level await in non-modules, multi-statement const.

nodes.label: JSX interpolation is expression-only
nodes.rationale: if is a statement, so JSX uses && and ternaries. Arrow ()=>{id:1} parses id: as a label and returns undefined.

nodes.label: Automatic semicolon insertion
nodes.rationale: Semicolons are not optional. ASI inserts only where the next token would otherwise be a syntax error, so valid continuations are taken even when unintended.

nodes.label: Restricted productions
nodes.rationale: Newline after return/throw/break/continue/yield/postfix ++/-- forces a semicolon. return\n{a:1} yields undefined.

nodes.label: Five dangerous ASI line starts
nodes.rationale: ( [ ` + - and / continue the previous line. + and - produce no error, just a wrong number. Semicolon-free style needs a leading ;.

nodes.label: Labelled break and continue
nodes.rationale: One good use: exit nested loops. Prefer extract-and-return. Second use: break a loop from inside a switch.

nodes.label: Labels are not goto
nodes.rationale: A label can only be targeted by break/continue inside the labelled statement. Cannot jump backwards, into a block, or out of a function.

nodes.label: Accidental label in arrow body
nodes.rationale: ()=>{id:1} parses id: as a label; no return so undefined. Fix: ()=>({id:1}).

nodes.label: Bitwise ToInt32 coercion
nodes.rationale: Every bitwise operator converts to 32-bit signed first. 2**31|0 is -2147483648; 2**32|0 is 0. Only 31 usable flags; 1<<31 is negative.

nodes.label: ~~ is not Math.trunc
nodes.rationale: ~~1e10 is 1410065408. Valid only below 2^31. Same for x|0, x>>0, x<<0. Use Math.trunc.

nodes.label: >> vs >>>
nodes.rationale: >> keeps the sign (-5>>1 is -3). >>> fills with zeros (-5>>>1 is 2147483645). Only unsigned 32-bit result.

nodes.label: Bitwise permission flag set
nodes.rationale: 1<<n, combine with |, test (flags&MASK)!==0, add |=, remove &= ~MASK, toggle ^=. Prefer Set of strings in app code.

nodes.label: delete creates array holes
nodes.rationale: delete arr[1] leaves length 3 and 1 in arr false. map preserves holes. Use splice/filter/toSpliced. Returns true even if the key never existed.

nodes.label: in vs Object.hasOwn
nodes.rationale: 'toString' in {} is true (prototype). hasOwn is false. hasOwn distinguishes missing from present-undefined. On arrays in tests indices.

nodes.label: void operator
nodes.rationale: Evaluates operand, always returns undefined. void 0 was a safe undefined before ES5. Modern leftover: discard a floating promise for a linter.

nodes.label: Comma operator
nodes.rationale: Evaluates left to right, returns last. Lowest precedence so x=1,2,3 assigns 1. One readable use: two-pointer for header.

nodes.label: Phase 2 — Operators, expressions and control flow
nodes.rationale: Fifteen high-frequency topics. Invisible-on-review bugs: precedence (?? with ||, right-assoc **) and ASI.

nodes.label: Function declaration hoisting
nodes.rationale: Name and body exist from the top of the scope, even out of unreachable code. Only form callable before its line.

nodes.label: Function expression TDZ
nodes.rationale: const/let expressions throw ReferenceError: Cannot access before initialization. var f=function(){} hoists as undefined then TypeError: f is not a function.

nodes.label: Arrow functions lack function machinery
nodes.rationale: No own this, arguments, prototype, super, or new.target. new A() is TypeError: A is not a constructor. prototype is undefined.

nodes.label: Inferred function .name
nodes.rationale: Assigned functions pick up the binding name. Only never-bound expressions have name ''. Named expressions appear in stack traces.

nodes.label: Named function expression inner binding
nodes.rationale: const fact=function inner(n){…} — inner is visible only inside the body, a recursion handle that survives reassignment of fact.

nodes.label: Arrow closes over outer arguments
nodes.rationale: Module-scope arrow: ReferenceError. Nested arrow silently reports the enclosing call's arguments (4 args in, length 2). Use rest.

nodes.label: Function.prototype.toString source
nodes.rationale: Returns exact source. Method shorthand m(){return 1;} is not a valid standalone expression, so DI that evals toString breaks.

nodes.label: Phase 3 — Functions, scope and closures
nodes.rationale: 20 topics. Master 01–08 written 2026-08-13; 09–20 deferred. this, closures, and the scope chain are assumed by later phases.

nodes.label: Defaults evaluated at call time
nodes.rationale: Stored unevaluated; run left to right only for omitted arguments. order(1,undefined,3) evaluates only b.

nodes.label: Only undefined triggers a default
nodes.rationale: null is a value: greet(null) is 'hi null'. Missing key vs DB NULL are not interchangeable. Use ?? in the body if null should fall back.

nodes.label: Parameter-list TDZ
nodes.rationale: Later defaults can read earlier parameters (h=w*2). Forward refs throw at runtime only when that default runs. (a=a) is TDZ too.

nodes.label: Shared-default myth
nodes.rationale: list=[] is fresh each call. list=shared mutates one outer array. Constructing defaults are safe; referencing defaults are not.

nodes.label: fn.length stops at first default
nodes.rationale: (a=1,b)=>0 reports 0. Express error handlers (length===4) silently stop routing if a default is added. Default in the body instead.

nodes.label: Parameter scope vs body scope
nodes.rationale: Any default creates two scopes. A default closure keeps the parameter x; var x in the body is a different binding. scopes('param') is ['body','param'].

nodes.label: Arity is never enforced
nodes.rationale: Too few arguments become undefined; extras are ignored by the parameter list but still counted by arguments.length. Downstream TypeError is the usual symptom.

nodes.label: Rest parameters
nodes.rationale: A real array, empty rather than undefined when nothing extra is passed. Must be last; cannot have a default. Works in arrows.

nodes.label: arguments object
nodes.rationale: Array-like ([object Arguments]), no .map, absent in arrows. Prefer rest in new code.

nodes.label: Sloppy-mode arguments aliasing
nodes.rationale: On a simple parameter list, arguments[i] and the parameter share one slot both ways. Off in strict, and if any default, rest, or destructured parameter makes the list non-simple.

nodes.label: Non-simple parameter list
nodes.rationale: Any default, rest, or destructured parameter. Turns off sloppy arguments aliasing, forbids a body use-strict directive, and changes .length.

nodes.label: Destructured parameters
nodes.rationale: Property defaults cover missing keys; = {} covers a missing object. Every optional destructured level needs its own default.

nodes.label: Positional plus options-object signature
nodes.rationale: Two or three required positionals, then an options object destructured with defaults. Explicit guards replace the arity check JavaScript will not do.

nodes.label: Parameter list is its own language
nodes.rationale: Own scope, own TDZ, own evaluation order, and a simple vs non-simple rule that silently changes arguments.

nodes.label: this is bound at call time
nodes.rationale: Not a property of the function. Behaves like a hidden first parameter the call site fills in.

nodes.label: Four this binding rules
nodes.rationale: new, then explicit call/apply/bind, then implicit obj.fn(), then default. Arrows are outside the tree.

nodes.label: Default this binding
nodes.rationale: Bare fn() is undefined in strict and globalThis in sloppy. Strict turns a silent global write into TypeError.

nodes.label: Implicit this binding
nodes.rationale: obj.fn() binds this to whatever is left of the last dot. nested.inner.read() binds inner, not nested.

nodes.label: Explicit this binding
nodes.rationale: call and apply invoke immediately; bind returns a new function with this fixed forever.

nodes.label: new this binding
nodes.rationale: Fresh object, prototype linked to Fn.prototype, this bound, returned unless the constructor returns an object. A returned primitive is ignored.

nodes.label: this precedence
nodes.rationale: new beats bind beats call/apply beats implicit beats default. new on a bound function discards bound this but keeps bound arguments.

nodes.label: Module top-level this
nodes.rationale: ES module top-level this is undefined. CommonJS top-level this is module.exports. Use globalThis for the global object.

nodes.label: Lost this
nodes.rationale: Implicit binding is a property of the call site. Assigning, destructuring, or passing a method drops the receiver.

nodes.label: thisArg
nodes.rationale: forEach/map/filter/some/every/find/findIndex/flatMap honour thisArg. reduce and sort do not.

nodes.label: Arrow callback this fix
nodes.rationale: An arrow has no this, so the inner obj.method() keeps its receiver. Wrong as the method itself at module scope.

nodes.label: bind identity trap
nodes.rationale: bind returns a new function each call, so removeEventListener never matches. Store the bound function once.

nodes.label: Class field arrow
nodes.rationale: Per-instance own property capturing constructor this. Survives detach; not on the prototype so it cannot be stubbed or overridden there.

nodes.label: this is an argument not a variable
nodes.rationale: Decided by how a function is called, not where it was written. Look at the call site, not the definition.

nodes.label: Lexical this
nodes.rationale: An arrow has no this. The identifier is a free variable resolved through the scope chain like any other.

nodes.label: Object literal is not a scope
nodes.rationale: An arrow used as a method looks past the object literal to module this (undefined).

nodes.label: call apply bind cannot change arrow this
nodes.rationale: They silently do nothing to this and still pass arguments. bind still returns a function so nothing signals failure.

nodes.label: Arrow inherited bindings
nodes.rationale: this, arguments, super, and new.target are inherited, not banned. Only prototype is genuinely absent.

nodes.label: Arrow has no prototype
nodes.rationale: hasOwnProperty('prototype') is false, so new A() throws TypeError: A is not a constructor.

nodes.label: Arrow inherited arguments
nodes.rationale: At module scope arguments is not defined. Inside a function the arrow reports the outer call count, not its own. Use rest.

nodes.label: Arrow object-literal trap
nodes.rationale: n => { value: n } is a labelled statement returning undefined. One property parses; two properties are SyntaxError. Parenthesise: ({value: n}).

nodes.label: Concise arrow body
nodes.rationale: Expression position only. if and return are SyntaxError. Ternary and ?? remain legal.

nodes.label: No generator arrow
nodes.rationale: async () => is supported. *() => {} is SyntaxError. Generators must be function*.

nodes.label: Prototype method vs class-field arrow
nodes.rationale: Prototype methods are shared and stubbable. Field arrows are per-instance own enumerable keys. Use a field arrow only when the method is passed as a value.

nodes.label: Arrow is a different kind of callable
nodes.rationale: Not shorter function syntax. No own this, arguments, super, or new.target, and no prototype at all.

nodes.label: call apply bind
nodes.rationale: All three set this. Only bind defers the call. apply takes an array. bind returns a new function every time.

nodes.label: thisArg coercion
nodes.rationale: Strict passes thisArg untouched. Sloppy boxes primitives and replaces null/undefined with globalThis.

nodes.label: Sloppy primitive boxing
nodes.rationale: Each call(42) boxes a fresh Number, so state written to this is discarded. Strict throws TypeError on the write.

nodes.label: Bound function exotic object
nodes.rationale: Name prefixed bound , length reduced by bound args, no own prototype, this permanently fixed. Later bind still accumulates arguments.

nodes.label: new discards bound this
nodes.rationale: [[Construct]] discards bound this, keeps bound arguments, and delegates the prototype chain to the target. Still instanceof the original.

nodes.label: Hand-written bind
nodes.rationale: Naive apply misses new. Use new.target ? this : thisArg and set bound.prototype from the target. User code cannot match native name, length, or absent prototype.

nodes.label: bind reduces function.length
nodes.rationale: Reduced by the number of bound arguments. Express error handlers that dispatch on fn.length === 4 change behaviour.

nodes.label: Method borrowing
nodes.rationale: Array methods are generic: they need length and integer keys. [].slice.call(arrayLike) and push on a plain object both work. Array.from replaced most of this.

nodes.label: Object.prototype.toString.call type check
nodes.rationale: Reads the internal tag. typeof cannot distinguish array, null, Date, or Map. Defeated by Symbol.toStringTag; user classes are always [object Object].

nodes.label: apply and spread argument limit
nodes.rationale: Both hit RangeError Maximum call stack size exceeded at large arity. Spread is not a fix. Use reduce or chunk.

nodes.label: Partial application with bind
nodes.rationale: Fills arguments from the left only. Bindings accumulate. null thisArg is safe only if the function never touches this.

nodes.label: call apply bind cost
nodes.rationale: Direct call is about 3x faster than any indirect form. call, apply, and spread are indistinguishable. Hoist bind out of loops. Tens of nanoseconds per call.

nodes.label: The three methods that make this explicit
nodes.rationale: Spread replaced most of apply. call and bind remain load-bearing. toString.call is still the only correct built-in type check.

nodes.label: Closure captures the variable not the value
nodes.rationale: A live reference to the binding, read at call time. Explains both counter factories and the loop bug.

nodes.label: var-in-a-loop bug
nodes.rationale: var is function-scoped so one i is shared. Closures report the final 3. Fixes: let, IIFE parameter, or forEach.

nodes.label: let per-iteration binding
nodes.rationale: for (let) copies the loop variable into a fresh binding each iteration. Closures that mutate n do not interfere.

nodes.label: IIFE loop-variable capture
nodes.rationale: A function parameter is a fresh binding per call. Pre-ES6 fix that let automates.

nodes.label: setTimeout is not the loop-bug cause
nodes.rationale: The synchronous var loop also yields [3,3,3]. The timer only guarantees callbacks run after the loop.

nodes.label: Closure private state
nodes.rationale: The oldest privacy and the oldest leak. Variables stay alive as long as the function does.

nodes.label: Counter factory
nodes.rationale: count is unreachable from outside. Each factory call creates a new scope so instances are independent.

nodes.label: One scope per enclosing call
nodes.rationale: Closures created during one call share that call's bindings. Not one scope per closure.

nodes.label: V8 captures referenced bindings only
nodes.rationale: Unused 300k-object arrays added 0 MB; referenced ones retained 69 MB. Optimisation, not a spec guarantee. heapUsed misses typed-array external memory.

nodes.label: Stale closure
nodes.rationale: Closing over a copy or a previous-render binding freezes the value. Fix with the live variable, a mutable ref, a recreated closure, or an updater.

nodes.label: Closure
nodes.rationale: A function together with the variables it still has access to. Every JS function is one; the word matters when the function outlives its defining scope.

nodes.label: Lexical scope
nodes.rationale: Fixed by where the function appears in the source, not where it is called. Makes closures possible and lets engines resolve names to slot indices.

nodes.label: Scope chain lookup
nodes.rationale: Walks outward and stops at the first match. Outer scopes cannot see inner bindings.

nodes.label: What creates a scope
nodes.rationale: Function bodies, blocks for let/const/class, modules, for heads with let/const, and catch. Object literals, if parentheses, templates, and var-in-a-block do not.

nodes.label: Shadowing
nodes.rationale: An inner binding hides an outer one for its scope and does not overwrite it. let cannot redeclare a parameter in the same function scope; var merges.

nodes.label: with is banned in strict mode
nodes.rationale: Injects an object's properties into the scope chain so names cannot be resolved statically.

nodes.label: Direct eval
nodes.rationale: Can introduce bindings into the surrounding scope. Indirect eval (0, eval)(...) runs in global scope instead.

nodes.label: Function scope vs block scope
nodes.rationale: var ignores blocks and attaches to the nearest function. let/const attach to the nearest block.

nodes.label: const fixes the binding not the value
nodes.rationale: The name cannot be pointed at something else; object and array contents can still change. Redeclaration is SyntaxError; reassignment is TypeError.

nodes.label: Object.freeze
nodes.rationale: Shallow. Nested objects remain mutable. Strict throws on a frozen write; sloppy fails silently.

nodes.label: Module top level is not global
nodes.rationale: Top-level var is a global only in a classic script. ES modules and CommonJS keep it off globalThis. let/const never create global properties.

nodes.label: Accidental global
nodes.rationale: Assigning to an undeclared name creates a global in sloppy mode and throws ReferenceError in strict/modules.

nodes.label: const by default
nodes.rationale: const first, let when you reassign, var never. Use-before-declaration then throws instead of producing undefined.

nodes.label: Scope is decided where code is written
nodes.rationale: Lexical scoping makes closures possible, makes var and let differ, and lets engines resolve most lookups before the program runs.

nodes.label: Two-step scope entry
nodes.rationale: Nothing is relocated. Scope entry first creates a binding for every declaration, then code runs. What differs is whether the slot is initialised.

nodes.label: Value hoisting
nodes.rationale: Functions (and function*, async function) are usable before their line because the slot holds the finished function.

nodes.label: Declaration hoisting
nodes.rationale: var is referenceable before its line without ReferenceError, but the value is always undefined until assignment.

nodes.label: Behavioral hoisting
nodes.rationale: let/const/class create a dead zone above their line: the binding exists but is uninitialised.

nodes.label: Side-effect hoisting
nodes.rationale: import bindings are available early and the imported module's side effects run before the rest of the file.

nodes.label: HoistableDeclaration
nodes.rationale: The spec term is not hoisting. HoistableDeclaration covers function declarations only.

nodes.label: Environment record
nodes.rationale: One per scope, chained to its parent. Hoisting is how that record is populated before its code runs.

nodes.label: Three binding error types
nodes.rationale: x is not defined means no binding; x is not a function means the binding holds a non-callable; Cannot access before initialization means uninitialised TDZ.

nodes.label: var declaration vs initialization split
nodes.rationale: var x = 1 is two operations: the declaration hoists to function scope as undefined; the assignment stays where it is.

nodes.label: Function declaration value hoisting
nodes.rationale: The only form that is usefully hoisted: the slot holds the finished function before the first line runs.

nodes.label: Function expression not hoisted
nodes.rationale: var f = function(){} hoists the binding as undefined; calling it above the line is TypeError, not ReferenceError.

nodes.label: var and function name collision
nodes.rationale: At scope entry the function wins regardless of source order. Only an initializer overwrites it at execution time.

nodes.label: Script top-level var as non-configurable global
nodes.rationale: In a classic script, top-level var is a non-configurable global property and cannot be deleted. Modules do not do this.

nodes.label: Temporal dead zone
nodes.rationale: From block entry until the let/const/class declaration initialises the binding. The slot exists but is empty; a read throws ReferenceError.

nodes.label: TDZ is temporal not positional
nodes.rationale: A function defined above a let may close over it. Only a read that runs before the declaration throws.

nodes.label: Declaration closes the TDZ
nodes.rationale: let x; initialises to undefined and ends the zone. const without an initialiser is a parse-time SyntaxError.

nodes.label: Self-referential initializer
nodes.rationale: let x = x throws because the RHS is evaluated before initialisation. var y = y silently assigns undefined.

nodes.label: Per-iteration TDZ binding
nodes.rationale: for (const item of items) is legal because each iteration declares a new binding. Same machinery as let-in-a-loop closures.

nodes.label: typeof throws in the TDZ
nodes.rationale: typeof still reads the binding. The 'undefined' special case applies only to names with no binding at all.

nodes.label: TDZ is a feature
nodes.rationale: Fails at the wrong line instead of later; lets const guarantee one observable value; makes a shadow own its name for the whole block.

nodes.label: TDZ engine error messages
nodes.rationale: V8: Cannot access 'X' before initialization. SpiderMonkey names the declaration. JavaScriptCore omits the identifier.

nodes.label: globalThis feature detect
nodes.rationale: globalThis.SomeGlobal !== undefined cannot hit a dead zone. typeof is only safe for genuinely undeclared names.

nodes.label: Block-level function declaration
nodes.rationale: A function declaration inside a block is not top-level hoisting. Strict mode scopes it to that block; sloppy mode is Annex B and engine-dependent.

nodes.label: Strict-mode block functions
nodes.rationale: In strict mode (every module and class body) block-level function declarations hoist to the top of that block and do not exist outside it.

nodes.label: Annex B sloppy-mode block functions
nodes.rationale: Non-strict block function declarations behave strangely and differ across Chrome, Firefox and Safari. Scope setup still runs even if the if body never executes.

nodes.label: Prefer const-assigned function expressions in blocks
nodes.rationale: Never write a function declaration inside a block. Assign a function expression to let or const so the binding is exactly where you wrote it in every engine.

nodes.label: Parameter list TDZ
nodes.rationale: The parameter list is its own scope and initialises left to right. A default that reads a later parameter throws Cannot access before initialization.

nodes.label: Parameter scope is parent of body
nodes.rationale: Default initialisers run in the parameter scope, a parent of the body. Body functions and even var bindings are not visible; the error is X is not defined, not a TDZ access.

nodes.label: var shadowing a parameter
nodes.rationale: A var of the same name in the body is a separate binding. A closure created in a default captures the parameter, never the body's var.

nodes.label: Class lexical declaration and TDZ
nodes.rationale: class is commonly regarded as non-hoisted. Using one above its declaration throws Cannot access before initialization. Classes are block-scoped and do not create globalThis properties.

nodes.label: Const-like inner class binding
nodes.rationale: Inside the class body the class name is an immutable binding. Outside it is a reassignable let-like binding. The class body always runs in strict mode.

nodes.label: extends evaluated at declaration
nodes.rationale: extends is an expression evaluated when the class statement runs, not at new. Two classes cannot extend each other; method bodies have no such constraint.

nodes.label: Import hoisting
nodes.rationale: Import declarations are hoisted: imported values are available before their line and the imported module's side effects run first. Position in the file does not change evaluation order.

nodes.label: Live read-only import bindings
nodes.rationale: Imports are read-only views like const. You cannot reassign the imported binding; only the exporting module can change the value, and the change is live.

nodes.label: Circular ESM import TDZ
nodes.rationale: Module evaluation is depth-first. A top-level read of a not-yet-initialised import throws Cannot access before initialization. Defer the read inside an exported function. A cycle is not automatically a bug.

nodes.label: CommonJS circular require
nodes.rationale: require has no dead zone. A circular require returns a partially populated module.exports, typically undefined properties, with no error.

nodes.label: Hoisting and the temporal dead zone
nodes.rationale: Nothing is moved. Entering a scope creates a binding for every declaration before any code runs. What went into the slot differs by declaration kind.

nodes.label: Nothing is moved to the top
nodes.rationale: The spec has no hoisting. Bindings are created at scope entry. The TDZ is a stretch of time, not a region of source.

nodes.label: Declaration binding table
nodes.rationale: function is usable before its line; var is undefined; let/const/class throw ReferenceError; import is a live binding with side effects first.

nodes.label: Phase 4 — Objects, prototypes and classes
nodes.rationale: Everything non-primitive. Prototype rows make class stop being magic; the copy row is the one that costs teams real money. Master topics 01, 03–08 are written.

nodes.label: Shorthand property names
nodes.rationale: { a } means { a: a }. It cannot rename, so API boundaries that change casing still need the full form.

nodes.label: Computed property names
nodes.rationale: Square-bracket expressions become keys, evaluated in source order while the object is built. A symbol key has no other literal form.

nodes.label: Conditional key spread idiom
nodes.rationale: ...(cond && { k }) keeps the object one expression. Spreading a falsy non-object is a no-op. Prefer this over delete.

nodes.label: Method shorthand is not a function property
nodes.rationale: Methods cannot be constructors and only methods have super, because they have a home object. Prefer method shorthand in literals.

nodes.label: Arrow this in an object literal
nodes.rationale: Neither method nor function-valued property gives lexical this. An arrow in a literal captures enclosing this, undefined at module top level.

nodes.label: Getter and setter properties
nodes.rationale: Accessors look like data from outside but run functions. Spread and Object.assign invoke getters and store values, converting accessors to data.

nodes.label: Object spread own enumerable shallow
nodes.rationale: Spread copies own enumerable properties shallowly, excluding the prototype. Spreading a class instance drops methods. Later spreads win as a replace, not a deep merge.

nodes.label: Object.assign triggers setters
nodes.rationale: Object.assign mutates the target and runs its setters. Spread defines properties on a fresh Object.prototype object. Reach for spread by default.

nodes.label: Duplicate keys last wins
nodes.rationale: After ES2015 duplicate names are legal even in strict mode because computed keys cannot be checked at parse time. A spread after an explicit key is almost always a bug. Private elements must still be unique.

nodes.label: Keys are string or symbol only
