nodes.rationale: Always, including for libraries. It governs your CI; consumers' own lockfiles govern them. There is no downside and a real supply-chain upside.

nodes.label: package.json overrides
nodes.rationale: Forces a nested dependency version when the parent has not updated. You override the parent's declared compatibility.

nodes.label: npm day to day
nodes.rationale: The dozen commands you actually run, and two decisions: which list a package belongs in, and whether this machine should resolve ranges.

nodes.label: npm ci --omit=dev
nodes.rationale: What production installs. Getting dependencies vs devDependencies wrong fails only in production.

nodes.label: npx
nodes.rationale: Resolves a local binary first, then downloads to a cache and executes without installing. A typo'd package name is a real attack vector.

nodes.label: Avoid global npm installs
nodes.rationale: Global packages are unversioned, invisible to the project, and differ per machine. Put the tool in devDependencies or use npx.

nodes.label: npm explain
nodes.rationale: Prints the dependency chain that pulled a package in. Do not import a transitive package directly.

nodes.label: save-exact
nodes.rationale: Makes npm install write exact versions instead of ^ ranges. Useful for applications; less so for libraries.

nodes.label: npm, pnpm, yarn
nodes.rationale: All three install packages. The difference that matters is the shape of node_modules and whether an undeclared dependency can accidentally work.

nodes.label: Hoisted node_modules
nodes.rationale: npm and yarn flatten transitive dependencies into top-level node_modules so duplicates collapse.

nodes.label: Phantom dependencies
nodes.rationale: A package your code imports without declaring it, because a hoisted transitive sat at the top level. It breaks when the real dependent drops it.

nodes.label: pnpm content-addressable store
nodes.rationale: One copy of each version on disk; node_modules is symlinks exposing only declared dependencies. Undeclared imports fail immediately.

nodes.label: Corepack
nodes.rationale: Pins the package manager per project via packageManager. Ships with Node but is not enabled by default.

nodes.label: Workspaces
nodes.rationale: One repo, several packages, one install, one lockfile. Siblings are symlinked. They do not give you build orchestration.

nodes.label: Type stripping
nodes.rationale: Node replaces type annotations with whitespace and runs the result. Enabled by default since v23.6.0; Stability 2 as of v24.12.0.

nodes.label: Node is not a type checker
nodes.rationale: Native execution removes the build, not the check. Dropping tsc --noEmit means type errors reach production.

nodes.label: Erasable vs non-erasable syntax
nodes.rationale: Annotations, interface, generics, import type erase cleanly. enum, runtime namespace, and parameter properties must generate JavaScript.

nodes.label: ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX
nodes.rationale: Thrown for TypeScript enum in strip-only mode. --experimental-transform-types works but drops the stability guarantee.

nodes.label: ERR_UNSUPPORTED_NODE_MODULES_TYPE_STRIPPING
nodes.rationale: Node refuses to strip types inside node_modules. Published packages should ship JavaScript plus .d.ts.

nodes.label: Import the .ts extension
nodes.rationale: ESM does not rewrite .js to .ts. Running .ts directly requires ./helper.ts and allowImportingTsExtensions.

nodes.label: tsc --noEmit
nodes.rationale: Type checking stays a separate step in CI, editor, and pre-commit. Required in every situation even when the build is optional.

nodes.label: Publishing a package
nodes.rationale: A checklist rather than a skill. The two irreversible parts are what ends up in the tarball and the version number you burn.

nodes.label: Scoped package names
nodes.rationale: A scope is a namespace you own. Scoped packages default to private; publish publicly with --access public or publishConfig.access.

nodes.label: npm pack --dry-run
nodes.rationale: The only way to see what you are actually shipping. Catches secrets going out and needed files staying home.

nodes.label: A published version is permanent
nodes.rationale: npm unpublish is restricted to 72 hours and only when nothing depends on it. Recovery is npm deprecate plus a new version.

nodes.label: Pre-release dist-tag
nodes.rationale: Without --tag a pre-release becomes latest and everyone running npm install gets a beta.

nodes.label: npm publish --provenance
nodes.rationale: Attaches a signed statement linking the tarball to the exact commit and workflow. Only works from supported CI.

nodes.label: Ship ESM only by default
nodes.rationale: require(esm) works from Node 22.12 and is stable in 24.15, so CommonJS consumers are served without a second build.

nodes.label: node:module API
nodes.rationale: The programmable side of the module system. You go years without needing it, then need it for a loader, a test double, or a startup-time win.

nodes.label: enableCompileCache
nodes.rationale: Persists V8 compilation output to disk. Call before heavy imports, or set NODE_COMPILE_CACHE. Keyed by Node version and architecture.

nodes.label: module.register()
nodes.rationale: Registers resolve and load customization hooks. Still experimental in Node 24. Register before the modules they affect via --import.

nodes.label: Loader hooks run on a separate thread
nodes.rationale: Stops a loader from deadlocking the main thread. No shared memory; communicate through register() data and a MessagePort.

nodes.label: module.isBuiltin
nodes.rationale: Whether a specifier is a built-in, prefix or not. isBuiltin('fs') and isBuiltin('node:fs') are both true.

nodes.label: Phase 1 — Modules and packages
nodes.rationale: Fourteen pages on how code gets into your program. Target runtime Node 24.19.0 with npm 12.0.2.

nodes.label: Phase 1 gate: dual-consumer exports map
nodes.rationale: A package with type module, an exports map that blocks deep imports, works from import and require, and ships only what files allows.

nodes.label: require(esm) stable in v24.15.0
nodes.rationale: Advice written before 2025 says CommonJS cannot load ES modules. On Node 24 it can.

nodes.label: Structured logging
nodes.rationale: A production log line is a searchable record. Every line is one JSON object with a small set of agreed keys.

nodes.label: console.log can block the event loop
nodes.rationale: console is synchronous on some destinations. When stdout is a pipe a slow consumer can block the loop under a traffic spike.

nodes.label: Log levels
nodes.rationale: fatal/error, warn, info, debug, trace. Default production to info. Turning on debug fleet-wide fills a disk.

nodes.label: Minimum log schema
nodes.rationale: time, level, msg, service/version, reqId/traceId, and domain ids as dedicated fields — never only buried in msg.

nodes.label: Logs, traces, and metrics
nodes.rationale: Logs are discrete events. Metrics are aggregates. Traces connect work across services. None replaces the others.

nodes.label: pino
nodes.rationale: A fast JSON logger with the knobs production uses: child bindings, redaction paths, and serializers.

nodes.label: pino child loggers
nodes.rationale: Bind reqId and orderId once so every subsequent line carries them. One child per request or job. base is process-lifetime facts.

nodes.label: pino redact
nodes.rationale: Redact at the logger, not in every call site. Defense in depth, not a substitute for not putting secrets on the object.

nodes.label: pino serializers
nodes.rationale: stdSerializers.err pulls type, message, and stack. Pass the error under an err field on the merge object.

nodes.label: Do not pretty-print in production
nodes.rationale: Aggregators parse JSON. Colourized multi-line output is for humans on a laptop.

nodes.label: Correlation and request IDs
nodes.rationale: Generate or accept one id at the edge and thread it through logs, outbound calls, jobs, and errors until the work is done.

nodes.label: AsyncLocalStorage for request context
nodes.rationale: Preserves the id across await points without threading an extra argument. Enter the context once at the edge.

nodes.label: x-request-id
nodes.rationale: Trust a well-formed incoming header from your own edge, mint a UUID when missing, echo it on the response. Validate length and charset.

nodes.label: Persist request id on job payloads
nodes.rationale: Otherwise background failures are orphaned from the HTTP request that caused them. Re-enter ALS in the worker.

nodes.label: ALS does not cross threads
nodes.rationale: Worker threads and child processes do not inherit ALS. Pass the id in workerData or the message.

nodes.label: What to log
nodes.rationale: Log decisions and outcomes: authz denies, state transitions, dependency failures, exhausted retries, config fallbacks.

nodes.label: Never log secrets or raw PII
nodes.rationale: Passwords, tokens, full PAN/CVV, government ids, raw address books, private keys. Logs have wider read access than the database.

nodes.label: Data minimization vs redaction
nodes.rationale: Minimization means not putting sensitive fields on the object. Redaction strips fields that slipped through. Minimization first.

nodes.label: Access logs vs app logs
nodes.rationale: Access log: method, path, status, duration, request id. App log: domain events and failures. Duplicating every request as info doubles cost.

nodes.label: Log volume discipline
nodes.rationale: Do not log every SQL query, full bodies, debug fleet-wide, or inside tight loops. Sample high-volume success; always keep errors.

nodes.label: OpenTelemetry
nodes.rationale: Instrument once and export to many backends. Vendor SDKs lock you in; OTel is the portable layer.

nodes.label: Span
nodes.rationale: One unit of work with a start, an end, attributes, and optional status. Manual spans belong on business operations.

nodes.label: Trace
nodes.rationale: A tree of spans sharing a trace id. Answers where a request spent time across services.

nodes.label: W3C Trace Context
nodes.rationale: traceparent / tracestate is the standardized join key across processes. The cousin of x-request-id.

nodes.label: Trace sampling
nodes.rationale: Full traces for 100% of traffic melts a backend. Head-based ratio, always-sample errors/slow, or tail sampling at the collector.

nodes.label: Error tracking
nodes.rationale: Sentry, Bugsnag, GlitchTip group the same crash across thousands of events, show the release that introduced it, and page on rate changes.

nodes.label: Error fingerprinting
nodes.rationale: Groups events into issues by root cause. Unique ids in the message string split one bug into hundreds of issues.

nodes.label: Error tracker release
nodes.rationale: An identifier for the code version, often git SHA. Without it, new in this deploy is guesswork.

nodes.label: captureException on handled failures
nodes.rationale: If you log and continue without captureException, the tracker never sees production's most common failures — the ones you already catch.

nodes.label: diagnostics_channel
nodes.rationale: Zero-dependency in-process pub/sub. Libraries publish named events; observability glue subscribes without monkey-patching private APIs.

nodes.label: hasSubscribers
nodes.rationale: The performance gate. Keep payloads small on hot paths so the path stays cheap when nobody is listening.

nodes.label: TracingChannel
nodes.rationale: Request-shaped helper: tracingChannel('myservice:charge').tracePromise(() => doCharge(orderId), {orderId}).

nodes.label: Node diagnostic report
nodes.rationale: Structured JSON dump of stacks, handles, versions, resource usage on demand or on fatal conditions. Large and may contain env secrets.

nodes.label: trace_events
nodes.rationale: Low-level V8/node trace categories. Scope to a critical section; leaving global tracing on under traffic collapses latency.

nodes.label: --report-on-fatalerror
nodes.rationale: Writes a report when the process dies fatally. Needs a writable --report-directory in the container.

nodes.label: Event loop lag
nodes.rationale: The metric that turns 'the server feels slow' into a number you can alert on. One thread runs all JS — if the loop is late, every request on that process is late.

nodes.label: monitorEventLoopDelay histogram
nodes.rationale: Values are nanoseconds; divide by 1e6 for milliseconds. Enable process-wide at boot; export p99 and max each scrape; reset or slide the window so one incident does not poison the day.

nodes.label: Idle p50 is the sampling resolution
nodes.rationale: At resolution 10, idle p50 sits near 10 ms. Alerting on p50 > 5 ms at that resolution is alerting on arithmetic.

nodes.label: Lag max vs p99
nodes.rationale: One 100 ms block moved only max (10.29 → 115.34 ms). Five blocks raised p99 to ~109 ms. max is the smoke alarm; p99 is the trend.

nodes.label: Lag is not downstream I/O wait
nodes.rationale: A slow downstream API is I/O wait, not lag. Sync bcrypt, image resize, GC thrash, and stdout backpressure do show up as lag.

nodes.label: Health checks — liveness vs readiness
nodes.rationale: Conflating liveness and readiness is how a temporary dependency blip becomes a restart storm.

nodes.label: Liveness probe
nodes.rationale: Answers 'should this process be killed?'. Must depend on almost nothing. If /live checks the database and it blips, every pod restarts at once.

nodes.label: Readiness probe
nodes.rationale: Answers 'should this process receive traffic?'. Allowed to be strict: DB pool, required caches, acceptingTraffic flag. Temporary and reversible without a kill.

nodes.label: Startup probe
nodes.rationale: Optional. Has boot finished? Wait; do not kill yet. Same checks as readiness, but only during boot.

nodes.label: acceptingTraffic flag
nodes.rationale: Flip true only after validate config, connect pools, and listen. Ready before the pool exists means health already passed while first requests fail.

nodes.label: Readiness drain on SIGTERM
nodes.rationale: Set readiness false, wait for in-flight requests, close server, exit. The balancer stops new traffic because readiness failed, not because the process vanished mid-request.

nodes.label: Four golden signals
nodes.rationale: From Google's SRE workbook. Latency, traffic, errors, and saturation tell you whether a service is healthy — everything else is a breakdown or a distraction.

nodes.label: Latency signal
nodes.rationale: How long successful and failed work takes. Histogram by status class. Average latency hides the long tail.

nodes.label: Traffic signal
nodes.rationale: Demand: requests/sec, jobs enqueued/sec, messages consumed/sec. Alert on sudden drop or spike vs baseline.

nodes.label: Errors signal
nodes.rationale: Rate of failed work (5xx ratio, failed jobs). Error ratio, not absolute count. Often only 5xx plus selected 4xx belong in the SLO.

nodes.label: Saturation signal
nodes.rationale: Leading indicator: event loop lag, pool wait, heap ratio, queue depth, CPU. Traffic and latency go bad after the constrained resource is full.

nodes.label: Low-cardinality metric labels
nodes.rationale: route is the template (/orders/:id), never the raw URL or userId. Unbounded labels kill Prometheus.

nodes.label: perf_hooks
nodes.rationale: Built-in stopwatch and observer bus for in-process timings. Does not replace OpenTelemetry across services.

nodes.label: performance.now monotonic clock
nodes.rationale: Monotonic high-resolution clock inside the process. Date.now can step on NTP adjustments and skew durations.

nodes.label: Performance marks and measures
nodes.rationale: Named timestamps and the duration between them. Clear entries in long-running processes or the buffer grows.

nodes.label: PerformanceObserver GC entries
nodes.rationale: Observe entryTypes gc; histogram duration and watch multi-ms spikes. kind maps through NODE_PERFORMANCE_GC_* constants.

nodes.label: Process metrics — RSS, heap, handles
nodes.rationale: RSS, heap used, and active handles together debug 'memory is high' without guessing.

nodes.label: RSS resident set
nodes.rationale: Pages in RAM including heap, stacks, code, native addons. Alert on RSS and cgroup memory for Kubernetes OOM risk, not V8's opinion.

nodes.label: heapUsed
nodes.rationale: V8 heap currently live. Climbing over hours with flat traffic is the leak signal. heapTotal growth then plateau is reservation, not a leak.

nodes.label: v8.getHeapStatistics
nodes.rationale: Default heap_size_limit ~4288 MB here. With --max-old-space-size=256 the reported limit was 448 MB, not 256.

nodes.label: Active handles and requests
nodes.rationale: Open servers, timers, sockets keep the loop alive — correct for a server, a bug for a CLI that should exit. Underscore APIs are not a public contract.

nodes.label: process.resourceUsage
nodes.rationale: CPU attribution over a window (user vs system) and cumulative FS ops. Export deltas between scrapes.

nodes.label: Exposing metrics for Prometheus
nodes.rationale: Expose low-cardinality time series that map to the golden signals — not every event as a metric.

nodes.label: Prometheus pull scrape
nodes.rationale: Prometheus scrapes GET /metrics. Pull keeps service discovery, failure detection, and timestamps with the collector. Pushgateway is for short-lived jobs.

nodes.label: Counter, gauge, histogram, summary
nodes.rationale: Counters only go up (requests, errors). Gauges for lag, heap, pool wait. Histograms enable p50/p95/p99. Summaries are less common in modern setups.

nodes.label: Metric cardinality
nodes.rationale: Each unique label combination is a separate time series. userId, orderId, full URL, or exception message unbounded-series the cluster.

nodes.label: /metrics endpoint
nodes.rationale: Internal only — NetworkPolicy, sidecar scrape, or a separate port. Same public API hostname without auth is a leak.

nodes.label: Finding the bottleneck
nodes.rationale: The bottleneck is the resource that is full. Optimizing anything else is a hobby.

nodes.label: Measure then change one thing
nodes.rationale: Reproduce with a number, check golden signals and loop lag, time dependencies, profile only if the loop or CPU is hot, change one thing, remeasure.

nodes.label: High lag plus high CPU
nodes.rationale: Sync JS, crypto, or JSON on the loop. Profile and move work off the request path.

nodes.label: Low lag plus high p99
nodes.rationale: Waiting on I/O or a queue, not blocking the event loop. Look at downstream and pool wait times. CPU profiles show idle.

nodes.label: Staged request timings
nodes.rationale: Three spans (load, charge, save) beat a single 'checkout is slow' log. Sample or push the same boundaries as OTel spans under volume.

nodes.label: Caching strategy
nodes.rationale: A cache is a correctness trade: stale in exchange for not hitting the expensive path. If you cannot name the invalidation rule, you have a future incident.

nodes.label: TTL and write-path invalidation
nodes.rationale: TTL bounds how wrong you can be; it is not the only invalidation. Delete or overwrite the key on write when updates must show sooner.

nodes.label: Cache stampede
nodes.rationale: Many concurrent misses on one expired hot key overload the origin. Mitigate with single-flight, distributed locks, jittered TTLs, or stale-while-revalidate.

nodes.label: Single-flight cache fill
nodes.rationale: In-process Map of inflight promises collapses concurrent misses in one process. Does not protect a 20-pod fleet.

nodes.label: In-process vs Redis cache
nodes.rationale: In-process is fastest and per pod; after scale-out you have N independent caches. Redis is shared, networked, operational.

nodes.label: Negative cache
nodes.rationale: Caching 'not found' without TTL, or caching 5xx, turns a transient failure into a long outage.

nodes.label: Memory leaks
nodes.rationale: Almost always a growing set of objects still reachable from a root — a Map, a closure, a listener list — not malloc forgot free.

nodes.label: Heap snapshot
nodes.rationale: v8.writeHeapSnapshot returns a string path. Take two snapshots minutes apart under the same load and diff retained size.

nodes.label: Retainer path
nodes.rationale: The reference chain to a GC root. That path is the bug: something pushed and never removed.

nodes.label: Rising heapUsed under stable load
nodes.rationale: Live set not returning after GC. Growth that tracks traffic may be a working set or a poorly intended unbounded cache.

nodes.label: Common leak sources
nodes.rationale: Most Node leaks are unbounded caches, never-removed listeners, closures over large objects, or uncleared timers/sockets.

nodes.label: Unbounded cache leak
nodes.rationale: Module-level Map with no max or TTL. Bound by count and bytes; LRU or Redis maxmemory.

nodes.label: Unremoved event listeners
nodes.rationale: The emitter retains the function, which retains its closed-over scope. on and off must share the same function reference.

nodes.label: Closure retention of large objects
nodes.rationale: A timer callback that closes over hugeBuffer keeps the allocation alive for the full delay. Close over the derived scalar instead.

nodes.label: Uncleared timers and handles
nodes.rationale: setInterval without clearInterval, plus unclosed servers, Redis clients, and fs.watch keep the process from settling.

nodes.label: CPU and heap profiling
nodes.rationale: When the event loop is hot or CPU is pegged, a profile shows which functions ate the samples.

nodes.label: --cpu-prof
nodes.rationale: Samples during the run and writes .cpuprofile on exit. Hard kill (-9) skips flush. Wrong tool when lag is low and you are I/O bound.

nodes.label: --heap-prof
nodes.rationale: Allocation timeline-style profile. For what is retained right now, prefer heap snapshots.

nodes.label: Node Inspector --inspect
nodes.rationale: Live CPU/Memory session without waiting for exit. Exposing --inspect on a public IP is a remote code surface — treat like a root shell.

nodes.label: Benchmarking
nodes.rationale: A benchmark answers a specific question under a specific load shape. A microbenchmark answers a different question with confidence it has not earned.

nodes.label: autocannon HTTP load
nodes.rationale: Right tool when the claim is about the running service: RPS plus p50/p95/p99, error rate, and server saturation under concurrency.

nodes.label: Microbenchmarks lie
nodes.rationale: V8 over-optimizes monomorphic toys, DCE can erase unused work, and a 3 ns win does not move p99 when the DB takes 40 ms.

nodes.label: Observe-result sink
nodes.rationale: Consume the microbench result into a sink the runtime cannot prove unused, or the work may vanish.

nodes.label: GC basics
nodes.rationale: V8 frees memory you can no longer reach. You control heap size, allocation rate, and whether GC pauses show up as event-loop lag.

nodes.label: Generational GC
nodes.rationale: New objects start young and cheap to collect (scavenges). Survivors age into old space with more expensive major GC.

nodes.label: --max-old-space-size
nodes.rationale: Roughly the old-space heap budget. Hitting it yields heap OOM; it is not a cgroup RSS limit. Too high on a small container lets the kernel OOMKiller fire first.

nodes.label: heap_size_limit vs flag value
nodes.rationale: Default limit ~4288 MB; --max-old-space-size=256 produced ~448 MB. The limit includes more than old space.

nodes.label: cgroup OOM vs V8 heap OOM
nodes.rationale: Kernel kills on container RSS including off-heap. Align the flag and container limits; watch RSS.

nodes.label: Flame graphs
nodes.rationale: Stacked picture of where CPU samples landed. Use when a CPU profile's call table is hard to see.

nodes.label: Flame graph width is sample time
nodes.rationale: Width is portion of samples in that stack frame subtree. Thin towers or empty app frames often mean I/O wait.

nodes.label: 0x flame graphs
nodes.rationale: Low-ceremony capture plus interactive HTML. Same family of data as --cpu-prof; automates visualization.

nodes.label: Clinic.js suite
nodes.rationale: Doctor for triage (CPU vs I/O vs memory), Flame for CPU, Bubbleprof for async delay, Heapprofiler for allocation views. On-demand or canary, not every prod pod.

nodes.label: Startup time
nodes.rationale: Cold-start and deploy latency until readiness. Optimize when you scale to zero or restart often; ignore it on a long-lived API that starts once a week.

nodes.label: module.enableCompileCache
nodes.rationale: Persists compilation artifacts. Measured status 1 under /tmp/node-compile-cache. Ephemeral /tmp in Kubernetes gives no cross-restart benefit.

nodes.label: Lazy imports
nodes.rationale: Eager slows boot, speeds first request. Lazy speeds boot, moves cost to first use. Eager-import the hot path.

nodes.label: Time to readiness
nodes.rationale: Measure the full ready path — load config, import routes, connect DB, listen — not only import time. DNS to Postgres can be 80% of the wait.

nodes.label: Phase 10 Observability and performance
nodes.rationale: Logs, traces, metrics, health, and the performance workflow that turns a 3 a.m. page into a measured change. Target Node 24.19.0.

nodes.label: 12-factor config
nodes.rationale: Config is injected by the environment, parsed once at boot, and refused loudly when required values are missing.

nodes.label: Env validation at boot
nodes.rationale: required() throws on missing DATABASE_URL. A throw here is a failed deploy, not a half-up process accepting traffic.

nodes.label: No default secrets
nodes.rationale: A default DATABASE_URL lets a misconfigured deploy silently talk to localhost or a shared dev DB.

nodes.label: NODE_ENV is not a feature flag
nodes.rationale: NODE_ENV=production changes dependency behaviour. Do not overload it for customer tier. Use explicit flags.

nodes.label: .env local only
nodes.rationale: Node 24 --env-file is for local development. Never the only copy of prod secrets. Env values are strings — parse booleans explicitly.

nodes.label: Boot sequence
nodes.rationale: Any other order accepts requests the process cannot serve, or fails half-way with sockets already open.

nodes.label: Validate, connect, listen, ready
nodes.rationale: Validate env, connect dependencies, start listening, then report ready. Listening early is the bug.

nodes.label: Parallel independent connects
nodes.rationale: Promise.all for Redis and Postgres is fine if both are required before ready. Optional deps can degrade without blocking ready.

nodes.label: Shutdown is the reverse of boot
nodes.rationale: SIGTERM → fail readiness → drain → close server → close pools → exit.

nodes.label: Dockerizing Node
nodes.rationale: A good Node image is small, runs as non-root, caches dependencies separately from app code, and does not copy secrets or laptop node_modules.

nodes.label: Multi-stage Docker build
nodes.rationale: deps / build / runner stages. Copy lockfile + package.json before source so code edits do not invalidate the dependency layer.

nodes.label: .dockerignore
nodes.rationale: Without it you send host node_modules and .env into the build context — slow and dangerous.

nodes.label: Non-root container user
nodes.rationale: USER after files are copied with correct ownership. Limits blast radius of filesystem and some remote exploits.

nodes.label: Exec-form CMD
nodes.rationale: CMD ["node", "dist/server.js"] so Node is PID 1 and receives signals. CMD npm start is a different footgun.

nodes.label: PID 1 and signal handling
nodes.rationale: If PID 1 is a shell or npm that never passes SIGTERM to Node, every deploy becomes a hard kill after the grace period.

nodes.label: npm start swallows SIGTERM
nodes.rationale: npm is often PID 1 and may not forward SIGTERM to the Node child, so graceful shutdown never runs.

nodes.label: SIGTERM then SIGKILL
nodes.rationale: Orchestrators send SIGTERM to PID 1, wait terminationGracePeriodSeconds (often 30s), then SIGKILL.

nodes.label: Node as PID 1
nodes.rationale: Exec Node directly in the image. Use npm scripts on the laptop. Register SIGTERM and SIGINT to drain and exit.

nodes.label: tini / dumb-init
nodes.rationale: If you must use a shell wrapper, a tiny init reaps zombies and forwards signals. Prefer avoiding the wrapper.

nodes.label: Environment parity
nodes.rationale: Parity is runtime version, config shape, and dependency graph — not copying production secrets onto laptops.

nodes.label: Same Node major and lockfile
nodes.rationale: Same Active LTS line in CI, staging, prod. One lockfile; immutable install. Same variable names, different values.

nodes.label: Honest staging
nodes.rationale: SQLite in staging while prod uses Postgres is a lie for dialects, transactions, and concurrency.

nodes.label: CI as an environment
nodes.rationale: Failures that only happen in CI are still production risks if CI matches prod closer than the laptop does.

nodes.label: Behind a reverse proxy
nodes.rationale: TLS usually terminates at the load balancer. Trust hop-by-hop headers only from that proxy or attackers forge client IPs.

nodes.label: X-Forwarded-* headers
nodes.rationale: X-Forwarded-For, Proto, Host, and RFC 7239 Forwarded. Only trust if the socket peer is your proxy.

nodes.label: trust proxy
nodes.rationale: Tell the framework how many hops of forwarded headers to trust when computing IP and protocol. Not blind true without understanding hop count.

nodes.label: TLS termination at the edge
nodes.rationale: Node often speaks HTTP on a private network. Redirects and Secure cookies must use X-Forwarded-Proto, not req.socket.encrypted.

nodes.label: Spoofed X-Forwarded-For
nodes.rationale: If Node is reachable directly, anyone can send X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4 and break rate limits, redirects, and cookies.

nodes.label: Zero-downtime deploys — rolling restarts, drain, readiness
Zero-downtime deploy
nodes.rationale: New pods take traffic before old pods die; old pods stop receiving work before they exit.

nodes.label: Kubernetes-style rolling update
nodes.rationale: Ready too early means users hit 500s; platform knobs are maxUnavailable and maxSurge.

nodes.label: Readiness gate and SIGTERM drain
nodes.rationale: On SIGTERM mark not-ready immediately, close the server, finish in-flight work, then exit.

nodes.label: Readiness is not liveness
nodes.rationale: Failing readiness removes traffic without killing the pod mid-drain; liveness restarts.

nodes.label: Expand/contract migrations
nodes.rationale: Old and new code run together during a rollout; schema must be compatible with both briefly.

nodes.label: terminationGracePeriodSeconds
nodes.rationale: Bounds how long SIGTERM has before SIGKILL; keep-alive sockets can hang server.close.

nodes.label: CI/CD — Node version matrix, caches, artifacts
Node CI/CD pipeline
nodes.rationale: Lockfile-faithful install, tests on production Node, and a reproducible artifact — not a rebuild on the deploy agent.

nodes.label: yarn install --immutable
nodes.rationale: Fail when the lockfile would change so CI cannot silently drift.

nodes.label: Promote image digest
nodes.rationale: Production must run the exact bits that passed staging, not a hopeful rebuild.

nodes.label: Node CI version matrix
nodes.rationale: Apps match production Node 24; libraries may matrix 22+24; canary Current is optional.

nodes.label: Cache package downloads not node_modules
nodes.rationale: Restored node_modules across OS/arch runners can restore wrong native binaries.

nodes.label: Image size and hardening — distroless, alpine, slim, libc
node:24-bookworm-slim
nodes.rationale: Default for most fullstack APIs: glibc addon compatibility plus multi-stage and non-root.

nodes.label: node:24-alpine musl
nodes.rationale: Smaller, but native prebuilds often target glibc first and fail or rebuild on musl.

nodes.label: Distroless Node image
nodes.rationale: Minimal shell and package manager reduce attack surface; debug with kubectl debug, not bash.

nodes.label: glibc vs musl for native addons
nodes.rationale: Pick slim/distroless/alpine from libc and ops needs, not from a blog title.

nodes.label: Node image hardening checklist
nodes.rationale: Non-root USER, read-only root FS, no secrets in layers, pin digests, drop capabilities.

nodes.label: Process managers — pm2, systemd, or the orchestrator
One owner for restarts and signals
nodes.rationale: In Kubernetes the orchestrator already restarts and health-checks; a second supervisor fights it.

nodes.label: systemd as VM supervisor
nodes.rationale: OS-native restart policy, env files, TimeoutStopSec, journald; ExecStart should be node, not npm.

nodes.label: pm2 inside Docker/K8s is double supervision
nodes.rationale: pm2 plus kubelet murky PID 1, disagreeing metrics, and logs stolen from stdout.

nodes.label: cluster module vs platform replicas
nodes.rationale: cluster multiplies processes on one machine; replicas multiply machines. Prefer replicas in K8s.

nodes.label: Scaling — vertical vs horizontal, cluster vs replicas
Vertical vs horizontal scaling
nodes.rationale: One Node process uses one JS core well for concurrent I/O; extra cores need more processes.

nodes.label: node:cluster on one machine
nodes.rationale: Prefer when packing cores on a single VM without an orchestrator; not usually inside each pod.

nodes.label: Horizontal replicas
nodes.rationale: Need stateless handling or a shared session store; connection pools multiply with replica count.

nodes.label: Autoscale on lag and saturation
nodes.rationale: CPU-only HPA misses I/O-bound APIs that are slow but idle on CPU.

nodes.label: Connection pool multiplication
nodes.rationale: Ten pods times pool size can knock over Postgres; right-size pools or use PgBouncer.

nodes.label: Semantic Versioning
nodes.rationale: MAJOR breaking, MINOR compatible feature, PATCH compatible fix — a promise to consumers.

nodes.label: Conventional commits
nodes.rationale: feat/fix/feat! machine-map to MINOR/PATCH/MAJOR and generate changelogs.

nodes.label: semantic-release automation
nodes.rationale: Optional automation of SemVer policy; still needs least-privilege write tokens in CI.

nodes.label: False patch
nodes.rationale: A PATCH-labeled release that changes behaviour consumers relied on — a SemVer violation.

nodes.label: Immutable digest plus human version tag
nodes.rationale: Kubernetes apps deploy by digest; a marketing/version tag is for humans, not latest.

nodes.label: Blue/green deploy
nodes.rationale: Two full environments; rollback is a second flip if sessions and schemas allow.

nodes.label: Canary deploy
nodes.rationale: Gradual traffic slice with metrics gates; include write paths so the mix is representative.

nodes.label: Rolling vs canary vs blue/green
nodes.rationale: Rolling is default K8s; canary shrinks blast radius at analysis cost; blue/green needs 2x capacity.

nodes.label: Canary metrics gates
nodes.rationale: Pods ready is not enough — watch errors, latency percentiles, lag, and business KPIs.

nodes.label: Serverless Node — cold starts, connection reuse, pooling
Cold start
nodes.rationale: New isolate pays runtime init, module graph import, and first DB connect before the first request.

nodes.label: Module-scope connection reuse
nodes.rationale: Warm reuse is good; hundreds of isolates times pool size exhausts Postgres — cap pool at 1 or use a proxy.

nodes.label: Serverless freeze model
nodes.rationale: Process may freeze without a SIGTERM you control; setInterval may pause; disk and global cache are per-isolate.

nodes.label: When serverless is the wrong default
nodes.rationale: Long-lived WebSockets, heavy steady CPU, or DB-heavy work without a pool proxy.

nodes.label: node:vm — and why it is not a security sandbox
node:vm
nodes.rationale: Runs a JS string in a configured V8 context for soft isolation, tests, and REPLs — not hostile code.

nodes.label: node:vm is not a security sandbox
nodes.rationale: Node documents vm as not a security mechanism; hostile code reaches the outer realm and process.

nodes.label: vm constructor-chain breakout
nodes.rationale: this.constructor.constructor("return process")() returned process.version v24.19.0 against createContext({}).

nodes.label: vm timeout is best-effort
nodes.rationale: Timeouts focus on the synchronous run; async scheduled work can outlive the option.

nodes.label: WebAssembly in Node — CPU-bound work when it fits
WebAssembly in Node
nodes.rationale: Portable near-native compute after a profile shows a CPU kernel; not a default architecture.

nodes.label: Wasm vs worker_threads vs N-API
nodes.rationale: Workers solve parallelism; Wasm solves faster sandboxed compute; N-API is full native power with a build matrix.

nodes.label: Wasm security is only as strong as imports
nodes.rationale: Not a security sandbox if the host exposes dangerous imports; no ambient Node fs inside the module.

nodes.label: V8 flags — what they actually control
--max-old-space-size
nodes.rationale: Most common production V8-related flag; heap_size_limit is not always equal to the number passed.

nodes.label: --trace-gc is diagnostic only
nodes.rationale: Log volume and overhead; not a production default. Random blog flags add unowned risk.

nodes.label: V8 heap limit vs cgroup RSS
nodes.rationale: Heap flag is V8's; cgroup kills on RSS including off-heap. Size them together.

nodes.label: Node-API stable ABI
nodes.rationale: Sits between C/C++ and Node/V8 so addons are less tied to V8 churn across majors than NAN.

nodes.label: node-addon-api
nodes.rationale: C++ wrappers over Node-API for safer, more ergonomic addon code.

nodes.label: process.versions.napi 10
nodes.rationale: Node-API version supported on Node 24.19.0.

nodes.label: Native addon prebuilds
nodes.rationale: Users and CI may lack compilers; ship binaries per platform via prebuildify/prebuild.

nodes.label: C++ addons and the embedder API
C++ addon
nodes.rationale: A shared library Node loads into the process via require of a .node file.

nodes.label: Node embedder API
nodes.rationale: Opposite direction: your C++ binary hosts Node/V8. Not the path for typical HTTP services.

nodes.label: Addon segfaults kill the process
nodes.rationale: Native memory corruption and signals abort outside JS try/catch.

nodes.label: FFI — calling native libraries without a full addon
Foreign Function Interface
nodes.rationale: Call C ABI functions from JS via a binding library without writing a dedicated addon.

nodes.label: FFI type declarations are load-bearing
nodes.rationale: A wrong struct layout or pointer lifetime is undefined behaviour at process level.

nodes.label: FFI vs Node-API addon
nodes.rationale: FFI trades build complexity for runtime binding risk; prefer a real addon for chatty or complex APIs.

nodes.label: WASI
nodes.rationale: Portable Wasm syscalls for files, clocks, and similar, mediated by the host — not a full OS.

nodes.label: uvwasi 0.0.23
nodes.rationale: Node's WASI implementation version via process.versions.uvwasi on Node 24.19.0.

nodes.label: WASI preopens
nodes.rationale: Map guest paths to host directories; overly broad maps leak or overwrite data. WASI is not safe because Wasm.

nodes.label: Custom module loaders and resolution hooks
Custom module loaders
nodes.rationale: Power tools for tooling authors — transpile, mock, policy — not the default for application code.

nodes.label: Do not transpile on the fly in production
nodes.rationale: Hurts startup, complicates debugging, and drifts from the artifact tested in CI.

nodes.label: V8/Node startup snapshot
nodes.rationale: Freezes initialized heap after bootstrap so the next launch skips re-parse; specialist lever for CLIs.

nodes.label: Compile cache vs startup snapshot
nodes.rationale: Compile cache stores compilation artifacts; snapshots store initialized heap state. Cache is the practical win for many apps.

nodes.label: Snapshots are tied to the Node/V8 build
nodes.rationale: Rebuild in CI per runtime artifact; native addons and listen() during bootstrap are not snapshot-safe.

nodes.label: Contributing to Node.js core
nodes.rationale: Large C++/JS monorepo with TSC governance and CITGM-scale impact; most product bugs are still in app code.

nodes.label: lib/ JS builtins vs src/ C++
Failing test then fix
nodes.rationale: Small PR: failing test first, then fix; explain why; follow existing style.

nodes.label: Node core SemVer compatibility culture
nodes.rationale: Millions of dependents; breaking changes are rare and deliberate. Features that belong in userland get closed.

nodes.label: Event loop phases
nodes.rationale: One thread, six phases in fixed order: timers, pending, idle/prepare, poll, check, close.

nodes.label: Timers phase
nodes.rationale: Runs expired setTimeout/setInterval; delay is a minimum, not a promise.

nodes.label: Check phase
nodes.rationale: Runs setImmediate; immediately after poll, so I/O callbacks see setImmediate before the next timers lap.

nodes.label: Close callbacks phase
nodes.rationale: Last phase of a tick — socket/server close events run after check even if destroy was called first.

nodes.label: nextTick and microtasks are not phases
nodes.rationale: Drained between every phase and every individual callback, so phase order alone does not predict output.

nodes.label: setTimeout(0) vs setImmediate race from main
nodes.rationale: From the main module the order depends on startup vs timer threshold; inside an I/O callback setImmediate is first.

nodes.label: process.getActiveResourcesInfo and unref
nodes.rationale: The process exits when no phase has work and nothing waits on I/O; unref excludes a handle from that count.

nodes.label: Poll phase
nodes.rationale: Run ready I/O callbacks, then decide whether to block and for how long. Where an idle server spends its life.

nodes.label: Poll blocking vs blocked event loop
nodes.rationale: Poll blocking is sleeping in a kernel call at ~0% CPU; a blocked loop is JS hogging the thread at 100% of one core.

nodes.label: epoll / kqueue / IOCP idle wait
nodes.rationale: Thousands of idle sockets cost file descriptors and almost no CPU because they share one blocking kernel call.

nodes.label: libuv thread pool signals poll
nodes.rationale: File reads, dns.lookup, crypto.pbkdf2 and zlib finish on the pool then wake poll; sockets do not compete for the pool.

nodes.label: setTimeout delay is a floor
nodes.rationale: Poll blocks at most until the nearest timer, then the loop must reach the timers phase; slow callbacks push firing later.

nodes.label: process.nextTick queue
nodes.rationale: Drains completely at a checkpoint, including entries added while draining, before the microtask queue. That complete drain is what makes recursive nextTick starvation possible.

nodes.label: Microtask queue
nodes.rationale: Promise.then, await resumptions and queueMicrotask. Drains after nextTick at a checkpoint, but once inside a microtask the microtask queue keeps draining first.

nodes.label: Macrotasks
nodes.rationale: Timers, setImmediate and I/O callbacks belong to event-loop phases and get one turn per lap. Microtasks and nextTick are not phases; they drain between every phase and every callback.

nodes.label: ESM top-level is a microtask
nodes.rationale: Module evaluation is a promise job, so nextTick scheduled at ESM top level runs after pending microtasks. Identical code as .cjs and .js prints different order.

nodes.label: queueMicrotask vs process.nextTick
nodes.rationale: Prefer queueMicrotask: portable, same queue as promises, less starvation. nextTick only when you must run before pending promise continuations, classically deferring an emit so a caller can subscribe.

nodes.label: await yields to the microtask queue
nodes.rationale: await does not give the event loop a turn. An await-heavy loop over in-memory values never runs timers or I/O; CPU-bound work needs setImmediate, a real phase.

nodes.label: setImmediate
nodes.rationale: Schedules into the check phase, after poll in the same lap. Use it to run after the current phase, yield so I/O can run, or chunk CPU work. Does not escape a blocked thread.

nodes.label: setTimeout(fn, 0) 1ms clamp
nodes.rationale: There is no true zero delay. The timer is clamped to 1ms and runs in the timers phase on a later lap. Almost always the wrong tool versus setImmediate.

nodes.label: Main-module setImmediate vs setTimeout race
nodes.rationale: Order depends on whether process startup took >=1ms before the first timers phase. Both orders are correct. CI machines are slower so the timer more often wins.

nodes.label: setImmediate wins inside an I/O callback
nodes.rationale: I/O callbacks run in poll; check is the next phase in the same lap. A timer must wait a full lap, so setImmediate always runs first inside any I/O callback.

nodes.label: nextTick starvation
nodes.rationale: Recursive process.nextTick never empties the queue, so the loop never advances. Process stays alive at 100% CPU with no error; timers, I/O and setImmediate never run.

nodes.label: nextTick drain-to-exhaustion rule
nodes.rationale: The nextTick queue drains including entries added during draining. Bounded recursion still delays the loop for the whole drain; await cannot fix it because microtasks also drain before the loop.

nodes.label: Recursive setImmediate does not starve
nodes.rationale: setImmediate schedules into check, one turn per lap, so timers fire and I/O is served. Recursion belongs on setImmediate, never on nextTick.

nodes.label: Event loop delay cannot detect starvation
nodes.rationale: The metric is sampled by a timer, and timers never run while starved. Use --cpu-prof or attach the inspector instead.

nodes.label: Timeout object
nodes.rationale: Node setTimeout/setInterval return a Timeout with unref, ref and refresh, not a number as in browsers. Treat the return as opaque.

nodes.label: Timer delay is a floor
nodes.rationale: The callback runs no earlier than the delay, when the loop next reaches timers and the thread is free. A long callback elsewhere delays it arbitrarily.

nodes.label: TimeoutOverflowWarning
nodes.rationale: Delays above 2147483647 ms (~24.8 days) overflow and fire immediately with a warning. Long schedules need stages or an absolute-time check.

nodes.label: setInterval drift and overlap
nodes.rationale: Schedules by period, not completion. Slow async work queues and spacing collapses. Prefer a self-scheduling timeout after the work finishes.

nodes.label: Timeout.unref
nodes.rationale: Removes a timer from the handles keeping the process alive without cancelling it. Use for background metrics, cache sweeps, heartbeats. process.getActiveResourcesInfo names leftover handles.

nodes.label: node:timers/promises
nodes.rationale: Cancellable sleep, async-iterable interval, awaitable setImmediate, scheduler.yield and scheduler.wait. Stop writing a hand-rolled sleep that leaks when abandoned.

nodes.label: Promise pending / fulfilled / rejected
nodes.rationale: Transitions exactly once from pending to fulfilled or rejected, then immutable. Settled means fulfilled or rejected. Resolved-with-a-promise stays pending until that one settles.

nodes.label: Promises are eager
nodes.rationale: Work starts when the promise is created, not when it is awaited. To defer, wrap creation in a function. Settling twice is a silent no-op.

nodes.label: Return or it is not chained
nodes.rationale: .then returns a new promise that adopts whatever the handler returns. Forget return and the inner work detaches; its rejection is unhandled.

nodes.label: Promise.prototype.finally
nodes.rationale: Runs on both paths and passes the outcome through. Return value is ignored; throw inside finally replaces the outcome.

nodes.label: .then(f, g) vs .then(f).catch(g)
nodes.rationale: Two-argument g only sees upstream rejections, not errors thrown by f. A chained .catch is downstream of f. Prefer .then().catch().

nodes.label: async function
nodes.rationale: Makes the function return a promise and permits await. Return fulfils; throw rejects. Adds no capability beyond promises, only syntax.

nodes.label: await is a microtask yield
nodes.rationale: Body runs synchronously until the first await; resumption is a microtask. Does not yield to timers or I/O. await setImmediate() is the real phase yield.

nodes.label: await accepts any thenable
nodes.rationale: Non-promises are wrapped and still cost a microtask. await null is a cheap yield to microtasks only.

nodes.label: Top-level await
nodes.rationale: ES modules can await outside a function; importers wait. The module cannot be require()d from CommonJS.

nodes.label: await inside forEach
nodes.rationale: Array.prototype.forEach ignores the returned promise, so the callback is fire-and-forget. Use for...of sequentially or Promise.all(map) in parallel.

nodes.label: Promise.all
nodes.rationale: Settles when all fulfil; rejects immediately on first failure. Attaches handlers to every input so later rejections are handled but silently discarded. Starts everything at once — not a concurrency limiter.

nodes.label: Promise.allSettled
nodes.rationale: Never rejects. Returns {status, value|reason} per input. Use when partial success is meaningful.

nodes.label: Promise.race
nodes.rationale: Settles with the first to settle, success or failure. Stops waiting, not working — losers keep running. Use AbortSignal for real cancellation.

nodes.label: Promise.any
nodes.rationale: Settles with the first to fulfil, ignoring rejections. Rejects only if all reject, with AggregateError.errors. Use for redundant sources.

nodes.label: Promises have no cancellation
nodes.rationale: all rejecting or race resolving does not stop other work. Timed-out HTTP still holds its socket; raced queries still occupy pool connections.

nodes.label: Sequential independent awaits
nodes.rationale: Three independent awaits sum their latencies. Test: does this line need the previous line's value? If not, start together with Promise.all.

nodes.label: map plus Promise.all
nodes.rationale: Preserves input order regardless of completion. Starts every item at once — a few dozen is fine; thousands need a bounded pool.

nodes.label: Create then await is already parallel
nodes.rationale: Promises are eager, so creating both before either await is parallel. Separate awaits risk unhandled rejection if one rejects before its await. Promise.all is the safer default.

nodes.label: When sequential is right
nodes.rationale: Dependency chains, rate limits, ordered writes, and memory. Parallel is useless for CPU-bound work on one thread.

nodes.label: try/catch with await
nodes.rationale: A rejected promise that you await throws at the await. If there is no await, there is no catch — the try finishes synchronously.

nodes.label: Catch only what you can handle
nodes.rationale: A giant try cannot say what failed. Recover, add context, or let the rest propagate to a boundary. Log-and-rethrow unchanged is usually noise.

nodes.label: error.cause
nodes.rationale: throw new HigherLevelError(msg, { cause: original }) keeps the root attached. Tooling prints the chain.

nodes.label: .catch placement
nodes.rationale: Covers everything upstream, nothing downstream. Mid-chain recovers and the chain continues fulfilled; end-of-chain is a safety net.

nodes.label: Floating promise
nodes.rationale: A promise-returning call nobody awaited or handled. Rejection is fatal since Node 15; fulfilment may silently skip a side effect. Happens via forgotten await, forEach, or missing return in .then.

nodes.label: void plus .catch for fire-and-forget
nodes.rationale: void marks intent for readers and linters; .catch is what makes it safe. Never leave the catch off.

nodes.label: @typescript-eslint/no-floating-promises
nodes.rationale: Flags discarded promise results; no-misused-promises catches forEach and async callbacks where sync is expected. Both need TypeScript types.

nodes.label: Error-first callback convention
nodes.rationale: cb(err) or cb(null, value), exactly once, always asynchronously. Mixed sync/async firing is why you defer early returns with process.nextTick.

nodes.label: util.promisify
nodes.rationale: Assumes last argument is error-first (err, value) called once. Multiple success values, wrong this, or non-standard shape need a manual wrapper or promisify.custom.

nodes.label: util.callbackify
nodes.rationale: Hands an async function to a callback consumer. Rare in apps; for libraries keeping a callback API over promises.

nodes.label: util.promisify.custom
nodes.rationale: Author-defined promise form when the mechanical translation is wrong. promisify checks that symbol first.

nodes.label: new Promise only wraps callback APIs
nodes.rationale: The one legitimate use of the Promise constructor. Prefer built-in fs/promises, dns/promises, timers/promises, stream/promises over promisify.

nodes.label: Unbounded Promise.all
nodes.rationale: Starts every item immediately. Hits 429s, pool timeouts, EMFILE, memory, then a burst of callbacks. Fine at 20 items; an outage at 10,000.

nodes.label: mapLimit worker pool
nodes.rationale: Exactly N workers claim the next index with next++. Single-threaded so the increment needs no lock. results[i] preserves order. First worker rejection can abandon the rest.

nodes.label: Chunked Promise.all vs worker pool
nodes.rationale: Each batch waits for its slowest member so one slow item idles workers. A pool keeps every worker busy. Batching is fine when items are uniform.

nodes.label: Picking a concurrency limit
nodes.rationale: Derive from the bottleneck: API rate limit, pool size, or in-flight memory. Right value is where throughput stops improving. CPU-bound work is not helped by concurrency.

nodes.label: unhandledRejection
nodes.rationale: Fatal by default since Node 15 (exit code 1). --unhandled-rejections=warn restores the old warn-and-continue for a temporary audit only.

nodes.label: uncaughtException
nodes.rationale: Synchronous throw escaped every try/catch. State afterwards is unknown, likely corrupt. Definitely not safe to continue.

nodes.label: Process crash handler
nodes.rationale: Log first, stop accepting, drain in-flight, hard-cap with unrefed setTimeout, be idempotent. Pair with SIGTERM. Set exitCode rather than immediate process.exit so stdout drains.

nodes.label: Log and continue is wrong
nodes.rationale: After an uncaught exception a function stopped partway — lock, transaction, counter, half-written file. Restart into a known state.

nodes.label: rejectionHandled
nodes.rationale: A handler attached on a later tick fires this after Node already reported unhandled. Attach handlers at creation time.

nodes.label: Branch on err.code not err.message
nodes.rationale: Messages are prose — reworded, translated, interpolated. code is the contract. Node uses ENOENT. instanceof fails across dual package copies; code survives.

nodes.label: Custom error class
nodes.rationale: Extend Error, set name and a stable code, carry structured context as properties, forward options so cause works. Keep the hierarchy shallow.

nodes.label: Operational vs programmer errors
nodes.rationale: Operational (timeout, 404, disk full) is expected — handle it. Programmer (TypeError, typo) is a bug — crash. Retrying TypeError loops forever; crashing on 404 is absurd.

nodes.label: isOperational flag
nodes.rationale: Boundary returns statusCode and code for operational errors; programmer errors shut the process down.

nodes.label: Never leak internals in error responses
nodes.rationale: Return a stable code plus requestId. Log the stack server-side. Never send SQL or stack traces to the client.

nodes.label: AggregateError
nodes.rationale: Several failures, one reason is not enough. Promise.any throws one; use it for batches where the caller needs every failure.

nodes.label: Explicit construction antipattern
nodes.rationale: Wrapping an already-promise API in new Promise adds a forgotten-reject path and a never-settling promise. new Promise belongs only around callback or event APIs.

nodes.label: Async Promise executor
nodes.rationale: throw rejects the executor's own promise, which nobody holds. The constructed promise stays pending forever. On modern Node the orphaned rejection is a fatal unhandledRejection.

nodes.label: Nesting .then instead of chaining
nodes.rationale: Rebuilds the callback pyramid. Inner promises are floating; an outer .catch never sees their rejections.

nodes.label: Forgotten return inside .then
nodes.rationale: a => { get(a); } returns undefined so the chain resolves immediately while inner work is unwatched. Concise a => get(a) avoids it.

nodes.label: return await inside try is not redundant
nodes.rationale: Without await the promise is returned before it settles, so the enclosing catch never runs. Everywhere else return await just adds microtask ticks.

nodes.label: for await...of
nodes.rationale: Awaits each value so it can iterate sequences that arrive over time. Strictly sequential — never parallel. Use a pool for independent items.

nodes.label: async function*
nodes.rationale: await inside, yield out. Consumer pulls one value at a time so the producer does no work in advance and only one item is in memory.

nodes.label: Symbol.asyncIterator
nodes.rationale: for await looks for a next() that returns a promise of {value, done}. Async generators produce this protocol.

nodes.label: Pull-based backpressure
nodes.rationale: The generator suspends at yield until the consumer asks for the next value. A slow consumer automatically slows the producer.

nodes.label: Generator finally cleanup on break
nodes.rationale: break, return and throw call iterator.return(), resuming the generator at finally. That is where to close a file handle or connection.

nodes.label: Promises cannot be cancelled
nodes.rationale: A promise is a view of a result, not a handle on the work. Many consumers can await the same promise; cancelling for one would break the rest.

nodes.label: AbortController
nodes.rationale: The remote: only the owner calls abort(). Hand callees the signal, never the controller.

nodes.label: AbortSignal
nodes.rationale: Read-only side: aborted, reason, throwIfAborted, abort event. Operations reject with a generic AbortError; custom reason is on signal.reason. Check aborted before listening — the event does not re-fire.

nodes.label: AbortSignal.timeout
nodes.rationale: Replaces racing a promise against setTimeout and actually stops the work. Timer is unrefed so it will not hold the process open.

nodes.label: AbortSignal.any
nodes.rationale: Aborts when any input aborts and adopts that reason. Cancellation counterpart of Promise.race for combining user cancel, deadline and shutdown.

nodes.label: Thread { signal } through every layer
nodes.rationale: Cancellation is cooperative. One layer that drops the signal makes everything below uncancellable. Call throwIfAborted between units of work.

nodes.label: AsyncLocalStorage
nodes.rationale: Per-request store that Node restores across await, timers and I/O. Solves request-id-in-every-log without a ctx parameter. A module-level variable is overwritten by interleaved requests.

nodes.label: AsyncLocalStorage.run
nodes.rationale: Scopes the store to fn and its async descendants. getStore() is undefined outside any run. Prefer a fresh object per request.

nodes.label: enterWith leaks context
nodes.rationale: Sets the store for the rest of the current async context with no visible boundary. Prefer run(). enterWith is for framework points with no callback.

nodes.label: ALS is hidden state with a cost
nodes.rationale: Use only for cross-cutting concerns (trace ids, tenant, current transaction). Pass real arguments for domain data. Async context tracking makes operations measurably slower.

nodes.label: executionAsyncId and triggerAsyncId
nodes.rationale: Every async operation gets an id and the id of what created it. That tree is what AsyncLocalStorage walks. Context is lost wherever the tree is broken.

nodes.label: async_hooks.createHook
nodes.rationale: Stability 1 experimental. Fires on every async operation. console.log inside a hook recurses. Exists for APM vendors. Use ALS or diagnostics_channel instead.

nodes.label: AsyncResource.bind
nodes.rationale: Captures async context at bind time and restores it when the callback runs. Fix for EventEmitter listeners and queues that store callbacks.

nodes.label: EventEmitter listener context loss
nodes.rationale: Listeners run in the context of emit, not registration. A listener registered inside als.run still loses the store if emit happens in a timer.

nodes.label: diagnostics_channel
nodes.rationale: Supported instrumentation: named channels, near-zero cost when nobody is subscribed. Prefer over createHook.

nodes.label: CPU-bound work
nodes.rationale: Busy work (JSON.parse of 50MB, image resize, bcrypt sync, ReDoS) holds the single thread. Waiting I/O is fine. Node's genuine weakness; the fix is never async.

nodes.label: async does not stop blocking
nodes.rationale: async changes the return value, not whether the body blocks. There is no await that makes a for loop yield.

nodes.label: Chunk CPU work with setImmediate
nodes.rationale: Yield to check so pending I/O runs. Aim 10–50ms per chunk. Improves others' latency, not throughput. Occasional work that splits naturally.

nodes.label: worker_threads for CPU work
nodes.rationale: Real parallelism on another thread. Spawning is expensive — use a piscina pool, not one worker per request. Data copies via structured clone; transfer ArrayBuffers.

nodes.label: Async crypto on the libuv thread pool
nodes.rationale: crypto.pbkdf2, scrypt and async bcrypt run off the loop; *Sync variants block it. Often the cheapest real fix.

nodes.label: Event loop delay misses a fully blocked loop
nodes.rationale: Sampled by a timer that cannot fire while blocked. A 1.2s block reported worst gap 0ms because it recorded no samples. Missing data is the signal.

nodes.label: Phase 2 — Async and the event loop
Phase 2 output-order gate
nodes.rationale: Move on when you can predict order of nextTick, queueMicrotask, resolved promise, setTimeout(0) and setImmediate, including that nextTick priority depends on already being inside a microtask.

nodes.label: Buffer
nodes.rationale: Fixed-length raw bytes outside the V8 heap. Strings are UTF-16; network and disk are bytes. Every Node I/O boundary hands you one.

nodes.label: Buffer.from and Buffer.alloc
nodes.rationale: from encodes text or copies exact bytes; alloc zeros safely. new Buffer is deprecated DEP0005 and unsafe.

nodes.label: Buffer.length is bytes
nodes.rationale: héllo is 5 characters and 6 UTF-8 bytes. Content-Length and size limits must use Buffer.byteLength, not str.length.

nodes.label: JSON.stringify of a Buffer
nodes.rationale: Produces {type:Buffer,data:[...]}. Convert with toString(base64) or toString() before res.json.

nodes.label: Buffer.subarray shares memory
nodes.rationale: A view, not a copy. Buffer.prototype.slice is an alias and unlike Array/Uint8Array.slice does not copy. Return a copy for anything you store.

nodes.label: Buffer.concat
nodes.rationale: Pass totalLength when known to skip a summing pass. Collect HTTP body as buffers then concat once — never string-concatenate chunks.

nodes.label: crypto.timingSafeEqual vs Buffer.equals
nodes.rationale: equals short-circuits on the first differing byte — a timing oracle for tokens and HMACs.

nodes.label: Collect HTTP body with a size limit
nodes.rationale: Sum chunk.length, destroy and 413 past the limit, then Buffer.concat(chunks, size). Counting characters lets multi-byte payloads through.

nodes.label: Buffer encodings
nodes.rationale: An encoding is the rule for turning bytes into text and back. Wrong choice yields mojibake, silent truncation, or a size limit off by 33% — nothing throws.

nodes.label: utf8 encoding
nodes.rationale: Default and lossless for all text. 1–4 bytes per character. There is no case where ascii beats utf8.

nodes.label: base64 vs base64url
nodes.rationale: base64url swaps +/ for -_ and drops = padding for JWTs and URL-safe tokens. Node accepts both alphabets; other languages do not.

nodes.label: latin1 vs ascii
nodes.rationale: latin1 maps every byte 0–255 to the same code point and round-trips bytes. ascii masks the high bit and silently destroys bytes above 127.

nodes.label: Invalid UTF-8 becomes U+FFFD
nodes.rationale: Buffer.toString('utf8') substitutes the replacement character and does not throw, so corruption travels into storage.

nodes.label: TextDecoder fatal true
nodes.rationale: Only built-in way to make bad bytes loud: throws TypeError on malformed UTF-8. Use at trust boundaries.

nodes.label: Base64 decode is not validation
nodes.rationale: Node's decoder ignores characters outside the alphabet and tolerates missing padding, so garbage still decodes.

nodes.label: Base64 +33% size cost
nodes.rationale: 3 bytes become 4 ASCII chars. Acceptable for tokens and data URIs; wrong for file payloads — use multipart or raw binary.

nodes.label: Buffer.alloc
nodes.rationale: Zero-fills and never uses the pool. Default for anything holding user data, secrets, or crossing a response boundary.

nodes.label: Buffer.allocUnsafe
nodes.rationale: Returns recently freed process memory unzeroed — about 20× faster. Must overwrite every byte before anything reads it.

nodes.label: Buffer pool
nodes.rationale: 64 KB slab (Buffer.poolSize 65536 in Node 24). allocUnsafe below half the pool is carved from the slab. buf.buffer is the whole shared slab.

nodes.label: Buffer.allocUnsafeSlow
nodes.rationale: Skips the pool: own exactly-sized ArrayBuffer, byteOffset 0. Still uninitialized; safe to retain long-term.

nodes.label: new Buffer deprecated DEP0005
nodes.rationale: A numeric argument dispatched to allocUnsafe, so new Buffer(req.body.size) was a remote memory disclosure. Split into Buffer.from and Buffer.alloc.

nodes.label: allocUnsafe memory disclosure
nodes.rationale: After 5000 fake request bodies, 44% of subsequent 80-byte allocUnsafe calls contained the password. Mechanism behind CVE-2016-2216-class bugs.

nodes.label: Buffer extends Uint8Array
nodes.rationale: Same memory model plus encoding methods, numeric read/write, and the pool. Why crypto.subtle, fetch, TextDecoder and Web Streams accept a Buffer.

nodes.label: Buffer.slice shares memory
nodes.rationale: Buffer.prototype.slice returns a view; Uint8Array.prototype.slice copies. Use subarray for a view and Buffer.from for a copy.

nodes.label: Buffer.from copy vs view overloads
nodes.rationale: Buffer.from(typedArray) and Buffer.from(buffer) copy. Buffer.from(arrayBuffer[, offset, length]) creates a view.

nodes.label: Prefer Uint8Array outside Node
nodes.rationale: Buffer is a Node global. Shared browser/Worker/Deno code should use Uint8Array plus TextEncoder/TextDecoder.

nodes.label: StringDecoder
nodes.rationale: Holds a partial trailing byte sequence and prepends it to the next write so multi-byte characters split on chunk boundaries survive.

nodes.label: Per-chunk toString corruption
nodes.rationale: Chunk boundaries fall on bytes, not characters. Decoding each half independently substitutes U+FFFD and the character is lost irreversibly.

nodes.label: stream.setEncoding
nodes.rationale: Installs a StringDecoder internally. After string mode you cannot recover exact bytes; size limits become character counts.

nodes.label: Character vs token boundaries
nodes.rationale: StringDecoder fixes character boundaries only. A regex still misses a token split across chunks — that needs a framing Transform.

nodes.label: Endianness
nodes.rationale: BE stores the most significant byte first (network byte order). LE stores the least first. Wrong order yields a valid but wrong number with no error.

nodes.label: Buffer typed read and write
nodes.rationale: Uniform family: read/write + type + BE/LE. Named methods throw ERR_BUFFER_OUT_OF_BOUNDS or ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE; index assign wraps modulo 256.

nodes.label: readBigInt64 / readBigUInt64
nodes.rationale: A JS number holds integers exactly only to 2^53−1. Database IDs and Snowflake IDs must stay BigInt.

nodes.label: Length-prefixed framing
nodes.rationale: Fixed header of type plus payload length, then payload. Buffer remainder on incomplete frames. Validate attacker-controlled length before allocating.

nodes.label: DataView endianness API
nodes.rationale: Same ground with per-call littleEndian. Portable to the browser. Use in shared code; Buffer named methods in Node-only parsers.

nodes.label: Index assign skips validation
nodes.rationale: buf[i] = 256 stores 0 with no throw. writeUInt8 throws ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE, which a parser wants on a malformed frame.

nodes.label: Streams keep memory constant
nodes.rationale: Process data in chunks so peak memory is independent of input size. 216 MB log: 670 MB RSS buffered vs 88 MB streamed.

nodes.label: V8 MAX_STRING_LENGTH
nodes.rationale: 0x1fffffe8 characters (~512 MB). readFile utf8 or toString on a larger file throws ERR_STRING_TOO_LONG with no workaround except streaming.

nodes.label: When not to stream
nodes.rationale: If data is bounded and small, buffer it. Streaming costs error handling, backpressure, and forbids whole-value ops like JSON.parse.

nodes.label: A chunk is not a line
nodes.rationale: Default high water mark is 64 KB (raised from 16 KB in Node 22). Chunks split lines, JSON records and multi-byte characters arbitrarily.

nodes.label: Readable stream
nodes.rationale: Source: for await, pipe/pipeline, or events. Mixing consumers loses data. Paused mode is pull — backpressure comes free.

nodes.label: Writable stream
nodes.rationale: _write callback means done with this chunk. Forget it and the stream hangs with no error. end() is required for final/finish.

nodes.label: Duplex stream
nodes.rationale: Independent read and write halves, e.g. net.Socket. end() sends FIN on write only; stream.finished waits for both.

nodes.label: Transform stream
nodes.rationale: Duplex where output derives from input. Transform is a Duplex is a Readable, so it can sit anywhere in a pipeline.

nodes.label: PassThrough
nodes.rationale: Transform that changes nothing. Used to tap a pipeline, expose a stream before its source exists, or fan out.

nodes.label: Readable.from
nodes.rationale: Turns an array, iterable, or async generator into a stream. Replaces most custom Readables.

nodes.label: _write callback contract
nodes.rationale: Call callback exactly once on every path. Never calling it hangs forever; twice throws ERR_MULTIPLE_CALLBACK.

nodes.label: Backpressure
nodes.rationale: write() returns false when the destination queue hits highWaterMark. Ignoring it moves data into an unbounded in-memory queue.

nodes.label: write() returns false
nodes.rationale: Does not mean the write failed — the chunk was queued. Means stop until drain. 4000×64KB ignored: 250 MB queued vs 0 KB respected.

nodes.label: drain event
nodes.rationale: Fires when the queue falls below the high water mark. Use once, not on — on inside a loop leaks listeners and trips MaxListenersExceededWarning.

nodes.label: writableLength
nodes.rationale: Queued byte (or object) count. Direct measure of backpressure; legitimate disconnect threshold for a slow consumer.

nodes.label: Fan-out without per-client backpressure
nodes.rationale: One slow client queues at the full production rate and can OOM the server. Check write() per destination; drop, throttle, or disconnect laggards.

nodes.label: stream.pipeline
nodes.rationale: Errors from any stage in one place; every stream destroyed on any outcome; backpressure wired between stages. Import from node:stream/promises.

nodes.label: .pipe()
nodes.rationale: Does not forward errors or clean up. A mid-chain failure leaves handles open (EMFILE) or an unhandled error event kills the process.

nodes.label: pipeline AbortSignal
nodes.rationale: Pass { signal } so client disconnect tears the chain down with AbortError ABORT_ERR. { end: false } keeps the destination open.

nodes.label: Never .pipe() in a server
nodes.rationale: Every .pipe() in a request handler is a latent descriptor leak. After a Transform error, src.destroyed and dst.destroyed were both false.

nodes.label: for await of Readable
nodes.rationale: Default way to read a stream: backpressure, try/catch errors, automatic cleanup. Next chunk is requested only when the loop body finishes.

nodes.label: stream/consumers
nodes.rationale: text, json, buffer, arrayBuffer, blob collect a whole stream. No size limit of their own — never point at unbounded input.

nodes.label: readline createInterface
nodes.rationale: Line-oriented async iterable. crlfDelay: Infinity treats \r\n as one break so Windows files do not leave a stray \r.

nodes.label: Readable iterator helpers
nodes.rationale: map, filter, take, reduce, toArray and more since v17. Stability 1 Experimental in Node 24. map/filter accept { concurrency }.

nodes.label: break destroys the stream
nodes.rationale: break, return and throw call the iterator return(), which destroys the stream. It cannot be resumed.

nodes.label: on data async has no backpressure
nodes.rationale: .on() ignores the returned promise, so the source keeps emitting while every handler runs concurrently.

nodes.label: Flowing vs paused mode
nodes.rationale: readableFlowing is null (no consumer), true (pushing via data), or false (paused after flowing). on('data'), pipe, resume switch to flowing.

nodes.label: Stream events end finish close
nodes.rationale: end is readable exhausted and only fires if consumed. finish is writable flushed after end(). close is last and the only event guaranteed after error.

nodes.label: Late data handler data-loss window
nodes.rationale: Once flowing, chunks emitted before a handler attaches are gone. One tick after resume received 0 of 3 chunks.

nodes.label: readable event plus read n
nodes.rationale: Explicit pull API. read(n) returns exactly n bytes or null — the one thing for await cannot do. Do not mix with data.

nodes.label: Cleanup on close not end
nodes.rationale: destroy(err) emits error then close, never end. Cleanup in end leaks on every failure. Prefer finished() or pipeline.

nodes.label: objectMode
nodes.rationale: Carries arbitrary JS values. High water mark counts items (default 16) not bytes (65536). Writing an object to a byte stream throws ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE synchronously.

nodes.label: One-sided object mode
nodes.rationale: readableObjectMode is bytes in, records out (parser). writableObjectMode is records in, bytes out (serialiser).

nodes.label: push null is end of stream
nodes.rationale: push(null) terminates in every mode. A legitimate null value must be wrapped. undefined is likewise unusable.

nodes.label: Object-mode memory is unmeasured
nodes.rationale: Sixteen 10 MB documents is 160 MB. No coalescing: each object is a separate _write. Lower the mark or batch with _writev.

nodes.label: Readable.from high water mark 1
nodes.rationale: Object mode on, hwm 1 so a generator wrapping a paged API does not prefetch.

nodes.label: Web Streams
nodes.rationale: WHATWG ReadableStream, WritableStream, TransformStream. Globals in Node since v18. fetch bodies are web streams.

nodes.label: Readable.toWeb and fromWeb
nodes.rationale: Convert at the boundary. Node chunks are Buffers; web chunks are Uint8Array. Each conversion adds a queue — convert once.

nodes.label: fetch Response.body
nodes.rationale: A ReadableStream. pipeline(Readable.fromWeb(res.body), createWriteStream) streams a download; res.arrayBuffer buffers the whole file.

nodes.label: Web stream locking and tee
nodes.rationale: Exactly one reader; getReader/for await/pipeTo lock. res.json() then res.text() fails. tee/clone buffers the slower branch.

nodes.label: Default to Node streams in Node
nodes.rationale: Node streams have pipeline, object mode and every Node API. Use web streams for edge/browser or when you never leave fetch/Response.

nodes.label: zlib Transform streams
nodes.rationale: createGzip, createDeflate, createBrotliCompress drop into a pipeline with constant memory. Use streams for file- or response-sized data.

nodes.label: gzip compression level
nodes.rationale: Default 6. Level 9 is 2.2× CPU for 0.8% smaller. Level 1 is half the CPU for 16% larger — usually right for dynamic responses.

nodes.label: brotli default quality 11
nodes.rationale: 75.7 s on 19 MB vs 0.78 s gzip level 6. Intended for pre-compressed static assets. Per-request brotli needs quality 4.

nodes.label: zlib on libuv thread pool
nodes.rationale: Async zlib runs on the four-thread pool shared with fs and dns.lookup. *Sync variants block the main thread for the whole duration.

nodes.label: Zip bomb maxOutputLength
nodes.rationale: A few KB of gzip can expand to gigabytes. maxOutputLength throws ERR_BUFFER_TOO_LARGE. Never decompress untrusted input without a ceiling.

nodes.label: Compress in nginx or CDN
nodes.rationale: Keeps CPU off the event loop and the libuv pool. Compress in Node only for files you write, required upstreams, or no proxy.

nodes.label: Custom Readable _read
nodes.rationale: _read is a request: eventually push or push(null). push() false means stop. Never throw — this.destroy(err). Never call _read yourself.

nodes.label: Custom Writable _write _writev _final
nodes.rationale: _writev receives the queued batch — one INSERT per drain instead of per row. _final flushes the partial batch; forget it and last rows vanish.

nodes.label: _destroy resource cleanup
nodes.rationale: Runs exactly once on success and failure. Only correct place to release a connection or delete a temp file. pipeline calls destroy on every stream.

nodes.label: Prefer Readable.from over a class
nodes.rationale: Write the class only for pull control, _writev batching, or _destroy cleanup. Generators have no _read/callback contract.

nodes.label: stream.finished
nodes.rationale: One promise for end, finish, error and close. Fires on every path unlike end. { cleanup: true } removes listeners; { signal } cancels.

nodes.label: stream.compose
nodes.rationale: Glues stages into one Duplex so a multi-stage pipeline ships as one value. Stability 1 Experimental. Always consume through pipeline.

nodes.label: Readable.from string special case
nodes.rationale: Strings and Buffers emit as one chunk, not per character. Other iterables emit one chunk per element.

nodes.label: consumers impose no size limit
nodes.rationale: await json(req) will buffer a 2 GB body. Size-limit first, then collect.

nodes.label: highWaterMark
nodes.rationale: How much a stream buffers before backpressure. Node 24 defaults: 65536 bytes, 16 object-mode items. Raised from 16 KiB in Node 22.

nodes.label: High water mark throughput curve
nodes.rationale: 4 KB is 10× slower than 64 KB on a 216 MB file; 1 MB is no faster than 256 KB. Default sits where the curve flattens.

nodes.label: When to raise or lower highWaterMark
nodes.rationale: Raise for sequential bulk reads (ceiling ~256 KB). Lower for heavy objects, many concurrent sockets, or latency-sensitive SSE. Peak ≈ sum of stage marks × connections.

nodes.label: Phase 3 Buffers and streams
nodes.rationale: Two ideas: a Buffer is raw bytes outside the V8 heap, and a stream keeps memory constant no matter how much data arrives. 19 pages, Node 24.19.0.

nodes.label: Phase 3 gate pipeline
nodes.rationale: Stream-process a file larger than RAM: read, SplitLines, redact, gzip level 1, write, with signal. Must explain write false, pipe leaks, and redaction without framing.

nodes.label: _transform and _flush
nodes.rationale: _transform handles each chunk and emits zero or more outputs. _flush runs after input ends and emits buffered state such as a trailing partial line.

nodes.label: Transform chunk boundary problem
