nodes.rationale: A per-chunk regex misses a token that straddles two chunks. A tok_live_ secret split across chunks was not redacted.

nodes.label: SplitLines framing Transform
nodes.rationale: Holds everything after the last newline as #tail; _flush emits the remainder. Frame into records first, then operate on whole records.

nodes.label: Frame then match
nodes.rationale: One stage re-frames bytes into records; downstream transforms then work on complete records and become trivially correct.

nodes.label: decodeStrings
nodes.rationale: Default true converts written strings to Buffers before _transform. decodeStrings: false passes the original string through.

nodes.label: Transform is sequential
nodes.rationale: One chunk at a time preserves order and forbids parallelism. Concurrent work belongs on readable.map({ concurrency }) or a bounded pool.

nodes.label: Async generator pipeline stage
nodes.rationale: Same backpressure and error propagation with no callback contract. Write a class when you need a reusable object, _writev, _destroy, or custom hwm.

nodes.label: Transform streams topic
nodes.rationale: Reusable middle of a pipeline. Two methods — _transform and _flush — and the difficulty is that chunk boundaries do not respect data structure.

nodes.label: node:fs/promises
nodes.rationale: Default filesystem API. Every operation returns a promise, errors are ordinary exceptions with a code, nothing blocks the event loop.

nodes.label: writeFile truncates
nodes.rationale: writeFile overwrites an existing file. appendFile or { flag: 'a' } appends; { flag: 'wx' } fails with EEXIST if the file exists.

nodes.label: fs error codes
nodes.rationale: Branch on err.code never err.message. ENOENT, EEXIST, EACCES, EISDIR, ENOSPC, EMFILE, EXDEV. Swallowing every error hides EACCES as an empty config.

nodes.label: rename atomicity
nodes.rationale: Atomic within one filesystem. EXDEV across devices — common when /tmp is a separate mount. Put the temp file in the destination directory.

nodes.label: fs on libuv thread pool
nodes.rationale: 200 async reads 45 ms with 23 timer ticks; 200 sync reads 86 ms with 0 ticks. Unbounded Promise.all still hits EMFILE.

nodes.label: readFile vs stream
nodes.rationale: readFile is correct for bounded small files. If a user controls size, stream and cap — peak RSS is file size × concurrency.

nodes.label: Phase 4 — Filesystem, paths, and URLs
nodes.rationale: Complete 14-page phase on Node 24.19.0. Difficulty is failure modes: races, traversal, partial writes, leaked descriptors.

nodes.label: Phase 4 upload phase gate
nodes.rationale: A correct upload mid-stream limits, realpath-checks the destination, renames on one filesystem, and cleans up in finally.

nodes.label: The three flavors
nodes.rationale: Every fs operation exists as promise, callback, and sync. Promise is the default after listen.

nodes.label: fs callback, sync, and promise flavors
nodes.rationale: Import from node:fs/promises by default; node:fs callbacks are error-first; *Sync blocks the whole process.

nodes.label: Sync fs blocks the event loop
nodes.rationale: 200 readFileSync calls blocked a 1 ms timer for 86 ms with zero ticks; one thread owns JS until the syscall returns.

nodes.label: Sync fs only at startup, CLI, workers, crash handlers
nodes.rationale: Before server.listen there is no concurrency to protect. After listen, request paths use fs/promises.

nodes.label: Hidden sync I/O
nodes.rationale: require(), existsSync, template-engine loaders, and console.log to a file all do synchronous disk I/O.

nodes.label: node:path
nodes.rationale: Never build paths with + or templates. join vs resolve is a security boundary.

nodes.label: path.join
nodes.rationale: Concatenates and normalises; an absolute later argument is treated as a relative segment.

nodes.label: path.resolve
nodes.rationale: Always absolute; restarts at any absolute argument, discarding earlier segments.

nodes.label: join vs resolve is a security boundary
nodes.rationale: resolve gives the true final path to validate against a root; join can look contained after an absolute input.

nodes.label: path.posix
nodes.rationale: Use for URL paths, S3 keys, tar and git paths — always forward slashes. Default path is the host platform.

nodes.label: import.meta.dirname
nodes.rationale: ESM replacement for __dirname on Node 21.2+; undefined for non-file: URLs.

nodes.label: path.extname last extension only
nodes.rationale: report.tar.gz yields .gz. File-type checks from extname are bypassed by evil.php.jpg.

nodes.label: Path traversal
nodes.rationale: Any filesystem path from user input is a security boundary.

nodes.label: Path traversal attack
nodes.rationale: ../, absolute paths, encoded separators, and symlinks turn a file-serving endpoint into read-any-file.

nodes.label: Root plus separator containment check
nodes.rationale: After path.resolve, require equality with ROOT or startsWith(ROOT + path.sep). startsWith(ROOT) alone lets uploads-evil through.

nodes.label: realpath then re-check containment
nodes.rationale: A path inside the root can still be a symlink to ../secret.txt. String checks cannot see through links.

nodes.label: Zip-slip
nodes.rationale: Archive entries named ../../etc/cron.d/x write outside the extract directory unless each entry is containment-checked.

nodes.label: Store files under generated IDs
nodes.rationale: Best defence is not accepting paths: UUID storageKey plus metadata filename and ownership checks.

nodes.label: Decode user paths once before validating
nodes.rationale: ..%2f is a literal until something decodes it. Decode once, then validate; never after.

nodes.label: node:url
nodes.rationale: WHATWG URL and URLSearchParams are globals. url.parse is deprecated DEP0169.

nodes.label: WHATWG URL
nodes.rationale: Same objects as the browser. A leading slash on the two-argument form discards the base path.

nodes.label: url.parse deprecated DEP0169
nodes.rationale: Legacy parser differs from the standard and has caused SSRF and open-redirect bypasses.

nodes.label: URL host vs hostname
nodes.rationale: host includes the port; hostname does not. Allowlists must compare hostname.

nodes.label: URLSearchParams
nodes.rationale: Decodes on read, encodes on write. get returns only the first value; spaces serialise as +.

nodes.label: fileURLToPath and pathToFileURL
nodes.rationale: file:// plus a path is wrong: spaces need %20 and Windows drives need conversion.

nodes.label: SSRF URL validation
nodes.rationale: Check protocol and hostname on the parsed object, never with a regex on the raw string. DNS can still resolve public names to private IPs.

nodes.label: File streams
nodes.rationale: createReadStream and createWriteStream live on node:fs, not fs/promises.

nodes.label: fs.createReadStream
nodes.rationale: Constructor never throws; open happens later. Failures arrive as error events. Use pipeline.

nodes.label: Inclusive start/end byte range
nodes.rationale: {start:3,end:7} returns five bytes, matching HTTP Range: bytes=3-7.

nodes.label: HTTP range request via createReadStream
nodes.rationale: stat, parse Range, 206 with Content-Range, or 416. Content-Length is end-start+1.

nodes.label: createWriteStream default truncate
nodes.rationale: flags 'w' creates or empties the file immediately, even if nothing is written. Use 'a' to append.

nodes.label: stat then writeHead then pipeline
nodes.rationale: stat first so 404 is possible before headers; treat ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE as a normal disconnect.

nodes.label: Directories
nodes.rationale: readdir gives names; withFileTypes gives type without a stat per entry.

nodes.label: readdir withFileTypes
nodes.rationale: Avoids one stat syscall per entry and the libuv thread-pool cost on large directories.

nodes.label: Dirent.parentPath
nodes.rationale: Replaced deprecated Dirent.path. Full path is path.join(parentPath, name).

nodes.label: readdir order is not guaranteed
nodes.rationale: Filesystem-dependent. Unsorted numbered migrations fail when ext4 vs overlayfs differ.

nodes.label: opendir async iterator
nodes.rationale: Constant-memory walk; one directory handle per open level. Also the cheap empty-directory test.

nodes.label: fs.rm recursive force
nodes.rationale: Replaces deprecated rmdir recursive (DEP0147). force makes a missing path a no-op for finally cleanup.

nodes.label: stat and checking existence
nodes.rationale: Does this file exist is almost always the wrong question.

nodes.label: TOCTOU race
nodes.rationale: Between existsSync and readFile the file can be deleted, replaced, or swapped for a symlink.

nodes.label: existsSync
nodes.rationale: Not deprecated, unlike fs.exists (DEP0018). Fine at startup and CLI; never a security check or request-path guard.

nodes.label: stat vs lstat
nodes.rationale: stat follows links and never reports isSymbolicLink; lstat describes the link and works on broken links.

nodes.label: fs.access is still TOCTOU
nodes.rationale: Node docs say not to use access before open/read/write. Use it as a boot self-check only.

nodes.label: ino plus dev file identity
nodes.rationale: Hard links, symlinks, bind mounts and case-insensitive filesystems make path comparison lie. ino is unreliable on Windows.

nodes.label: File handles
nodes.rationale: open returns a FileHandle owning an OS descriptor. One leak per request takes the server down with EMFILE.

nodes.label: FileHandle
nodes.rationale: Positional I/O, fh.stat on the descriptor, fh.sync, exclusive-create flags. GC does not reliably close it.

nodes.label: EMFILE too many open files
nodes.rationale: Per-process fd limit. Exhaustion fails every subsequent file and socket. ulimit varies by orders of magnitude.

nodes.label: wx exclusive create
nodes.rationale: Atomic create-if-absent; fails with EEXIST. How you implement a lock file without a check-then-create race.

nodes.label: FileHandle.sync fsync
nodes.rationale: write resolving means the OS accepted bytes, not that they reached disk. datasync skips metadata.

nodes.label: Close FileHandle in finally
nodes.rationale: Any throw between open and close leaks the descriptor for the process lifetime. close is idempotent.

nodes.label: Atomic writes and temp files
nodes.rationale: writeFile is not atomic. Write a same-directory temp, fsync, then rename.

nodes.label: Temp plus fsync plus rename
nodes.rationale: rename is atomic within one filesystem. Readers of the old inode keep the old contents.

nodes.label: EXDEV cross-device rename
nodes.rationale: os.tmpdir is often a different mount in a container. Write the temp in the destination directory.

nodes.label: mkdtemp
nodes.rationale: Atomically creates a directory with a random six-character suffix. Argument is a prefix, not a directory.

nodes.label: Mid-stream upload size limit
nodes.rationale: Content-Length is client-supplied and absent under chunked encoding. Count bytes as they arrive.

nodes.label: Boot-time orphan temp sweeper
nodes.rationale: SIGKILL leaks temp dirs. Sweep stale .incoming-* with a grace period so in-flight uploads survive boot.

nodes.label: fsync before rename
nodes.rationale: Without sync the rename can persist before contents; power loss leaves the new name on an empty file.

nodes.label: node:os
nodes.rationale: os reports the host. In a container that is a lie for CPU and memory.

nodes.label: os reports host not cgroup
nodes.rationale: A 0.5-CPU pod on a 64-core node still sees 64 cpus and host RAM. Size pools from config.

nodes.label: os.availableParallelism
nodes.rationale: Respects CPU affinity but not CFS quota --cpus=0.5. Prefer over cpus().length, still clamp and configure.

nodes.label: process vs os memory and CPU
nodes.rationale: Alerts use process.memoryUsage and process.cpuUsage. os.totalmem and freemem describe a shared machine.

nodes.label: os.EOL
nodes.rationale: For local human text files only. HTTP is always CRLF; protocols and JSON must not follow the host.

nodes.label: Watching files
nodes.rationale: fs.watch is fast and inconsistent; fs.watchFile is consistent and expensive. Production uses chokidar.

nodes.label: fs.watch
nodes.rationale: inotify/FSEvents/ReadDirectoryChangesW. eventType is only rename or change. One writeFile produced two change events.

nodes.label: fs.watchFile
nodes.rationale: Polls with stat. Reliable on network mounts. Deletion is mtimeMs === 0. unwatchFile is mandatory.

nodes.label: chokidar
nodes.rationale: Debounces, distinguishes add/change/unlink, awaitWriteFinish, and falls back to polling for container mounts.

nodes.label: inotify misses Docker bind mounts
nodes.rationale: inotify is a local kernel mechanism. macOS/Windows volumes into Linux containers often deliver no events.

nodes.label: Do not watch config in production
nodes.rationale: Containers are immutable, events miss production volumes, partial writes get loaded, reload paths are untested.

nodes.label: ENOSPC inotify watch limit
nodes.rationale: Not disk space. One watch per directory; recursive node_modules exhausts max_user_watches.

nodes.label: Permissions and symlinks
nodes.rationale: POSIX octal bits, umask subtracts, and symlinks make a validated path read something else.

nodes.label: umask
nodes.rationale: Per-process mask of bits to remove. mode is a maximum: requested 0o666 with umask 022 becomes 644.

nodes.label: stat.mode file-type bits
nodes.rationale: Mask with 0o777 before comparing. A 644 file reports 0o100644. Always write octal literals.

nodes.label: Directory execute is traverse
nodes.rationale: r without x lists names and cannot open entries. chmod 644 on a directory is a half-broken state.

nodes.label: symlink
nodes.rationale: symlink(target, path) like ln -s. Relative targets resolve against the link's directory, not cwd.

nodes.label: readlink vs realpath
nodes.rationale: readlink is the literal maybe-relative target. realpath follows the whole chain to an absolute path.

nodes.label: Hard link
nodes.rationale: Second name for the same inode; one filesystem only. Space is freed when last link and last fd are gone.

nodes.label: Atomic current symlink deploy
nodes.rationale: ln -sfn releases/X current.tmp && mv -T current.tmp current swaps the app directory with no missing window.

nodes.label: Virtual filesystems
nodes.rationale: An object implementing the fs interface without a disk: tests and single-executable assets.

nodes.label: memfs
nodes.rationale: In-memory fs with the same API. Hides EXDEV, umask, permissions, symlinks, EMFILE.

nodes.label: Inject filesystem as a dependency
nodes.rationale: Tests pass memfs, production passes node:fs/promises. Stream constructors also accept an fs option.

nodes.label: node:sea Single Executable Applications
nodes.rationale: Stability 1.1 prefix-only builtin. Assets are inside the binary; readFile cannot find them. Branch on isSea().

nodes.label: node:http — the server
nodes.rationale: createServer hands you two streams. Frameworks are a router on exactly this.

nodes.label: http.createServer
nodes.rationale: req is IncomingMessage, res is ServerResponse. Header names are lower-cased; req.url is path plus query only.

nodes.label: ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT
nodes.rationale: Headers flush on the first body byte. Guard error paths with res.headersSent and destroy if too late.

nodes.label: headersTimeout requestTimeout connectionsCheckingInterval
nodes.rationale: Timeouts are swept every 30s by default. Lowering requestTimeout alone does nothing until the next check.

nodes.label: Thrown handler is not a 500
nodes.rationale: node:http has no error handling. Exceptions become uncaughtException or unhandledRejection and the client hangs.

nodes.label: server clientError
nodes.rationale: Malformed request line or illegal header never becomes req/res. Write 400 on the raw socket.

nodes.label: server.keepAliveTimeout
nodes.rationale: Default 5s. If a proxy idle timeout is longer, reuse of a closing socket surfaces as 502.

nodes.label: Request bodies are streams
nodes.rationale: There is no req.body. An unbounded read is a denial-of-service you wrote yourself.

nodes.label: req is a readable stream
nodes.rationale: Handler runs when headers are parsed. Body arrives in Buffer chunks; concat then decode.

nodes.label: Mid-stream request body limit
nodes.rationale: Content-Length is a claim. Count bytes, reply 413, then destroy. stream/consumers json is unbounded.

nodes.label: Respond 413 before req.destroy
nodes.rationale: Destroy first and the client sees UND_ERR_SOCKET, which looks retryable. 413 is not.

nodes.label: Drain or destroy unread bodies
nodes.rationale: Unread bytes sit in the socket buffer and block keep-alive reuse. req.resume() or destroy.

nodes.label: HTTP in practice
nodes.rationale: Methods, status codes, negotiation and CORS — the parts argued in review.

nodes.label: Safe vs idempotent methods
nodes.rationale: Safe means no state change. Idempotent means n identical requests leave the same state as one. POST retries need a key.

nodes.label: HTTP status semantics
nodes.rationale: 401 vs 403 is who vs may-not; 400 vs 422 is parse vs business rule. Node drops bodies on 204 and HEAD.

nodes.label: Vary header
nodes.rationale: Any response that varies by a request header must say so or shared caches poison representations.

nodes.label: CORS is a browser rule not authorization
nodes.rationale: Node fetch with a spoofed Origin read the whole response with no CORS headers. Protects the browser user only.

nodes.label: CORS preflight
nodes.rationale: Non-simple requests (JSON, custom headers, PATCH/DELETE) send OPTIONS. * and credentials are mutually exclusive.

nodes.label: Cookies
nodes.rationale: Node has no cookie API. Cookie attributes are the security model of session authentication.

nodes.label: Cookie request header
nodes.rationale: Duplicates join with semicolon, not comma. Parse with indexOf equals; first occurrence wins.

nodes.label: Set-Cookie as an array
nodes.rationale: One cookie per header line. Joining with semicolon produces one malformed cookie.

nodes.label: HttpOnly Secure SameSite
nodes.rationale: HttpOnly blocks document.cookie XSS theft; Secure blocks plaintext; SameSite blunts CSRF. Session cookies want all three.

nodes.label: URLSearchParams is the wrong cookie parser
nodes.rationale: Form decoding: plus becomes space, last duplicate wins, valueless tokens become empty keys.

nodes.label: __Host- cookie prefix
nodes.rationale: Browser refuses unless Secure, Path=/, and no Domain. Hardening unforgeable by a subdomain.

nodes.label: Opaque session id vs JWT cookie
nodes.rationale: Opaque id keeps authority server-side so revocation is a delete. JWT needs a denylist, reintroducing the store.

nodes.label: fetch
nodes.rationale: Global stable undici fetch. Two outage behaviours: no throw on HTTP errors, unread bodies pin the pool.

nodes.label: fetch does not throw on 4xx or 5xx
nodes.rationale: A rejected promise means the exchange failed. Check res.ok (200-299) before treating the body as data.

nodes.label: Response body is single-use
nodes.rationale: json/text/arrayBuffer consume a ReadableStream. Second read is Body is unusable. clone buffers.

nodes.label: Unread fetch body holds the connection
nodes.rationale: With connections:1 the second request never starts. Consume or res.body.cancel() including on error paths.

nodes.label: TypeError fetch failed cause
nodes.rationale: Every transport failure is the same TypeError. Diagnosis is err.cause.code: ECONNREFUSED, ENOTFOUND, UND_ERR_SOCKET.

nodes.label: undici
nodes.rationale: Implementation of Node fetch. Pool, keep-alive and retries live on an undici Dispatcher, not on fetch itself.

nodes.label: Do not set Content-Type on FormData
nodes.rationale: A hand-set header overwrites the generated multipart boundary and the receiver cannot parse fields.

nodes.label: Outbound timeouts
nodes.rationale: A fetch with no timeout has no upper bound. One slow dependency takes down the service.

nodes.label: fetch has no default timeout
nodes.rationale: TCP connect may give up around 130s on Linux. Once connected, a silent server never times out.

nodes.label: AbortSignal.timeout
nodes.rationale: Covers the whole exchange including a dribbling body. Unref'd so a pending timeout does not keep the process alive.

nodes.label: Slow dependency worse than dead
nodes.rationale: Down fails in microseconds with ECONNREFUSED. Slow holds pooled connections and handlers until the pool and health checks collapse.

nodes.label: One deadline for the whole handler
nodes.rationale: Three sequential 5s timeouts are a 15s worst case. Share AbortSignal.timeout and combine with AbortSignal.any.

nodes.label: A timed-out write is unknown not failed
nodes.rationale: Abort does not undo server work. Retrying POST /charge without an idempotency key charges twice.

nodes.label: Keep-alive and connection pooling
nodes.rationale: Two unrelated pools: http.Agent for http.request and undici Dispatcher for fetch.

nodes.label: http.Agent
nodes.rationale: keepAlive default true since Node 19. maxSockets is a per-origin concurrency cap that queues overflow.

nodes.label: undici Agent dispatcher
nodes.rationale: Default dispatcher opens a connection per parallel request. Bound with Agent({connections}). Bundled undici is not importable.

nodes.label: Built-in fetch rejects npm undici Agent
nodes.rationale: UND_ERR_INVALID_ARG: bundled and npm copies are different classes. Use setGlobalDispatcher or undici.fetch.

nodes.label: Proxy 502 from keepAliveTimeout race
nodes.rationale: Raise server.keepAliveTimeout above the proxy idle timeout (65s vs ALB 60s) and keep headersTimeout higher.

nodes.label: Outbound client discipline
nodes.rationale: One shared client, a deadline, bounded retries with backoff, Retry-After honoured, idempotency on money.

nodes.label: One client per dependency
nodes.rationale: Shared module owns the pool bound, auth header, default deadline and metrics so payment bursts cannot starve email.

nodes.label: Retry only what is safe
nodes.rationale: Transport-before-bytes, 502/503/504, 429 after Retry-After, and GETs. Timed-out writes only with a key. Never 4xx besides 429.

nodes.label: Exponential backoff with jitter
nodes.rationale: Without jitter every instance retries together and the recovering upstream meets a thundering herd.

nodes.label: Retry-After
nodes.rationale: Authoritative over computed backoff. Seconds or an HTTP date. Ignoring it turns a rate limit into a ban.

nodes.label: Idempotency-Key
nodes.rationale: Generate once per logical operation and reuse across retries. A new key per attempt creates a second charge.

nodes.label: rejectUnauthorized false is never the fix
pipeline over pipe for streaming responses
Default to SSE unless the client sends often
The process object and exit codes
A signal listener replaces default terminate
Log and exit from crash handlers
Do not use a shell with user input
Prefer container replicas over cluster on an orchestrator
Phase 6 — Data access
nodes.rationale: Node-side data access only: pooling, parameterization, transactions, N+1, cursors. Planners and MVCC belong to the database sections.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL from Node
nodes.rationale: pg is the driver Knex, Drizzle, Prisma adapters and TypeORM sit on; learn it so the layer above is never magic.

nodes.label: pg Pool vs Client
nodes.rationale: Pool is the default for servers. Client or pool.connect() only when consecutive statements must share one connection: transactions, cursors, LISTEN, migrations.

nodes.label: int8 and numeric as strings
nodes.rationale: Neither fits JS number safely. Returning a float would corrupt money and large ids, so count(*) + 1 concatenates to "50001".

nodes.label: pg date column trap
nodes.rationale: DATE becomes a Date at local midnight; JSON.stringify ships yesterday in UTC+05:30. Keep DATE as YYYY-MM-DD via setTypeParser(1082).

nodes.label: RETURNING
nodes.rationale: Generated row in the same round trip as the write, with no race. select max(id) after insert can see another transaction.

nodes.label: Named prepared statements
nodes.rationale: Server plans once per connection. Measured 120 ms to 78 ms for 200 lookups. One name must always mean one SQL.

nodes.label: LISTEN / NOTIFY
nodes.rationale: Needs a dedicated Client. Fire-and-forget: a disconnected listener misses payloads. Cache invalidation or wake-up, never a queue.

nodes.label: SQLSTATE error codes
nodes.rationale: Match err.code not err.message. 23505 unique, 23503 FK, 25P02 aborted tx, 57014 timeout, 53300 too many clients.

nodes.label: MongoDB from Node
nodes.rationale: The official driver is not a thin wrapper around Mongoose — it is the other way round.

nodes.label: MongoClient is the pool
nodes.rationale: One per process at module scope. Default maxPoolSize 100; one client per request opens unbounded connections.

nodes.label: w=majority
nodes.rationale: Write acknowledged by a majority so it survives failover. Costs latency; single-node ack can vanish when the primary steps down.

nodes.label: ObjectId type-strict equality
nodes.rationale: findOne({_id: urlString}) returns null forever. Wrap with new ObjectId after ObjectId.isValid.

nodes.label: updateOne vs replaceOne
nodes.rationale: updateOne applies operators to named fields. replaceOne substitutes the whole document, so omitted fields disappear.

nodes.label: find() returns a cursor
nodes.rationale: Nothing is sent until toArray() or iteration. 200000 docs: 486 MB RSS vs 143 MB iterating.

nodes.label: Indexes belong in migrations
nodes.rationale: createIndex at boot in every pod triggers expensive index builds N times during deploy.

nodes.label: Transactions from Node
nodes.rationale: A transaction lives on one connection. Every statement must go through that connection, and nothing else may.

nodes.label: pool.query BEGIN bug
nodes.rationale: Each pool.query takes a free connection. Concurrent flows scatter; one flow's ROLLBACK can run on another's connection. Quiet processes hide it.

nodes.label: withTransaction helper
nodes.rationale: pool.connect, BEGIN, fn(client), COMMIT or ROLLBACK, release in finally. Write it once; never write BEGIN in a handler.

nodes.label: Pass executor vs AsyncLocalStorage
nodes.rationale: Repos take a db that is pool or tx client, or ALS holds the client. Explicit is greppable; ALS keeps call sites clean. One statement on the wrong executor undoes the point.

nodes.label: 25P02 and SAVEPOINT
nodes.rationale: A failed statement poisons the Postgres transaction. Continuing requires a SAVEPOINT taken beforehand.

nodes.label: No HTTP inside a transaction
nodes.rationale: A transaction pins a connection and locks. Four open txs in a max:4 pool left the next query waiting 103 ms.

nodes.label: Mongo session.withTransaction
nodes.rationale: Retries the callback on transient errors, so it must be idempotent. Omitting {session} commits outside the transaction with no warning.

nodes.label: N+1 query
nodes.rationale: One query for the list, then one per item. Cost is round trips, not query work — 101 queries 111 ms vs 2 queries 7 ms on localhost.

nodes.label: Promise.all is not the N+1 fix
nodes.rationale: 111 ms to 49 ms but 100 simultaneous queries demand 100 pool connections and can exhaust the process.

nodes.label: Batch with ANY / $in
nodes.rationale: Collect ids, one child query, group in memory. Two queries regardless of page size; works across services. DataLoader does this per tick.

nodes.label: json_agg join
nodes.rationale: One query, JSON arrays already shaped. Need left join plus filter to avoid dropping childless parents or [null].

nodes.label: Query count per request
nodes.rationale: An endpoint whose query count grows with result size is an N+1. Assert it in tests; slow-query logs miss it.

nodes.label: Driver, query builder, ORM
nodes.rationale: The choice is who writes the SQL and what happens when it is wrong. 500 lookups: pg 296 ms, Drizzle 388 ms, Prisma 597 ms — noise next to an N+1.

nodes.label: One tool owns schema and pool
nodes.rationale: Do not mix three layers. A second tool for reports means two migration histories and two pools against the same connection budget.

nodes.label: Mongoose schemas, models, middleware
nodes.rationale: Mongoose adds the schema MongoDB does not have. Every convenience has an edge where it does something you did not ask for.

nodes.label: Validators skip on update
nodes.rationale: updateOne wrote a 40-character name past maxlength 30. Pass runValidators: true; they only see fields in the update.

nodes.label: Hooks are per-operation
nodes.rationale: pre('save') does not fire for updates. Password hashing in pre-save plus updateOne writes plaintext.

nodes.label: Mongoose .lean()
nodes.rationale: Plain objects instead of hydrated documents. 5001 docs: 136 ms hydrated vs 57 ms lean. Lose save, virtuals, getters.

nodes.label: Mongoose autoIndex
nodes.rationale: Defaults true; every instance of every deploy issues createIndex. Turn off in production; create indexes in a migration.

nodes.label: Mongoose query buffering
nodes.rationale: Queries issued before connect hang for bufferTimeoutMS (10s) instead of failing at boot. Await connect at startup.

nodes.label: Driver types must not leak
nodes.rationale: One file owns SQL and mapping. Domain tests run without a database: four tests in 139 ms with a three-line fake.

nodes.label: Named methods per aggregate
nodes.rationale: A generic Repository<T> findWhere becomes a query language. Named methods leave SQL free.

nodes.label: Translate 23505 to domain errors
nodes.rationale: catch (e) { if (e.code === '23505') } in a service couples the domain to PostgreSQL.

nodes.label: An ORM is not a repository
nodes.rationale: A Prisma client in business logic leaks call shapes and error classes just like pool.query leaks rows.

nodes.label: Migration system four parts
nodes.rationale: Ordered files, schema_migrations ledger, advisory lock before reading the ledger, one transaction per file, plus checksums.

nodes.label: pg_advisory_lock
nodes.rationale: Session lock on a fixed key. Second deploy waited 1306 ms then found nothing to do. Must be taken before reading the ledger.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL transactional DDL
nodes.rationale: A failed second ALTER rolled back the first. MySQL and Mongo leave half-applied schema; write those migrations idempotent.

nodes.label: Expand and contract
nodes.rationale: A rename is three deploys: add nullable, write both, drop old later. Old and new code run together during rollout.

nodes.label: Migrations as a gated deploy step
nodes.rationale: Not at app boot: every instance races and a failure crash-loops. Use a DDL role the app does not have.

nodes.label: node:sqlite
nodes.rationale: Node ships SQLite 3.53.3. Zero-setup SQL for learning, tests, and local tools — not a networked PostgreSQL replacement.

nodes.label: DatabaseSync
nodes.rationale: Synchronous by design: a local file, not a socket. A slow query blocks the event loop.

nodes.label: SQLite integers throw above MAX_SAFE_INTEGER
nodes.rationale: ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE rather than silent rounding. setReadBigInts(true) returns BigInt.

nodes.label: SQLite autocommit fsync
nodes.rationale: Each write outside a transaction is its own fsync. 1000 inserts: 66 ms autocommit vs 1 ms in one transaction.

nodes.label: SQLite defensive mode
nodes.rationale: Blocks writing sqlite_schema and loading extensions because a database file is untrusted input.

nodes.label: Schema-first vs SQL-first
nodes.rationale: Prisma owns a .prisma file and generates a client. Drizzle declares schema in TypeScript and prints SQL via toSQL().

nodes.label: Prisma 7 driver adapter
nodes.rationale: url in datasource is P1012. Connection lives in prisma.config.ts; client requires PrismaPg over a pg pool.

nodes.label: Prisma include is two queries
nodes.rationale: Batched IN pair, not a join. Avoids one-to-many row multiplication. Nested includes multiply statements.

nodes.label: Tagged-template escape hatches parameterize
nodes.rationale: sql`…` and $queryRaw send hostile strings as $1. sql.raw() and $queryRawUnsafe interpolate.

nodes.label: Transient vs permanent errors
nodes.rationale: Retry ECONNREFUSED, 57P01, 40001, 40P01. Never retry 23505, 42601, 28P01. A timeout is not knowing whether the write committed.

nodes.label: Exponential backoff with full jitter
nodes.rationale: Math.random() * backoff spreads correlated failures. Without jitter every instance retries in a synchronised wave.

nodes.label: Retry the whole transaction
nodes.rationale: Never retry a statement inside an aborted tx (25P02). Retry from BEGIN on a fresh checkout. Correct for 40001 and 40P01.

nodes.label: pg retries nothing; mongodb retries once
nodes.rationale: mongodb retryWrites/retryReads attach a server-side txn id. pg is one query, one outcome. Mongo selection timeout stacks under your loop.

nodes.label: Read-your-own-writes
nodes.rationale: Write then immediate replica read returned 0 rows on an idle localhost pair with 1.6 ms replay_lag. Pin post-write reads to primary.

nodes.label: Primary and replica pools
nodes.rationale: A mis-routed write errors with 25006 cannot execute INSERT in a read-only transaction. Alert on it.

nodes.label: Replicas add capacity not speed
nodes.rationale: Same query plus a hop. Fix N+1, add indexes, cache first. A replica is not automatic failover.

nodes.label: Mongo causal consistency
nodes.rationale: A session with causalConsistency: true sees its own prior writes wherever routed. LSN tracking done for you.

nodes.label: pool.query buffers the result
nodes.rationale: 500000 rows: 300 MB RSS vs 111 MB Cursor.read(1000). Peak memory scales with the result, enough to OOM a 256 MB container.

nodes.label: pg-cursor
nodes.rationale: Server-side state on one checked-out client. Same dedicated-connection rule as transactions.

nodes.label: Object-mode QueryStream cost
nodes.rationale: Same memory as a raw cursor, 5.7× slower (6353 vs 1110 ms). Use streams when piping with backpressure; Cursor.read when looping.

nodes.label: Keyset pagination
nodes.rationale: APIs should not hold a server cursor across requests. where id > $1 order by id limit $2. offset walks and discards skipped rows.

nodes.label: Sync vs background
nodes.rationale: The request path should do the minimum the user is waiting on. One event loop: 120 ms resize produced 1246 ms p95 at 10 concurrent vs 19 ms queued.

nodes.label: 202 Accepted for queued work
nodes.rationale: Work is accepted, not done. 200 plus fire-and-forget is how a frontend polls a receipt that failed silently.

nodes.label: res.json then doSlowThing is not a queue
nodes.rationale: No retry, no visibility, no backpressure; a restart deletes it. Still runs on the API event loop.

nodes.label: Durable exclusive claim visibility ack
nodes.rationale: Exactly-once is not on the list. Every queue is at-least-once, which is why jobs must be idempotent.

nodes.label: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
nodes.rationale: Each worker locks a different row. 3 workers, 20 jobs: 94 ms and unique 20. Without skip locked 189 ms serialising on the first row.

nodes.label: BullMQ
nodes.rationale: Retries, delayed jobs, priorities, rate limits. Enqueue is not transactional with the database. Set removeOnComplete or Redis grows forever.

nodes.label: Payload is an identifier
nodes.rationale: {orderId: 42}, not the whole order. The job may run minutes later; a copied object is stale.

nodes.label: Worker processes
nodes.rationale: Same codebase, two entry points. Same image, different command. CPU isolation, independent scale, independent failure.

nodes.label: Worker concurrency
nodes.rationale: In-flight promises on one event loop, not threads. Helps I/O; CPU work needs more processes. Match pool size to concurrency.

nodes.label: Split queues by latency expectation
nodes.rationale: A video-encoding backlog starves receipts if they share one worker. Alert on oldest-job age, not just error rate.

nodes.label: Stalled vs failed jobs
nodes.rationale: Failed threw and counted an attempt. SIGKILL left active:1 with no error. Visibility timeout recovers stalls. attempts:1 still double-sends if the lease expires.

nodes.label: Visibility timeout / lockDuration
nodes.rationale: Set above p99 duration and renew. On a DB queue attempts increment at claim time, which is how a poison job is spotted.

nodes.label: UnrecoverableError
nodes.rationale: 4xx except 429 should fail permanently. Retrying a 422 five times turns a clear error into a slow mystery.

nodes.label: Job idempotency
nodes.rationale: Every job will eventually run twice because at-least-once is the only guarantee.

nodes.label: Domain-derived idempotency key
nodes.rationale: order-paid-email:${orderId}. A UUID generated inside the job is new every attempt and deduplicates nothing.

nodes.label: jobId vs handler dedup
nodes.rationale: jobId stops duplicate enqueue. Only on conflict do nothing in the handler stops redelivery of a claimed job.

nodes.label: Ledger insert guards relative updates
nodes.rationale: Insert ledger on idempotency_key, apply delta only if rowCount is 1, both in one transaction.

nodes.label: Versioned updates ignore stale events
nodes.rationale: Jobs are not ordered. update … where status_version < $2 makes late refunds/payments no-ops.

nodes.label: Dual-write problem
nodes.rationale: Two systems cannot commit together. Queue down: order exists, jobs enqueued = 0. try/catch is a third write that can also fail.

nodes.label: Outbox table
nodes.rationale: Insert the intent in the same transaction as the business row. Rollback left neither. Same checked-out client required.

nodes.label: Outbox relay
nodes.rationale: Marks published_at then enqueues; crash republishes. At-least-once with jobId outbox:${id}. A jobs table in the same DB is the outbox.

nodes.label: Poison message
nodes.rationale: Fails every time. Without a DLQ it retries forever or piles into an unread failed set.

nodes.label: BullMQ has no built-in DLQ
nodes.rationale: Exhausted jobs stay in failed, mixing today's blips with last month's poison. Move on failed when attemptsMade reaches attempts.

nodes.label: Alert on DLQ arrival rate
nodes.rationale: Depth becomes noise. Alert on new arrivals and oldest unreviewed age. Replay into the original queue.

nodes.label: setInterval is not a scheduler
nodes.rationale: Drifts (35 ms over 8 ticks with a 30 ms job), overlaps (3 concurrent 250 ms jobs on a 100 ms interval), runs once per process, dies on restart.

nodes.label: Advisory lock for clustered schedules
nodes.rationale: pg_try_advisory_lock on a checked-out client. pool.query can hand the same session so both instances report true.

nodes.label: DST and wall-clock schedules
nodes.rationale: 2 a.m. New York skips a day in March and runs twice in November. Billing wants wall-clock; batches want fixed intervals.

nodes.label: Catch up from state not the clock
nodes.rationale: where processed_at is null, not where created_at::date = today. Missed 2 a.m. is then self-healing.

nodes.label: Background work
nodes.rationale: Producer/consumer shape for work that must not sit in the request path. Framework-free: AbortSignal, plain functions, separate processes.

nodes.label: Resilience
nodes.rationale: Timeouts, cancellation, retry classification, backoff, and concurrency limits that keep a process from becoming the outage.

nodes.label: Queue every outbound call
nodes.rationale: A third party's latency and availability become yours in the request path. Their p99 is your p99, their 503 is your 500, and the request cannot retry.

nodes.label: Four outbound-job properties
nodes.rationale: Idempotent on a domain-derived key, bounded by a timeout, classified so 4xx die permanently, and recorded locally as the idempotency guard.

nodes.label: One delivery job per webhook subscriber
nodes.rationale: A dispatcher enqueues N jobs. One job looping over subscribers fails as a unit and re-delivers to those that already succeeded.

nodes.label: Signed outbound webhook payload
nodes.rationale: HMAC over the body with a per-subscriber secret plus a timestamp so a captured request cannot be replayed. Include an event id for receiver dedup.

nodes.label: Provider idempotency key
nodes.rationale: Domain-derived key such as order-receipt:orderId, plus the provider's own key, closes the window a local sent-table cannot.

nodes.label: Store UTC, convert at the edge
nodes.rationale: An instant is unambiguous; a calendar date depends on who is looking. User timezone is data you must store — it cannot be recovered from an instant.

nodes.label: Instant vs calendar date
nodes.rationale: toISOString().slice(0,10) is always the UTC day. 2026-08-10T18:45Z is the 10th in UTC and the 11th in IST. Format with an explicit timeZone.

nodes.label: Calendar arithmetic vs elapsed milliseconds
nodes.rationale: Adding 7*24*3600*1000 across DST moved 7:00 a.m. New York to 8:00 a.m. Use Temporal, date-fns-tz, Luxon, or PostgreSQL interval in a named zone.

nodes.label: timestamptz not timestamp
nodes.rationale: timestamptz stores an instant. timestamp stores a wall-clock reading with no zone and silently means different moments after a region change.

nodes.label: Do not trust a scheduled job's clock
nodes.rationale: Jobs run late, twice, or in another zone. Pass the window in and select on state (processed_at is null) so a 2:47 run matches a 2:00 run.

nodes.label: SIGTERM drain via worker.close
nodes.rationale: Measured: killed 1.2s into a 3s job, await worker.close() finished in 2125 ms and completed exactly once. Stop claiming, finish in-flight, then close resources.

nodes.label: SIGKILL leaves the job active
nodes.rationale: No error, no retry scheduled. Recovered only when the visibility timeout expires and the stall sweep redelivers from the beginning — the deploy-duplication bug.

nodes.label: Acknowledge after the effect
nodes.rationale: Ack after the effect and a crash is a duplicate, which idempotency handles. Ack first and a crash is silent loss, which nothing handles.

nodes.label: node must be PID 1
nodes.rationale: CMD npm run worker or sh -c makes the shell PID 1; SIGTERM never reaches the handler. Use exec-form CMD ["node", "src/worker.js"].

nodes.label: Close worker before resources
nodes.rationale: Closing the pool first turns every in-flight job into a connection error — graceful-looking SIGKILL. Drain timeout must sit under terminationGracePeriodSeconds.

nodes.label: fetch has no default timeout
nodes.rationale: Node fetch waits as long as the socket stays open. AbortSignal.timeout(300) aborted after 306 ms with TimeoutError.

nodes.label: Timeout budget
nodes.rationale: One deadline for the operation; each step gets the remainder. After a 200 ms step of a 500 ms budget the next call got 300 ms and aborted at 301 ms.

nodes.label: Timeouts must shrink down the stack
nodes.rationale: If the caller allows 2 s and the callee has 3 s, the client gives up first and the callee's work is wasted while still holding resources. Retries live inside the budget.

nodes.label: statement_timeout vs query_timeout
nodes.rationale: statement_timeout is enforced by PostgreSQL and cancels the query. query_timeout is client-side: the client stops waiting while the server keeps running.

nodes.label: A timeout is an unknown state
nodes.rationale: The remote side may have completed after you stopped waiting. Retrying a timed-out write requires idempotency. Timeouts are not a circuit breaker.

nodes.label: One AbortSignal threaded through
nodes.rationale: When the client leaves, the work they started should stop. Measured: one abort() cancelled three children and signal.reason carried 'client disconnected'.

nodes.label: AbortSignal.any composition
nodes.rationale: Compose timeout, client disconnect, and shutdown. Whichever fires first stops the operation through a single signal parameter.

nodes.label: Cancellation is cooperative
nodes.rationale: fetch, timers, streams, and fs/promises honour a signal. Your loops need throwIfAborted(). A synchronous JSON.parse cannot be interrupted.

nodes.label: Propagation stops at the queue
nodes.rationale: A cancelled request must not cancel a job it already enqueued — the work still needs doing. Also stop before anything already committed.

nodes.label: Abort on request close
nodes.rationale: req close fires on normal completion too. Check !req.readableEnded before aborting or successful work is cancelled.

nodes.label: Transient and safe-to-repeat
nodes.rationale: Both must be yes. Three of four matrix cells say do not retry. Duplicate charges come from retrying a transient but unsafe POST.

nodes.label: Transient vs permanent HTTP failures
nodes.rationale: 429 and 5xx retry. Other 4xx fail identically forever. 409 only after re-read. Retrying 422 burns the attempt budget and looks like an outage.

nodes.label: A timeout is not a failure
nodes.rationale: The request may have succeeded after you stopped listening. Retrying an unguarded POST /charge is a second execution of work that already happened.

nodes.label: Domain-derived idempotency key
nodes.rationale: Provider header or unique constraint plus ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. Then repetition is harmless and retrying is free.

nodes.label: Retry at one layer
nodes.rationale: Client × service × job attempts: 5×5×5 is 125 hits on a struggling dependency. In a job, throw and let the queue reschedule — do not sleep in the handler.

nodes.label: Exponential backoff with cap
nodes.rationale: min(cap, base * 2^(attempt-1)). Uncapped doubling from 100 ms is 200 seconds by attempt 12. Cap delay and attempt count.

nodes.label: Full jitter
nodes.rationale: random(0, backoff). AWS full-jitter default. Equal jitter when a minimum spacing is required. Decorrelated for long-running pollers.

nodes.label: Thundering herd of synchronised retries
nodes.rationale: 500 clients, no jitter: all 500 in one 100 ms bucket at 700 ms. Full jitter: busiest bucket 122. Failures are correlated; deterministic schedules stay correlated.

nodes.label: Honour Retry-After
nodes.rationale: If the server tells you when to come back, obey it rather than your own schedule.

nodes.label: Circuit breaker after repeated failures
nodes.rationale: Backoff does not reduce total load during a long outage. Fail fast after N consecutive failures, then probe with a single request.

nodes.label: Unbounded Promise.all
nodes.rationale: map starts everything; all only waits. 200 items peaked at 200 in-flight. Exhausts the pool, overruns APIs, and holds every pending result.

nodes.label: mapLimit worker pool
nodes.rationale: N runners pull a shared cursor. next++ must be synchronous or two runners claim the same index. Measured peak 8 vs 200.

nodes.label: Count the product of limits
nodes.rationale: Limit 10 inside concurrency 5 across 4 processes is 200 against one database. Match the scarcest resource, usually below pool.max.

nodes.label: Backpressure vs concurrency limiting
nodes.rationale: Limiting bounds work you initiate; backpressure bounds work pushed at you. A job queue is backpressure — backlog sits in Redis/Postgres, not the process.

nodes.label: A password hash must be slow
nodes.rationale: SHA-256 is excellent at being fast, which is the attacker's advantage. Measured ~344k SHA-256/s vs ~11 scrypt hashes at N=2^15 on one core.

nodes.label: argon2id
nodes.rationale: Password Hashing Competition winner. Memory-hard and side-channel resistant. First choice for a new project; needs the argon2 package.

nodes.label: scrypt
nodes.rationale: Memory-hard, built into node:crypto. Store scheme$N$r$p$salt$hash. Uses ~128*N*r bytes per concurrent hash; never scryptSync on a request path.

nodes.label: bcrypt
nodes.rationale: Acceptable and ubiquitous. Silently truncates input past 72 bytes.

nodes.label: Per-password salt
nodes.rationale: 16 random bytes from a CSPRNG, stored next to the hash. Not secret. Makes one precomputed table useless and identical passwords hash differently.

nodes.label: Rehash at login
nodes.rationale: Parameters live in the stored string so cost can rise when you have the plaintext. Bulk recomputation is impossible — that is the point. Hash on unknown-email too.

nodes.label: timingSafeEqual for secrets
nodes.rationale: === leaks how much of the value matched through timing. Guard length first — timingSafeEqual throws on mismatched buffers.

nodes.label: libuv thread-pool login capacity
nodes.rationale: Default four threads. At N=2^15 four hashes take ~166 ms like one, then throughput flattens at about 23 logins/s per process.

nodes.label: Revocation versus a database lookup
nodes.rationale: Sessions delete a row and the next request is denied. A JWT is valid because the maths says so until expiry. Short expiry plus refresh rebuilds sessions with extra steps.

nodes.label: Opaque server-side session
nodes.rationale: Random id in an HttpOnly cookie; server holds the truth. Default for a single browser app. Instant revocation, ~32 bytes on the wire.

nodes.label: JWT
nodes.rationale: Signed claims, readable by anyone holding the token. No storage to validate. Roles bake in at issue time. Pin algorithms; check iss and aud.

nodes.label: alg none and HS256-as-RS256
nodes.rationale: A library that trusts the header skips verification for alg:none, or uses the public key as an HMAC secret. Always pass an explicit algorithms allowlist.

nodes.label: Short access JWT plus opaque refresh
nodes.rationale: 5–15 minute access JWT plus revocable refresh in an HttpOnly cookie. Accept a revocation window equal to the access lifetime — a deliberate trade.

nodes.label: Asymmetric JWT signing
nodes.rationale: RS256/EdDSA so verifiers hold only a public key. With HS256 every service holds the signing secret and is a forgery risk.

nodes.label: HttpOnly cookie credential
nodes.rationale: JavaScript cannot read it. XSS can still act as the user on that page but cannot exfiltrate a portable credential. Flags: httpOnly, secure, sameSite; leave domain unset.

nodes.label: localStorage token
nodes.rationale: Readable by any script on the page, including a compromised dependency. sessionStorage is equally readable. Stolen JWTs often cannot be revoked.

nodes.label: Double-submit CSRF token
nodes.rationale: Random value in a readable cookie must be echoed in a header. Attacker can cause a request carrying cookies but cannot read them. Compare with timingSafeEqual.

nodes.label: SameSite cookie attribute
nodes.rationale: Lax is the current browser default and stops classic cross-site POSTs. Strict logs users out from external links. None re-opens CSRF and requires Secure plus a token.

nodes.label: In-memory SPA access token
nodes.rationale: Short-lived JWT in memory; refresh in an HttpOnly cookie scoped to /auth/refresh. Persisting the access token for convenience undoes the design.

nodes.label: Authentication
nodes.rationale: Who you are. One chokepoint at the edge. 401 means I do not know who you are.

nodes.label: Authorization
nodes.rationale: What that identity may do. A decision at every object, always server-side. Hidden buttons and JWT role claims are not enforcement.

nodes.label: Broken object-level authorization
nodes.rationale: Authenticated, never checks the record is yours. Put the owner in the WHERE so the unscoped fetch is unreachable. Near the top of the OWASP API list.

nodes.label: Return 404 not 403 for foreign objects
nodes.rationale: A 403 confirms the record exists and leaks invoice numbering, user counts, registered emails. Reserve 403 for actions where existence is not a secret.

nodes.label: RBAC and ABAC
nodes.rationale: Start with ownership. RBAC when permissions are not 'is this mine' — name actions, not screens. ABAC is more expressive and harder to audit; do not start there.

nodes.label: Deny by default at the router
nodes.rationale: A route with no declared permission should throw at startup. A Friday endpoint with no check is the common regression; enumerate routes in a test.

nodes.label: Session fixation
nodes.rationale: Attacker gets the victim to use a known session id, then rides it after login. Works whenever the identifier survives the privilege change.

nodes.label: Rotate session on privilege change
nodes.rationale: Destroy and recreate on login, logout, password/email change, MFA completion, role elevation. 32 bytes from randomBytes, never Math.random.

nodes.label: Server-side logout
nodes.rationale: clearCookie only removes this browser's copy. Anyone who captured the id still has a working credential. Delete the Redis row.

nodes.label: Idle and absolute session timeouts
nodes.rationale: Idle alone lets a daily session live forever; absolute alone interrupts active users. Redis TTL is only idle; absolute reads stored createdAt.

nodes.label: Per-user session index
nodes.rationale: user-sessions:userId is how 'log out everywhere' and password-change revocation work. Cannot be added retroactively for sessions already issued.

nodes.label: OAuth 2.0
nodes.rationale: Delegated authorization. Issues an access token so an application can act on the user's behalf. Says nothing reliable about who the user is.

nodes.label: OpenID Connect
nodes.rationale: Authentication layered on OAuth. ID token is a JWT with sub, iss, aud, exp addressed to your client. Sign in with Google is OIDC.

nodes.label: Authorization Code with PKCE
nodes.rationale: The only flow to use for web, SPA, and mobile. PKCE binds the code to the starter so an intercepted code is useless without the verifier. Implicit and ROPC are deprecated.

nodes.label: Access token as identity (confused deputy)
nodes.rationale: An access token is a bearer credential for an API, not addressed to you. A token from another app may still call /userinfo. Validate an ID token whose aud is your client id.

nodes.label: OAuth state parameter
nodes.rationale: CSRF defence for the callback. Without it an attacker feeds you their authorization code and links their provider account to the victim's session.

nodes.label: (iss, sub) account link
nodes.rationale: sub is unique only within an issuer; email is mutable and can be reassigned. After OIDC, mint your own session rather than depending on provider tokens.

nodes.label: TOTP
nodes.rationale: HMAC of the current 30-second time step with a shared secret, dynamically truncated to six digits. A second factor turns a stolen password into a failed login.

nodes.label: HOTP
nodes.rationale: HMAC-SHA1 over an 8-byte counter with dynamic truncation. TOTP is HOTP of floor(unix/step).

nodes.label: RFC 6238
nodes.rationale: Implementation reproduced SHA-1 and SHA-256 test vectors. HMAC-SHA1 is not weakened by SHA-1 collision attacks and is what authenticator apps implement.

nodes.label: TOTP drift window
nodes.rationale: Adjacent steps produce unrelated codes. ±1 accepts a 90-second span. Wider gets sloppy; narrower generates support tickets.

nodes.label: Record accepted TOTP step
nodes.rationale: Without storing the last accepted step, TOTP is not single-use. A code observed in transit can be replayed for the rest of the step.

nodes.label: WebAuthn / passkeys
nodes.rationale: Credential bound to origin; the browser will not sign for a lookalike. TOTP is a shared secret and can be relayed in real time. Passkeys are phishing-resistant; TOTP is the pragmatic fallback.

nodes.label: Hashed MFA recovery codes
nodes.rationale: Ten single-use codes hashed like passwords. Without them, support becomes the recovery path — a social-engineering surface weaker than the password you just strengthened.

nodes.label: Never concatenate code and data
nodes.rationale: Every injection is data read as instructions. The fix is never escaping: send code and data on separate channels so the interpreter is told which is which.

nodes.label: SQL injection
nodes.rationale: Concatenated email plus x'; drop table sessions; -- dropped the table on the simple protocol. $1 returned 0 rows. Placeholders cannot be identifiers.

nodes.label: NoSQL injection
nodes.rationale: Structural, not concatenated. {"password":{"$ne":null}} logged in as admin. Coerce with $eq:String(v) and validate body shape at the boundary.

nodes.label: Command injection
nodes.rationale: exec spawns a shell. Six syntaxes including a bare newline ran id. Escaping is a denylist of someone else's grammar.

nodes.label: execFile / spawn without a shell
nodes.rationale: Argument array, no shell: report.txt; id is one filename. shell:true concatenates and now emits DEP0190.

nodes.label: Identifier allowlist
nodes.rationale: select * from $1 is 42601. Dynamic sort columns must be checked against a Set you wrote, then interpolated.

nodes.label: Encode on output, not input
nodes.rationale: The same string is safe in one context and executable in another. Input filters guess every future context, miss one, and corrupt O'Brien.

nodes.label: JSON.stringify inside a script tag
nodes.rationale: </script> inside the JSON string terminates the block. Replace < with \u003c; also escape U+2028/U+2029. Or use type=application/json.

nodes.label: Content-Type and nosniff
nodes.rationale: Node sets no Content-Type. The browser sniffs and may parse JSON as HTML. Set the type plus X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.

nodes.label: javascript: URL in href
nodes.rationale: JSX escapes interpolation but treats javascript:alert(1) as a valid attribute. Validate scheme against http/https. dangerouslySetInnerHTML is the other hole.

nodes.label: Allowlist HTML sanitiser
nodes.rationale: Do not write the sanitiser. Allowlist tags and attributes; sanitise on output as well as storage so a library update improves stored content.

nodes.label: path.join is not a security boundary
nodes.rationale: join('/srv/app/uploads', '../../../etc/passwd') returns /etc/passwd with no error. Normalising .. is its job, not a defence.

nodes.label: Resolve then check containment
nodes.rationale: path.resolve then p === root || p.startsWith(root + sep). Bare startsWith(root) matches uploads-evil. Also catches resolve(root, '/etc/passwd').

nodes.label: Zip slip
nodes.rationale: Archive entry named ../../etc/cron.d/x escapes the extraction directory. Validate every entry path against the destination root before writing.

nodes.label: Symlink escape
nodes.rationale: path.resolve is string arithmetic. A file inside the root can point outside. fs.realpath and re-check for attacker-controlled uploads.

nodes.label: Opaque generated storage key
nodes.rationale: User names a record; you look it up scoped to them and derive the path from a UUID you generated. Traversal then has no input.

nodes.label: CSRF is an authority problem
nodes.rationale: Nothing in the request is malformed. The browser attaches the destination's cookie to a request the attacker composed. The server sees a valid authenticated POST.

nodes.label: SameSite=Lax default
nodes.rationale: Withholds cookies from cross-site POST/fetch/XHR. Node writes the Set-Cookie string unvalidated — measured sid=abc123; Path=/; HttpOnly with no SameSite. Set it explicitly.

nodes.label: CORS does not stop CSRF
nodes.rationale: CORS governs whether the attacker may read the response. The write still happens. A form-urlencoded POST is a simple request with no preflight.

nodes.label: Origin allowlist check
nodes.rationale: Compare new URL(origin).origin. Origin:null is a real value and new URL('null') throws. Prefer Origin; Referer is often stripped.

nodes.label: Signed double-submit CSRF token
nodes.rationale: Plain double-submit trusts only you can write the cookie; a subdomain XSS breaks that. HMAC over sid.nonce so a token from another session fails. Verified.

nodes.label: DNS rebinding
nodes.rationale: Check-then-fetch resolves twice. A one-second TTL can return public to the validator and private to the connection. Only a check at connect time closes it.

nodes.label: Unvalidated fetch redirects
nodes.rationale: fetch follows redirects by default. A public URL that 302s to 169.254.169.254 passes any up-front check. Use redirect:manual and re-validate each hop.

nodes.label: Literal IPs bypass custom lookup
nodes.rationale: lookup is NEVER CALLED for http://127.0.0.1/ — there is no name. Parse-time net.isIP is required alongside the connect-time guard.

nodes.label: Parse, connect-time, and redirect re-check
nodes.rationale: Allowlist http/https at parse (data: returns 200). guardedLookup rejects private names. Re-parse every Location. Need all three.

nodes.label: Egress proxy for user URLs
nodes.rationale: Allowlist hosts when destinations are knowable. For webhooks, send outbound through a host whose firewall permits public ranges only. Node 24 has no --allow-net.

nodes.label: WHATWG URL IP normalisation
nodes.rationale: 2130706433, 0x7f000001, 0177.0.0.1 and 127.1 all become hostname 127.0.0.1. Strip IPv6 brackets; ::ffff:127.0.0.1 becomes ::ffff:7f00:1.

nodes.label: Recursive merge pollution
nodes.rationale: Reading target['__proto__'] returns Object.prototype; the recursive write then assigns isAdmin onto it. Process-wide, persists until restart. constructor.prototype is the other door.

nodes.label: JSON.parse is not the vulnerability
nodes.rationale: JSON.parse creates __proto__ as an ordinary own property and does not invoke the setter. Damage happens in the merge, config loader, or path-setter that walks it.

nodes.label: Block __proto__, constructor, prototype
nodes.rationale: All three keys, at every nesting level. JSON.parse reviver is a free place. Schema validation that strips unknown keys scales better than remembering each merge.

nodes.label: Object.create(null) or Map
nodes.rationale: No prototype to pollute or inherit from. Map treats keys as values so __proto__ is just a string. Strongest structural defence.

nodes.label: --disable-proto and freeze
nodes.rationale: --disable-proto=throw aborts the merge. Object.freeze prevents the write but is a silent no-op in sloppy CJS. Neither covers constructor.prototype. structuredClone does not sanitise.

nodes.label: ReDoS
nodes.rationale: One backtracking regex on the event loop stalls the whole Node process. Verified Node 24.19.0: 28 chars → 3.6 s CPU, 10 ms interval fired zero times.

nodes.label: Regular expression denial of service
nodes.rationale: A slow regex is a security problem because Node matches synchronously on the only request thread. Node 24 has no engine-level regex timeout.

nodes.label: Catastrophic backtracking
nodes.rationale: Nested quantifiers, overlapping alternation, or a quantified group that can fail. The failing near-match is the expensive case; valid inputs short-circuit.

nodes.label: ReDoS input length cap
nodes.rationale: Input length is the exponent. Cap then reject — do not truncate, which can turn a hostile non-match into an accidental match. Cheapest mitigation.

nodes.label: Worker-thread regex timeout
nodes.rationale: AbortSignal and setTimeout cannot interrupt a synchronous match. A worker_threads worker can be terminate()d; re2 is the linear-engine alternative.

nodes.label: Deserialization, open redirects, mass assignment
nodes.rationale: Three bugs, one root: the request decided the data shape and the code accepted it. Fix: name what you accept and ignore the rest.

nodes.label: Insecure deserialization
nodes.rationale: JSON.parse is inert data. RCE appears when eval, new Function, vm, YAML custom tags, or function-reviving libraries sit on top.

nodes.label: Open redirect
nodes.rationale: //evil and /\evil both start with / and resolve off-origin. includes(own-domain) matches fragments. Bypass of OAuth redirect_uri is account takeover.

nodes.label: safeNext origin check
nodes.rationale: Parse with new URL(next, BASE), compare origin, return pathname+search+hash only. Fail closed to a fixed path, never throw on malformed next.

nodes.label: Mass assignment
nodes.rationale: Spreading req.body onto a record lets the client set isAdmin/credits. prisma.user.update({ data: req.body }) is the same bug with a DB round trip.

nodes.label: Field allowlist over denylist
nodes.rationale: A denylist fails open on the column added next month. An allowlist (or schema that strips unknown keys) fails safe when the schema grows.

nodes.label: Timing attacks
nodes.rationale: How long code takes is data. Naive compare staircase 5.4→141.2 ms; the exploited leak is 83 ms user enumeration on login.

nodes.label: Timing attack
nodes.rationale: A first-mismatch loop leaks the matching prefix. Remote byte-level attacks need thousands of samples; endpoint-level millisecond leaks survive jitter.

nodes.label: crypto.timingSafeEqual
nodes.rationale: Compares every byte. Throws ERR_CRYPTO_TIMING_SAFE_EQUAL_LENGTH on unequal lengths. Takes Buffer/TypedArray, not strings. ~0.2 µs per call.

nodes.label: Login user enumeration
nodes.rationale: Skipping the password hash for unknown emails is an 83 ms oracle. Same error text, status, and signup/reset behaviour are also required.

nodes.label: Dummy password hash
nodes.rationale: Verify against a boot-time dummy with the same algorithm parameters when the user is missing. Measured 71.2 vs 69.5 ms. Random delay is not a fix.

nodes.label: Input validation at the boundary
nodes.rationale: The one Master practice in front of the prior nine bugs. Content-type, size cap, JSON.parse, then schema. Verified zod 4.4.3 / valibot 1.4.2.

nodes.label: Parse, don't validate
nodes.rationale: A validator returns a boolean and leaves the untrusted object. A parser returns a new typed value; unchecked fields no longer exist.

nodes.label: HTTP boundary check order
nodes.rationale: Content-type → size cap → JSON.parse → schema. JSON.parse of 20 MB is 40.7 ms of event loop; the cap rejects at 1 KB in 0.002 ms.

nodes.label: Request body size cap
nodes.rationale: A schema cannot defend a payload it has not received. .max() on an array runs after every element is parsed and can be slower than no max.

nodes.label: Zod unknown-key modes
nodes.rationale: z.object strips, z.strictObject rejects, z.looseObject keeps and copies inherited properties. Privileged fields must be omitted from the schema, not validated.

nodes.label: Zod coercion pitfalls
nodes.rationale: z.coerce.number is Number(): '', [] and null become 0. z.coerce.boolean maps 'false' to true. Repeated query keys arrive as arrays.

nodes.label: Secrets handling
nodes.rationale: Getting a secret into the process is configuration; keeping it from leaving is the hard part. Verified sandbox/p8-security/ex17-secrets.mjs.

nodes.label: Node --env-file
nodes.rationale: No expansion, real env wins, missing file exits 9. Values never enter /proc/self/environ. Development convenience, not a secret manager.

nodes.label: Secret wrapper type
nodes.rationale: toString, toJSON and util.inspect.custom return [redacted]; only .expose() yields the value. Pair with logger key-name redaction.

nodes.label: Secret rotation
nodes.rationale: Two values valid at once (kid), read at use not import, schedule so first rotation is not during an incident, expiry beats revocation.

nodes.label: Committed secret in git history
nodes.rationale: git rm plus .gitignore leaves history intact. Rotate first; history rewrite is optional cleanup that never reaches existing clones.

nodes.label: Child process environment inheritance
nodes.rationale: spawn/exec/fork inherit the full environment by default. Pass an explicit env allowlist; helpers can dump process.env.

nodes.label: HTTPS, HSTS and cookie flags
nodes.rationale: TLS encrypts; HSTS stops the plaintext first request; cookie flags remain if either fails. Node validates no cookie attribute.

nodes.label: HTTP Strict Transport Security
nodes.rationale: Ignored on plaintext by spec. includeSubDomains makes uncertified hosts unreachable. preload takes months to remove. Ramp max-age from 300.

nodes.label: Session cookie flags
nodes.rationale: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, Max-Age, __Host- prefix. Node sends invalid flags with 200; browsers drop them silently. ~4096-byte cap.

nodes.label: X-Forwarded-Proto trust
nodes.rationale: Client-settable. Trust req.socket.encrypted when Node terminates TLS; trust the header only if a controlled proxy overwrites it and the origin is unreachable.

nodes.label: TLS 1.3 session resumption trap
nodes.rationale: getSession() in the connect callback does not resume on TLS 1.3. Cache the ticket from the session event. Measured 3.82 ms resumed vs 5.58 ms full.

nodes.label: node:crypto
nodes.rationale: About six calls from 52 hashes and 134 ciphers. Verified Node 24.19.0 / OpenSSL 3.5.7 via sandbox/p8-security/ex19-crypto.mjs.

nodes.label: node:crypto primitives
nodes.rationale: crypto.hash for one-shot, createHash for streams. MD5 is slower than SHA-256 on this CPU (5.11 vs 3.68 µs). SHA-256 is not password storage.

nodes.label: HMAC vs length-extension
nodes.rationale: sha256(secret+msg) is length-extendable. HMAC closes it at 6.87 vs 3.68 µs. Compare tags with timingSafeEqual. HMAC proves key-holder, not which party.

nodes.label: CSPRNG APIs
nodes.rationale: Math.random is not for secrets. randomUUID 0.45 µs (122 bits); randomBytes(32) base64url for tokens. Async randomBytes for kilobyte-scale output.

nodes.label: Modulo bias
nodes.rationale: byte % 100 is 40.7% bucket spread; crypto.randomInt(100) is 2.9%. Use randomInt for ranges, shuffles, numeric OTPs.

nodes.label: KeyObject vs Buffer key
nodes.rationale: A raw Buffer is converted every call. createSecretKey once at startup: HMAC 9.41 vs 35.91 µs; GCM 13.07 vs 38.48 µs.

nodes.label: Rate limiting and brute-force protection
nodes.rationale: Takes volume away so timing, stuffing and ReDoS stop being practical. Algorithm, key and store are the three decisions.

nodes.label: Rate limiting
nodes.rationale: In-memory Map is per-process (4 workers → 4× limit) and unbounded (200k keys / 31.2 MB). Redis INCR+TTL is the shared store.

nodes.label: Fixed window, sliding window, token bucket
nodes.rationale: Fixed window allowed 10 in 80 ms against 5/s. Sliding has no boundary. Token bucket separates burst and refill. Sliding for login; token bucket for APIs.

nodes.label: Redis INCR then EXPIRE race
nodes.rationale: Death between INCR and EXPIRE leaves ttl -1 and a permanent lock. One Lua script: INCR, PEXPIRE only when n==1.

nodes.label: Limiter fail-open vs fail-closed
nodes.rationale: Open keeps a read API up unprotected; closed keeps login protected while unavailable. Silent fail-open is never acceptable — alert on limiter errors.

nodes.label: Account lockout as DoS
nodes.rationale: Hard lock after N failures lets anyone lock any known email. Use exponential per-account delay plus per-IP limit; sit the limiter in front of scrypt.

nodes.label: Security headers and CSP
nodes.rationale: Browser instructions, not API access control. helmet() is 0.80 µs and 356 bytes; only CSP needs a decision.

nodes.label: helmet defaults
nodes.rationale: x-xss-protection: 0 is deliberate. Default HSTS includes includeSubDomains. Node sends none of these headers itself.

nodes.label: Content Security Policy
nodes.rationale: script-src 'unsafe-inline' is not a CSP. Per-response nonce; a fixed nonce is a permanent password. Roll out via Report-Only. Second line behind output encoding.

nodes.label: X-Content-Type-Options nosniff
nodes.rationale: Without it browsers sniff bytes so text/plain containing script can execute. Node sends no Content-Type by default. Pair with a correct type and a separate origin for uploads.

nodes.label: CORS is not access control
nodes.rationale: CORS relaxes the browser SOP; curl and server fetch ignore it. Dangerous only with cookie auth plus reflected Origin and Allow-Credentials.

nodes.label: Supply chain
nodes.rationale: Installed code runs at install and at runtime with your env. Verified Node 24.19.0 / npm 12.0.2 / yarn 4.18.

nodes.label: npm supply-chain threat
nodes.rationale: Dependency minimisation is the only defence that scales. Node stdlib absorbed fetch, --env-file, node:test, parseArgs, randomUUID, structuredClone, glob.

nodes.label: npm 12 allowScripts
nodes.rationale: Install scripts blocked unless allowlisted. An approved postinstall read 103 env vars. Yarn uses enableScripts; npm ci --ignore-scripts is belt-and-braces.

nodes.label: Lockfile integrity
nodes.rationale: npm ci, never npm install, in CI. Integrity hashes produce EINTEGRITY on a swapped tarball. Review lockfile diffs for packages with no package.json change.

nodes.label: npm provenance attestations
nodes.rationale: Registry signatures say the registry served what it recorded. Provenance is Sigstore SLSA that a CI workflow built this commit. Signal, not a gate (3 of 11 here).

nodes.label: Release cooldown min-release-age
nodes.rationale: Most malicious versions are unpublished in days. npm min-release-age / yarn npmMinimalAgeGate of 7–14 days. ENOVERSIONS rather than a quiet newer install.

nodes.label: npm audit limits
nodes.rationale: Matches known disclosed advisories only. Misses a package compromised today; reports build-only ReDoS. Pair --audit-level=high with signatures and a cooldown.

nodes.label: The Permission Model
nodes.rationale: In-process sandbox from the CLI. Blast-radius reduction against chosen dependencies, not a sandbox for untrusted code.

nodes.label: Node Permission Model
nodes.rationale: --permission denies all; grant fs-read/write, child-process, worker, addons, wasi, inspector. No runtime re-grant API. Policy lives only on the command line.

nodes.label: No --allow-net on Node 24
nodes.rationale: --allow-net is a bad option. A process with only --allow-fs-read still opened TCP. process.permission.has('net') is false for any unrecognised scope. Cannot contain SSRF.

nodes.label: --allow-child-process escape
nodes.rationale: The child is a new process with no permission model. Granting it discards every other restriction. Same for --allow-addons / process.dlopen.

nodes.label: Web Crypto API
nodes.rationale: Same primitives as node:crypto via the browser standard. Global, entirely async, stricter. Verified sandbox/p8-security/ex23-webcrypto.mjs.

nodes.label: Web Crypto SubtleCrypto
nodes.rationale: globalThis.crypto === crypto.webcrypto. Every subtle op returns a promise. verify() is constant-time inside the API. No MD5, no scrypt, no streaming.

nodes.label: extractable: false
nodes.rationale: node:crypto KeyObject can always be exported. A non-extractable CryptoKey still signs; exportKey throws InvalidAccessError. Containment node:crypto cannot express.

nodes.label: Web Crypto vs node:crypto choice
nodes.rationale: Shared with browser/Workers → Web Crypto. Server-only streaming or scrypt → node:crypto. Do not mix for one concern. HMAC ~5× slower (43 vs 8.85 µs).

nodes.label: Encryption, signing and key management
nodes.rationale: Most app code needs AES-256-GCM used correctly, plus the key management that makes rotation possible.

nodes.label: AES-256-GCM AEAD
nodes.rationale: ECB leaks structure. CBC decrypts tampered data with no error and its padding is an oracle. GCM fails authentication on tamper. AAD binds context.

nodes.label: GCM IV reuse
nodes.rationale: Same key+IV → same keystream; c1 XOR c2 XOR known plaintext recovers the other message. Random 96-bit IV per message, or a persisted never-reset counter.

nodes.label: Envelope encryption
nodes.rationale: KEK wraps a per-row DEK stored beside ciphertext with v and kid. Rotating the KEK re-wraps DEKs and never re-encrypts data. Two keys valid during overlap.

nodes.label: Ed25519 vs RSA-2048
nodes.rationale: Ed25519 for new work: keygen 0.4 vs 107 ms, sign 151 vs 998 µs, 64 vs 256-byte signatures. RSA verifies faster. HMAC when both sides share a secret.

nodes.label: Audit logging and tamper-evidence
nodes.rationale: Who did what to which record, when, and did it work. When Needed — privileged actions, regulated data, multi-tenant.

nodes.label: Audit event schema
nodes.rationale: Actor+type, closed action vocabulary, target type+id, before/after, outcome including denials, requestId. Write next to the update, not in the controller.

nodes.label: HMAC hash chain
nodes.rationale: Each record HMACs canonical({payload, seq, prev}). Unkeyed sha256 lets an editor recompute the chain. Canonical key order is required.

nodes.label: Hash-chain truncation blindness
nodes.rationale: Deleting from the end leaves a shorter valid chain. Publish the head MAC to a system the app cannot rewrite; the anchoring period is the attacker window.

nodes.label: Append-only is a storage property
nodes.rationale: Opening with 'a' does not stop the same process truncating. Enforce with chattr +a, object-lock, or no UPDATE/DELETE for the app user.

nodes.label: Phase 8 — Security
nodes.rationale: All 27 pages written on Node 24.19.0. Node-side concerns; Express owns route authz; data-access owns query hardening.

nodes.label: node:test — the built-in runner
nodes.rationale: No dependency to test a Node app. describe/it, hooks, mocks, timers, coverage, snapshots, watch. Verified Node 24.19.0, 8 cores.

nodes.label: node:test runner
nodes.rationale: A test fails when it throws. test and it are the same function. Hooks may be async; a rejected before fails every test in the suite.

nodes.label: node --test file discovery
nodes.rationale: Picks up *.test.*, *-test.*, and everything in test/. Not *.spec.* — that suite runs zero tests and still exits 0. A directory positional is a module, not a search.

nodes.label: Test process isolation
nodes.rationale: Default --test-isolation=process: one child per file. none is ~2× faster and hides cross-file state. Local loop, not CI.

nodes.label: node:test concurrency
nodes.rationale: Files run in parallel up to core count. Tests in one file are serial unless {concurrency: true}. it.only needs --test-only or it is ignored.

nodes.label: node:assert — strict mode and deep equality
nodes.rationale: Import node:assert/strict, never the legacy == module. Verified Node 24.19.0.

nodes.label: node:assert/strict
nodes.rationale: legacy.equal(1, '1') passes. An assertion that ignores type is worse than none. assert.equal in strict is strictEqual.

nodes.label: deepStrictEqual rules
nodes.rationale: Object.is: NaN equals NaN, 0 ≠ -0. Prototypes compared so a class instance ≠ a literal. Holes ≠ undefined. Explicit undefined keys count. Maps ignore insertion order.

nodes.label: assert.throws matcher
nodes.rationale: Regexp, property subset, or class. A string is the failure message and can raise ERR_AMBIGUOUS_ARGUMENT. Matcher functions must return true. rejects must be awaited.

nodes.label: Unit, integration and e2e
nodes.rationale: Categories are about what you replace, not size. 50-test unit suite 0.22 s; Postgres container start ~5.6 s.

nodes.label: Unit vs integration vs e2e
nodes.rationale: Draw the boundary at I/O. Many unit, some integration (one real dependency), few e2e on money paths. Separate by filename glob, not experimental tags.

nodes.label: Do not mock the thing that can be wrong
nodes.rationale: If mocking the dependency removes the risk, it is an integration test. Do not mock the DB driver. An in-memory SQLite is not Postgres.

nodes.label: Writing testable code
nodes.rationale: Hard-to-test is usually a hidden grab. Pass the dependency in. Verified ESM import-time process.env bake-in.

nodes.label: Dependency injection via parameters
nodes.rationale: Factory closing over deps, or db as first argument so a pool or a transactional client can be handed in. Defaults keep tests from constructing the world.

nodes.label: Hidden dependency
nodes.rationale: new Date, Math.random, process.env at import, module-scope Pool, fixed-URL fetch, top-level logger. ESM evaluates config before any test body.

nodes.label: No DI container in Node
