nodes.rationale: A function taking an object already is DI. Wire by hand in main.mjs. A container is a signal about design, not a missing framework.

nodes.label: API testing
nodes.rationale: Make HTTP requests. Do not fake req/res. fetch + listen(0) or supertest 7.2.2 against express 5.2.1.

nodes.label: Ephemeral real server
nodes.rationale: Boot the real app so middleware runs. Bind 127.0.0.1 not localhost (verbatim DNS can yield ::1). Close in after; closeAllConnections if keep-alive hangs.

nodes.label: listen(0) ephemeral port
nodes.rationale: Hardcoded ports plus file-parallelism produce EADDRINUSE as a race. Read server.address().port after listen(0).

nodes.label: supertest
nodes.rationale: Starts the app on an ephemeral port, chained .expect() for status/headers/body. Empty res.body usually means missing Content-Type. Pick fetch or supertest, not both.

nodes.label: Async testing done right
nodes.rationale: The runner ends when the test function settles. A missing await moves assertions past that point. Corrects the 'passes silently' folklore on Node 24.19.0.

nodes.label: Forgotten await misattribution
nodes.rationale: Test prints ✔; file prints ✖ and exit 1 with 'asynchronous activity after the test ended'. A .catch() swallows the evidence and CI goes green.

nodes.label: assert.rejects shapes
nodes.rationale: Await rejects, return the promise, or await fn().catch(e => e). No default timeout — set --test-timeout in CI. Prefer allSettled so siblings do not outlive the test.

nodes.label: try/catch rejection test trap
nodes.rationale: If the code stops throwing, catch never runs and the test passes. assert.rejects reports Missing expected rejection.

nodes.label: Mocking — mock.fn, mock.method and timers
nodes.rationale: Built-in mocking. t.mock auto-restores; the top-level mock leaks. Verified Node 24.19.0.

nodes.label: t.mock vs top-level mock
nodes.rationale: Top-level mock.method stayed fake in the next test. Use t.mock, or mock.restoreAll() in afterEach.

nodes.label: mock.fn
nodes.rationale: Records callCount and calls[].arguments/result/error/this/target. mockImplementationOnce varies per call. resetCalls clears history; restore puts the original back.

nodes.label: mock.method spy vs stub
nodes.rationale: Two args spies (original runs); a third stubs. Zero recorded calls usually means the code captured the original reference before the mock.

nodes.label: mock.timers
nodes.rationale: Enable only the APIs needed; tick one ms before the boundary then over it. Do not mix fake time with real I/O. Pass now when faking Date.

nodes.label: Module mocking with mock.module()
nodes.rationale: Verified 2026-08 on Node 24.19.0. Experimental, Stability 1.0 Early development.

nodes.label: mock.module()
nodes.rationale: Replaces a module in the loader so importers get the test version. Escape hatch for a dependency you cannot inject.

nodes.label: --experimental-test-module-mocks
nodes.rationale: Without the flag mock.module is not a function — TypeError, not a helpful message. Put it on the test script.

nodes.label: Mock-first then dynamic import
nodes.rationale: A static import evaluates the module under test before the mock exists. Even a later await import() returns the cached module. Mock first, then dynamic-import.

nodes.label: mock.module exports option
nodes.rationale: namedExports is deprecated on 24.19.0. Use options.exports for named and default exports.

nodes.label: t.mock.module scoped restore
nodes.rationale: t.mock.module is undone when the test ends; top-level mock.module is not. Default process-per-file isolation prevents leaks between files; --test-isolation=none can leak.

nodes.label: Prefer dependency injection over mock.module
nodes.rationale: Use mock.module only for third-party import-time side effects, uninjectable builtins, or legacy code. Injection has no flag, no import-order rule, and a visible signature.

nodes.label: Test doubles — stub, spy, mock, fake
nodes.rationale: Verified 2026-08 on Node 24.19.0. The four are distinguished by what they replace and what you assert on.

nodes.label: Stub
nodes.rationale: Returns canned values; assert on the result of the code under test. Reach for this most often. Nothing is asserted about the stub itself.

nodes.label: Spy
nodes.rationale: Records calls while real behaviour continues. t.mock.method(obj, name) with two arguments spies; a third argument stubs.

nodes.label: Mock (interaction assertion)
nodes.rationale: Canned values plus expectations about calls. Correct when the call itself is the behaviour — payments, emails, webhooks.

nodes.label: Fake
nodes.rationale: Working simplified implementation. Best when several tests need the collaborator to actually work. Drift risk — back with one integration test against the real thing.

nodes.label: Over-mocking as a design smell
nodes.rationale: Seven doubles for one assertion restates implementation. Setup size equals collaborator count. Extract pure functions; leave one thin wiring test.

nodes.label: Never double your own database driver
nodes.rationale: Stubbing pool.query goes green against invalid SQL, a missing column, and a missing constraint. If mocking removes the risk, it is an integration test.

nodes.label: Fixtures, factories, and test data
nodes.rationale: Verified 2026-08 on Node 24.19.0. Test data rots when written once, shared everywhere, and then nobody dares change it.

nodes.label: Factory with defaults and overrides
nodes.rationale: Sensible valid defaults plus a spread override. Each test names only the field it is about. A schema change is a one-place edit.

nodes.label: Shared fixture rot
nodes.rationale: A shared JSON imported by 40 tests cannot change, hides the subject field, and goes stale when the state machine adds required fields.

nodes.label: Determinism beats faker
nodes.rationale: Random faker data produces unreproducible fortnightly failures. Use a counter for uniqueness; use property-based testing when you genuinely want random input.

nodes.label: Transaction per test rollback
nodes.rationale: BEGIN in beforeEach, ROLLBACK in afterEach, pass the checked-out client. Faster than truncate-and-reseed. Fails for code that manages its own transactions.

nodes.label: Captured static fixture
nodes.rationale: Right for input you did not author — webhooks, OAuth responses, a real CSV that broke the importer. Comment provenance; never edit captured payloads.

nodes.label: Coverage — why 100% is a bad target
nodes.rationale: Verified 2026-08 on Node 24.19.0. Coverage measures which lines executed, not whether anything was checked.

nodes.label: --experimental-test-coverage
nodes.rationale: Built in on Node 24 — no nyc or c8. Include/exclude, per-metric thresholds, lcov output.

nodes.label: Coverage records execution not assertions
nodes.rationale: withVat(19.99) returns 23.987999999999996 under 100% line, branch and function coverage. A float-money bug ships green because the line executed.

nodes.label: 100% coverage is actively harmful
nodes.rationale: Rewards assertion-free tests, makes defensive code a liability, ends in istanbul ignore comments, and buys false confidence.

nodes.label: Uncovered lines column
nodes.rationale: The useful part of the report: error branches, catch blocks, leftover functions. Read the column, not the percentage.

nodes.label: Coverage threshold as a ratchet
nodes.rationale: Set slightly below current (80 when at 84) to fail large untested additions. Do not ratchet toward 100.

nodes.label: Vitest and Jest — when they earn their place
nodes.rationale: Verified 2026-08: node:test 0.22s, Vitest 4.1.10 1.43s, Jest 30.4.2 1.52s on the same 50-test suite.

nodes.label: node:test as default backend runner
nodes.rationale: describe/it, hooks, mocks, timers, coverage, snapshots, watch, sharding, JUnit with zero dependencies. Startup ~6× faster than Vitest or Jest.

nodes.label: Vitest
nodes.rationale: Earns its place for a shared frontend runner, DOM (jsdom/happy-dom), expect/vi.mock, interactive UI, and first-class TypeScript.

nodes.label: Jest native ESM friction
nodes.rationale: Needs NODE_OPTIONS=--experimental-vm-modules plus transform: {}. Without them: SyntaxError Cannot use import statement outside a module. Hardest of the three to justify on a new ESM project.

nodes.label: vi.mock hoisting
nodes.rationale: Vitest's transform hoists vi.mock above imports, so it avoids the import-order trap that mock.module suffers. Bought with a transform step.

nodes.label: toEqual vs deepStrictEqual
nodes.rationale: expect(a).toEqual(b) ignores undefined properties and does not compare prototypes; deepStrictEqual does both. Migrations surface real object-shape mismatches.

nodes.label: Testcontainers — real database integration tests
nodes.rationale: Verified 2026-08: testcontainers 12.1.0, pg 8.23.0, postgres:18-alpine, rootless podman 5.8.4.

nodes.label: PostgreSqlContainer
nodes.rationale: Starts a real database from inside the test process. getConnectionUri() uses a random host port so parallel files and CI jobs never collide.

nodes.label: Real SQLSTATE from a real engine
nodes.rationale: Measured 23505 orders_sku_key and 23514 orders_qty_check. A mocked pool can only return whatever you already believed.

nodes.label: Container start cost
nodes.rationale: 5585 ms and 6355 ms on a warm postgres:18-alpine image; queries 15–20 ms after. Start once per file in before, not per test. Separate script from the unit suite.

nodes.label: Testcontainers under rootless podman
nodes.rationale: DOCKER_HOST=unix:///run/user/1000/podman/podman.sock and TESTCONTAINERS_RYUK_DISABLED=true. Missing first: no working container runtime. Missing second: Ryuk wait '/.*Started.*/' never received.

nodes.label: GenericContainer wait strategy
nodes.rationale: Mapped port exists before the process is listening. Without Wait.forLogMessage or Wait.forListeningPorts you get intermittent ECONNREFUSED.

nodes.label: Runner flags worth knowing
nodes.rationale: Verified 2026-08 on Node 24.19.0. Several flags find bugs in the suite; two can make a broken suite report green.

nodes.label: --test-randomize
nodes.rationale: Not --test-random-order, which does not exist. Shared-state three-test suite: seeds 1/2/3/7/11 gave 2/1/1/0/3 failures. Seed 7 passed entirely.

nodes.label: --test-rerun-failures
nodes.rationale: State file records passes and replays them without executing. A test edited to throw still printed ✔ (passed on attempt 0) and exited 0. Local iteration only; never CI.

nodes.label: --experimental-test-tag-filter
nodes.rationale: Key is tags, plural, array. Singular tag: is silently ignored — a filtered CI job can run zero tests and exit 0. Filename globs are safer until this leaves experimental.

nodes.label: --test-force-exit
nodes.rationale: Exits after the last test regardless of open handles. Legitimate for a third-party leak you cannot close. On your own code it hides a production shutdown bug.

nodes.label: --test-global-setup
nodes.rationale: globalSetup runs before any file, teardown after the summary. Start one database for the whole run; pass the connection string via env because files are separate processes.

nodes.label: --test-shard
nodes.rationale: Cheapest honest CI speed-up. Unlike rerun-failures or tag filtering it cannot make a broken suite look green.

nodes.label: Snapshot testing
nodes.rationale: Verified 2026-08 on Node 24.19.0. t.assert.snapshot() needs no flag on this version.

nodes.label: t.assert.snapshot()
nodes.rationale: Records output and fails when it changes. First run needs --test-update-snapshots. Commit the .snapshot file — it is the expected value.

nodes.label: Blind --test-update-snapshots trap
nodes.rationale: Measured: after changing the renderer the flag rewrote the file and reported ✔ with zero failures. The regression became the new expectation. Run without the flag first; review the diff.

nodes.label: Snapshot normalization
nodes.rationale: Scrub ids and timestamps, sort collections, or inject a clock and id generator. Multiple snapshot() calls in one test are keyed by call order — prefer one per test.

nodes.label: ESLint flat config, Prettier, or Biome
nodes.rationale: Verified 2026-08: eslint 10.8.1, prettier 3.9.6, @biomejs/biome 2.5.8 on Node 24.19.0.

nodes.label: Linter vs formatter
nodes.rationale: A formatter rewrites layout and has no opinion about correctness; a linter finds legal code that is probably wrong. You need both, from two tools or one.

nodes.label: ESLint flat config
nodes.rationale: eslint.config.mjs is the only format in ESLint 9+. No extends (spread objects), no env (globals package), no nested-file cascade — one file scoped by files globs.

nodes.label: Prettier
nodes.rationale: Formatting only, almost unconfigurable. Pair with eslint-config-prettier so ESLint stylistic rules do not fight it on save.

nodes.label: Biome
nodes.rationale: Measured 0.09s vs 0.75s for ESLint plus Prettier, doing lint, format and import organisation. No JS plugin API and no type-aware rules.

nodes.label: Type-aware lint rules
nodes.rationale: no-floating-promises needs the type checker. Biome cannot replace typescript-eslint. Highest-value Node rule: catches a missing await at write time.

nodes.label: Linting as cheapest testing layer
nodes.rationale: A type-aware linter catches a floating promise, unused variable and == in milliseconds on every file. Wire it into CI via verify, not just the editor.

nodes.label: Property-based and mutation testing
nodes.rationale: Verified 2026-08: fast-check 4.9.0, @stryker-mutator/core 9.6.1 on Node 24.19.0.

nodes.label: Property-based testing
nodes.rationale: State a rule for all inputs; the library generates cases and shrinks failures. Asks: are there inputs you did not think of?

nodes.label: fast-check
nodes.rationale: Found a slugify trailing-dash bug after a 12-char cap: Counterexample ["0 0 00 A AA    0"], shrunk 35 times. Default fc.string() never reached the cap.

nodes.label: Round-trip, idempotence, invariant, oracle
nodes.rationale: Round-trip is the highest-value backend property: encoders, JWT, query-string builders, money formatting. Not useful for orchestration.

nodes.label: Mutation testing
nodes.rationale: Changes source (>= to >, + to -) and reruns. A surviving mutant means nothing checked that line's behaviour. Asks: do your tests actually check anything?

nodes.label: Stryker
nodes.rationale: On discount() with 100% line coverage: 13 killed, 2 survived at total >= 10, mutation score 86.67%. Directory positional node --test test/ fails the initial run.

nodes.label: Mutation testing cost
nodes.rationale: Runs the suite once per mutant. Fifteen mutants on a tiny file took 2 seconds; a codebase is hours. Scope to one module; run occasionally, not per commit.

nodes.label: Load testing
nodes.rationale: Verified 2026-08 on Node 24.19.0. Testing-phase view of what a load test is for and how it lies. Methodology lives in Phase 10 page 20.

nodes.label: autocannon
nodes.rationale: Quick single-URL answer: connections, duration, warmup. Scriptable enough to assert p99 and non2xx. Run against a production-like build.

nodes.label: k6
nodes.rationale: When the shape of load matters: ramps, user journeys, think time. thresholds make it exit non-zero so CI can gate. Failures cluster at transitions.

nodes.label: Four ways a load test lies
nodes.rationale: No warmup (JIT/cold caches), generator is the bottleneck, one hot cached row, and reporting the average. A 45 ms mean can hide a 4-second p99.

nodes.label: Report p99 not the average
nodes.rationale: With 100 requests per page load, most sessions hit the tail. Report p50, p95, p99 and max. Also check event-loop lag and memory after the run.

nodes.label: Stress, soak, and spike tests
nodes.rationale: Stress increases until break. Soak is moderate load for hours (leaks, pool exhaustion). Spike is instant 10× for autoscaling and cold starts. Nightly against staging, not in the PR pipeline.

nodes.label: Contract testing and consumer-driven contracts
nodes.rationale: Verified 2026-08 on Node 24.19.0 with zod 4.4.3. Where a green unit suite still ships a broken frontend.

nodes.label: Contract test
nodes.rationale: Tests the agreement between sides, not each side's beliefs. A createdAt rename failed the provider suite in 18 ms: expected string, received undefined.

nodes.label: Consumer-owned contract
nodes.rationale: Only the consumer knows which fields it reads. A provider-written contract describes the implementation and grows to cover everything, so it stops constraining anything.

nodes.label: Contract written independently of the model
nodes.rationale: A schema generated from the model cannot fail: both sides agree on the new shape while the frontend still breaks. Independence is the entire mechanism.

nodes.label: Pact consumer-driven contracts
nodes.rationale: Consumer publishes a pact file to a broker; provider replays it in its CI; can-i-deploy gates release. Worth it with several independent teams; one team should share a schema package.

nodes.label: Shared Zod UserResponse schema
nodes.rationale: Provider validates the real handler; consumer validates the mock. Both sides fail on a breaking change; neither can change it alone.

nodes.label: Schema compatibility — breaking vs non-breaking
nodes.rationale: Verified 2026-08 on Node 24.19.0 with zod 4.4.3. Mechanical answer to is this change breaking.

nodes.label: Response add-safe, request tighten-unsafe
nodes.rationale: Response: adding is safe, removing or narrowing is not. Request: relaxing is safe, tightening is not. Adding a required request field is breaking; adding a response field is not.

nodes.label: Rename is removal plus addition
nodes.rationale: Consumer error is identical to a deletion: createdAt expected string, received undefined. There is no just renaming a field across an API boundary.

nodes.label: Adding a response enum value is breaking
nodes.rationale: A consumer with an exhaustive switch or TypeScript union meets a value it has no branch for. Ship handling first, wait for deploy, then emit.

nodes.label: Changing a field's meaning, same type
nodes.rationale: Worst change on the table: amount in euros becoming cents validates perfectly and is off by a hundred. Never redefine a field — add a new one and deprecate the old.

nodes.label: Expand, migrate, contract
nodes.rationale: Add the new field alongside the old, let consumers move, remove the old when telemetry shows zero usage. Version only for restructures that cannot expand.

nodes.label: Deprecation and Sunset headers
nodes.rationale: Standard headers a client can log. Pair with a usage metric so the contract step is a decision from data, not an announcement.

nodes.label: Phase 9 — Testing
nodes.rationale: Complete — 20 pages on Node 24.19.0. Built on node:test; Vitest or Jest only where they earn it. Measurements are the point.

nodes.label: Phase 9 measurement corrections
nodes.rationale: Forgotten await is not silent (file fails). Directory positional fails MODULE_NOT_FOUND. rerun-failures can go green. tags must be plural array. Flag is --test-randomize.

nodes.label: Node 24.19.0 phase 9 target
nodes.rationale: Active LTS as of August 2026. Third-party pins: vitest 4.1.10, jest 30.4.2, testcontainers 12.1.0, fast-check 4.9.0, stryker 9.6.1, biome 2.5.8, zod 4.4.3.

nodes.label: Node.js syllabus consolidated review
nodes.rationale: Historical record of a 2026-08-09 review of 240 topics. Findings applied afterwards; syllabus is now 248 topics at docs/nodejs/syllabus/.

nodes.label: Node syllabus covers the Node layer
nodes.rationale: Strong enough for the Node layer of a fullstack platform. Not the whole backend: Express, PG/Mongo, Redis, Docker/Nginx remain separate.

nodes.label: Node stops before the framework
nodes.rationale: Do not pull pagination, RBAC routes, middleware stacks, or OpenAPI into Node. Express would become empty and Master % balloons.

nodes.label: Suggested Node platform topics
nodes.rationale: Transactional outbox, outbound side-effects as jobs, time on the server, large payloads and temp files, outbound HTTP client discipline, boot sequence.

nodes.label: Master share 35% vs 25–30% guideline
nodes.rationale: 240 topics: Master 84 (35%), Understand 79, Know 47, When Needed 30. Demotion target roughly 70–75 Master (~30%).

nodes.label: Part 1 — Foundations
nodes.rationale: Phases 0–2. The part that makes you actually good at Node and most courses skip.

nodes.label: Phase 0 — The runtime model
nodes.rationale: V8 + libuv + C++ bindings + stdlib. Single-threaded execution vs multi-threaded I/O. Every Node is weird complaint traces here.

nodes.label: Phase 1 — Modules and packages
nodes.rationale: ESM, CJS, node: prefix, package.json, semver, CJS↔ESM interop, exports map. Type stripping stable as of v24.12.0 on the Node 24 LTS target.

nodes.label: Phase 2 — Async and the event loop
nodes.rationale: Loop phases, poll, microtasks vs macrotasks, nextTick starvation, combinators, AbortController, AsyncLocalStorage. Worth more than any framework.

nodes.label: Phase 0 gate
nodes.rationale: Explain why a 3-second for loop stalls every request but a 3-second database query does not.

nodes.label: Phase 2 gate
nodes.rationale: Hand-predict output order of nextTick, queueMicrotask, a resolved promise, setTimeout(0) and setImmediate.

nodes.label: Part 2 — Core I/O
nodes.rationale: Phases 3–5. Node exists to do I/O well.

nodes.label: Phase 3 — Buffers and streams
nodes.rationale: Buffer, encodings, allocUnsafe. Four stream types. Backpressure is the streaming concept. pipeline over pipe.

nodes.label: Backpressure
nodes.rationale: write() returning false means stop. Ignoring it exhausts memory. Gate: stream-process a file larger than RAM with errors propagating.

nodes.label: Phase 4 — Filesystem, paths, and URLs
nodes.rationale: fs/promises default. Path traversal as a security bug. Large payloads streamed to a sink with size limits and cleanup on every exit path.

nodes.label: Phase 5 — Networking, HTTP, and processes
nodes.rationale: node:http, bodies as streams, fetch, AbortSignal.timeout, graceful SIGTERM shutdown, child_process, cluster, worker_threads.

nodes.label: Graceful shutdown
nodes.rationale: Stop accepting, drain in-flight, close pools, exit. The thing that makes deploys stop dropping requests. Gate includes surviving SIGTERM mid-request.

nodes.label: Part 3 — Application Layer
nodes.rationale: Phases 6–9. Data access, background work, security, testing. Parallelizable alongside building.

nodes.label: Phase 6 — Data access
nodes.rationale: Node-side only: pooling, parameterized queries, pg and Mongo drivers, transactions, N+1, repository pattern. Databases live in their own sections.

nodes.label: Phase 7 — Background work and resilience
nodes.rationale: Framework-free. Job idempotency, transactional outbox, timeout budgets, retry only safe failures, exponential backoff with jitter, concurrency limiting.

nodes.label: Phase 8 — Security
nodes.rationale: argon2/scrypt/bcrypt, sessions vs JWT, injection/XSS/CSRF/SSRF/prototype pollution/ReDoS, zod at the boundary, secrets, Permission Model.

nodes.label: Phase 9 — Testing (syllabus)
nodes.rationale: node:test, assert, unit/integration/e2e, DI, API and async testing, mock.module (Stability 1.0), doubles, coverage, Vitest/Jest, Testcontainers, contracts.

nodes.label: Syllabus flag names predating page 14 measurements
nodes.rationale: Part 3 still lists --test-random-order and --test-name-tag. Phase 9 pages measured those names do not exist on Node 24.19.0.

nodes.label: Part 4 — Production
nodes.rationale: Phases 10–12. The difference between it works on my machine and it works at 3 a.m.

nodes.label: Phase 10 — Observability and performance
nodes.rationale: Structured logging, request IDs via AsyncLocalStorage, OpenTelemetry, event loop lag, liveness vs readiness, caching, memory leaks, benchmarking.

nodes.label: Phase 11 — Deployment and operations
nodes.rationale: 12-factor config, boot sequence, Dockerize Node, PID 1 and SIGTERM, trust proxy, zero-downtime deploys.

nodes.label: Phase 12 — Native and advanced
nodes.rationale: Optional. node:vm is not a security sandbox. Wasm, N-API, FFI, WASI, custom loaders.

nodes.label: API design belongs to Express
nodes.rationale: Nobody builds an API on raw node:http. Node teaches it so Express is not magic. REST, middleware, pagination, versioning, OpenAPI, RBAC stay in Express.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL syllabus
nodes.rationale: 14 phases, 233 topics in 4 parts. Relational model, SQL, planner, concurrency, ops, plus Node-side raw pg. Verified 2026-08 against PostgreSQL 18.4.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL example policy
nodes.rationale: Every page carries SQL or shell and the Node pg code that issues it. A psql-only page is incomplete for Phases 2–13. Real output, not plausible-looking.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL 18.4 target
nodes.rationale: Server and psql 18.4, pg on Node 24, postgres:18-alpine on 127.0.0.1:55432 never localhost. Node Phase 6/7 pages were measured on 17.10 — re-check version-sensitive links.

nodes.label: Recap rule with Node Phase 6
nodes.rationale: Pool sizing, transaction propagation, N+1, repository rationale, ORM comparison belong to Node 6. PG Part 3 recaps ≤40 lines and links; it does not re-own those pages.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL tier distribution
nodes.rationale: Master 62 (27%), Understand 127 (54%), Know 35 (15%), When Needed 9 (4%). Master by part: 20 / 14 / 14 / 14.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL explanation pages
nodes.rationale: Target PostgreSQL 18.4 · Node 24 · pg. Phase 0–1 executed against the sandbox; remaining pages follow measured conventions.

nodes.label: What PostgreSQL is
nodes.rationale: Understand-tier. PostgreSQL is a free open-source object-relational database server, not a library, not a document store, not SQL syntax alone.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL object-relational server
nodes.rationale: Long-running program that stores data, enforces rules, and answers queries over a network protocol. Custom types, jsonb, arrays, full-text, extensions.

nodes.label: Database cluster
nodes.rationale: One data directory on disk; may contain many databases. Distinct from the server process, the SQL catalog, and the client.

nodes.label: App is a guest with a connection
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL owns the durable truth. Application code is bad at concurrent writers, crash recovery, indexes, and access control. The server does not care whether the client is psql or pg.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL License
nodes.rationale: Permissive BSD-style. No single commercial owner of the core. The engine is free; hosting is the product.

nodes.label: select version() PostgreSQL 18.4
nodes.rationale: Verified 2026-08 via psql and pg.Pool against 127.0.0.1:55432. PostgreSQL 18.4 on x86_64-pc-linux-musl, Alpine gcc 15.2.0.

nodes.label: Phase 0 — PostgreSQL architecture
nodes.rationale: Twelve pages on what the server is before serious SQL. Target PostgreSQL 18.4 from Node 24 with pg, measured on postgres:18-alpine at 127.0.0.1:55432.

nodes.label: Phase 0 gate
nodes.rationale: Move on when you can explain why a Node process must pool connections, name the four namespace levels, and open psql into the container without guessing the port.

nodes.label: Target PostgreSQL 18.4
nodes.rationale: Every Phase 0 example was executed against postgres:18-alpine. Use 127.0.0.1, never localhost.

nodes.label: Process-per-connection model
nodes.rationale: Each client connection is a dedicated OS backend process. Isolation and simpler memory accounting cost startup time and RAM, so Node pools instead of opening a connection per request.

nodes.label: Backend process
nodes.rationale: Parses SQL, plans, executes, holds session state, and can crash without taking down other clients. Appears as backend_type client backend in pg_stat_activity.

nodes.label: max_connections
nodes.rationale: Server-wide cap on concurrent backends. Measured default 100 on PostgreSQL 18.4 alpine. Exceeding it yields sorry, too many clients already.

nodes.label: Node connection pool
nodes.rationale: One global pg.Pool at module scope reuses backends. Two checkouts produced two client backends. pool.query borrows and returns a client; it does not start a new process each time.

nodes.label: PgBouncer
nodes.rationale: External pooler that exists because process-per-connection is expensive. Taught in Phase 13, not Phase 0.

nodes.label: pg_stat_activity
nodes.rationale: Catalog view of backends and workers. Measured 18.4 types: autovacuum launcher, background writer, checkpointer, client backend, io worker, logical replication launcher, walwriter.

nodes.label: Four-level namespace
nodes.rationale: cluster → database → schema → relation. Confusing any two levels is the root of relation does not exist bugs and multi-tenant layout mistakes.

nodes.label: Cluster
nodes.rationale: One data directory / one running server instance. You do not switch cluster without a new connection target.

nodes.label: Database
nodes.rationale: Named catalog inside the cluster; a connection picks exactly one. Stronger isolation than schemas, but no ordinary cross-database joins without FDW.

nodes.label: Schema
nodes.rationale: Namespace inside one database (public, app, billing). Not a separate database. Default landing place is public.

nodes.label: search_path
nodes.rationale: Schemas checked for unqualified names, in order. Measured default "$user", public. Session state, changeable with SET search_path; attacker-influenced path is a later least-privilege topic.

nodes.label: Qualify names in migrations
nodes.rationale: Always write app.users, not bare users, so a path change cannot silently hit another table.

nodes.label: Shared buffers
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL's shared-memory cache of 8 KB table/index pages used by all backends. Measured alpine default 128MB. Too large fights the OS cache.

nodes.label: OS page cache
nodes.rationale: Kernel caches file pages the server read or wrote. PostgreSQL benefits from it but does not manage it as its own API. A shared-buffer miss may still be an OS-cache hit.

nodes.label: work_mem
nodes.rationale: Backend-private sort/hash memory. Not the main row cache. Distinct from shared buffers.

nodes.label: 8 KB pages
nodes.rationale: Unit of table/index I/O in shared buffers and on disk.

nodes.label: Write-ahead log
nodes.rationale: Sequential record of changes flushed so the database can recover after a crash and stream changes to replicas. Never delete WAL files by hand.

nodes.label: COMMIT flushes WAL
nodes.rationale: Under default synchronous settings COMMIT succeeds only after the needed WAL is flushed. BEGIN is cheap; modifying data generates WAL; commit makes it durable.

nodes.label: Change is written twice
nodes.rationale: Once to WAL immediately for durability/order, later to heap/index files via dirty shared buffers, checkpoints, and the background writer. Normal, not a bug.

nodes.label: wal_level = replica
nodes.rationale: Measured usual default on PostgreSQL 18.4. Supports physical replication.

nodes.label: Checkpoint
nodes.rationale: Writes dirty buffers out so data files catch up with WAL. Lagging checkpoints can grow pg_wal.

nodes.label: Role
nodes.rationale: The real catalog object (CREATE ROLE). User and group are both roles wearing different habits.

nodes.label: LOGIN user vs NOLOGIN group
nodes.rationale: A user is a role with LOGIN. A group is usually a role without LOGIN used for membership. GRANT group TO login.

nodes.label: session_user vs current_user
nodes.rationale: session_user is who authenticated; current_user can change after SET ROLE. Node uses the connection-string role unless SET ROLE is used.

nodes.label: Least-privilege app role
nodes.rationale: Container bootstrap user is a superuser — fine for local learning, wrong as the production app role. App should do DML on app tables, not drop the database or bypass RLS.

nodes.label: Container-first local Postgres
nodes.rationale: Pin major version, reset in one command, match CI. Prefer that over fighting a distro package until you have a reason to go native.

nodes.label: postgres:18-alpine sandbox
nodes.rationale: podman run docker.io/library/postgres:18-alpine with POSTGRES_USER/DB/PASSWORD=devbible. Verified PostgreSQL 18.4 on x86_64-pc-linux-musl.

nodes.label: Published host port 55432
nodes.rationale: Non-default host port so nothing collides with a system Postgres on 5432. Inside the container the listen port remains 5432.

nodes.label: Use 127.0.0.1 not localhost
nodes.rationale: Node's DNS order prefers ::1; IPv4 port publishes fail with confusing errors if you use localhost.

nodes.label: postgresql:// connection URI
nodes.rationale: postgresql://USER:PASSWORD@HOST:PORT/DATABASE. Sandbox example: postgresql://devbible:devbible@127.0.0.1:55432/devbible. Easy to pass around and easy to log by accident.

nodes.label: PG* environment variables
nodes.rationale: PGHOST, PGPORT, PGUSER, PGPASSWORD, PGDATABASE. PGPASSWORD is convenient and easy to leak in process lists.

nodes.label: DATABASE_URL
nodes.rationale: Common app convention; not read by psql by default. Never print it in error handlers or APM breadcrumbs.

nodes.label: pg_hba.conf
nodes.rationale: Decides who may connect how (trust, scram-sha-256, peer) from which addresses. Missing entry yields no pg_hba.conf entry for host.

nodes.label: SQLSTATE 28P01
nodes.rationale: invalid_password / authentication failure. Measured from Node as err.code 28P01 on a wrong DATABASE_URL password.

nodes.label: .pgpass
nodes.rationale: hostname:port:database:username:password file for psql. Permissions must be tight (0600) or psql silently ignores it.

nodes.label: inet_server_port()
nodes.rationale: Shows the server listen port inside its network namespace (5432), not Docker's published host port (55432).

nodes.label: Postmaster
nodes.rationale: Supervisor parent that accepts connections and starts backends. Managed by the service or container; do not kill random postgres PIDs.

nodes.label: Client backend
nodes.rationale: The process that runs your SQL for one connection. Scales with connections.

nodes.label: WAL writer
nodes.rationale: Helps flush WAL efficiently. backend_type walwriter.

nodes.label: Checkpointer
nodes.rationale: Writes dirty buffers out and advances checkpoints. A stuck checkpointer is an ops signal (Phase 13).

nodes.label: Background writer
nodes.rationale: Writes dirty buffers between checkpoints so checkpoints are cheaper.

nodes.label: Autovacuum launcher
nodes.rationale: Starts workers that clean dead tuples. Why updates/deletes do not free space instantly (Phase 11). CPU after bulk load is expected.

nodes.label: I/O workers
nodes.rationale: Assist asynchronous I/O paths (v16+). Measured three io worker rows on 18.4 alpine.

nodes.label: Major vs minor versions
nodes.rationale: Major (17→18) needs planned upgrade via pg_upgrade, dump/restore, or logical replication. Minor (18.3→18.4) is same on-disk major: install and restart.

nodes.label: Five-year major support
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL ships a new major roughly once a year and supports each major for about five years. Upgrade minors promptly; treat majors as a project.

nodes.label: server_version_num
nodes.rationale: Integer form useful in scripts. Measured 180004 = 18.4. Gate multi-major features on this, rarely needed for one product database.

nodes.label: CREATE DATABASE
nodes.rationale: Copies an existing database as a template (default template1). Only superusers or CREATEDB roles. App runtime roles must not. Cannot run inside a transaction.

nodes.label: template1
nodes.rationale: Default source for CREATE DATABASE. May hold encodings/extensions you want on every new DB. A dirty template1 puts unexpected objects in every new database.

nodes.label: template0
nodes.rationale: Pristine factory image. datallowconn is usually false. Use TEMPLATE template0 when template1 was customized.

nodes.label: postgres database
nodes.rationale: Ordinary DB created for admin connections; not magic beyond convention. Not a template (datistemplate false).

nodes.label: PostgreSQL vs MySQL vs SQLite
nodes.rationale: Most folklore is out of date. MySQL 8 is strict by default, SQLite has transactional DDL, sequence gaps happen everywhere. Surviving differences change the schema.

nodes.label: Transactional DDL
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL and SQLite can roll back CREATE TABLE. MySQL cannot. Inverts the usual the-embedded-one-is-limited assumption. Measured on PG 18.4, MySQL 8.4.11, SQLite 3.53.3.

nodes.label: MySQL implicit commit on DDL
nodes.rationale: CREATE TABLE ends the transaction before the statement runs, so a later failure leaves the schema half-migrated. Why MySQL tools ship down scripts.

nodes.label: MySQL strict mode
nodes.rationale: Default since 5.7. Measured MySQL 8.4 rejects out-of-range smallint (1264) and oversized varchar (1406). CHECK enforced since 8.0.16. ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY in default sql_mode since 5.7.

nodes.label: SQLite type affinities
nodes.rationale: Column types are affinities, not constraints. Text sits in an integer column; varchar(3) holds eight characters. Prototype-on-SQLite surprises appear on PostgreSQL.

nodes.label: SQLite STRICT tables
nodes.rationale: SQLite 3.37+ opt-in type enforcement. Use when prototyping on SQLite and deploying on PostgreSQL.

nodes.label: Non-transactional sequence gaps
nodes.rationale: A rolled-back insert consumes its id on PostgreSQL and MySQL (1,3). Sequences never block. Never present ids as a count. First measurement was wrong because batched psql -c shared a transaction.

nodes.label: Default isolation level
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL READ COMMITTED vs MySQL REPEATABLE READ. A second SELECT in one transaction sees new commits on PG and the same rows on MySQL. Silent port behaviour change.

nodes.label: Identifier case folding
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL down-cases unquoted identifiers (createdAt → createdat). Quoted MixedCol keeps case forever. MySQL and SQLite preserve what you typed. Corpus convention is snake_case.

nodes.label: RETURNING
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL returns affected rows in one round trip. MySQL ERROR 1064 near returning.

nodes.label: UPDATE … ORDER BY … LIMIT
nodes.rationale: MySQL allows a bounded ordered UPDATE. PostgreSQL syntax error at order. On PG use WHERE id IN (SELECT id … ORDER BY … LIMIT n).

nodes.label: Real BOOLEAN type
nodes.rationale: Only PostgreSQL has a real boolean and rejects non-booleans. MySQL BOOLEAN is TINYINT(1) and stores 2. SQLite reports integer for true.

nodes.label: SQLite single-writer lock
nodes.rationale: Whole-database write lock. Second writer errors with database is locked rather than waiting. PostgreSQL row-locks and both succeed. Line between application and embedded database.

nodes.label: pg bigint as string
nodes.rationale: pg hands bigint and numeric as strings to protect precision. node:sqlite throws above Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER. Quiet failure vs loud throw.

nodes.label: Three psql connection forms
nodes.rationale: Flags (-h -p -U -d), postgresql:// URI, or PG* environment. Mixable; omitted values fall back to env then OS username. URI is the same DATABASE_URL the app uses.

nodes.label: Four connection failure messages
nodes.rationale: Connection refused never reached a server. database does not exist proves host/port/user/password. Wrong user and wrong password both say password authentication failed, deliberately.

nodes.label: \conninfo
nodes.rationale: First thing to run when something is confusing. Backend PID matches pg_stat_activity. Superuser explains works-in-psql-not-in-app.

nodes.label: podman exec psql over unix socket
nodes.rationale: podman exec -it devbible-pg psql -U devbible -d devbible. No host, port, or password. Fastest check that the server itself is healthy.

nodes.label: musl vs glibc sort order
nodes.rationale: version() names the platform (x86_64-pc-linux-musl on alpine). musl and glibc sort text differently, which can explain local-vs-production ORDER BY differences.

nodes.label: ex31-psql-basics.sh
nodes.rationale: sandbox/pg-api measurement script for Phase 1 psql pages. Verified 2026-08 on PostgreSQL 18.4 and psql 18.4.

nodes.label: Backslash commands are not SQL
nodes.rationale: psql interprets them locally and issues catalog queries. Unavailable from pg, Prisma, or any driver. Line-oriented; cannot mix into a statement.

nodes.label: \d family
nodes.rationale: \l databases, \dn schemas, \dt tables, \di indexes, \dv views, \ds sequences, \df functions, \dm materialized views. + adds detail; S includes system objects.

nodes.label: psql name patterns
nodes.rationale: Use * and ?, not SQL % and _. Unquoted names fold to lower. \dt *.* lists every table in every schema.

nodes.label: \c reconnect
nodes.rationale: Connects to another database or user. Discards SET, temp tables, prepared statements, and any open transaction.

nodes.label: psql -E echo hidden
nodes.rationale: Prints the catalog query behind each meta-command so you can pin it in application code for a target version.

nodes.label: \d table
nodes.rationale: Columns, defaults, every index (including partial WHERE), check constraints, FKs with ON DELETE, and Referenced by on the parent. Adapts to indexes, views, and sequences.

nodes.label: \d+
nodes.rationale: Adds storage (plain vs extended/TOAST), stats target, comment, named NOT NULL constraints (PostgreSQL 17+), access method, sizes, and view definition.

nodes.label: Normalised CHECK display
nodes.rationale: \d shows the server's stored expression, not typed DDL. IN ('open','paid','shipped') displays as = ANY (ARRAY[...]). Compare semantics, not text.

nodes.label: pg_dump --schema-only
nodes.rationale: Produces replayable DDL. \d is a report, not source of truth for migrations.

nodes.label: \sv and \sf
nodes.rationale: Print the source of a view or function, ready to copy into a migration.

nodes.label: \x expanded output
nodes.rationale: One column per line. \x auto switches only when the row does not fit — the setting to keep in .psqlrc.

nodes.label: -At unaligned tuples-only
nodes.rationale: No header, no padding, no row-count footer. Pipe-friendly pair for a single value into a shell variable.

nodes.label: --csv
nodes.rationale: Proper CSV including quoting. Prefer over -A -F ',' which does not quote commas or quotes.

nodes.label: \pset null
nodes.rationale: By default NULL and empty string render identically as blank. Highest-value single .psqlrc line: \pset null '(null)'.

nodes.label: \o and \g redirect
nodes.rationale: \o file is a persistent output mode; \g file is one-shot; \g | cmd pipes. Both write rendered output.
Documents psql's own backslash commands. \? variables lists AUTOCOMMIT, ON_ERROR_STOP, VERBOSITY. \? options is psql --help.

nodes.label: \h SQL syntax
nodes.rationale: Offline grammar plus doc URL for the connected major (measured /docs/18/sql-createindex.html). Covers SQL commands only, not functions — those use \df/\sf.

nodes.label: ON_ERROR_STOP
nodes.rationale: Default prints the error, continues, and exits 0. -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 stops and exits 3. Put on every non-interactive invocation.

nodes.label: --single-transaction
nodes.rationale: Wraps the whole file so a failing later statement rolls back earlier ones. Measured 0 leftover rows. Cannot wrap CREATE DATABASE, VACUUM, CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, ALTER SYSTEM. Holds every lock until the end.

nodes.label: psql exit codes
nodes.rationale: 0 success, 1 psql fatal, 2 connection lost, 3 SQL error with ON_ERROR_STOP. Code 3 never appears without the flag.

nodes.label: -c vs -f vs stdin
nodes.rationale: Several -c flags are separate statements/transactions. -c does not expand psql variables. Use -f or stdin when :var is involved.

nodes.label: --no-psqlrc / -X
nodes.rationale: Stops a developer's .psqlrc from changing script behaviour. Required in every scripted invocation.

nodes.label: psql query buffer
nodes.rationale: SQL is sent only when terminated. Meta-commands execute immediately. A missing semicolon looks like a hang.

nodes.label: psql prompt suffixes
nodes.rationale: =# ready, -# mid-statement, '# unterminated string, (# unbalanced parentheses. Ctrl-C clears the buffer.

nodes.label: \g family
nodes.rationale: ; and \g send the buffer. \gx forces expanded. \gexec executes each returned value as SQL. \gdesc describes columns without running.

nodes.label: \gset
nodes.rationale: Stores each column of exactly one result row into a psql variable. Prefix avoids collisions. Together with \if, scripts can branch on data.

nodes.label: \e editor
nodes.rationale: Opens $EDITOR on the buffer. Trailing semicolon executes on save. \ef/\ev fetch a function or view as CREATE OR REPLACE.

nodes.label: Variables are textual substitution
nodes.rationale: Client-side paste before SQL is sent. Not parameters, no binding, no type checking. Acceptable for scripts you control; untrusted input belongs in application code with real placeholders.

nodes.label: Three interpolation forms
nodes.rationale: :var raw text for names/numbers/fragments. :'var' quoted escaped string literal. :"var" quoted escaped identifier. Same value status produced literal status vs column value paid.

nodes.label: -c does not interpolate
nodes.rationale: Identical -v variable and query: syntax error at or near ":" via -c; correct answer 4 via stdin or -f.

nodes.label: Unset variable left as text
nodes.rationale: No error for an undefined name. Guard with \if :{?name} and \q 1.

nodes.label: Bare :var is injectable
nodes.rationale: \set danger '1; DROP TABLE something; --' becomes two statements. Mitigate with :'var' / :"var". Untrusted input belongs in app parameterized queries.

nodes.label: Built-in psql variables
nodes.rationale: DBNAME, USER, HOST, PORT, SERVER_VERSION_NAME, VERSION_NUM, ROW_COUNT, ERROR, SQLSTATE, LAST_ERROR_MESSAGE, plus ON_ERROR_STOP, AUTOCOMMIT, VERBOSITY.

nodes.label: Phase 1 — psql, mastered
nodes.rationale: psql is the verification tool for the rest of the syllabus; master the shell before racing ahead to SQL text.

nodes.label: SQL COPY
nodes.rationale: COPY is SQL executed by the server and reads the server filesystem; it needs superuser or pg_read_server_files / pg_write_server_files.

nodes.label: psql \copy
nodes.rationale: Default to \copy: it trades throughput for reach, needs no server privileges, and is the only option against a managed or containerised database.

nodes.label: COPY is one transaction
nodes.rationale: One malformed value rolls back the entire load; a three-row file with one bad value loaded zero rows.

nodes.label: All-text staging table for untrusted CSV
nodes.rationale: Load into text columns then INSERT … SELECT with casts and a filter; there is no skip-bad-rows option except ON_ERROR ignore on PostgreSQL 17+.

nodes.label: \copy TO STDOUT
nodes.rationale: Streams row by row rather than buffering the full result, so it is the right tool for exports larger than memory.

nodes.label: \timing
nodes.rationale: Measures the full client round trip — network, planning, execution, transfer and rendering — not server execution alone.

nodes.label: \watch
nodes.rationale: Polls, and polling costs; keep watched queries cheap and prefer count= limits so a forgotten watch cannot poll forever.

nodes.label: \o /dev/null to discard rendering
nodes.rationale: A large SELECT * spends real time formatting an ASCII table; that time is in \timing and is not the database's fault.

nodes.label: \i include
nodes.rationale: Resolves paths against the current working directory; fails when CI runs from the repository root.

nodes.label: \ir include
nodes.rationale: Use \ir for anything a file includes; it nests correctly so a tree of seed scripts can be reorganised without rewriting paths.

nodes.label: ON_ERROR_STOP
nodes.rationale: A session setting that governs the whole run including every \ir; not the default.

nodes.label: Seed includes vs migration runner
nodes.rationale: If losing the database is an inconvenience, psql includes are enough; if it is an incident, use a migration runner that records applied versions.

nodes.label: \conninfo
nodes.rationale: Superuser | on explains most works-here-not-there reports; a superuser bypasses every privilege check.

nodes.label: current_user vs session_user
nodes.rationale: session_user is who authenticated; current_user is who you act as after SET ROLE or inside SECURITY DEFINER. Privilege checks use current_user.

nodes.label: GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA
nodes.rationale: Without schema USAGE every table is invisible however many table grants exist.

nodes.label: ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES
nodes.rationale: GRANT ON ALL TABLES applies only to tables that exist now; default privileges cover the next migration's table.

nodes.label: Test as the application role
nodes.rationale: Working as a superuser hides every privilege problem until production; develop against a production-like role.

nodes.label: .psqlrc
nodes.rationale: Makes interactive psql pleasant and everyone else's psql different; configure freely, pass -X in every script.

nodes.label: psql -X / --no-psqlrc
nodes.rationale: A colleague's .psqlrc can change how a script's output parses; measured NULL displayed as (null) with the file and blank with -X.

nodes.label: ON_ERROR_ROLLBACK interactive
nodes.rationale: Implicit savepoint before each interactive statement so a typo does not abort the whole transaction (25P02); deliberately does not apply to scripts.

nodes.label: PROMPT1 %x and %#
nodes.rationale: %x shows an open transaction; %# shows superuser. Colour the production prompt red as the cheapest safety measure.

nodes.label: SQLSTATE
nodes.rationale: Five-character standard code, stable across versions and locales; the only safe thing to branch on.

nodes.label: SQLSTATE classes 23 and 40
nodes.rationale: Class 23 maps to user-facing validation; class 40 means retry. Class 42 is a SQL bug and should never be caught.

nodes.label: pg error object mapping
nodes.rationale: SQLSTATE is err.code, CONSTRAINT NAME is err.constraint; two unique constraints both raise 23505 and only the constraint name distinguishes them.

nodes.label: psql -At
nodes.rationale: -A drops padding, -t drops header and footer; what remains is exactly the data a Unix filter expects.

nodes.label: set -o pipefail
nodes.rationale: A pipeline reports the last command's status; measured exit=0 naively and exit=1 with pipefail.

nodes.label: \gexec
nodes.rationale: Executes each returned value as SQL; always run the SELECT alone first so a DROP does not reach more tables than intended.

nodes.label: Cron psql flags
nodes.rationale: -X so no .psqlrc, -w so it fails instead of hanging on a password, -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 for a real exit code, -At for bare output.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL index
nodes.rationale: A second sorted copy of some columns written on every INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE so some SELECTs can stop scanning. You buy read speed with write time and disk.

nodes.label: Index write cost
nodes.rationale: One index took a 200000-row insert from 1239 ms to 2266 ms; three took it to 4035 ms with indexes 36 MB against 15 MB of heap.

nodes.label: PRIMARY KEY is a unique index
nodes.rationale: A table is never truly at zero indexes if it has a PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE constraint.

nodes.label: idx_scan
nodes.rationale: Zero over a full business cycle means the index is only costing you.

nodes.label: B-tree
nodes.rationale: The default CREATE INDEX; serves equality, ranges, ORDER BY, min/max endpoints, and prefix LIKE only with a byte-order opclass.

nodes.label: text_pattern_ops
nodes.rationale: Fixes prefix LIKE under a non-C collation (34.5 ms to 4.1 ms) but cannot serve collation-aware ORDER BY; keep both indexes.

nodes.label: Prefix LIKE on a B-tree
nodes.rationale: LIKE 'abc%' is logically a range but under a non-C collation the B-tree sort is not byte order.

nodes.label: EXPLAIN
nodes.rationale: Free and lies a little: prints the chosen plan with estimates without running the query.

nodes.label: EXPLAIN ANALYZE
nodes.rationale: Honest and costs you the query: ANALYZE executes the statement, including INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, and does not roll it back.

nodes.label: EXPLAIN loops
nodes.rationale: actual time and rows are per loop; multiply by loops for the total. The single most misread part of a plan.

nodes.label: Seq scan vs index scan vs bitmap heap scan
Index Scan
nodes.rationale: Walk the index and fetch each heap row directly. Chosen for a handful of rows.

nodes.label: Bitmap Heap Scan
nodes.rationale: Collect matching locations first, then read the heap in physical order so each page is visited at most once.

nodes.label: Seq Scan
nodes.rationale: Not a failure: forcing an index on 80% of 500000 rows took 272 ms and 400358 buffers versus 91 ms and 3712 for the sequential scan.

nodes.label: enable_seqscan = off
nodes.rationale: A diagnostic, not a fix: it prices sequential scans absurdly high. Never leave it in a migration or connection setup.

nodes.label: random_page_cost
nodes.rationale: Default 4.0 dates from spinning disks; ~1.1 on SSD is the knob that actually shifts the index/seq balance.

nodes.label: Why an index is not being used
Function around the column
nodes.rationale: lower(email) is a different value from email; measured 0.139 ms to 105 ms, 755× slower.

nodes.label: Cast on the indexed column
nodes.rationale: Casting the column is casting every row. pg sends parameters as untyped text so the danger is the :: you add by hand.

nodes.label: Low selectivity
nodes.rationale: Not a bug: forcing the index for a value matching 99.89% of rows took 115.8 ms versus 101.9 ms for the sequential scan.

nodes.label: Stale statistics
nodes.rationale: Signature is estimated rows=1 against actual rows=400001; ANALYZE dropped the query from 157 ms to 58 ms.

nodes.label: Non-indexable predicate shape
nodes.rationale: <> / NOT IN / leading wildcard cannot seek; OR is fine only when every branch has its own usable index.

nodes.label: Leftmost-prefix rule
nodes.rationale: An index on (a, b, c) serves any leading prefix but not b or c alone. Measured 0.226 ms on the leading column, 56.9 ms on the second.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL 18 skip scan
nodes.rationale: Safety net for low-cardinality leading columns, shown by Index Searches: 7; not a licence to stop thinking about column order.

nodes.label: Equality first, range second
nodes.rationale: (user_id, created_at) used 23 buffers where (created_at, user_id) used 396 for the same query.

nodes.label: BUFFERS
nodes.rationale: The only plan measurement independent of cache state and machine load. Two plans 3× apart in time were 108× apart in buffer accesses.

nodes.label: shared hit vs shared read
nodes.rationale: hit is in shared_buffers; read is from OS cache or disk — PostgreSQL cannot distinguish those two. shared read is an upper bound on physical I/O.

nodes.label: Correlated-column estimate error
nodes.rationale: Planner multiplied two independent-looking filters and estimated 33080 against actual 100000; hunt the deepest node with the worst actual-to-estimated ratio.

nodes.label: Index-only scans, INCLUDE and the visibility map
Index-only scan
nodes.rationale: Answers from the index alone only if every selected column is in the index and the visibility map says heap pages are all-visible.

nodes.label: Visibility map
nodes.rationale: VACUUM sets all-visible bits. Without them PostgreSQL must check each row in the heap; one UPDATE took Heap Fetches from 0 to 58.

nodes.label: INCLUDE columns
nodes.rationale: Payload in the leaves only — returnable, not searchable or sortable. Required when the index is UNIQUE and the key must not change.

nodes.label: Partial index
nodes.rationale: Indexes only matching rows: 8792 kB full versus 104 kB partial for 4000 live rows of 400000. The planner uses it only when it can prove implication.

nodes.label: Partial-index predicate implication
nodes.rationale: Write the query predicate as a literal matching the index; a generic plan planned without $1 may not prove implication.

nodes.label: Partial UNIQUE index
nodes.rationale: The one thing a table constraint cannot express: uniqueness among live rows. Violations still raise 23505.

nodes.label: Expression index
nodes.rationale: A second physical copy of a derived value that only serves the exact expression it stores. lower(email) went from 97.2 ms to 0.083 ms.

nodes.label: IMMUTABLE index expressions
nodes.rationale: timestamptz::date depends on session TimeZone so it is STABLE and raises 42P17. Name the zone: date_trunc('day', created_at, 'UTC').

nodes.label: Expression-index statistics
nodes.rationale: ANALYZE gathers stats for the expression under the index name; creating one purely to give the planner statistics is a legitimate move.

nodes.label: GIN for jsonb, arrays and full text; pg_trgm for LIKE
GIN
nodes.rationale: Indexes the parts of a value so @>, @@ and LIKE '%x%' become indexable. 130× faster on a one-row match, slower than seq scan on a 16% match.

nodes.label: jsonb_ops vs jsonb_path_ops
nodes.rationale: path_ops is smaller and faster for @> but cannot serve ? / ?| / ?&. Default to jsonb_ops.

nodes.label: pg_trgm
nodes.rationale: Makes infix LIKE indexable. Short patterns under three characters return most of the table and can be slower than a sequential scan.

nodes.label: gist_trgm_ops distance ordering
nodes.rationale: GIN cannot do <-> nearest-neighbour at all; GiST did it in 110 ms versus 766 ms seq scan, at 48 MB against GIN's 13 MB.

nodes.label: GIN pending list
nodes.rationale: Buffers inserts so the 3.2× write cost is deferred into VACUUM or a later query; fastupdate=off trades insert speed for predictable reads.

nodes.label: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY
nodes.rationale: Avoids the ShareLock that blocks writers; costs two table passes plus a wait for every pre-existing transaction, including idle-in-transaction elsewhere.

nodes.label: CREATE INDEX ShareLock
nodes.rationale: Conflicts with RowExclusiveLock; reads continue, writes queue. On a minutes-long build that is an outage.

nodes.label: indisvalid
nodes.rationale: A failed CONCURRENTLY leaves an index with indisvalid=false: unusable by queries but still maintained by writes. There is no resume.

nodes.label: SQLSTATE 25001
nodes.rationale: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction block; mark the migration non-transactional.

nodes.label: Unused-index audit
nodes.rationale: idx_scan=0 is necessary not sufficient: exclude UNIQUE/constraint-backing indexes, check stats_reset, audit every replica, wait a full business cycle.

nodes.label: Duplicate indexes
nodes.rationale: PRIMARY KEY and UNIQUE already create indexes; grouping pg_index by full definition finds exact duplicates.

nodes.label: stats_fetch_consistency cache
nodes.rationale: Backends flush counters on a timer and the reader caches its snapshot; never conclude unused from a reading taken seconds after the query.

nodes.label: pg_stat_statements
nodes.rationale: Ranks by total time so a 4 ms query run 500 times beats an 87 ms query run twice. Requires shared_preload_libraries and a restart.

nodes.label: total_exec_time vs mean_exec_time
nodes.rationale: Mean flags rare heavyweight queries; total finds the frequent moderate ones that dominate the workload. Measured 9240 ms versus 173 ms.

nodes.label: Literal normalisation in pg_stat_statements
nodes.rationale: Constants become $n so three literal variants collapse to one row; no parameter values are stored, which is why the view is safe to expose.

nodes.label: pg_stat_statements.max and dealloc
nodes.rationale: Default 5000 distinct statements; unbounded IN-list shapes evict useful rows. Growing dealloc means raise max or fix query generation.

nodes.label: BRIN index
nodes.rationale: Stores min/max per 128-page range; 24 kB vs 64 MB B-tree on 3 M ordered rows. A filter not a lookup — always a bitmap scan with recheck. Useless when physical correlation is near 0.

nodes.label: pg_stats.correlation
nodes.rationale: Check before creating BRIN. Near 1 or −1 is excellent; measured 0.0119 on shuffled data and the planner ignored the index.

nodes.label: Hash index
nodes.rationale: Equality only; 16 MB vs 28 MB B-tree here. Cannot UNIQUE (0A000), ranges, INCLUDE, or index-only scans. WAL-logged and crash-safe since PostgreSQL 10.

nodes.label: GiST index
nodes.rationale: A framework for predicates with no total order: overlap, containment, distance. Backs exclusion constraints; serves <-> ordering that GIN cannot.

nodes.label: EXCLUDE USING gist
nodes.rationale: No two bookings for the same room may overlap. Cannot be expressed with UNIQUE or CHECK; app-level checks race. Use '[)' bounds so back-to-back bookings do not overlap.

nodes.label: Specialist indexes vs default B-tree
nodes.rationale: If unsure which applies, the answer is B-tree. BRIN, hash and GiST exist only when you know exactly why the B-tree is wrong.

nodes.label: ANALYZE
nodes.rationale: The planner looks at a sample, not the data. A table analyzed at 2000 rows and grown to 402000 estimated 1 row of 400001 and took 157 ms instead of 58 ms. Last statement of every bulk load.

nodes.label: Extended statistics
nodes.rationale: Per-column stats assume independence and multiply selectivities. CREATE STATISTICS (dependencies, ndistinct) moved 33607 → 100990 against an actual 100000. Must be created by hand and take effect only after ANALYZE.

nodes.label: default_statistics_target
nodes.rationale: Histogram buckets and most-common-values. Raise per column, not globally: 101 buckets at 100, 1001 at 1000, ANALYZE 1309 ms.

nodes.label: Autoanalyze threshold
nodes.rationale: Fires at threshold + scale_factor × reltuples — 50 + 10% by default. On a 10-million-row table that is a million modifications; lower scale_factor to 0.01 on large tables.

nodes.label: Index bloat
nodes.rationale: Every UPDATE of an indexed column writes a new index entry and leaves the old one dead. Measured 8792 kB → 34 MB after six rewrites of a third of 400000 rows, row count unchanged.

nodes.label: VACUUM does not shrink indexes
nodes.rationale: Same asymmetry as heap VACUUM: dead entries become reusable inside the file so growth stops, but 34 MB stays 34 MB. Only REINDEX rebuilds the file.

nodes.label: REINDEX CONCURRENTLY
nodes.rationale: Builds a new index, swaps, drops old under SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE. Measured 34 MB → 9968 kB in 783 ms. Cannot run in a transaction; needs disk for both copies; can leave invalid _ccnew/_ccold.

nodes.label: Referencing-side FK index
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL indexes the referenced PK/UNIQUE side automatically and never the referencing column. Without that index every parent DELETE scans the child — 33.2 ms vs 6.2 ms on 300000 children.

nodes.label: FK-without-index audit query
nodes.rationale: pg_constraint contype=f vs a valid index whose leading columns match the FK columns. Composite counts if leftmost prefix and order match; indisvalid required.

nodes.label: ON DELETE CASCADE needs child FK index
Phase 10 — Indexes and the query planner
Atomicity and aborted transactions
nodes.rationale: A failed statement aborts the whole transaction. Later commands return 25P02. COMMIT on an aborted transaction is executed as ROLLBACK.

nodes.label: Consistency as constraints
nodes.rationale: Consistency is whatever constraints say. UNIQUE, PRIMARY KEY, EXCLUDE and foreign keys can be DEFERRABLE; CHECK and NOT NULL are always immediate.

nodes.label: Default isolation READ COMMITTED
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL's default trades isolation for concurrency; the anomalies it allows are the source of most real transaction bugs.

nodes.label: Durability and WAL flush
nodes.rationale: COMMIT does not return until the WAL record is flushed. 112 bytes for one UPDATE. Batching 500 inserts in one transaction (128 ms) beat turning synchronous_commit off (170 ms).

nodes.label: synchronous_commit
nodes.rationale: Off buys 6× write throughput (1042 ms → 170 ms) for a window of lost recent commits. Not corruption — lost commits. Check commit frequency first.

nodes.label: pool.query BEGIN bug
nodes.rationale: Idle pool luck: all three statements share one connection. Under load BEGIN, UPDATE and ROLLBACK hit backends 1055/1056/1056 — the update autocommits and a stray open transaction remains.

nodes.label: withTransaction helper
nodes.rationale: One client from pool.connect(); ROLLBACK.catch to avoid masking; release() in finally. Isolation goes on BEGIN, not SET after the first query (25001).

nodes.label: Transaction cost is connection-seconds
nodes.rationale: A transaction holds a connection for its entire duration. Do not open it across HTTP calls; that exhausts the pool and stalls VACUUM.

nodes.label: READ COMMITTED and the anomalies it allows
READ COMMITTED
nodes.rationale: A fresh snapshot per statement. Allows non-repeatable reads and phantoms; never dirty reads. No 40001, so no retry loop — silent wrong data instead of errors.

nodes.label: One statement, one snapshot
nodes.rationale: Snapshot is fixed when the statement starts. A 400 ms SELECT saw pre-update values for every row even after a mid-scan commit.

nodes.label: UPDATE re-evaluates WHERE after wait
nodes.rationale: After a row-lock wait the UPDATE re-reads the newest committed version. Put the condition in WHERE and trust rowCount.

nodes.label: The lost update, and four ways to stop it
Lost update
nodes.rationale: Read-modify-write under READ COMMITTED: last writer wins with a stale value. 20 concurrent increments produced qty=2. No error, no deadlock.

nodes.label: SQL arithmetic UPDATE
nodes.rationale: SET qty = qty + 1 is atomic in one statement. Fastest of the four (37.9 ms, 20/20). Limited to values expressible in SQL.

nodes.label: SELECT FOR UPDATE then UPDATE
nodes.rationale: Serialises the read-modify-write so application logic can live in JS. 58.0 ms. Lock held until COMMIT.

nodes.label: Optimistic version column
nodes.rationale: WHERE version = $2; rowCount 0 means retry. Right for think-time / cross-request edits. Worst under single-row contention: 170 retries, 337.4 ms.

nodes.label: REPEATABLE READ turns lost updates into 40001
Bounded retry with jitter
nodes.rationale: Unbounded retry is livelock; no jitter collides in lockstep. Cap attempts; backoff with jitter. Retry 40001 and 40P01 only.

nodes.label: MVCC
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL never overwrites a row. UPDATE writes a new version and marks the old one ending; DELETE only stamps xmax. Explains lock-free reads, table growth, and why VACUUM exists.

nodes.label: MVCC snapshot xmin:xmax:in-progress
nodes.rationale: Visible if xmin committed before the snapshot and is not in-progress, and xmax is absent or not yet committed. xmax is one past the last completed transaction.

nodes.label: HOT update
nodes.rationale: New version on the same page and no indexed column changed, so indexes stay untouched. fillfactor 100 → 0.1% HOT and 24 MB; fillfactor 70 → 76.6% HOT and 13 MB; index on updated column → 0% HOT.

nodes.label: REPEATABLE READ
nodes.rationale: One snapshot for the whole transaction, taken at the first statement. Read-only work cannot fail with 40001. Writers that touch a changed row get 40001 concurrent update.

nodes.label: Write skew
nodes.rationale: Two transactions write different rows after reading an overlapping set and together break an invariant neither saw break. REPEATABLE READ allows it; SERIALIZABLE aborts one.

nodes.label: SERIALIZABLE
nodes.rationale: Outcome equals some serial execution via SSI. Degrades sharply with conflict rate: 135 attempts and 12.4 s vs ordered FOR UPDATE 20 attempts and 71.2 ms for 20 transfers.

nodes.label: SQLSTATE 40001 serialization failure
nodes.rationale: due to concurrent update = you wrote a row someone else wrote. due to read/write dependencies = SSI found a cycle involving what you read. Same SQLSTATE, different detection.

nodes.label: withSerializable retry loop
nodes.rationale: Re-run the whole transaction; retry 40001/40P01 only; bound attempts; jitter; no external side effects. Sleep after release, never inside catch before finally.

nodes.label: Never await while holding a pooled client
nodes.rationale: Sleeping in catch before finally pins a connection while idle and turns a retry storm into a pool shortage.

nodes.label: Row locks: FOR UPDATE and friends
FOR UPDATE
nodes.rationale: Strongest row lock; held until the transaction ends. Transaction length is blocking length. Lock only rows you will write, in a deterministic order.

nodes.label: FOR KEY SHARE
nodes.rationale: What an FK insert takes on the parent. Conflicts only with FOR UPDATE, so a child insert does not block a non-key parent update.

nodes.label: lock_timeout
nodes.rationale: Bounds only the wait for a lock (55P03). Prefer SET LOCAL so it does not leak on a pooled connection — pg does not reset session state on release().

nodes.label: Row locks live in the tuple header
SKIP LOCKED and the job queue
FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
nodes.rationale: Omits locked rows instead of waiting. 8 workers, 200 jobs: 168.6 ms, 0 duplicates, all 8 busy. Plain FOR UPDATE 499 ms and only 3 workers; no lock 593 duplicates.

nodes.label: Table-backed job queue
nodes.rationale: Use the table when enqueue must commit with the business write. Use a broker for tens of thousands/s, fan-out, or jobs unrelated to the database.

nodes.label: At-least-once delivery
nodes.rationale: Commit the claim, then work. A crash leaves running; a reaper on started_at plus idempotent handlers. Exactly-once is not configurable.

nodes.label: SAVEPOINT
nodes.rationale: The only way to survive a statement error inside a transaction. Must be taken before the risky statement. Prefer ON CONFLICT when a single statement can express recovery.

nodes.label: Savepoint subtransaction XIDs
nodes.rationale: Each writing savepoint burns a real xid. 2000 inserts 2.3× slower wrapped in SAVEPOINT/RELEASE (599.8 ms → 1362.5 ms). Past 64 subxids the cache overflows and other sessions hit SubtransSLRU.

nodes.label: No nested transactions
nodes.rationale: ORMs implement nesting as SAVEPOINT. An inner commit is RELEASE; the outer rollback still discards it.

nodes.label: DDL lock queue convoy
nodes.rationale: A waiting ACCESS EXCLUSIVE ALTER queues every later query, even SELECTs compatible with the current holder. How a 2 ms ADD COLUMN takes a site down.

nodes.label: Metadata-only vs table-rewrite DDL
nodes.rationale: Constant DEFAULT is metadata since PG11 (2.0 ms). Volatile default or non-binary-coercible type rewrite (319–345 ms on 200000 rows).

nodes.label: lock_timeout on migrations
nodes.rationale: Fail with 55P03 after a few seconds and retry, instead of queuing the pool empty.

nodes.label: ADD CONSTRAINT NOT VALID then VALIDATE
Deadlock
nodes.rationale: Two transactions each hold what the other needs. Detected after deadlock_timeout (1 s), one aborted with 40P01. Opposite lock order 1155 ms; same order both committed in 326.2 ms.

nodes.label: Consistent lock order
nodes.rationale: ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE in every path. Sorting an array passed to ANY() does nothing — lock order is plan order unless a locking SELECT has ORDER BY.

nodes.label: Long-running transactions and the xmin horizon
xmin horizon
nodes.rationale: VACUUM may only remove versions no running transaction could need. The oldest snapshot pins cleanup for every table. With a blocker, 0 of 100000 dead rows removed and the file grew 27 MB → 40 MB.

nodes.label: Idle READ COMMITTED read-only does not block VACUUM
nodes.rationale: Between statements a READ COMMITTED session holds no snapshot. All 100000 dead rows were still removed. Contradicts the common any-idle-in-transaction-stalls-cleanup advice.

nodes.label: Transactions that pin the horizon
nodes.rationale: REPEATABLE READ/SERIALIZABLE even idle (snapshot lives); any writer (backend_xid); any still-executing statement including a long SELECT.

nodes.label: Replication slot and prepared-xact horizon pins
VACUUM
nodes.rationale: Marks dead space reusable under SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE; does not return space to the OS. Deleting half of a 46 MB table left it 46 MB after VACUUM; later inserts reused the space.

nodes.label: VACUUM FULL
nodes.rationale: Rewrites the table under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE and returns space to the OS (46 MB → 23 MB, 260 ms). Only when the table will not regrow. Never on a schedule.

nodes.label: Autovacuum threshold
nodes.rationale: 50 + 0.2 × live_rows. 90000 live → 18050 dead. A 10-million-row table waits for two million dead rows. Override per table, not globally.

nodes.label: idle in transaction
nodes.rationale: BEGIN then silence. wait_event=ClientRead: the server waits on the client. Holds a pool slot, locks, and possibly the horizon until COMMIT/ROLLBACK.

nodes.label: transaction_timeout 25P04
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL 17+. Kills any transaction older than N, busy or idle. Covers the always-active case the idle timeout misses.

nodes.label: statement_timeout does not kill idle transactions
nodes.rationale: A session idle 600 ms with statement_timeout=200ms was still alive. No statement is running.

nodes.label: pg pool error event on backend kill
nodes.rationale: Timeouts kill the backend. pg emits an error event, not a rejected promise. Unhandled, it crashes Node. pool.on('error') is mandatory; release(true) to destroy the client.

nodes.label: Leaked transaction costs a pool slot
Advisory lock
nodes.rationale: A named mutex keyed by a number, not a row. The database enforces the lock, not the invariant. Visible in pg_locks as locktype=advisory.

nodes.label: Session vs transaction advisory locks
nodes.rationale: Prefer pg_advisory_xact_lock: released at COMMIT/ROLLBACK and cannot leak. Session locks survive COMMIT and return to the pool still held.

nodes.label: release(held) after session advisory lock
nodes.rationale: If unlock fails, destroy the pooled connection. A leaked session lock makes every later runIfLeader return false for the process lifetime.

nodes.label: XID wraparound
nodes.rationale: 32-bit XIDs; visibility is modular comparison. If the counter advanced 2^31 past a row's xmin the row would appear future-dated and vanish.

nodes.label: Row freezing
nodes.rationale: VACUUM marks old rows frozen: visible to everyone, no id comparison. relfrozenxid tracks progress; age(relfrozenxid) grows with every database transaction, even on idle tables.

nodes.label: autovacuum_freeze_max_age
nodes.rationale: Anti-wraparound autovacuum at 200 million, under 10% of the 2^31 budget. Runs even if autovacuum is off.

nodes.label: xidWarnLimit and xidStopLimit
nodes.rationale: WARNING at ≈2.134 billion (10 million before stop). Writes refused at ≈2.144 billion. Ten million XIDs is minutes at a few thousand writes/s.

nodes.label: Alert at 500 million not the WARNING
nodes.rationale: The WARNING is the you-already-lost line. Alert at 500 million; treat 200 million as the number that matters. Age past 200 million means the anti-wraparound vacuum cannot advance a pinned horizon.

nodes.label: XID consumption rate
nodes.rationale: One xid per write statement in autocommit (201 for 200 UPDATEs). SELECTs burn zero. Batching 100 writes costs one id. 10000 tx/s exhausts 2^31 in under three days without freezing.

nodes.label: Phase 11 gate: prevent lost updates and idle-in-transaction
Views — naming a query, and their limits
View is a stored query not stored data
nodes.rationale: pg_relation_size is 0 bytes. The view is substituted before planning so the planner optimises one combined query.

nodes.label: View predicate pushdown
nodes.rationale: Filtering on a GROUP BY key pushed down (0.8 ms); filtering the aggregate result forced a full scan (135.8 ms, 170×).

nodes.label: View optimisation fence
nodes.rationale: Aggregates then filtered, DISTINCT, window functions, LIMIT inside the view, and set operations materialise the view before the outer filter.

nodes.label: A view cannot take a parameter
nodes.rationale: CREATE VIEW ... WHERE customer = $1 raises 42P02. Workaround is LANGUAGE sql STABLE SRF or filter at the call site.

nodes.label: WITH CHECK OPTION
nodes.rationale: Without it a write can insert a row that immediately vanishes from the view. With it the insert raises 44000.

nodes.label: Automatically updatable view
nodes.rationale: One table, no aggregate, DISTINCT, GROUP BY, window, or set operation. Otherwise 55000 and an INSTEAD OF trigger is required.

nodes.label: security_invoker views
nodes.rationale: Views run with the owner's privileges by default, bypassing caller RLS. PostgreSQL 15+ security_invoker = true uses the caller's privileges.

nodes.label: BEFORE vs AFTER triggers
nodes.rationale: BEFORE can modify NEW and cancel with RETURN NULL. AFTER assignment to NEW is silently discarded — the row is already written.

nodes.label: FOR EACH ROW vs FOR EACH STATEMENT
nodes.rationale: One UPDATE of 1000 rows: 1000 row firings, 1 statement firing. A statement trigger still fires when zero rows match.

nodes.label: Trigger transition tables
nodes.rationale: REFERENCING OLD TABLE / NEW TABLE lets a statement trigger audit bulk changes in one insert instead of 1000 row inserts.

nodes.label: Trigger WHEN clause
nodes.rationale: Evaluated before the plpgsql call. Measured 0.86× of an unconditional row trigger. Cannot be used on INSTEAD OF.

nodes.label: BEFORE RETURN NULL cancels the row
nodes.rationale: 10 submitted, 5 stored; rowCount reported 5. Prefer RAISE EXCEPTION so the caller sees a rejection.

nodes.label: Trigger firing order is alphabetical
nodes.rationale: Created zebra, alpha, middle; fired alpha, middle, zebra. Name with numeric prefixes if order matters.

nodes.label: Triggers maintain data not behaviour
nodes.rationale: Invisible from the application: right for updated_at and audit, wrong for business rules or external side effects inside the transaction.

nodes.label: Extension available vs installed
nodes.rationale: Available = files on disk (60 in postgres:18-alpine). Installed = CREATE EXTENSION in this database. pg_available_extensions vs pg_extension.

nodes.label: Extensions are per database not per cluster
nodes.rationale: CREATE DATABASE does not copy extensions. digest() works in one database and raises 42883 in another on the same server.

nodes.label: DROP EXTENSION blocked by type users
nodes.rationale: 2BP01 while any column uses a type the extension provides. CASCADE drops those columns.

nodes.label: shared_preload_libraries for pg_stat_statements
nodes.rationale: CREATE EXTENSION alone is not enough; the library must be preloaded and the server restarted.

nodes.label: unnest bulk-insert bridge
nodes.rationale: 5000 rows through 3 parameters. VALUES needs 15000 and caps at 21845 rows because the protocol allows 65535 parameters. Mismatched arrays pad with NULL.

nodes.label: jsonb_to_recordset
nodes.rationale: One parameter for any number of rows when the body is already JSON. Column types declared in the AS list. unnest is generally faster.

nodes.label: generate_series
nodes.rationale: Endpoints inclusive (hourly over one day = 25 rows). Descending needs a negative step. Step 0 raises 22023. Gap-fill needs count(e.id) not count(*).

nodes.label: WITH ORDINALITY
nodes.rationale: The only way to preserve array input order once values become rows. pos is bigint; pg returns it as text.

nodes.label: Put SRFs in FROM not SELECT
nodes.rationale: SRFs produce rows. Two SRFs in SELECT run in lockstep with NULL padding. An SRF in WHERE raises 0A000. ROWS FROM makes zipping explicit.

nodes.label: Materialized view stores its result
