nodes.rationale: Appears in FROM; alias required. Any rows × any columns. Runs once if uncorrelated.

nodes.label: Correlated subquery
nodes.rationale: A reference to an outer column makes any of the three kinds correlated and changes the cost class entirely — SubPlan loops per outer row, an N+1 inside one statement.

nodes.label: NOT IN versus NOT EXISTS
nodes.rationale: Three spellings of one membership question. Negated IN returns nothing when a NULL appears, because of three-valued logic. NOT EXISTS does not have that trap.

nodes.label: Counting for pagination
nodes.rationale: The page is cheap; the total is not. Decide which question the list endpoint is actually being asked. Work down the four-answer list, not up it.

nodes.label: limit + 1 has-more
nodes.rationale: Fetch pageSize+1; if the extra row arrives there is another page, then slice it off. Measured 2.10 ms vs 2.11 ms for the plain page — free and exact. Cannot render Page 1 of N. Classic bug: forgetting to slice so the last page returns 21 items.

nodes.label: Exact count(*)
nodes.rationale: A second query returning the exact total. Measured 48.83 ms vs 2.11 ms for the page (~23×) over 125000 matching rows. Scales with matches; the page stays bounded by LIMIT. Required only for a numbered pager.

nodes.label: count(*) OVER ()
nodes.rationale: One-query total. Measured 152.77 ms — three times a separate count(*). WindowAgg must see every matching row before emitting the first, so LIMIT cannot stop early.

nodes.label: WindowAgg defeats LIMIT
nodes.rationale: count(*) OVER () is unknown until the last matching row. Plan showed WindowAgg actual rows=125000 feeding a Limit of 20. You pay a full scan and carry the total on every returned row.

nodes.label: Planner row estimate
nodes.rationale: EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON) Plan Rows is free and was 125833 vs actual 125000 (0.7% high) here. Accuracy is not guaranteed: multi-column filters, correlated columns, and stale statistics can miss by orders of magnitude. Label it approximate.

nodes.label: Capped count
nodes.rationale: count(*) over a subquery with LIMIT cap. Exact below the ceiling, report 1000+ at the cap. Pays only when matches are plentiful: 1.46 ms vs 33.85 ms (23×) at 125000 matches; 3.01 vs 3.02 ms at 120 matches — no saving.

nodes.label: reltuples
nodes.rationale: Approximate whole-table row count in pg_class, maintained by VACUUM/ANALYZE. Good for order of magnitude; stale between maintenance; never for a user-reconciled total.

nodes.label: Ordered-set aggregates
nodes.rationale: Aggregates that need input ordered first. Syntax: fraction as argument, column in WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ...). That ORDER BY is the aggregate's definition order, not query output order. Family costs 3.1× avg() because sorting is unavoidable.

nodes.label: WITHIN GROUP
nodes.rationale: Supplies the ordering an ordered-set aggregate is defined over. Syntax tell of the family. percentile_cont(0.5, amount) is a syntax error; the column goes in WITHIN GROUP.

nodes.label: percentile_cont
nodes.rationale: Interpolates; can return a value not in the input (2.5 from 1,2,3,4). Numeric and interval only. Standard choice for p95/p99 latency. Ignores NULLs. two-arg round needs ::numeric.

nodes.label: percentile_disc
nodes.rationale: Returns an actual value from the set. Works on anything sortable. percentile_disc(1.0) is max(); percentile_disc(0.0) is min().

nodes.label: percentile_cont array form
nodes.rationale: percentile_cont(ARRAY[0.5, 0.9, 0.99]) sorts once and returns an array. Separate calls would sort three times. Dashboard form.

nodes.label: Percentiles do not compose
nodes.rationale: You cannot average hourly p95s to get a daily p95. Store enough per bucket to recompute, or use a mergeable sketch (t-digest). Measured 178.32 ms vs 57.41 ms for avg() on 500k rows.

nodes.label: mode()
nodes.rationale: Most common value. Ties broken by WITHIN GROUP order, with no tie flag. Four kinds tied at 125000 each returned click (or view if reversed). Empty set is NULL. Prefer top-N with counts for a UI.

nodes.label: bool_and
nodes.rationale: Set version of all. Empty set is NULL, not true — same aggregate-empty rule as sum(). JS if (row.all_paid) treats NULL as false, so a customer with no orders looks unpaid. coalesce(..., true). every() is the SQL alias.

nodes.label: bool_or
nodes.rationale: Set version of any. Pair with a FILTERed count. Empty-set default should be coalesce(..., false).

nodes.label: every()
nodes.rationale: Standard-SQL alias for bool_and. Measured identical. Pick one spelling.

nodes.label: Hypothetical-set aggregates
nodes.rationale: Where a value would rank if inserted: rank, dense_rank, percent_rank, cume_dist. Argument list must match ORDER BY in number and type. Window rank ranks existing rows; this ranks a value that is not there.

nodes.label: rank() WITHIN GROUP
nodes.rationale: rank(150) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY amount) returned 66721. bigint in the driver until ::int.

nodes.label: percent_rank() WITHIN GROUP
nodes.rationale: Maps a value to a fraction — inverse of percentile_cont. percent_rank(150) returned 0.1334. Use when you have a score and want its percentile.

nodes.label: Window frames
nodes.rationale: A window aggregate is computed over a slice of the partition. You get a frame whether or not you write one. Syntax: {ROWS|RANGE|GROUPS} BETWEEN start AND end [EXCLUDE ...]. Omitting BETWEEN implies AND CURRENT ROW.

nodes.label: ROWS frame
nodes.rationale: Counts physical rows. Running total that advances one row at a time. Write ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING even when ORDER BY is unique, because RANGE and ROWS only agree until peers appear.

nodes.label: RANGE frame
nodes.rationale: Treats equal ORDER BY values as peers sharing one frame. Default. Running total per distinct ordering value. Two same-day rows both showed 30 under RANGE versus 10 then 30 under ROWS.

nodes.label: Default window frame
nodes.rationale: RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW. Why a running total over a non-unique ORDER BY jumps two rows at once. Hidden in development against unique keys.

nodes.label: Window peers
nodes.rationale: Rows with equal ORDER BY values are indistinguishable to a RANGE frame and share one total. Add a unique tiebreaker or write ROWS.

nodes.label: Partial moving-average window
nodes.rationale: Frame clips at the partition edge rather than returning NULL. First row of a 3-row MA is its own value. Detect with count(*) over the same frame and blank short windows.

nodes.label: Ranking functions ignore the frame
nodes.rationale: row_number, rank, dense_rank, lag, lead are defined over the partition. PostgreSQL accepts a frame clause and silently ignores it — even an absurd frame produced identical output. Worse than a rejection. Aggregates plus first_value/last_value/nth_value do depend on the frame.

nodes.label: RANGE value offset
nodes.rationale: Measures the frame in ORDER BY units, so a missing day narrows the window rather than silently widening it. Only correct frame over a sparse series. Exactly one ORDER BY column (42P20). Type must support subtraction (0A000 on text). '6 days' PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW is 7 inclusive days.

nodes.label: GROUPS frame
nodes.rationale: Counts distinct ordering values present in the data. Previous two trading days, not last 48 hours. Accepts multi-column ORDER BY — workaround when 42P20 blocks a RANGE offset. Agrees with RANGE on a dense series; diverges on gaps.

nodes.label: EXCLUDE CURRENT ROW
nodes.rationale: Removes this row from the frame. Leave-one-out: others = 210 minus own amount. Shape for compare-to-the-rest.

nodes.label: EXCLUDE GROUP
nodes.rationale: Removes this row and its peers. Compare this day against all other days. GROUP = TIES + CURRENT ROW.

nodes.label: EXCLUDE TIES
nodes.rationale: Removes peers but keeps the current row. Only option that keeps this row while dropping equals. For a row with one peer: 6→5 versus GROUP 6→4; alone: TIES removes nothing.

nodes.label: EXCLUDE NO OTHERS
nodes.rationale: Default EXCLUDE. Writing it changes nothing; exists to make the default explicit.

nodes.label: 42P20 RANGE offset one ORDER BY column
nodes.rationale: RANGE with offset PRECEDING/FOLLOWING requires exactly one ORDER BY column. Collides with the unique-tiebreaker advice. Drop the tiebreaker or use GROUPS.

nodes.label: 0A000 RANGE offset unsupported type
nodes.rationale: RANGE offset is not supported for text — no defined subtraction. Hits when ordering by a formatted date string instead of the date.

nodes.label: WITH RECURSIVE
nodes.rationale: Follows a parent pointer to arbitrary depth in one statement. Anchor plus recursive term joined by UNION ALL, repeated until the rule produces nothing. The only construct in this phase whose stopping condition lives in the data.

nodes.label: Recursive CTE anchor
nodes.rationale: Starting set, run once. Cast types here so UNION ALL branches agree (name::text). Anchor row is included in subtree aggregates — off-by-one for descendant counts.

nodes.label: Recursive term
nodes.rationale: Joins the table to the CTE, not to itself. c.parent_id = t.id descends; t.parent_id = c.id climbs. Carries depth and path. Table is scanned once per iteration — index the join column or cost is depth × full scan.

nodes.label: Recursive Union
nodes.rationale: Plan node for the whole construct. First child is the anchor; second is the recursive term. loops= on the term is iteration count (depth). Measured loops=4 on a 4-level tree.

nodes.label: WorkTable Scan
nodes.rationale: Rows produced by the previous iteration — the only input the recursive term reads. Not everything found so far.

nodes.label: generate_series instead of recursion
nodes.rationale: Use WITH RECURSIVE when following data shape (hierarchy, graph). When the next value is a pure function of the last, generate_series is simpler and faster.

nodes.label: Recursive CTE cycle
nodes.rationale: A cycle means an iteration never produces no new rows. Measured 107 rows from an 8-row table before d<40 stopped it. A self-referencing FK guarantees the parent exists, not acyclicity. No standard constraint enforces a tree.

nodes.label: Recursive depth guard
nodes.rationale: WHERE t.d < N in the recursive term. Universal, production-mandatory even on believed trees. Cannot distinguish a deep hierarchy from a loop; truncates both silently. Choose a bound above any legitimate depth.

nodes.label: UNION instead of UNION ALL
nodes.rationale: Discards already-produced rows so a second lap yields nothing and recursion stops. Measured 8 unique rows and termination. Pays comparison cost. Incompatible with depth or path columns — every lap is a different row. UNION and a path column do not compose.

nodes.label: CYCLE clause
nodes.rationale: PG 14+. CYCLE id SET is_cycle USING path. Only option that reports the cycle. Measured root twice, second is_cycle true, then stop. Prefer when cycles may be legitimate. Pair with a depth guard.

nodes.label: SEARCH clause
nodes.rationale: SEARCH DEPTH FIRST BY id SET ord (or BREADTH FIRST). Creates a sortable column; you must still ORDER BY ord. Replaces a hand-rolled path used only for sorting.

nodes.label: 42P19 recursive term restrictions
nodes.rationale: Recursive reference must not appear more than once; aggregates forbidden in the recursive term (would summarise only the previous iteration). Also bars LEFT JOIN against the CTE, ORDER BY and LIMIT inside the term. Aggregate outside.

nodes.label: Missing RECURSIVE is 42P01
nodes.rationale: Plain WITH cannot self-reference. Error is the ordinary relation does not exist, so it is misdiagnosed as a typo or search_path problem. Keyword attaches to WITH, not the CTE name.

nodes.label: GROUPING SETS
nodes.rationale: Ask for several grouping levels in one statement. () is the empty set — the grand total. One scan feeding MixedAggregate, but grouping sets are not parallelised.

nodes.label: ROLLUP
nodes.rationale: ROLLUP (a, b) expands to GROUPING SETS ((a,b), (a), ()) — drop columns from the right. Hierarchy shorthand. n+1 sets. Does not produce per-b totals. ROLLUP (a,b) GROUPING levels are 0, 1 and 3 — never 2.

nodes.label: CUBE
nodes.rationale: CUBE (a, b) is every subset: ((a,b), (a), (b), ()). 2^n sets. Three columns is 8, four is 16. Measured 12 rows vs 9 ROLLUP vs 5 plain. Ask for the sets you need instead of reaching for CUBE.

nodes.label: Empty grouping set ()
nodes.rationale: Group by nothing — the grand-total row over the whole filtered table.

nodes.label: MixedAggregate
nodes.rationale: Plan node that maintains several hash tables from one pass. One Hash Key line per grouping set over a single Seq Scan.

nodes.label: Grouping sets are not parallelised
nodes.rationale: Like-for-like on the same three sets, cached 500k table: GROUPING SETS 293.67 ms vs three separate GROUP BYs 170.22 ms (0.58× — one scan loses). Plain GROUP BY got Gather Merge and two workers. One-pass wins when I/O dominates, not when CPU does.

nodes.label: GROUPING()
nodes.rationale: Returns 1 if that column was rolled up in this row, 0 if it is a real grouping value. Several columns yield a bit mask, MSB first. 42803 if the argument is not a grouping expression. The only reliable discriminator.

nodes.label: Subtotal NULL versus data NULL
nodes.rationale: A rolled-up column is NULL; so is a genuine missing value. Measured two country:null rows, n=1 is_subtotal=0 versus n=7 is_subtotal=1. Invisible until a NULL exists in the data — same latent shape as the NOT IN trap. Label with CASE WHEN GROUPING=1 THEN ALL ELSE coalesce(col,'(none)').

nodes.label: pg.Pool
nodes.rationale: One Pool, created once at module scope, exported, shared by every request. pg 8.23.0, pure JavaScript, no libpq. Default import then pg.Pool is the form that has never broken.

nodes.label: Lazy pool connection
nodes.rationale: new Pool() performs no I/O. Measured totalCount 0 idleCount 0 after construct, 1 and 1 after first query. Bad host is ECONNREFUSED on first query, not at startup. Add await pool.query('SELECT 1') before listen().

nodes.label: pool.on('error')
nodes.rationale: Idle pooled connections can be killed server-side. Unhandled 'error' on the pool is an uncaught exception that kills the process. Handler usually just logs; the pool discards the dead connection.

nodes.label: application_name
nodes.rationale: Appears in pg_stat_activity so every connection is attributable. Costs nothing. Without it the column is empty strings during an incident.

nodes.label: One pool per process
nodes.rationale: Two pools of max 10 are 20 connections against default max_connections 100 shared by every client. Exceptions: replica pool, dedicated Client for LISTEN, short-lived migration pool. Per-request pools defeat pooling.

nodes.label: pg.Client
nodes.rationale: Exactly one connection you own from connect() to end(). Right when a session must outlive a single query and pooling buys nothing. Single-use; connect() twice raises Client has already been connected.

nodes.label: pool.connect()
nodes.rationale: Checks one connection out of the pool. Use for transactions, SET, cursors, advisory locks, named prepared statements — anything session-stateful. release() in finally. Not a bare Client.

nodes.label: LISTEN needs a dedicated Client
nodes.rationale: LISTEN via pool.query() returns the connection to the pool with no handler; notifications are lost. The real new pg.Client() case. Also honest for one-shot migration/admin scripts.

nodes.label: waitingCount
nodes.rationale: max is a queue depth, not a speed limit. Fourth query against max:3 raised waitingCount to 1. Persistent waitingCount>0 means the pool is the bottleneck. Unreleased clients exhaust it.

nodes.label: connectionString
nodes.rationale: One of three config sources (URL, object, PG* env). Mixing URL with database/user looks like overrides and is not — the parsed string wins with no warning. Pool-level options (max, idleTimeoutMillis, ssl object) combine safely. Percent-encode passwords.

nodes.label: sslmode=require
nodes.rationale: In pg 8.x treated as verify-full — encrypts AND verifies, stricter than libpq. pg 9.0 will adopt libpq semantics so connections that verify today will silently stop verifying. Write sslmode=verify-full now.

nodes.label: sslmode=verify-full
nodes.rationale: Encrypt and verify certificate and hostname. What production should write explicitly. For a private CA pass ssl:{ca:...}; rejectUnauthorized:false is local-dev only.

nodes.label: password as function
nodes.rationale: Evaluated when a connection is opened, not per query. Measured called 1× for 2 queries on 1 connection. Makes IAM/RDS tokens work. Keep idleTimeoutMillis below token TTL.

nodes.label: connection options passthrough
nodes.rationale: options: '-c search_path=app,public -c statement_timeout=5000' applies on every connection the pool opens. SET through pool.query() lands on one arbitrary connection and is lost.

nodes.label: pool.query
nodes.rationale: query(text), query(text, values), query(configObject). Object form needed for name, rowMode, types. All return the same Result. Callback form exists; do not use it in new code.

nodes.label: Positional $n placeholders
nodes.rationale: $1 is values[0], 1-based, may repeat. Numbering must be contiguous; extra values are silently ignored. Wire-protocol $n unchanged. Renumbering is the failure mode — build fragments and the array together.

nodes.label: ANY($1::int[])
nodes.rationale: One parameter for a variable-length list. Statement text stays constant for the plan cache. Sidesteps NOT IN null trap and the 65535-parameter ceiling.

nodes.label: undefined becomes SQL NULL
nodes.rationale: null and undefined both become SQL NULL with no error. A misspelled property inserts NULL. Validate the object before building the array.

nodes.label: Identifiers are not parameters
nodes.rationale: ORDER BY $1 sorts every row by the same constant string and raises no error. Column names, table names and sort direction need an allowlist.

nodes.label: 65535 parameter ceiling
nodes.rationale: 21845 rows ok (65535 params); 21846 rows → 08P01 bind message has 2 parameter formats but 0 parameters. Fix with unnest or chunk. Parameterized calls also reject multi-statement text (42601).

nodes.label: SQLSTATE / err.code
nodes.rationale: Branch on the five-character SQLSTATE, never on err.message. Messages are localised and version-dependent. Class 42 is always a bug (500), never a user 400. Socket failures are Node errnos, not SQLSTATEs. Test /^[0-9A-Z]{5}$/.

nodes.label: 23505 unique_violation
nodes.rationale: Map to HTTP 409. Match err.constraint, not just the code — a table can have several unique constraints. Insert-and-catch is the race-free check. 23505 fills constraint, not column; 23502 fills column.

nodes.label: Retryable 40001 and 40P01
nodes.rationale: Serialization failure and deadlock are isolation doing its job. Retry the whole transaction with backoff and jitter, not the failed statement. Connection errors retryable for reads; writes only if idempotent.

nodes.label: err.detail leaks data
nodes.rationale: detail contains the offending value (Key (email)=(a@x.com) already exists). Returning it enables user enumeration. Log detail; return your own message keyed off code and constraint.

nodes.label: FATAL errors arrive as events
nodes.rationale: When the server terminates a connection there may be no in-flight query to reject, so pg emits 'error' on the client or pool. Unhandled, the process dies. Reinforces pool.on('error').

nodes.label: pg Result object
nodes.rationale: Public fields: rows, rowCount, command, fields, oid. Underscore fields are internal. Multi-statement without params resolves to an array of Results, so result.rows is undefined.

nodes.label: rowCount
nodes.rationale: Rows the statement acted on, not rows.length. UPDATE without RETURNING: rowCount 1, rows []. DDL: rowCount null, not 0 — if (!rowCount) treats CREATE as failure. MERGE sums inserts, updates and deletes.

nodes.label: Result.fields
nodes.rationale: Column metadata: name and dataTypeID (OID). 20=int8, 25=text, 23=int4. Present even when zero rows. Driver uses OID to choose a parser — why int8 arrives as a string.

nodes.label: SELECT * duplicate column collapse
nodes.rationale: Joined SELECT * can return four columns in fields and two keys in the row object. Last name wins, no error. Alias columns or use rowMode array.

nodes.label: rowMode: array
nodes.rationale: Rows as positional arrays. Preserves duplicate names, suits CSV, skips object construction on large results. Cost is position-dependent code.

nodes.label: Phase 7 — The pg driver, end to end
nodes.rationale: Target PostgreSQL 18.4, Node 24, pg. Gate: open a pool, parameterize queries, map 23505, and never leak clients.

nodes.label: pool.connect and release
nodes.rationale: Checkout is yours until release(). A missed release never returns the connection. release() does not close, roll back, or reset session state.

nodes.label: Pool total idle waiting counters
nodes.rationale: totalCount, idleCount, waitingCount. A request past max waits rather than errors. Sustained waitingCount > 0 is the leak or undersize signal.

nodes.label: Pooled connection leak
nodes.rationale: A thrown query before release() loses the client for process lifetime. After max leaks, later requests hang until connectionTimeoutMillis.

nodes.label: withClient helper
nodes.rationale: Never write checkout by hand. connect, run fn(client), release in finally so every path returns the client.

nodes.label: withTransaction helper
nodes.rationale: BEGIN/COMMIT must share one connection. Wrap ROLLBACK so a dead connection does not mask the original error. release() stays in finally.

nodes.label: release(true) destroys the connection
nodes.rationale: Truthy release discards the socket. Use after FATAL, client-side query_timeout, or unknown session state so one bad request cannot poison later borrows.

nodes.label: DISCARD ALL before release
nodes.rationale: release() keeps search_path, temp tables, and prepared statements. DISCARD ALL resets them but cannot run inside a transaction.

nodes.label: pg type parsing
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL sends text; pg converts by column type OID. json/jsonb arrive parsed, arrays as arrays, bytea as Buffer, NULL as null.

nodes.label: bigint arrives as string
nodes.rationale: JS number is exact only to 2^53-1. int8 goes to 2^63-1. Auto-convert would silently corrupt. count(*) therefore returns '12'.

nodes.label: numeric arrives as string
nodes.rationale: numeric is arbitrary precision; float rounding is unacceptable for money. Keep the string and use a decimal library.

nodes.label: date and timestamp read in Node timezone
nodes.rationale: date becomes Date at local midnight; timestamp assumes local offset. Passes UTC CI and is wrong east of UTC. Keep date as a string.

nodes.label: timestamptz as instant
nodes.rationale: timestamptz is a genuine instant and converts correctly. Prefer it for every moment in time.

nodes.label: PostgresInterval object
nodes.rationale: Months and days are not fixed durations, so there is no correct millisecond value. Use extract(epoch FROM …) for a number.

nodes.label: Type OID parser key
nodes.rationale: fields[i].dataTypeID selects the parser. Array OIDs are distinct from element OIDs. Custom types get per-database OIDs.

nodes.label: Outbound objects need JSON.stringify
nodes.rationale: Parameters do not auto-serialise objects. Insert JSON.stringify(obj) with $1::jsonb or the column stores [object Object].

nodes.label: pg.types.setTypeParser
nodes.rationale: One process-wide registry. Affects every pool, query, and library using pg. Register once before opening the pool.

nodes.label: Override date OID 1082 to string
nodes.rationale: The almost-always-right global override. A date is a calendar label; Date-at-local-midnight produces off-by-one days.

nodes.label: int8 parser Number vs BigInt
nodes.rationale: Number is silent-lossy above 2^53-1. BigInt is exact but contagious and JSON.stringify throws. Corpus default: cast per query.

nodes.label: TypeOverrides per query
nodes.rationale: Scopes a parser to one query or one pool. Safe form when a single report needs numbers and the rest of the app does not.

nodes.label: SQL casts instead of global parsers
nodes.rationale: No global state, visible at the call site. Overflow raises rather than silently truncating.

nodes.label: Array types have their own OIDs
nodes.rationale: Changing 1700 (numeric) does not change 1231 (numeric[]). Override both or aggregated columns surprise you.

nodes.label: Custom type OID lookup in pg_type
nodes.rationale: Enums, domains, composites get OIDs at creation. Look them up at startup; never hard-code.

nodes.label: Named prepared statements
nodes.rationale: query({name}) issues server PREPARE. First call Parse; later Bind/Execute. Measured 1.6x on a hot single-row lookup.

nodes.label: Custom vs generic plan after five executions
nodes.rationale: First five executions use custom plans with real values. From the sixth PostgreSQL may switch to a generic plan, which is wrong on skewed data.

nodes.label: plan_cache_mode
nodes.rationale: force_custom_plan always plans with values; force_generic_plan never replans; auto is default. Use force_custom_plan on skewed tables.

nodes.label: Prepared statements are per session
nodes.rationale: A name prepared on one backend is invisible to another. A pool of N prepares up to N times. Names must be a small fixed unique set.

nodes.label: PgBouncer breaks named statements
nodes.rationale: Transaction or statement pooling routes consecutive queries to different backends. Symptom: 26000 prepared statement does not exist.

nodes.label: statement_timeout
nodes.rationale: Server-side cancel. Raises 57014; connection stays usable. The only timeout that stops the database doing work. Prefer ALTER ROLE.

nodes.label: query_timeout
nodes.rationale: Client-side: pg rejects while the server keeps executing. Use with statement_timeout set slightly lower. release(true) afterwards.

nodes.label: idle_in_transaction_session_timeout
nodes.rationale: Kills a session that is open but idle. Protects VACUUM xmin and locks. Arrives as a Client error event, not a rejected query.

nodes.label: connectionTimeoutMillis
nodes.rationale: Give up acquiring a connection, including waiting for a free pooled one. Fires when a leak saturates the pool.

nodes.label: idleTimeoutMillis
nodes.rationale: Close unused pooled connections. Set below intermediary idle TCP drops to avoid connection terminated unexpectedly.

nodes.label: lock_timeout
nodes.rationale: Fail fast when waiting on a lock. Use before ALTER TABLE so ACCESS EXCLUSIVE does not queue the whole site.

nodes.label: pool.on error handler
nodes.rationale: FATAL with no in-flight query emits an unhandled error event and kills Node. Mandatory for idle-in-transaction termination.

nodes.label: Simple query protocol
nodes.rationale: No values argument: the string is a script. Several statements run and query() returns an array of Result objects.

nodes.label: Extended query protocol
nodes.rationale: A values argument permits exactly one statement. Extra commands raise 42601, which is stacked-statement injection protection.

nodes.label: Empty params array is not parameterized
nodes.rationale: pg switches protocols on present-and-non-empty values. query(sql, []) still uses the simple protocol.

nodes.label: Multi-statement implicit transaction
nodes.rationale: A simple-query string is one implicit transaction. A later failure rolls back earlier successes. Feature for migration files.

nodes.label: One statement per call
nodes.rationale: Default everywhere except schema files. Buys parameters, attributable errors, and a consistent Result. Use a CTE, not concatenated statements.

nodes.label: pool.end
nodes.rationale: Waits for in-flight queries, closes every connection, permanently retires the pool. Second end() throws. Queries after end reject.

nodes.label: HTTP close then pool.end
nodes.rationale: server.close first, drain in-flight requests, then pool.end. Reverse order turns every deploy into a burst of 500s.

nodes.label: client.end vs release
nodes.rationale: end() closes a standalone Client. A client from pool.connect() gets release(). end() on a pooled client is a bug.

nodes.label: Module-scope pool keeps the event loop alive
nodes.rationale: An open socket keeps Node running. Tests hang after results; scripts never exit. await pool.end() in teardown or finally.

nodes.label: LISTEN/NOTIFY from Node
nodes.rationale: Push to a connected client. Needs a dedicated Client, delivers on COMMIT, stores nothing. Treat as a hint, never a queue.

nodes.label: Dedicated Client for LISTEN
nodes.rationale: LISTEN is session state. pool.query returns the connection immediately so notifications are lost. Sending via pool is fine.

nodes.label: pg_notify function
nodes.rationale: NOTIFY channel and payload are syntax. pg_notify takes ordinary parameters so a dynamic payload is not concatenated.

nodes.label: NOTIFY delivery on COMMIT
nodes.rationale: Nothing is delivered while the transaction is open. ROLLBACK discards them. Notify in the same transaction as the write.

nodes.label: NOTIFY dedup within a transaction
nodes.rationale: Identical channel/payload pairs fold to one delivery. You cannot count notifications.

nodes.label: NOTIFY 8000-byte payload limit
nodes.rationale: Over 8000 bytes raises 22023. Send an id and let the listener fetch the row.

nodes.label: NOTIFY plus queue table
nodes.rationale: No persistence, ack, or replay. Queue table is truth; NOTIFY only removes latency. Poll with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED.

nodes.label: pg-cursor streaming
nodes.rationale: Fetches in batches so memory stops depending on row count. Needs a checked-out client, read(n) until empty, close then release.

nodes.label: pool.query buffers the whole result
nodes.rationale: Heap grew +101 MB for 300000 rows, linear in result size. First row waits for the last.

nodes.label: DECLARE cursor dies on COMMIT
nodes.rationale: FETCH after COMMIT is 34000. WITH HOLD materialises the whole result at commit. pg-cursor uses a protocol portal with the same binding.

nodes.label: Long cursor snapshot pins xmin
nodes.rationale: A twenty-minute export is twenty minutes of no VACUUM database-wide. Hidden cost of streaming.

nodes.label: Keyset batching instead of a cursor
nodes.rationale: Each LIMIT chunk is its own short transaction on a pooled connection. Interruptible, no long snapshot. Sees rows committed during the run.

nodes.label: postgres.js
nodes.rationale: Tagged templates replace $1. Result is the array. Built-in pool, sql.begin, sql.listen, cursors. Smaller ecosystem than pg.

nodes.label: Interpolation is parameterization
nodes.rationale: ${} inside the tag is a bind parameter, never SQL text. Identifiers need sql(name) and still an allowlist.

nodes.label: sql.begin transaction API
nodes.rationale: Makes release-in-finally structural. Same semantics as withTransaction; you cannot forget the rollback.

nodes.label: Choose pg unless greenfield ESM
nodes.rationale: Most tooling expects a pg Pool. Migrating every query for API polish is rarely worth it. Neither driver changes schema, indexes, or plans.

nodes.label: Migrations
nodes.rationale: A numbered file that runs exactly once, inside a transaction, with the fact that it ran recorded in the database.

nodes.label: schema_migrations tracking table
nodes.rationale: version PRIMARY KEY, applied_at, checksum. The database records its own version. Second run applies nothing.

nodes.label: Forward-only migrations
nodes.rationale: Down migrations are untested, run months later, and cannot restore DROP COLUMN data. Recovery is a new forward file plus backup.

nodes.label: Migration file checksum
nodes.rationale: Never edit a shipped file. Hash comparison fails the deploy when two environments share a version and differ in schema.

nodes.label: Lexical migration filename order
nodes.rationale: Unpadded sort is 1, 10, 11, 2. Surfaces as 42P01 on a fresh database. Zero-pad or UTC timestamps.

nodes.label: pg_advisory_xact_lock around migrate
nodes.rationale: Taken inside the same transaction that reads the tracking table and applies files. Five concurrent runners: one applied, four no-ops.

nodes.label: Migrations as a deploy step
nodes.rationale: Not at app boot. A failed migration should stop the deploy. App role should not have CREATE/ALTER. Long ACCESS EXCLUSIVE must not block old instances.

nodes.label: Seeding
nodes.rationale: A seed runs more than once. If twice is not identical to once, it is a data-corruption script.

nodes.label: ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
nodes.rationale: Requires a unique constraint. Idempotency is enforced by the database. SELECT-then-INSERT is not safe under concurrency.

nodes.label: ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE
nodes.rationale: Reassert reference data the code depends on. EXCLUDED is the row that would have been inserted. Use DO NOTHING when a human may edit the row.

nodes.label: Identity consumed on skipped conflict
nodes.rationale: ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING draws the identity before detecting conflict. Two rows, three runs, sequence at 6. Sequences are not gapless.

nodes.label: Deterministic fixtures
nodes.rationale: Math.random, Date.now, or unseeded faker make tests unreproducible. Pin emails and timestamps. Volume via generate_series.

nodes.label: Bulk insert that scales
nodes.rationale: One row per query is the common Node performance bug. 10000 rows: 20165 ms autocommit loop vs 84 ms unnest — 240x.

nodes.label: Autocommit WAL flush cost
nodes.rationale: Each standalone INSERT commits and flushes WAL. One transaction around the loop: 20165 to 2559 ms. Remaining cost is 10000 round trips.

nodes.label: INSERT SELECT unnest
nodes.rationale: One array per column; statement text is constant. Casts required. Supports ON CONFLICT and RETURNING. Materialises all values in heap.

nodes.label: COPY FROM STDIN from Node
nodes.rationale: Streaming, bounded memory, no ON CONFLICT or RETURNING. From Node, unnest beat pg-copy-streams 2.7–3x because of JS CSV formatting.

nodes.label: 65535 parameter wire limit
nodes.rationale: Protocol encodes parameter count in 16 bits. 21845 rows of 3 columns ok; 21846 is 08P01. Batch by floor(65535/columns) or use unnest.

nodes.label: SQL in .sql files
nodes.rationale: Template-literal SQL is invisible to formatters, linters, and psql. Files restore tooling, reviewable diffs, and a boundary against concatenation.

nodes.label: Cached sql file loader
nodes.rationale: Read once per process into a Map. Skip the cache in development so edits take effect without restart.

nodes.label: Resolve SQL paths from import.meta.url
nodes.rationale: process.cwd() is launch directory and differs in tests vs production. import.meta.url is the module location.

nodes.label: Named parameter shim
nodes.rationale: Rewrite :name to $n at load time. Values never enter SQL text. Regex must not match :: casts.

nodes.label: Transactional DDL
nodes.rationale: Failed migration leaves nothing behind, including the tracking row. Makes forward-only practical. MySQL/Oracle need manual cleanup.

nodes.label: Statements that cannot run in a transaction
nodes.rationale: CREATE/DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY, VACUUM, CREATE/DROP DATABASE fail with 25001 inside BEGIN.

nodes.label: INVALID leftover CONCURRENTLY index
nodes.rationale: A failed CONCURRENTLY build is not rolled back. Planner ignores it; writes still maintain it. Find via pg_index WHERE NOT indisvalid.

nodes.label: SET LOCAL lock_timeout in migrations
nodes.rationale: SET LOCAL reverts at commit. Plain SET on a pooled connection leaks into later app queries. 55P03 is the good fail-fast outcome.

nodes.label: migrate no-transaction directive
nodes.rationale: Per-file opt-out so CONCURRENTLY can run unwrapped. Honest shape: most DDL should be atomic; non-blocking statements cannot be.

nodes.label: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS
nodes.rationale: Makes a statement idempotent. Not concurrency-safe, not a migration, does not compare definitions. Three gaps the syntax hides.

nodes.label: IF NOT EXISTS is not concurrency-safe
nodes.rationale: Catalog check and insert are not one atomic step. 228 of 500 concurrent attempts failed with 23505 on pg_type_typname_nsp_index.

nodes.label: IF NOT EXISTS is a name check
nodes.rationale: Editing CREATE to add a column is a silent no-op where the table exists. Migrations express change; IF NOT EXISTS expresses absence.

nodes.label: ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS type trap
nodes.rationale: Matches column name only. Existing integer vs expected text is a silent no-op. CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS compares name, not definition.

nodes.label: Minimal migration runner
nodes.rationale: About sixty lines: tracking table, one client, advisory lock after BEGIN, lexical sort, checksum, apply plus record in one transaction.

nodes.label: Batch vs per-file migration transaction
nodes.rationale: Batch is all-or-nothing and simpler. Per-file resumes, releases locks, and is the only way to opt a CONCURRENTLY file out. Tools default to per-file.

nodes.label: Where sixty lines stops being enough
nodes.rationale: Switch at CONCURRENTLY opt-out, timestamped generator, dry-run/status, baselining, down migrations, or JS backfills.

nodes.label: pg-copy-streams
nodes.rationale: Turns client.query into a writable stream. Needs a checked-out client because COPY is a distinct protocol mode.

nodes.label: pipeline not pipe for COPY
nodes.rationale: pipeline propagates errors and destroys both ends. .pipe() leaves the connection stuck mid-COPY and poisons the pool.

nodes.label: COPY text vs csv format
nodes.rationale: text is default: tab delimiter, \N is NULL. csv needs WITH (FORMAT csv). Comma data on text dumps the line into column one.

nodes.label: COPY NULL representation
nodes.rationale: text: \N is NULL, empty field is ''. csv: unquoted empty is NULL, "" is ''. Common NOT NULL violation source.

nodes.label: UNLOGGED all-text staging table
nodes.rationale: COPY is all-or-nothing. Stage as text, then INSERT SELECT with validation to restore ON CONFLICT and inspect rejects. UNLOGGED skips WAL.

nodes.label: Local development database
nodes.rationale: Disposable, version-matched to production, on a non-colliding port. postgres:18-alpine on 55432.

nodes.label: Connect on 127.0.0.1 never localhost
nodes.rationale: Node DNS verbatim order resolves localhost to ::1 first. A container published on IPv4 only yields connection refused.

nodes.label: pg_isready readiness loop
nodes.rationale: Container running is not accepting TCP. First init starts the server twice. sleep 5 is flaky or slow; poll pg_isready or compose healthcheck.

nodes.label: alpine musl vs debian glibc collation
nodes.rationale: Same PostgreSQL 18.4 and en_US.utf8, different ORDER BY. musl locale is a stub and falls back to byte order. Match base image or pin ICU.

nodes.label: tmpfs disposable data directory
nodes.rationale: With working migrations and seeds, rebuild in seconds. Faster (no disk sync) and cannot drift. Never mistake it for a real deployment.

nodes.label: Resetting between test runs
nodes.rationale: Strategy sets suite speed. Timed on 10000 rows: DELETE 12.7 ms, TRUNCATE 4.4 ms, RESTART IDENTITY 4.7 ms, BEGIN/ROLLBACK 0.8 ms.

nodes.label: Transaction rollback per test
nodes.rationale: 16x faster than TRUNCATE because seeds survive. Requires every query on the injected client. Cannot test commit-only behaviour.

nodes.label: TRUNCATE for test reset
nodes.rationale: List every table in one statement, CASCADE for FKs, RESTART IDENTITY for sequences. Separate TRUNCATEs deadlock under parallel files.

nodes.label: TRUNCATE RESTART IDENTITY
nodes.rationale: Plain TRUNCATE left next id at 10001. Tests asserting id === 1 fail on the second run. Prefer not asserting on generated ids.

nodes.label: Inject client into repositories
nodes.rationale: Module-level pool writes commit outside the test transaction and leak. Testability is why repositories take a client first.

nodes.label: Migration tools
nodes.rationale: Every tool implements a tracking table. Choose on workflow assumption: you write SQL, or the tool derives it.

nodes.label: node-pg-migrate
nodes.rationale: SQL or JS files, you own the schema. Natural next step from the hand-written runner for raw SQL and pg.

nodes.label: graphile-migrate
nodes.rationale: One idempotent current.sql re-run on every save, then committed as a numbered file. Fits functions, triggers, views, RLS; poor for incremental ALTER TABLE.

nodes.label: Prisma Migrate
nodes.rationale: schema.prisma is source of truth; migrations are generated by diff. Do not use without Prisma Client.

nodes.label: drizzle-kit
nodes.rationale: TypeScript schema objects; SQL generated by diff. Same write-vs-derive split as Prisma.

nodes.label: Write SQL vs derive migrations
nodes.rationale: Writing SQL keeps CONCURRENTLY, exclusion constraints, triggers. Derived tools type for free but escape-hatch anything the schema language cannot express.

nodes.label: Baselining an existing database
nodes.rationale: Dump schema as one initial migration and mark it applied without running. History before the baseline is no longer replayable.

nodes.label: Schema drift
nodes.rationale: Live schema no longer matches what the code assumes. With migrations it still happens via manual psql fixes, env-only applies, restored backups, ORM sync, or rolled-back deploys. Failure surfaces later as 42703.

nodes.label: Boot-time schema check
nodes.rationale: Compare expected columns against information_schema at boot and process.exit(1). A container that will not start is rollback-able; a running container serving 500s is not.

nodes.label: information_schema type flattening
nodes.rationale: data_type reports numeric for every numeric(p,s), varchar as character varying, identity column_default as null. Privilege-filtered views can hide existing columns.

nodes.label: Generate expected schema in CI
nodes.rationale: A hand-maintained EXPECTED object drifts. Generate after migrations and commit, or diff a scratch migrated catalog against production.

nodes.label: Generating TypeScript types from the schema
Generated TypeScript types
nodes.rationale: A hand-written interface is a guess. Types plus a boot check cover different moments; types are not runtime validation.

nodes.label: pool.query generic is an assertion
nodes.rationale: pg does not validate rows against User. A dropped or renamed column still compiles.

nodes.label: pg default JS type mappings
nodes.rationale: bigint and numeric return as strings; timestamptz and date return Date. Generated id: number for bigint is wrong; user.id + 1 becomes '11'.

nodes.label: Introspect live database for types
nodes.rationale: drizzle-kit pull, kanel. Migrations stay source of truth; types are a committed build artefact.

nodes.label: Query-level type inference
nodes.rationale: pgtyped types the actual SELECT projection. Table-level types still let user.name compile after SELECT id, email.

nodes.label: db:check CI type diff
nodes.rationale: Regenerate types and git diff --exit-code so drift fails the merge, not the deploy.

nodes.label: Phase 8 Schema and data from Node
Phase 8 gate
nodes.rationale: Move on when you can migrate forward-only and seed idempotently without runtime DDL in requests.

nodes.label: DDL as ordinary query
nodes.rationale: CREATE TABLE via client.query returns command CREATE, rowCount null, empty fields. Success is no thrown error.

nodes.label: Identifiers cannot be parameters
nodes.rationale: CREATE TABLE $1 raises 42601 at parse time. Dynamic identifiers need format('%I') plus an allowlist.

nodes.label: Transactional DDL
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL rolls DDL back with the transaction. CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, VACUUM, CREATE DATABASE cannot run inside BEGIN (25001).

nodes.label: Simple vs extended query protocol
nodes.rationale: No params or [] uses simple protocol and returns an array of results. A non-empty params array forces extended protocol: 42601 cannot insert multiple commands.

nodes.label: ADD COLUMN DEFAULT no rewrite
nodes.rationale: Since PostgreSQL 11, ADD COLUMN NOT NULL DEFAULT is O(1); relfilenode unchanged. Changing a column type usually rewrites.

nodes.label: ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock
nodes.rationale: ALTER TABLE takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE, which conflicts with every mode including ACCESS SHARE from SELECT.

nodes.label: DDL lock queue pile-up
nodes.rationale: A 12 ms ALTER queued behind a long read blocked later SELECTs for 2.4 s because locks are granted in request order.

nodes.label: lock_timeout for migrations
nodes.rationale: SET lock_timeout fails with 55P03 instead of stalling the table. statement_timeout is not a substitute because a lock wait is not executing.

nodes.label: CREATE INDEX lock modes
nodes.rationale: CREATE INDEX takes ShareLock (reads ok, writes block). CONCURRENTLY permits writes at the cost of two scans and no transaction.

nodes.label: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS race
nodes.rationale: Catalog check and insert are not atomic. 228 of 500 concurrent attempts failed with 23505 on pg_type_typname_nsp_index.

nodes.label: Silent startup seed duplication
nodes.rationale: 20 workers, 20 duplicate admin rows, zero errors. Fix with a unique constraint plus ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING.

nodes.label: pg_advisory_xact_lock
nodes.rationale: Serialises bootstrap; 500 of 500 succeeded. Prefer the _xact_ form so a crash releases the lock at rollback. Session-scoped pg_advisory_lock can wedge migrations.

nodes.label: Idempotent vs concurrency-safe
nodes.rationale: Idempotent means twice in sequence is the same. Concurrency-safe means twice at the same time is also correct. IF NOT EXISTS buys only the first.

nodes.label: Where DDL belongs
nodes.rationale: Numbered recorded migrations are the normal way. ensureSchema at startup races and is unversioned. DDL in a request handler takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on a live table.

nodes.label: Creating tables from Node
nodes.rationale: pg will run CREATE TABLE. The question is when: from a replayable migration, never from a request handler or application startup.

nodes.label: list with filtering, sorting and pagination
Assembled list query
nodes.rationale: Filter values and limit/offset are parameters. Filter fields, sort column and direction come from an allowlist. Clamp limit to avoid DoS.

nodes.label: ORDER BY unique tiebreaker
nodes.rationale: ORDER BY on a non-unique column is underspecified. Paging 100 rows without , id returned 54 distinct and 46 duplicates. Instability is between offsets, not per-query jitter.

nodes.label: OFFSET pagination cost
nodes.rationale: OFFSET n produces and discards n rows and cannot stay correct under concurrent writes. Use keyset for deep or crawlable lists.

nodes.label: Expensive total count
nodes.rationale: Filtered count(*) scans matching rows. Prefer limit+1 hasMore. Count and page must share one transaction snapshot.

nodes.label: INSERT ... RETURNING
nodes.rationale: Returns the stored row including generated id and DEFAULT now() without a second query. currval is per-session and unsafe through pool.query.

nodes.label: Named RETURNING columns
nodes.rationale: RETURNING * publishes every later column, including password_hash. Name the mapper's columns.

nodes.label: unnest multi-row insert
nodes.rationale: One array parameter per column stays under the 65535-parameter wire limit. RETURNING order is not guaranteed.

nodes.label: Database clock for created_at
nodes.rationale: DEFAULT now() is one clock. Node-generated timestamps disagree across API instances.

nodes.label: Missing row is a successful empty result
nodes.rationale: rowCount 0, rows [], no throw. Any 404 is application-added.

nodes.label: findX null vs getX throw
nodes.rationale: Return null when absence is expected; throw when the caller cannot continue. Names at the call site document the choice.

nodes.label: Do not return undefined
nodes.rationale: JSON.stringify drops undefined keys. rows[0] ?? null keeps the response shape.

nodes.label: Malformed bigint id is 400
nodes.rationale: GET /users/abc raises 22P02. Validate at the edge; map SQLSTATE as a backstop.

nodes.label: Partial updates COALESCE vs built SET
COALESCE patch form
nodes.rationale: Static statement, but absent and explicit null are both null in JS so clearing a field is impossible.

nodes.label: Built SET list
nodes.rationale: Assignments from keys the client sent distinguish absent from null. Keys go through an allowlist; values are parameters.

nodes.label: IS DISTINCT FROM no-op guard
nodes.rationale: SET city = city still writes a row version. IS DISTINCT FROM skips no-ops; <> is NULL when either side is NULL. rowCount 0 then means no change or not found.

nodes.label: jsonb shallow merge patch
nodes.rationale: data || $1 stores JSON null rather than removing a key. Removal is data - key. || is shallow.

nodes.label: Hard delete with RETURNING
nodes.rationale: ON DELETE CASCADE fires. Missing row is rowCount 0, not an error — map to 404.

nodes.label: Soft delete as UPDATE
nodes.rationale: SET deleted_at = now() WHERE deleted_at IS NULL. Foreign keys do not cascade. Every query must filter forever.

nodes.label: Partial unique index for live emails
nodes.rationale: A full unique index blocks re-registration with 23505. CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ... WHERE deleted_at IS NULL. The partial index is unusable if the query omits that predicate.

nodes.label: Soft delete is not an audit log
nodes.rationale: It records that a row is currently deleted, not who or previous values. Later UPDATE overwrites in place.

nodes.label: Idempotency-Key unique constraint
nodes.rationale: The unique index is correctness. Ten racing inserts without ON CONFLICT produced 1 row and 9 23505s. Key must come from the client.

nodes.label: ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING trap
nodes.rationale: Conflict path writes nothing so RETURNING is empty. Retry cannot answer with the resource.

nodes.label: DO UPDATE RETURNING xmax
nodes.rationale: SET key = EXCLUDED.key makes RETURNING fire. (xmax = 0) AS was_inserted distinguishes 201 from 200.

nodes.label: Idempotency-key response table
nodes.rationale: Store status, response jsonb, request_hash. In-flight is 409. Hash mismatch is 422. Scope PRIMARY KEY (user_id, key).

nodes.label: Naturally idempotent operations
nodes.rationale: PUT, DELETE, absolute SET are idempotent. Relative SET balance = balance + 10 and POST that creates a resource are not.

nodes.label: Pool handed instead of client
nodes.rationale: After ROLLBACK, orders=0 items=1. Different backend pids, no PostgreSQL error. Half the request committed.

nodes.label: Pass db through every layer
nodes.rationale: Only the outermost layer names pool. A service that opens its own transaction cannot be composed.

nodes.label: AsyncLocalStorage ambient client
nodes.rationale: Removes the argument so forgetting db is impossible. ?? pool silently autocommits when async context is lost; missing store should throw.

nodes.label: Lost update across requests
nodes.rationale: Two concurrent read-modify-writes both reported ok and left 120 instead of 130. No transaction can span GET then later PUT.

nodes.label: Version column guard
nodes.rationale: UPDATE ... SET version = version + 1 WHERE version = $n. Increment must be in the same statement. updated_at fails when two updates share now().

nodes.label: rowCount 0 is 404 or 409
nodes.rationale: Missing row and stale version both yield rowCount 0. Re-read or a data-modifying CTE distinguishes them.

nodes.label: Retry only recomputable operations
nodes.rationale: Retry add-N. Do not retry an absolute assignment the user made against stale data — that is a 409.

nodes.label: SELECT FOR UPDATE inside a request
SELECT ... FOR UPDATE
nodes.rationale: Locks writers until commit. Meaningless without BEGIN because autocommit releases immediately. Readers still see the old MVCC version.

nodes.label: Do slow work then lock last
nodes.rationale: Eight requests × 100 ms: 863 ms with work inside the lock, 143 ms with lock taken only to write. Re-read the locked row before acting.

nodes.label: NOWAIT vs SKIP LOCKED
nodes.rationale: NOWAIT raises 55P03. SKIP LOCKED omits locked rows and is wrong for a point lookup. lock_timeout also raises 55P03 with a different message.

nodes.label: Lock rows in deterministic order
nodes.rationale: Opposite lock orders deadlock with 40P01. ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE. FOR UPDATE OF table restricts which join rows lock.

nodes.label: Shaping the response in SQL vs JavaScript
jsonb_agg is slower than grouping in JS
nodes.rationale: 5000 orders: jsonb_agg 284.8 ms vs JS group 90.7 ms. json_agg 131.2 ms. Server CPU parsing jsonb, and a larger payload.

nodes.label: jsonb_agg LEFT JOIN empty-children trap
nodes.rationale: Plain jsonb_agg yields [{sku:null}]. Need FILTER WHERE child.id IS NOT NULL plus coalesce to [].

nodes.label: numeric through jsonb becomes number
nodes.rationale: Column path keeps '11.00' string; jsonb path yields JS number 11. jsonb also reorders keys.

nodes.label: N+1 per-parent queries
nodes.rationale: 2986 ms extrapolated for 5000 parents. Still the one to avoid.

nodes.label: Who owns the response shape
nodes.rationale: SQL that emits the API payload couples schema to contract. Default to one join grouped in JS behind the mapper.

nodes.label: Per-test transaction rollback
nodes.rationale: 1.66 ms vs 42.50 ms truncate+reseed with 2000 seed rows. Parallel-safe because nothing commits.

nodes.label: Sequences are not transactional
nodes.rationale: Rolled-back insert still consumes an id. Never assert on a literal id.

nodes.label: Tests must inject the executor
nodes.rationale: Code using pool.query cannot see uncommitted fixtures. The harness enforces the executor contract.

nodes.label: BEGIN/COMMIT remapped to savepoints
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL has no nested transactions. Inner COMMIT ends the test transaction. Map to SAVEPOINT / RELEASE / ROLLBACK TO.

nodes.label: Committed test suite
nodes.rationale: Deferred constraints, LISTEN/NOTIFY, and two-connection lock tests need real COMMIT and TRUNCATE cleanup.

nodes.label: created_at and updated_at trigger or application
created_at DEFAULT now()
nodes.rationale: A DEFAULT covers every insert path. No trigger needed for created_at.

nodes.label: BEFORE UPDATE updated_at trigger
nodes.rationale: App-managed stamp stays stale on migrations and psql fixes. Trigger cost ~1.23–1.29× on the update. BEFORE so NEW is written in the same row version.

nodes.label: now() is the transaction timestamp
nodes.rationale: Every row in one transaction shares now(). clock_timestamp() moved 303 ms. That is why updated_at cannot be an optimistic version.

nodes.label: Unquoted identifiers fold to lower case
nodes.rationale: fullName becomes fullname. Quoted camelCase requires quoting forever or 42703.

nodes.label: Explicit row-to-domain mapper
nodes.rationale: One place, an allowlist by construction. Reverse sort params via a lookup map, not camelToSnake.

nodes.label: Generic snake-to-camel rewriter
nodes.rationale: Publishes every column. Fails to round-trip oauth2_token. 2.3× slower than an explicit mapper over 20000 rows.

nodes.label: Quoted SQL alias trap
nodes.rationale: AS "customerName" then ORDER BY customerName raises 42703 column customername. Fine for a fixed SELECT, awkward when dynamic.

nodes.label: Phase 9 CRUD patterns for a real API
Phase 9 gate
nodes.rationale: Move on when list/filter/sort is allowlisted and transactions use try/catch/finally release.

nodes.label: Executor contract
nodes.rationale: Every repository function takes db as first argument. Never import the pool. BoundPool and Client are interchangeable at the .query() surface.

nodes.label: pool.query vs held client
nodes.rationale: pool.query checks out, runs one statement, releases. Consecutive calls may be different sessions. A client shares a transaction.

nodes.label: Unreleased client leak
nodes.rationale: With max 2, the third call timed out after 1501 ms. pool.end() never resolves while a client is stranded. release() belongs in finally.

nodes.label: SET naming does not defeat HOT
nodes.rationale: COALESCE naming all columns: 1090 HOT; single-column SET: 1096. Only changing the indexed value dropped HOT to 0 of 2500.

nodes.label: toDomain row mapper
nodes.rationale: Maps a pg row to the API contract: String(id), snake_case to camelCase, Date to ISO, and only named fields. Lives in the repository next to the SELECT list.

nodes.label: bigint arrives as a String
nodes.rationale: pg will not silently lose precision past Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER. Treat ids as opaque strings; Number() is only safe under 2^53.

nodes.label: Missing SELECT row is not an error
nodes.rationale: A matching-nothing SELECT succeeds with rowCount 0 and rows []. rows[0] is undefined; normalise to null so JSON.stringify keeps the key.

nodes.label: rowCount versus rows.length
nodes.rationale: rowCount is rows affected; rows is what came back. They match for SELECT and diverge on writes without RETURNING. rowCount is null, not 0, for DDL/BEGIN/SET.

nodes.label: Mapper is an allowlist by construction
nodes.rationale: A column added later does not appear in responses until named here. SELECT * plus no mapper leaks password_hash the day it is added.

nodes.label: Keep mapper adjacent to the SELECT
nodes.rationale: The mapper can only produce what the query selected. Splitting them yields undefined fields instead of errors and makes SELECT * tempting. Alias for shape, mapper for contract.

nodes.label: toHttpError
nodes.rationale: Allowlists known codes to statuses; unrecognised errors are rethrown so they stay 500s. Returns constraint when present.

nodes.label: unique_violation 23505
nodes.rationale: Every unique index shares code 23505. Switch on err.constraint (named in DDL) to tell email_taken from username_taken.

nodes.label: 42xxx codes must stay 500s
nodes.rationale: 42703/42601/42P01 mean deployed SQL is wrong. Mapping them to 400 blames the client and hides a broken deploy.

nodes.label: Switch on constraint name not message
nodes.rationale: err.message is locale-dependent prose. constraint is populated only for 23xxx; column only for 23502. Name constraints explicitly in DDL.

nodes.label: err.detail leaks submitted values
nodes.rationale: 23505 detail echoes the key value; 23514 detail is the entire failing row. Log it; return a mapped machine-readable string.

nodes.label: Map SQLSTATE in middleware not the repository
nodes.rationale: The same 23505 is a 409 from signup and a retry signal inside an idempotent write. Only the caller knows which. Translate to domain errors in the repository only when it has intent the middleware cannot.

nodes.label: Validate in the app and still map 23505
nodes.rationale: SELECT then INSERT races. Only the unique index closes uniqueness. App checks are UX; the constraint is the correctness boundary.

nodes.label: Repository module per resource
nodes.rationale: Not a class or SQL abstraction — a module of plain functions whose first argument is whatever will run the query.

nodes.label: db as first parameter
nodes.rationale: The same function runs standalone on a Pool or inside a transaction on a Client without knowing which. Pool and Client are interchangeable at the query API.

nodes.label: One-pass WHERE fragment builder
nodes.rationale: Push value then fragment in one loop. Numbering follows push order, not request order. Test numeric/boolean filters with != null so 0 is not dropped.

nodes.label: Placeholder from params.length
nodes.rationale: $n is 1-based; params.length after the push is the number. A separate i++ drifts when a branch increments without pushing.

nodes.label: Bound parameter cannot become SQL
nodes.rationale: The statement is parsed before the value is bound. apple'; DROP TABLE … as $1 returned 0 rows and left the table intact.

nodes.label: = ANY($1::bigint[])
nodes.rationale: One array parameter keeps statement text constant across list lengths. Empty ANY('{}') matches nothing; generated IN () is a syntax error.

nodes.label: Omit WHERE when there are no filters
nodes.rationale: Emit the keyword only if where.length > 0. WHERE 1=1 works but leaves a permanently true predicate in every plan and log.

nodes.label: Escape ILIKE pattern metacharacters
nodes.rationale: A user % is not injection but forces a full scan. Escape \, %, _ then wrap; declare ESCAPE '\'. Leading-wildcard ILIKE needs pg_trgm.

nodes.label: listItems composes WHERE sort LIMIT
nodes.rationale: buildList supplies WHERE params; orderClause is vetted literal text; limit/offset are pushed last so numbering stays intact.

nodes.label: Sorting cannot use parameter machinery
nodes.rationale: ORDER BY needs an identifier. ORDER BY $1 silently sorts by a constant. Identifiers need an allowlist of authored SQL.

nodes.label: Hand-built predicates versus a query builder
nodes.rationale: Explicit SQL is pasteable into EXPLAIN. A builder removes boilerplate; every knex.raw/sql.raw reopens the hole this page closes.

nodes.label: Safe dynamic WHERE
nodes.rationale: Build predicate strings and the parameter array in the same loop so $n cannot drift. Separate construction is a runtime error or an injection hole.

nodes.label: ORDER BY $1 is a silent no-op
nodes.rationale: The parameter binds as a constant string, so every row sorts by the same value. Sorting by name and price returned byte-identical output and no error. ORDER BY 1 is a column index; $1 is not.

nodes.label: Concatenated ORDER BY drops the table
nodes.rationale: ?sort=name; DROP TABLE fs_items CASCADE; -- executed as two statements. The same payload as $1 left the table intact.

nodes.label: Simple query protocol stacked statements
nodes.rationale: query() with no parameter array uses the simple protocol, which permits multiple statements separated by ;. pg reported 2 statements executed.

nodes.label: The payload is not the problem — the position is
nodes.rationale: A value can always be a parameter and is then inert. An identifier can never be a parameter, so concatenation is the only way to vary it — which is why it needs an allowlist.

nodes.label: Allowlist is a lookup not validation
nodes.rationale: Use the request key into an object whose values are SQL you authored. The user's string never reaches the query. Unknown key is 400.

nodes.label: orderClause
nodes.rationale: Looks up SORTABLE[sortKey], ternaries direction, appends id ASC as a stable tiebreaker so pagination does not duplicate or drop rows.

nodes.label: Direction is a ternary never interpolated
nodes.rationale: dir === 'desc' ? 'DESC' : 'ASC' yields one of two literals. Interpolating ${dir} after a looks-like-direction check is the same class of bug.

nodes.label: Null-prototype or Map for user keys
nodes.rationale: A plain object resolves ?sort=constructor or __proto__ to something truthy that is not a column.

nodes.label: FILTERABLE column and operator map
nodes.rationale: Any field name (filter, groupBy, fields) has the same hole. Both column and operator come from the map; a client-supplied op is injection.

nodes.label: quote_ident and format('%I')
nodes.rationale: Quoting wraps a payload so ; and -- are characters in a name. It does not check existence, authorization, or sensibility. Use in addition to an allowlist.

nodes.label: format %I %L %s
nodes.rationale: %I quotes as an identifier, %L as a literal, %s is plain substitution. %s on user-influenced input is injection.

nodes.label: Allowlist is also the index contract
nodes.rationale: Sortable columns are a deliberate API decision and the set you have agreed to index. Reflecting information_schema re-adds the leak and exposes internal names.

nodes.label: Sort and filter allowlists
nodes.rationale: ?sort=price reintroduces SQL injection to a codebase that parameterizes everything else. Values can be parameters; column names and ASC/DESC cannot.

nodes.label: withTransaction wrapper
nodes.rationale: One place that knows connect/BEGIN/fn(client)/COMMIT/ROLLBACK/release. A handler cannot forget finally.

nodes.label: BEGIN is a statement on a connection
nodes.rationale: A transaction is a property of one connection. connect() before BEGIN; every statement inside uses that client.

nodes.label: pool.query('BEGIN') is not a transaction
nodes.rationale: Each pool.query is a separate checkout. Idle-pool tests reuse one pid and pass. With 8 concurrent inserts, 7 survived ROLLBACK. No error is raised.

nodes.label: try COMMIT catch ROLLBACK finally release
nodes.rationale: Swallowing the error turns a failed request into a silent 200. release() outside finally leaks a connection per failed request.

nodes.label: ROLLBACK catch must not replace the original error
nodes.rationale: If ROLLBACK throws (broken connection), wrap it and rethrow the original. Logs otherwise describe cleanup instead of the business failure.

nodes.label: 25P02 current transaction is aborted
nodes.rationale: After the first error the transaction is dead. SELECT 1 was refused after 22012. Accepts only ROLLBACK, COMMIT (as rollback), or ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT.

nodes.label: SAVEPOINT for an optional step
nodes.rationale: ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT rewinds to the savepoint, not the failing statement, and clears aborted state. Place it immediately before the group that belongs together.

nodes.label: idle in transaction
nodes.rationale: A 1240 ms external await held the xact open 1223 ms. Occupies a pool slot, holds locks, and pins xmin so VACUUM cannot clean tables the endpoint never touches.

nodes.label: idle_in_transaction_session_timeout
nodes.rationale: Kills sessions that sit idle in a transaction, turning an unbounded stall into a specific error. ALTER ROLE api_user SET … = '15s'.

nodes.label: Do external work outside the transaction
nodes.rationale: Charge first, then withTransaction. The new failure is money taken with no order — fix with idempotent charges and reconcile, not by putting the call back inside.

nodes.label: COMMIT on an aborted transaction reports success
nodes.rationale: It rolls back and does not raise. Catch-log-commit produces HTTP 200 with nothing written.

nodes.label: Savepoint-per-row overflows the 64-XID cache
nodes.rationale: Each writing subtransaction gets an XID. Thousands of savepoints push lookups to disk and degrade every backend. Batch instead of a savepoint per row.

nodes.label: Transactions in a request
nodes.rationale: Hold one connection for the request and give it back exactly once. Get the wrapper right and everything inside composes.

nodes.label: OFFSET versus keyset at depth
nodes.rationale: OFFSET 499980 produced 500000 rows and 501918 buffers to return 20 (295.87 ms). Keyset sought with Index Cond, 23 buffers, 1.23 ms.

nodes.label: Row-constructor tuple comparison
nodes.rationale: (created_at, id) < ($1, $2) is one lexicographic comparison, the same rule ORDER BY uses, and becomes a single B-tree seek.

nodes.label: Index Cond versus Filter
nodes.rationale: Index Cond chooses where the scan starts and stops. Filter is applied after rows are produced. A Filter on a large table is usually why a query is slow despite using the index.

nodes.label: Expanded OR comparison is 160× slower
nodes.rationale: a < $1 OR (a = $1 AND b < $2) looks equivalent and returned the same rows, but became a Filter that discarded 250001 rows (158.12 ms vs 0.99 ms).

nodes.label: Index must match ORDER BY column order
nodes.rationale: (created_at DESC, id DESC) matches the sort. A B-tree can be read backwards, so both-ASC also serves. (id, created_at) is useless for ORDER BY created_at, id.

nodes.label: ORDER BY must be total
nodes.rationale: created_at alone tied 100 rows per timestamp. Without unique id, the same row can appear on two pages. WHERE must use the same columns in the same order.

nodes.label: base64url cursor encoding
nodes.rationale: JSON of [ISO timestamp, String(id)] as base64url. Preserve full precision; bigint id as string. Base64 is not security — sign if unforgeable.

nodes.label: Fetch limit + 1 for hasMore
nodes.rationale: The extra row is whether another page exists. Costs one row instead of count(*). nextCursor is null at the end.

nodes.label: Tuple form cannot express mixed directions
nodes.rationale: (a,b) < (x,y) means DESC on both. Against ORDER BY a DESC, b ASC it returns a plausible wrong page. Write the comparison out and index (a DESC, b ASC), or avoid mixed directions.

nodes.label: Nullable sort column silently truncates the walk
nodes.rationale: Comparisons against NULL are never true. Page 1 includes nulls (no WHERE); later pages drop them. Measured 250000 of 500000 excluded. NULLS LAST does not fix the predicate. Prefer NOT NULL.

nodes.label: OFFSET is still right for shallow page-number UIs
nodes.rationale: At 50 pages OFFSET was 0.9× (slightly faster). At 500 pages keyset was 6.4× faster. Keyset for feeds, APIs, exports, crawlers; OFFSET for admin tables with page numbers.

nodes.label: Order by an immutable key
nodes.rationale: Keyset is stable against inserts elsewhere. A row whose sort key changes (updated_at) can be seen twice or missed. Prefer created_at or the primary key.

nodes.label: Keyset (cursor) pagination
nodes.rationale: Remember the last row and ask for what comes after it. The query starts at the right place in the index rather than walking to it.

nodes.label: 216 of 228 pages are template stamps
nodes.rationale: 94.7% carry Hold the model in your head before memorizing syntax. How it works and the first interview answer reprint the one-liner. Average 77 lines versus Node 198–267.

nodes.label: Twelve genuinely hand-written pages
nodes.rationale: Phase 0 architecture pages plus phase-10-indexes/18-fk-indexes.md. 05-wal.md is the model. vs-other-databases was a stamp then rewritten 2026-08-13.

nodes.label: False Verified stamps on 210 pages
nodes.rationale: 210 pages claim Verified 2026-08 on PostgreSQL 18.4 attached to code that cannot have produced the topic. Strip 210→12 before any rewrite.

nodes.label: Five stamped page variants
nodes.rationale: psql/ops 83, SQL 49, Node 48, DDL 19, Types 16 — identified by Why it matters. Five shared code blocks; 168 pages share the same two gotchas.

nodes.label: Critical Phase 8–9 topics were stamps
nodes.rationale: DDL-from-Node showed INSERT. Soft delete never mentioned deleted_at. list/WHERE/allowlists were byte-identical and had no predicate-building code.

nodes.label: Rewrite against the Node corpus standard
nodes.rationale: Keep syllabus and phase indexes. Sequence Phase 8 → 9 → 3 → 4. Do not review stamps one at a time. progress.js must stop counting stamps as finished.

nodes.label: Proposed PostgreSQL syllabus (2026-08-11)
nodes.rationale: Row-level inventory for review, excluded from the build until approved. Target PostgreSQL 18.4 from Node 24 with pg. No explanation pages until approval.

nodes.label: Every page carries SQL and Node pg
nodes.rationale: Runnable SQL, the pg call with $1 placeholders, actual output, and the Node-side failure (SQLSTATE, error.code, constraint). A psql-only page is incomplete.

nodes.label: Node Phase 6 versus PG Part 3 boundary
nodes.rationale: Pool sizing, transaction propagation, N+1, repository rationale, ORM stay in Node 6. Writing SQL through the driver, DDL/seeding, CRUD patterns are PG Part 3. Needs explicit sign-off.

nodes.label: 228 topics in 14 phases
nodes.rationale: 60 Master (26%), 124 Understand, 35 Know, 9 When Needed. Master-only path: schema, every CRUD query, drive from Node, read EXPLAIN.

nodes.label: Part 1 Foundations (proposed)
nodes.rationale: Phases 0–3, 63 topics, 19 Master. Architecture, psql mastered, types, DDL. Not Node-specific; every page still shows the pg counterpart.

nodes.label: Part 2 SQL (proposed)
nodes.rationale: Phases 4–6, 49 topics, 14 Master. CRUD/DML, joins, aggregation, windows, CTEs. Tuple comparison is the keyset primitive.

nodes.label: Part 3 Node + raw pg (proposed)
nodes.rationale: Phases 7–9, 48 topics, 14 Master. Raw-SQL-first. Overlap with Node Phase 6 is recap-plus-link, never a second full treatment.

nodes.label: Phase 9 CRUD patterns for a real API
nodes.rationale: 18 topics: repository, list, safe dynamic WHERE, allowlists, request transactions, keyset, optimistic concurrency. Where injection re-enters a parameterized codebase.

nodes.label: Part 4 Performance and production (proposed)
nodes.rationale: Phases 10–13, 68 topics, 13 Master. Indexes/planner, MVCC, advanced features, security and ops. Most defensible part to defer.

nodes.label: Part 1 Foundations (live syllabus)
nodes.rationale: Phases 0–3, 65 topics, 20 Master. Adds Modelling money (Master) and Multi-tenancy as a decision. Phase 0–3 explanation pages already written.

nodes.label: Modelling money
nodes.rationale: numeric vs integer cents vs float, rounding, and the ledger shape. Live-syllabus addition versus the proposed 63-topic Foundations part.

nodes.label: Multi-tenancy as a decision
nodes.rationale: Shared schema with tenant_id vs schema-per-tenant vs database-per-tenant, and what each costs to operate.

nodes.label: RETURNING
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL's way to get a generated id back without a second query.

nodes.label: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL upsert via DO NOTHING / DO UPDATE / EXCLUDED instead of extra round trips.

nodes.label: Parameterized queries
nodes.rationale: Never string-build values; driver $1 placeholders are the safety mechanism.

nodes.label: Logical query processing order
nodes.rationale: FROM → WHERE → GROUP BY → HAVING → SELECT → ORDER BY → LIMIT; a SELECT alias therefore fails in WHERE.

nodes.label: LEFT JOIN + WHERE bug
nodes.rationale: Filtering the right-hand table in WHERE turns a LEFT JOIN back into an inner join.

nodes.label: NOT IN NULL trap
nodes.rationale: One of two SQL mistakes most likely to ship silently, alongside the LEFT JOIN + WHERE bug.

nodes.label: jsonb_agg
nodes.rationale: One query can return a fully shaped API response instead of Node stitching result sets.

nodes.label: CTEs (WITH)
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL 12+ inlines CTEs unless MATERIALIZED is specified.

nodes.label: Part 3 — Node + raw pg
nodes.rationale: Raw-SQL-first on purpose; no ORM writes the queries.

nodes.label: Phase 8 — Schema and data from Node
Phase 9 — CRUD patterns for a real API
pool.query() with $1 placeholders
nodes.rationale: The safe path every time, including IN lists via = ANY($1).

nodes.label: pg type parsing
nodes.rationale: bigint and numeric arrive as strings; finding that out in production is a bad day.

nodes.label: Migrations from Node
nodes.rationale: Forward-only, one file per change, applied inside a transaction, recorded in a tracking table.

nodes.label: Repository module per resource
nodes.rationale: Plain functions taking a client and returning rows; layering rationale lives in Node Phase 6.

nodes.label: Safe dynamic WHERE
nodes.rationale: Build predicates and a parameter array together; identifiers cannot be parameterized so sort/filter need allowlists.

nodes.label: Phase 10 — Indexes and the query planner
EXPLAIN vs EXPLAIN ANALYZE
nodes.rationale: ANALYZE actually runs the query.

nodes.label: Why an index is not being used
nodes.rationale: Type mismatch, a function wrapping the column, low selectivity, or stale statistics.

nodes.label: Lost update
nodes.rationale: Promoted to Master because every application hits the read-modify-write bug.

nodes.label: MVCC
nodes.rationale: Snapshots and row versions; readers never block writers.

nodes.label: When a column beats JSON
nodes.rationale: The schema-versus-document decision is made early and lived with for years.

nodes.label: pg_dump and pg_restore
nodes.rationale: Restore once to verify; backups are Master-tier.

nodes.label: Application role should not own the schema
React computes a description of the UI
nodes.rationale: A renderer applies the description. This split is why react and react-dom are separate, why Server Components can exist, why keys matter, and why mutation never works.

nodes.label: ViewTransition (experimental only)
nodes.rationale: Still not in the stable 19.2.8 package despite blog posts and talks; pages must never teach it as shippable.

nodes.label: Part 3 — Concurrent React and the server
React reading order
nodes.rationale: Do not skip Phase 3; do not start effects before the render cycle is solid; do not start RSC before Suspense.

nodes.label: React page verification policy
nodes.rationale: Phases 0–1 are sandbox-proven; from Phase 2 onward pages are validated against react.dev and carry no reconstructed console blocks.

nodes.label: Phase 0 load-bearing pages
nodes.rationale: Pages 01, 03, 04 and 07 are the four to read if you only read four.

nodes.label: Declarative UI model
nodes.rationale: You describe what the UI is for a given value and never write transitions; cost is a diff on every update and losing direct DOM control.

nodes.label: react package
nodes.rationale: Knows components, elements, state and hooks; document.createElement does not occur in the package.

nodes.label: react / react-dom version-match rule
nodes.rationale: The packages share private internals that are not a stable API; mismatch is undefined behaviour.

nodes.label: React element
nodes.rationale: A frozen plain object describing desired UI. Creating one runs nothing.

nodes.label: $$typeof / react.transitional.element
nodes.rationale: A symbol so JSON.parse cannot inject a fake element — XSS mitigation.

nodes.label: key is not a prop
nodes.rationale: key is the third jsx() argument; React 19 leaves a non-enumerable getter that warns and returns undefined.

nodes.label: Render phase
nodes.rationale: React calls component functions; the result may be repeated or discarded. The DOM still shows the previous UI.

nodes.label: Commit phase
nodes.rationale: Applies DOM operations then runs refs and effects. Cannot be thrown away; children commit before parents.

nodes.label: Render must be pure
nodes.rationale: Render can run repeatedly and be discarded, so observable work in the body is a bug.

nodes.label: useLayoutEffect
nodes.rationale: Runs after DOM mutation but before paint; blocks painting. Use only to avoid flicker.

nodes.label: Reconciliation two rules
nodes.rationale: Different types produce different trees; key identifies a child across renders. Comparison unit is (position, type, key).

nodes.label: Type change remounts the subtree
nodes.rationale: Changing a parent div to span, wrapping in a new depth, or defining a component inside another all destroy state.

nodes.label: Fiber
nodes.rationale: Replaces the call stack with a linked list React owns so rendering can pause, resume, or be abandoned.

nodes.label: Fiber double buffering
nodes.rationale: current and work-in-progress trees point at each other through alternate; the DOM pointer is not retargeted each render.

nodes.label: Hook state lives on the fiber
nodes.rationale: A function component has no instance; hooks are a linked list keyed by call order.

nodes.label: hydrateRoot
nodes.rationale: Expects server-rendered HTML and attaches handlers; argument order is container first, unlike createRoot().render.

nodes.label: One root per container
nodes.rationale: A second createRoot on the same element produces NotFoundError: Node.removeChild on unmount.

nodes.label: StrictMode
nodes.rationale: Development-only detector: double-invokes components and double-mounts effects so impurity fails immediately.

nodes.label: Cleanup must fully undo setup
