nodes.rationale: A didInit ref silences the symptom; a re-runnable effect with abort in cleanup is the real fix.

nodes.label: canary channel
nodes.rationale: Every passing commit, intended for frameworks that pin an exact build; applications should install latest.

nodes.label: use
nodes.rationale: The only React API allowed inside a condition; reads a promise or a context during render.

nodes.label: Activity
nodes.rationale: Hide a subtree, keep its state, unmount its effects.

nodes.label: useEffectEvent
nodes.rationale: Read latest props/state inside an effect without adding them as dependencies.

nodes.label: ref is an ordinary prop
nodes.rationale: forwardRef is no longer needed for function components in React 19.

nodes.label: Vite SPA starter
nodes.rationale: Default for this bible's MERN/PERN stack: Express already owns the API, so a second React server is extra deployment cost.

nodes.label: Framework vs Vite SPA
nodes.rationale: Choose a framework when pages must be indexable, first paint matters, or you specifically want Server Components.

nodes.label: React Compiler
nodes.rationale: Build-step automatic memoization via a per-fiber cache array; stable at babel-plugin-react-compiler 1.0.0.

nodes.label: Compiler is not a linter
nodes.rationale: It compiled a component that mutates a prop; eslint-plugin-react-hooks owns Rules of React validation.

nodes.label: Profiler API
nodes.rationale: actualDuration vs baseDuration is the memoization signal; onRender is compiled out of production.

nodes.label: Renderer host config
nodes.rationale: react never learns what a node is; a renderer supplies createInstance, appendChild, commitUpdate and about thirty more.

nodes.label: React Native
nodes.rationale: Learn once, write anywhere — not write once, run anywhere. Hooks transfer; host elements and styling do not.

nodes.label: react-test-renderer
nodes.rationale: Still published in lockstep but deprecated in React 19 docs; React Testing Library is the replacement.

nodes.label: Re-render + diff vs signals
nodes.rationale: React's unit of update is the component; signals update the exact binding. Stale closures and dependency arrays follow from React's choice.

nodes.label: jsx vs jsxs
nodes.rationale: jsxs means children were written literally so React skips the key check; that is why a hand-written sibling list never asks for keys.

nodes.label: React.createElement
nodes.rationale: Still exported in 19.2.8; the automatic runtime is a compiler change, not an API removal.

nodes.label: JSX falsy render rules
nodes.rationale: null, undefined, true and false render nothing; 0 and NaN stringify. That is why {items.length && <X/>} leaves a 0 on screen.

nodes.label: Renderable child types
nodes.rationale: React renders strings, numbers, bigints, elements, and iterables of those (arrays, Set, Map, generators).

nodes.label: Silent no-render values
nodes.rationale: null, undefined, true, false, symbols and functions render nothing. Functions warn in development only.

nodes.label: Objects are not valid as a React child
nodes.rationale: Plain objects and Date throw. Production is Minified React error #31 with args[] naming the shape.

nodes.label: Iterables as children
nodes.rationale: Set renders. Map yields key/value pairs and is warned. A generator is consumed by render, so StrictMode blanks it on the second pass.

nodes.label: Promise child suspends
nodes.rationale: React 19 unwraps a promise only under Suspense. Without a boundary the root withholds its commit — no DOM, no error.

nodes.label: Returning undefined throws
nodes.rationale: Nothing was returned from render. Return null to render nothing on purpose. Missing return or JSX after return is the usual cause.

nodes.label: Four host-prop outcomes
nodes.rationale: A JSX prop on a host element is renamed, passed through, dropped, or — in React 19 — class/for accepted with a warning.

nodes.label: className and htmlFor
nodes.rationale: class and for are reserved words. Raw class/for also reach the DOM since React 16, with a development warning.

nodes.label: onclick is silently dropped
nodes.rationale: Unknown on* is parsed as an event and discarded. Production prints nothing. Highest-cost typo on the page.

nodes.label: Boolean host attributes
nodes.rationale: Known booleans: true emits the empty attribute, false removes it. disabled="false" is truthy. aria-* and data-* stringify.

nodes.label: null/undefined remove attributes
nodes.rationale: Idiomatic conditional omit: href={isExternal ? url : undefined}.

nodes.label: Unknown host props
nodes.rationale: String/number: lowercased with a warning. Boolean: dropped. on*: dropped as unknown event.

nodes.label: style must be an object
nodes.rationale: A string throws. The one attribute where pasted HTML fails loudly.

nodes.label: Prop vs attribute
nodes.rationale: A prop is a JSX object key. An attribute is what lands in the DOM. Host elements are mapped; custom components are not.

nodes.label: Capitalization decides host vs component
nodes.rationale: Lowercase compiles to a string (host). Uppercase compiles to the identifier. Hyphen is a custom element. Any member expression is a component.

nodes.label: Lowercase component is a silent host element
nodes.rationale: function button() in scope plus <button/> never calls it. No error in either build.

nodes.label: Element type is invalid: undefined
nodes.rationale: Capitalized identifier is undefined — default vs named import. Production: Minified React error #130.

nodes.label: Do not call components as functions
nodes.rationale: Header() has no fiber: hooks belong to the caller, no independent state or bail-out.

nodes.label: The && zero trap
nodes.rationale: && returns the falsy left operand. 0, NaN, -0 and 0n render as text. Put a boolean on the left.

nodes.label: Four conditional forms
nodes.rationale: && for render-or-nothing; ternary for either/or; early return null for the whole component; lookup object for three-plus keyed states.

nodes.label: Conditionals decide identity
nodes.rationale: Same type at the same depth keeps the instance. Different depth remounts. && / ternary-to-null unmount when false.

nodes.label: Early return after every hook
nodes.rationale: A return above a hook changes hook count between renders and throws.

nodes.label: Reset a subtree with key
nodes.rationale: Do not fake a remount with a conditional. <ProfileForm key={userId} /> is the deliberate reset.

nodes.label: A key is an identity, not an index
nodes.rationale: Answers which sibling from last render this is. Scoped to siblings, not a prop, stringified, compared before position.

nodes.label: Index keys rewrite text in place
nodes.rationale: Measured: index keys do not remount. React keeps DOM nodes and rewrites contents, so uncontrolled input state stays with the slot.

nodes.label: Stable keys move DOM nodes
nodes.rationale: key={item.id} moves real nodes and rewrites no text. Same three Row instances either way.

nodes.label: Key on the map callback's outermost child
nodes.rationale: A key on an inner element is silent and useless. Shorthand <> cannot take a key — syntax error; use Fragment.

nodes.label: Missing-key warning is deduplicated
nodes.rationale: The first offending list with a given parent tag warns; later ones stay silent even in other components. Absence proves nothing.

nodes.label: Duplicate keys may omit children
nodes.rationale: React's own warning: children may be duplicated and/or omitted. A missing row with no error is usually this.

nodes.label: Fragment groups without a DOM node
nodes.rationale: A component returns one element; a fragment lets that element be several siblings with no extra box for CSS to match.

nodes.label: Shorthand fragment accepts no attributes
nodes.rationale: <> cannot take key — syntax error. Keyed dt/dd lists need <Fragment key={…}>.

nodes.label: Wrapper div breaks HTML nesting and flex
nodes.rationale: div inside tr is invalid HTML and a hydration error. A wrapper inside flex/grid becomes the item; intended children are no longer laid out.

nodes.label: Fragment allows only key and children
nodes.rationale: No DOM node, so className or onClick warn. Need a real element to style or listen.

nodes.label: Fragment occupies a React-tree position
nodes.rationale: Transparent to depth while it stays a fragment. Swapping a fragment for a div is a type change and destroys subtree state.

nodes.label: children is an ordinary prop
nodes.rationale: Nesting is syntax for setting it. Nesting wins over an explicit children attribute because JSX writes children last.

nodes.label: jsx vs jsxs decides children shape
nodes.rationale: One child is the element itself (jsx); two or more is an array (jsxs). props.children.map throws on a single child.

nodes.label: Children.toArray
nodes.rationale: Flattens nested arrays, drops null/undefined/booleans, keeps strings and numbers, rewrites keys with a path prefix (.$k1, .2:$k2).

nodes.label: A fragment child counts as one
nodes.rationale: Children.count says 1 while markup has two elements. Layouts that branch on children.length fail when the caller wraps in a fragment.

nodes.label: Four ways to pass content
nodes.rationale: Default slot (children); named element props; children as a function (render prop); a slot-object of per-item functions.

nodes.label: Children helpers discouraged in new code
nodes.rationale: React docs prefer composition. Helpers remain correct when you must inspect an unknown children set.

nodes.label: Spread precedence is later keys win
nodes.rationale: {...props} type="text" forces the type. type="text" {...props} is an overridable default.

nodes.label: Rest spread leaks component props to the DOM
nodes.rationale: Unknown on* and unknown booleans are dropped; other unknowns become attributes. Destructure non-DOM props out first.

nodes.label: key inside a spread is warned
nodes.rationale: key compiles to a separate argument, so a spread key is pulled out at runtime. Pass key directly.

nodes.label: Spreading onto a component has no DOM rules
nodes.rationale: Every key arrives untouched. Unknown-attribute warnings fire only when something later spreads onto a host element.

nodes.label: Spread the set, not a domain object
nodes.rationale: Right for DOM passthrough and framework props objects. {...user} silently changes the component when the object gains a field.

nodes.label: style is a camelCase object with automatic px
nodes.rationale: Numbers get px except the unitless list. A unitless string such as fontSize: '12' is invalid CSS and is dropped silently.

nodes.label: Unitless style properties
nodes.rationale: lineHeight, zIndex, opacity, flex, flexGrow, fontWeight, order, columnCount, gridRow, aspectRatio, scale, tabSize — ratios, counts, indexes.

nodes.label: CSS custom properties in style
nodes.rationale: {'--gap': 8} is --gap: 8 with no px. Cleanest way to pass a runtime value into a stylesheet.

nodes.label: Hyphenated style keys still apply
nodes.rationale: React warns and applies. A camelCase typo is silent. null/undefined/false remove a declaration.

nodes.label: Inline style cannot express pseudos or queries
nodes.rationale: One declaration block: no :hover, ::before, @media, @supports, keyframes, or cascade. Use for JS-known runtime values only.

nodes.label: React escapes text and attributes by default
nodes.rationale: Ordinary XSS vectors are closed unless you opt in. The name and nested __html key are deliberate speed bumps.

nodes.label: React 19 rewrites javascript: URLs
nodes.rationale: Rewritten to throw on click, but the href still appears in markup — scanners flag a finding that is already mitigated.

nodes.label: Must be {__html: ...} and exclusive of children
nodes.rationale: Wrong shape throws #61. children plus innerHTML throws #60. Nested key prevents an accidental server object from matching.

nodes.label: script tags do not run; img onerror does
nodes.rationale: innerHTML never executes script elements. Measured: img onerror and iframe srcdoc ran. Filtering <script> is not a sanitizer.

nodes.label: Sanitize with a real library or do not inject
nodes.rationale: Safe only if HTML is entirely yours, or DOMPurify (allowlist attributes, not just tags) as close to render as possible.

nodes.label: JSX whitespace rules
nodes.rationale: Newline-adjacent whitespace is stripped at compile time. Newline between elements is removed; between words becomes one space. Within a line, spaces are kept.

nodes.label: Disappearing space between elements
nodes.rationale: Breaking Hello world across lines deletes the space. {' '} is an expression and survives Prettier.

nodes.label: {' '} vs
nodes.rationale: U+0020 collapses and may break. U+00A0 does neither. Entities work in JSX text, not inside {}.

nodes.label: Strings in braces are literal
nodes.rationale: Compile-time whitespace rules apply only to JSX text. Template literals keep newlines; CSS still has to not collapse them.

nodes.label: Classic vs automatic JSX runtime
nodes.rationale: Classic emits React.createElement and needs React in scope, children as rest args, key in props. Automatic emits jsx/jsxs from react/jsx-runtime.

nodes.label: ReferenceError: React is not defined
nodes.rationale: Signature of the classic transform without an import. A build-config problem — nested .babelrc, leftover @jsx pragma, test runner mismatch.

nodes.label: @jsxImportSource
nodes.rationale: Changes which package the automatic runtime is imported from — preact or a CSS-in-JS jsx factory. Compiler option preferred over per-file pragma.

nodes.label: createElement is not deprecated
nodes.rationale: Still exported in 19.2.8 and correct without a build step. createFactory, ReactDOM.render, hydrate and unmountComponentAtNode were removed.

nodes.label: TypeScript jsx: preserve
nodes.rationale: Leave JSX for Babel/SWC/the bundler. A file compiled that way and never passed downstream ships literal JSX.

nodes.label: Phase 1 — JSX and what a component returns
Load-bearing pages 01, 02, 04, 07
nodes.rationale: JSX-as-a-call, embedding expressions, attributes vs props, and lists/keys are the four to read if you read only four.

nodes.label: sandbox/react-p1
nodes.rationale: Every console block comes from a named script run on Node 24.19.0 / Firefox 153.0. Scratch stays under sandbox/react-p1/tmp/.

nodes.label: Two folklore contradictions
nodes.rationale: Index keys do not remount; the missing-key warning is suppressed after the first offending parent tag.

nodes.label: Phase 1 gate
nodes.rationale: Hand-compile JSX including key; say what a swapped list does with index vs stable keys; explain {items.length && <List/>}.

nodes.label: Controlled vs uncontrolled
nodes.rationale: Controlled: React state is the value (value + onChange). Uncontrolled: the DOM owns it (defaultValue). Pick once per field for its lifetime.

nodes.label: value without onChange is read-only
nodes.rationale: Warns unless readOnly. value={null} is controlled-with-nothing; use '' to clear and undefined to go uncontrolled.

nodes.label: value attribute vs value property
nodes.rationale: The attribute stays at the initial value; the property holds what the user typed. Assert on element.value, not markup.

nodes.label: React onChange is the DOM input event
nodes.rationale: Fires every keystroke with the value after the stroke. Native change afterwards fires nothing. No built-in 'finished' event — use onBlur or debounce.

nodes.label: Store the raw string, convert at the edge
nodes.rationale: Number() on each keystroke destroys intermediate states (1., -, 1.0) and jumps the caret. Initialise to '' / false / [], never undefined.

nodes.label: Uncontrolled-to-controlled warning
nodes.rationale: value was undefined then defined — usually a fetch. Fix with ?? '' or do not render the form until data exists.

nodes.label: File inputs are always uncontrolled
nodes.rationale: The picker sets the value; JS cannot assign it. Read via ref or FormData.

nodes.label: select takes value, not option selected
nodes.rationale: selected on option is stripped and warned. multiple takes an array; read selectedOptions, not e.target.value.

nodes.label: textarea takes value, not children
nodes.rationale: Children warn; children plus defaultValue throws. Rendered markup still puts text between the tags.

nodes.label: File input FileList and clear
nodes.rationale: e.target.files is a FileList. Clear with node.value = ''. Same file twice does not fire onChange unless reset.

nodes.label: Read a form with FormData
nodes.rationale: name is the key; e.currentTarget is the form; preventDefault stops navigation. Unchecked checkboxes are absent; repeated names need getAll.

nodes.label: Start uncontrolled, upgrade fields that need it
nodes.rationale: Most forms need per-keystroke state for none of their fields. Controlled when you validate as they type or fields constrain each other.

nodes.label: Form elements are where the DOM already holds state
nodes.rationale: React either takes that state over or leaves it alone. Every warning in the topic exists because the two got mixed.

nodes.label: Props are immutable by contract, not enforcement
nodes.rationale: React does not freeze props or the objects they reference. Each render builds a fresh props object; a mutation is discarded on the next parent render.

nodes.label: Mutating a prop appears to work
nodes.rationale: Breaks later: parent refresh drops the field, a sibling reads undefined, memo skips the mutating render, StrictMode doubles, concurrent abandon leaves the write.

nodes.label: One-way data flow
nodes.rationale: Props down, events up. Only the owner can change a value, so debugging walks up to the useState. Mutation destroys that guarantee.

nodes.label: Mutating array methods on props
nodes.rationale: sort, reverse, splice, push and friends mutate in place. sort is the trap because it reads like a query. Use toSorted / a copy.

nodes.label: Reassigning a destructured prop is legal
nodes.rationale: Changes only a local binding. The violation is a write through the prop to the object it points at.

nodes.label: react.dev Passing Props to a Component
defaultProps removed for function components
nodes.rationale: Replaced by ES6 default parameters. Class components keep defaultProps — there is no ES6 equivalent for a class's props.

nodes.label: propTypes is silently ignored in React 19
nodes.rationale: No error, no warning. The migration hazard is the silence. TypeScript is the documented replacement.

nodes.label: Default parameters fire only on undefined
nodes.rationale: null, 0, '' and false suppress the default. For props that can be null, use ?? in the body.

nodes.label: ?? rather than || for fallbacks
nodes.rationale: || swallows every falsy value, so 0 disappears. Almost every 'the zero disappeared' bug is this.

nodes.label: Rest destructuring for wrappers
nodes.rationale: Name consumed props so they stay out of ...rest; the rest forwards onClick, disabled, aria-* to the host.

nodes.label: Wrapper children pattern
nodes.rationale: Adds markup or behaviour around arbitrary content and does not inspect children. Cheapest performance tool: the caller's element object is unchanged.

nodes.label: Layout with named element props
nodes.rationale: Name the region, keep primary content in children, make slots optional. Do not slice children positionally.

nodes.label: Compound components via context
nodes.rationale: Parent provides shared state; caller arranges parts freely. Context beats cloneElement because it ignores intervening structure.

nodes.label: Function as children
nodes.rationale: A render prop named children. Hooks usually win; this survives when the component controls placement or values are per-item.

nodes.label: Hooks largely replaced function-as-children
nodes.rationale: No extra tree node, no wrapper hell, values usable anywhere, composable with other hooks.

nodes.label: ref is an ordinary prop in React 19
nodes.rationale: JSX used to strip ref. Now it travels through spreads, wrappers and HOCs. key is still a third argument.

nodes.label: forwardRef is deprecated, not removed
nodes.rationale: Still works in 19. Still required in libraries that support React 18. New app code on 19 should pass ref as a prop.

nodes.label: Ref cleanup functions
nodes.rationale: A callback may return a detach cleanup. Implicit arrow returns now look like cleanups — use braces.

nodes.label: String refs removed
nodes.rationale: ref="input" with this.refs.input no longer works. Class-only; codemod react/19/replace-string-ref.

nodes.label: findDOMNode removed
nodes.rationale: Slow, fragile, first-child only, broke abstraction. Replacement is an ordinary ref on the element you want.

nodes.label: React v19 blog — ref as a prop
Split by responsibility, not length
nodes.rationale: Thinking in React: one concern, less granular than CSS classes. A 200-line one-thing component is fine.

nodes.label: Five reasons that justify a split
nodes.rationale: Second caller; owns state nothing above needs; different update frequency; different data source; server/client boundary.

nodes.label: When splitting hurts
nodes.rationale: Hides flow, manufactures a props contract for local variables, invites speculative variants. More than about five local-variable props is a smell.

nodes.label: Colocation
nodes.rationale: Keep a component next to its only caller. Location communicates scope; deleting a feature deletes its parts. Promote on a second caller.

nodes.label: Naming as a design check
nodes.rationale: And in the name is two components. Wrapper/Inner often means no responsibility. Position names go stale when the design moves.

nodes.label: createPortal
nodes.rationale: createPortal(children, domNode, key?). Called in the return position. The node must already exist. Not a component or a hook.

nodes.label: Portal changes DOM placement only
nodes.rationale: Events, context, state, error boundaries, Suspense and unmount follow the React tree, not the DOM tree.

nodes.label: Portals escape overflow and stacking contexts
nodes.rationale: overflow:hidden clips; transform/filter/opacity create stacking contexts z-index cannot cross; position:fixed inside a transform is relative to the ancestor.

nodes.label: dialog showModal and the top layer
nodes.rationale: Native top layer escapes stacking without moving the node, and brings focus trap, Escape and inertness.

nodes.label: Portal accessibility obligation
nodes.rationale: React provides none. Focus in, trap, restore, Escape, inert background. react.dev flags this as a pitfall and points at WAI-ARIA.

nodes.label: React events vs native events on portals
nodes.rationale: React bubbling follows the React tree; document click-outside sees the portal at body. Compare against the portal node or the dropdown closes as it opens.

nodes.label: createPortal is client-only
nodes.rationale: Targets a real DOM node. Render after mount, or use a framework portal-aware component.

nodes.label: Render prop
nodes.rationale: A function prop a component calls to decide what to render. The owner keeps state and behaviour; the caller keeps markup. The prop need not be named render — children is the same pattern.

nodes.label: Function-as-children
nodes.rationale: Same inversion as a render prop with children as the function, which JSX can nest inside the element.

nodes.label: Wrapper hell
nodes.rationale: Composing several render-prop components nests JSX and closures until the code is unreadable. Custom hooks were introduced to solve this.

nodes.label: Hooks replaced render props
nodes.rationale: Hooks share logic without extra tree nodes, make values usable anywhere in the component, and compose linearly instead of nesting.

nodes.label: When render props still win
nodes.rationale: Hooks cannot render. Render props remain right when the component controls placement, values are per-item, or rendering must run inside a boundary it owns.

nodes.label: Inline render prop defeats memoization
nodes.rationale: An inline arrow is a new function each render, so PureComponent or memo never skips. Fix with useCallback only if the child is actually memoized.

nodes.label: Higher-order component
nodes.rationale: A function that takes a component and returns a new one by wrapping, not mutating. Apply at module level, once.

nodes.label: Never apply a HOC during render
nodes.rationale: A new enhanced type each render makes React unmount and remount the subtree, losing all state. Same nesting-rule bug.

nodes.label: HOC does not copy static methods
nodes.rationale: The wrapper is a different function object. Copy statics or use hoist-non-react-statics. Mostly historical now.

nodes.label: HOC refs and React 19
nodes.rationale: Before 19, ref was not a prop so spreads dropped it. Function-component HOCs that spread props now forward ref automatically. Class instance refs and React 18 still need forwardRef.

nodes.label: HOC prop collisions are silent
nodes.rationale: Injected names collide by spread order with no warning. Wrapper stacks hide where a prop came from.

nodes.label: HOC wraps around a component
nodes.rationale: A hook cannot wrap from the outside. memo, forwardRef, error boundaries, instrumentation and injected Suspense stay HOC-shaped.

nodes.label: HOC displayName convention
nodes.rationale: Set displayName from the wrapped component or DevTools shows anonymous wrappers.

nodes.label: Component PureComponent shouldComponentUpdate
nodes.rationale: Always render, shallow skip, or custom comparison. Function equivalents are plain, memo, and memo with a compare function.

nodes.label: Shallow comparison Object.is
nodes.rationale: New objects, arrays or inline functions each render make the check always fail. You pay the comparison and skip nothing.

nodes.label: PureComponent and mutation are mutually exclusive
nodes.rationale: Mutating then setState of the same reference drops the update silently. Wrong UI, not slow UI.

nodes.label: Memoization does not stop context updates
Skipping a render is a hint not a contract
nodes.rationale: React may re-render anyway. Returning false does not stop children when their own state changes. Memoization is never a correctness mechanism.

nodes.label: Never deep-compare in shouldComponentUpdate
nodes.rationale: JSON.stringify makes cost proportional to data size and breaks on undefined, functions, Map, Set, cycles and key order.

nodes.label: memo compares props only
nodes.rationale: Unlike PureComponent, memo does not compare state because useState already bails out on the same value.

nodes.label: cloneElement
nodes.rationale: Returns a new element with merged props. Uncommon and fragile, not deprecated. Only reaches direct children and hides data flow.

nodes.label: Children namespace
nodes.rationale: Traverses the opaque children structure. Fragments are not traversed; arrays are flattened; elements are not rendered.

nodes.label: Children.toArray key rewriting
nodes.rationale: Drops empty nodes and prefixes keys with nesting and position so flattening cannot collide keys from different branches.

nodes.label: isValidElement
nodes.rationale: True only for React elements. Strings, numbers and arrays render but return false.

nodes.label: children is source structure not rendered output
nodes.rationale: There is no way to see what an inner component will render. One wrapper component is one child.

nodes.label: Make data flow visible
nodes.rationale: Prefer exported parts, data props, render props, context or hooks. Cloning hides where values come from.

nodes.label: Phase 2 load-bearing pages 01 02 03 05
nodes.rationale: Topics 12–16 are pre-hooks era: read them to read code, not to write it.

nodes.label: Phase 2 Dialog gate
nodes.rationale: A Dialog through a portal, header and footer as element props, Escape and backdrop close, dual-mode open.

nodes.label: propTypes removed silently in React 19
nodes.rationale: React 19 ignores propTypes with no warning, so an upgrade quietly deletes runtime prop checks.

nodes.label: What makes a function a component
React calls the component not you
nodes.rationale: A helper is a function you call. Ownership of the call is what lets React attach state, effects, position and identity.

nodes.label: Capital letter is a JSX compilation rule
nodes.rationale: Lowercase compiles to a string tag, so React creates an unknown DOM element and the function never runs.

nodes.label: Element versus direct call
nodes.rationale: Widget() inlines output into the caller. Hooks join the caller list; a conditional call breaks hook order.

nodes.label: Props are one argument
nodes.rationale: JSX builds a fresh object each render so identity comparison on props is always false. React 19 put ref in that same object.

nodes.label: Hooks matched by call order
nodes.rationale: No name, no key — just position on the fiber. Conditional hooks shift every subsequent slot.

nodes.label: Component identity and the nesting rule
Nesting rule
nodes.rationale: Reconciliation compares type by Object.is. A new function each render is a different component, so the subtree remounts. Never nest definitions.

nodes.label: Type change remount cost
nodes.rationale: State, refs, effects, DOM, focus, scroll, animations and uncontrolled inputs are all destroyed and recreated.

nodes.label: Four disguises of unstable identity
nodes.rationale: Local arrows, HOCs in render, and memo or lazy called during render. A map of module-level components is safe.

nodes.label: key for deliberate remount
nodes.rationale: A changed key is treated as a different position. Reset forms with key={record.id}, not by swapping types.

nodes.label: The two rules of a pure component
Component purity
nodes.rationale: Mind your own business and same inputs same output. React assumes this of every component and does not verify it at runtime.

nodes.label: Inputs are props state and context
nodes.rationale: Output depending on time, window, localStorage or a module variable is impure no matter how stable that source looks.

nodes.label: Module-level write during render
nodes.rationale: react.dev Cup example yields guests 2, 4, 6 under StrictMode because output depends on call count.

nodes.label: useSyncExternalStore for external sources
nodes.rationale: The hook for mutable sources React can track, including under concurrent rendering. Window size belongs here.

nodes.label: Writing a ref during render is unsupported
nodes.rationale: A ref exists before the render. Mutate refs in effects and handlers.

nodes.label: Local mutation
nodes.rationale: Objects created during this render are yours to mutate. The test is whether the object existed before the render started.

nodes.label: Side effects belong in event handlers
nodes.rationale: Handlers run after render so they sit outside the rule. useEffect is the fallback after handlers are exhausted. Derivations are neither — compute during render.

nodes.label: Three tiers of impurity cost
nodes.rationale: Visible in StrictMode today; wrong UI when Compiler or memoization changes call count; un-undoable side effects from abandoned concurrent renders.

nodes.label: StrictMode, the Compiler and how purity is enforced
StrictMode doubling is the test
nodes.rationale: React cannot inspect purity, so it runs the function twice in development. The second call is the detector, not overhead.

nodes.label: What StrictMode cannot catch
nodes.rationale: Production-only paths, unrun branches, idempotent writes, event handlers, and effects after the first mount. A clean dev run is not proof.

nodes.label: React Compiler is a static purity checker
nodes.rationale: It bails out instead of rewriting impure components. Skipped components are a purity report covering code that never ran.

nodes.label: useRef guard is the wrong StrictMode fix
nodes.rationale: It hides the symptom. The effect still cannot be re-run on remount, Fast Refresh or Activity restore.

nodes.label: Features that assume calling is free
nodes.rationale: Batching, memo, Compiler, transitions, Suspense, Activity, SSR and offscreen prerendering all assume render has no consequences.

nodes.label: Configuration trap
nodes.rationale: A component becomes an interpreter of a private option language. API grows without bound, combinations go untested, every caller pays unused imports, and markup is hidden.

nodes.label: Composition over configuration
nodes.rationale: A prop that exists only to be rendered should have been the rendered thing. Pass the Button, not actionLabel plus onAction plus actionVariant.

nodes.label: Elements are ordinary values
nodes.rationale: Creating an element does not render it. Where it is created decides what it can close over.

nodes.label: When configuration is the right answer
nodes.rationale: Keep a prop for data, component-owned behaviour, closed design-system variants, or consistency. Design decisions are props; caller markup is composition.

nodes.label: Slots, children and the context hole
children is the free slot
nodes.rationale: A hole the parent fills with arbitrary JSX. Use when there is one content area and no opinion about it.

nodes.label: Slots pattern
nodes.rationale: Named element props for fixed regions. Community name, not a React API. Do not slice children by index.

nodes.label: Compound components
nodes.rationale: Parent provides shared state through context; parts consume it and can be arranged freely. Parts only work inside the parent.

nodes.label: Context hole
nodes.rationale: Create the element in the scope that has the value and pass the finished object down. Intermediates never mention the value.

nodes.label: RSC composition requirement
nodes.rationale: A Client Component cannot import a Server Component but can receive one as children. Composition keeps server code out of the client bundle.

nodes.label: React 19 context as provider
nodes.rationale: Render the context object directly as ThemeContext value={theme}. The .Provider form still works.

nodes.label: Passing children skips wrapper re-renders
nodes.rationale: The element object is created by the outer owner. When the wrapper re-renders, props.children is identical so React skips that subtree.

nodes.label: Controlled versus uncontrolled
nodes.rationale: Informal terms asked per piece of state. Controlled means the important information is driven by props; uncontrolled means local state the parent cannot influence.

nodes.label: Controlled flexibility versus uncontrolled ease
nodes.rationale: Uncontrolled needs less API but cannot coordinate. Controlling lifts state, so updates re-render the owner and everything below.

nodes.label: Five triggers to control a value
nodes.rationale: Coordination, persistence, validation, programmatic control, or reflecting external data. Do not control in case.

nodes.label: Controlled API naming
nodes.rationale: value/onChange, checked/onChange, open/onOpenChange, defaultX for the uncontrolled initial. Call the handler with the next value.

nodes.label: The switch warning, and supporting both
undefined decides controlled mode
nodes.rationale: value === undefined on first render is uncontrolled. Empty string and 0 are controlled. Mode cannot change over the input lifetime.

nodes.label: value={x ?? ''} fix
nodes.rationale: ?? only replaces null and undefined. || also replaces 0 and empty string.

nodes.label: Dual-mode controlled component
nodes.rationale: Decide with !== undefined, own internal state only when uncontrolled, always notify, never sync the prop into state with an effect.

nodes.label: State in two places test
nodes.rationale: If you can delete one copy and compute it from the other, delete it. A draft that is supposed to differ until save is not duplication.

nodes.label: Lift state in three steps
nodes.rationale: Remove child state, pass hardcoded data from the parent, then add state and handlers. The middle step separates wiring bugs from update bugs.

nodes.label: Closest common parent owns state
nodes.rationale: Count components that render based on the value, not ones that only pass it through. Invent a component solely to own state if needed.

nodes.label: Single source of truth
nodes.rationale: One owner per piece, not all state in one store. The forbidden case is the same information in two places.

nodes.label: Inverse data flow
nodes.rationale: Data down as props, changes up as function calls. Name handlers for the event so the owner keeps its state shape private.

nodes.label: The cost, and how to pay less of it
Lifting moves the re-render
nodes.rationale: A state change re-renders that component and all descendants by default. Children re-render because the parent did, not because a prop changed.

nodes.label: Push state down
nodes.rationale: If only one branch reads the state, extract that branch and move the state into it. The large component stops re-rendering.

nodes.label: memo is last resort
nodes.rationale: Shallow compare is not free, fails on fresh objects, and does not stop context. Structural fixes survive the Compiler; hand memoization largely does not.

nodes.label: Lift then compose then context then store
nodes.rationale: Two or three siblings lift. Threads through unused layers compose. Rarely changing many-depth values use context. Frequent sliced updates use an external store. Server data is a cache.

nodes.label: Class components still supported
nodes.rationale: Not recommended for new code and receive no new features. Not scheduled for removal. Read them; do not write them except error boundaries.

nodes.label: setState merges useState replaces
nodes.rationale: Porting a state object wholesale to useState silently drops unrespread fields. The classic conversion bug.

nodes.label: this binding in class handlers
nodes.rationale: Extracting this.handleClick loses the receiver. Class bodies are strict so this is undefined. Prefer a class-field arrow; call-site arrows defeat PureComponent.

nodes.label: Legacy context removed in React 19
nodes.rationale: contextTypes and getChildContext are gone. A class consumes one context via static contextType.

nodes.label: Class defaultProps survives
nodes.rationale: Kept because there is no ES6 default-parameter equivalent for a class.

nodes.label: forceUpdate
nodes.rationale: Forces a re-render without a state change. Almost always means state is kept somewhere React cannot see.

nodes.label: Error boundaries stay classes
nodes.rationale: The conversion that cannot be done. A hook cannot implement an error boundary.

nodes.label: Class instance fields become useRef
nodes.rationale: Timer ids, sockets and caches persist without triggering a render. useState would re-render on every assignment.

nodes.label: Phase 3 — State and the render cycle
State belongs to a tree position
useState initial value is read once
Three cases where updater form is required
Props changing is not a render trigger
Four things that stop render descent
Cannot update a different component during render
useReducer is the named queue fold
Lift per-row UI state to the list
Same type and position keep state
Five rules for set during render
Three shapes of infinite render loops
Phase 4 — Effects and synchronization
nodes.rationale: useEffect is misused as run-after-render. The phase follows two ideas: an effect is caused by rendering, and setup and cleanup are a pair React may run any number of times.

nodes.label: Phase 4 gate
nodes.rationale: Rewrite a keystroke-fetching effect so it debounces, cancels superseded requests, never renders an old query, and survives StrictMode — and name which mechanism does each.

nodes.label: What an effect is for
nodes.rationale: An effect synchronizes a component with a system outside React. It is not run-after-render, not componentDidMount, and not where you respond to a click.

nodes.label: Synchronize with an external system
nodes.rationale: If you are not synchronizing with a browser API, widget, network, or non-React component, you probably do not need an Effect.

nodes.label: Effects versus events
nodes.rationale: Effects are caused by rendering itself. Events are caused by a particular interaction. If why names a user action, it is a handler.

nodes.label: componentDidMount is the wrong model
nodes.rationale: useEffect(fn, []) stays connected to the first room forever. Synchronization with real deps and cleanup handles mount, update and unmount.

nodes.label: Effects only run on the client
nodes.rationale: They do not run during server rendering, so fetched data is absent from initial HTML, and they are where window, document and localStorage are legal.

nodes.label: Effect timing relative to paint is not guaranteed
nodes.rationale: An interaction-caused Effect may run before paint; React may also repaint before processing state updates inside it. useLayoutEffect or setTimeout for a guarantee.

nodes.label: react.dev You Might Not Need an Effect
useEffect anatomy
nodes.rationale: Three parts: setup after commit, optional cleanup that undoes it, and a dependency array with three distinct forms.

nodes.label: Three dependency-array forms
nodes.rationale: No array: after every commit. Empty: after the initial commit only. Populated: initial commit and when a dependency changes by Object.is.

nodes.label: cleanup(old) then setup(new)
nodes.rationale: Cleanup closes over the render that created it, so it disconnects the old room. At unmount it runs one final time.

nodes.label: Dependency array must be a constant-size literal
nodes.rationale: Dependencies are compared positionally. A changing size is meaningless; a variable defeats exhaustive-deps.

nodes.label: Setup function cannot be async
nodes.rationale: React expects a cleanup function; async returns a Promise. Declare an inner async function and return a real cleanup.

nodes.label: One effect per concern
nodes.rationale: Merging concerns unions their dependency lists, so each tears down for the other's reasons. Split by what is synchronized, not when it runs.

nodes.label: The dependency array is not a preference
nodes.rationale: The array declares what the effect reads. It is true or false. Lying produces an effect that reads one render's values forever.

nodes.label: You cannot choose Effect dependencies
nodes.rationale: Every reactive value the setup reads must be declared. To remove a dependency you must prove to the linter it is not read.

nodes.label: Reactive values
nodes.rationale: Props and all variables and functions declared directly inside the component. Module constants, setters, dispatch and ref objects are not.

nodes.label: Omitted dependency freezes the first render
nodes.rationale: Each render creates a new setup closure. An empty array means only the first ever runs. The component re-renders; the connection stays on the old room.

nodes.label: react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
nodes.rationale: Computes the correct array from the code. A disable comment converts a compile-time complaint into a runtime stale-value bug.

nodes.label: Object and function identity re-runs the Effect
nodes.rationale: Object.is fails every render for a new object or function. Depend on primitives, move inside, extract an Effect Event, or useMemo/useCallback last.

nodes.label: ref.current is not tracked
nodes.rationale: The ref object is stable; reading ref.current does not make the effect reactive. That is occasionally correct and also how people hide dependencies.

nodes.label: StrictMode double-invocation
nodes.rationale: One extra setup+cleanup cycle in development before the first real setup. It tests the mount path only.

nodes.label: Extra setup+cleanup cycle
nodes.rationale: Mount is setup → cleanup → setup where production is setup. If those are indistinguishable to the user, cleanup is complete.

nodes.label: StrictMode only doubles the mount
nodes.rationale: The extra cycle is before the first real setup, not every setup. A leak on the dependency-change path passes StrictMode.

nodes.label: Double render versus extra effect cycle
nodes.rationale: Double render finds impurity in the component body and useState/useMemo/useReducer functions. Extra effect cycle finds missing cleanup. Event handlers are in neither.

nodes.label: Callback refs get the same extra cycle
nodes.rationale: React 19 ref cleanup functions make the symmetry expressible. A missing cleanup doubles registry counts.

nodes.label: Partial StrictMode skips the extra effect cycle
nodes.rationale: When StrictMode is not at the root, React will not double child effects without parent effects, because that cannot happen in production.

nodes.label: DevTools dims second-render logs
nodes.rationale: A missing second log is not evidence of a single render. Effect setup logs are not dimmed.

nodes.label: Doubled development analytics is not a bug
nodes.rationale: You do not want development traffic in production metrics. The real bug nearby is a doubled mutation that belonged in a handler.

nodes.label: Fetching data in an effect
nodes.rationale: Fetching is the one You-Might-Not-Need case that survives as a legitimate effect, and react.dev still recommends something else.

nodes.label: Four documented fetching-in-Effect downsides
nodes.rationale: No server run so HTML is a spinner; structural waterfalls; no preload or cache; enough boilerplate that most codebases ship the buggy version.

nodes.label: Fetching on mount is the weak strategy
nodes.rationale: The four downsides apply to fetching after mount in any library. Effects are just the most direct way to express it.

nodes.label: Network waterfall
nodes.rationale: A child cannot render until its parent has, and an effect cannot run until its component has rendered, so requests serialize along tree depth.

nodes.label: Framework fetching or a client cache
nodes.rationale: A framework can start the request before render. TanStack Query, useSWR and React Router 6.4+ address cache and ergonomics but still fetch after mount.

nodes.label: useData fixes ergonomics only
nodes.rationale: One race-condition guard instead of twenty. Still no cache, still after mount, still a waterfall and empty server HTML.

nodes.label: Clear stale data before the next fetch
nodes.rationale: setBio(null) at the top of setup. Without it Alice's bio stays on screen labelled as Bob. Ignore prevents applying the wrong response; clearing prevents displaying it.

nodes.label: Race conditions
nodes.rationale: The screen shows the answer to a question the user has already moved on from. No error, no failed request — just the wrong data, sometimes.

nodes.label: Responses may arrive out of order
nodes.rationale: The most recent response is not the most recent request. Both succeed; the last arrival wins. Intermittent on slow or uneven networks.

nodes.label: ignore flag
nodes.rationale: let ignore = false inside setup; cleanup sets it true. One flag per request. Fixes the render. Does not cancel the transfer.

nodes.label: AbortController
nodes.rationale: Stops the request. Catch must ignore DOMException named AbortError. Only works with APIs that accept a signal.

nodes.label: AbortError is not a failure
nodes.rationale: An aborted fetch rejects with AbortError. Treating every rejection as failure turns cancel into a visible error.

nodes.label: Race guards are not a cache
nodes.rationale: Neither ignore nor abort deduplicates, remembers a return visit, or starts the request earlier.

nodes.label: An effect has its own lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Components mount, update and unmount. Effects only start and stop synchronizing. One mount can contain many start/stop cycles.

nodes.label: Start and stop, not mount and unmount
nodes.rationale: Ask what start means and what stop means. If both have clean answers the effect is resilient to being started and stopped as many times as needed.

nodes.label: Door-lock analogy
nodes.rationale: React starts and stops the Effect one extra time in development to check the lock — that start and stop are a matched pair.

nodes.label: One synchronization process per Effect
nodes.rationale: A connection and a visit log start together but are unrelated. The test: if you need the word and, split.

nodes.label: Mutable-outside-React values cannot be dependencies
nodes.rationale: location.pathname and ref.current can change outside the render data flow. A dependency array records what a render produced.

nodes.label: All linter errors on dependencies are legitimate
nodes.rationale: There is always a way to fix the code without breaking the rules. The array is the input React uses to decide whether to re-synchronize.

nodes.label: useEffectEvent
nodes.rationale: Read the latest props and state from inside an effect without making them dependencies. The only sanctioned way to do that.

nodes.label: Effect Events are non-reactive
nodes.rationale: They always see the latest values, but their execution does not re-run the surrounding Effect. Theme can style a notification without reconnecting chat.

nodes.label: Effect Event identity is intentionally unstable
nodes.rationale: A runtime assertion: put it in a dependency array and the effect re-runs every render. Never wrap it in useCallback.

nodes.label: Effect Event call-site rules
nodes.rationale: Top-level Hook. Call only from Effects or other Effect Events. Never during render, never from a handler, never pass to another component or Hook.

nodes.label: Do not use useEffectEvent to avoid dependencies
nodes.rationale: Wrapping the whole setup to reach [] hides real staleness. Only genuinely event-like logic belongs in an Effect Event.

nodes.label: useEffectEvent is stable in React 19.2
nodes.rationale: Re-checked 2026-08-14: the reference has no experimental banner. The React 19.2 release post (1 Oct 2025) lists it as shipped.

nodes.label: useLayoutEffect
nodes.rationale: Same hook as useEffect except it fires before the browser repaints. That difference is the reason to use it and the reason not to.

nodes.label: useLayoutEffect blocks paint
nodes.rationale: The guarantee is the blocking. Code and state updates scheduled inside sit on the critical path. Prefer useEffect when possible.

nodes.label: Measure then place before paint
nodes.rationale: A tooltip renders, measures height, re-renders in the right place. Two renders either way; useLayoutEffect only decides whether the user sees the first.

nodes.label: Layout state update executes remaining Effects immediately
nodes.rationale: A setState here drags every pending useEffect into the blocking window, including expensive work elsewhere in the tree.

nodes.label: useLayoutEffect does nothing on the server
nodes.rationale: No layout information and no paint. Options: useEffect, client-only Suspense, isMounted after hydration, or useSyncExternalStore.

nodes.label: Effect ordering
nodes.rationale: Three kinds of effect in three passes, and inside each pass every cleanup before any setup.

nodes.label: Three effect passes per commit
nodes.rationale: useInsertionEffect, then DOM mutation, then useLayoutEffect before paint, then browser paint, then useEffect. Each pass finishes across the whole commit.

nodes.label: All cleanups then all setups
nodes.rationale: When any setup runs, everything being torn down in that pass is already gone, including other components. Exclusive resources can transfer safely.

nodes.label: Effects run children before parents
nodes.rationale: A parent measuring a child needs the child's refs attached. That is why ref.current is null during render and populated in effects.

nodes.label: useInsertionEffect interleaves cleanup and setup
nodes.rationale: One component at a time, unlike other Effects. Refs are not attached yet and you cannot update state. Exists for CSS-in-JS.

nodes.label: Do not use effect order as coordination
nodes.rationale: Order explains failures; it is not timing under concurrent rendering, a render is not a commit, and insertion vs DOM mutation is unspecified.

nodes.label: Cleanup
nodes.rationale: The only correct effect is one where setup → cleanup → setup is indistinguishable from setup alone.

nodes.label: The cleanup contract
nodes.rationale: Cleanup is the stop half of a start/stop pair. React will call that pair as many times as it needs to.

nodes.label: setup → cleanup → setup must match setup once
nodes.rationale: If the screen, network or outside world looks different after the extra cycle, the cleanup is incomplete.

nodes.label: Cleanup is not unmount code
nodes.rationale: It runs on dependency change with old values, on unmount, and once extra under StrictMode. Tied to dependencies, not the component lifetime.

nodes.label: Cleanup closes over the old render
nodes.rationale: A cleanup that saw new values would disconnect a room it never connected to. A missing dependency leaves handles never released.

nodes.label: Symmetrical cleanup
nodes.rationale: Read setup line by line and name each inverse. Symmetry is about the observable effect: a fetch is undone by ignoring its result.

nodes.label: Ref guard anti-fix
nodes.rationale: hasRun hides the extra cycle but the resource survives unmount. The question is how to survive remounting, not how to run once.

nodes.label: Cleanup without setup is a code smell
nodes.rationale: Usually reaching for when this unmounts. Cleanup also runs on every dependency change. If there is no external system, remove the Effect.

nodes.label: Cleanup recipes
nodes.rationale: The contract resolves differently depending on what the effect touches. Two of react.dev's cases need no cleanup.

nodes.label: Idempotent setup needs no cleanup
nodes.rationale: map.setZoomLevel(12) twice leaves the map at 12. Setters are usually idempotent; anything that opens, pushes or begins usually is not.

nodes.label: dialog.showModal needs close
nodes.rationale: A second showModal on an already-open dialog throws. Cleanup makes the extra cycle legal and closes on unmount.

nodes.label: removeEventListener needs the same handler reference
nodes.rationale: Declare the handler inside setup so both calls close over one binding. A recreated function silently removes nothing.

nodes.label: Undo an animation by resetting, not reversing
nodes.rationale: opacity 1 then 0 then 1 matches setting 1 once. For tweening libraries reset the timeline to its initial state.

nodes.label: Analytics POST needs no cleanup
nodes.rationale: The double call is development-only and development traffic should not be in the metrics. A POST that changes application state has neither property.

nodes.label: When cleanup is not the answer
nodes.rationale: Some effects fire twice because the code was never an effect. No cleanup will fix them.

nodes.label: Buying a product is not an Effect
nodes.rationale: You want to buy when the user clicks, not when they visit. Back-navigation remounts and would buy again. Same HTTP verb as analytics, opposite answer.

nodes.label: Remount principle
nodes.rationale: Visiting a page should match visiting, clicking a link, then Back. StrictMode remounts once in development because that journey remounts in production.

nodes.label: Application init belongs at module level
nodes.rationale: Module code runs once per page load. No component-scoped mechanism can promise once, because components mount more than once.

nodes.label: typeof window guard around module init
nodes.rationale: The module is also evaluated during server rendering, where localStorage does not exist. Without the guard the import throws.

nodes.label: You might not need an effect
nodes.rationale: Effects are an escape hatch. If there is no external system, you should not need an Effect.

nodes.label: Transform during render; handle events in handlers
nodes.rationale: An Effect has lost the information about what caused it. That is the defining property that makes effects wrong for event logic.

nodes.label: Twelve cases; only fetching survives
nodes.rationale: Cases 1–4 are Phase 3 state-shape. Case 12 is a legitimate effect that still prefers a framework or cache. That ratio is the point.

nodes.label: Displayed versus interaction test
nodes.rationale: Code that runs because a component was displayed belongs in Effects; the rest belongs in events.

nodes.label: Logic that belongs to an event
nodes.rationale: Logic triggered by a user action ended up in an effect, where the information about what the user did no longer exists.

nodes.label: Share handler logic with a plain function
nodes.rationale: Hoisting shared follow-up into an effect fires it on mount and every product change, so a user already in-cart sees Added on page load.

nodes.label: POST placement depends on causation
nodes.rationale: Analytics stays in an Effect because the form was displayed. Registration belongs in the submit handler. Same verb, opposite answers.

nodes.label: State as a message queue
nodes.rationale: Handler sets jsonToSubmit so an effect will POST. Extra render, null skip, StrictMode double-submit. Delete both and call the function.

nodes.label: Chains of effects
nodes.rationale: Each effect sets the state that wakes the next. One card costs four renders. The cascade is only visible when you read all four together.

nodes.label: An effect chain cannot be replayed
nodes.rationale: Attached to state changing, not the user acting. Undo, history, session restore and tests that seed state re-fire the cascade. Handler logic is inert until called.

nodes.label: Snapshot trap when collapsing a chain
nodes.rationale: Inside a handler, state is a snapshot. Name nextRound = round + 1. The chain had been getting fresh values only because each link ran in a later render.

nodes.label: Chains are often stored derived state
nodes.rationale: isGameOver was always round > 5. Each stored derivation needs a maintaining effect. Delete the storage and the effect goes with it.

nodes.label: State that belongs elsewhere
nodes.rationale: The effect papers over a state-location problem. The fix moves the state and the effect disappears.

nodes.label: Notifying the parent from an Effect runs too late
nodes.rationale: Child sets state, renders, then the effect notifies the parent — two commits. Both updates in one handler batch into one render.

nodes.label: Lift the state up instead of copying
nodes.rationale: If two components need the same value, ask which should own it, not how to copy it. One source of truth cannot disagree with itself.

nodes.label: Pass data down, do not push it up
nodes.rationale: A child pushing via onFetched breaks the one-directional walk that makes a wrong value traceable. Fetch in the parent and pass down.

nodes.label: useSyncExternalStore
nodes.rationale: Reads the value when React needs it, takes a server snapshot, and will not resubscribe while subscribe keeps the same identity. Prevents tearing.

nodes.label: subscribe must be declared outside the component
nodes.rationale: Inline it is a new function every render, so React tears down and rebuilds the subscription every time.

nodes.label: Objects and functions as dependencies
nodes.rationale: Objects and functions created at different times are different. Avoid object and function dependencies.

nodes.label: Move 1 — static object outside the component
nodes.rationale: If it involves no props or state it is not reactive. Module scope makes [] genuinely correct.

nodes.label: Move 2 — build the object inside the Effect
nodes.rationale: The effect makes the object rather than reading it. What remains is a primitive like roomId. This is the default answer.

nodes.label: Move 3 — destructure object props to primitives
nodes.rationale: Destructure during render, not inside setup. A parent that rebuilds options every render then causes no reconnection.

nodes.label: Move 4 — call a pure function prop during render
nodes.rationale: getOptions() must be safe during render. An impure function prop belongs in useEffectEvent instead.

nodes.label: Restructuring the effect
nodes.rationale: Four moves that change what the effect is, rather than what it reads, so the unwanted dependency becomes genuinely irrelevant.

nodes.label: Move 5 — updater form
nodes.rationale: setMessages(msgs => [...msgs, msg]) stops reading messages, so the chat no longer reconnects on every received message.

nodes.label: Move 6 — extract an Effect Event
nodes.rationale: Read isMuted or an inline callback prop without reacting to it. Muting should not reconnect the chat.

nodes.label: Move 7 — move the code to an event handler
nodes.rationale: A submitted flag plus theme in the array re-registers the user when the theme changes. The trigger state and the effect disappear together.

nodes.label: Move 8 — split into several Effects
nodes.rationale: Merged, [country, city] refetches cities when the city changes. Each request keeps its own ignore flag.

nodes.label: The illegitimate fixes
nodes.rationale: Two ways to silence the linter without changing what the effect depends on. Both freeze one render's values forever.

nodes.label: Suppressing exhaustive-deps is a lie
nodes.rationale: There's always a better solution than ignoring the linter. If none of the eight moves apply, the effect probably should not exist.

nodes.label: Suppressed interval freezes the counter at 1
nodes.rationale: onTick from the first render closed over count 0 and increment 1, so every tick calls setCount(0 + 1). Not lagging — frozen.

nodes.label: Ref used to hide a dependency
nodes.rationale: The same lie with no comment. The sanctioned way to read latest without reacting is useEffectEvent. Test: replace the ref with the value.

nodes.label: Dependencies should match the code
nodes.rationale: You cannot choose Effect dependencies. To remove one, prove to the linter it is unnecessary by editing the surrounding code.

nodes.label: Eight legitimate dependency-removal moves
nodes.rationale: Move static values outside the component, build them inside the effect, depend on primitives, call during render, updater form, useEffectEvent, event handler, or split effects.

nodes.label: Illegitimate dependency fixes
nodes.rationale: Suppressing the linter, a counter that always shows 1, and refs used to hide a dependency produce confusing bugs.

nodes.label: useEffectEvent
nodes.rationale: Read the latest value without reacting to it — one of the eight legitimate moves.

nodes.label: Render, reconcile, commit
nodes.rationale: Render is pure and can be thrown away; commit touches the DOM and cannot be undone. Almost every React rule follows from this split.

nodes.label: Fiber
nodes.rationale: Unit of work and linked tree that made the render phase interruptible (work loop, double buffering, alternate).

nodes.label: StrictMode
nodes.rationale: Double-renders components and double-mounts effects in development only. A bug detector; switching it off ships the bug.

nodes.label: State is a snapshot
nodes.rationale: The value in a given render is frozen for that render. This is the whole explanation for stale closures, and it is not a bug.

nodes.label: Automatic batching
nodes.rationale: Multiple setState calls become one render, including inside promises, timeouts and native handlers since React 18; flushSync is the escape.

nodes.label: useEffect as synchronization
nodes.rationale: An effect synchronizes a component with an external system. Not a lifecycle callback and not the place to respond to a click.

nodes.label: useEffectEvent
nodes.rationale: Stable in 19.2. Read latest props and state from an effect without making them dependencies. Call only from effects in the same component.

nodes.label: React Compiler v1.0
nodes.rationale: Build-time automatic memoization, stable as of Oct 2025. Changes the ending of the memoization story, not the reasoning.

nodes.label: Rules of Hooks
nodes.rationale: Call at the top level only, from a component or another hook. Hooks are stored positionally; a conditional hook shifts the list.

nodes.label: useSyncExternalStore
nodes.rationale: Subscribe to an external mutable store without tearing under concurrent rendering.

nodes.label: Part 3 — Concurrent React and the server
Concurrent rendering
nodes.rationale: React can start rendering, stop, do something more urgent, and throw unfinished work away. Purity becomes a correctness requirement.

nodes.label: Suspense
nodes.rationale: A component threw a promise React knows about. A plain fetch inside useEffect cannot suspend no matter how many boundaries wrap it.

nodes.label: Server Components
nodes.rationale: Runs only on the server; code never reaches the browser. No state, effects, event handlers, or browser APIs — and it can be async.

nodes.label: 'use client' directive
nodes.rationale: Marks an entry point into the client graph, not 'this file is a component'. Everything it imports goes to the browser too.

nodes.label: 'use server' directive
nodes.rationale: Marks a Server Function and has nothing to do with Server Components. Every Server Function is a public HTTP endpoint.

nodes.label: Actions
nodes.rationale: A function passed to form action. React calls it with FormData, wraps it in a transition, tracks pending state, and resets on success.

nodes.label: Hydration
nodes.rationale: hydrateRoot attaches React to server HTML. Hydration costs roughly a full render's worth of JavaScript.

nodes.label: Partial Pre-rendering
nodes.rationale: React 19.2 resume APIs: prerender a static shell at build time, resume per request to fill dynamic holes.

nodes.label: Four state buckets
nodes.rationale: Server state, URL state, form state and UI state. Wrong bucket is the source of most global-state complexity.

nodes.label: Server state is a cache
nodes.rationale: Data owned by the API is borrowed, may be stale, and needs invalidation rather than mutation. Deletes half of a typical Redux store.

nodes.label: Error boundaries
nodes.rationale: Still class-only in 19.2.8 via getDerivedStateFromError and componentDidCatch. Do not catch event handlers, timeouts, or SSR errors.

nodes.label: D1–D5 review scoring rubric
nodes.rationale: Weighted composite: D1 explanation 35%, D2 examples 20%, D3 gotchas 15%, D4 interview 15%, D5 provenance 15%. Invented output forces WRONG.

nodes.label: Review evidence rule
nodes.rationale: Every dimension below 8 needs location, quote, gap, and add. Vague 'needs more depth' is not a finding.

nodes.label: Clustering tell
nodes.rationale: Files bunched in a narrow band just under the 300-line cap evidence writing to a budget rather than to the topic.

nodes.label: Review work order
nodes.rationale: The work-order table is the point: executable top to bottom by someone who has not read the pages.

nodes.label: No new sandboxes
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md rule 8: validate against official docs; no run means no output block. Unvalidated pages are listed here, not flagged on the page.

nodes.label: Node and Express verification backlog
nodes.rationale: Node: 229 Verified lines but only 10 cite sandbox (238 no proof). Express: 91 pages, 0 sandbox cites. PostgreSQL is the healthy corpus.

nodes.label: 81 pages clustered 169–269 lines
nodes.rationale: All 81 rewritten pages in phases 1, 2, 5, 10, 11 fall inside 169–269. Not one exceeds 270. Clustering tell: YES.

nodes.label: SET cannot take bind parameters
nodes.rationale: SET LOCAL TIME ZONE $1 fails 42601. Replacement is SELECT set_config($1, $2, true).

nodes.label: XID wraparound warning threshold
nodes.rationale: Warning is near 2.13 billion, not 1 billion. Page on autovacuum_freeze_max_age (200 million), not the wrap warning.

nodes.label: Session advisory lock pool leak
nodes.rationale: pg_try_advisory_lock on a pooled client plus client.release() without destroy returns a connection that still holds the lock.

nodes.label: Merge join needs equality
nodes.rationale: A pure range ON clause is nested loop only. Merge join requires mergejoinable btree equality operators.

nodes.label: Item 14 re-split queue
nodes.rationale: 20 Master-tier single-file pages still inside the clustering band. Write to deserved depth, then chunk on concept boundaries.

nodes.label: Types are erased
nodes.rationale: TypeScript is a build-time checker that leaves nothing behind at runtime. Downstream of this: validation still exists, as is dangerous, enum is unlike other type constructs.

nodes.label: TypeScript 7.0.2 native compiler
nodes.rationale: Native Go compiler. Root export is only version keys; classic ts.createProgram moved to typescript/unstable/*.

nodes.label: Phase 0 How TypeScript runs
nodes.rationale: 13 pages written. Phases 1–12 planned except Phase 1 also written.

nodes.label: TypeScript is a checker, not a runtime
tsc emit-on-error default
nodes.rationale: tsc reports errors and emits JavaScript anyway, exit 2. --noEmitOnError stops output. A build that ignores the exit code ships broken output.

nodes.label: tsc --noEmit CI gate
nodes.rationale: If tsc --noEmit does not run somewhere automatic, you are writing JavaScript with extra syntax.

nodes.label: Erasable vs non-erasable syntax
nodes.rationale: Erasable syntax describes values that already exist. Non-erasable syntax creates runtime objects: enum, runtime namespace, parameter properties, legacy decorators.

nodes.label: Numeric enum IIFE
nodes.rationale: enum emits an IIFE building a two-way map. It cannot be tree-shaken and Node strip-only rejects it.

nodes.label: The three ways to run TypeScript
tsc, transpilers, and Node 24
nodes.rationale: Only tsc checks types. esbuild/swc/Vite/Babel and Node 24 strip and run. Pair a fast runner with tsc --noEmit.

nodes.label: Node strip-only mode
nodes.rationale: Annotations become whitespace so stack traces stay accurate. Syntax that must generate code is ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX at load.

nodes.label: erasableSyntaxOnly
nodes.rationale: tsc rejects non-erasable syntax with TS1294. Enable whenever anything runs .ts directly. Defaults to false.

nodes.label: strict and the flags it turns on
strict defaults to true in TypeScript 7
nodes.rationale: TS 7 default true; 5.9.3 default false. Old projects that never set strict light up on upgrade.

nodes.label: strictNullChecks
nodes.rationale: Without it null is assignable to every type so | null is decoration. Load-bearing flag of the seven; required by strictPropertyInitialization.

nodes.label: types empty array
nodes.rationale: Stops auto-including every @types/* walked from node_modules. This repo's 5.9.3 run pulled @types/mdx from three directories up.

nodes.label: exclude only removes roots
nodes.rationale: A file imported by an included file is still checked even if listed in exclude.

nodes.label: Classic ts.* API moved
nodes.rationale: require('typescript') exports only version and versionMajorMinor. Sync/async API plus 409-export AST live under typescript/unstable/*.

nodes.label: Compiler speed benchmark confound
nodes.rationale: First run reported 10x because 5.9.3 auto-included ancestor @types via cwd. Honest figure is 3x (0.76s vs 2.32s) after asserting zero diagnostics on both sides.

nodes.label: Four type sources
nodes.rationale: Inference, bundled .d.ts, DefinitelyTyped @types/*, or a local ambient declaration. Missing all four is TS7016.

nodes.label: A declaration is a promise, not a check
nodes.rationale: The compiler enforces your .d.ts across the codebase without ever verifying it matches the JavaScript.

nodes.label: The language server is not the build
Editor vs CI disagreements
nodes.rationale: Different compiler version, file set, unsaved buffers, or tsconfig. Same file: four errors on 7.0.2, silence on 5.9.3.

nodes.label: isolatedModules
nodes.rationale: Rejects constructs a single-file transpiler cannot compile: type re-exports without export type, const enum, ambient-only files.

nodes.label: Whole-program check vs one-file transpile
nodes.rationale: A transpiler never opens imports. A checker must build a type graph over the whole program. They cannot be the same pass.

nodes.label: Set rootDir explicitly
nodes.rationale: Unset rootDir is the common ancestor of all inputs. One extra file silently moves output from dist/server.js to dist/src/server.js.

nodes.label: Pin the TypeScript compiler
nodes.rationale: Minors add checks, so a caret range lets a colleague's npm install produce errors yours does not have. Semver intuition does not transfer.

nodes.label: Upgrade path 5.9 to 6.0 to 7.0
nodes.rationale: 6.0 is the JavaScript-implemented deprecation bridge. Tooling that imports typescript is the risky part of jumping to 7.

nodes.label: // @ts-check
nodes.rationale: First comment at the top of a .js file turns the checker on for that file. Types come from JSDoc. Same TS2345 as TypeScript; Node still runs the file unchanged.

nodes.label: checkJs project-wide
nodes.rationale: "checkJs": true checks every .js in the project. Inverse // @ts-nocheck opts one file out. Needs allowJs.

nodes.label: JSDoc type annotations
nodes.rationale: @param, @returns, @type, @typedef, @template, and import('./x.js').T cover ordinary application code. Conditional, mapped, and satisfies types get unreadable.

nodes.label: TypeScript Playground
nodes.rationale: Isolation: reproduce without local tsconfig/@types/editor version, toggle one option, compare compiler versions, inspect emitted JS, share a runnable link.

nodes.label: JSDoc checking vs converting to .ts
nodes.rationale: JSDoc costs no build or rename; converting gives the full language. If types get hard to write in JSDoc, that file wants to be TypeScript.

nodes.label: Phase 0 How TypeScript runs
nodes.rationale: 13 pages before syntax: what the tool is, what it leaves behind, and which of the three programs that accept .ts actually reads the types.

nodes.label: Erasure as the foundation fact
nodes.rationale: Types are deleted and never checked at runtime. Once internalised, enum reputation, erasableSyntaxOnly, runtime validation, and why a green bundler proves nothing stop being separate facts.

nodes.label: strict defaults to true in TypeScript 7
nodes.rationale: Measured: no-flag was not a loose baseline. esModuleInterop and moduleResolution changed defaults too.

nodes.label: tsc emits broken JavaScript by default
nodes.rationale: tsc emits rejected JS and exits 2. --noEmitOnError and --noEmit exit 1. Ignoring the exit code ships output the compiler already rejected.

nodes.label: Type inference
nodes.rationale: Most types are written by nobody. The compiler infers differently for let vs const. Read inferred types from emitted .d.ts, not tooltips.

nodes.label: Literal widening let vs const
nodes.rationale: let x = 'Hyderabad' infers string because it can be reassigned. const keeps "Hyderabad". Object properties widen even under const because contents stay mutable.

nodes.label: Annotate inputs infer outputs
nodes.rationale: Parameters are not inferred (TS7006 under noImplicitAny). Defaults make parameters optional. Returns are inferred from the body. Annotate exported returns to pin the public contract.

nodes.label: noUncheckedIndexedAccess
nodes.rationale: Same first<T>(items: T[]) source emits T or T | undefined depending on the flag, because indexing can miss.

nodes.label: Literal type
nodes.rationale: A type inhabited by exactly one value — 'pending', 42, true. In a union it is the main modelling tool: autocompletion, typo errors, and narrowing.

nodes.label: as const
nodes.rationale: On a literal expression: every property becomes readonly and every literal keeps its type. On an array it produces a readonly tuple. Applies only to literals, not computed values.

nodes.label: Derived union from as const list
nodes.rationale: const STATUSES = [...] as const; type Status = (typeof STATUSES)[number]. One runtime list; the type updates when an entry is added.

nodes.label: satisfies vs as const
nodes.rationale: satisfies checks against a type without replacing the inferred one. An annotation would widen; as const alone would not check. Use it for computed values that as const cannot wrap.

nodes.label: as const is not as T
nodes.rationale: as const asks for the narrowest inference of something already written and cannot lie. as T asserts a type the compiler cannot verify.

nodes.label: Array type T[]
nodes.rationale: T[] and Array<T> are the same. Inference unions elements and forgets length and position. mixed[99] type-checks.

nodes.label: Tuple type
nodes.rationale: Fixed structure: what is in it, in what order, and how many. Named members are documentation only. Optional and rest elements are allowed. Prefer objects past two or three members.

nodes.label: readonly T[]
nodes.rationale: Removes mutating methods from the type; does not freeze at runtime. T[] assigns to readonly T[], not the reverse. Better parameter type for non-mutating functions.

nodes.label: Hook return as const tuple
nodes.rationale: return [value, inc] without as const infers (number | (() => void))[] so both destructured names become that union. as const makes readonly [number, () => void].

nodes.label: Object types
nodes.rationale: Optional properties, readonly, index signatures, and nesting cover almost every shape. ? and readonly are compile-time only.

nodes.label: Optional property vs undefined union
nodes.rationale: ? means the key may be absent. T | undefined means the key must exist and may hold undefined. exactOptionalPropertyTypes stops ? accepting explicit undefined.

nodes.label: Index signature and Record
nodes.rationale: Every key is assumed to exist unless noUncheckedIndexedAccess. Record with a union key produces required properties. Prefer Map when keys are runtime data.

nodes.label: Excess property checks
nodes.rationale: A fresh object literal assigned to a typed target is checked for unknown properties (TS2353). Store it in a variable and freshness is gone.

nodes.label: Weak type detection
nodes.rationale: A type whose properties are all optional rejects a value with no properties in common (TS2559). Add one required property and the same typo through a variable passes silently.

nodes.label: Union types
nodes.rationale: One of these. Until you prove which, you may only touch members common to every branch — that restriction is the feature.

nodes.label: Union common-members rule
nodes.rationale: Accessible members of A | B are the intersection of the branches' members. Anything else requires narrowing.

nodes.label: Discriminated union
nodes.rationale: Shared property with a distinct literal in each member. Makes illegal combinations unrepresentable, unlike { ok: boolean; data?; error? }.

nodes.label: assertNever exhaustiveness
nodes.rationale: After every case, the value is never. A missing case names itself (Type '"cancelled"' is not assignable to type '1'). A default fallback hides new variants.

nodes.label: any
nodes.rationale: Assignable to and from everything. Spreads through inference. Measured: the two any lines produced no diagnostics. JSON.parse returns any.

nodes.label: unknown
nodes.rationale: Everything assigns to it; it assigns to nothing until narrowed. Correct type for input you did not create. catch is unknown under useUnknownInCatchVariables.

nodes.label: never
nodes.rationale: Empty type. Return of a function that always throws or loops; assignable to everything vacuously; result of narrowing everything away. Unexpected never means a branch is unreachable.

nodes.label: void
nodes.rationale: Return value is not part of the contract. A function returning something is assignable to () => void. That lets forEach(push) compile and lets async arrows slip into useEffect.

nodes.label: unknown at the door never any
nodes.rationale: Assign fetch/json to unknown and prove it with a schema. The narrowing step is the work any skips and the bug any ships.

nodes.label: Declaration merging
