nodes.rationale: Two interfaces with the same name combine. Type aliases error TS2300 Duplicate identifier. Merging is how you augment Express.Request and ProcessEnv.

nodes.label: type alias
nodes.rationale: Only aliases can be unions, tuples, primitives, mapped, conditional, and template literal types. Discriminated unions force a large share of types to be aliases.

nodes.label: interface
nodes.rationale: Always an object shape. Needed when something must be augmentable. extends checks compatibility and reports TS2430 on conflict.

nodes.label: extends vs intersection on conflict
nodes.rationale: interface extends reports the conflict at the declaration. An intersection silently produces string & number, i.e. never, discovered at the call site.

nodes.label: Interface error-message folklore
nodes.rationale: Measured: a plain object alias and an equivalent interface produced identical TS2741 text, each naming its type. Aliases of intersections or mapped types can still expand.

nodes.label: Function types
nodes.rationale: A contract with a caller. Two unintuitive rules: fewer parameters are assignable where more are expected, and a function returning something is assignable where void is expected.

nodes.label: Contextual typing
nodes.rationale: The one place parameters infer: when the target type is known. Callbacks to typed functions need no annotations; a standalone function always does (TS7006).

nodes.label: Fewer parameters assignability
nodes.rationale: Ignoring an argument is safe; demanding one the caller never sends is not. Makes arr.map(x => ...) legal without declaring index and array.

nodes.label: Function overloads
nodes.rationale: Implementation signature is not callable. Only declared overloads are visible. First matching overload wins. Prefer a union or generic unless return type truly depends on arguments.

nodes.label: Default makes parameter optional
nodes.rationale: subject = 'none' is subject? for callers and string in the body. subject?: string is string | undefined in the body.

nodes.label: Structural typing
nodes.rationale: A is assignable to B when A has at least B's members of compatible types. Names never matter. Extra members are fine; missing ones are not. Opposite of Java nominal typing.

nodes.label: Function parameter contravariance
nodes.rationale: A function may accept less and return more. Returns compare covariantly. Method parameters are bivariant; strictFunctionTypes tightens function-typed properties, not method shorthand.

nodes.label: Branded types
nodes.rationale: type UserId = string is the same type as OrderId. Brand with string & { readonly __brand: 'UserId' } so the shapes differ. The brand is erased at runtime.

nodes.label: Private members are nominal
nodes.rationale: Two classes with identically named private fields are not interchangeable. Each private declaration is unique to its class — the one place TypeScript is nominal without a brand.

nodes.label: Read assignability errors bottom-up
nodes.rationale: The innermost Type A is not assignable to type B names the real mismatch. Outer lines are the property path the compiler walked.

nodes.label: strictNullChecks
nodes.rationale: Without it, null and undefined belong to every type and | null is decoration. With it they are ordinary union members (TS18047). Defaults true via strict in TypeScript 7.

nodes.label: null vs undefined
nodes.rationale: undefined is not provided; null is deliberately empty. Produce undefined internally, accept null from JSON/SQL, normalise at the boundary. JSON.stringify drops undefined and keeps null.

nodes.label: ?? vs ||
nodes.rationale: ?? falls back only on null/undefined. || falls back on every falsy value, so a legitimate 0 or '' is replaced.

nodes.label: Optional chaining ?.
nodes.rationale: Short-circuits the whole chain to undefined, never to null, even when the missing link was null. Result is always T | undefined.

nodes.label: Non-null assertion !
nodes.rationale: Removes null/undefined with no check. A claim, not a proof. An explicit throw fails at the cause instead of Cannot read properties of null later.

nodes.label: Narrowing lost inside a callback
nodes.rationale: Measured on 7.0.2: narrowing of a property survives await in the same function and is discarded inside forEach, which could run later. Copy to a const first.

nodes.label: Intersection types
nodes.rationale: A & B means both at once. Unions widen values and narrow usable members; intersections do the reverse. Mixin pattern for composing named fragments.

nodes.label: Intersection conflicting members become never
nodes.rationale: No error at the declaration. First assignment is Type 'string' is not assignable to type 'never'. interface extends reports TS2430 instead.

nodes.label: Intersection distributes over union
nodes.rationale: (A | B) & C becomes (A & C) | (B & C). Adds a shared field to every branch of a discriminated union without breaking the discriminant.

nodes.label: Call signature
nodes.rationale: The arrow form cannot carry properties. An interface with a call signature types middleware, memoised functions with .cache, and decorated handlers.

nodes.label: Construct signature
nodes.rationale: new (...) => T describes a constructor, not an instance. abstract new accepts abstract classes that a plain new rejects.

nodes.label: typeof Class static side
nodes.rationale: Widget is the instance type. typeof Widget is the constructor plus static members. Property 'create' does not exist on type 'Repo' means the static lives on typeof Repo.

nodes.label: Hybrid type
nodes.rationale: Call or construct signature plus ordinary properties. Rare in new code, common in .d.ts for pre-module libraries such as jQuery $.

nodes.label: enum
nodes.rationale: Emits an IIFE two-way map. Cannot be stripped (ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX / erasableSyntaxOnly). Resists tree-shaking. Numeric enums log as numbers and are nominally typed.

nodes.label: String literal union
nodes.rationale: Default for a fixed set of values. Zero runtime cost, readable serialisation, no import. Cannot iterate members at runtime.

nodes.label: const object plus derived union
nodes.rationale: const Status = {...} as const; type Status = (typeof Status)[keyof typeof Status]. Same name in value and type namespaces. Call sites keep Status.Pending. Erases cleanly.

nodes.label: const enum
nodes.rationale: Inlines values at call sites — a whole-program transform. Banned by isolatedModules and breaks under esbuild, swc, and Vite.

nodes.label: readonly
nodes.rationale: Compile-time promise only. Stops assignments the checker can see. Erased at runtime and bypassed by as. readonly items: T[] blocks replacement; items: readonly T[] blocks mutation.

nodes.label: readonly T[] parameter
nodes.rationale: T[] assigns to readonly T[] but not the reverse. Declaring readonly accepts both kinds and documents that the function does not mutate.

nodes.label: readonly is shallow
nodes.rationale: Readonly<T> maps top-level properties only. c.db.host still mutates. Deep immutability needs a recursive type and costs compile time and error quality.

nodes.label: Object.freeze
nodes.rationale: The only runtime guarantee. Also shallow. Most codebases rely on readonly for intent; freeze when a runtime write must throw.

nodes.label: Recursive type aliases
nodes.rationale: A type may refer to itself through an object, array, or function member. Direct self-reference in an intersection circularly references itself.

nodes.label: JsonValue
nodes.rationale: string | number | boolean | null | JsonValue[] | { [key: string]: JsonValue }. Honest alternative to any for arbitrary JSON. Interfaces lack an implicit index signature and may not satisfy it.

nodes.label: TS2589 instantiation too deep
nodes.rationale: Depth 50 and 500 compiled; 5000 tripped it on 7.0.2. Means type-level arithmetic or a deep mapped type, not that ordinary nested data is too deep.

nodes.label: reduce type argument pins accumulator
nodes.rationale: Without reduce<number>, the accumulator infers from the array element type (JsonValue), not from the initial 0. Measured TS18047 and TS2365 until the type argument was supplied.

nodes.label: object (lowercase)
nodes.rationale: Any non-primitive. Excludes strings and numbers. Exposes no members, so you cannot read properties from it.

nodes.label: Object wrapper interface
nodes.rationale: Members of Object.prototype. Primitives satisfy it by autoboxing. Same trap as String, Number, Boolean — lowercase primitives only.

nodes.label: Empty object type {}
nodes.rationale: Not an empty object: any value with at least zero members, i.e. everything except null and undefined. Legitimate as T extends {} meaning defined.

nodes.label: Record<string, unknown>
nodes.rationale: What to write for any object whose properties you will read. unknown plus narrowing if you will prove the shape first.

nodes.label: symbol
nodes.rationale: Unique key that cannot collide. Invisible to Object.keys, JSON.stringify, and for...in. let widens to symbol; const keeps unique symbol.

nodes.label: unique symbol
nodes.rationale: Type of one specific symbol. Two Symbol('key') values are different types. Symbol.for is typed symbol because it is not unique.

nodes.label: Well-known symbols
nodes.rationale: Symbol.iterator, asyncIterator, toPrimitive, hasInstance, toStringTag hook a class into language behaviour.

nodes.label: Symbol keys skipped by JSON
nodes.rationale: JSON.stringify and Object.keys skip symbol keys. Useful for in-process metadata; silent data loss across a network or structuredClone.

nodes.label: Computed key unique symbol folklore
nodes.rationale: Older TypeScript required unique symbol (TS1170). On 7.0.2 both an interface and a type alias accepted a let symbol as a computed key. Still prefer const so the binding cannot be reassigned.

nodes.label: Phase 1 The type vocabulary
nodes.rationale: 17 pages. Every type you will write for the next year. Gate: model an API payload without any and say why each choice is not a neighbour.

nodes.label: typeof narrowing
nodes.rationale: A typeof check changes the type inside the branch. Works on string, number, bigint, boolean, symbol, undefined, function. object is a bucket. Narrows the else by elimination too.

nodes.label: typeof object includes null
nodes.rationale: typeof null === 'object' is a 1995 JavaScript bug that TypeScript models. Measured: string | number | null | undefined | string[] narrows to string[] | null. Pair with !== null.

nodes.label: Array.isArray type guard
nodes.rationale: Built-in type guard. Narrows to string[] cleanly where typeof object cannot tell an array from a Date, a plain object, or null.

nodes.label: Reveal narrowed type via impossible assignment
nodes.rationale: const r: 1 = v reports Type 'X' is not assignable to type '1', naming the exact type the checker holds. Settles narrowing arguments without a runtime print.

nodes.label: Equality narrowing
nodes.rationale: Comparing against a literal removes everything else. Narrows both operands when they are both unions. Mechanism behind discriminated unions and switch exhaustiveness.

nodes.label: != null nullish check
nodes.rationale: The one legitimate use of loose equality: excludes null and undefined and nothing else. Use it for string, number, and boolean that may be missing.

nodes.label: Truthiness narrowing
nodes.rationale: if (v) and v != null produce identical types. At runtime if (v) also skips '' and 0. The compiler cannot warn because '' is still string. Safe only for objects and functions.

nodes.label: JavaScript falsy values
nodes.rationale: false, 0, -0, 0n, '', null, undefined, NaN. [] , {}, '0', and 'false' are truthy, so if (arr) is true for an empty array.

nodes.label: in operator narrowing
nodes.rationale: When two object types differ by which properties they have and there is no discriminant or constructor, in is the only built-in narrowing left. It costs clarity: the check names a property rather than a variant, so a rename silently changes which branch runs.

nodes.label: Optional properties break in narrowing
nodes.rationale: in narrows on declared properties. If the distinguishing property is optional, a value of that type may lack it at runtime, so the else branch stays a union.

nodes.label: in walks the prototype chain
nodes.rationale: in checks the prototype chain, so 'toString' in {} is true. Object.hasOwn is the safer runtime check for untrusted data even though it does not narrow.

nodes.label: k in obj narrows obj never k
nodes.rationale: A common misreading: k in obj narrows the object, never the key. Narrow the key with a type predicate returning k is keyof T.

nodes.label: Prefer a discriminant for designed types
nodes.rationale: in is right for shapes you do not control. For shapes you design, a discriminant is clearer, survives refactoring, and enables exhaustiveness checking.

nodes.label: instanceof narrowing
nodes.rationale: instanceof is precise, needs no helper, and narrows unknown in one step inside a single application. It is nominal, so it breaks across realms and duplicate package copies, and cannot see plain object types.

nodes.label: instanceof on unknown catch
nodes.rationale: catch (err) is unknown under strict. Check most-specific class first, then Error, then stringify non-Error throws — JavaScript can throw anything.

nodes.label: instanceof fails across realms
nodes.rationale: A value from an iframe, vm context, worker, or a duplicate package copy has a different constructor identity, so instanceof Error is false.

nodes.label: Structural isError predicate
nodes.rationale: typeof e === 'object' && e !== null && 'message' in e && 'stack' in e survives realm and duplicate-package boundaries. Node also provides util.types.isNativeError.

nodes.label: Discriminated union
nodes.rationale: One literal-typed property shared by every member lets the compiler tell variants apart from ===. Highest-value pattern: illegal states become unrepresentable and exhaustiveness checking becomes possible. Costs a property on every member and more verbose construction.

nodes.label: Literal-typed discriminant
nodes.rationale: A discriminant widened to string matches every member, so nothing is eliminated. Validate at the boundary so the validator produces the literal type.

nodes.label: Result ok discriminated union
nodes.rationale: { ok: true; data: T } | { ok: false; error: Error } — one check gives a fully-typed branch either way, and there is no state where both data and error exist.

nodes.label: Illegal states unrepresentable
nodes.rationale: A single object with optional data/error and status: string type-checks illegal combinations. The union makes those combinations unrepresentable and turns a new variant into a compile error.

nodes.label: Exhaustiveness with never
nodes.rationale: Handle every variant and the residual type becomes never. Miss one and the error names it. Turns adding a status from a bug hunt into a compile error at every site that must change.

nodes.label: assertNever
nodes.rationale: A helper whose parameter is never: compile-time error when a variant is added, and a runtime throw if unvalidated data carries an impossible variant. Types are erased; the throw is the only runtime protection.

nodes.label: Default fallback swallows variants
nodes.rationale: A default that returns a fallback compiles forever no matter how many variants you add. Either assertNever in default, or no default with an explicit return type.

nodes.label: Record union exhaustive map
nodes.rationale: Record<Union, T> for value lookups is exhaustive by construction — a missing key is TS2739 at the table, with no helper. Prefer this for pure lookups; switch when branches do work.

nodes.label: Type predicate
nodes.rationale: A return type of the form x is T lets narrowing survive a function call. A plain boolean return narrows nothing. Reuses one check everywhere and works with filter/find, but the compiler takes your word for the body.

nodes.label: Compiler does not check guard body
nodes.rationale: function isCat(p): p is Cat { return true } compiles. A predicate is an assertion in function form — written once and trusted at every call site, so a wrong one is more expensive than a wrong as.

nodes.label: isDefined filter guard
nodes.rationale: filter(v => v != null) keeps (T | null)[] because the arrow is not a type predicate. A named isDefined<T>(v): v is T lets filter narrow to T[].

nodes.label: isKeyOf type predicate
nodes.rationale: The only way to convince the compiler a string is a valid key: k is keyof T. The in operator narrows the object, never the key.

nodes.label: Schema validator over hand-written guards
nodes.rationale: Guards for small structural checks. A validator (zod, valibot) for anything crossing a boundary: it performs the runtime check and derives the type from one declaration.

nodes.label: TypeScript type erasure
nodes.rationale: TypeScript type-checks then throws the types away. Annotations, interfaces and type aliases vanish; enum, namespace, parameter properties and decorators emit code.

nodes.label: Three ways to run TypeScript
nodes.rationale: tsc emit, transpile-only tools (esbuild/swc/Babel/tsx), and Node 24 running .ts directly. Only one of the three actually type-checks.

nodes.label: strict tsconfig flag
nodes.rationale: One line in tsconfig.json that changes what the language means; never start a project without it.

nodes.label: Structural typing
nodes.rationale: TypeScript compares shapes, not names. An unrelated object is assignable; the object literal still errors via excess property checks.

nodes.label: Phase 2 narrowing and CFA
nodes.rationale: The compiler reads if statements. This phase makes unions usable and is the most common source of 'why is this still possibly undefined?'.

nodes.label: Module augmentation
nodes.rationale: declare module adds properties to somebody else's types — how req.user, custom globalThis keys and library plugins are typed.

nodes.label: module and moduleResolution
nodes.rationale: Pick the setting that matches what actually loads the code. Most 'it compiles but crashes at runtime' reports come from the compiler modelling a module system the runtime does not use.

nodes.label: import type and verbatimModuleSyntax
nodes.rationale: A type-only import must be erasable. A vanished runtime import can break a side effect.

nodes.label: Path aliases trap
nodes.rationale: tsc resolves @/lib; Node does not. The alias must be resolved again at runtime by a bundler, imports map or loader.

nodes.label: Typed Express handlers
nodes.rationale: Request generics (Params, ResBody, ReqBody, Query) type the slots. A typed body is a promise the compiler cannot keep.

nodes.label: pg query T is an assertion
nodes.rationale: query<T>() is an assertion, not a check: the driver never verifies the row shape, so a renamed column is a runtime undefined with a green build.

nodes.label: Parse, don't validate
nodes.rationale: Types are erased, so nothing crosses the network typed. Convert unknown into a domain type once at the edge and let the type system carry it from there.

nodes.label: Schema-first with zod or valibot
nodes.rationale: z.infer as the single source of truth. Never hand-write a type that duplicates a schema.

nodes.label: JSON does not round-trip types
nodes.rationale: Date becomes a string, undefined disappears, BigInt throws, Map/Set flatten.

nodes.label: useReducer discriminated actions
nodes.rationale: The pattern where TypeScript pays for itself most obviously in React: the action union types both dispatch and every reducer case from one declaration.

nodes.label: noUncheckedIndexedAccess
nodes.rationale: arr[0] and record[key] become T | undefined. The flag that finds the most real bugs and annoys people the most.

nodes.label: TypeScript unsound by design
nodes.rationale: Assertions, any, index access, method bivariance, mutation through an alias, and Object.keys returning string[]. Trusting a guarantee you do not have is worse than having no guarantee.

nodes.label: tsc --noEmit CI gate
nodes.rationale: A transpile-only build cannot replace type checking. A green vite build proves nothing about types.

nodes.label: allowJs incremental migration
nodes.rationale: allowJs first, file-by-file conversion, leaf modules before shared ones, and never converting and refactoring in the same commit.

nodes.label: Never invent a number or console output
nodes.rationale: Every figure must have been executed on the target runtime. A plausible invented number is worse than no number. Emit a <!-- VERIFY --> marker instead.

nodes.label: 300-line page cap
nodes.rationale: Hard file-size cap. If the topic needs more, say so at the top and stop — do not compress by deleting code or gotchas.

nodes.label: Two-pass review
nodes.rationale: Pass 1 quality by a different model than the author. Pass 2 measures every VERIFY marker on Node 24. Self-review is worth nothing.

nodes.label: progress.js UI bump
nodes.rationale: Bump pages after every landed page; keep pagesPlanned mid-phase. Do not wait for a green build to bump the count. yarn build once per completed phase.

nodes.label: Fable corpus verdict
nodes.rationale: Strong. One factual error, one structural defect, twelve stamps. Written corpus is the best material in the repo; eight phases treated the 300-line cap as a content budget.

nodes.label: Syllabus review — accuracy and fullstack fit
boolean-dates granularity merge
nodes.rationale: Phase 2 rows 9 and 10 were merged into 09-boolean-dates.md. Boolean three-valued logic and interval arithmetic have nothing in common; the time type has no section. Split restores the 229 topic count.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL fullstack fit 93 percent
nodes.rationale: Only 6 of 229 rows are genuine DBA territory and every one is already Know or When Needed. The gap is what is missing, not what is present.

nodes.label: Transactional outbox
nodes.rationale: You cannot write to PostgreSQL and publish to a queue atomically. Insert the event in the same transaction as the business write, then a SKIP LOCKED poller drains it. Highest-value missing syllabus row.

nodes.label: Multi-tenancy as a decision
nodes.rationale: Shared table + tenant_id vs schema-per-tenant vs database-per-tenant. Schema-per-tenant turns every migration into N migrations at 400 tenants.

nodes.label: Modelling money
nodes.rationale: numeric(12,2) vs bigint minor units. numeric arrives in JavaScript as a string, which is why the choice matters in Node.

nodes.label: The 300-line cap read as a content budget
Cap treated as content budget
nodes.rationale: 269 files, max 299, zero overruns. Master topics median 530 lines where chunked, 220 where not. Clustering at 200–290 is evidence of budgeting, not of topics that happened to be that size.

nodes.label: EXPLAIN 186 vs count 821
nodes.rationale: Both Master, same corpus. EXPLAIN is the tool behind every performance diagnosis and got 23 percent of the space given to counting rows because Phase 10 was written before the rule was corrected.

nodes.label: MERGE RETURNING works on PostgreSQL 17+
nodes.rationale: 13-merge.md says seven times that MERGE has no RETURNING in PostgreSQL 18. RETURNING and merge_action() landed in 17 and were executed on the live 18.4 sandbox.

nodes.label: WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL 17 clause that deletes target rows the source omits. The page's proxy WHEN MATCHED AND s.v IS NULL only fires for rows that are in the source.

nodes.label: Phase 13 template stamps
nodes.rationale: Twelve files, 66 lines each, byte-identical in structure. They pass every structural check while containing nothing. Strip to one honest not-yet-written line.

nodes.label: Shared buffers measurement confound
nodes.rationale: 44.52 ms vs 2.64 ms includes TCP connect, SCRAM, backend fork and session startup on a never-connected Pool. Measure Buffers shared read then hit on one already-warm connection.

nodes.label: Phase 0 under-explained
nodes.rationale: 12 topics, 116 lines each against a corpus median of 226. Treat as a rewrite, not a patch.

nodes.label: Three quality strata
nodes.rationale: Written corpus 8.8–9.7, Phase 0 3.7–5.1, stamps 0. No middle. A page is either genuinely good or unwritten.

nodes.label: Gotchas as strongest feature
nodes.rationale: 1519 gotchas, 5.6 per page, every page has a section, symptom-first. Twelve of those are stamp boilerplate.

nodes.label: Interview star inflation
nodes.rationale: 74 percent of questions are starred. Cap at one third, defined as asked verbatim in a real interview more than once.

nodes.label: Twelve product spines
nodes.rationale: Not proposed pages. One scenario per phase group as a capstone. Nine of twelve need no new syllabus rows. Reach 13 of 14 phases.

nodes.label: Session and auth store scenario
nodes.rationale: Refresh-token rotation is a read-modify-write. UPDATE WHERE token_hash and revoked_at IS NULL with rowCount 0 means replay.

nodes.label: Catalogue filter sort search paginate
nodes.rationale: Best single capstone candidate: six phases, the endpoint every product has.

nodes.label: Background job queue in PostgreSQL
nodes.rationale: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED as the claim. LISTEN/NOTIFY is at-most-once and therefore an optimisation, never the transport.

nodes.label: Top five Fable fixes
nodes.rationale: If you only do five: correct MERGE RETURNING, remove the confounded shared-buffers benchmark, strip twelve stamps, chunk EXPLAIN, reframe client-server as a budget.

nodes.label: Condensed syllabus scenarios and work order
Sandbox npm vs site yarn
nodes.rationale: Each phase folder is its own npm project so a sandbox install can never disturb the site's yarn 4 lockfile.

nodes.label: Connect with 127.0.0.1 never localhost
nodes.rationale: Node DNS order is verbatim by default, so localhost resolves ::1 first and every connection to a container published on IPv4 fails.

nodes.label: musl vs glibc collation
nodes.rationale: Alpine sorts en_US.utf8 by byte value; Debian applies dictionary rules. Same PostgreSQL 18.4. That is why ex6 needs both containers.

nodes.label: Run before you write
nodes.rationale: A number on a page that was not produced by a script here does not belong on the page. Scripts print, they do not assert.

nodes.label: Git 2.55.0 environment probe
nodes.rationale: Measured porcelain surface, default branch, ref backend, object hash, pull-on-diverge, switch/restore, empty identity, and blob hashing on git 2.55.0.

nodes.label: Git porcelain surface
nodes.rationale: 46 main commands from git help -a first section; 172 commands on PATH.

nodes.label: filter-repo and LFS absent
nodes.rationale: switch, restore, sparse-checkout, worktree, maintenance, replay, backfill, last-modified, bundle, range-diff, filter-branch are builtins; filter-repo and lfs are ABSENT; scalar reports git version 2.55.0.

nodes.label: init.defaultBranch unset uses master
nodes.rationale: With init.defaultBranch unset, git init still names the first branch master and hints that Git 3.0 will change the default to main. HEAD points at refs/heads/master.

nodes.label: Git ref storage backend
nodes.rationale: Default ref format is files; loose-ref layout is heads and tags.

nodes.label: reftable ref format
nodes.rationale: reftable is supported; on-disk tables.list shows a 0x000000000001-0x000000000001-5d9a0b8b.ref table.

nodes.label: Default object hash SHA-1
nodes.rationale: Default object hash is sha1; sha256 is supported as an alternate object format.

nodes.label: Divergent pull requires reconcile
nodes.rationale: With pull.rebase unset, a bare git pull on diverged branches is fatal: Need to specify how to reconcile divergent branches. Options are pull.rebase false (merge), true (rebase), or pull.ff only.

nodes.label: git switch
nodes.rationale: git switch is a builtin and is no longer advertised as experimental; usage is git switch [<options>] [<branch>].

nodes.label: git restore
nodes.rationale: git restore is a builtin; usage is git restore [<options>] [--source=<branch>] <file>...

nodes.label: Empty author identity failure
nodes.rationale: Why every setup guide starts with user.email: commit fails with Author identity unknown / Please tell me who you are until user.email and user.name are set.

nodes.label: Empty blob hash e69de29
nodes.rationale: hash-object of an empty file is e69de29bb2d1d6434b8b29ae775ad8c2e48c5391; raw object header is blob.

nodes.label: Blob header plus content hash
nodes.rationale: SHA-1 of blob 6\0hello\n is ce013625030ba8dba906f756967f9e9ca394464a and matches what git reports.

nodes.label: Git object model probe
nodes.rationale: Walks content-addressed objects, the three trees, commits as snapshots, refs, packfiles, config layers, and plumbing-built commits.

nodes.label: Content-addressed Git objects
nodes.rationale: An object is content addressed by the hash of header+content. The filename is nowhere in the hash: greeting.txt and copy-of-greeting.txt share ce013625030ba8dba906f756967f9e9ca394464a.

nodes.label: git hash-object
nodes.rationale: Nothing is stored until -w writes. Without -w, cat-file fails with could not get object info. After -w the object lives at .git/objects/ce/013625… and is type blob size 6.

nodes.label: Working tree, index, and HEAD
nodes.rationale: Git keeps three trees. ?? is working-tree only; A is in the index. git diff is working tree vs index; git diff --staged is index vs HEAD.

nodes.label: Git index
nodes.rationale: The index is a real file with real blobs. ls-files --stage shows mode, blob SHA, stage, and path. file .git/index reports Git index, version 2.

nodes.label: Staged and modified at once
nodes.rationale: Editing after add leaves the old content staged. Status AM means staged AND modified at the same time.

nodes.label: Commit is a snapshot
nodes.rationale: A commit is a tree, parents, and metadata. Subdirectories are their own tree objects.

nodes.label: Four Git object types
nodes.rationale: blob, tree, commit, and tag. After the first commit: 3 blob, 1 commit, 2 tree. An annotated tag adds a tag object.

nodes.label: Annotated tag object
nodes.rationale: An annotated tag is an object (object, type, tag, tagger, message). Lightweight tags are not objects.

nodes.label: Refs and HEAD are plain files
nodes.rationale: .git/HEAD is ref: refs/heads/main. The branch file holds the same 40-character SHA that rev-parse HEAD and symbolic-ref HEAD report.

nodes.label: A branch costs 41 bytes
nodes.rationale: git branch feature/pricing writes a 41-byte ref file. Object count is unchanged: a branch is a pointer, not a copy.

nodes.label: Commit graph is parents not timestamps
nodes.rationale: A commit dated 2030 is still the child of its parent. git log --reverse is ancestry order, not date order.

nodes.label: .git directory layout
nodes.rationale: COMMIT_EDITMSG, config, description, HEAD, hooks, index, info, logs, objects, refs. repositoryformatversion 0, filemode true, bare false, logallrefupdates true.

nodes.label: Loose objects become a packfile
nodes.rationale: Before gc: 51 loose files, 204K. After git gc: 2 non-pack files, 36K, in-pack 51 across 2 packs totaling 6.03 KiB.

nodes.label: Git config layers and precedence
nodes.rationale: Local .git/config user.email is work@example.com. git -c user.email=once@example.com is scope command and wins for that invocation.

nodes.label: Plumbing vs porcelain commit
nodes.rationale: A commit built only from blob, tree, and commit plumbing is a real commit (45c50f3 Made with plumbing only) even when reachable from no branch.

nodes.label: Sandbox artifacts stay inside the project
nodes.rationale: Scratch output is kept inside the project deliberately so sandbox artifacts do not land in the host /tmp. Everything here is regenerable; scripts recreate what they need on each run. Set 2026-08-13.

nodes.label: devbible-pg container
nodes.rationale: podman run -d --name devbible-pg maps 55432:5432. Connect at 127.0.0.1:55432 as user/db/password devbible. Use pg from this folder (npm install pg).

nodes.rationale: Firefox Glean telemetry client_id 1dee9a49-7f70-4d7b-aef9-6845e8b97e82 for the react-p0 .ffprof profile.

nodes.label: NSS Internal PKCS #11 Module (react-p1)
nodes.rationale: Firefox profile NSS module. configdir is sql:…/.claude/worktrees/react-phases/sandbox/react-p1/.ffprof, so this profile was created from a worktree path.

nodes.label: Glean client ID (react-p1)
nodes.rationale: Firefox Glean telemetry client_id 57a0dc83-3bf7-433c-87ff-01598547499a for the react-p1 .ffprof profile.
